13424: कडत्र कडत्र, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. गड्), a kind of vessel or receptacle. See कलत्र।
13425: कडन्दिका कडन्दिका, f. science, = कलन्-दिका, कलिन्दिका।
13426: कडम्ब कडम्ब, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कड्), the end or point; the stalk of a pot-herb; (ई), f. the pot-herb Convolvulus Repens. See कलम्ब।
13427: कडार कडार, अस्, ई, अम् (said to be fr. rt. गड्), tawny; (अस्), m. tawny (the colour); a servant.
13428: कडितुल कडितुल, अस्, m. a sword, a scymi-tar, a sacrificial knife; [cf. कटी-तल।]
13429: कड्ड् कड्ड्, cl. 1. P. कड्डति, -डितुम्, to be hard, rough; to be harsh or severe.
13430: कण् कण्, cl. 1. P. कणति, चकाण, कणि-ष्यति, अकणीत् or अकाणीत्, कणितुम्, to become small; to sound, cry as in distress; to go or approach: Caus. काणयति, -यितुम्, aor. अचीकणत् and अचकाणत्, to sigh, sound; cl. 10. P. काणयति, यितुम्, to wink; to close the eye with the lids or lashes.
13431: कणित, अम्, n. crying out with pain.
13432: कण कण, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कण्; according to others related to कना, कनिष्ठ, कनीयस्, कन्या, in all of which the notion of small-ness prevails), a grain, a single seed; a grain or particle of dust; flake (of snow); a drop of water; a spark of fire, the spark or facet of a gem; an ear of corn; an atom, a minute particle; small, minute; (आ), f. a kind of fly, commonly कुमीरापोका; long pepper; cummin seed; (ई), f. a drop, an atom; the plant Premna Spinosa or Longifolia; a kind of corn; see कणिका. —कण-गुग्गुलु, उस्, m., N. of a plant; [cf. गन्धराज, स्वर्णकर्ण, and others.] —कण-जीर, अस्, m. a white kind of cummin seed. —कण-जीरक, अम्, n. small cummin seed. —कण-भक्ष, अस्, m. ‘eating atoms or grains’ (?), i. e. liv-ing on minute particles of food; a nickname of the philosopher Kaṇāda. —कण-भक्षक, अस्, m. a kind of bird; [cf. भारिट, श्यामचतक, शैशिर।] —कण-भक्षण, अम्, n. the eating of grains. —कण-भुज्, क्, m. nickname of Kaṇāda; see कण-भक्ष. —कण-लाभ, अस्, m. a whirlpool. —कण-शस्, ind. in small parts, in minute particles. —कणान्न (°ण-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one whose food consists of grains. —कणान्न-ता, f. the state of one who is made to feed on grains (of rice).
13433: कणिक, अस्, m. a grain, an ear of corn; the meal of parched wheat, the heart of wheat (commonly suji or semoule); a small particle, as a crystal &c.; an enemy; N. of a purificatory ceremony, viz, whirling round lamps at sacrificial rites [cf. नीराजन]; N. of a minister of king Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (आ), f. a drop, an atom, a small particle; small, minute; the plant Premna Spinosa or Longifolia; a kind of corn or rice.
13434: कणिश, अस्, अम्, m. n. an ear or spike of corn.
13435: कणिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. कनिष्ठ], the small-est, the most minute.
13436: कणीक, अस्, आ, अम्, small, diminutive.
13437: कणीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, very small; young, younger; [cf. कनीयस्।]
13438: कणप कणप, अस्, m. a kind of spear or lance; (various readings have कणय and कनय।)
13439: कणभ कणभ, अस्, m. a kind of fly with a sting; [cf. कणा।]
13440: कणाटीन कणाटीन or कणाटीर or कणाटीरक, अस्, m. a wagtail.
13441: कणाद कणाद, अस्, m., N. of a celebrated sage, considered as the author of the Vaiśeṣika philosophy, a branch of the Nyāya. He is also called Kāśyapa, and considered as a Devarṣi; the nicknames कण-भक्ष and कण-भुज् refer to the etymology of this name कण-अद, ‘eating atoms or grains;’ a goldsmith; [cf. कलाद।]
13443: कणीचि कणीचि, इस्, and कनीची, f. a sound; a tree (पल्लविन्); a creeper in flower; the plant Abrus Precatorius; a cart; [cf. कनीचि।]
13444: कणूकय कणूकय, nom. P. (connected with rt. कण्), Ved. to desire to utter words of blame or censure.
13445: कणे कणे, ind. a particle expressing the satisfying of a desire. —कणे-हत्य, ind. (rt. हन्), satiating one's self (e. g. कणे-हत्य पयः पिबति, he drinks milk till he is satiated.)
13446: कणेर कणेर, अस्, m., N. of a tree, Cascaria Ovata [cf. कर्णिकार]; (आ), f. a she-elephant; a courtezan.
13447: कणेरु, उस्, m., N. of a tree; f. a she-elephant; a courtezan.
13448: कण्ट् कण्ट्, cl. 1. P. कण्टति, -टितुम्, to go, to move.
13449: कण्टक कण्टक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. rt. कण्ट्?), a thorn; anything pointed, the point of a pin or needle, a prickle, sting; a fish-bone; a finger-nail [cf. कर-कण्टक]; the erection of the hair of the body in thrilling emotions, horripilation; any troublesome seditious person who is, as it were, a thorn to the state and an enemy of order and good government, a paltry foe (क्षुद्र-शत्रु); a sharp stinging pain, symptom of a disease; a vexing or injurious speech; any annoyance or source of vexation; a term in the Nyāya philosophy implying refutation of argu-ment, detection of error, &c.; impediment, obstacle; the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth lunar mansion; (अस्), m., N. of a barber; N. of the horse of Śākya-muni (a wrong form for कण्ठक); N. of an Agra-hāra; (according to lexicographers also) a bamboo; a workshop, a manufactory; fault, defect; N. of Makara or the marine monster, the symbol of Kāma-deva; (ई), f. a species of Solanum. (कण्टक takes the form कण्ट at the beginning of some compounds and in कण्टल, कण्टालु, कण्टिन्; cf. Gr. κεντέω κεσ-τός, κέσ-τρον.) —कण्टक-द्रुम, अस्, m. a tree with thorns, a thorn bush; the Sālmali or silk-cotton tree, Bombax Heptaphyllum. —कण्टक-प्रावृता, f. the plant Aloe Perfoliata. —कण्टक-फल, अस्, m. the Jaka or bread-fruit tree, Arto-carpus Integrifolia; another plant, Ruellia Longifolia (commonly called Go-kṣura); the castor-oil tree; the Datura; the term is applicable to any plant the fruit of which is invested with a hairy or thorny coat; [cf. कण्टकि-फल।] —कण्टक-भुज्, क्, m. a camel (‘eating thorns’). —कण्टक-मर्दन, अस्, ई, अम्, treading down thorns; suppressing disturbances, an-noyances, &c.; (अम्), n. the act of beating or treading down thorns; suppressing disturbances &c. —कण्टक-युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having thorns, thorny. —कण्टक-वृन्ताकी, f. the plant Solanum Jacquini, a species of nightshade with thorny leaves. —कण्-टक-श्रेणी, f. the Solanum Jacquini; a porcupine. —कण्टक-स्थली, f., N. of a region. —कण्टका-ख्य (°क-आख्या), अस्, m. the plant Trapa Bispinosa. —कण्टकागार (°क-अग्°), अस्, m. a kind of lizard; a porcupine. —कण्टकाशन (°क-अश्°), अस्, m. the camel (eating thorns, thistles, &c.; cf. कण्टक-भुज्). —कण्टकाष्ठील (°क-अष्°), अस्, m. a kind of fish, having many bones. —कण्टकी-कारी, f., Ved. working in thorns. —कण्टकी-द्रुम, अस्, m. Acacia Catechu. —कण्टकी-फल = कण्टकि-फल. —कण्ट-कुरण्ट, अस्, m. = झिण्टी, Barleria Cristata. —कण्टकोद्धरण (°क-उद्°), अम्, n. weeding, extracting thorns &c.; removing annoy-ances; extirpating thieves, rogues, &c., or all national and public nuisances. —कण्ट-तनु, उस्, f. a species of Solanum. —कण्ट-दला, f. the plant Pandanus Odoratissimus. —कण्ट-पत्त्र, अस्, m. the plant Flacourtia Sapida. —कण्टपत्त्र-फला, f., N. of a plant, = ब्रह्मदण्डी. —कण्ट-पाद = कण्ट-पत्त्र. —कण्ट-फल, अस्, m., N. of several plants, = गोक्षुर; bread-fruit tree, Datura Fastuosa, = लताकरञ्ज = तेजःखल (?); Ricinus Communis; (आ), f. = देवदालीलता. —कण्ट-वल्ली, f. = श्रीवल्ली-वृक्ष. —कण्ट-वृक्ष, अस्, m. = तेजःफल-वृक्ष. —कण्टा-फल, अस्, m. = कण्ट-फल। —कण्टार्तगला (°ट-आर्°), f. the plant Barleria Cærulea. —कण्टाह्वय (°ट-आह्°), अम्, n. the tube-rous root of the lotus.
13450: कण्टकार, अस्, m., N. of a plant; (ई), f., N. of several plants, Solanum Jacquini; Bombax Hepta-phyllum, the silk-cotton tree; Flacourtia Sapida.
13451: कण्टकारिका, f. Solanum Jacquini; also the fruit of this plant.
13452: कण्टकाल, अस्, m. = कण्टक-फल, q. v.
13454: कण्टकित, अस्, आ, अम्, thorny; covered with erect hairs.
13455: कण्टकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, thorny, prickly; vexatious, annoying; (ई), m., N. of several thorny plants, Acacia Catechu; Vanguiera Spinosa; Ruellia Longi-folia; Zizyphus Jujuba, bamboo; a fish; (नी), f., N. of several plants, Solanum Jacquini, red amaranth. —कण्टकि-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced from a fish; produced by the Mimosa tree. —कण्टकि-फल, अस्, m. the Indian bread-fruit tree or Jaka; see कण्टक-फल. —कण्टकि-लता, f. a gourd.
13456: कण्टकिल, अस्, m. a thorny kind of bamboo, Bambusa Spinosa.
13457: कण्टल, अस्, m. the plant Mimosa Arabica; gene-rally वावल, a tree yielding a species of Gum Arabic; the branches are prickly, whence the name.
13458: कण्टालु, उस्, m., N. of different plants; Solanum Jacquini; another species of Solanum; a bamboo.
13459: कण्टिन्, ई, m., N. of several plants, Achyranthes Aspera; Acacia Catechu; Ruellia Longifolia.
13460: कण्ठ् कण्ठ्, cl. 1. P. A., 10. P. कण्ठति, -ते, -ठितुम्, कण्ठयति, -यितुम्, to mourn; to long for; [cf. उत्कण्ठ्; cf. also Gr. πένθος, πόθος; Lat. patior.]
13461: कण्ठ कण्ठ, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. कण्), the throat, the neck (e. g. आकण्ठ-तृप्त, filled up to the throat, quite satiated); the voice (e. g. सन्न-कण्ठेन, with broken voice); sound, espe-cially guttural sound; the neck (of a pitcher or other vessel); the opening of the womb; metaphorically a bud on a stalk; immediate proximity; the space of an inch from the edge of the hole in which sacrificial fire is deposited; the tree Vanguiera Spinosa; N. of a Maharṣi; (ई), f. neck, throat; a rope or leather round the neck of a horse; a necklace, a collar; [cf. अधर-कण्ठ, उत्-कण्ठा; cf. also Lat. collum?]. —कण्ठ-कुब्ज, अस्, m. a kind of fever. —कण्ठ-कुब्ज-प्रतीकार, अस्, m. the cure of the preceding disease. —कण्ठ-कूणिका, f. the Vīṇā or Indian lute. —कण्ठ-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, reaching or extending to the throat. —कण्ठ-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, being at or in the throat; approaching or reaching the throat. —कण्ठ-तट, अस्, अम्, m. n. the side of the neck. —कण्ठ-तलासिका (°ल-अस्°?), f. the leather or rope passing round the neck of a horse. —कण्ठ-दघ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, reaching to the neck. —कण्ठ-धान, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —कण्ठ-नीडक, अस्, m. Falco Cheela; a kite. —कण्ठ-नीलक, अस्, m. a torch, a whisp of lighted straw &c. (= उल्का, commonly मसाल). —कण्ठ-पण्डित, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —कण्ठ-पाशक, अस्, m. a halter; a rope passing round an elephant's neck. —कण्ठ-बन्ध, अस्, m. a rope tied round an elephant's neck. —कण्ठ-भूषा, f. a collar or short necklace. —कण्ठ-मणि, इस्, m. a jewel worn on the throat, a dear or beloved object. —कण्ठ-रव, अस्, m., N. of an author; N. of a certain medical writer. —कण्ठ-लग्न, अस्, आ, अम्, fastened or suspended round the throat; clinging to, embracing. —कण्ठ-लता, f. a collar; a horse's halter. —कण्ठ-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being in the throat; [cf. कण्ठ-गत।] —कण्ठ-शालूक, अम्, n. a hard tumour in the throat. —कण्ठ-शुण्डी, f. swelling of the tonsils. —कण्ठ-शोष, अस्, m. drying the throat; fruitless expostulation. —कण्ठ-श्रुत्य्-उपनिषद्, त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad belonging to the Atharva-veda. —कण्ठ-सज्जन, अम्, n. hanging on or round the throat. —कण्ठ-सूत्र, अम्, n. a kind of em-brace. —कण्ठ-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, sticking in the throat; being in or upon the throat; guttural; being in the mouth ready to be repeated by rote, learnt and ready to be recited. —कण्ठागत (°ठ-आग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, come to the throat (as the breath or soul of a dying person). —कण्ठाग्नि (°ठ-अग्°), इस्, m. a bird (digesting in the throat or gizzard). —कण्ठा-भरण (°ठ-आभ्°), अम्, n. a neck-ornament, a necklace; a shorter N. of the work called Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa. —कण्ठाभरण-दर्पण, अस्, m. a commentary of Rāmasiṃha-deva on the last. —कण्ठाभरण-मार्जन, a commentary by Hari-nātha on the same work. —कण्ठावसक्त (°ठ-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, clinging to the neck, em-bracing. —कण्ठी-रव, अस्, m. a lion (roaring from the throat); an elephant in rut; a pigeon; (ई), f. the plant Gendarussa Vulgaris. —कण्ठे-काल, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva (‘blue on the neck’). —कण्ठे-विद्ध, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कण्ठेश्वर-तीर्थ (°ठ-ईश्°), N. of a Tīrtha. —कण्ठोक्त (°ठ-उक्°), अम्, n. personal testimony.
13462: कण्ठक, अस्, m., N. of a horse of Śākya-muni; [cf. कण्टक।]
13463: कण्ठतस्, ind. from the throat, with distinct words, explicitly.
13464: कण्ठिका, f. a necklace of one string or row.
13465: कण्ठिन्, ई, इनी, इ, belonging to the throat.
13466: कण्ठ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being at or in the throat; suitable to the throat; belonging to the throat, pro-nounced from the throat, guttural; (according to a Prātiśākhya the guttural letters are अ, ह्, and the जिह्वामूलीय; according to Pāṇini अ, क्, ख्, ग्, घ्, न्, and ह्; according to Vopadeva also ए।) —कण्ठ्य-वर्ण, अस्, m. a guttural letter. —कण्ठ्य-स्वर, अस्, m. a guttural vowel, i. e. अ and आ।
13467: कण्ठाल कण्ठाल, अस्, m. a boat, a ship; a hoe, a spade; war; an esculent root, Arum Campa-nulatum; a camel [cf. कण्टकाशन and कण्डोल]; a churning-vessel; (आ), f. a churning-vessel.
13468: कण्ठील, अस्, m. a camel; (अस्, आ), m. f. a churn-ing-vessel.
13469: कण्ड् कण्ड्, cl. 1. P. A. कण्डति, -ते, -डि-तुम्, to be glad; cl. 10. P. कण्डयति, यितुम्, to separate the chaff from the grain; to protect; [cf. कड्: cf. also Lith. kándu, ‘to bite;’ Cambro-Brit. cat, ‘a fragment.’]
13470: कण्डन, अम्, n. threshing, separating the chaff from the grain in mortar; that which is separated from the grain, chaff; (ई), f. a wooden bowl or mortar in which the cleaning or threshing of grain is performed.
13471: कण्डरा कण्डरा, f. a sinew (of which six-teen are considered to be in the human body); a principal vessel of the body, a large artery, vein, &c.
13472: कण्डरीक कण्डरीक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kauśika.
13473: कण्डानक कण्डानक, अस्, m., N. of a servant of Śiva.
13474: कण्डिका कण्डिका, f. a short section, the shortest subdivision in the arrangement of certain Vedic compositions, as in the White Yajur-veda; [cf. काण्ड and काण्डिका।]
13475: कण्डु कण्डु, उस्, m. f. or usually कण्डू, ऊस्, f. (fr. rt. कण्ड्), scratching; itching, the itch; (उस्), m., N. of a Ṛṣi. —कण्डू-करी, f. the plant Mu-cuna Pruritus. —कण्डू-घ्न, अस्, m. the plant Cathartocarpus (Cassia) Fistula; white mustard. —कण्डूमका, f. (मका = मक्षिका or मशक?), a kind of insect with a poisonous bite. —कण्डू-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, scratching, itching. —कण्ड्व्-आदि, अयस्, m. pl. the nominal verbs, in the list of which कण्डूयति is the first.
13476: कण्डुक, अस्, m., N. of a barber.
13477: कण्डुर, अस्, आ, अम्, scratching; (अस्), m. the plant Momordica Charantia, a species of reed; (आ), f. the plants Mucuna Pruritus and Aty-amlaparnī.
13478: कण्डूति, इस्, f. scratching; itching, the itch.
13479: कण्डूय, nom. P. A. कण्डूयति, -ते, -यितुम्, to scratch, scrape, rub: Desid. कण्डूयियिषति।
13480: कण्डूयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, scratching, rubbing.
13481: कण्डूयन, अम्, n. scratching, scraping, rubbing, itching; (ई), f. a brush for rubbing.
13482: कण्डूयनक, अस्, ई, अम्, scratching, scraping; (अस्), m. a tickler, one who tickles or scratches.
13486: कण्डूयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, scratching, a scratcher.
13487: कण्डूरा, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus; ‘what causes itching,’ alluding to the irritating property of this plant.
13488: कण्डूल, अस्, आ, अम्, having or feeling the itch, itchy; (अस्), m. an esculent root (Arum Campanu-latum).
13489: कण्डोल कण्डोल, अस्, m. a basket for holding grain, made of bamboo or canes; a safe, any place in which provisions are kept; a camel; [cf. कण्-ठाल;] (ई), f. the lute of the Cāṇḍāla; [cf. कटोल, गण्डोल।] —कण्डोल-वीणा, f. the lute of the Cāṇ-ḍāla, a vulgar lute.
13490: कण्डोलक, अस्, m. a basket, a safe, a store-room.
13491: कण्डोष कण्डोष, अस्, m. a caterpillar.
13492: कण्व कण्व, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. कण्), deaf; (अस्), m., Ved. a peculiar class of evil spirits, against whom charms are used; a praiser; N. of a renowned Ṛṣi, author of several hymns of the Ṛg-veda; he is called a son of Ghora and is said to belong to the family of Aṅgiras; (आस्), m. pl. the family or descendants of Kaṇva; (besides the cele-brated Ṛṣi there occur a Kaṇva Nārṣada, Kaṇva Śrā-yasa, Kaṇva Kāśyapa; the founder of a Vedic school; a prince, son of Pratiratha and father of Medhātithi; a son of Apratiratha; a son of Ajamīḍha and father of Medhātithi; the author of a law-book; a gram-marian.) The name कण्व was perhaps originally mythic, and afterwards transferred to a human family, as was the case with the name Aṅgiras; (अम्), n. sin, evil. —कण्व-जम्भन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. consuming or destroying the evil spirits called Kaṇvas. —कण्व-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. very much like Kaṇva, very wise. —कण्व-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. prepared after the manner of the Kaṇvas (as Soma); (Sāy.) united with praisers or with the Kaṇvas (as Indra). —कण्व-वत्, ind. like Kaṇva. —कण्व-सखि, आ, m., Ved. a friend of the Kaṇvas, friendly disposed towards them. —कण्व-होतृ, ता, m., Ved. one whose Hotṛ priest is a Kaṇva.
13493: कण्वाय, nom. A. कण्वा-यते, -यितुम्, to do mischief; perhaps originally ‘to act like a Kaṇva or evil spirit.’
13494: कत कत, अस्, m. the clearing nut plant; see the following; N. of a Muni or saint. —कत-फल, अस्, m. the clearing nut plant.
13495: कतक, अस्, m. the clearing nut plant, Strychnos Potatorum, (one of the seeds of this plant being rubbed upon the inside of the water-jars used in Bengal occa-sions a precipitation of the earthly particles diffused through the water and removes them.)
13496: कतम कतम, अस्, आ, अत् (superlative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of many ? (e. g. कतमेन पथा यातास् ते, by which road have they gone?). कतम is often a mere strengthened substitute for क, the superlative affix imparting emphasis. Hence it may occasionally be used for ‘who or which of two?’ (e. g. तयोः कत-मस्मै, to which of these two ?). It may option-ally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e. g. कतमः कठः or कतम-कठः, which Kaṭha out of many?). When followed by च and preceded by यतम an indefinite expression is formed equivalent to ‘any whosoever,’ ‘any whatso-ever,’ &c. (e. g. यतमद् एव कतमच् च विद्यात्, he may know anything whatsoever). In negative sentences कतम with चन or कतम with अपि = not even one, none at all (e. g. न कतमच्-चनाहः, not even on a single day, on no day at all). In addition to the above uses कतम is said to mean ‘best,’ ‘excessively good-looking;’ [cf. 3. क।] —कतमोरग (°म-उर्°), अस्, m., N. of a man.
13497: कतर, अस्, आ, अत् (comparative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of two? whether of two? Analogously to कतम above कतर may occasionally be used to express ‘who or which of many’ (e. g. कतरस्यां दिशि, in which quarter ?), and may optionally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e. g. कतरः कठः or कतर-कठः). In negative sentences कतर with चन = neither of the two (e. g. न कतरश्-चन जिग्ये, neither of the two was conquered; [cf. Gr. πότερος, κότερος; Goth. hvathar; Eng. whether; Lat. uter; Old Germ. huedar; Slav. kotoryi.]
13498: कतरतस्, ind. on which of the two sides ?
13499: 1. कति (fr. 2. क, declined in pl. only, Gram. 227. अ, all the cases except the nom. voc. and acc. taking terminations, whereas the correlative इति has become fixed as an indeclinable adverb), how many? quot? several (e. g. कति देवाः, how many gods? कति व्यापादयति कति वा ताडयति, some he kills and some he strikes). In the sense of ‘several,’ ‘some,’ कति is generally followed by चिद् or अपि (e. g. कतिचिद् अहानि, for several or some days). कति may be used as an adverb with चिद् in the sense of ‘oftentimes,’ ‘much,’ ‘in many ways’ (e. g. कतिचित् स्तुतः, much or often praised). कति-कृत्वस्, ind. how many times? कति-विध, अस्, आ, अम्, of how many kinds? कति-शस्, how many at a time?
13500: कतिथ, अस्, ई, अम्, to what place or stage or degree advanced? (the how-maniest?) with चिद् = advanced to such and such a point (e. g. अहं कतिथश्चिद् आस, I was so far advanced on to such and such a point).
13501: कतिधा, ind. in how many places? in how many parts? how often? कतिधा चित्, everywhere.
13502: कतिपय, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (pl. m. ए and आस्), several, some; a certain number, so many; कति-पयेन अहर्गणेन, after some days; also कति-पयैर् अहोभिः, कतिपयाहस्य, &c. —कतिप-येन or कतिपयात्, ind. with some exertion; [the affix पय has been compared with Gr. ποῖος]
13503: कतिपयथ, अस्, ई, अम्, advanced to a certain place or degree.
13504: कतमाल कतमाल, अस्, m. fire; the right form is खतमाल; [cf. also कचमाल and कर-माल।]
13505: कति 2. कति, इस्, m., N. of a sage, son of Viśvā-mitra and ancestor of Kātyāyana. (For 1. see above.)
13506: कतिक or कतिका, f., N. of a town.
13507: कतीमुष कतीमुष, अम्, n., N. of an Agra-hāra.
13508: कत्ताशब्द कत्ता-शब्द, अस्, m. the rattling sound of dice.
13509: कत्तृण कत्-तृण, कत्-तोय, कत्-त्रि। See under 2. कद्।
13510: कत्थ् कत्थ्, cl. 1. A. कत्थते, -थितुम्, to boast; to mention with praise, to praise or celebrate; to flatter or coax; to abuse, revile.
13511: कत्थन, अस्, आ, अम्, boasting, praising; a boaster, praiser; (अम्), n. boasting.
13512: कत्पय कत्-पय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. कद् and पय fr. पी = प्यै), Ved. swelling, rising; (Sāy.) one whose waters cause happiness.
13513: कत्र् कत्र्, cl. 10. P. कत्रयति, -यितुम्, to loosen, slacken, remove.
13514: कत्सवर कत्सवर, अम्, n. the shoulder, the shoulder-blade.
13515: कथ् कथ् (this rt. is perhaps connected with कथम्), cl. 10. P., ep. also A. कथयति, -ते, aor. अचकथत् or अचीकथत्, -यि-तुम्, to converse with any one (with inst. c. alone or after सह); to tell, relate, narrate, report, inform, speak about, declare, explain (with acc. of the thing or person spoken about); to describe; to denounce, betray; to suppose, state; Pass. कथ्यते, to be called; be regarded or considered as: Desid. चिक-थयिषति, to desire to tell; [cf. Goth. qvath; Eng. quoth and quote; Gr. κωτίλος, κωτίλλω.]
13516: कथक, अस्, आ, अम्, a narrator, a relater, one who recites a story or who publicly reads and ex-pounds the Purāṇas &c., one who speaks or tells; (अस्, आ), m. f. the speaker of a prologue or mono-logue; a professional story-teller; chief actor; (अस्), m., N. of a man.

13519: कथयान, अस्, आ, अम्, telling, speaking.
13520: कथयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be told, to be men-tioned, to be communicated.
13521: 1. कथा, f. conversation, speech, tale; a fable, a feigned story; talk, mention; (in phil.) disputation; का कथा (with gen. or more commonly with loc. and sometimes with प्रति), what should one say of? how should one speak of? 13522: कथानक, अम्, n. a small tale; [cf. क्रयाणक, भयानक, &c.]
13523: कथापय, nom. P. कथापयति, -यितुम्, to tell, relate, &c.
13524: कथिक, अस्, ई, अम्, a narrator, a relater, a story-teller by profession.
13525: कथित, अस्, आ, अम्, told, said, related; (अम्), n. a conversation, discourse. —कथित-पद, अम्, n. repetition, tautology.
13526: कथी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to transform into a tale. —कथी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, transformed into a tale, deceased, dead (e. g. कथी-कृतं वपुः, a body of which one can only give a history, a deceased body).
13527: कथ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be spoken about, to be told, fit to be mentioned.
13528: कथ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being told or mentioned, under narration.
13529: कथम् कथम् (fr. 2. क), ind. how? in what manner? whence? (e. g. कथम् एतत्, how is that? कथम् इदानीम्, how now? what is now to be done? कथम् मारात्मके त्वयि विश्वासः, how can there be reliance on thee of murderous mind? कथम् उत्सृज्य त्वां गच्छेयम्, how can I go away deserting you? कथम् बुद्ध्वा भविष्यति सा, how will she be when she awakes? कथम् मृ-त्युः प्रभवति वेदविदाम्, whence is it that death has power over those that know the Veda? कथम् अवगम्यते, whence is it inferred?). Sometimes कथम् merely introduces an interrogation (e. g. क-थम् आत्मानं निवेदयामि कथं वा आत्मा-पहारं करोमि, shall I declare myself or shall I withdraw ?).
13530: कथम् is often found in connection with the particles इव, नाम, नु, स्विद्, which appear to gene-ralize the interrogation (how possibly? &c.); with नु it sometimes = किमु or कुतस् (e. g. कथं नु, how much more! न कथं नु, how much less!).
13531: कथम् is often connected, like किम्, with the particles चन, चिद्, and अपि, which give an inde-finite sense to the interrogative (e. g. कथं चन, in no way, not at all). When not itself negative कथं चन = in some way, some how; scarcely, with difficulty; न कथं चन, in no way; क-थञ्चित्, some how or other, by some means or other, in any way, with some difficulty, scarcely, in a moderate degree, a little; न कथञ्चित्, not at all, in no way whatever; न कथञ्चिद् न, in no way not, i. e. most decidedly; यथा कथञ्चित्, in any way whatsoever; कथञ्चिद् यदि जीवति, it is with difficulty that he lives; कथम् अपि, some how or other, with some difficulty, scarcely, a little; कथम् अपि न, by no means, not at all. In addition to the above senses lexicographers assert that कथम् may imply ‘amazement, surprise, pleasure, abuse;’ [with कथम् cf. Gr. κατά.] At the beginning of an adjective compound कथम् may have the same sense as किम्. —कथं-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, of what shape ? —कथं-वीर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, of what power? —कथङ्-कथिक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. कथम् कथम्), one who is always asking questions, an inquisitive person. —कथङ्-कथिक-ता, f. questioning, inquiring, inquisitiveness. —कथङ्कथित (?), अस्, m. an interrogant, one who puts questions. —कथन्-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, how acting. —कथङ्-कारम्, ind. in which manner? —कथन्-ता, f. enquiry, question, demand. —क-थम्-प्रमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, of what measure? —क-थम्-भाव, अस्, m. what state? —कथम्-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, how being? of what kind?
13532: 2. कथा, ind. (for कथम्), Ved. how? whence? why? Sometimes merely a particle of interrogation (e. g. कथा शृणोति इन्द्रः, does Indra hear? यथा कथा च, in any way whatsoever).
13533: कद् 1. कद्, cl. 1. A. कदते, -दितुम्, perf. चकाद, to be confused, suffer mentally; to grieve; to confound; to kill or hurt; to call; to cry or shed tears; चकाद कदनम्, he accomplished a destruction; [cf. Gr. κῆδας; Goth. hatan: cf. also कन्द्।]
13534: कदन, अम्, n. destruction, killing, slaughter; war, sin. —कदन-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —क-दन-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, loving slaughter.
13535: कद् 2. कद्, ind. (originally the neuter form of the interrogative pronoun क), Ved. a particle of interrogation, where? कद् is used, like किम्, with the particles चन and चिद् (e. g. न कच्चन उपब्दिः शृण्वे रथस्य, not at any time or in any manner is heard the noise of thy chariot; वेति दिवः-कच्चिद् आ, he comes from heaven now and then). —कच्चिद् is sometimes used, like the simple कद्, as a particle of in-terrogation (e. g. कच्चिद् दृष्टा त्वया दमयन्ती, was Damayantī seen by thee?). कच्चिद् may some-times be equivalent to ‘I hope that’ (e. g. व्याधिर् न कच्चित् ते शरीरम् प्रतिबाधते, I hope no illness afflicts thy body).

P. कदर्थयति, -यि-तुम्, to despise, to estimate lightly; to torment, tor-ture, trouble. —कदर्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, despised, disdained, rejected; rendered useless. —कदर्थी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to disdain, despise, to estimate at small value. —क-दर्थी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, despised, disdained, ren-dered useless and unavailing. —कद्-अर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, avaricious, miserly; little, insignificant, mean; bad, disagreeable; (अस्), m. a miser. —कदर्य-ता, f. or कदर्य-त्व, अम्, n. avarice; insignificance; badness. —कदर्य-भाव, अस्, m. avarice, stingi-ness. —कद्-अश्व, अस्, m. a bad horse. —कद्-आकार, अस्, आ, अम्, ill-formed, ugly. —कद्-आख्य, अम्, n. the plant Costus Speciosus (‘having a bad name,’ i. e. कुष्ठ or दुष्ट). —कद्-आचार, अस्, आ, अम्, wicked, abandoned, following evil practices; (अस्), m. bad conduct. —कद्-इन्द्रिय, आणि, n. pl. bad organs of sense. —कद्-उष्ट्र, अस्, m. a bad camel. —कद्-उष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, tepid, lukewarm; (अम्), n. warmth, lukewarmness, gentle warmth; [cf. कवोष्ण, कोष्ण।] —कद्-रथ, अस्, m. a bad carriage. —कद्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, containing the word क. —कद्-वद, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking ill or inaccu-rately or indistinctly; contemptible, vile, base. —कल्-लोल, see s. v.

13542: कदम्बद, अस्, m. the mustard-seed plant, Si-napis Dichotoma.

13611: कन्या, f. Zend kainê; Hib. cain, ‘chaste, undefiled;’ caile, ‘a country-woman, a harlot;’ caileamhuil, ‘girlish, effeminate.’] —कन्-या-काल, अस्, m. the time of virginity. —कन्या-कुब्ज or कन्य-कुब्ज, अम्, n., N. of an ancient city of great note, in the north of Hindūstan, situated on the काली नदी, a branch of the Ganges, in the modern district of Furruckabad. The popular spelling of the name presents, perhaps, greater variations than that of any place in India (e. g. Kunnoj, Kunnouj, Kinoge, Kinnoge, Kinnauj, Kanoj, Kannauj, Kunowj, Canowj, Canoje, Canauj, &c.). In antiquity this city ranks next to Ayodhyā in Oude. It is known to classical geography as Canogyza; but the name applies also to its dependencies and the surrounding district; the etymology (कन्या, a girl, and कुब्ज, round-shouldered or crooked) refers to a legend relat-ing to the hundred daughters of Kuśanābha, the king of this city, who were all rendered crooked by Vāyu for non-compliance with his licentious desires. 13669: कम् 1. कम्, ind. (Gr. κεν), well, bene (op-posed to अकम्, ‘badly’), a particle placed after the word to which it belongs with an affirmative sense (Well, Yes), which sense, however, is generally so weak that the Indian grammarians are perhaps right in enumerating कम् among the expletives; it is often found attached to a dat. case, giving to the latter a stronger meaning, and is generally placed at the end of the Pāda (e. g. अजीजन ओस्कधीर् भोजनाय कम्, thou didst create the plants for actual food); it is also used as an enclitic with the particles नु, सु, and हि, but is nevertheless treated in the Padapāṭha as a separate word. Rarely कम् seems to be used, like कद् and किम्, as an interrogative particle; some-times it occurs, like किम् and कद्, at the beginning of compounds, marking the strange or unusual cha-racter of anything, [cf. कन्दर्प]: according to native lexicographers कम् means also head; water; food. —कम्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. lovely.
13670: कम्ब or कम्भ, अस्, आ, अम्, well (?).
13671: कम् 2. कम्, A. (not used in the con-jugational tenses) चकमे, कमिष्यते, अचकमत, कमितुम्, to wish, desire, long for; to love, be in love with; to have sexual intercourse with: Caus. A. Lat. comis; also amo with loss of the initial; câ-rus for cam-rus; Hib. caemh, ‘love, desire; fine, hand-some, pleasant;’ caomhach, ‘a friend, a companion;’ caomhaim, ‘I save, spare, protect:’ perhaps Old Germ. scim, scimo, ‘splendor;’ Armen. kamim.]

13763: करम्भ करम्भ, अस्, m. groats or coarsely ground oats &c.; a dish of parched grain; a cake, flour or meal mixed with curds, a kind of gruel, generally offered to Pūṣan (as having no teeth to masticate hard food); a mixture, a mixed odour; N. of a species of poisonous plant; N. of a son of Śakuni and father of Devarāta; N. of a brother of Rambha; (आ), f. the plant Asparagus Racemosus; another plant, = प्रियङ्गु-वृक्ष; N. of a daughter of a king of Kaliṅga and wife of Akrodhana. —करम्भाद् (°भ-अद्), त्, त्, त्, Ved. eating groats or gruel, epi-thet of Pūṣan.
13764: करम्भक, अस्, m., N. of a man; (अम्), n. groats, coarsely ground oats &c.; a cake, flour or meal mixed with curd.
13765: करम्भि, इस्, m., N. of a son of Śakuni and father of Devarāta.
13766: करम्भिन्, ई, इणी, इ, Ved. having groats.
13767: करवी करवी, f. the leaf of the plant Asa Fœtida; [cf. कर्वरी, कवरी, कावरी।]
13768: करवीक करवीक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain; [cf. कर-वीर।]
13771: करहञ्चा करहञ्चा, f., N. of a metre of four lines, each consisting of seven syllables.
13772: करहाट करहाट, अस्, m. the tree Vangueria Spinosa; the fibrous root of a lotus; N. of a region.
13773: करहाटक, अस्, m. the tree Vangueria Spinosa; N. of an heretical prince.
13774: कराङ्गण कराङ्गण, अस्, m. a market or fair visited by many men; [cf. अङ्गण।]
13775: करायिका करायिका, f. a bird, a small kind of crane.
13776: कराल कराल, अस्, आ, अम्, opening wide, cleaving asunder, gaping (as a wound); having for-midable projecting teeth, formidable, dreadful, terrible (especially as an epithet of the Rākṣasas, of Śiva, of Kāla, of Viṣṇu, and of a certain Devagandharva); great, large, high, lofty; spacious, wide; deformed; (अस्), m. a certain species of animal; resin, pitch, or a mixture of oil and the resin of the tree Shorea Robusta; N. of a region; (आ), f. the plant Hemi-desmus Indicus; an epithet of Durgā; N. of a certain woman; (ई), f. one of the seven tongues and nine Samidhs of Agni; (अम्), n. a kind of Ocimum. —कराल-कर, अस्, आ, अम्, having a powerful arm or hand; having a large trunk, as an elephant. —कराल-केशर, अस्, m., N. of a lion in the Pañcatantra. —कराल-त्रिपुटा, f. a species of corn. —कराल-दंष्ट्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having terrific teeth. —कराल-लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, terrific. —क-राल-वदना, f. an epithet of Durgā. —करालानन (°ल-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, terrific.
13777: करालक, अम्, n. a kind of Ocimum.
13778: करालिक, अस्, m. a tree; a sword; (आ), f. an epithet of Durgā.
13779: करालित, अस्, आ, अम्, rendered formidable; afraid of, alarmed by or at; magnified.
13781: करिभ करिभ, अस्, m. the tree Ficus Re-ligiosa.
13782: करिर करिर, अस्, अम्, m. n. the shoot of a bamboo. See करीर।
13783: करिष्ठ करिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superlative fr. 1. कर), doing most, doing very much.
13784: करिष्णु, used in comp. See अलङ्-करिष्णु and निर्-आकरिष्णु।
13785: करिष्य, अस्, आ, अम् (?) , Ved. to be done (?).
13786: करिष्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, willing to do, about to do.
13787: करिष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, about to do, going to do.
13788: करीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (comparative fr. 1. कर), doing more; one who does much.
13790: करीति करीति, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
13791: करीर करीर, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ), the shoot of a bamboo; (अस्), m. a water-jar; a thorny plant, described as growing in deserts and fed upon by camels, Capparisaphylla; (अम्), n. the fruit of this plant; (आ or ई), f. the root of an elephant's tusk; a cricket, a small grasshopper. —करीर-कुण, अस्, m. the fruit season of Cap-parisaphylla. —करीर-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town; (a various reading has करीरि-प्रस्थ।)
13792: करीरिका, f. the root of an elephant's tusk.
13793: करीरक करीरक, अम्, n. fight, battle.
13794: करीलदेश करील-देश, अस्, m., N. of a region.
13795: करीष करीष, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. 1. कॄ), rub-bish, refuse, dung; dry cow-dung; N. of a mountain; [cf. आखु-करीष।] —करीष-गन्धि, इस्, m., N. of a man. —करीषङ्-कष, अस्, आ, अम्, sweeping away dung; (आ), f. a strong wind, a gale. —करी-षाग्नि (°ष-अग्°), इस्, m. a fire of dry cow-dung; (this substance is very generally used as fuel in Hindūstan.)
13796: करीषक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
13797: करीषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, abounding in dung; (इणी), f. a region abounding in cow-dung; N. of a river.
13798: करुण करुण, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ, but in some of its meanings fr. 1. कृ), mourn-ful, miserable, lamenting; (अम्), ind. mournfully, wofully, pitifully, in distress; (अस्), m. that which causes pity, sorrow, affliction, tenderness, pity, com-passion; one of the nine Rasas or sentiments of a poem, the pathetic sentiment; a fruit tree, the pamplemousse, Citrus Decumana; N. of a Buddha; a Jaina saint; N. of an Asura; (आ), f. pity, com-passion; (ई), f., N. of a plant, also called ग्रीष्म-पुष्पी, चारिणी, &c.; (अम्), n., Ved. an action, a holy work. —करुण-ध्वनि, इस्, m. a cry of distress. —करुण-पुण्डरीक, अम्, n. title of a Buddhist work. —करुण-मल्ली, f. the plant Jasmi-num Sambac; also read करुणा-मल्ली. —करुण-वेदि-त्व, अम्, n. compassion, sympathy. —करुण-वेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, knowing affliction or distress, sympathising, pitiful. —करुणाकर (°ण-आक्°), अस्, m. the father of Padmanābha. —करुणात्मक (°ण-आत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, compassionate, tender-hearted. —करुणात्मन् (°ण-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, kind. —क-रुणा-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, compassionate, tender. —करुणा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, gentle, compassionate. —करुणारम्भ (°ण-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, engaging in deplorable actions. —करुणार्द्र (°ण-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, tender-hearted, soft, sensitive. —करुणार्-धित (°ण-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, kind. —करुणा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, being in a pitiful state, pitiable. —करुणा-विप्रलम्भ, अस्, m. grief of separation with the un-certainty of meeting again, fears occurring in absence. —करुणा-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, disposed to pity. —क-रुणा-वेदिता, f. charitableness, kindliness, sympathy.
13799: करुणाय, nom. P. A. -णायति, -ते, -यितुम्, to be in a pitiful condition.
13800: करुणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being in a pitiful condition, pitiable.
13801: करुत्थाम करुत्थाम, अस्, m., N. of a prince, a son of Dushyanta and father of Ākrīḍa; [cf. अश्वत्थामन्।]
13802: करुन्धक करुन्धक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Śūra and brother of Vasu-deva.
13803: करुम करुम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. an epithet of certain spectral or ghost-like appearances.
13804: करूकर करूकर, अम्, n., Ved. the joint of the neck and the chine.
13805: करूळतिन् करूऌअतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. one whose teeth are decayed and broken; [cf. the next.]
13806: करूष करूष, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people descended from a son of Manu Vaivasvata, (a prince of this people is named Danta-vakra.)
13807: करूषक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Manu Vaiva-svata; (अम्), n., N. of a species of fruit.
13808: करेट करेट, अस्, m. a finger-nail.
13809: करेटव्या करेटव्या, f. or करेटु, उस्, m. the numidian crane; [cf. करटु, कर्कट, &c.]
13810: करेणु करेणु, उस्, m. f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. कृ; cf. 1. कर), a male or female elephant, gene-rally used for the latter; according to some also करेणू; (उस्), m. the tree Pterospermum Aceri-folium; (उस्), f., N. of a plant used as a drug and supposed to grow in Kāśmīra. —करेणु-पाल, अस्, m. the groom or keeper of a female elephant; N. of a man; [cf. कारेणुपालि।] —करेणु-भू, ऊस्, m. an epithet of Pālakāpya. —करेणु-मती, f., N. of the wife of Nakula, daughter of a king of Cedi. —क-रेणु-वर्य, अस्, m. a large or powerful elephant. —करेणु-सुत, अस्, m. an epithet of Pālakāpya.
13811: करेणुक, अम्, n. the poisonous fruit of the plant Kareṇu.
13812: करेणू, ऊस्, m. f. a male or female elephant.
13813: करेनर करेनर, अस्, m. benzoin or storax. See करेवर।
13814: करेन्दुक करेन्दुक, अस्, m. a species of grass, = भू-तृण।
13815: करेवर करेवर, अस्, m. benzoin or storax.
13816: करोट करोट, अस्, m. f. a basin, a cup; the bones of the head, the skull.
13817: करोटक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga.
13818: करोटि, इस्, or करोटी, f. a basin, a cup; the skull.
13819: करोत्कर करोत्कर, करोत्पल, &c. See under 1. and 2. कर।
13820: कर्क् कर्क्, to laugh; a Sautra root, or one occurring in grammatical Sūtras but not in the Dhātu-pāṭha.
13821: कर्क कर्क, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. 1. कृ), white; good; excellent; (अस्), m. a white horse; a crab; the sign Cancer; a water-jar; fire; a mirror; N. of various plants, = कर्कट, कर्केतन, and कर्केतिल; beauty; N. of a commentator on Kātyā-yana's Śrauta-sūtras; (ई), f., Ved. a white cow (?). —कर्क-खण्ड, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —कर्क-चिर्भिटी (?), f. a small cucumber. —कर्क-फल, अम्, n., N. of a plant. —कर्क-सार, अम्, n. flour or meal mixed with curds. —कर्की-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town.
13822: कर्कट, अस्, m. a crab; the sign Cancer; a kind of bird, the numidian crane, Lanius Excubitor; N. of a plant with poisonous tubers, the fibrous root of a lotus; the curved end of the beam of a balance (to which the strings supporting the scale are attached); a kind of coitus; the radius of a circle; compass, circuit; (आ), f. the plant Momordica Mixta; (ई), f. a female crab; a snake (?); a kind of cucumber, Cucumis Utilissimus; the fruit of the plant Bombax Heptaphyllum; the curved end of the beam of a balance &c.; a small water-jar; [cf. कर्कर, कर्-कश; cf. also Gr. καρκῖνος; Lat. cancer.] —कर्कट-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —कर्कट-शृङ्ग, अम्, n. the claw of a crab. —कर्कट-शृङ्गिका or कर्कट-शृङ्गी, f. a plant, the fruit of which is compared to the claw or feelers of a crab, the horn of a goat &c., see अज-शृङ्गी; other names of this plant are काम-नाशिनी, कौलीरा, कुलिङ्गी, &c. —कर्कटाक्ष (°ट-अक्°), अस्, m. the plant Cucu-mis Utilissimus. —कर्कटाख्या (°ट-आख्°), f. the plant Karkaṭa-śriṅgī. —कर्कटाङ्गा (°ट-अङ्°), f. the same plant. —कर्कटास्थि (°ट-अस्°), n. the shell or crust of a crab. —कर्कटाह्व (°ट-आह्°), अस्, m. the plant Ægle Marmelos; (आ), f. the plant Karkaṭa-śṛṅgī. —कर्कटेश (°ट-ईश), अस्, m., N. of a sanctuary.
13823: कर्कटक, अस्, m. a crab; the sign Cancer; the plant Momordica Mixta (?); a kind of sugar-cane; a hook shaped like the claw of a crab; N. of a Nāga; (ई), f. a female crab; (अम्), n. a poisonous root; a particular fracture of the bones. —कर्कटक-रज्जु, उस्, m. a rope with a hook attached to it, shaped like the claw of a crab. —कर्कटकास्थि (°क-अस्°), n. the shell or crust of a crab.
13824: कर्कटि, इस्, f. a sort of cucumber, Cucumis Uti-lissimus.
13825: कर्कटिका, f., N. of a plant, a kind of gourd; a kernel.
13826: कर्कटिनी, f. the plant Curcuma Xanthorrhiza.
13827: कर्कटु, उस्, m. the numidian crane; [cf. करटु, &c.]
13828: कर्कन्धु कर्कन्धु, उस्, ऊस्, m. f. (considered by some as an irregular compound of कर्क and अन्धु), the jujube tree, Zizyphus Jujuba; a species of this tree with a larger fruit; (उ), n. the fruit of this tree, or the uneatable fruits of a wild species; (ऊस्), f. the berry of this tree; (उस्), m., N. of a man. —कर्कन्धु-कुण, अम्, n. the fruit season of the Karkandhu tree. —कर्कन्धु-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town. —कर्कन्धु-मती, f., N. of a woman (?). —कर्कन्धु-रोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, red like the berries of the jujube tree.
13830: कर्कर कर्कर, अस्, आ, अम्, hard, firm; (अस्), m. a bone; a hammer; a mirror [cf. कर्फर]; a strap of leather (?); N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. stone, limestone, especially the nodule found in Bengal un-der the name of Kaṅkar; [cf. कर्कट, कर्कश।] —कर्कराक्ष (°र-अक्°), अस्, m. a wagtail. —कर्कराङ्ग (°र-अङ्°), अस्, m. a kind of bird, a gallinule (?). —कर्करान्धुक (°र-अन्°), अस्, m. a blind well, one of which the mouth is overgrown with grass &c. so as to be hidden; also read कर्क-रान्धक; see अन्ध-कूप।
13831: कर्कराटु कर्कराटु, उस्, m. a glance, a side-look.
13832: कर्कराटुक कर्कराटुक, अस्, m. the numi-dian crane.
13833: कर्करेटु, उस्, m. = the preceding; [cf. करटु, &c.]
13834: कर्कराल कर्कराल, अस्, अम्, m. n. a curl, a ringlet.
13835: कर्करि कर्करि, इस् or ई, f., Ved. a kind of musical instrument, a lute; (ई), f. a water-jar.
13837: कर्करेट कर्करेट, अम्, n. the hand curved as a claw for the purpose of grasping anything.
13839: कर्कश कर्कश, अस्, आ, अम्, hard, harsh, rough (opposed to कोमल, श्लक्ष्ण); intangible; violent, cruel; unfeeling, unmerciful; harsh, unkind, miserly; (अस्), m. a sword, a scymitar; N. of several plants, = काम्पिल्ल = गुण्डारोचनी (commonly called Sunda Rochani); a kind of cassia, Cassia or Senna Esculenta; a species of sugar-cane; (आ), f. a thorny plant, Tragia Involucrata; (ई), f. the wild jujube; [cf. कर्कट, कर्कर।] —कर्कश-च्छद, अस्, m. the plants Trophis Aspera and Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. the plant Luffa Acutangula. —कर्कश-त्व, अम्, n. hardness, harshness, rough manners. —कर्-कश-दल, अस्, m. the plant Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. another plant. —कर्कश-वाक्य, अम्, n. harsh or contumelious speech.
13842: कर्कारु कर्कारु, उस्, उ, m. n. a kind of gourd, Beninkasa Cerifera.
13843: कर्कारुक, अस्, m. the plant Convolvulus Pani-culatus.
13844: कर्कि कर्कि, इस्, m. the sign of the zodiac, Cancer; also read कर्किन्, ई, m.
13846: कर्केतन कर्केतन or कर्केतर, अस्, m. (?) a kind of gem or precious stone.
13847: कर्कोट कर्कोट, अस्, m. one of the principal serpents or Nāgas of Pātāla; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (अम्), n. a poisonous fruit.
13848: कर्कोटक, अस्, m. several plants, Momordica Mixta; Ægle Marmelos; the sugar-cane; N. of a Nāga or serpent; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a barbarous tribe of low origin; (ई), f., N. of a plant; (का), f. the plant Momordica Mixta. —कर्कोटक-विष, अम्, n. the poison of Karkoṭaka.
13849: कर्चूर कर्चूर, अस्, m., N. of a plant, a kind of Curcuma; (अम्), n. gold; an orpiment; [cf. कर्-बुर and कर्बूर।]
13850: कर्चूरक, अस्, m. the plant Curcuma Zerumbet; also read कर्बूरक।
13851: कर्ज् कर्ज्, cl. 1. P. कर्जति, -जितुम्, to pain or make uneasy.
13852: कर्ण् कर्ण्, cl. 10. P. कर्णयति, -यितुम्, to pierce, bore. See आ-कर्ण्।
13853: कर्ण कर्ण, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ), the ear, the handle or ear of a vessel; the helm or rudder of a ship; the plants Cassia Fistula and Calo-tropis Gigantea; (in prosody) a spondee, a foot of two long syllables; (in geometry) the hypothenuse of a triangle or the diagonal of a tetragon; N. of a renowned hero in the Mahā-bhārata, king of Aṅga and elder brother by the mother's side of the Pāṇḍu princes, being the son of the god Sūrya by Pṛthā or Kuntī, before her marriage with Pāṇḍu. (Afraid of the censure of her relatives, Kuntī deserted the child and exposed it in the river, where it was found by a charioteer named Adhi-ratha and nurtured by his wife Rādhā; hence कर्ण is sometimes called Sūta-putra or Sūta-ja, sometimes Rādheya, though named by his foster-parents Vasu-ṣeṇa); अपि कर्णे, Ved. behind the ear or back, from behind, after [cf. अपि-कर्ण]; कर्णं दा, to give ear to, listen to; कर्णम् आ-गम्, to come to one's ears, become known to. —कर्ण-कण्डु, उस् or ऊ, ऊस्, m. f. painful itching of the ear. —कर्ण-कीटा, f. an insect or worm with many feet and of a reddish colour, Julus Cornifex; a small centipede; according to some कर्ण-कीटी. —कर्ण-कुब्ज, अम्, n., N. of an imaginary town. —कर्ण-क्ष्वेड, अस्, m. an affection of the ear, a roaring or constant noise in it. —कर्ण-खरिक, अस्, m., N. of a Vaiśya. —कर्ण-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, touching the ear, hanging on it, next to the ear, extending to the ear. —कर्ण-गूथ, अम्, n. ear-wax; (अस्), m. or कर्ण-गूथक, अस्, m. hardening of the wax of the ear. —कर्ण-गृहीत, अस्, आ, अम्, seized by the ear. —कर्ण-गृह्य, ind. seizing by the ear. —कर्ण-गोचर, अस्, आ, अम्, perceptible to the ear, audible. —कर्ण-ग्राह, अस्, m. a helmsman. —कर्ण-ग्राह-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with a helmsman (as a ship). —कर्ण-च्छिद्र, अम्, n. the outer auditory passage; [cf. कर्ण-पुट, कर्ण-रन्ध्र, &c.] —कर्ण-जप, अस्, m. ‘ear-whisperer,’ an in-former. —कर्ण-जलूका, f. an insect, Julus; a small centipede; [cf. कर्ण-कीटा।] —कर्ण-जलौका, f. or कर्ण-जलौकस्, आस्, f. the same. —कर्ण-जाप or कर्ण-जप, अस्, m. whispering in the ear, tale-bearing, calumniating. —कर्ण-जाह, अम्, n. the root of the ear. —कर्ण-जित्, त्, m. ‘the conqueror of Karṇa,’ an epithet of Arjuna; (Karṇa having taken the part of the Kurus, was killed by Arjuna in one of the great battles between them and the Pāṇḍus.) —कर्ण-तस्, ind. away from the ear. —कर्ण-ताल, अस्, m. the flapping of an elephant's ears. —कर्ण-दर्पण, अस्, m. an ear-ring, an ornament for the ear. —कर्ण-दुन्दुभि, इस्, f. a kind of worm (making a noise in the ear like a drum); see कर्ण-कीटा. —कर्ण-देव, अस्, m., N. of a king. —कर्ण-धार, अस्, m. a helmsman, a pilot. —कर्णधार-ता, f. the office of an helms-man. —कर्ण-धारिणी, f. a female elephant. —कर्ण-नाद, अस्, m. ringing in the ear. —कर्ण-नासा, f. the ears and the nose. —कर्णन्दु, उस्, f. a woman's ear-ring; see कर्णान्दु. —कर्ण-प, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कर्ण-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. the tragus, a part of the external ear. —कर्ण-पथ, अस्, m. the compass or range of hearing; कर्णपथम् आ-या or उपे (उप-इ), to come within the range of the ear, to be heard. —कर्ण-पर, अस्, m. an ornament for the ear. —कर्ण-परम्-परा, f. going from one ear to another. —कर्ण-पराक्रम, अस्, m. title of a work. —कर्ण-पर्वन्, अ, n. ‘the Karṇa section,’ title of the eighth book of the Mahā-bhārata. —कर्ण-पाक, अस्, m. inflammation of the outer ear. —कर्ण-पालि, इस्, f. the lobe of the ear; the outer and curving edge of the ear; (ई), f. an ornament of the ear, a garland or string of jewels pendent from it; N. of a river. —कर्ण-पाश, अस्, m. a beautiful ear. —कर्-ण-पुट, अम्, n. the auditory passage of the ear. —कर्ण-पुर्, ऊर्, f. or कर्ण-पुरी, f. the capital of Karṇa, i. e. Campā, the ancient N. of Bhagalpur. —कर्ण-पुष्प, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = मोरट। —कर्ण-पूर, अस्, m. an ornament of flowers worn round the ears; an ear-ring; N. of several plants, blue lotus; Acacia Sirissa; Jonesia Aśoka; N. of the father of Kavicandra, author of the Alaṅkāra Kau-stubha. —कर्ण-पूरक, अस्, m. the Kadamba tree, Nauclea Cadamba; N. of a servant. —कर्ण-पूरण, अम्, n. the act of filling the ears (with cotton &c.); any substance used for that purpose; (अस्), m. = कर्ण-पूर. —कर्ण-प्रतिनाह or कर्ण-प्रतीनाह, अस्, m. a disease of the ear, sup-pression of its excretion or wax, which is supposed to have dissolved and pass by the nose and mouth. —कर्ण-प्रयाग, अस्, m., N. of the confluence of the river Gaṅgā and Pindar. —कर्ण-प्रान्त, अस्, m. the lobe of the ear. —कर्ण-प्रावरण, अस्, आ, अम्, using the ears for a covering; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a fabulous people. —कर्ण-फल, अस्, m. a sort of fish, Ophiocephalus Kurrawey. —कर्ण-भूषण, अम्, n. or कर्ण-भूषा, f. an ear ornament. —कर्ण-मद्गुर, अस्, m. a sort of sheat fish, Silurus Unitus. —कर्ण-मल, अम्, n. the excretion or wax of the ear. —कर्ण-मुकुर, अस्, m. an ear ornament; an ear-ring. —कर्ण-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, headed by Karṇa, having Karṇa as leader. —कर्ण-मूल, अम्, n. the root of the ear. —कर्णमूलीय, अस्, आ, अम्, near the root of the ear. —कर्ण-मोटि, इस्, f. an epithet of Devī or Durgā in one of her forms or incarnations (Cāmuṇḍā). —कर्ण-योनि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having the ear as a source or starting-point, going forth from the ear, an epithet of an arrow, because in shooting the bow-string is drawn back to the ear. —कर्ण-रन्ध्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. the orifice or auditory passage of the ear; [cf. कर्ण-च्छिद्र, कर्ण-पुट, &c.] —कर्ण-रोग, अस्, m. disease of the ear. —कर्णरोग-प्रतिषेध, अस्, m. cure of a disease of the ear. —कर्णरोग-विज्ञान, अम्, n. diagnosis of any disease of the ear. —कर्ण-लता, f. or कर्ण-लतिका, f. the lobe of the ear. —कर्ण-वंश, अस्, m. an elevated plat-form of bamboo. —कर्ण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having ears, long-eared; furnished with tendrils or hooks; having a helm. —कर्ण-वर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, earless; (अस्), m. a snake. —कर्णविट्क, अस्, आ, अम्, fur-nished with ear-wax. —कर्ण-विद्रधि, इस्, f. ulcer-ation of the ear. —कर्ण-विवर, अम्, n. the audi-tory passage of the ear. —कर्ण-विष्, ट्, f. ear-wax. —कर्ण-वेध, अस्, m. ‘ear-piercing,’ a religious ceremony performed to prevent a person from dying, if the birth of a third son be expected; piercing the ear to receive ear-rings. —कर्ण-वेधनी or कर्ण-वेधनिका, f. an instrument for piercing the ear of an elephant. —कर्ण-वेष्ट, अस्, m. an ear-ring; N. of a prince. —कर्ण-वेष्टक, अस्, m. the flaps of a cap protecting the ear; (अस् or अम्), m. n. (?) an ear-ring. —कर्ण-वेष्टन, अम्, n. an ear-ring. —कर्ण-शष्कुली, f. the outer part of the ear, the exterior cartilaginous portion leading to the auditory passage. —कर्ण-शिरीष, अस्, m. a Śirīṣa flower fastened to the ear as an ornament. —कर्ण-शूल, अस्, अम्, m. n. ear-ache. —कर्णशूलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having ear-ache. —कर्ण-शोभन, अम्, n., Ved. an ear ornament. —कर्ण-श्रव, अस्, आ, अम्, audible, loud. —कर्ण-श्रवस्, आस्, m., N. of a Brāhman. —कर्ण-श्रुत्, त्, m., N. of the author of several hymns of the Ṛg-veda. —कर्ण-संस्राव or कर्-ण-स्रव or कर्ण-स्राव, अस्, m. running of the ear, discharge of pus or ichorous matter from the ear. —कर्ण-सू, ऊस्, m. the father of Karṇa, an epithet of Sūrya or the sun. —कर्ण-सूचि, इस्, m. a kind of insect. —कर्ण-स्फोटा, f. a sort of creeper (com-monly काणफाटा). —कर्ण-कर्णि, ind. from ear to ear, whispering into each other's ears. —कर्-णाञ्जलि (°ण-अञ्°), इस्, m. the auditory passage of the outer ear. —कर्णाढक (°ण-आढ्°), अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of this man. —कर्णादेश (°ण-आद्°), अस्, m. an ear-ring (?). —कर्णानुज (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. an epithet of Yudhiṣṭhira, the younger brother of Karṇa, one of the five Pāṇḍu princes. —कर्णान्तिक (°ण-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, near or close to the ear. —कर्णान्दु (°ण-अन्°), उस् or ऊ, ऊस्, f. an ornament for the ear; an ear-ring. —कर्णाभरणक (°ण-आभ्°), अस्, m. the tree Cathartocarpus (Cassia) Fistula. —कर्-णारा (°ण and rt. ऋ?), f. an instrument for perfo-rating the ear of an elephant. —कर्णारि (°ण-अरि), इस्, m. an epithet of Arjuṇa (as the enemy of Karṇa); the tree Terminalia Arjuna. —कर्णार्पण (°ण-अर्°), अम्, n. applying the ear, giving ear, paying attention, listening to. —कर्णालङ्कार (°ण-अल्°), अस्, m. or कर्णालङ्क्रिया, f. or कर्णालङ्कृति, इस्, f. an ear ornament, an ear-ring. —कर्णाश्व (°ण-अश्°?), अस्, m., N. of a man. —कर्णास्फाल (°ण-आस्°), अस्, m. the flapping to and fro of an elephant's ears. —कर्णे-चुरुचुरा, f. tale-bearing. —कर्णे-जप, अस्, आ, अम्, a slanderous whisperer, a secret traducer, a tale-bearer, an informer. —कर्णे-टिरि-टिरा, f. tale-bearing. —कर्णेन्दु (°ण-इन्°), उस्, f. a semicircular ornament of the ear, an ear-ring; [cf. कर्णान्दु।] —कर्णोत्पल (°ण-उत्°), अस्, m., N. of a poet. —कर्णोदय (°ण-उद्°), N. of a book. —कर्णोपकर्णिका (°ण-उप्°), f. a female tale-bearer or informer. —कर्णोर्ण (°ण-ऊर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having wool on the ears (as any animal).
13854: कर्णक, अस्, m., Ved. a prominence, handle, or projection on the side or sides (of a vessel &c.); a tendril; applied also to the legs when spread out; N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of this man. —कर्णक-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. furnished with tendrils or side branches.
13855: कर्णकित, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with tendrils.
13856: कर्णल, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with ears.
13857: कर्णिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having ears, having large or long ears; having a helm; (अस्), m. a steersman; pl., N. of a people; N. of a king in Potāla; (आ), f. an ear-ring or ornament for the ear; a knot, tubercle; round protuberance (e. g. the round protuberance at the end of a reed or cane); the pericarp of a lotus; a fruit-stalk; the tip of an elephant's trunk; the middle finger; chalk; a pen or small brush; a trowel; the plants Premna Spinosa or Longifolia, and Odina Pinnata; a bawd; N. of an Apsaras; N. of the wife of Kaṅka. —कर्णिकाचल, अस्, m. an epithet of the fabulous mountain Meru; (fr. कर्णिका, the seed vessel of a lotus, and अचल, a mountain, Meru being in the centre of the world, the divisions of which are compared to the leaves of a lotus); also कर्णि-काद्रि, &c.
13858: कर्णिकार, अस्, m. the tree Pterospermum Aceri-folium; also Cassia Fistula; the pericarp of a lotus; (अम्), n. the flower of the tree Pterospermum Ace-rifolium and of Cassia Fistula. —कर्णिकार-प्रिय, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva.
13860: कर्णिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having ears, relating to the ear; long-eared; (at the end of compounds) having (any-thing) attached to the ear; furnished with flaps or anything similar (said of shoes); barbed, furnished with knots &c. (as an arrow); having a helm; (ई), m. the side of the neck, the part near the ear; a steersman; N. of a mountain, one of the seven prin-cipal ranges of the mountains, dividing the universe; (इनी), f. (scil. योनि) a disease of the uterus, prolapsus or polypus uteri. —कर्णी-रथ, अस्, m. (for कर्णि-रथ), a covered car, or (according to some) a litter for the conveyance of women &c., borne on men's shoulders.
13862: कर्णी, a fem. form related to कर्ण and appear-ing in compounds (e. g. अयस्-कर्णी). —कर्णी-सुत, अस्, m. an epithet of Kaṃsa, the enemy of Kṛṣṇa; according to the scholiast the author of a thieves' manual.
13863: कर्ण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in or at the ear; suita-ble to the ear.
13864: कर्णाट कर्णाट, आस्, m. pl., N. of a country and the people inhabiting it, whence the modern Karnatic; the name, however, was anciently applied to the central districts of the peninsula, including Mysore; (ई), f. a princess of Karṇāṭa; a plant, com-monly Haṃsapadī; one of the Rāgiṇīs or female personifications of the musical modes, the bride of the Rāga Mālava. —कर्णाट-देश, अस्, m. the Karṇāṭa country.
13865: कर्णाटक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a country and the people inhabiting it. —कर्णाटक-देश, अस्, m. the Karṇāṭa country. —कर्णाटक-भाषा, f. the dia-lect of Karṇāṭa.
13867: कर्त् कर्त् (a various reading for कत्र्, कर्त्र्), cl. 10. P. कर्तयति, -यितुम्, to slacken or unloose, to remove.
13868: कर्त कर्त, अस्, m. (fr. 1. कृत्?), Ved. a hole, a cavity; (a more recent form is गर्त।)
13869: कर्तन 1. कर्तन, अम्, n. (fr. 1. कृत्), cutting, cutting off or in pieces, excision; (ई), f. scissors.
13871: कर्तरिका, f. a knife, a small sword or cutlass; a hunter's knife or sword, a couteau de chasse; scissors.
13872: कर्तरी, f. a scissors or shears; a knife; a small sword or cutlass; the part of an arrow to which the feathers are attached.
13873: कर्तन 2. कर्तन, अम्, n. (fr. 2. कृत्), spin-ning cotton or thread.
13874: कर्तरीय कर्तरीय, a kind of poisonous plant.
13875: कर्तव्य कर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fut. pass. part. fr. 1. कृ), to be done, made or accomplished, what ought to be done; to be imposed (as a punishment); to be turned towards (as the mind); to be offered; to be acted; (अम्), n. what ought to be done, obliga-tion, duty, task. —कर्तव्य-ता, f. or कर्तव्य-त्व, अम्, n. necessity, obligation; propriety, fitness; suit-able measures.
13876: कर्तु, the base of several cases, used as infinitives of the verb कृ in the Veda (e. g. कर्तुम्, कर्तवे, कर्तवै, कर्तोस्). —कर्तु-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, de-sirous or intending to do.
13877: कर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, a doer, a maker, one who makes or does, an agent, one who practises what he knows; one who acts in a religious ceremony, a priest; (very often at the end of compounds, e. g. भय-कर्तृ, राज्य-कर्तृ, &c.); (ता), m. the creator of the world, an epithet of Brahmā, of Viṣṇu, and of Śiva; (in gram.) an agent, one who acts of his own accord (स्व-तन्त्रः), the active noun, the nominative case. —कर्तृ-ता, f. the state of being the agent of an action. —कर्तृ-त्व, अम्, n. agency, the act or property of an agent. —कर्तृ-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —कर्तृ-वाच्य, अस्, m. the active voice. —कर्तृ-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing or being within the agent. —कर्तृस्थ-क्रियक, अस्, आ, अम्, any (root &c.) whose action stands within the agent. —कर्तृस्थ-भावक, अस्, आ, अम्, any (root &c.) whose state or भाव stands within the agent.
13878: कर्तृक, अस्, आ, अम्, an agent, one who does anything. —कर्तृक-त्व, अम्, n. agency, action.
13879: कर्त्र, अम्, n., Ved. an incantation, charm.
13880: कर्त्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be done or accom-plished; (अम्), n. obligation, duty; task.
13881: कर्तित कर्तित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. कृत्), cut, cut off.
13882: कर्तिष्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, or कर्तिष्य-माण, अस्, आ, अम्, intending or wishing to cut.
13883: कर्त्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cut down, to be killed.
13884: कर्त्तृका, f. a small sword, a knife; [cf. the next.]
13886: कर्त्त्री, f. a pair of scissors.
13887: कर्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cut down.
13888: कर्त्र् कर्त्र्, cl. 10. P. कर्त्रयति, -यितुम्, to unloose, remove; [cf. कर्त् and कत्र्।]
13889: कर्द् कर्द्, cl. 1. P. कर्दति, -दितुम्, to rum-ble, as the bowels; to caw, as a crow; or to make any similar noise; [cf. पर्द्; Gr. χορδή.]
13890: कर्दन, अम्, n. rumbling of the bowels, bor-borygmi; (ई), f. the day of full moon in the month Caitra.
13891: कर्द कर्द, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कर्द्), mud; clay.
13892: कर्दट, अस्, m. mud, dirt; the fibrous root of the lotus (= करहाट); any aquatic weed, as Vallisneria &c.
13893: कर्दम, अस्, m. mud, slime; mire, clay; dirt, filth, sin; a kind of plant; a poisonous kind of bulb; N. of a Nāga; N. of a Prajāpati, born from the shadow of Brahmā, or son of that god by Chāyā, and the husband of Devahūti and father of Kapila; a son of Prajāpati Pulaha; (ई), f., N. of a plant; (अम्), n. flesh; (अस्, आ, अम्), furnished with mud, mire, dirt, filth. —कर्दम-राज, अस्, m. or कर्दम-राजन्, आ, m., N. of a man, a son of Kṣema-gupta. —कर्दमाटक (°म-आट्°), अस्, m. a receptacle for filth, a sewer, &c.; [cf. कन्याट, पत्न्याट।]
13894: कर्दमक, अस्, m. a kind of granulous fruit; a poisonous kind of bulb; a kind of serpent.
13895: कर्दमित, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with mud, dirty.
13897: कर्दमिल, अम्, n., N. of a region.
13898: कर्पट कर्पट, अस्, अम्, m. n. old or patched or ragged garments; [cf. कार्पटिक and पञ्च-कर्पट।] —कर्पट-धारिन्, ई, m. a religious men-dicant, a beggar in patched or ragged clothes, or some-times with merely a cloth to cover the privities.
13899: कर्पटिक, अस्, आ, अम्, or कर्पटिन्, ई, इनी, इ, covered with patched or ragged garments, clothed in beggar's raiment.
13900: कर्पण कर्पण, a kind of lance or spear; [cf. कणप and कर्पर।]
13901: कर्पर कर्पर, अस्, m. a cup, a pot, an iron saucepan or frying-pan (according to some also n. in this sense); the skull, the cranium; a kind of weapon; the plant Ficus Glomerata, [cf. उदुम्-बर]; (ई), f. a collyrium extracted from the Amo-mum Anthorhiza, [cf. घट-कर्पर, खर्पर।]

13921: कर्मन् कर्मन्, अ, n. (fr. rt. 1. कृ; according to some also m.), action, work, deed; performance, business; office; specific action, moral duty, the obligation imposed by peculiarities of tribe, occupa-tion, &c.; labour (as opposed to rest, प्रशान्ति); any religious action or rite (as sacrifice, ablution, &c., especially as originating in the hope of future re-compense and as opposed to speculative religion or knowledge of spirit); action consisting in motion as the third among the seven categories of the Nyāya philosophy, (of these motions there are five, viz. उत्-क्षेपण, throwing upwards; अव-क्षेपण, throwing downwards; आ-कुञ्चन, contraction; प्र-सारण, extension or dilatation; and गमन, going or motion in general); product, result, effect; organ of sense [cf. कर्मेन्द्रिय]; natural or active pro-perty (as maturity, of heat; support, of earth; disper-sion, of wind, &c.); the immediate object of an agent or act; (in grammar) the idea or notion expressed by the acc. case, (this object is of four kinds, viz. a. निर्वर्त्य, when anything new is produced, e. g. कटं करोति, ‘he makes a mat;’ पुत्रम् प्रसूते, ‘she bears a son:’ b. विकार्य, when change is implied either of the substance and form, e. g. काष्ठम् भस्म करोति, ‘he makes ashes out of fuel;’ or of the form only, e. g. सुवर्णं कुण्डलं क-रोति, ‘he fashions gold into an ear-ring:’ c. प्राप्य, when any desired object is attained, e. g. ग्रामं गच्छति, ‘he goes to the village;’ चन्द्रम् पश्यति, ‘he sees the moon:’ d. अनीप्सित, when an undesired object is abandoned, e. g. पापं त्यजति, ‘he leaves the wicked’); fate, the certain consequence of previous acts [cf. कर्म-पाक and कर्म-विपाक]; (in as-tronomy) the tenth lunar mansion. —कर्म-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, working for other people, a hired labourer, a servant of any kind (as a pupil &c.) who is not a slave, an agent, any one who does work or business; (अस्), m. an epithet of Yama, the regent of the dead; (ई), f. the plant Sanseviera Zeylonica; the plant Momor-dica Monadelpha. —कर्म-कर्तृ, ता, m. ‘an object-agent’ or ‘object-containing agent,’ i. e. an agent which is at the same time the object of an act on (this is the idea expressed by the reflexive passive, as in ओदनः पच्यते, ‘the mashed grain cooks of itself,’ see Gram. 461. c); one who performs any act (without receiving wages for it, according to native lexicographers); (अस्), m. a bull; a blacksmith (forming a mixed caste re-garded as the progeny of the divine artist Viśva-karman and a Śūdrā woman); (ई), f. the plants Sanseviera Zeylonica and Momordica Monadelpha. —कर्म-कारक, अस्, आ, अम्, one who does any act or work. —कर्मकारापय, nom. (fr. कर्म-कार) A. कर्मकारापयते, -यितुम्, to cause any one to work as a servant. —कर्म-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, working, doing any work or act, (in compounds preceded by an adjective or pronoun, e. g. शुभ-कर्म-कारिन्, doing good works; (अस्), m. the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa; the Kali-yuga or fourth and present age of the world, the age of iniquity. —कर्मज-गुण, अस्, m. a property resulting from human acts (as separation, reunion, &c.). —कर्म-जित्, त्, m., N. of a prince. —कर्म-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, skilled in any work; [cf. कर्म-विपाक।] —कर्म-प्रदीप, अस्, m. title of a work of Kātyāyana; N. of a work of Miśra. —कर्मप्रदीप-विवृति, N. of Śivarāma's com-mentary on the Karmapradīpa. —कर्म-प्रदीपिका, f. title of a work of Kāma-deva. —कर्म-प्रव-चनीय, employed for the definition of an action; (अस्), m. (scil. शब्दस्) a term for certain preposi-tions, particles, or adverbs, not connected with a verb, but with a case of a noun; (according to Pāṇini the first and general category to which prepositions belong is that of Nipātas or particles; they are Upasargas and Gatis when they are in connection with verbal action, i. e. with the tenses of a verb; but the term गति is more comprehensive than उपसर्ग, and is applicable also when the verbal root becomes de-veloped into a noun substantive, adjective, or parti-ciple. Moreover, the term उपसर्ग is confined to the prepositions with सु and दुस्, whereas the Gatis include many other adverbial prefixes such as अलम् and the nouns and adjectives which take the affix च्वि &c. Lastly, prepositions are Karmapravacanīyas if they are unconnected with verbs and govern a noun either separated from it or forming a compound with it. A Karmapravacanīya never loses its accent, and exercises no euphonic influence on the initial letters of a fol-lowing verb.) —कर्म-प्रवाद, अस्, m., N. of the eighth of the fourteen Pūrvas or oldest religious writings of the Jainas. —कर्म-फल, अम्, n. the fruit or recompense of actions; pain, pleasure, &c., considered as the consequence of acts; the fruit of the tree Averrhoa Carambola; [cf. कर्मरङ्ग।] —कर्मफलोदय (°ल-उद्°), अस्, m. the occur-rence of consequences. —कर्म-बन्ध, अस्, m. the tie of works (by which the soul is attached to pleasure &c.). —कर्म-बन्धन, अस्, आ, अम्, bound by acts; (अम्), n. confinement to repeated existence, as the consequence of acts. —कर्म-भू, ऊस्, f. tilled or cultivated ground. —कर्म-भूमि, इस्, f. the land or region of religious actions, i. e. where such actions are performed; (according to Hemacandra the Karmabhūmis are Bharata, Airāvata, and Videha, but not the district of the Kurus; the other Varṣas are फल-भूमयस्, i. e. lands of recompense; cf. कर्म-क्षेत्र।) —कर्म-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, con-sisting of works, resulting from works. —कर्म-मार्ग, अस्, m. the way of work; a technical term used by thieves for the breaking of walls &c. —कर्-म-मीमांसा, see s. v. मीमांसा. —कर्म-मूल, अम्, n. (fr. कर्मन् and ऋघ in ऋघाय), N. of a teacher. —कर्म-वचन, अम्, n. (with Buddhists) the ritual. —कर्म-वज्र, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘whose thunderbolt is work;’ an epithet of the Śūdra. —कर्म-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, busy with a work, em-ployed in it. —कर्म-वश, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the power of or subject to former actions; 13928: कर्मारक, अस्, m. the plant Averrhoa Carambola.
13929: कर्मिक, अस्, आ, अम्, acting, active.
13930: कर्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, acting, active, busy; performing a religious action; engaged in any work or business; belonging or relating to any act.
13931: कर्मिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be a superlative of the last), very active, assiduous, diligent.
13932: कर्मीण = कर्मन् at the end of a compound; [cf. अलङ्कर्मीण।]
13933: कर्मन्द कर्मन्द, अस्, m., N. of a man, author of a Bhikṣu-sūtra.
13934: कर्मन्दिन्, ई, m. a beggar, a religious mendi-cant, a member of the fourth order (lit. ‘a follower of Karmanda’).
13935: कर्मर कर्मर and कर्मरक, अस्, m. the plant Averrhoa Carambola.
13936: कर्मरङ्ग, अस्, m., N. of the same plant; (अम्), n. the acid fruit of this plant.
13937: कर्मरी कर्मरी, f. the manna of the bam-boo; [cf. वंश-रोचना।]
13939: कर्मस कर्मस, अस्, m., N. of a son of Pulaha and Kṣamā; [cf. कर्म-श्रेष्ठ।]
13940: कर्मीर कर्मीर, अस्, आ, अम्, variegated; (a various reading for किर्मीर।)
13941: कर्मीरक, अस्, m. a small tree, Trophis Aspera.
13942: कर्व् कर्व्, cl. 1. P. कर्वति, -वितुम्, to be proud, to boast; [cf. खर्व् and गर्व्।]
13943: कर्व कर्व, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ), love, desire; a rat.
13944: कर्वट कर्वट, अस्, अम्, m. n. declivity of a mountain; a village, market-town, the capital of a district (of two or four hundred villages) in a pleasant site and of handsome construction; (अस्), m., N. of a country or a people; (ई), f., N. of a river; (अम्), n. a city.
13945: कर्वटक, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?) declivity of a mountain.
13946: कर्वर 1. कर्वर, अम्, n. (fr. rt. 1. कृ), Ved. a deed, action.
