14956: कुटि, इस्, ई, m. f. a curvature, a curve; a hut, cottage, house, hall, shop; (ई), f. a vessel with openings used for fumigations; a bawd, a procuress or go-between; a nosegay, a bundle or tuft of flowers or vegetables; a kind of perfume, commonly Murā; spirituous liquor; (इस्), m. the body; a tree; [cf. Eng. hut; Germ. Hütte.] —कुटि-चर, अस्, m. a crocodile or porpoise. —कुटि-पार्थिव, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कुटी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, curved, curled, twisted, frizzled; (अम्), n. anything (as woollen cloth) curled or twisted. —कुटी-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, inside the house. —कुटी-गु, उस्, m., N. of a man. —कुटी-चक, अस्, m. a kind of religious mendicant, one who lives at his son's expense; (lit. ‘delighting in staying in the house.’) —कुटी-चर, अस्, m. an ascetic of a particular order, one who consigns the care of his family to his son and remains at home en-gaged solely in devotion; or one who goes begging from one house to another. —कुटी-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of a house (?). —कुटी-मुख, अस्, m., N. of one of the attendants of Kuvera.
14957: कुटिक, अस्, आ, अम्, bent, crooked; (आ), f., N. of a river.
14958: कुटित, अस्, आ, अम्, crooked, bent.
14959: कुटितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, making crooked; acting dishonestly; being bent.
14960: कुटिर, अम्, n. a hut, a cottage.
14961: कुटिल, अस्, आ, अम्, bent, crooked, curved, round, running in curved lines, crisped, curled; going crookedly, tortuous; insincere, dishonest, fraudu-lent; (आ), f., N. of a plant [cf. तगरपादी]; N. of a river; (according to some) N. of the Sarasvatī; N. of a metre containing four lines of fourteen sylla-bles each; (अम्), n., N. of a plant [cf. तगर, कुञ्चित, वक्र]; a kind of perfume; tin. —कुटिल-गति, इस्, f. a species of the Atijagatī metre, = चन्-द्रिका. —कुटिल-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going crookedly, tortuous. —कुटिल-ता, f. or कुटिल-त्व, अम्, n. crookedness; guile, dishonesty. —कुटिल-पक्ष्म, अस्, आ, अम्, having curved eyelashes or brows. —कुटिल-स्वभाव, अस्, आ, अम्, crooked-minded, disingenuous. —कुटिलाशय (°ल-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ill-intentioned, malevolent.
14962: कुटिलक, अस्, इका, अम्, bent, curved, crooked, winding; (इका), f. crouching, coming stealthily as a hunter on his prey; a peculiar movement or gesture (in theatrical language); an instrument used by a blacksmith, a blacksmith's forge.
14964: कुटीय, nom. P. कुटीयति, -यितुम्, to imagine one's self in a hut.
14965: कुटीर, अस् or अम्, m. n. a small house, a hut, a hovel; a kind of plant; (अम्), n. sexual intercourse; exclusiveness.
14967: कुटङ्क कुटङ्क, अस्, m. (connected with कुट above), a roof, a thatch; [cf. कुटुङ्गक, कुडङ्ग, कुण्डङ्ग, कुटल।]
14968: कुटङ्ग कुटङ्ग, N. of a place.
14969: कुटङ्गक कुटङ्गक, अस्, m. an arbour formed by creeping plants overrunning a tree; a roof or thatch; a house, a small house, a hut or cottage; [cf. कुटुङ्गक।]
14970: कुटच कुटच, अस्, m. (for कुट-ज), the medicinal tree Wrightia Antidysenterica.
14971: कुटज कुट-ज। See under कुट above.
14972: कुटन्नक कुटन्नक, अम्, n. the fragrant grass Cyperus Rotundus; [cf. also the following.]
14973: कुटन्नट कुटन्नट, अस्, m. the tree Calos-anthes Indica; (अम्), n. the fragrant grass Cyperus Rotundus.
14974: कुटप कुटप, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कुट्), a measure of grain &c. (= कुडव); a saint, a divine sage or Muni; a garden or grove near a house (= निष्कुट); (अम्), n. a lotus.
14975: कुटर कुटर, अस्, m. a post round which the string passes that works the churning-stick [cf. कुटक and कुठर]; N. of a Nāga.
14976: कुटरु कुटरु, उस्, m., Ved. a cock; a tent, a house of cloth or canvas.
14977: कुटरुणा कुटरुणा, f. a plant, commonly Teöri, Ipomœa Turpethum.
14978: कुटल कुटल, अम्, n. a roof, a thatch; [cf. कुटङ्क।]
14979: कुटि कुटि, कुटिर। See under rt. कुट् above.
14980: कुटिकोष्टिका कुटिकोष्टिका, f., N. of a river.
14981: कुटिल कुटिल। See under rt. कुट्, col. 2.
14982: कुटीर कुटीर। See under rt. कुट्, col. 2.
14983: कुटुङ्गक कुटुङ्गक, अस्, m. an arbour or bower formed of creeping plants; a creeper winding round a tree; a thatch, a roof; a hut, a cottage; a granary, a store-room; [cf. कुटङ्क, कुटङ्गक, कुडङ्ग।]
14984: कुटुनी कुटुनी, f. a wrong reading for कुट्टनी, q. v.
14985: कुटुम्ब कुटुम्ब, अम्, n. a household, the collective members of a household, a family; the care of a family, house-keeping; the care taken by a householder for the members of his family, hence metaphorically care or anxiety about anything; (अस्, अम्), m. n. name; race; a kinsman, a relation by descent; a connection, a relation by marriage by the mother's side; offspring, progeny. —कुटुम्ब-क-लह, अस्, अम्, m. n. domestic dissension, family feud. —कुटुम्ब-व्यापृत, अस्, m. a provident and attentive father of a family. —कुटुम्बार्थम् (°ब-अर्°), ind. for the support or on account of a family. —कुटुम्बौकस् (°ब-ओक्°), अस्, n. apartments &c. appropriated to the accommodation of relations &c.
14986: कुटुम्बक, अस्, आ, अम्, being of one family; (अम्), n. a household; the duties and cares of a house-holder; a family, kindred.
14987: कुटुम्बय, nom. A. -यते, to support a family.
14988: कुटुम्बिक, अस्, आ, अम्, taking care of a family or household; (अस्), m. the slave of a house.
14989: कुटुम्बिन्, ई, m. a householder, a paterfamilias; one who supports or takes care of a family; meta-phorically one who takes care of anything (especially at the end of a compound); a member of a family, any one belonging to a household; a peasant, a cultivator of the soil; (इनी), f. the wife of a house-holder and mother of a family, a matron; a large household, a large family; a small shrub used in medicine, a kind of moon-plant, = क्षीरिणी. —कु-टुम्बि-ता, f. or कुटुम्बि-त्व, अम्, n. family con-nection or union, living as one family.
14990: कुटेर कुटेर, अस्, m. a hut, a cottage; [cf. कुटीर।]
14991: कुट्ट् कुट्ट्, cl. 10. P. कुट्टयति, अचुकुट्टत्, यितुम्, to cut, divide; to grind or pound; to multiply; to censure, abuse.
14992: कुट्ट, अस्, ई, अम्, (at the end of compounds) cut-ting, dividing, making small; grinding, pounding; (अस्), m. a multiplier such that a given dividend being multiplied by it and a given quantity added to (or subtracted from) the product, the sum (or difference) may be measured by a given divisor. —कुट्टप-रान्त or कुट्टापरान्त (°ट-अप्°), आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —कुट्ट-प्रचरण and कुट्ट-प्रा-वरण, आस्, m. pl., N. of two nations.
14993: कुट्टक, अस्, आ, अम्, what cuts or divides, what pounds or grinds; (अस्), m. a grinder or pulverizer, a multiplier, &c. [cf. कुट्ट]; a kingfisher. —कुट्टक-व्यवहार, अस्, m. or कुट्टकाध्याय (°क-अध्°), अस्, m. that branch or chapter of arithmetic which treats of the कुट्ट or कुट्टक।
14994: कुट्टन, अम्, n. cutting, dividing; pounding, grinding, beating, threshing; abusing; (ई), f. a bawd, a procuress, a go-between.
14995: कुट्टन्ती, f. a kind of dagger.
14996: कुट्टाक, अस्, ई, अम्, what cuts or divides.
14997: कुट्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, cut, divided; pounded, flat-tened; (आ), f., scil. सिरा, unskilful opening of a vein, the latter being cut to pieces by repeated application of the knife.
14998: कुट्टिन्, ई, इनी, इ, what cuts or pounds; (नी), f. a bawd, a procuress.
14999: कुट्टिम, अस्, आ, अम्, plastered with small stones, decorated with mosaic; (अस्, अम्), m. n. an inlaid or paved floor, pavement, ground paved with mosaic or small stones, ground smoothed and plastered; ground prepared for the site of a mansion; a jewel mine; a hut, a cottage; the pomegranate.
15000: कुट्टमित कुट्टमित, अम्, n. one of the ten blandishments of women, affected repulse of a lover's caresses; [cf. कुट्टुमित।]
15001: कुट्टार कुट्टार, अस्, m. a mountain; (अम्), n. sexual intercourse; pleasure; a woollen cloth or blanket; exclusion; oneness; [cf. कुटीर and कुट्-टीर।]
15002: कुट्टिहारिका कुट्टिहारिका, f. a female servant, a slave; [cf. कुट-हारिका।]
15003: कुट्टीर कुट्टीर, अस्, m. a mountain; [cf. कुटीर and कुट्टार।]
15004: कुट्टीरक कुट्टीरक, अम्, n. (?) a small house, a hut; (a wrong reading for कुटीरक?).
15005: कुट्टुमित कुट्टुमित, अम्, n. = कुट्टमित above.
15006: कुट्मल कुट्मल, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. कुट्), opening or expanding as the blossom of a flower, blossoming; (अस्, अम्), m. n. an opening bud; (अम्), n. one of the twenty-one hells in which sinners are punished (where they are bound with ropes).
15008: कुठ कुठ, अस्, m. a tree; (generally written कुट।)
15009: कुठर कुठर, अस्, m. the post round which the string of the churning-stick winds; [cf. कुटर।]
15010: कुठाकु कुठाकु, उस्, m. a bird, the wood-pecker, Picus Bengalensis, commonly Kāṭhṭhākro.
15011: कुठाटङ्क कुठाटङ्क, अस्, आ, m. f. an axe.
15012: कुठार कुठार, अस्, ई, m. f. an axe; a sort of hoe or spade; (अस्), m. a tree; N. of a man.
15013: कुठारक, अस्, m. an axe; (इका), f. a small axe or adze; also a similarly shaped instrument used in surgery for scarification; N. of a woman.
15015: कुठारु कुठारु, उस्, m. an ape, a monkey; a tree; an armourer.
15016: कुठि कुठि, इस्, m. a tree; a mountain; [cf. कुटि।]
15017: कुठिक कुठिक, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = कुष्ठ, मृत्फली, a kind of Costus, commonly called Kuṭh.
15018: कुठुमि कुठुमि, इस्, m., N. of a preceptor, author of a law-book; [cf. कुथुमि।]
15019: कुठेर कुठेर, अस्, m. fire; a kind of Basi-licum. —कुठेर-ज, अस्, m. a white kind of Basi-licum, Ocimum Gratissimum.
15020: कुठेरक, अस्, m. a kind of Basilicum, Ocimum Sanctum; a white sort of the same, Ocimum Gra-tissimum.
15021: कुठेरु कुठेरु, उस्, m. the wind produced by a fan or chowrie.
15022: कुड् कुड्, cl. 6. P. कुडति, चुकोड, कुडितुम्, to play or act as a child, to trifle; to eat; to heap; to plunge under water, be immersed, dive (?).
15023: कुडङ्ग कुडङ्ग, अस्, m. a bower, an arbour; [cf. कुटङ्क, कुटुङ्गक, कुण्डङ्ग।]
15024: कुडप कुडप, अस्, अम्, m. n. = कुडव below.
15025: कुडव कुडव, अस्, m. a measure of grain, wood, iron, &c., the fourth part of a Prastha, de-scribed by some as a vessel four fingers wide and as many deep and containing twelve Prakṛtis or hand-fuls; it is also said to contain 13(1/2) cubic Angulas; or to be a finger and a half deep, and three fingers each in length and breadth; in medicine it is equal to two Prakṛtis or thirty-two Tolakas.
15026: कुडि कुडि, इस्, m. the body; [cf. कुटि।]
15027: कुडिका कुडिका, f. an earthen or wooden water-pot used by ascetics; [cf. कुट।]
15028: कुडिश कुडिश, अस्, m. a kind of fish, com-commonly Kūrchi, Cyprinus Curchius.
15029: कुडी कुडी, f. a small house, a hut; (a wrong reading for कुटी?).
15030: कुडुप कुडुप, अस्, m. the clasp or fastening of a necklace or bracelet.
15031: कुड्मल कुड्मल, अस्, आ, अम्, opening or ex-panding as the blossom of a flower, blossoming; (अस्), m. an opening bud; (अम्), n. a particular hell; some-times also spelt कुद्मल; [cf. कुट्मल।] —कुड्-मल-दन्ती, f., N. of a metre, = अनुकूला; also spelt कुद्मल-दन्ती।
15032: कुड्मलित, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with opening buds; budded, blossomed; cheerful, smiling (as the countenance).
15033: कुड्य कुड्य, अम्, आ, n. f. a wall; plaster-ing (a wall); eagerness, curiosity. —कुड्य-च्छेदिन्, ई, m. a housebreaker, a thief. —कुड्य-च्छेद्य, अम्, n. an opening, a hole in a wall, a breach. —कुड्य-मत्सी, f. or कुड्य-मत्स्य, अस्, m. a house-lizard.
15035: कुण् कुण्, cl. 6. P. कुणति, -णितुम्, to sound; to cherish, to support or aid with gifts &c.; to be in pain (?); cl. 10. P. कुणयति, -यितुम्, to counsel or advise; to converse with, to speak to, address; to salute; to invite; [cf. Lat. cano, sono; Lith. zwanu.]
15036: कुण कुण, अस्, m. in composition with अश्वत्थ and other trees or flowers; the time when a plant bears fruit, e. g. पीलु-कुण, q. v.
15037: कुणक कुणक, अस्, m. a young animal just born.
15038: कुणञ्जर कुणञ्जर, अस्, m. or कुणञ्जा, f. or कृणञ्ज, अस्, m. a species of Chenopodium; (com-monly Vanavetuā.)
15039: कुणप कुणप, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. क्वण्), a dead body, a corpse; a carcase; said contemptuously of living persons; (अस्), m. a spear; N. of a people; a stench, a foul smell; (ई), f. a small bird, a kind of Maina or Salik [cf. विट्-सारिका]; (अस्, ई, अम्), mouldering, smelling like a dead body, foul smelling; stinking. —कुणप-गन्ध, अस्, m. the smell of a dead body.
15040: कुणरबाडव कुणर-बाडव, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian.
15041: कुणारु कुणारु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having a distorted arm (?); (Sāy. fr. rt. कुण्) crying out.
15042: कुणाल कुणाल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. क्वण्), a kind of bird; N. of a son of Aśoka; N. of a country.
15043: कुणि कुणि, इस्, इस्, इ, a cripple with a crooked or withered arm, or without a hand or finger; (इस्), m. a whitlow; the tree Cedrela Toona (तुन्न); N. of a prince, a son of Jaya and father of Yugan-dhara; N. of a Muni; N. of the author of a Dharma-śāstra. —कुणि-बाहु, उस्, m., N. of a Muni.
15044: कुणिताहि कुणिताहि, इस्, m., N. of the author of a Dharma-śāstra.
15045: कुणिन् कुणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, only in कुणी कण-भः, a kind of bug; [cf. उत्कुण, मत्कुण।]
15046: कुणिन्द कुणिन्द, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कुण्), sound, sounding.
15048: कुण्टक कुण्टक, अस्, ई, अम्, fat, corpulent.
15049: कुण्ठ् कुण्ठ्, cl. 1. P. कुण्ठति, -ठितुम्, to be lame or mutilated, to be blunted or dulled; to be lazy or stupid; cl. 10. P. कुण्ठयति, यितुम्, to cover, conceal.
15050: कुण्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, blunt, dull; stupid; weak; indolent, lazy, slow; foolish; [cf. अ-कुण्ठ।] —कुण्-ठ-ता, f. bluntness, dulness, indolence.
15051: कुण्ठक, अस्, आ, अम्, stupid, ignorant, a fool; (अस्), m., N. of a pupil of Luṇṭaka; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
15052: कुण्ठित, अस्, आ, अम्, blunted, dulled; mutilated, stupid; grasped, held, encircled. —कुण्ठिताश्रि (°त-अश्°), इस्, इस्, इ, having its edge or corners blunted.
15053: कुण्ड् कुण्ड्, cl. 1. P. कुण्डति, to mutilate; cl. 1. A. कुण्डते, -डितुम्, to burn; cl. 10. P. कुण्डयति, -यितुम्, to protect.
15054: कुण्ड कुण्ड, अस्, ई, अम्, m. f. n. (said to be fr. rt. कुण्), a bowl-shaped vessel, a basin, bowl, pitcher, jar, pot, water-pot; (अम्), n. a particular measure; a clump, e. g. दर्भ-कुण्डम्, a clump of Darbha grass; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a round hole in the ground, a hole in the ground for receiving and preserving water; a hole in general (e. g. in comp. अग्नि-कुण्ड, a hole in the ground for receiving and preserving consecrated fire); a pit, a vat; a pool, a well, a spring or basin of water, especially consecrated to some holy purpose or person; (अस्), m. a son born in adultery, an adulterine, the son of a woman by another man than her husband, while the husband is alive; N. of a Nāga; a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; an epithet of Śiva; (आ), f. an epithet of Durgā. —कुण्ड-कीट, अस्, m. the son of a woman of the Brāhmanical tribe born in adultery with a man of an inferior caste; a keeper of concubines, a man who has female slaves; a follower of the Cārvāka doctrine or the tenets of those who deny the authority of the Vedas. —कुण्ड-कील, अस्, m. a low, a vile man; see नागर. —कुण्ड-कौ-मुदी or कुण्ड-मण्डप-कौमुदी, f. title of a work by Viśvanātha. —कुण्ड-गोल, अस्, m. and कुण्ड-गोलक, अम्, n. sour rice, gruel; see काञ्जिक। —कुण्ड-ज, अस्, m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —कुण्ड-जठर, अस्, m., N. of an old sage; [cf. कुण्डोदर।] —कुण्ड-धार, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; also of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —कुण्ड-पायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, drinking out of pitchers; कुण्ड-पायिनाम् अयनम्, a particular religious ceremony [cf. कौण्डपायिन]. —कुण्ड-पाय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (scil. क्रतु, &c.), a particular ceremony or sacrifice at which ewers or pitchers are used for drinking; (अस्), m., N. of a man (?). —कुण्ड-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town. —कुण्ड-भेदिन्, ई, m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —कुण्ड-मण्डप-सिद्धि, इस्, f., N. of a work by Viṭṭhaladīkṣita. —कुण्ड-रत्ना-कर, अस्, m., N. of a work by Viśvanātha. —कुण्ड-शायिन्, ई, m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —कुण्-डाग्नि (°ड-अग्°), इस् or इ (?), m. or n. 15075: कुतस् कुतस्, ind. (fr. 1. कु), from where? whence? from whence? whereto? where? in which direction? wherefore? why? from what cause or motive? because; how? in what manner? in which way? how much less? much less. कुतस् is used sometimes for the abl. case of 2. क = कस्मात् (e. g. कुतः कालात्, since what time?). In अ-कुतस्, which occurs at the beginning of some compounds, कुतस् has an indefinite sense (e. g. अकुतो-मृत्यु, not fearing death from any quarter; cf. अकुतो-भय); कुतस् is also indefinite when connected with the particles अपि, चिद्, and चन (e. g. कुतो ऽपि, from any quarter, from any cause; कुतश्चिद्, from any one, from anywhere; अकुतश्चिद्-भय, not fearing danger from any quarter, not presenting danger on any side; कुतश् चन, (in Ved.) from no side, to no side; यतः कुतश्चिद्, from any person soever). —कुतस्-तराम्, ind. how? in what manner? —कुतो-नि-मित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having what cause or reason? —कुतो-मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, having what origin?

15285: कुरु कुरु, अवस्, m. pl. (said to be fr. 1. कृ), N. of a people of India and their country, situated near the country of the Pañcālas (hence often con-nected with Pañcāla or Pāñcāla; see कुरु-पञ्चाल below); the Kurus derive their origin from Kuru (son of Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī, daughter of the Sun), who is the ancestor of both Pāṇḍu and Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, though the patronymic derived from his name is usually applied only to the sons of the latter, the sons and descendants of the former being called Pāṇḍavas; another Kuru is the son of Agnīdhra and grandson of Priya-vrata. The उत्तर-कुरवः or उत्तराः कुर-वः are the northern Kurus, the most northerly of the four Mahā-dvīpas or principal divisions of the known world (distinguished Mahā-bh. I. 4346. from the दक्-षिणाः कुरवः or southern Kurus), by other sys-tems regarded as one of nine divisions or Varṣas of the same; it was probably a country beyond the most northern range of the Himālaya, often described as a country of everlasting happiness, and considered by some to be the ancient home of the Āryan race. कुरू, ऊस्, f. a princess of the Kuru race. According to native lexicographers the word कुरु has also the following meanings; a priest; boiled rice; the plant Solanum Jacquini, = कण्टकारिक; [cf. कौरव, कौरवक, कौरव्य।] —कुरु-कत, आस्, m. pl. the Kurus and Katas. —कुरु-कन्दक, अम्, n. horse-radish, Raphanus Sativus (= मूलक). —कुरु-कुरुक्षेत्र, अम्, n. the country of the Kurus and Kurukṣetra. —कुरु-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. the field of the Kurus, N. of a region or extensive plain near Delhi, the scene of the great battles between the Kurus and Pāṇḍus; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of this country, renowned for their bravery. —कुरु-क्षेत्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, with योग, a solar day, in the course of which three lunar days, three asterisms and three yogas occur. —कुरु-चिल्ल, अस्, m. a crab; [cf. कुरचिल्ल।] —कुरु-जाङ्गल, अम्, n., N. of a country; (आस्), m. pl., N. of the people inhabiting it. —कुरु-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —कुरु-नदिका, f. according to native authorities, = कु-न-दिका. —कुरु-नन्दन, अस्, m. a descendant of Kuru as Arjuna, Yudhiṣṭhira, &c. —कुरु-पञ्चाल, आस्, m. pl. the Kurus and Pañcālas. —कुरुपञ्चाल-त्रा, ind., Ved. as among the Kurus and Pañcālas. —कुरु-पथ, अस्, m., N. of a man (?); [cf. कौरुपथि।] —कुरु-पुङ्गव, अस्, m. a Kuru chief. —कुरु-राज्, ट्, m. an epithet of Duryodhana. —कुरु-राज, अस्, m. an epithet of Yudhiṣṭhira. —कुरु-राज्य, अम्, n. the Kuru realm. —कुरु-वत्स, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —कुरु-वर्णक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; or perhaps (अस्, आ, अम्), be-longing to the race of the Kurus. —कुरु-वश, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —कुरु-वाजपेय, अस्, m. a particular kind of Vājapeya. —कुरु-विस्त, अस्, m. a Pala of gold, a weight of gold equal to about 700 troy grains. —कुरु-वृद्ध, अस्, m. an epithet of Bhīṣma. —कुरु-श्रवण, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —कुरु-श्रेष्ठ or कुरु-सत्तम, अस्, m. an epi-thet of Arjuna. —कुरु-हार, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), N. of an Agra-hāra.

15592: कृ 1. कृ। The conjugational tenses are formed in the Veda according to four different methods, as follows: I) According to the rule for cl. 2, Pres. 2nd sing. P. कर्षि, du. कृथस्, pl. कृथ; A. कृषे; Impf. 2nd sing. P. अकर्, 3rd अकर् and अकत्; 3rd du. अकर्ताम्; pl. अकर्म, अकर्त, अक्रन्; A. अक्रि, अकृथास्, अकृत, अक्राताम्, अक्रत; Impv. P. कृधि, कृतम्, कृत; A. कृष्व, कृध्वम्: Leṭ, 2nd and 3rd sing. कर्, pl. कर्म, कर्त and कर्तन, क्रन्; A. 3rd sing. कृत; 3rd pl. क्रन्त: Pot. क्रियाम; Part. nom. pl. m. क्रन्तस्; A. क्राण। II) According to the rule for cl. 1. Pres. P. करसि, करति, करथस्, कर-तस्, करन्ति; A. करसे, करते, करामहे; Impf. अकरम्, अकरस्, अकरत्; Impf. कर, करतम्, करताम्: Leṭ, करम्, कराणि, करस्, करत्, कराम, करन्; A. करामहै; Part. करन्ती। III) According to the rule for cl. 5, Pres. P. कृणोमि, &c.; A. कृण्वे, du. कृण्वैते; Impf. P. अकृणवम्, &c., 2nd pl. अकृणुत and अकृणो-तन; A. 3rd sing. अकृणुत; Impv. P. कृणु or कृणुहि or कृणुतात्, कृणोतु; कृणुतम्, कृणुताम्; कृणुत or कृणोत or कृणोतन; कृण्वन्तु; A. कृणुष्व, कृणुताम्, कृण्वाथाम्, कृणुध्वम्; Leṭ, कृणवस्, कृणवत् and कृण-वात्, कृणवाव, कृणवाम, कृणवाथ, कृणव-थ, कृणवन्; A. कृणवै, कृणवसे, कृण-वते, कृणवावहै, कृणवामहै, 3rd pl. कृण-वन्त or कृणवन्ते or कृण्वत: Pot. A. कृण्वीत; Part. P. कृण्वत्, A. कृण्वान। IV) According to the rule for cl. 8, (this is the usual formation in the Brāhmaṇas, Sūtras, and in classical Sanskrit), Pres. P. करोमि (ep. कुर्मि), करोषि, &c., कुर्मस्; A. कुर्वे; Impf. P. अकरवम्; A. 3rd sing. अकुरुत; Impv. P. कुरु, करोतु (in the earlier language for 2nd and 3rd sing. कुरुतात्), कुरुत or कुरुतन; A. कुरुष्व, कुरुध्वम्, कुर्वताम्: Leṭ, P. करवाणि, करवस्, करवात्, &c.; A. करवै, कुरुथास्, करवावहै (ep. करवावहे), कर-वैथे, करवैते, करवामहै (ep. करवा-महे); Pot. P. कुर्याम्, A. कुर्वीय; Part. P. कुर्वत्, A. कुर्वाण: Perf. P. चकार, चकर्थ, &c.; A. चक्रे, &c.; Part. P. चकृवस् (Acc. sing. Ved. चक्रुषम्); A. चक्राण; 2nd Fut. करिष्यति; Leṭ, 2nd sing. करिष्यास्; 1st Fut. कर्ता; Prec. क्रियासम्; Aor. P., Ved. चकरम्, अचक्रिरन्, अचक्रत्; A. कृषे; Class. अकार्षीत् (poet. अका-रषीत्); Pass. Aor. reflex. अकारि and अकृत; Inf. कर्तुम्; Ved. कर्तवे, कर्तवै, कर्तोस्; Ind. Part. कृत्वा, Ved. कृत्वी and कृत्वाय; to do, make, perform, accomplish, cause, effect, prepare, undertake; to do anything for the advantage or injury of another (with gen. or loc. of the person); to execute, carry out (as an order or command); to manufacture, prepare, work at, elaborate, build; to form, construct one thing out of another (with abl. or inst. of the thing); to compose, describe; to cultivate; to make a sound, utter, pronounce (often in comp. with the sounds फट्, फुट्, भाण्, वषट्, स्वधा, स्वाहा, हिम्); to employ, use; to make use of (with inst.); to accomplish any period, bring to completion, spend (e. g. वर्षाणि दश चक्रुः, they spent ten years; क्षणं कुरु, wait a mo-ment); to place, put, lay, bring, lead, to take hold of (with acc. or loc. or inst., e. g. अर्धं कृ, to win over to one's own side or party; हस्ते or पाणौ कृ, to take by the hand, to marry; हृदयेन कृ, to place in one's heart, love); to direct the thoughts, mind &c. (मनः or मतिम् or बुद्धिम् or भा-वम् &c.) towards any object, turn the attention to, resolve upon, determine on (with loc., dat., or inf. of the object, e. g. मा शोके मनः कृथाः, do not turn your mind to grief; गमनाय मतिं चक्रे, he resolved upon going; अलाबुं स्रष्टुं चक्रे, he resolved to create a gourd); to consider, turn in the mind, think; to make, to render (with two acc., e. g. आदित्यं काष्ठाम् अकुर्वत, they made the sun their goal); to procure for another, bestow, grant; A. to procure for one's self, appropriate, assume; to give aid, help any one to perform an action; to make liable; to injure, violate (e. g. कन्यां कृ, to violate a maiden); to appoint, institute; to give an order, commission; to cause to get rid of, free from (with abl.); to begin (e. g. चक्रे शोभयितुम् पुरीम्, he began to adorn the city); to proceed with, put in practice; to worship, sacrifice; (with numeral adverbs ending in धा) to divide, separate, or break up into parts, e. g. द्विधा कृ, to divide into two parts; सहस्रधा कृ, to break into a thousand pieces; (with adverbs ending in वत्) to make like or similar, to consider equivalent, e. g. राज्यं तृणवत् कृत्वा, valuing the kingdom like a straw; (with adverbs ending in सात्) to reduce anything to, cause to become, make subject, e. g. भस्मसात् कृ, to reduce to ashes; आत्मसात् कृ, to subject to one's self. The above senses of कृ may be variously modified or almost infinitely extended according to the noun with which this root is connected, as in the following exam-ples: सख्यं कृ, to contract friendship with; पूजां कृ, to honour; राज्यं कृ, to reign; स्नेहं कृ, to show affection; आज्ञां or निदेशं or शासनं or कामं or याचनां or वचः or वचनं or वाक्यं कृ, to perform any one's command or wish or request &c.; धर्मं कृ, to do one's duty; नखानि कृ, to clean one's nails; उदकं or सलिलं कृ, to offer a libation to the dead, to perform ablutions &c.; अस्त्राणि कृ, to practice the use of weapons; दर्दुरं कृ, to play on the flute; दण्डं कृ, to inflict punishment &c.; स्वरं कृ, to utter a sound; शब्दं कृ, to make a noise; कालं कृ, to bring one's time to an end, i. e. to die; चिरं कृ, to be long in doing any-thing, to delay; मनसि कृ, to take to heart, to mind, to determine, resolve upon; मनसा कृ, to place in one's mind, think of, meditate; हृदि कृ, to place in the heart, remember; वशे कृ, to place in subjection, become master of; शिरसा कृ, to place on the head; मूर्ध्ना कृ, to place on one's head, to obey, to honour: Caus. कारयति, -ते, -यि-तुम्, to cause to act or do, to cause another to perform, to have anything made or done by another (with acc. or double acc., e. g. सभां कारितवान्, he caused an assembly to be made; राज-दर्शनम् मां कारय, cause me to have an audience of the king; बानिज्यं कारयेद् वैश्यम्, he ought to cause the Vaiśya to engage in trade; or with acc. and inst., e. g. न शक्ष्यामि किञ्चित् कारयितुं त्वया, I shall not be able to have anything done by thee); to cause to manufacture or form or cultivate; to cause to place or put, to have anything placed, put upon, &c. (e. g. तं चित्र-पटं वास-गृहे भित्ताव् अकारयत्, he had the picture placed on the wall in his house). Sometimes the Caus. of कृ is used for the simple verb or without a causal significa-tion (e. g. पदं कारयति, he pronounces a word &c.; मिथ्या कारयति, he pronounces wrongly; कैकेयीम् अनु राजानं कारय, treat or deal with Kaikeyī as the king does): Desid. चिकीर्षति, -ते, to wish to make or do; to intend to do, to design, intend, begin, strive after; to wish to sacrifice or worship: Intens. चर्कर्ति, चरिकर्ति, चरीकर्ति, चर्करीति, चरिकरीति, चरीकरीति, चेक्रीयते, Ved. 3rd pl. करिक्रति, to do repeatedly; [cf. Hib. caraim, ‘I perform, execute;’ ceard, ‘an art, trade, business, function;’ sucridh, ‘easy;’ Cambro-Brit. creu, ‘to form;’ Island. gerdh, ‘action;’ Old Germ. kara-wan, ‘to prepare;’ Mod. Germ. gar, ‘prepared (as food);’ Lat. creo, cœremonia, ars (for cars); Gr. κραίνω, κρόνος.]
15593: 1. कृत्, त्, त्, त्, making, doing, performing, accom-plishing, effecting, manufacturing, acting; one who accomplishes or performs anything, an author; often occurring at the end of compounds, see सु-कृत्, कर्म-कृत्, पाप-कृत्, &c.; (त्), m. an affix used to form nouns from roots; a noun formed with this affix. —कृद्-अन्त, अस्, m. a word ending with a Kṛt affix (such a word would be called by Pāṇini simply कृत्). —कृल्-लोप, अस्, m. the rejection of a Kṛt affix.
15594: कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done, made, accomplished, per-formed; prepared, made ready; obtained, gained, acquired; placed at hand; well done, proper, good. The preceding senses are mostly found in the Veda; the numerous other senses found in classical writers may be inferred from the meanings of the rt. कृ above. The neuter of कृत is used with सह or with the inst. alone in the sense of ‘done with,’ ‘away with,’ ‘enough of,’ ‘no need of,’ &c. (e. g. कृतं सन्देहेन, away with doubt; कृतम् परिहासेन, enough of joking). कृत is often found at the end of a compound, e. g. पूर्व-कृत, done formerly; जन्मान्तर-कृत, done in a former state of existence; (अस्), m., N. of one of the Viśva-devās; of a son of Vasu-deva; of a son of Sannati and pupil of Hiraṇya-nābha; of a son of Kṛta-ratha and father of Vibudha; of a son of Jaya and father of Haryavana; of a son of Cyavana and father of Upari-cara; (अम्), n. deed, work, action; service done, kind action, benefit; consequence, result; aim, object, design; stake at a game; prize or booty gained in battle; N. of the die or of the side of a die marked with four points; (according to some) the collective name of the four dice in opposition to the fifth die, called कलि; N. of the first of the four ages of the world (also called सत्य or ‘the golden age’) comprehending together with the morning and even-ing dawn 4,800 years of men, according to the Mahā-bhārata; but according to the Purāṇas 4,800 years of the gods, or 1,728000 years of men. —कृत-कपट, अस्, आ, अम्, deceiving, beguiling, fraudulent. —कृत-कर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has performed what was to be done, who has done his duty; 15595: कृतक, अस्, आ, अम्, artificial, factitious, done arti-ficially, made, prepared, not produced spontaneously; not natural, adopted (as a son); assumed, simulated, false; (अम्), ind. in a simulated manner; (अस्), m., N. of a son of Vasu-deva, also of a son of Cyavana.
15596: कृतय, nom. P. कृतयति, -यितुम्, to take the die called Kṛta.

15599: कृतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, expert; clever, skilful, knowing, wise, learned; good, virtuous; pure, pious; following, obeying, doing what is enjoined; one who has at-tained an object or accomplished a purpose, satisfied; (ई), m., N. of a son of Cyavana and father of Upari-cara; N. of a son of Sannatimat.

15601: कृतेयुक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Raudrāśva.
15602: कृत्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, working well, able to work, powerful; skilful, clever, an artificer or mechanic, an artist.
15603: कृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be done or performed; practicable, feasible; right, proper to be done; one who may be seduced from allegiance or alliance, one who may be bribed or hired as an assassin, treacherous; (अस्), m., scil. प्रत्यय, the class of affixes forming the fut. pass. part. &c. (as तव्य, अनीय, य, एलिम, &c.); a kind of evil spirit or ghost, either with or without the addition of यक्ष, मानुष, असुर, &c.; (आ), f. action, act, deed; magic; a female deity to whom sacrifices are offered for destructive and magical purposes; N. of a river; (अम्), n. what ought to be done; duty, office; purpose, end, object; what is proper or fit; motive, cause. —कृत्य-कल्प-तरु, उस्, m. title of a work on jurisprudence. —कृत्य-कल्प-लता, f., N. of a work by Vācaspati-miśra. —कृत्य-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m. title of a work by Śivarāma. —कृत्य-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, who knows what is to be done, learned, wise. —कृत्य-तत्त्व, अम्, n. ‘the true nature of duty or obligation,’ title of a work. —कृत्य-ता, f. seduction from allegiance or alliance. —कृत्य-रत्नाकर, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. In the earlier language कृत्वस् is used as a separate word, but native grammarians regard it only as an affix, and it is so used in classical Sanskrit; it was perhaps originally an acc. plur. fr. a noun कृतु, formed by the affix तु fr. the root 1. कृ; [cf. also कृत् in सकृत्।]
15608: कृत्वा, ind. having made or done.
15609: कृत्वी, f., N. of a daughter of Śuka, wife of Aṇuha (Nīpa) and mother of Brahma-datta.
15610: कृत्व्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. one who is able to perform anything, strong, efficacious; having accom-plished many deeds, exerting one's power.
15611: क्रियमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being done, made, &c.
15612: कृ 2. कृ, cl. 3. P., Ved. चकर्ति, अकारीत्, Intens. चर्कर्ति, to make mention of, to praise, to speak highly of (with gen.); [cf. कारु, कीरि, कीर्ति।]
15613: कृ 3. कृ, to injure &c. See 2. कॄ।

15615: कृक कृक, अस्, m. the throat, the larynx.

15617: कृकणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or relating to a partridge.
15618: कृकणेयु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Raudrāśva.
15619: कृकदाशु कृकदाशु, उस् or ऊस्, m., Ved. one who hurts or injures.

15621: कृकला कृकला, f. long pepper; [cf. पिप्पली।]

15623: कृकवाकु कृकवाकु, उस्, m. a cock, a gallina-ceous fowl; a peacock; a lizard, a chameleon; [with the first part of this word cf. Hib. cearc, ‘a hen.’] —कृ-कवाकु-ध्वज, अस्, m. an epithet of Kārttikeya.
15624: कृकषा कृकषा, f. a kind of bird; [cf. कङ्-कणहारिका।]
15625: कृकाट कृकाट, अम्, n., Ved. the joint of the neck.
15626: कृकाटक, अम्, n. the neck; a part of a column; (इका), f. the back of the neck; the raised and straight part of the neck.
15627: कृकालिका कृकालिका, f. a kind of bird.
15628: कृकिन् कृकिन्, ई, m., N. of a mythical king.
15629: कृकुलास कृकुलास, अस्, m. a lizard, a cha-meleon; [cf. कृकलाश।]
15630: कृच्छ्र कृच्छ्र, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps fr. rt. कृष् and connected with कष्ट), causing trouble or pain, painful, attended with pain or labour; being in a difficult or painful situation; bad, miserable, evil, wicked, sinful; 15632: कृच्छ्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, encompassed with difficulties, being in trouble, feeling pain; angry.

15635: कृणु कृणु, उस्, m. a painter.

P. कृन्तति, चकर्त, कर्त्स्यति and कर्तिष्यति, अकर्तीत्, कर्तितुम्, to cut, cut in pieces, cut off, divide; to tear asunder, destroy: Caus. कर्तयति, to cut, divide, &c.: Desid. चिकर्तिषति and चिकृत्सति: Intens. चरीकृत्यते, चरीकर्त्ति; [cf. Lith. kertu, inf. kirsti, ‘to cut;’ Gr. κείρω, κάρσις Slav. korjû, ‘to split;’ Lat. curtus, culter; Hib. ceartaighim, ‘I prune, trim, cut;’ cuirc, ‘a knife.’]
15637: कृत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, cut, divided; desired, sought, wished for.

15641: कृन्तन, अम्, n. cutting, cutting off, dividing.

15643: कृतद्-वसु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. distributing goods (?).
15645: कृत्स, अम्, n. water; entire, whole; [cf. the next.]
15646: कृत्स्न, अस्, आ, अम् (rarely used in pl.), all, whole, entire; (अम्), n. water; the flank or hip; the belly. —कृत्स्न-ता, f. totality, completeness. —कृत्स्न-विद्, त्, त्, त्, omniscient, knowing all things. —कृत्स्न-शस्, ind. wholly, entirely, altogether. —कृत्स्न-हृदय, अम्, n. the whole heart. —कृत्स्नायत (°न-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. stretched out to its full length.
15647: कृत्स्नक, अस्, आ, अम्, all, every.

15654: कृप् 2. कृप् (connected with rt. क्रप्), cl. 1. A. कर्पते, to have pity or mercy on; cl. 10. P. कृपयति or कृपापयति, -यितुम्, to be weak; to pity; to mourn, grieve, lament; [cf. Gr. ἔλπω]
15655: कृप, अस्, m., N. of a man described in the Veda as a friend of Indra; (अस्), m. and (ई), f., N. of the son and daughter of the sage Śaradvat, (he performed severe penance and thereby alarmed the jealous Indra, who sent a nymph to tempt him, but without success; however, twin sons were born to the sage in a clump of grass (शर-स्तम्बे), who were found by king Śāntanu and out of pity (कृपा) taken home and reared as his own; the daughter, Kṛpī, married Droṇa, and had by him a son called Aśvatthāman; the son, Kṛpa, became one of the privy council at Hastināpur, and is sometimes called Gautama, some-times Śāradvata. 15658: कृपणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, miserable, one who is in misery.

(In the earlier legends he ap-pears as a great hero and teacher; in the more recent he is deified, and is often represented as a young and amorous shepherd with flowing hair and a flute in his hand. The following are a few particulars of his birth and history as related in the Purāṇas &c.: Vasu-deva, who was a descendant of Yadu and Yayāti, had two wives, Rohiṇī and Devakī. The latter had eight sons, of whom the eighth was Kṛṣṇa. Kaṃsa, king of Mathurā and cousin of Devakī, was informed by a prediction that one of these sons would kill him. He therefore kept Vasu-deva and his wife in confinement, and slew their first six children. The seventh was Bala-rāma, who was saved by being abstracted from the womb of Devakī and transferred to that of Rohiṇī. The eighth was Kṛṣṇa, who was born with black skin and a peculiar mark on his breast. His father Vasu-deva managed to escape from Mathurā with the child, and favoured by the gods found a herdsman named Nanda, whose wife Yaśodā had just been delivered of a son, which Vasu-deva conveyed to Devakī, after substituting his own in its place. Nanda with his wife Yaśodā took the infant Kṛṣṇa and settled first in Gokula or Vraja, and afterwards in Vṛndāvana, where Kṛṣṇa and Bala-rāma grew up together, roaming in the woods and joining in the sports of the herdsmen's sons. Kṛṣṇa as a youth contested the sovereignty of Indra, and was victorious over that god, who descended from heaven to praise Kṛṣṇa, and made him lord over the cattle. Kṛṣṇa is described as sporting constantly with the Gopīs or shepherdesses, of whom a thousand became his wives, though only eight are specified, Rādhā being the favourite. Kṛṣṇa built and fortified a city called Dvāraka in Gujarāt, and thither transported the inhabitants of Mathurā after killing Kaṃsa. Kṛṣṇa had various wives be-sides the Gopīs, and by Rukmiṇī had a son Pra-dyumna, who is usually identified with Kāma-deva; with Jainas, Kṛṣṇa is one of the nine black Vasu-devas; with Buddhists he is the chief of the black demons, who are the enemies of Buddha and the white demons); N. of a king of the Nāgas; N. of an Asura or demon; N. of Arjuna, the most renowned of the Pāṇḍu princes (so named apparently from his colour as a child, see Mahā-bh. (?) a comb. —केश-मार्जन, अम्, n. a comb; cleaning the hair. —केश-मुष्टि, इस्, m. a handful of hair; N. of two plants, (also विष-मुष्टि and महा-निम्ब।) —केश-रचना, f. arranging or dressing the hair. —केश-रञ्जन or केश-राज, अस्, m., N. of a vegetable, = भृङ्ग-राज. —केश-रुहा, f., N. of a plant, = भद्र-दन्तिका. —केश-रूपा, f., N. of a parasitical plant. —केश-लुञ्चक, अस्, आ, अम्, pulling the hair. —केश-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a fine head of hair; having long hair; having a mane. —केश-वपनीय, अस्, m., N. of a festival. —केश-वर्-धन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. causing the hair to grow. —केश-वर्धिनी, f., N. of a plant, a kind of Sida. —केश-वेश, अस्, m. a tress or fillet of hair. —केश-वेष्ट, अस्, m. the parting of the hair. —केश-हन्त्री, f., N. of a tree, = शमी. —केश-हस्त, अस्, m. much or ornamented hair, a tuft. —केशा-केशि, ind. hair to hair, head to head; pulling each other's hair. —केशाग्र (°श-अग्°), अम्, n. the top of a hair. —केशान्त (°श-अन्°), अस्, m. the tip or end of a hair; long hair hanging down, a lock of hair, a tuft; cutting off the hair finally, as a religious cere-mony performed upon Brāhmans at sixteen years of age, Kṣatriyas at twenty-two, and Vaiśyas at twenty-four. —केशान्तिक, अस्, आ, अम्, extending to the end of the hair as far as the forehead; relating to the ceremony of final tonsure. —केशारि (°श-अरि), इस्, m. the plant Mesua Ferrea. —केशारुहा (°श-आर्°), f., N. of a plant, = सह-देवी. —केशार्हा (°श-अर्°), f., N. of a plant, = महानीली. —केशावमर्षण (°श-अव्°), अम्, n. pulling the hair, especially amo-rously playing with it, rubbing it, &c. —केशोच्चय (°श-उच्°), अस्, m. much or handsome hair.
15784: केशक, अस्, आ, अम्, skilful in dressing hair, be-stowing care upon the hair.
15785: केशव, अस्, आ, अम्, having long or much or hand-some hair; (अस्), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa; N. of the author of a lexicon called Kalpa-dru; the author of the Dvaita-pariśiṣṭa; the father of Govinda and Rucikara; N. of the father of Brāhma and uncle of Maheśvara; N. of the son of Viśvadhara and brother of Karinātha; N. of the father of Vopadeva; N. of a plant, = पुन्नाग. —केशव-जातक-पद्-धत्य्-उदाहरण, अम्, n. a commentary by Viś-vanātha on the work Jātaka-paddhati. —केशव-जी-नन्द-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of an author. —केशव-दास, अस्, m., N. of an author. —केशव-दैवज्ञ, अस्, m., N. of an astronomer. —केशव-भक्ति, इस्, f. devotion to Kṛṣṇa. —केशव-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of an author. —केशव-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a grammarian. —केशवायुध (°व-आय्°), अस्, m. the Mango tree; any of Kṛṣṇa's weapons. —केशवार्क (°व-अर्°), अस्, m., N. of the author of the poem Kṛṣṇa-krīḍita, a son of Jayāditya and grandson of Rāṇiga; N. of the author of a work called Jātaka-paddhati; N. of the author of a work called Vivāha-vṛndāvana —केशवालय (°व-आल्°) or केशवा-वाल (?) or केशवावास (°व-आव्°), अस्, m. the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa.
15786: केशि, इस्, m., N. of an Asura; [cf. केशिन्।]
15787: केशिक, अस्, ई, अम्, having fine or luxuriant hair, relating to the hair; (आ), f. the plant Asparagus Racemosus.
15788: केशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having fine or long hair, having a mane; epithet of Indra's and Agni's horses; epithet of Rudra; (ई), m. a lion; N. of a race; N. of an Asura slain by Kṛṣṇa; an epithet of Kṛṣṇa; N. of a son of Vasu-deva and Kauśalyā; (इनी), f. the plant Chrysopogon Aciculatus; another plant, Nar-dostachys Jaṭāmāṃsī; an epithet of the goddess Durgā; N. of an Apsaras; N. of a daughter of the king of Vidarbha, wife of Sagara and mother of Asamañja; N. of the wife of Ājamīḍha (Suhotra) and mother of Jahnu; N. of the wife of Viśravas and mother of Rāvaṇa and Kumbhakarṇa; N. of a Rākṣasī; N. of a servant of Damayantī. —केशि-निसूदन or केशि-मथन or केशि-सूदन, अस्, m. or केशि-हन्, आ, m. &c. epithet of Kṛṣṇa the slayer of the Asura Keśin.
15789: केश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in or on the hair; suit-able to the hair; (अस्), m., N. of a plant; (अम्), n. black Aloe wood.
15790: केशट केशट, अस्, m. a goat; a bug; a louse; N. of a tree, commonly Sonapat, = शोणक; the parching arrow of Kāma-deva, the god of love; a brother; an epithet of Viṣṇu.
15791: केशारुका केशारुका, f. = कशेरुका, the back-bone.
15792: केसर केसर or केशर, अस्, अम्, m. n. (the former form being more usual in Vedic and the latter in classical literature), the hair; the mane (of a horse or lion); the filament of a lotus or of any vegetable; a fibre (as of a Mango fruit); (अम्), n. the tail of the Bos Grunniens, used as a fan for driving away flies; (अस्), m., N. of several plants, Rottleria Tinctoria; Mimusops Elengi; Mesua Ferrea; (अम्), n. the flower of these plants; gold; sulphate of iron; N. of a metre consisting of four lines of eighteen syllables each; (अस्, आ, अम्), m. f. n. Asa Fœtida; [cf. Lat. cœsaries; Angl. Sax. haer; Eng. hair; Germ. Haar.] —केसर-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a Grāma. —केसर-प्राबन्धा, f., Ved., N. of a woman. —केसर-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a mane. —केसर-वर, अम्, n. saffron. —केसरा-चल (°र-अच्°), अस्, m. ‘the filament mountain,’ N. of the mountains situated round Meru, which is called ‘the seed-vessel of the earth.’ —केसराम्ल (°र-अम्°), अस्, m. the citron.
15793: केसरि, इस्, m., N. of the father of Hanumat.
15794: केसरिन् and केशरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having a mane; (ई), m. a lion; a horse; N. of several plants, Rottle-ria Tinctoria; Mesua Ferrea; a citron tree; a variety of Moringa with red flowers (= रक्त-शिग्रु); N. of a man; of a monkey, husband of the mother of Hanumat. —केसरि-सुत, अस्, m., N. of Hanumat.
15795: केह्लदेव केह्ल-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man.
15796: कै कै, cl. 1. P. कायति, चकौ, कास्यति, कातुम्, to sound.
15797: कैकय कैकय, अस्, m. the king of the Kekayas; (आस्), m. pl. the sons of this king; (ई), f. a daughter of this king.
15798: कैकेय, अस्, m. a descendant of Kekaya, who was prince of the Kekayas; a son of Śivi; Dṛṣṭaketu, king of the Kekayas and father of the five Kaikeyas; (आस्), m. pl. the Kekayas; (ई), f. a daughter of the prince of the Kekayas, one of the wives of Daśa-ratha, mother of Bharata; a shrew, a scold.
15799: कैङ्कर्य कैङ्कर्य, अम्, n. (fr. किङ्-कर), the office of a servant or slave; service, servitude.
15800: कैट कैट, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कीट), coming from an insect.
15801: कैटज कैटज, अस्, m. = कुटज, the plant Wrightia Antidysenterica.
15802: कैटभ कैटभ, अस्, m., N. of an Asura slain by Viṣṇu; title of a class of writings; (आ and ई), f. an epithet of Durgā. —कैटभ-जित्, त्, m. or कै-टभ-हन्, आ, m. or कैटभारि (°भ-अरि), इस्, m. or कैटभार्दन (°भ-अर्°), अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu.
15803: कैटर्य कैटर्य, अस्, m. a plant used in medicine, commonly Kayaphal; the Nimb tree; Mayana Vangueria Spinosa.
15804: कैडर्य, अस्, m., N. of two plants, = कट्फल and कटभी।
15805: कैतक कैतक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. केतक), coming from the plant Pandanus Odoratissimus; (अम्), n. the flower of the tree Pandanus Odoratissimus.
15806: कैतव कैतव, अस्, m. (fr. कितव), a patro-nymic of Ulūka; (अम्), n. the stake in a game; gambling; deceit, fraud, cheating, roguery; the lapis lazuli. —कैतव-प्रयोग, अस्, m. a trick, a device. —कैतव-वाद, अस्, m. falsehood, evasion.
15808: कैतवेय or कैतव्य, अस्, m. a patronymic of Ulūka.
15809: कैदार कैदार, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. केदार), being on or growing in a field or meadow, especially one under water; (अस्), m. rice, corn; (अम्), n. a multi-tude of fields.
15810: कैदारक or कैदारिक or कैदार्य, अम्, n. a multitude of fields.
15811: कैदार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to a field.
15812: कैन्नर कैन्नर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. किन् नर), coming from Kinnara.
15813: कैयट कैयट or कैय्यट, अस्, m., N. of a son of Jaiyaṭa, author of a commentary on Patañ-jali's Mahā-bhāṣya.
15814: कैरलेय कैरलेय, अस्, m. a king of the Keralas.
15815: कैरव कैरव, अस्, m. a gambler, a cheat, a rogue; an enemy; (अम्), n. the white esculent water-lily or lotus blossoming at night; (ई), f. moon-shine, moonlight; N. of a plant, = मेथिका. —कै-रव-बन्धु, उस्, m. an epithet of the moon.
15816: कैरविन्, ई, m. the moon; (इणी), f. a place or pond abounding in water-lilies, an assemblage of them. —कैरविणी-खण्ड, अम्, n. a multitude of spots filled with water-lilies.
15817: कैराटक कैराटक, अस्, m. a species of vegetable poison, one of the fixed kinds.
15818: कैरात कैरात, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. किरात), relating or belonging to the Kirātas; (अस्), m. a prince of the Kirātas; a strong man; N. of a serpent; (अम्), n. the plant Agathotes Chirayta; a kind of sandal-wood.
15819: कैरातक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the Kirāta people.
15820: कैरातिक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging to the Kirātas.
15821: कैराल कैराल, अम्, ई, n. f., N. of a plant, used as a remedy for worms; [cf. विडङ्ग।]
15822: कैरिशि कैरिशि, इस्, m. (fr. किरिशि), a patro-nymic of Sutvan.
15823: कैर्मेदुर कैर्मेदुर, अस्, अम्, m. n. (?), N. of a place; (अस्, ई, अम्), coming from that place.
15824: कैल कैल, अम्, n. sport, pleasure.
15825: कैलकिल कैलकिल, an epithet of Yavana.
15826: कैलावत कैलावत, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
15827: कैलास कैलास, अस्, m., N. of the mountain Kailāsa, the fabulous residence of Kuvera and paradise of Śiva; it is placed by the Hindūs in the Himālaya range, and is regarded as one of the loftiest peaks to the north of the Mānasa lake. —कैलास-नाथ, अस्, m. the sovereign of the Kailāsa mountain, i. e. the god Kuvera. —कैलास-निकेतन, अस्, m. an epithet of Kuvera of Śiva —कैलास-पण्डित, अस्, m., N. of a copyist. —कैलासौकस् (°स-ओक्°), आस्, m. an epi-thet of Kuvera.
15828: कैवर्त कैवर्त, अस्, m. [cf. केवर्त], a fisherman, born of a prostitute by a Kṣatriya or of an Āyogava female by a Niṣāda father; (ई), f. the wife of a fisherman; a kind of grass, Cyperus Ro-tundus; [cf. परिपेल।] —कैवर्त-मुस्त or कै-वर्त-मुस्तक, अम्, n. the grass Cyperus Rotundus.
15830: कैवर्तिका, f., N. of a plant, = सुरङ्गा, लता, वल्ली, दशरुहा, &c.
15831: कैवर्ति-मुस्तक or कैवर्ती-मुस्तक, अम्, n. a fragrant kind of grass, Cyperus Rotundus.
15832: कैवल कैवल, अम्, n. a kind of plant, used as a remedy for worms, = कैराल।
15833: कैवल्य कैवल्य, अम्, n. (fr. केवल), perfect isolation, abstraction, detachment from all other con-nections, detachment of the soul from matter or fur-ther transmigrations; becoming one with the Supreme; eternal happiness, emancipation, beatitude; exclusive-ness, soleness, individuality, totality; (अस्, आ, अम्), con-nected with this state of mind. —कैवल्य-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —कैवल्य-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary by Hemādri. —कैवल्याश्रम (°य-आश्°), अस्, m. a pupil of Govinda, author of a commentary on the poem Ānanda-laharī. —कैव-ल्येन्द्र (°य-इन्°), अस्, m., N. of the instructor of Rāyaṇendra. —कैवल्योपनिषद् (°य-उप्°), त्, f. title of an Upaniṣad.
15834: कैशव कैशव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. केशव), be-longing to Keśava, (Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.)
15835: कैशिक कैशिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. केश), hair-like, fine as a hair; (अस्), m. love, passion, lust; N. of a subdivision of the Yādavas, descended from Kaiśika, who was son of Vidarbha and brother of Kratha; (ई), f., scil. वृत्ति, one of the four varieties of dramatic style, the graceful style, suited especially to the passion of love; N. of a place or river; an epithet of Durgā; (अम्), n. a quantity of hair, a head of hair.
15836: कैशिन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. केशिन्), connected with Keśin Dārbhya.
15837: कैश्य, अम्, n. (fr. केश), the whole mass of hair, a head of hair, much or ornamented hair.
15838: कैशोर कैशोर, अम्, n. (fr. किशोर), youth, boyhood, from the age of ten to that of fifteen. —कैशोरक-वयस्, अस्, n. the age or life of a youth.
15839: कैष्किन्ध कैष्किन्ध, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from Kiṣkindhā.
15840: को को, a prefix in a number of words, as in को-जागर, को-मल, को-विद, &c., related to 1. कु; [cf. the prefixes क, कव, का, किम्, कु।]
15841: कोक कोक, अस्, m. (an onomatopoetic word), a wolf; a cuckoo; the ruddy goose; a frog; a small lizard or chameleon; a kind of noxious parasitical animal; the wild date tree; an epithet of Viṣṇu; N. of a man, a son of Śoṇa; N. of a river. —कोक-देव, अस्, m. a pigeon. —कोक-नख, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —कोक-बन्धु, उस्, m. the friend of the Cakravāka or ruddy goose, an epithet of the sun. —कोक-यातु, उस्, m., Ved. a demon or ghost in the shape of a cuckoo. —कोक-वाच, अस्, m. a sort of animal living in caves, a fox (?). —कोक-शास्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a very indecent treatise on the art of love, ascribed to a Paṇḍit named Koka. —कोकाग्र (°क-अग्°), अस्, m., N. of a plant, = समष्ठिल।
15842: कोकड कोकड, अस्, m. an animal of a brown colour, with a bushy tail, lurking in holes, perhaps a hare or fox.
15843: कोकनद कोकनद, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (अम्), n. the red lotus; the red water-lily. —कोकनद-च्छवि, इस्, m. the colour of the red lotus; (इस्, इस्, इ), of the colour of the red lotus.
15844: कोकरक कोकरक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
15845: कोकलिक कोकलिक, अस्, m., N. of a man.
15846: कोकली कोकली, f., N. of a woman.
15847: कोकामुख कोकामुख, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a Tīrtha.
15848: कोकाह कोकाह, अस्, m. a white horse; (per-haps a foreign word.)
15849: कोकिल कोकिल, अस्, m. (an onomatopoetic word; but by some said to be fr. rt. कुक्), the Kokila or Koïl, the black or Indian cuckoo, Cuculus Indicus; a kind of mouse; a kind of poisonous insect; a firebrand, a lighted coal; N. of a poet; N. of a Rājaputra; (आ), f. the female of a Kokila, (the Kokila or Koïl is frequently alluded to in Hindū poetry, and its musical cry is supposed to inspire pleasing and tender emotions.) —कोकिल-नयन, अस्, m. a plant bearing a dark black flower, Capparis Spinosa; it is also applied to Barleria Longifolia; [cf. कोकिलाक्ष।] —कोकिल-मैत्रावरुण, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the duties or office of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest at the Kaukilīṣṭi; (अम्), n. title of a treatise. —कोकिल-होत्र, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the duties or office of the Hotṛ priest at the Kaukilīṣṭi; (अम्), n. title of a treatise. —कोकिलाक्ष (°ल-अक्°), अस्, m. ‘having eyes like those of the Koïl,’ the plant Asteracantha Longifolia or Capparis Spinosa. —कोकिलाक्षक, अस्, m. the same plant. —कोकिला-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. title of a part of the Skanda-purāṇa. —कोकिलावास (°ल-आव्°), अस्, m. the Mango tree; [cf. आम्र।] —कोकि-लेक्षु (°ल-इक्°), उस्, m. the black variety of sugar-cane; [cf. कृष्णेक्षु।] —कोकिलेष्टा (°ल-इष्°), f., N. of a plant, = महा-जम्बू. —कोकिलोत्सव (°ल-उत्°), अस्, m. the Mango tree.
15850: कोकिलक, अस् or अम्, m. or n (?), N. of a metre of four lines, each containing seventeen syllables.
15852: कोक्क्वोक कोक्क्वोक, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Rati-rahasya.
15853: कोङ्क कोङ्क, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
15854: कोङ्कट कोङ्कट, अस्, m., N. of a scholiast on the Amara-koṣa; (a various reading has कोक्कट।)
15855: कोङ्कण कोङ्कण, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people on the western shore of the Dekhan; (अम्), n. a kind of weapon; (आ), f. a female of the Koṅkaṇa people. —कोङ्कणा-वती, f., N. of a river. —कोङ्-कणा-सुत, अस्, m. an epithet of Paraśu-rāma, the son of Koṅkaṇā.
15856: कोङ्कणक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people on the western shore of the Dekhan.
15857: कोङ्कार कोङ्-कार, अस्, m. the sound कोम्।
15858: कोच कोच, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. कुच्), drying, becoming dry; (अस्), m. drying up, desiccation, aridity; a man of mixed caste, the offspring of a fisherman by a female of the butcher tribe.
15859: कोजागर को-जागर, अस्, m. a kind of festi-val, the night of full moon in the month Āśvina (September — October), celebrated with various games; (according to some authorities from कः and जागर, ‘who is awake?’ the exclamation of Lakṣmī, who descending on this night, promised wealth to all that were awake; hence the night is spent in festivity and games of chance in honour of the goddess.)
15860: कोञ्ज कोञ्ज, अस्, m. = कौञ्च, N. of a mountain.
15861: कोट कोट, अस्, m. (rt. कुट्), a fort, a strong-hold; a shed, a hut [cf. कुट, कुटी]; crookedness, curvature; a beard. —कोट-चक्र, अम्, n. a sort of diagram.
15862: कोटक, अस्, ई, अम्, who or what curves or bends; (अस्), m. a builder of sheds or huts, a thatcher, a carpenter; a mixed caste, the son of a mason and of the daughter of a potter.
15863: कोटर, अस्, अम्, m. n. the hollow of a tree; a cave in general; (ई), f. a naked woman; an epithet of the goddess Durgā. —कोटरा-वण, अम्, n. a wood in which there are hollow trees.
15864: कोटवी, f. a naked woman; a form of the goddess Durgā (represented naked).
15865: कोटि, इस् or ई, f. the curved end of a bow or of claws, &c.; the end or top of anything; the edge or point of a sword; the horns of the moon; the highest point, eminence, excellence; the highest number in the older system of numbers, viz. a Krore or ten millions; the complement of an arc to 90°; the side of a right-angled triangle; N. of a plant, Piring or Asparac, Medicago Esculenta, = कोटि-वर्षा. —कोटि-कर्ण, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कोटि-जित्, त्, m. a conqueror of ten millions; an epithet of the poet Kālidāsa. —कोटि-ज्या, f. the cosine of an angle in a right-angled triangle. —कोटि-तीर्थ, अस्, m., N. of a Tīrtha. —कोटि-द्वय, अम्, n. ‘the two ends,’ i. e. two alternatives. —कोटि-पात्र, अम्, n. a rudder or large oar used as one. —कोटि-पाल, अस्, m. the guard of a stronghold? (a wrong reading for कोट्ट-पाल ?). —कोटि-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —कोटि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with a point. —कोटि-वर्ष, अम्, n., N. of a city, Vāṇapura or Devikote, on the Coromandel coast; (आ), f. a plant used medicinally, either Medicago Esculenta or Trigonella Corni-culata. —कोटि-वेधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, striking an edge or point, i. e. performing the most difficult things. —कोटि-शस्, ind. by tens of millions, in innumerable multitudes. —कोटि-श्री, f. an epithet of the goddess Durgā. —कोटी-वर्ष, अम्, n., N. of the town Vāṇapura on the Coromandel coast; (आ), f. the plant Medicago Esculenta or Trigonella Corniculata; [cf. कोटि-वर्ष।] —कोटीश्वर (°टि-ईश्°), अस्, m. the lord of ten millions, a millionaire.
15866: कोटिक, अस्, आ, अम्, forming the highest point, top or summit of anything, placed in the highest position, e. g. मानुष-कोटिका, a princess; (अस्), m., scil. मण्डूक, a frog; an insect, coccinella of various kinds; N. of the son of a prince. —कोटि-कास्य (°क-आस्°), अस्, m., N. of a son of king Suratha.
15867: कोटिर, अस्, m. the hair (collected on the forehead in the shape of a horn); an ichneumon, Viverra Ichneumon; an insect, coccinella of various kinds [cf. कोटिक]; an epithet of Indra.
15868: कोटिश, अस्, m. a harrow; N. of a Nāga.
15869: कोटीर, अस्, m. long entangled hair; a crest, a diadem.
15870: कोटीश, अस्, m. a harrow; [cf. कोटिश।]
15871: कोट्ट कोट्ट, अस्, अम्, m. n. a fort, a castle, a stronghold; [cf. कोट।]
15872: कोट्टवी कोट्टवी, f. (fr. को-आर्तव?), a naked woman; an epithet of Durgā; the mother of Vāṇa, an Asura; [cf. कोटवी, कौटवी, कोटरी।] —कोट्टवी-पुर, अम्, n., N. of the town Vāṇapura on the Coromandel coast; [cf. कोटि-वर्ष and कोटी-वर्ष।]
15873: कोट्टार कोट्टार, अस्, m. a fortified town, a stronghold; a pond; the stairs of a pond; a liber-tine; [cf. कोट्ट।]
15874: कोठ कोठ, अस्, m. (fr. कुष्ठ), a species of leprosy with large round spots; ringworm, im-petigo.
15875: कोठर कोठर, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = अङ्-कोट; [cf. कोटर।] —कोठर-पुष्पी, f. the plant Convolvulus Argenteus.
15876: कोण कोण, अस्, m. a corner, an angle (= अश्रि); an intermediate point of the compass; the quill or bow of a lute, a fiddle-stick, &c.; a sort of musical instrument, a stringed musical instrument; a drum-stick; the sharp edge of a sword; a stick, a staff, a club; a N. of Maṅgala, the planet Mars; a N. of the planet Saturn (in this sense fr. the Gr. κρόνος). —कोण-कुण, अस्, m. a bug; [cf. कोल-कुण, उत्कुण, मत्कुण।] —कोण-वादिन्, ई, m. an epithet of Śiva. —कोण-स्पृग्-वृत्त, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), a circle in contact with the angles of a figure; an exterior circle; one circumscribed. —को-णा-कोणि, ind. from angle to angle, from one corner to the other, cornerwise, diagonally; athwart.
15877: कोणि कोणि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a crooked arm; [cf. कुणि।]
15878: कोणेरभट्ट कोणेर-भट्ट, अस्, m. a N. of a son of Viṣṇu and father of Rudra-bhaṭṭa.
15879: कोण्डभट्ट कोण्ड-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian.
15880: कोथ कोथ, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. कुथ्), afflicted with pain, churned; (अस्), m. putrefaction, corrup-tion; a sore; gangrene; a disease of the eyes, inflammation and ulceration of the angles of the eyelids; churning.
15881: कोदण्ड को-दण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. a bow; (अस्), m. an eyebrow (shaped like a bow); a creeping plant; N. of a country.
15882: कोदण्डिन्, ई, इनी, इ, armed with a bow; an epithet of Śiva.
15883: कोदार कोदार, अस्, अम्, m. n. (?), a kind of grain.
15884: कोद्रव कोद्रव, अस्, m. a species of grain eaten by the poor, Paspalum Scrobiculatum.
15885: कोनालक कोनालक, अस्, आ, m. f. a kind of aquatic bird.
15886: कोनालि कोनालि, इस्, m. or f. (?), a kind of plant.
15887: कोन्तल कोन्तल, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; [cf. कुन्तल।]
15888: कोन्व कोन्व, अस्, m., N. of a mountain; [cf. कोल, कोल्लक, कोलगिरि, कोल्वगिरेय।]
15889: कोन्वशिर कोन्वशिर, आस्, m. pl., N. of a degraded warrior-tribe.
15890: कोप कोप, अस्, m. (fr. rt. कुप्), morbid irritation or disorder of the humours of the body; passion, wrath, anger, rage, (स-कोप, enraged; स-को-पम्, angrily.) —कोप-कारण, अम्, n. cause of anger.  — 1. कोप-क्रम, अस्, m. one who goes to anger, an angry or passionate man. —कोप-ज्वलित, अस्, आ, अम्, inflamed with wrath, enraged. —कोप-तस्, ind. through anger, angrily. —कोप-दीप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, incensed or inflamed with anger. —कोप-पद, अम्, n. appearance of anger, pretended wrath. —कोप-परीत, अस्, आ, अम्, affected by anger. —कोप-लता, f., N. of a plant, = कर्ण-स्फोटा. —कोप-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, angry; passionate; (ती), f., N. of a metre consisting of four lines of fourteen syllables each. —कोप-वश, अस्, m. subjection to anger. —कोप-वेग, अस्, m. violence, impetuosity of passion; N. of a Ṛṣi. —कोप-समन्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, affected by anger. —कोपाकुल (°प-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, furious, enraged. —कोपा-कोपि, ind. in mutual anger, in reciprocal wrath. —कोपाविष्ट (°प-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, affected with anger.
15891: कोपन, अस्, आ, अम्, inclined to passion, passionate, wrathful, angry; irritating, causing morbid irritation or disorder of the humours; (अस्), m., N. of an Asura; (अम्), n. irritating; becoming angry; (आ), f. a pas-sionate woman.
15892: कोपनक, अम्, n. a kind of perfume; [cf. चोरक।]
15893: कोपयिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, intending to exasperate, inclined to make angry.
15894: कोपित, अस्, आ, अम्, enraged, furious.
15895: कोपिन्, ई, इनी, इ, angry, passionate, wrathful; (at the end of a compound) irritating, stirring up; (ई), m. a bird called the water-pigeon (जल-पारावत).
15896: कोपक्रम 2. कोपक्रम (क-उप्°), अम्, n. Brahmā's creation; see 3. क। (For 1. कोप-क्रम see under कोप above.)
15897: कोपज्ञ कोपज्ञ (क-उप्°), अम्, n. Brahmā's creation.
15898: कोम कोम, अम्, n. = क्लोम, q. v.
15899: कोमल को-मल, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. को = कु and मल fr. rt. म्लै, ‘easily fading away?’), tender, soft (opposed to कर्कश); bland, sweet, low; pleasing, agreeable, beautiful; (आ), f., N. of a plant; (अम्), n. water. —कोमल-गीत or कोमल-गीतक, अम्, n. a pleasing song. —कोमल-ता, f. or कोमल-त्व, अम्, n. softness, tenderness, agreeableness. —कोमल-स्वभाव, अस्, आ, अम्, tender-hearted.
15900: कोमलक, अम्, n. the fibres of the stalk of a lotus.
15901: कोमासिका कोमासिका, f. a budding fruit; [cf. जालिका।]
15902: कोम्य कोम्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = काम्य, lovely (?).
15903: कोयष्टि को-यष्टि, इस्, or कोयष्टिक, अस्, m. the lapwing; a small white crane, commonly called a paddy-bird.
15904: कोर कोर, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कुर्), a movable joint, as the fingers, the knee, &c.; amphi-arthrosis; a bud (see the next).
15905: कोरक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a bud, an unblown flower; the fibres of the stalk of a lotus; a species of perfume, commonly Cor (चोर); another perfume, a berry containing a resinous and fragrant substance; [cf. कक्कोलक।]
15906: कोरकित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with buds.
15907: कोरित, अस्, आ, अम्, budded, sprouted; ground, pounded, comminuted.
15908: कोरङ्गी कोरङ्गी, f. small cardamoms; [cf. एला।]
15909: कोरदूष कोर-दूष or कोरदूषक, अस्, m. a kind of grain eaten especially by the poor, Paspalum Scrobiculatum. See कोद्रव।
15910: कोरली कोरली or कोरिला, f., N. of a town.
15911: कोल कोल, अस्, m. a hog; a raft, a float, a boat; a kind of weapon; the breast, the haunch, the hip or flank, the lap [cf. क्रोड]; an embrace, embracing; N. of a plant (= चित्र, चित्रक); the planet Śani or Saturn; N. of a son of Ākrīḍa; N. of a degraded warrior-tribe; an outcast, one of a tribe degraded by Sagara from the military order; a man of a mixed caste; a barbarian, a Kol, a tribe inhabit-ing the hills and forests in central India; (आ or ई), f. the jujube tree, Zizyphus Jujuba; (आ), f. Piper Longum, and Piper Chaba (चव्य); (अम्), n. the fruit of the jujube; black pepper; the weight of one Tola; [cf. Lith. kuilys, kiaule; Hib. cullach; Gr. χοῖρος.] —कोल-कन्द, अस्, m. a sort of bulbous plant, used as a remedy for worms; [cf. कृमि-घ्न, पञ्जल, &c.] —कोल-कर्कटिका, f., N. of a plant, = मधु-खर्जूरिका. —कोल-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —कोल-दल, अम्, n. a kind of perfume, = नखी. —कोल-नासिका, f., N. of a plant, = वङ्-किणी. —कोल-पुच्छ, अस्, m. a heron. —कोल-मूल, अम्, n. the root of long pepper. —कोल-वल्ली, f. the plant Pothos Officinalis, a plant with a pungent fruit resembling pepper, = गज-पिप्पली; another plant, Piper Chaba (चव्य). —कोल-शिम्बी, f., N. of a plant, commonly called Ālakuśī, Carpopogon Pruri-ens; [cf. कृत-फला, खट्वा, &c.] —कोला-कोलि, ind. with mutual embraces. —कोलाञ्च (°ल-अञ्°), अस्, m. a N. of Kaliṅga, the Coromandel coast from Cuttack to Madras; but, according to some, this place is in Gangetic Hindūstan, with Kanouj for the capital. —कोला-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town.
15912: कोलक, अस्, m., N. of two plants, = अङ्कोठ and बहु-वार; (अम्), n. a kind of perfume, = कक्को-लक; black pepper.
15913: कोलकिल कोलकिल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a town; (also read किलकिल, किलिनकिल, कोलिकिल।)
15914: कोलकुण कोलकुण, अस्, m. a bug; [cf. कोणकुण, उत्कुण, मत्कुण।]
15915: कोलम्बक कोलम्बक, अस्, m. (fr. को + लम्-बक ?), the body of a lute, the whole of it except the strings.
15916: कोलाहल कोलाहल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (an onomatopoetic word), a loud and confused sound, an uproar, a great and indistinct noise (of men, animals, &c.); (अस्), m., N. of a personified moun-tain.
15917: कोलि कोलि, इस्, इस् or ई, m. f. the jujube tree, Zizyphus Jujuba; [cf. कर्कन्धु।] —कोलि-सर्प, अस्, m., N. of a degraded warrior-tribe.
15918: कोलिकिल कोलिकिल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a town (?); [cf. कोलकिल।]
15919: कोलित कोलित, अस्, m. an epithet of Maud-galyāyana.
15920: कोलुह कोलुह, अस्, m., N. of a man.
15921: कोलूक कोलूक, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a country; also कोलूत and शैलूत; [cf. उलूक, उलूट, उतूल, कुलूट, कुलूत, कौलूत।]
15922: कोल्या कोल्या, f. Piper Longum; [cf. कोला।]
15923: कोल्लक कोल्लक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain; [cf. कोन्व, कोन्वशिर, कोल, कोलगिरि, कोल्वगि-रेय।] —कोल्ल-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain.
15924: कोल्वगिरेय कोल्व-गिरेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
15925: कोविद को-विद, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. को and rt. विद्, to know), experienced, skilled, learned, wise (with loc., gen., and at the end of comp., e. g. अश्वेषु or अश्वानाम् or अश्व-कोविद, skilled in horses).
15926: कोविदार को-विदार, अस्, m. a tree, Bauhinia Variegata; also one of the trees of paradise.
15927: कोश कोश, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. rt. कुश् or कुष् ?, related to कुक्षि and कोष्ठ?; in the earlier literature generally spelt कोश; later books read both कोश and कोष), a cask, a vessel for holding liquids; (metaphorically) a cloud; a pail; a bucket; a drink-ing-vessel, a cup, a vessel in general; a box, a cup-board, a drawer, a trunk; the interior or inner part of a carriage; a sheath, a scabbard, &c.; a case, a covering, a cover; store-room, store, provisions; a treasury, the apartment where money or plate is kept; treasure, accumulated wealth, money; gold or silver, wrought or unwrought, as plate, jewellery, &c.; a kind of bandage (in surgery); a dictionary, lexicon, or vocabulary; a bud; the sheath or integument of a plant; a pod or any similar seed-vessel; a nutmeg, a nut-shell; the inner part of the fruit Artocarpus Integrifolia; the cocoon of a silk-worm; the vulva, the womb; the penis; a testicle or the scrotum; an egg; (in the Vedānta philosophy) a term for the three sheaths or succession of cases which make up the various frames of the body enveloping the soul, (these are, 1. the आनन्द-मयः कोशः or ‘sheath of pleasure,’ forming the कारण-शरीर or ‘causal frame;’ 2. the विज्ञान-मयः or बुद्धि-मयः or मनो-मयः or प्राण-मयः कोशः, ‘the sheath of intellect or will or life,’ forming the सूक्ष्म-शरीर or ‘subtile frame;’ 3. the अन्न-मयः कोशः, ‘the sheath of nourishment,’ forming the स्थूल-शरीर or ‘gross frame’); a ball or globe (e. g. सूत्र-कोष, a ball of thread; नेत्र-कोष, the eye-ball &c.); judicial trial, ordeal by fire, water, poison, the balance, heated balls of iron, boiling oil &c., attesting a deity with thrice-repeated drinking of the water in which some idol has been washed; the water used at an ordeal; an oath; (आ), f., N. of a river; (ई), f. a bud; a seed-vessel; the beard of corn; a shoe, a sandal; [cf. Hib. gucog, ‘a bud, a sprout;’ Gr. κόκκος] —कोश-कार, अस्, m. one who makes scabbards, cases, boxes, &c.; the compiler of a diction-ary, a lexicographer; the silk-worm or the insect while in its cocoon; 16321: क्व क्व, ind. (fr. 1. कु; according to Pāṇ. V. 3, 12, VII. 2, 104, formed first fr. किम् and then fr. the substitute कु with affix अत्), where? in what place? whither? how? when? (rarely) how much less! [cf. कुतस्]; connected with the particles इद्, स्विद्, नु, &c., in the same manner as 2. क, q. v. (e. g. क्व नु ते क्षत्रियाः शूराः, where now are those Kṣatriya heroes ?); क्व appears to be used as a loc. of 2. क in Manu X. 66. (e. g. क्व श्रेयस्-त्वम्, in whom is the preference?); क्व with भू, अस्, or गत, may denote, how is it with? what has become of? (e. g. क्व अहम् भवानि, what will become of me? क्व गतस् तव मय्य् अनुरागः, what has become of your affection for me?), or क्व alone may have the same meaning (e. g. क्व सुखम्, where is happiness? i. e. there is no such thing as happiness); क्व — क्व or कुत्र — क्व implies ex-cessive incongruity, where is this? where is that? how distant is this from that, how little does this agree with that (e. g. क्व शूर्य-प्रभवो वंशः क्व च अल्प-विषया मतिः, how can my limited intellect describe the solar race?); क्वापि (क्व अपि), anywhere, somewhere, to some place, to any place, in a certain place; sometimes; क्व च, anywhere, somewhere, at any time; क्व च न, anywhere (originally negative); न क्वचन, nowhere; क्व-चिद्, anywhere, somewhere, to any place, in a certain place; in a certain case, sometimes; at some time, once upon a time; क्वचिद् — क्वचिद्, here — there, here and there, in various places; now — then, now and then; न क्वचिद्, nowhere, never, by no means; यत्र क्वापि or यत्र क्वच, wherever, whereso-ever, to whatsoever place, anywhere; यत्र क्व-चन, to whatsoever place, hither and thither, any-where; whenever, at any time, when, in any case or matter whatever; यत्र क्व वाथ — तत्र तत्रापि, wherever — there. —क्व-जन्मन्, आ, आ, अ, where born? —क्व-निवास, अस्, आ, अम्, where dwelling?

16352: क्षत्र क्षत्र, अम्, अस्, n. m. 16786: खलु खलु, ind. (as a particle of assevera-tion or affirmation), indeed, verily, certainly, truly, yes; (as a continuative particle), now, now then, now further; (as a particle employed in syllogistic forms of speech), but now, = the Latin atqui. It occurs only once in the Ṛg-veda; oftener in the Brāhmaṇas and Buddhist compositions, especially when combined with other particles, thus अथ खलु, उ खलु, वै खलु, and खलु वै, = now then, now further. In later Sanskrit खलु frequently does little more than lay stress on the word by which it is preceded, and is sometimes merely an expletive. According to native lexicographers खलु is also a particle of prohibition, endearment, conciliation, and inquiry. न खलु, by no means, not at all, indeed not.
