23824: ननु न-नु, ind. (fr. 2. न + नु), a strong negative particle = ‘not at all’ (Ved.); a particle of interrogation = the Latin नोन्ने, ‘not?’ ‘is not?’ ‘are not?’ ‘does he not?’ often a particle of affir-mation = ‘is it not so?’ i. e. ‘it certainly must be so,’ hence = ‘certainly,’ ‘assuredly,’ or with an impe-rative = ‘pray,’ ‘do,’ ‘just,’ ‘well,’ ‘do now,’ &c., or sometimes with an interrogative pronoun (e. g. ननु को भवान्, pray who art thou?); in argumentative writings often a mere inceptive particle = ‘now then,’ ‘but then,’ ‘but’ (e. g. ननु न किञ्चिन् मानम् इति चेन् न, now if it be said that there is no proof, not so); नन्व् अस्तु तथापि, ‘well, be it so, never-theless;’ ननु च, ‘and (is it) not so?’ ‘is not then?’ ‘there can be no doubt.’ According to native lexi-cographers ननु is also a vocative particle = ‘ho,’ ‘hallo;’ a particle implying kindness, conciliation, &c., = ‘pray,’ ‘good friend;’ a responsive particle; a parti-cle of reproach, perplexity, &c.

23839: नन्दायनीय, अस्, m., N. of a pupil of Bāṣkali.
23840: नन्दि, इस्, m. (for नन्दी see under नन्द), ‘the happy one,’ epithet of Viṣṇu; of Śiva; N. of an attendant of Śiva [cf. नन्दिन् and नन्दिकेश्वर]; N. of a man; of a Gandharva; (according to some also) the speaker of the prologue or prelude to a drama or one who pronounces the benediction, see नान्दी, नान्दिन्; (इस्, इ), m. n. gambling, gaming; (इस्), f. joy, delight, pleasure, happiness, prosperity, welfare, (in these senses said to be also m. n.); Joy personified as a daughter of Heaven or as the wife of Kāma and mother of Harṣa. —नन्दि-कुण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —नन्दि-क्षेत्र, अम्, n., N. of a district frequented by the gods. —नन्दि-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain; [cf. नन्दि-देवी।] —नन्दिगिरि-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the glory of Nandi-giri,’ N. of a work. —नन्दि-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a prince of Kaśmīra. —नन्दि-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a village (near the modern Daulatābād, where Bharata resided during Rāma's banishment). —नन्दिग्राम-दर्शन, अम्, n. ‘description of the village Nandi-grāma,’ the twenty-ninth chapter of the Pātāla-khaṇḍa of the Padma-Purāṇa. —नन्दि-घोष, अस्, m. cry of joy (= वन्दि-घोष); the proclamation of a panegyrist or herald; the chariot of Arjuna. —नन्दि-तरु, उस्, m. = धव, the tree Grislea Tomentosa. —नन्दि-तूर्य, अम्, n. a musical instrument played on joyful occasions. —नन्दि-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man; (ई), ? the common N. of one of the loftiest Himalayan peaks. —नन्दि-पुराण, अम्, n. ‘the Purāṇa of Nandi,’ N. of part of the Kedāra-kalpa. —नन्दि-मुख = नन्दी-मुख, a species of rice [cf. नदी-मुख]; N. of a man. —नन्दिमुख-सुघोष, अस्, m., N. of a man. —नन्दिमुखसुघोषावदान (°ष-अव्°), N. of a Buddhist work. —नन्दि-रुद्र, अस्, m., N. of Śiva in a joyful or serene form. —नन्दि-वर्धन, अस्, आ, अम्, increasing pleasure, promoting happiness; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; a son [cf. नन्दन]; a friend; the end of a half month, i. e. the day of full moon or new moon; N. of a particular form of temple (= नन्दिन्); N. of a prince, son of Udāvasu or of Janaka, (in this sense also read नन्दि-वर्ध); N. of a place. —नन्दि-वारलक, अस्, m. a species of fish. —नन्दि-वृक्ष or नन्दि-वृक्षक, अस्, m. the tree Cedrela Toona; [cf. नन्दी-वृक्ष।] —नन्दि-वेग, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —नन्दि-षेण or नन्दि-सेन, अस्, m., N. of one of Skanda's attendants. —नन्दिषेणेश्वर (°ण-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga. —नन्दी-मुख, अस्, m. (नन्दी for नन्दि?), ‘having joy on the face,’ an epithet of Śiva; a species of aquatic bird; a species of rice [cf. नन्दि-मुख, नदी-मुख, नान्दी-मुखी]; (आस्), m. pl. a class of manes or deceased ancestors who are worshipped on festival occasions [cf. नान्दी-मुख]; (ई), f. sleep (in which the face shows joy), drowsiness; a species of the Ati-śakvarī metre; (more correctly नान्दी-मुख।) —नन्दीश (°दि-ईश), अस्, m., N. of one of Śiva's attendants [cf. नन्दि, नन्दिन्]; N. of Śiva; a kind of time in music (= नन्दीश्वर). —नन्दीश्वर (°दि-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of joy,’ an epithet of Śiva; N. of Nandin, the leader of Śiva's attendants; N. of one of Kuvera's attendants; N. of a place held sacred by the Jainas; a kind of time in music (= नन्दीश)। —नन्दीश्वर-पुराण = नन्दि-पुराण. —नन्-दीश्वर-योगोपाख्यान (°ग-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of the thirty-first and thirty-second chapters of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नन्दीश्वरोत्-पत्ति (°दि-ईश्°, °र-उत्°), इस्, f. ‘the birth of Śiva,’ N. of the forty-second chapter of the Liṅga-Purāṇa. —नन्द्य्-आवर्त, अस्, m. a particular kind of diagram [cf. नन्दिकावर्त]; a sort of palace or temple built in the shape of the above diagram or in the form of a quadrangle without a western gate, (in this sense also अम्, n.); a species of large fish; a kind of tree; the shrub Tabernæmontana Corona-ria (= तगर, = भगवद्-द्रुम), probably the sacred fig-tree; a species of shell called so because of its convolutions (आवर्त). —नन्द्य्-उपपुराण, अम्, n. = नन्दि-पुराण. —नन्द्य्-उपाख्यान, अम्, n. ‘the episode of Nandi,’ N. of the forty-fifth to the fiftieth chapter of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa.
23841: नन्दिक, अस्, m. the Tūn tree (Cedrela Toona), the wood of which resembles mahogany and is used for furniture &c. [cf. नन्दी, नन्दी-वृक्ष]; N. of one of Śiva's attendants; N. of a pupil of Śākya-muni, chief of the village Uru-vilvā. —नन्दिका-चार्य-तन्त्र (°क-आच्°), N. of a medical work. —नन्दिकावर्त (°क-आव्°), अस्, m. a kind of diagram (= नन्द्य्-आवर्त); a species of plant. —नन्दिकेश (°क-ईश), अस्, m., N. of a temple or holy place. —नन्दिकेश-लिङ्ग, अम्, n., N. of the thirty-ninth chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नन्दि-केश्वर (°क-ईश्°), अस्, m., N. of one of Śiva's chief attendants [cf. नन्दिन्, नन्दि]; N. of an author. —नन्दिकेश्वर-काशिका, f., N. of a Vedānta work by Nandikeśvara treating of the first of Pāṇini's gram-matical aphorisms as containing the dogmas of the Ve-dānta belief. —नन्दिकेश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place mentioned in the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नन्दिकेश्वर-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa. —नन्दिकेश्वर-संहिता, f., N. of a work mentioned in the Tantra-sāra. —नन्दिकेश्वरा-भिषेक (°र-अभ्°), अस्, m., N. of the forty-third and forty-fourth chapters of the Liṅga-Purāṇa. —नन्दिकेश्वरोत्पत्ति (°र-उत्°), इस्, f., N. of the twenty-first chapter of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa.
23842: नन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ (at the end of a comp.), rejoic-ing, gladdening; happy, delighted; delighting in, liking; making happy, gladdening; (ई), m. ‘rejoicing (a father),’ a son; the speaker of the prelude or bene-diction at the opening of a drama [cf. नान्दिन्]; N. of several plants, the Indian fig-tree, Thespesia Popul-neoides, Phaseolus Radiatus; N. of a particular form of temple [cf. नन्दि-वर्धन]; N. of a being attending on Śiva and (commonly) of the bull on which he rides [cf. नन्दि, नन्दीश, नन्दिकेश्-वर]; N. of a Buddhist saint and teacher; (इनी), f. ‘rejoicing (a mother),’ a daughter; a husband's sister (= ननान्दृ); holy basil (= तुलसी); Nar-dostachys Jatamansi (= जटामांसि); a kind of per-fume (= रेणुका); a fabulous cow, daughter of Surabhi, related to the cow of plenty, and the property of the sage Vasiṣṭha; an epithet or a form of Durgā; an epithet of Gaṅgā or the Ganges; N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; of a place; of a river (also called Vala-jā). —नन्दिनी-तनय or नन्दिनी-सुत, अस्, m. ‘son of Nandinī,’ epithet of Vyāḍi. —नन्दिनी-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place.
23843: नन्दी, f. See under नन्द and नन्दि।
23844: नन्द्य (fr. नन्द), Nom. P. नन्द्यति, &c., to be glad, to rejoice.
23845: नन्दलाल नन्दलाल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
23846: नन्दीक नन्दीक, अस्, m. (?), a cock.
23847: नन्दीट नन्दीट, अस्, m. a bald-headed man.
23848: नन्नम नन्नम (fr. rt. नम्) in कु-न्°, q. v.
23849: नन्नम्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens.), bending or bowing very low.
23850: नपराजित् न-पराजित्, त्, m. ‘having no conquerer,’ ‘not overpowered (?),’ an epithet of Śiva.
23851: नपात् नपात् and नप्तृ, ता, m. (in Uṇādi-s. II. 96. derived fr. न + rt. पत्, ‘to fall;’ in Pāṇini VI. 3, 75, fr. न + पात् fr. rt. 3. पा, ‘to protect,’ according to which latter derivation नपात्, नप्तृ are for न-पातृ, ‘not the protector,’ allied to न-पितृ, ‘not the father;’ but a more probable deriva-tion is fr. rt. 1. नभ्, an older form of rt. 1. नह्, ‘to connect,’ a descendant being ‘the connecting relative;’ in the earlier Vedic language the strong cases are formed fr. नपात्, the weak fr. नप्तृ, e. g. acc. sing. नपातम्, dat. sing. नप्त्रे; in the later Sanskrit all the cases come fr. नप्तृ), a descendant, offspring in general, a son, &c. (Ved.); a grandson, a son's son, (in the later language restricted to this meaning); N. of one of the Viśve-devās; (according to Mahī-dhara on Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā XIX. 56. न-पातः = देव-यान-पथः, the path of the gods; according to Sāyaṇa on Ṛg-veda X. 15, 3, नपातः = विनाशाभावः); (ती), f., Ved. a daughter; a granddaughter, (in Atharva-veda IX. 1, 3, नप्ति); नप्ती and नप्त्या, f. du. = (in Sāma-veda) ‘the two pieces of wood for pressing out the Soma,’ or = ‘heaven and earth;’ or in Ṛg-veda IX. 9, 1, = ‘the hands;’ नप्त्यः, f. pl. in Ṛg-veda I. 50, 9, = ‘the female horses of the chariot,’ i. e. ‘the daughters of the chariot,’ (according to Sāy. so called ‘because with them the chariot does not fall’); in Ṛg-veda IX. 14, 5, नप्त्यः is said to = ‘rays’ or ‘fingers;’ horses as ‘granddaughters of the chariot;’ the fingers, the hands; (त्री), f. a granddaughter, (नप्त्री, f., and not नप्ती, is the only form used in classical Sanskrit); [cf. तनू-नपात्, प्र-नपात्: Zend नप्तर्, नपत्, ‘descendant;’ नप्त्-इ, ‘kindred;’ नप्त्य, ‘a family:’ Gr. ἀ-νεψιό-ς for ἁ-νεπτιό-ς, quasi चोन्-नेपोत्-इउ-स्, νέπ-ο-δες: Lat. nepō(t)-s, f. nept-i-s: Old Iceland. nefi, ‘brother;’ nift, ‘sister:’ Old Germ. nefo, ‘grandson, cousin;’ niftila, ‘female cousin:’ Goth. nithyi-s, m. ‘cousin;’ nith-yō, f. ‘a female cousin:’ Slav. netii, ‘a brother's son:’ Boh. neti, base neter, ‘a female cousin.’]
23852: नपात्क, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or belonging to a grandson; (applied to a particular sacrificial fire, = तृतीयो ऽग्निस्।)
23853: नप्तृका, f. a species of bird.
23854: नपुंस् न-पुंस्, -पुमान्, m. not a man, a eunuch.
23855: न-पुंस, अस्, m. not a male, a eunuch.
23856: न-पुंसक, अस्, अम्, m. n. neither man nor woman, a hermaphrodite; a eunuch, an impotent or imbecile man, a coward; (अम्), n. a word in the neuter gender; the neuter gender. —नपुंसक-पाद, अस्, m., N. of the eighth chapter of Durgā-dāsa's commentary on Vopa-deva's Mugdha-bodha, called Su-bodhā. —नपुंसक-लिङ्ग-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m., N. of a chapter of the grammatical work Nāma-liṅgānuśāsana by Amara-siṃha.
23857: नप्तृ नप्तृ, नप्ती, नप्त्री। See नपात् above.
23858: नभ् 1. नभ्, cl. 1. A. नभते, &c., Ved. to burst, to be torn or rent asunder; to hurt, injure, destroy, (नेभे occurs in Bhaṭṭi-kāvya XIV. 33); cl. 4. 9. P. नभ्यति, नभ्नाति, &c., to hurt, injure: Caus. P. नभयति, -यितुम्, to cause to burst, tear open.
23859: 2. नभ्, प्, f., Ved. (according to Sāy.) hurt, injury, destruction.
23860: नभनु, उस्, m. and ऊ, ऊस्, f., Ved. a spring, river, (water which bursts forth.)
23861: 1. नभन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नभन), Ved. burst-ing out, breaking or coming forth (as a hymn or as a horse). According to Sāy. = ‘being in the sky,’ ‘ethereal;’ ‘injuring,’ ‘destroying;’ ‘a hymn.’ (For 2. नभन्य see under नभ below.)
23862: नभन्व, अस्, m., Ved. a river; (according to modern scholars the form is नभनु।)
23863: नभ नभ, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. नह् with affix भ, but rather fr. नभ् an older form of 1. नह्, ‘to bind,’ ‘connect,’ as ‘connecting heaven and earth;’ according to others fr. rt. 1. नभ्, ‘to rend asunder or be broken up into clouds’), = नभस्, the sky, atmosphere; the month Śrāvaṇa (July — August); N. of a son of Manu Svārociṣa or of the third Manu (mentioned together with Nabhasya); N. of one of the seven sages of the sixth Manv-antara; N. of a demon, son of Vipra-citti by Siṃhikā; N. of a son of Nala (Niṣadha) and father of Puṇ-ḍarīka [cf. नभस्]; (आ), f. a spitting-pot (for नभास्?); N. of the city of the Sun; [cf. Zend nap-ta, ‘moist, wet;’ Gr. νέφ-ος, νεφ-έλη, ξυν-νέ-νοφε, νεφό-ω, probably δνόφος, ἰο-δνέφής, γνό-φος; Lat. nūb-ē-s, nūbilu-s, nēbula, probably Nep-tū-nu-s, nimbu-s for nembu-s; Old Iceland. nifl-heim-r; Old Germ. nib-ul; Mod. Germ. neb-el; Angl. Sax. ge-nip, ‘a cloud;’ Slav. neb-o, base neb-es, ‘sky;’ Lith. debes-i-s, ‘a cloud,’ through change of n into d, as in dewyni, ‘nine;’ Hib. neamh, ‘heaven;’ Cambro-Brit. nev, ‘heaven.’] —नभ-ग, अस्, m. ‘going on the sky,’ N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata; [cf. नभाग, नाभाग।]
23864: 2. नभन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy.) being in the sky, ethereal, heavenly; (see col. 2.)
23865: नभस्, अस्, n. fog, vapour; a cloud; sky, atmo-sphere, ether or heaven; ether as one of the five ele-ments; N. of a month in the rainy season (= श्रा-वण) or July-August, (according to lexicographers in this sense m.); period of life, age; the vapour or fluidity of the Soma (Ved.); water (Ved.); the sun (according to Nir. II. 14); (आस्), m. a cloud, the rains or the rainy season; the nose, smell; the fibres in the root of a lotus or a rope made of lotus fibres; a spitting-pot; N. of a prince, son of Nala and father of Puṇḍarīka; (असी), n. du. both worlds, heaven and earth. —नभः-केतन, अम्, n. ‘sky-banner,’ the sun. —नभः-क्रान्त, अस्, or नभः-क्रान्तिन्, ई, m. ‘going in the sky’ (from the lion-like shape of certain clouds), a lion. —नभः-पान्थ, अस्, m. ‘sky-traveller,’ the sun. —नभः-प्रभेद, अस्, m., N. of a descendant of Vi-rūpa and author of a Ṛg-veda hymn (X. 112). —नभः-प्राण, अस्, m. ‘sky-breath,’ air, wind; [cf. ख-श्वास, नभः-श्वास।] —नभः-श्रित्, त्, त्, त्, reaching to the sky, attaining heaven. —नभः-श्वास, अस्, m. ‘sky-breath,’ air, wind; [cf. नभः-प्राण।] —नभः-सद्, त्, m. ‘inhabiting the sky,’ a god; a star. —नभः-सरस्, अस्, n. ‘sky-lake,’ the clouds. —नभः-सरित्, f. ‘sky-river,’ the milky-way (= देव-पथ); the celestial Ganges. —नभः-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘situated in heaven,’ celestial, aerial, heavenly, ethereal. —नभः-स्थल, अस्, m. ‘whose residence is the sky,’ an epithet of Śiva; (ई), f. the sky. —नभः-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, abiding in heaven or in the sky; (अस्), m. a division of the infernal regions, a hell. —नभः-स्पृश्, क्, क्, क्, or नभः-स्पृश, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘sky-touching,’ reaching to the sky. —नभश्-चक्षुस्, उस्, m. ‘eye of the sky,’ the sun. —नभश्-चमस, अस्, m. ‘drinking vessel of heaven,’ the moon; a variegated cake (= चित्र-पूप); magic, conjuring. —नभश्-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘sky-going,’ going in the air; (अस्), m. an inhabitant of heaven, a god; a Vidyā-dhara or demi-god so called. —नभस्-तल, अम्, n. ‘the bottom of the clouds,’ the lower region of the sky, nether sky; the sky, atmosphere; (in astronomy) N. of the tenth solar mansion. —नभस्-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. vaporous, vapory, filled with vapour, exhaling vapour, misty, hazy; (Sāy.) bright as the sun.  — 1. नभस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, vaporous, filled with vapour, misty, cloudy; young; (आन्), m. air, wind; (अती), f., N. of the wife of Antar-dhāna and mother of Havir-dhāna. —२। नभस्-वत्, ind. like vapour. —नभो-ग, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. नॄ), hell, the place of torment (distinguished fr. पाताल, the lower regions, q. v.), including a num-ber of places of torture of various descriptions, gene-rally said to be twenty-one in number [cf. नारक]; (Hell is sometimes personified as a son of Anṛta and Nirṛti or Nikṛti); (अस्), m., N. of a demon, a son of Bhūmi or Earth (therefore called Bhauma, haunting Prāg-jyotiṣa and slain there by Kṛṣṇa); N. of a man; N. of a district; of a place of pilgrimage. —न-रक-कुण्ड, अम्, n. a pit or abyss in hell wherein the wicked are tormented, (eighty-six such are enume-rated). —नरक-जित्, त्, m. ‘vanquisher of the demon Naraka,’ epithet of Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa. —नरक-दे-वता, f. ‘the deity of hell,’ Nirṛti; Misfortune per-sonified as a goddess. —नरक-भूमि, इस्, f. a division of hell, (of which seven are enumerated.) —नरक-रूपिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘hell-formed,’ hellish. —नरक-वर्ग, अस्, m. ‘the hell chapter,’ N. of a chapter of Amara-siṃha's Nāma-liṅgānuśāsana. —नरक-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description of hell,’ N. of a chapter of the Revā-māhātmya. —नरक-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, living or being in hell; (आ), f. the river of hell, Vaitaraṇī. —नरक-स्वर्ग-प्राप्ति-प्रकार-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description of the mode of obtaining heaven and hell,’ N. of the eighth chapter of the Māgha-māhātmya. —नरकान्तक (°क-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘destroyer of the demon Naraka,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa-Viṣṇu. —नरकामय (°क-आम्°), अस्, m. the soul after death; a ghost or spirit. —नरकारि (°क-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of the demon Naraka,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa-Viṣṇu. —नरकावास (°क-आव्°), अस्, m. ‘one whose abode is hell,’ an inhabitant of hell. —नरकौकस् (°क-ओक्°), आस्, m. an inhabitant of hell.

23949: नर्म नर्म, अस्, m., Ved. sport, pastime; [cf. नरिष्टा।]
23950: नर्मठ, अस्, m. a jester; a rake, lecher, liber-tine; sport, amusement; coition; the nipple; the chin.
23951: नर्मन्, अ, n. sport, play, amusement, pastime; diversion; jest, joke, (नर्माणि कृ, to joke); wit, humour; (अणा), ind. in jest, by way of jest. —नर्-म-कील, अस्, m. a husband. —नर्म-गर्भ, अस्, m. a secret lover. —नर्म-द, अस्, आ, अम्, delight-ing, making happy, giving or causing pleasure; (अस्), m. a jester; the associate or companion of a person's sports or amusements; N. of the son of Lāḍana; (आ), f. the Narma-dā or modern Nerbudda river, which, rising in the Vindhya mountains, runs west-ward to the gulf of Cambay, (personified as the wife of Puru-kutsa and mother of Trasa-dasyu); a sister of the Uragas or serpents; a daughter of the Soma-pas; a species of plant (see पृक्का). —नर्मदा-तट-देश, अस्, m., N. of a district mentioned in the Ratna-koṣa. —नर्मदा-तीर-गमन, अम्, n., N. of the seventeenth chapter of the Uttara-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa. —नर्मदा-तीर्थ, अम्, n. a sacred bathing-place on the Narma-dā; [cf. नार्मद।] —नर्मदा-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the glory of Narma-dā,’ N. of the 173rd-181st chapter of the Matsya-Purāṇa. —नर्मदेश्वर (°दा-ईश्°), अस्, m. a form of Śiva. —नर्मदेश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of several sacred bathing-places. —नर्-मदेश्वर-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the glory of Śiva,’ N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नर्मदेश्व-र-लिङ्ग, अम्, n., N. of the ninety-second chapter of the Skanda-Purāṇa. —नर्म-द्युति, इस्, इस्, इ, bright with joy, cheerful, happy, merry; (इस्), f. enjoyment of a joke or any amusement. —नर्म-वती, f., N. of a comedy. —नर्म-सचिव, अस्, m. ‘amusement-companion,’ an associate or promoter of the amusements of a prince or man of rank. —नर्-म-साचिव्य, अम्, n. superintendence of a prince's amusements. —नर्म-सुहृद्, त्, m. = नर्म-स-चिव. —नर्म-स्फूर्ज, अस्, m. happiness or amuse-ment ending in alarm (?). —नर्म-स्फोट, अस्, m. slight or inferior amusement (?).
23952: नर्मय, Nom. P. नर्मयति, &c., to make happy or gladden by jests or sports, exhilarate by jesting and wit.
23953: नर्मट नर्मट, अस्, m. a potsherd; the sun.
23954: नर्मरा नर्मरा, f. a cavity, a valley; a bellows; an old woman past menstruation; a species of plant (= सरला).
23956: नल् नल्, cl. 1. P. नलति, &c., to smell; to pain (?); to bind (?); cl. 10. P. नाल-यति, &c., to speak or shine; to bind or confine, (the two meanings ‘smelling’ and ‘binding’ have probably arisen from a confusion between गन्धे and बन्धे in the Dhātu-pāṭha.)
23957: नल नल, अस्, m. (for नड, q. v.), a species of reed, Amphidonax Karka, eight to twelve feet high [cf. नड, नाल, देव-नल]; N. of a king of the Niṣadhas or of the country called Niṣadha, son of Vīra-sena and husband of Damayantī and hero of the celebrated tale called Nala and Damayantī; a son of Niṣadha and father of Nabha or Nabhas; a descendant of the latter Nala, son of Su-dhanvan and father of Uktha [cf. नड]; N. of a son of Yadu; N. of a monkey-chief, son of Tvaṣṭṛ or Viśva-karman, who made a bridge for Rāma from the continent to Laṅkā; N. of a Daitya; N. of a medical author; (in astrology) N. of a particular form of constellation in which all the planets or stars are grouped in double mansions; a deified proge-nitor, wrongly written for नल्व; (ई), f. a kind of fragrant substance, a perfume (= नटी); red arsenic, = मनः-सिला, कुनटी; (अम्), n. the blossom of Nelumbium Speciosum (?); smell, odour; [cf. rt. नल्।] —नल-कानन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people, (this word may perhaps be separated into नलक-आनन; also read नल-कालक, नभ-कानन।) —नल-कील, अस्, m. the knee. —नल-कूबर and नल-कूवर, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kuvera. —नल-चम्पू, ऊस्, f., N. of a work by Tri-vikrama-bhaṭṭa, also called Damayantī-kathā, describing the fortunes of Nala and Damayantī in a highly artificial mixed style, half prose, half verse; [cf. चम्पू।] —नल-द, अम्, आ, n. f. Indian spikenard, Nardostachys Ja-tamansi (= जटामांसी); (अम्), n. the root of Andro-pogon Muricatus (= उशीर); the honey or nectar of a flower; (आ), f., N. of a daughter of Raudrāśva. —नल-पट्टिका, f. a sort of mat made with reeds, a coarse mat. —नल-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —नल-मीन, अस्, m. a species of sprat or (according to some) a shrimp or prawn; (also read तल-मीन।) —नल-सेतु, उस्, m. ‘Nala's bridge,’ the causeway constructed by the monkey Nala, (a name given to the rocks between Ramisseram and Ceylon, com-monly called Adam's bridge.) —नलेश्वर-तीर्थ (°ल-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —न-लोत्तम (°ल-उत्°), अस्, m. a species of reed (= देव-नल). —नलोदय (°ल-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘Nala's rise,’ N. of an artificial poem ascribed to Kāli-dāsa and describing the restoration of the fallen Nala to pros-perity and power. —नलोपख्यान (°ल-उप्°), अम्, n. ‘the story of Nala (and Damayantī),’ N. of a celebrated episode of the Mahā-bhārata.
23958: नलक, अम्, n. a bone (hollow like a reed), any long bone of the body; the tibia; the radius of the arm; (इका), f. a kind of fragrant substance (= नली, commonly पवारी or पन्ठारी); the legu-minous plant Dolichos Lablab; the plant Polianthes Tuberosa; Dæmia Extensa.
23959: नलकिनी, f. (fr. an unused नलकिन्), the knee-cap or knee-pan; the leg.
23960: नलदिक, अस्, ई, अम्, dealing in Indian spikenard.
23961: नलित, अस्, m. a species of vegetable, (commonly नालिता।)
23962: नलिन, अम्, n. (connected with नल, its stalk being hollow like that of a reed), a lotus flower or water-lily, Nelumbium Speciosum or Nymphæa Ne-lumbo; the indigo plant; water; (ई), f. a lotus, Nelumbium Speciosum, the flexible stalk of the water-lily; an assemblage of the Nelumbium Speciosum or of lotus flowers; a pond in which the lotus grows or may grow, a place abounding in lotuses, (नलिनी is to नलिन as अब्जिनी to अब्ज, पङ्कजिनी to पङ्क-ज, and पद्मिनी to पद्म); the Ganges of heaven or rather an arm of it; a mystical N. of one of the nostrils (= नलिका); a kind of fragrant substance; the fermented and intoxicating juice of the cocoa-nut; N. of the wife of Aja-mīḍha and mother of Nīla; (अस्), m. the Indian crane (as a synonym of पुष्-कर); a species of shrub (= कृष्ण-पाक-फल)। —नलिन-दल, अम्, n. a leaf of the lotus flower; [cf. नलिनी-दल, नव-नलिन-दलाय।] —नलिनी-खण्ड, अम्, n. an assemblage of the Nelumbium Speciosum. —नलिनी-दल, अम्, n. a leaf of the lotus plant; [cf. नलिन-दल।] —नलिनी-नन्दन, अम्, n. ‘the divine garden near the Nalinī (?),’ N. of a garden of Kuvera. —नलिनी-पद्म-कोष, अस्, m., N. of a particular position of the hands in dancing. —नलिनी-रुह, अस्, आ, अम्, what comes forth or has come forth from a Nelumbium Speci-osum; (अस्), m. an epithet of Brahmā; (अम्), n. the fibres of the stalk of Nelumbium Speciosum. —नलिने-शय, अस्, m. (नलिने, loc. sing.), ‘reclin-ing on a lotus,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu.
23963: नलिनीक at the end of comp. = नलिनी, q. v.
23965: नल्व नल्व, अस्, m. a furlong, a measure of distance = 400 or 104 (?) cubits; (wrongly read नल्ल, नल।) —नल्व-वर्त्मग, अस्, आ, अम्, going the distance of a Nalva; (आ), f. a spreading plant; the orange tree (= काकाङ्गी for नारङ्ग?).
23966: नव 1. नव, अस्, आ, अम् (probably connected with the particle 1. नु, q. v., or less probably with नु for prep. अनु, or by some derived fr. rt. 4. नु, to praise), new, fresh, recent, young, modern; (अस्), m. a crow; a species of plant (= रक्त-पुनर्-नवा); N. of a son of Uśīnara and Navā; (आ), f., N. of a wife of Uśīnara and mother of Nava; (अम्), ind. recently, newly, lately, a short time ago, not long since, just, (the crude नव is prefixed to a past pass. part. in this sense, see नव-बद्ध); [for 2. नव see p. 473, col. 1: cf. Zend नव: Gr. νέο-ς, for νέϝο-ς, νεός, νειός, νε-αρό-ς, νε-ᾱν, νεᾱν-ία-ς, νέ-ᾱξ, νε-οσσό-ς, νε-οττ-ία, νε-οχ-μό-ς, νε-βρό-ς, νέ-ατο-ς, νεί-αιρα, νει-ρό-ν: Lat. novu-s, Noviu-s, nov-īciu-s, nov-āli-s, nov-ellu-s, nov-āre, nov-er-ca, nū-nt-iu-s, de-nuo, nū-per: Osk. Nuv-la, Nuceria: Goth. niu-yi-s, ‘new;’ niuyi-tha, ‘newness:’ Angl. Sax. niwe, neow, niwa: Lith. naú-ye-s, ‘new;’ nauyó-ka-s, ‘a novice:’ Slav. nov-ŭ, ‘new:’ Hib. nua, nuadh.] —नव-कारिका, f. a bride, a woman newly married, (probably wrong reading for नव-वरिका); a new Kārikā or comment. —नव-कालिका, f. (fem. of नव-कालक), a young woman, either one recently married or one in whom menstruation has lately commenced. —नव-कृत्, wrongly for नव-गत्. —नव-गत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. first-born (?). —१। न-व-ग्रह, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see under नवन्), lately caught; [cf. नव-बद्ध।] —नव-च्छात्त्र, अस्, m. a new scholar, a student, novice. —नव-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, recently born, lately produced, new, young (e. g. नव-जः शशी, the new moon or the moon just becoming visible). —नव-जा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. lately produced, new, young. —नव-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. born anew, new-born, fresh, new. —नव-तर, अस्, आ, अम् (compar.), newer, younger, fresher, &c.; [cf. नवीयस्।] —नव-ता, f. or नव-त्व, अम्, n. freshness, novelty. —नव-दल, अम्, n. the fresh leaf of a lotus flower, any young leaf. —नव-द्वीप, अस्, m. ‘the new island,’ N. of a place now called Nuddea, sixty miles from Calcutta, in the district of Burdwan on the right bank of the Bhāgīrathī or great western branch of the Ganges at the point where it is joined by the Jellinghee. —नव-नगर, अम्, n. ‘the new town,’ N. of a town. —नव-नलिन-दलाय (fr. नव-नलिन-दल), Nom. A. नव-नलिन-दलायते, &c., to resemble the leaf of a fresh lotus blossom. —नवनलिनदलायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, resembling the leaf of a fresh lotus flower. —नव-नी, ईस्, f. or नव-नीत, अम्, n. fresh butter. —नवनीतक, अम्, n. clarified butter. —न-वनीत-धेनु, उस्, f. a quantity of butter presented to Brāhmans, see धेनु. —नव-पर्णादि-भक्-षण, अम्, n. ‘eating of new leaves &c.,’ N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva. —नव-पल्लव, अम्, n. a new shoot, young sprout. —नव-प्रसूता, f. a woman who has lately brought forth (a child). —नव-प्राशन, अस्, m. eating of new rice or new barley. —नव-फलिका, f. a bride, a newly-married woman; a girl in whom menstruation has recently begun. —नव-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, lately caught, recently bound. —नव-मल्लिका, f. Arabian jasmine, Jasminum Sambac; (also read नव-मालिका।) —न-व-मालिका, f. many-flowered Nykanthes, Jasminum Sambac (= नव-मल्लिका); N. of a daughter of Dharma-vardhana, king of Śrāvasti. —नव-मालिनी, f. a kind of metre consisting of four lines of twelve syllables each. —नव-मेघ, अस्, m. a new cloud or one just appearing. —नव-यज्ञ, अस्, m. sacrifice or oblation of the first-fruits of the harvest; [cf. ना-वयज्ञिक, नवशस्येष्टि, नव-शस्य।] —नव-यौवन, अम्, n. fresh or incipient youth, bloom of youth, prime; (अस्, आ, अम्), being in the bloom of youth; (आ), f. a young woman. —नवयौवन-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, blooming with the freshness of youth. —नव-रक्तक, अम्, n. a newly-dyed gar-ment. —नव-रजस्, आस्, f. a girl who has only recently menstruated. —नव-वधू, ऊस्, f. a bride, a newly-married woman; a daughter-in-law. —नव-वरिका, f. a newly-married woman; [cf. नव-कारिका।] —नव-वस्त्र, अम्, n. new cloth. —नव-वास्त्व, अस्, m., Ved., N. of a man or of an evil spirit. —नव-शशि-भृत्, त्, m. ‘bearing the new moon (on his brow),’ an epithet of Śiva. —नव-शस्य, अम्, n. the first-fruits of the year's harvest, the grain first matured. —नवशस्येष्टि (°य-इष्°), इस्, f. ‘sacrifice of first-fruits,’ a sacrifice performed on eating the first matured rice or grain of the year; (wrongly written नवसस्येष्टि; cf. नव-यज्ञ।) —नव-श्राद्ध, अम्, n. the first series of Śrāddhas collectively, or funeral offerings on the first, third, fifth, seventh, ninth, and eleventh days after a person's demise. —नव-सङ्घाराम (°घ-आर्°), अस्, m., N. of a monastery. —नव-सू, ऊस्, f., Ved. a cow that has recently calved. —नव-सूतिका, f. a milch cow; a woman recently delivered. —नवाङ्कुर (°व-अङ्°), N. of a work. —नवान्न (°व-अन्°), अम्, n. new rice, new grain, the first-fruits; the grain first ripened, rice or grain recently matured; a cere-mony observed on first eating the new rice, &c. —नवान्न-भक्षण, अम्, n. ‘eating of new grain,’ N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva. —नवान्न-स्थाली-पाकामन्त्र, आस्, m. pl., N. of a work. —नवान्नेष्टि (°न-इष्°), इस्, f. sacrifice of the first-fruits, see नवशस्येष्टि. —नवाम्बर (°व-अम्°), अम्, n. new and unbleached cloth. —नवाम्बु (°व-अम्°), n. fresh water. —नवार्म (°व-अर्°), अम्, n., N. of a place. —नवाह (°व-अह), अस्, m. a new day, the first day of a fortnight. —नवी-करण, अम्, n. making new, doing anew, renewing. —नवी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to make new, renew, restaurate, revive. —नवी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done or made anew, renewed, revived. —नवी-भाव, अस्, m. becoming young or new, renovation. —नवी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become new, renewed, revived. —नवेतर (°व-इत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘other than new,’ old. —न-वोढा (°व-ऊढा), f. a newly-married woman, a bride. —नवोद्धृत (°व-उद्°), अम्, n. fresh butter; [cf. नव-नीत।]
23967: 1. नवक, अस्, इका, अम्, = 1. नव, col. 2.
23968: नविष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. the newest, youngest, last; (अम्), ind. (?), at last.
23969: नवीन, अस्, आ, अम्, = 1. नव, new, fresh, recent, modern. —नवीन-चन्द्र, अस्, m. the new moon. —नवीन-मत-विचार, अस्, m. ‘inquiring into new opinions,’ N. of a philosophical work by Hari-rāma. —नवीन-वेदन्तिन्, ई, m. a modern Vedānta philosopher.
23970: नवीयस् or नव्यस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of 1. नव), Ved. new, fresh, young, recent, who has done anything or shown himself recently; very new; (अस्), ind. recently, lately; (असे or असा), ind. anew.
23971: 1. नव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. new, fresh, young; (अस्), m. a species of plant, = रक्त-पुनर्-नवा; [cf. Lith. nauya-s; Goth. niuyi-s.] —नव्य-मत-विचार, अस्, m. = नवीन-मत-विचार. —नव्य-वत्, ind. like new, ever new (?).
23973: नव 2. नव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 4. नु), praise; panegyric, celebration. (For 1. नव see p. 472, col. 2.)
23974: नवन, अम्, n. the act of praising, laudation.
23975: नविष्टि, इस्, f., Ved. a song of praise, hymn; (Sāy.) a new sacrifice or oblation, (as if fr. 1. नव।)
23976: 2. नव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be praised, praise-worthy, laudable, deserving of praise. —नव्य-वर्-धमान, अस्, m., N. of an author.
23977: नवत 1. नवत, अस्, m. (for 2. see col. 2), an elephant's painted or variegated housings; woollen cloth; a cover, blanket, wrapper.
23978: नवन् नवन्, m. f. n. pl. (said to be fr. rt. 4. नु), nine; [cf. Zend navan, ‘nine:’ Gr. ἐννέα, ἔνα-το-ς, ἔννα-το-ς, εἴνατο-ς, ἐννά-κις, ἐνάκις, εἰνάκις, ἐνα-κόσιοι, ἐννα-κόσιοι, ἐνενή-κοντα, ἐννή-κοντα: Lat. novem, nōnu-s, nov-iens, nōnā-ginta, non-genti: Goth. niun, ‘nine;’ niun-da, ‘the ninth:’ Angl. 24024: नहुष, अस्, m., Ved. = नहुस्, a man; N. of a son of Manu and author of a Ṛg-veda hymn; N. of an ancient king, one of the lunar race, son of Āyus and grandson of Purū-ravas, father of Yayāti, who took possession of Indra's throne in heaven for a time, but was afterwards deposed and changed into a serpent; (according to others) a son of Ambarīṣa, father of Nābhāga; N. of a serpent-demon; N. of a Marut; an epithet of Kṛṣṇa-Viṣṇu; [cf. नघु-ष, नाहुष, नाहुषि।] —नहुष-चरित, अम्, n. ‘the life of Nahuṣa,’ N. of the 112th chapter of the Bhūmi-khaṇḍa of the Padma-Purāṇa. —न-हुषाख्य (°ष-आख्°), अम्, n. the plant Taber-næmontana Coronaria (= तगर-पुष्प). —न-हुषात्मज (°ष-आत्°), अस्, m., N. of a king, the son of Nahuṣa, also called Yayāti.
24025: नहुष्टर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. nearer (?), nearer than a neighbour.
24026: नहुष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging to a de-scendant of Nahus, belonging to a man in general, human; (अस्), m. a man.
24027: ना ना, ind. = न, no, not.
24028: नाक नाक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. न + अ-क, where there is no unhappiness), heaven, the vault or ceiling of heaven, the upper sky, the firma-ment, sky, atmosphere, ether, paradise, (often in the Veda with दिवो, gen. of 3. दिव्, or with उत्तम or तृतीय; cf. त्रि-नाक, त्रि-दिव: in Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā XVII. 67, the scale upwards is given as follows, 1. पृथिवी, earth; 2. अन्तरीक्ष, atmo-sphere; 3. दिव्, sky; 4. दिवो-नाक, upper sky; 5. स्वर्-ज्योतिस्, heaven of light or sphere of the luminaries); the sun (?) ; N. of a Maudgalya; N. of a mythical weapon of Arjuna; (अस्, आ, अम्), ‘pain-less (?),’ N. of a dynasty. —नाक-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, walking in the sky (as the Pitṛs). —नाक-नाथ, अस्, m. or नाक-नाथक, अस्, m. ‘guardian of the sky,’ an epithet of Indra. —नाक-नायक, अस्, m. ‘chief of the sky,’ an epithet of Indra. —नाकना-यक-पुरोहित, अस्, m. ‘Indra's chief priest,’ an epithet of Bṛhas-pati. —नाक-पाल, अस्, m. guardian or lord of the sky. —नाक-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. ‘sky-ceiling,’ the upper sky, the uppermost heaven. —ना-क-पृष्ठ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the highest heaven. —नाक-लोक, अस्, m. the heavenly world. —नाक-वनिता, f. ‘a nymph of heaven,’ an Apsaras. —नाक-सद्, त्, त्, त्, resting in the firmament, in-habiting the sky; (त्), m. an inhabitant of heaven, a deity; (अस्), m. pl., N. of nine Ekāhas; (त्), f., N. of an Iṣṭakā. —नाकापगा (°क-आप्°), f. the river of heaven, the heavenly Gaṅgā. —नाकेश (°क-ईश), अस्, m. ‘the lord of the sky,’ an epithet of Indra. —नाकेश्वर (°क-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘the lord of heaven,’ a god. —नाकौकस् (°क-ओक्°), आस्, m. ‘whose dwell-ing is the sky,’ an inhabitant of heaven, a god.
24029: नाकिन्, ई, m. a deity, god (as dwelling in Nāka). —नाकि-नाथ, अस्, m. ‘chief of the gods,’ an epi-thet of Indra.
24030: नाकु नाकु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. नम्), an ant-hill or mole-hill, a burrow; a mountain; N. of a Muni or saint. —नाकु-सद्मन्, आ, m. a snake.
24031: नाकुल नाकुल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नकुल), re-lating or belonging to an ichneumon, ichneumon-like, similar to an ichneumon; (अस्), m. a patronymic from Nakula [cf. नाकुलि]; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (ई), f. the ichneumon plant, a particular plant sup-posed to furnish the ichneumon or mungoose with an antidote when bitten in a conflict with a snake [cf. गन्ध-नाकुली, नकुलेष्टा]; a sort of pepper, Piper Chaba (= चव्य); the root of the Seemul tree (= कुक्कुटी-कन्द) and several other plants, as य-व-तिक्ता, श्वेत-कण्ट-कारी, सर्प-गन्धा. —ना-कुलान्ध्य (°ल-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘ichneumon blindness,’ a kind of weakness of sight.
24032: नाकुलि, इस्, m. a descendant of Nakula, a patro-nymic of Śatānīka.
24033: नाक्र नाक्र, अस्, m., Ved. an aquatic animal; [cf. नक्र।]
24034: नाक्षत्र नाक्षत्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नक्षत्र), belonging to the constellations or lunar asterisms, starry, sidereal; (अम्), n. a month computed by the moon's passage through the twenty-seven mansions, or one of thirty days of sixty Ghaṭis each.
24035: नाक्षत्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to the lunar asterisms, sidereal; (अस्), m. a month of twenty-seven days, each day being the period of the moon's passage through a lunar asterism; (ई), f. the state or condition to which a person is subjected agreeably to the asterism presiding over his nativity.
24036: नाग नाग, अस्, m. (perhaps for original स्नाग; Angl. Sax. snaca; Eng. snake; or connected with नग, a mountain, or नग्न, naked; said to be fr. rt. 1. दह् through change of द् into न्), a snake in general, especially the spectacle-snake or cobra capella, Coluber; a Nāga or fabulous serpent-demon so called, having a human face with the tail of a ser-pent, (the race of these beings is said to have sprung from Kadrū, wife of Kaśyapa [or from Su-rasā], in order to people Pātāla, one of the regions below the earth, their city is called Bhoga-vatī); an elephant; a shark (= तन्तु-नाग); a cruel or tyrannical person; (at the end of a comp.) ‘an elephant of a man,’ any great or pre-eminent person; N. of several plants, the small tree with fragrant blossoms, Mesua Roxburghii [cf. नाग-केशर]; Rottlera Tinctoria (= पुन्-नाग); a Cyperus (= मुस्तक); Piper Betel; a poisonous plant (see नाग-स्तोकक); a cloud; a peg or nail projecting from a wall to hang anything upon; one of the five airs of the body, that which is expelled by eructation; N. of the number seven, (probably to be referred to seven mythical serpents, but eight principal Nāgas are mentioned); N. of a Sādhya; of a Buddhist teacher; of a king of Āryāvarta, contemporary of Samudra-gupta; N. of a dynasty consisting of nine or seven princes; N. of several men; N. of a mountain; of a district; (ई), f. a female Nāga; a female elephant; (अम्), n. tin; lead; one of the astronomical periods called Karaṇas, (it is one of those termed ध्रुव, q. v., or invariable, and corresponds to the last half of Amāvāsya or new moon); the effects of that period on anything done or happening during it; (अस्, ई, अम्), formed or consisting of snakes, serpentine, snaky; relating to serpents or serpent-demons; elephantine, belonging to or resembling an elephant; (आ), f., N. of a woman; [cf. क्षिति-न्°।] —नाग-कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of bulbous plant (= हस्ति-कन्द). —नाग-कन्यका, f. a serpent-virgin. —नाग-कर्ण, अस्, m. a kind of Ricinus (= रक्-तैरण्ड, हस्ति-कर्ण). —नाग-किञ्जल्क, अम्, n. the blossom of Mesua Roxburghii. —नाग-कुमार, अस्, m. a prince of the serpent-demons; N. of a class of deities among the Bhavanādhīśas guarding the treasures of Kuvera. —नाग-केश, अस्, m., N. of a minister of king Nageśa. —नाग-केशर or नाग-केसर, अस्, m. a small tree with fragrant blossoms (commonly Nageśar), Mesua Roxburghii or Ferrea; (अम्), n. the blossom of this tree. —नाग-खण्ड, N. of one of the nine divisions of Bhārata-varṣa. —नाग-गन्धा, f. a species of bulbous plant (= नाकुली or सर्प-गन्धा). —नाग-गर्भ, अम्, n. red lead. —नाग-चूड, अस्, m. ‘snake-crested’ or ‘whose top-knot consists of snakes,’ an epithet of Śiva. —नाग-च्छत्त्रा, f. a kind of plant, Tiaridium Indicum. —नाग-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced by or born from a Nāga, &c.; (अम्), n. red lead; tin. —नाग-जिह्वा, f. ‘snake-tongue,’ a species of plant, Asclepias Pseudosarsa; (see शारिवा।) —नाग-जिह्विका, f. red arsenic. —नाग-जीवन, अम्, n. tin. —नागजीवन-शत्रु, उस्, m. ‘enemy of tin,’ orpiment. —नाग-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —नाग-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, given by Nāgas or serpents; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; N. of a man related to Śākya-muni; of a king of Āryāvarta, contemporary of Samudra-gupta. —नाग-दन्त, अस्, m. elephant's tusk or ivory, the tooth or tusk of an elephant; a shelf, peg, or bracket projecting from a wall and used to hang things upon; (आ), f., N. of an Apsaras; (ई), f. a species of sun-flower, Helio-tropium Indicum; a harlot. —नागदन्तक, अस्, m. ivory; a wooden peg or bracket projecting from a wall, a shelf; (इका), f. a plant, commonly called Rāma-dūti, Tragia Involucrata. —नाग-दमनी, f. a particular plant (= जम्बू, जाम्बवती, वृक्का)। —नाग-दलोपम (°ल-उप्°), अम्, n. the tree Xylocarpus Granatum. —नाग-दाशक, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —नाग-देण्टिका, f. the betel plant. —नाग-देव, अस्, m., N. of an author. —नाग-द्रु, उस्, m. a species of Euphorbia used in offerings to the snake-goddess Manasā (= समन्त-दुग्ध)। —नाग-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of a Dvīpa in Jambū-khaṇḍa or Bhārata-varṣa. —नाग-नक्षत्र, अम्, n., N. of the three asterisms forming the Nāga-vīthi (?). —नाग-नाथ, अस्, m. the king of the ser-pents, a serpent-chief; (अम्), n., N. of a Liṅga sacred to Śiva; (also called नागनाथेश-लिङ्ग।) —नाग-नाभ, अस्, m., N. of a man. —नाग-नामक, अम्, n. tin. —नाग-नामन्, आ, m. holy basil (= तुलसी)। —नाग-नायक, अस्, m. the leader or chief of the Nāgas or snakes. —नाग-नासा, f. the trunk or pro-boscis of an elephant. —नागनासोरू (°सा-ऊरू), ऊस्, f. a woman whose thighs taper like the trunk of an elephant; [cf. करभोरू, p. 205, col. 2.] —नाग-निर्यूह, अस्, m. = निर्यूह and नाग-दन्त, a large pin or bracket projecting from a wall like a shelf. —नाग-पञ्चमी, f. a particular festival, the fifth day in the light half of month Śrāvaṇa; the fifth day in the dark half of month Āṣāḍhā. —नाग-पति, इस्, m. a serpent-chief. —नाग-पत्-त्रा, f. = नाग-दमनी. —नाग-पत्त्री, f. a species of plant (= लक्ष्मणा). —नाग-पद, अस्, m. a kind of coitus. —नाग-पर्णी, f. the betel plant. —नाग-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man; a prince of Sāśikya. —नाग-पाश, अस्, m. a sort of magical noose or lasso used in battle to entangle an enemy; ‘the serpent-noose,’ an epithet of the weapon of Varuṇa, regent of the waters; a kind of coitus. —नाग-पाशक, अस्, m. a kind of coitus. —नाग-पुर, अस्, m. ‘elephant's town,’ ancient Delhi (= गज-पुर, हास्तिन-पुर). —नाग-पुष्प, अस्, m. several plants, = Rottlera Tinctoria (= पुन्-नाग); Mesua Roxburghii (= नाग-केसर); Michelia Champaka (= चम्पक); (अम्), n. the blossom of this plant; (ई), f. = नाग-दमनी. —नागपुष्प-फला, f. the plant Benincasa Cerifera (= कुष्-माण्डी). —नाग-पुष्पिका, f. yellow jasmine (= स्वर्ण-यूथी). —नाग-फल, अस्, m. the plant Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. a various reading for नाग-बला. —नाग-बधू, ऊस्, f. a female ele-phant. —नाग-बन्धक, अस्, m. an elephant-catcher. —नाग-बन्धु, उस्, m. ‘elephant-friend, liked by elephants,’ the holy fig-tree, Ficus Religiosa (= अश्वत्थ). —नाग-बल, अस्, m. ‘having the strength of an elephant,’ an epithet of Bhīma; (आ), f. the plant Uraria Lagopodioides; (अम्), n. a par-ticular high number. —नाग-बुद्ध, अस्, m. or नाग-बोधि, इस्, m., N. of a Buddhist teacher. —नाग-बुद्धि, इस्, m., N. of a medical author. —नाग-बोध, अस्, m., N. of an author. —नाग-भगिनी, f. ‘serpent's sister,’ N. of the goddess Manasā; [cf. नाग-मातृ।] —नाग-भिद्, त्, m. ‘elephant-destroyer,’ a species of snake, Amphisbæna; (also written नाग-भृत्, = डुण्डु।) —नाग-भूषण, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘decorated with serpents,’ an epithet of Śiva; [cf. नाग-चूड।] —नाग-भोग, अस्, m. a species of serpent. —नाग-मण्डलिक, अस्, m. a snake-keeper; a snake-catcher. —नाग-मती, f. the plant Ocimum Sanctum. —नाग-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of or in elephants. —नाग-मल्ल, अस्, m. ‘an athlete among the elephants,’ an epithet of Indra's elephant Airāvata. —नाग-मातृ, ता, f. ‘mother of serpent-demons,’ an epithet of Su-rasā; an epithet of the goddess Manasā (supposed to preside over snakes); red arsenic. —नाग-मार, अस्, m. a species of pot-herb, also Keśa-rāja. —नाग-मुद्र, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist Sthavira (= नाग-सेन)। —नाग-यष्टि, इस्, f. or नाग-यष्टिका, f. a gradu-ated pole or post for showing the depth of water in a newly dug pond, a boring-rod or stick driven into the earth. —नाग-रक्त, अम्, n. red lead. —नाग-रङ्ग, अस्, m. the orange, (usually applied to the Silhet orange, Citrus Aurantium.) —नाग-रट्ट, अस्, m. a various reading for नाग-वट्ट, q. v. —नाग-राज्, ट्, m. a serpent-king, a chief of the Nāgas. —नाग-राज, अस्, m. ‘king of the serpents,’ an epithet of Ananta or of Vāsuki, chief of the serpents; a king among the elephants, a large elephant. —नागराज-कर, अस्, m. the trunk of the king of elephants. —नाग-राजन्, आ, m. a serpent-king. —नाग-रुक, अस्, m. = नाग-रङ्ग, the orange-tree. —नाग-रेणु, उस्, m. red lead. —नाग-लता, f. the penis; N. of a woman. —नाग-लेखा, f., N. of a woman. —नाग-लोक, अस्, m. the Nāga world or one of the regions below the earth, otherwise called Pātāla, the world of the serpent-demons, the abode of serpents or the race of serpents collectively. —नाग-वट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a man; [cf. नाग-रट्ट।] —नाग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, consisting of snakes; possessed of elephants. —ना-ग-वधू, see नाग-बधू. —नाग-वन, अम्, n. ‘serpent-wood,’ N. of a place. —नाग-वर्त्मन्, आ, m., N. of a Tīrtha. —नाग-वल्लरी or नाग-वल्लि, इस्, ई, or नाग-वल्लिका, f. Piper Betel, the betel plant. —नाग-वारिक, अस्, m. a royal elephant; an elephant-driver or keeper; a peacock; an epithet of Garuḍa, the bird of Viṣṇu; the chief person in a court or assembly. —नाग-वास, अस्, m. ‘abode of snakes,’ N. of a lake supposed to have been formed originally by the valley of Nepal. —नाग-वीथी, f. a row of serpents; the serpents' path, that part of the moon's path which contains the asterisms Svāti or (according to others) Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, and Kṛttikā; N. of a daughter of Yāmī who was the daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma; of a daughter of Kaś-yapa by Yāminī. —नाग-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a species of tree. —नाग-शत, अस्, m., N. of a mountain. —नाग-श्री, ईस्, f., N. of a queen. —नाग-सम्-भव, अम्, n. minium or red lead. —नाग-सम्-भूत, ‘produced from serpents,’ epithet of a sort of pearl. —नाग-साह्वय, अस्, आ, अम्, called after elephants, (generally with नगर = ‘elephant's town,’ i. e. Hāstina-pura.) —नाग-सुगन्धा, f. the ich-neumon plant (= सु-गन्धा, सर्प-सुगन्धा, भुजङ्गाक्षी; cf. नाकुली). —नाग-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist Sthavira; a king of Āryāvarta and contemporary of Samudra-gupta. —नाग-स्तोकक, अम्, n. a species of poisonous plant. —नाग-स्थल, N. of a village near Mathurā. —नाग-स्फोता or rather नाग-स्फोटा, f. two plants (= दन्ती and नाग-दन्ती). —नाग-स्वरूपिणी, f. a kind of metre con-sisting of four lines of eight syllables each. —नाग-हनु, उस्, m. a kind of perfume (= नख). —नाग-हन्त्री, f. a species of plant (= बन्ध्या-कर्को-टकी; cf. नागाराति). —नाग-ह्रद, अम्, n. a lake inhabited by snakes or serpent-demons. —ना-गाख्य (°ग-आख्°), अस्, m. = नाग-केसर, Mesua Roxburghii. —नागाङ्ग, अम्, n. Hāstina-pura. —ना-गाङ्गना (°ग-अङ्°), f. a female elephant; the pro-boscis of an elephant; [cf. नागाञ्जना।] —नागाञ्-चला (°ग-अञ्°), f. = नाग-यष्टि, q. v. —नागाञ्-जना, f. the female of an elephant (= नाग-यष्टि, q. v.). —नागाधिप (°ग-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘the ser-pent-prince,’ an epithet of Śeṣa. —नागाधिपति (°ग-अध्°), इस्, m. ‘serpent-chief,’ an epithet of Virūḍhaka. —नागाधिराज (°ग-अध्°), अस्, m. the king or chief of the elephants. —नागानन्द (°ग-आन्°), अस् or अम्, m. n. 24037: नागक, अस्, m., N. of a man.
24038: नागिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having serpents, covered with or surrounded by serpents; snaky.

24040: नागपैय नागपैय, अस्, m., N. of a poet mentioned in the Śārṅgadhara-paddhati.
24041: नागम्मा नागम्मा, f., N. of a female poet.
24042: नागर नागर, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. नगर), town-born, town-bred, city, citizen; relating or belonging to a town, civic; spoken in a town or city; polite, civil; clever, sharp, knowing; bad, vile; nameless; (अस्), m. a citizen; = पौर, a term for a prince engaged in war under certain circumstances and (in astrology) applied to a planet in a state of opposition to other planets; a husband's brother; an orange; a lecturer; denial of knowledge; hardship, toil, fatigue; desire of final beatitude; (ई), f. the Nāgarī or Deva-nāgarī (q. v.) character in which Sanskrit is commonly written; a species of Euphorbia (= स्नुही); a clever or crafty or intriguing woman; (अम्), n. dry ginger; the root of Cyperus Pertenuis; a sort of coitus. —नागर-खण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a section of the Skanda-Purāṇa. —नागर-घन, अस्, m. or नागर-मुस्ता, f. a species of grass, Cyperus. —नागराह्व (°र-आह्°), अम्, n. dry ginger. —नागरोत्था (°र-उत्°), f. = नागर-मुस्ता, q. v.
24043: नागरक, अस्, ई, अम्, living in a town, (op-posed to आरण्यक); clever, cunning; (अस्), m. a citizen; the chief of the police or of a town; an artist; a thief, (a various reading for नागरिक); (अम्), n. dry ginger; [cf. नागर।]
24044: नागरिक, अस्, ई, अम्, town-born, town-bred; living in or inhabiting a town; produced from a town; polite; clever, cunning; (अस्), m. a citizen, the chief of a town, superintendant of police; (अम्), n. the toll raised from a town. —नागरिक-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —नागरिक-बल, अम्, n. the guard of a police-officer.
24045: नागरेयक, अस्, ई, अम्, city, citizen.
24047: नागरमर्दि नागरमर्दि, इस्, m. (fr. नगर-मर्दिन्), a patronymic from Nagara-mardin.
24048: नागरीट नागरीट, अस्, m. a libertine, rake, blackguard; (probably for नागवीट below.)
24049: नागवीट, अस्, m. a rake; intriguer, match-maker.
24050: नागशुण्डी नागशुण्डी, f. a species of gourd; (also read नामशुण्डी।)
24051: नागुली नागुली, f., N. of a town.
24052: नागोजी नागोजी or नागोजि or नागोजि-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a modern grammarian, also called नागेश-भट्ट, author of a Vivaraṇa or interpreta-tion of Kaiyaṭa's commentary on Patañjali, of a grammar called Paribhāṣendu-śekhara, &c.
24053: नाग्नजित नाग्नजित, अस्, m. (fr. नग्न-जित्), a descendant of Nagna-jit; (ई), f., N. of one of the wives of Kṛṣṇa; (wrongly spelt नग्नजिती।)
24054: नाचिक नाचिक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Viśvā-mitra.
24055: नाचिकेत नाचिकेत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. न-चिकेत, q. v.), relating to Na-ciketa or Na-ciketas; (अस्), m. a synonym of fire, (wrongly written नाचिकेतु); N. of an ancient sage, son of Uddālaki; [cf. न-चिकेत, त्रि-णाचिकेत।]
24056: नाचीन नाचीन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
24057: नाज्जक नाज्जक, अस्, m., N. of a man.
24058: नाट नाट, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. rt. नट्), dancing, acting, a dance; (अस्), m., N. of a Nāga-rāja; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, = कर्णाटक, the Carnatic; (ई), f., scil. भाषा, the language spoken by the Nāṭas. —नाटाम्र (°ट-अम्°), अस्, m. the water-melon, Cucurbita Citrullus.
24059: नाटक, अस्, ई, अम्, dancing, acting; (अम्), n. a play, drama; the first of the ten pieces of dramatic compositions of the first order; (अस्), m. an actor, dancer, mime; N. of a mountain in Kāmākhyā; (इका), f. a kind of play, see below; (अकी), f. the court of Indra. —नाटक-प्रपञ्च, अस्, m. course or arrangement of a drama. —नाटक-रत्न-कोष, अस्, m. ‘treasure of jewels of plays,’ N. of a work. —नाटक-विधि, इस्, m. mimic art, dramatic action. —नाटकावतार (°क-अव्°), अस्, m., N. of a work.
24061: नाटकेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
24062: नाटार, अस्, m. (fr. नटी), the son of an actress; [cf. नाटेर, नाटेय।]
24063: नाटिका, f. a short or light comedy, the first of the Upa-rūpakas or dramas of the second order.
24064: नाटितक, अम्, n. a mimic representation, a gesture.
24065: नाटेय, अस्, m. the son of an actress or dancing-girl.

24069: नाडपित् नाडपित्, Ved., N. of a place.
24070: नाडायन नाडायन, अस्, m. (fr. नड), a patronymic from Naḍa.

[cf. नाडी-देह।] —नाडी-व्रण, अस्, m. an ulcer, a fistula, fistulous sore, sinus. —नाडी-शाक, अस्, m. a species of vegetable (= नाडीक)। —नाडी-शुद्धि, इस्, f., N. of a Yoga work. —नाडी-सङ्ख्या, f., N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva. —नाडी-सञ्चार, अस्, m., N. of the forty-second chapter of the Jñāna-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नाडी-स्नेह, अस्, m. a N. of Bhṛṅgin; 24073: नाडिक, अम्, n. the plant Ocimum Sanctum (= काल-शाक); (आ), f. a hollow stalk or stalk in general; any tubular organ of the body (as an artery, vein, intestine, &c.); a fistulous sore; a ray of the sun (supposed to be hollow); an Indian hour or twenty-four minutes = (1/60) of a sidereal day = (1/2) Muhūrta; a measure of length = (1/2) Daṇḍa, (also read नारिका); a piece of metal on which the hours are struck, an Indian clock, a gong. —नाडिका-दत्त, अस्, m., N. of an author mentioned in the Saṃskāra-tattva by Raghu-nandana; [cf. नाडी-दत्त।]
24074: नाडीक, अस्, m. a species of pot-herb (= com-monly पाट्शाक्); Corchorus Olitorius; (आ), f. the wind-pipe or throat.
24075: नाडिकेल नाडिकेल or नाडीकेल, अस्, m. = नारिकेल, the cocoa-nut palm.

24077: नाड्वलेय नाड्वलेय, अस्, m. a metronymic from Naḍvalā.
24078: नाणक नाणक, अम्, n. a coin or anything stamped with an impression. —नाणक-परीक्षा, f. ‘the testing of coin,’ assaying. —नाणक-परीक्षिन्, ई, m. ‘coin-tester,’ an assayer, assay-master.
24079: नातिचिर नाति-चिर, अस्, आ, अम्, not very long (in time), of no long duration; (आत् or ए), ind. in no very long time, soon.
24080: नातिदूर नाति-दूर (न-अति-द्°), अस्, आ, अम्, not very distant; (ए), ind. not far from (with abl. or gen.); (अम्), ind. not very far, no great distance, not far away. —नातिदूर-निरीक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, not seeing very far, not far-sighted.
24081: नातिभिन्न नाति-भिन्न (न-अति-भ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, not very different from (with abl.).

24083: नात्र नात्र, अम्, n. (for नान्त्र), praise, eulogium; surprise, wonder; (अस्), m. Śiva; a sage.

24085: नाथ, अम्, n. refuge, help; (अस्), m. a protector, patron, master, leader, ruler, lord, (often at the end of a comp., see जीवित-न्°, पर्जन्य-न्°, कु-न्°; and often used at the end of names of gods and men, see गोविन्द-न्°, जगन्-न्°, त्रैलोक्य-न्°); a hus-band [cf. अ-न्°]; a possessor [cf. स-नाथ, possessed of]; a rope passed through the nose of a draft ox [cf. नाथ-हरि]; N. of an author; [cf. अ-न्°, कु-न्°, गोविन्द-न्°।] —नाथ-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. seeking for help or protection, seeking a refuge. —नाथ-कुमार, अस्, m., N. of a poet mentioned in the Śārṅgadhara-paddhati. —नाथ-त्व, अम्, n. the office or dignity of a protector or patron, pro-tectorship, patronage. —नाथ-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a patron or protector, having a master, de-pendant, subservient, subject; (अती), f. having a husband. —नाथ-विद्, त्, त्, त्, or नाथ-विन्दु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. possessing or granting protection. —ना-थ-हरि, इस्, इस्, इ, carrying a master, any animal bridled by the nose. —नाथ-हार, अस्, ई, अम्, taking or carrying a master, &c.

24087: नाथाय, Nom. P. नाथायति, -यितुम्, to be-come a protector or patron, to grant a request.
24088: नाथित, अस्, आ, अम्, one who needs help, needy, oppressed.
24089: नाथिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a protector or master.
24090: नाद नाद, अस्, m. (fr. rt. नद्), a loud sound, cry, sounding, roaring, bellowing, crying, a sound or tone in general, (sometimes at the end of an adj. comp., e. g. दारुण-नाद, अस्, आ, अम्, sounding dreadfully); (in the Yoga) the nasal sound represented by a semicircle and used as an abbre-viation or hieroglyphic in mystical words; one who praises. —नाद-ता, f. the quality of sounding. —नाद-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of a Purāṇa treating of musical sounds. —नाद-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, pro-nounced with sound (as letters), sonant. —नाद-विन्दूपनिषद् (°दु-उप्°), त्, f., N. of an Upa-niṣad.
24091: नादि, इस्, इस्, इ, sounding, roaring.

24143: नामन् नामन्, अ, n. (fr. rt. 1. ज्ञा, the initial ज् being lost; said to be fr. rt. म्ना), a mark by which anything is known, sign, token (Ved.); form, manner, mode, character, personal character, nature, species (Ved.); name, appellation, (especially a per-sonal name, as opposed to गोत्र, a family name); merely the name (as opposed to the reality); (in grammar) appellative, common name for a class of objects, noun, word (e. g. मेघ-नामन्, [every] noun or word denoting cloud); substance, essence, (in the Mīmāṃsā phil. opposed to गुण, accidental quality); water (according to Naigh. 1. 11); नाम्ना वच् or नाम ग्रह्, to address by name, mention or call upon by name; नाम कृ or नाम दा or नाम धा or नाम्ना कृ or नाम्ना वि-धा, to give a name, to name, call (e. g. सावित्रीति नामास्याश् चक्रुः, they called her name Sāvitrī; लक्ष्मणम् इति नाम कृतवान्, he named him Lakṣmaṇa; तां दुःख-लब्धिकां नाम्ना चकार, he called her Duḥkha-labdhikā). नामन् often occurs at the end of an adj. comp., in which case the fem. is generally नाम्नी (e. g. विष्णु-शर्म-नामा पण्-डितः, a sage named Viṣṇu-śarman; नदी-नाम्नी कन्या, a girl with the name of a river); but the fem. may be also नामा from नामन् and नामा from a base नाम, which is rarely substituted for नामन् at the end of a comp. (नाम, acc. sing. used as an adverb =) namely, by name (e. g. मा-धवो नाम ब्राह्मणः, a Brāhman, Mādhava by name); indeed, certainly, forsooth, really, of course, even, probably, possibly, perhaps, agreed, granted, granting (e. g. अस्तु नाम स धनी मे किञ्चिद् दधाति, granting [which I doubt] that this rich man will offer me something). नाम as an emphatic particle may have some of the above senses, but is often untranslatable by any single equivalent English word. It is frequently placed after interrogative pronouns (e. g. किं नाम, कथं नाम, कदा नाम, को नाम), when it may be translated by ‘then,’ ‘indeed,’ &c.; अपि नाम at the beginning of a sentence = perhaps, probably, would that! oh that! of course; मा नाम = may it not be that, perhaps, but I hope not; ननु नाम, certainly, evidently; after an imperative नाम = I care not, no matter, if you like, &c. According to native lexicographers नाम implies certainty, possibility, anger, reproach, consent, promise, recollection, sur-prise, pretence, &c.; [cf. Zend nāman: Gr. ὄνο-μα(τ), ἀν-ώνυ-μο-ς, νώνυμν-ο-ς, ὀνομαίνω, ὀνο-μάζω: Lat. co-gnō-men, i-gnō-min-ia, nō-men, nōmin-ā-re, nam, quis-nam, quem-nam = Sanskrit कं नाम, nem-pe = Sanskrit नाम अपि: Umbr. nume, nome, dat. sing. nomn-e: Goth. namō, gen. sing. namin-s, namn-yan, ga-namn-yan, ‘to name:’ Mod. Germ. nāmen, nāme: Angl. Sax. nāma, nemn-an: Eng. name: Slav. i-man, ‘name;’ imen-ova-ti, ‘to name:’ Scot. ainm, ‘name:’ Cambro-Brit. env, ‘name.’] —नाम-करण, अस्, m. a nominal affix; (अम्), n. giving a name, naming a child after birth. —नाम-कर्-मन्, अ, n. the ceremony of naming a child after birth. —नाम-ग्रह, अस्, m. or नाम-ग्रहण, अम्, n. or (Ved.) नाम-ग्राह, अस्, m. addressing or mentioning by name. —नाम-ग्राहम्, ind., Ved. by mentioning the name, by naming. —नाम-तस्, ind., see col. 3. —नाम-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man. —नाम-द्वादशी, f. a religious ceremony, wor-shipping Durgā daily under one of her twelve appel-lations (Gaurī, Kālī, Umā, Bhadrā, Durgā, Kānti, Sarasvatī, Maṅgalā, Vaiṣṇavī, Lakṣmī, Śivā, and Nārāyaṇī). —नाम-ध, अस्, or नाम-धा, आस्, m., Ved. one who gives a name, a name-giver. —नाम-धातु, उस्, m. a verbal base derived from a noun, a nominal verb. —नाम-धारक, अस्, आ, अम्, bearing only the name, being anything only by name (e. g. पुरुषो नाम-धारकः, one who is a man only in name). —नाम-धेय, अम्, n. a name, a title, an appellation, (sometimes at the end of a comp., e. g. किन्-न्°, see under किम्; 24195: नार्षद नार्षद, अस्, m. (fr. नृ-षद्), Ved. a patronymic of Kaṇva; N. of a demon (?).

24227: नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying, annihilating, causing to be lost, causing to perish, removing, (commonly in comp. with the object; cf. दुःस्वप्-न-न्°); (अम्), n. destruction, removing, removal, expulsion; ruin, perishing; forgetting.

(said by some to be fr. rt. स्ना = rt. स्नु), the nose, (originally perhaps नासा, sing. = a nostril; नासे, du. = the two nostrils or the nose); a pro-boscis, the trunk of an elephant [cf. गज-न्°]; a piece of wood over a door projecting like a nose, the upper timber of a door [cf. नक्र]; the plant Gendarussa Vulgaris (= वासक); [cf. Lat. nāsus, nāris for nāsis; Old Germ. nāsa; Angl. Sax. nāse; Mod. Germ. nāse; Slav. nōsŭ; Lith. nōsis; Gr. νῆ-σος; Hib. neas, ‘a promontory,’ ness in Dunge-ness.] —नासाग्र (°सा-अग्°), अस्, m. the point or tip of the nose. —नासा-छिद्र, अम्, n. a nostril. —नासा-छिन्नी, f. a species of bird with a divided beak (= पूर्णिका). —नासा-ज्वर, अस्, m. a kind of disease of the nose (= नक्र). —नासा-दक्षिणावर्त (°ण-आव्°), अस्, m. wearing the nose-ring in the right nostril by rich women who have children (?). —नासा-दारु, n. = नासा, a piece of wood over a door pro-jecting like a nose; the upper timber of a door-frame. —नासा-नाह, अस्, m. thickening of the membrane of the nose, stoppage of the nostrils. —नासान्तिक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नासा-अन्त), reaching to the nose; [cf. केशान्तिक।] —नासा-परिशोष, अस्, m. heat and dryness of the nose. —नासा-परिस्राव, अस्, m. ‘nose-flow,’ running at the nose, a running cold. —नासा-पाक, अस्, m. a kind of disease of the nose attended with inflammation. —नासा-पुट, अस्, m. ‘nose-cup,’ the outside of the nostril, the nostril. —नासापुट-मर्यादा, f. the septum of the nose. —नासा-प्र-तीनाह, अस्, m. = नासा-नाह, thickening of the membrane of the nose, stoppage of the nostrils. —नासा-रक्त-पित्त, अम्, n. bleeding of the nose. —नासा-रन्ध्र, अम्, n. ‘nose-aperture,’ the nostril. —नासार्शस् (°सा-अर्°), आस्, m. polypus of the nose. —नासा-वंश, अस्, m. the bridge of the nose. —नासा-वामावर्त (°म-आव्°), अस्, m. wearing the nose-ring in the left nostril, a mark of sorrow or distress. —नासा-विवर, अस्, m. ‘nose-cavity,’ a nostril. —नासा-शोष, अस्, m. dryness of the nostrils. —नासा-संवेदन, अस्, m. 24250: नास्ति नास्ति (न-अस्ति), ind. non-existence, not so, it is not. —नास्ति-ता, f. or नास्ति-त्व, अम्, n. non-existence. —नास्ति-वाद, अस्, m. “assertion of ‘it is not’ or of non-existence,” infidelity.

24254: नाहल नाहल, अस्, m. a man of a bar-barous or outcast tribe; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a non-Āryan people (= म्लेच्छ).

24257: नाहुषि, इस्, m. a patronymic of Yayāti.
24258: नि नि (an indeclinable prefix to verbs and nouns, used as a preposition except in one passage in Atharva-veda X. 8, 7, where it stands alone as an adverb), in, into, within; down, under, back; on, upon. As a prefix to nouns नि appears sometimes to be a curtailed form of निस् in its sense of ‘without,’ ‘deprived of’ (e. g. in नि-किल्विष, नि-खिल, q. v.), but the idea of negation in such compounds may pos-sibly be derived from the meanings ‘down,’ ‘down-wards,’ ‘back,’ which properly belong to नि; occasion-ally, however, नि is inaccurately written for निः (= निस्), as in नि-शब्द for निः-शब्द; according to native lexicographers the senses in which नि may be used are expressed by the following Sanskrit words, क्षेप, भृशार्थ, नित्यार्थ, दान, सन्-नि-धान, उप-रम, सं-श्रय, आ-श्रय, राशि, मोक्ष, अन्तर्-भाव, अधो-भाव, बन्धन, कौशल, नि-वेश, वि-न्य्-आस; [नि is thought by some to be for primitive अनि; cf. अन्-तर्, अन्-तरा; Gr. ἐν, ἐνί, εἰν, εἰς, ἐς for ἐν-ς, ἐν-τό-ς, ἔν-δο-ν, ἔσ-ω, ἔνεροι, ἔνερ-θε, ὑπ-ένερ-θε, ἐνέρ-τερο-ς, ἔντερο-ν; Lat. en-do, in-du, in, in-ter, in-trā, in-ter-ior, in-tumu-s, in-tus; Umbr. en, an-der; Osk. an-ter; Goth. in, inna, innuma, inna-thrō, un-dar; Mod. Germ. nieder; Angl. Sax. in, nidhan.]

Impv. निंस्स्व), निनिंसे, निंसितुम्, &c., Ved. to touch, kiss, salute. (After प्र the initial न् is optionally cerebralized, cf. प्र-णिंसितव्य, प्र-निंसितव्य, परि-णिंसक; cf. also rt. निक्ष्।)
24260: निः निः, euphonically substituted for निस्, q. v., before श्, ष्, स्, and rarely before क्, ख्, प्, फ्।
