(in later writings mostly spelt पांशु; probably fr. rt. पंस् or पंश्, to destroy), crumbling soil, dust, sand; a particle of dust, grain of sand; dung, manure; a species of plant (= पर्पट); a kind of camphor; landed property; [cf. Lat. pulvis for pulcvis; Cambro-Brit. pain, ‘pollen, fine powder or dust.’] —पांसु-कासीस, अम्, n. sulphate of iron. —पांसु-कुली, f. ‘multitude of dust,’ a high road, highway. —पांसु-कूल, अम्, n. a dust-heap, particularly a collection of rubbish and rags out of which the Buddhist priests make up their clothing; a legal document not made out in any particular person's name. —पांसुकूल-सीवन, अम्, n. ‘the sewing together of rags from a dust-heap,’ N. of the place where Śākya-muni assumed his priestly dress. —पांसुकूलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, one who wears clothes made of rags from a dust-heap. —पांसु-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with dust, dusty. —पांसु-क्षार = पांसु-ज, q. v. —पांसु-गुण्ठित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with dust. —पांसु-चत्वर, अम्, n. hail. —पांसु-चन्दन, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva. —पांसु-चामर, अस्, m. a heap of dust; a tent; a bank covered with Dūrvā grass; praise; a small cucumber. —पांसु-ज, अम्, n. ‘earth-born,’ a kind of salt extracted from soil, rock or fossil salt. —पांसु-जालिक, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu. —पांसु-धूम्र, अस्, आ, अम्, dark-red or dark with dust; [cf. धूलि-धूम्र।] —पांसु-ध्वस्त-शिरोरुह, अस्, आ, अम्, having the hair soiled with dust. —पांसु-निपात, अस्, m. a fall of dust. —पां-सु-पटल, अम्, n. a coating or mass of dust. —पांसु-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a kind of vegetable, Che-nopodium Album. —पांसु-भव, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?) = पांसु-ज, q. v. —पांसु-मर्दन, अस्, m. ‘dust-destroying,’ an excavation for water round the root of a tree. —पांसु-रागिणी, f. a species of plant (= महा-मदा). —पांसु-राष्ट्र, अम्, n., N. of a country; (आस्), m. pl., N. of its inhabitants. —पांसु-वर्ष, अस्, m. a shower of dust, falling dust. —पांसु-समूहन, अस्, ई, अम्, collecting or raising dust (as the wind). —पांसुत्कर (°सु-उत्°), अस्, m., Ved. = पांसु-वर्ष।
28640: पांसक, अस्, आ, अम्, vitiating, spoiling; con-temptible, vile.
28641: पांसन, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) defiling, disgracing, dishonouring; vitiating, spoiling, destructive; contemptible, wicked, bad, infamous; (अम्), n. contempt.
28642: पांसव, अस्, आ, अम्, formed or consisting of dust; (अस्), m. a patronymic (Ved.); a kind of salt (in this sense spelt पांशव).
28643: पान्सिन्, ई, इनी, इ, = पांसन (for which it is probably only a wrong reading).
28644: पांसुक, आस्, m. pl. dust; (आ), f. a menstruous woman; a fragrant plant, Pandanus Odoratissimus.
28645: पांसुर, अस्, आ, अम्, dusty (Ved.); a gad-fly; a cripple carried or moving about in a chair.
28646: पांसुल or पांशुल, अस्, आ, अम्, dusty, covered with dust; sullied, defiled, disgraced; defiling, disgracing (e. g. कुल-पांसुल, disgracing a family, a disgrace to the family); (अस्), m. a wicked or profligate man, a libertine, paramour, gallant; one of Śiva's weapons (a sort of pole armed at the upper end with transverse pieces representing the breast-bone and adjoining ribs and surmounted by a skull); an epithet of Śiva; a species of tree, Cæsalpinia Bonducella; (आ), f. a menstruous woman; a licentious woman, (अ-पां-शुला, a chaste woman); the earth; Pandanus Odo-ratissimus.
28647: पाक 1. पाक, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. 1. पा, to drink), Ved. very young; sincere, simple, genuine, inartificial, honest; ignorant; (अस्), m. the young of animals, a child, an infant; N. of a Daitya slain by Indra; an owl. —पाक-त्रा, ind., Ved. in a simple or honest way, in simplicity; (Sāy.) = विपक्व-प्रज्ञेषु, towards the sincere-minded. —पाक-दूर्वा, f., Ved. a species of plant. —पाक-द्विष्, ट्, m. ‘the enemy of the Daitya Pāka,’ an epithet of Indra. —पाक-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a simple or domestic sacrifice (an oblation offered on building a house, liberating a bull, &c.; according to Āpastamba this term comprise the Aupāsana-homa, Vaiśvadeva, Pār-vaṇa, Aṣṭakā, Śrāddha, Sarpa-bali, Īśāna-bali; according to Baudhāyana, the Huta, Pra-huta, Ā-huta, Śūla-gava, Bali-haraṇa, Praty-avarohaṇa, Ash-ṭakā-homa; according to Gautama, the Aṣṭakā, Pārvaṇa, Śrāddha, Śrāvaṇī, Āgrahāyaṇī, Caitrī, Aśva-yujī); N. of a man. —पाकयज्ञिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the Pāka-yajña; (अस्), m. a per-former of the Pāka-yajña ceremony. —पाकयज्ञिय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the Pāka-yajña. —पाक-वत्, ind., Ved. simply, honestly. —पाक-शंस, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. honest-minded; (Sāy.) = परिपक्व-व-चन, सत्य-भाषिन्, speaking sincerely. —पाक-शाला, f. ‘cook-house,’ a kitchen. —पाक-शासन, अस्, m. ‘punisher of the Daitya Pāka or instructor of the ignorant,’ an epithet of Indra. —पाकशासनि, इस्, m. (a patronymic fr. the preceding), an epithet of Jayanta; of Arjuna. —पाक-संस्था, f. = पाक-यज्ञ, q. v. —पाक-सुत्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. offering Soma with a simple or sincere mind (Sāy. = वि-पक्वेन मनसा सोमस्याभिषोतृ). —पाक-स्थामन्, आ, m., Ved., N. of a man. —पाक-हन्-तृ, ता, m. ‘slayer of the Daitya Pāka,’ an epithet of Indra.
28648: पाक्य, अम्, n., Ved. honesty, simplicity; (आ), ind. in simplicity, in ignorance.
28649: पाक 2. पाक, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. पच्), cook-ing, baking, roasting, boiling, dressing food; burning (bricks or earthenware); digestion, assimilation of food; ripening, becoming ripe, ripeness; maturity, perfect development (e. g. धियस्, of the intellect), development of consequences (as of an act done in a former life or of any act); completion, perfection, fulfilment, accomplishment [cf. फल-प्°]; greyness of the hair, old age; inflammation, suppuration, ripeness of a boil; an abscess, ulcer; a vessel in which anything is cooked or dressed, cooking utensil (a saucepan, boiler, &c.); the domestic fire; general fear and panic resulting in national disaster or revo-lution; the subversion of a country; [cf. अ-प्°, इक्षु-प्°, कृष्ण-प्°।] —पाक-कृष्ण, अस्, m. the Caronda tree, Carissa Carondas (‘bearing a black fruit when ripe,’ also other similar compounds, as पाककृष्ण-फल, कृष्ण-पाक). —पाक-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, caused by cooking or roasting, produced by maturing; (अम्), n. ‘obtained by boiling,’ black salt; flatulence. —पाकज-त्व, अम्, n. production by warmth, capability of being affected by contact with fire. —पाक-पात्र, अम्, n. a cooking utensil, a boiler, &c. —पाक-पुटी, f. a potter's kiln, pottery. —पाक-फल, अस्, m. the Caronda tree (= कृष्ण-पाक-फल). —पाक-भाण्ड, अम्, n. a cooking utensil. —पाक-मत्स्य, अस्, m. a species of fish; a kind of fish-sauce; a species of venomous insect. —पाक-रञ्जन, अम्, n. the leaf of the Laurus Cassia. —पाक-राजेश्वर (°ज-ईश्°), अस्, m., N. of a writer on the art of cookery. —पाक-शाला, f. ‘hall for cooking,’ a kitchen. —पाक-शुक्ला, f. chalk. —पाक-स्थान, अम्, n. ‘place for cooking,’ a kitchen; (scil. कुलालस्य) a potter's kiln. —पाका-गार (°क-अग्° or -आग्°), अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), ‘cooking-room,’ a kitchen. —पाकातीसार (°क-अत्°), अस्, m. chronic dysentery; [cf. आमातीसार।] —पा-काध्याय (°क-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘chapter on cooking,’ N. of a chapter of the Sannipāta-kalikā treating of particular medical decoctions. —पाकारु (°क-अरु), उस्, m., Ved., N. of a particular disease.
28650: पाकल, अस्, आ, अम्, bringing to maturity; sup-purative, causing suppuration in a boil; (अस्), m. fever in an elephant; fire; wind; = वोधन-द्रव्य (probably an error for राधन-द्रव्य); (आ), f. Bignonia Suaveolens; (ई), f. Cucumis Utilis-simus; (अम्), n. Costus Speciosus.
28651: पाकलि, इस्, f. a species of plant (= रोहिणी).
28652: पाकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, (at the end of a comp.) becoming mature, ripening; being digested.
28653: पाकिम, अस्, आ, अम्, cooked, dressed, ripened (naturally or artificially); obtained by boiling or evaporation (as salt).
28655: पाक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cooked or matured; fit to cook, eatable; obtained by cooking or evapo-ration; (अम्), n. a kind of salt; (अस्), m. saltpetre.
28656: पाचक, अस्, इका, अम्, cooking, roasting, baking; causing digestion, digestive, peptic, tonic; maturing, bringing to maturity; (अस्, इका), m. f. a cook; (अस्), m. fire; (अम्), n. the bile which assists in digestion. —पाचक-स्त्री, f. a female cook. —पाचिका-भार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, having a cook for a wife, married to a cook.
28657: पाचन, अस्, ई, अम्, causing to cook or boil, cooking, ripening; softening, relaxing, digestive; suppurative; (अस्), m. fire; acidity, sourness; a species of plant (= रक्तैरण्ड); (ई), f. a species of Myrobalan, Terminalia Chebula; (अम्), n. the act of cooking or baking; ripening; causing a wound to close; a styptic for closing wounds; a medicinal preparation, infusion, decoction (of various drugs, chiefly carminatives or gentle stimulants given to bring the vitiated humors in fever &c. to maturity); ‘extraction by boiling,’ eliciting extraneous sub-stances from a wound or ulcer by means of cata-plasms &c.; a cataplasm; a sort of diet-drink; dissolving; a dissolvent, digestive; penance, expi-ation; (इका), f. cooking, maturing.
28658: पाचनक, अस्, m. borax; (अम्), n. a sort of diet-drink; causing a wound to close (by means of styptics &c.).
28659: पाचनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cooked or digested; dissolving, digestive.
28660: पाचल, अस्, m. whatever cooks, ripens, causes digestion, &c.; a cook; fire; wind; a thing dressed or matured without the aid of fire; (अम्), n. cook-ing, maturing.
28661: पाचा or पाचि, इस्, f. cooking, maturing.
28662: पाच्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cooked; capable of being matured.
28663: पाक्ष पाक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पक्ष), be-longing to a half month, fortnightly, relating to a side or party, &c.
28664: पाक्षपातिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पक्ष-पात), favouring a party or faction, partial, factious.
28665: पाक्षायण, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to or occurring in a Pakṣa or fortnight, &c.
28666: पाक्षिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पक्ष or पक्षिन्), belonging to a bird; belonging to a fortnight, fort-nightly; belonging to an argument, &c.; favouring a party or faction; subject to an alternative, that which may or may not take place, possible but not necessary, contingent, allowed but not prescribed; (अस्), m. a fowler, bird-catcher; an alternative.
28667: पाखण्ड पाखण्ड, अस्, m. a heretic, hete-rodox Hindū (adopting the exterior marks of the classes, but not respecting the ordinances of the Vedas; also पाषण्ड, q. v.).
28668: पागल पागल, अस्, आ, अम्, mad, deranged, demented.
28669: पाङ्क्त पाङ्क्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पङ्क्ति), con-sisting of five parts, fivefold (Ved.); relating to or composed in the Paṅkti metre; an epithet of a kind of Soma; (अम्), n., scil. सामन्, N. of a Sāman. —पाङ्क्त-ता, f. or पाङ्क्त-त्व, अम्, n., Ved. five-foldness, fivefold nature or condition.
28670: पाङ्क्तकाकुभ, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. पङ्क्ति-ककुभ्), Ved. an epithet of a Pra-gātha consisting of the Paṅkti and Kakubh metres.
28671: पाङ्क्तेय or पाङ्क्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to sit in the general row at meals, fit to be associated with, admissible into society, fit for respectable society.
28672: पाङ्क्त्र पाङ्क्त्र, अस्, m., Ved. (according to Mahī-dhara) a kind of mouse.
28673: पाङ्गुल्य पाङ्गुल्य, अम्, n. (fr. पङ्गुल), limping, halting, hobbling.
28675: पाची पाची, f. a species of climbing plant.
28676: पाजस् पाजस्, अस्, n. (said to be fr. rt. 3. पा), Ved. brightness, shining, glimmer, gleam, glit-ter, sheen [cf. सहस्र-प्°]; cheerfulness, freshness, activity, strength, vigour, impetuosity; a shining sur-face (said of the sky); (असी), n. du. ‘the two shining surfaces,’ heaven and earth; (Sāy.) = बलवत्यौ, powerful (as an epithet of Dyāvā-kṣāmā); (आंसि), n. pl. glittering hues, glowing colours; (Sāy.) = बलानि। —पाजस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. brilliant, strong.
28677: पाजस्य पाजस्य, अम्, n., Ved. the region of the belly (of an animal); the flanks, side; [cf. त्रि-प्°।]
28678: पाञ्चकपाल पाञ्चकपाल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-कपाल), relating to or forming part of an oblation offered in five cups.
28679: पाञ्चगतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-गति), con-sisting of five forms of existence.
28680: पाञ्चजनी, f. a patronymic of Asiknī the daughter of the Prajā-pati Pañca-jana.
28681: पाञ्चजन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. पञ्च-जन, q. v.), containing or relating to the five classes or races of men, extending over the five races (Ved.); (अस्), m., N. of the conch of Kṛṣṇa which was taken by him from the demon Pañca-jana, see पञ्च-जन, p. 522; fire; a species of fish (= पोट-गल); N. of one of the eight Upa-dvīpas in Jambu-dvīpa; (आ), f. a patronymic of Asiknī; (अम्), n. (?), N. of a forest. —पाञ्चजन्य-धर, अस्, m. ‘bearing the conch Pāñcajanya,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa.
28682: पाञ्चदश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-दशी), relating to the fifteenth day of a month.
28683: पाञ्चदश्य, अस्, शी, अम्, relating or belonging to the fifteenth day of a month, used on the fifteenth day of a half month; (अम्), n. the aggregate of fifteen.
28684: पाञ्चनख, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-नख), made of the skin of an animal with five claws.
28685: पाञ्चनद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-नद), pre-vailing in the land of the five rivers, observed in Pañca-nada or the Pañjāb; (अस्), m. a prince of the Pañjāb; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of the Pañjāb.
28686: पाञ्चभौतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-भूत), composed of or containing the five elements; (with आ-दान) the assumption of the five elements.
28687: पाञ्चमाह्निक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्चम + अहन्), Ved. belonging to the fifth day.
28688: पाञ्चमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, treated of in the fifth (book).
28689: पाञ्चयाज्ञिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-यज्ञ), re-lating or belonging to or included in the five great sacrifices or ceremonies; (अम्), n. any one of the five great sacrifices.
28690: पाञ्चरात्र, आस्, m. pl. (fr. पञ्च-रात्र), N. of a Vaiṣṇava sect following the doctrine of their sacred book called Pañca-rātra. —पाञ्चरात्र-रहस्य, अम्, n., N. of a work mentioned in the Sarva-darśana-saṅgraha by Mādhavācārya.
28691: पाञ्चरात्र्य-निबर्हण, अम्, n., N. of the eighth chapter of the Śaṅkara-vijaya by Anantānanda-giri.
28692: पाञ्चवर्षिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-वर्ष), five years old.
28693: पाञ्चवाज, अम्, n. (fr. पञ्च-वाज), N. of a Sāman.
28694: पाञ्चविध्य, अम्, n. (fr. पञ्च-विधि), N. of a Sūtra treating of the five Vidhis of the Sāman.
28695: पाञ्चशब्दिक, अम्, n. (fr. पञ्च-शब्द), music of five kinds; musical instruments in general.
28696: पाञ्चशर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पञ्च-शर), belonging to ‘the five-arrowed’ or the god of love.
28697: पाञ्चार्थिक, अस्, m. (fr. पञ्चन् + अर्थ), a follower or votary of Paśu-pati or Śiva.
28698: पाञ्चाल पाञ्चाल, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-longing to the Pañcālas, dwelling in or ruling over the country of the Pañcālas; (अस्), m. a prince of the Pañcālas; the country of the Pañcālas; (आस्), m. pl. the people of the Pañcālas; an association of five guilds (viz. those of the carpenter, weaver, barber, washerman, and shoe-maker); (ई), f. a princess of the Pañcālas; a N. of Draupadī the wife of the five Pāṇḍu princes; a doll, puppet; scil. रीति, epithet of a particular poetical style; the melodious combina-tion of five or six words. —पाञ्चाल-देश, अस्, m. the country of the Pañcālas. —पाञ्चाल-राज, अस्, m. the king of the Pañcālas.
28699: पाञ्चालक, अस्, इका, अम्, belonging to the people of the Pañcālas; (अस्), m. a sovereign of the Pañ-cālas; (इका), f. a princess of the Pañcālas; a doll, puppet (sometimes written पाञ्चलिका).
28700: पाञ्चालेय or पाञ्चाल्य, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the Pañcālas; (अस्), m. a prince of the Pañcālas.
28701: पाञ्चि पाञ्चि, इस्, m. (fr. पञ्चन्), a patro-nymic. —पाञ्चि-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a village.
28702: पाञ्चिक, अस्, m., N. of the leader of the Yakṣas.
28703: पाट् पाट्, ind. an interjection used in call-ing (सम्बोधने).
28704: पाट पाट, अस्, m. (fr. rt. पट्), breadth, expanse, extension; (in geometry) the intersection of a prolonged side and perpendicular or the figure formed by such intersection; (आ), f. regular or suc-cessive order, series, succession.
28705: पाटक, अस्, m. a splitter, divider, one who cleaves or tears asunder; the half of a village, part of a village, a kind of village; a shore, bank; a flight of steps leading to the water; a kind of musical instru-ment; a long span (= महा-किष्कु); expense or loss of capital or stock; throwing dice.
28706: पाटन, अम्, n. splitting, cleaving, slitting up, tearing up, breaking, cutting to pieces, destroying. —पाटन-क्रिया, f. lancing an abscess or ulcer.
28707: पाटल, अस्, आ, अम् (said by some to be connected with पाट above), pale-red, of a pink or pale-red colour; rose colour; pallid; (अस्, ई, अम्), made of the Pāṭalī or forming a part of it; (अस्), m. a pale-red hue, rose colour, redness; the trumpet-flower, Bignonia Suaveolens (a tree with sweet-scented blos-soms); a species of rice ripening in the rains; N. of a man; (आ), f. Bignonia Suaveolens (both the tree and its blossom); red Lodhra; a kind of fresh-water fish; an epithet of Durgā; a form of Dākṣāyaṇī; (अम्, आ), n. f. the flower of the Bignonia Suaveolens; saffron. —पाटल-गण्ड-लेख, अस्, आ, अम्, having the complexion of the cheek reddened. —पाटल-द्रुम, अस्, m. a species of tree, Rottleria Tinctoria (= पुन्-नाग). —पाटल-पुष्प-सन्निभ, अम्, n. a species of medicinal plant (= पद्म-काष्ठ). —पाटला-वती, f., N. of a river; an epithet of Durgā. —पाटलोपल (°ल-उप्°), अम्, n. a ruby.

28760: पाण्डुकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering from jaundice, jaundiced.
28761: पाण्डुर, अस्, आ, अम्, whitish, white, pale, yel-lowish-white; (अस्), m. a form of jaundice; a species of plant (= मरु-वक); N. of a being attendant upon Skanda; (आ), f. Glycine Debilis (= माष-पर्णी); (अम्), n. the white leprosy, vitiligo. —पाण्-डुर-ता, f. whiteness, white colour. —पाण्डुर-द्रुम, अस्, m. ‘the pale tree,’ Wrightia Antidy-senterica. —पाण्डुर-पृष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, = पाण्डु-पृष्ठ, q. v. —पाण्डुर-फली, f. a species of shrub (= पाण्डु-फली, पाण्डु, धूसरा, &c.). —पाण्-डुरेक्षु (°र-इक्°), उस्, m. ‘pale sugar-cane,’ a species of sugar-cane (= श्वेतेक्षु).
28762: पाण्डुरिमन्, आ, m. pale or white colour, paleness.
28763: पाण्डूक, अस्, m., Ved. a species of rice; [cf. पाण्डुक।]
28764: पाण्ड्य, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people and of the country in the Dekhan inhabited by them; (अस्), m. a prince of the Pāṇḍyas; N. of a son of Ā-krīḍa; N. of the mountain-range in the Pāṇḍya country. —पाण्ड्य-देश, अस्, m. the country of the Pāṇḍyas. —पाण्ड्य-वाट, Ved., N. of a district in which pearls are found.
28765: पाण्ड्व, अम्, n. an uncoloured woollen garment; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people in Madhya-deśa; (a various reading for पाण्डु and पाण्ड्य।)
28766: पाण्य 2. पाण्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. पण्), praiseworthy, excellent. (For. 1. पाण्य see p. 562, col. 3.)
28767: पात् 2. पात्, m. (fr. rt. 2. पत्), falling; sin, wickedness. (For 1. see under rt. 3. पा।)
28768: 2. पात, अस्, m. (for 1. see under rt. 3. पा), flying, mode of flying, flight; throwing one's self into or down, falling, fall, downfall; alighting, descending; a cast, throw, shot; a stroke (e. g. खड्ग-पात, a sword-stroke); shedding, discharging, emitting, pour-ing out; destruction, dissolution; an attack, inroad, incursion; falling out, happening, coming to pass; defect, failing, fault, transgression; (in astrology) a malignant aspect; the node in a planet's orbit; an epithet of Rāhu; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school of the Yajur-veda. —पाताधिकार (°त-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘chapter on malignant aspects,’ N. of the eleventh chapter of the Sūrya-Siddhānta and of the thirteenth of the Ārya-Siddhānta —पातोत्पात (°त-उत्°), आस्, m. pl. falls and rises, depressions and elevations, ups and downs.
28769: पातक, अस्, आ, अम्, causing to fall; (अस्, अम्), m. n. ‘that which causes to fall or sink,’ sin, crime. —पा-तक-योग, अस्, m. incurring guilt, acting sinfully.
28770: पातकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, guilty of a crime, criminal, wicked, sinful, a sinner.
28771: पातन, अस्, ई, अम्, causing to fall, felling, laying low, cutting down; (अम्), n. causing to fall, felling, bringing down, throwing down, knocking down, laying low; throwing (as dice); lowering, humbling; removing, bringing away; causing to fall asunder, dividing; nodding (?); (with दण्डस्य) causing the rod to fall, chastising, punishing; (with जलौकसाम्) application of leeches; (with गर्भस्य) destroying the fetus, causing an abortion.
28772: पातनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be caused to fall or alight, to be discharged or shot off.
28773: पातयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who causes to fall, one who throws (dice &c.).
28774: पातयित्वा, ind. having made to fall; having thrown or put down or in.
28775: पाताल, अम्, n. (probably connected with 2. पात, the termination is compared with आल = आलय in अन्तर्-आल; the names of the other hells point to some connection with तल), one of the seven regions under the earth and the abode of the Nāgas or serpents and demons (seven such regions are enumerated, viz. A-tala, Vi-tala, Su-tala, Rasā-tala, Talātala, Mahā-tala, and Pātāla; but Pātāla is some-times used as a general name for all: according to the Mahā-bhārata, Pātāla is also a town in the world of the serpent-race); an excavation, hole, chasm; submarine fire; (in astrology) the fourth sign from that in which the sun is present, the fourth house; (अस्), m. a sort of apparatus for distillation or for calcining and subliming metals (formed of two earthen pots, the upper one inverted over the lower, and the two joined together by their necks with cement and placed in a hole containing fire); an epithet of Jupiter's year of 361 days; N. of the attendant of the fourteenth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī. —पाताल-केतु, उस्, m., N. of a Daitya prince. —पाताल-खण्ड, अस्, m., N. of the fourth part of the Padma-Purāṇa and of a part of the Skanda-Purāṇa. —पाताल-गङ्गा, f. the Ganges of the lower regions. —पाताल-गरुडी, f. or पाताल-गरुडाह्वय (°ड-आह्°), अस्, m. a species of creeper (= गारुडी). —पाताल-निलय, अस्, or पाताल-वासिन्, ई, or पातालौकस् (°ल-ओक्°), आस्, m. an inhabitant of the nether world, a demon, Daitya, Asura; a Nāga or serpent-demon. —पाताल-भोगि-वर्ग, अस्, m., N. of a part of the Nāma-liṅgānuśāsana by Amara-siṃha. —पाताल-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description of hell,’ N. of the first chapter of the Pātāla-khaṇḍa of the Padma-Purāṇa. —पाताल-विजय, अस्, m. ‘victory over hell,’ N. of the twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth chapters of the Uttara-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa.
28776: पातिक, अस्, m. the Gangetic porpoise, Delphinus Gangeticus (= शिशु-मार).
28777: पातित, अस्, आ, अम्, made to fall, felled, thrown down, cast down, struck down; lowered, depressed, humbled, overthrown.
28778: पातित्य, अम्, n. (fr. पतित), the state of one who is fallen or sunk, loss of position or caste, degraded condition.
28779: पातिन्, ई, इनी, इ, flying, going to, going, alighting on; falling, sinking; being included or contained in; causing to fall, felling, throwing down; pouring forth, discharging, emitting; [cf. अन्तः-प्°, एक-प्°, गर्भ-प्°, दण्ड-प्°।]
28780: पातिली, f. a trap or snare for catching deer; a small earthen vessel or pot, especially used by religious mendicants; a woman of a particular class.
28781: पातुक, अस्, ई, अम्, falling frequently or habitually, apt or disposed to fall; falling, losing caste; going to hell; (अस्), m. the declivity of a mountain, a precipice; an aquatic animal of a large size; (figura-tively) the water-elephant.
28782: 1. पात्य, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see p. 564, col. 1), to be felled, to be caused to fall, to be precipitated; to be inflicted or imposed (as a penalty).
28783: पात्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being caused to fall, being precipitated.
28784: पातङ्ग पातङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पतङ्-ग), belonging or peculiar to a grasshopper or moth.
28785: पातङ्गि, इस्, m. the son of the Sun, Saturn.
28786: पातञ्जल पातञ्जल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पतञ्जलि), composed by Patañjali; (अम्), n., scil. शास्त्र, the Yoga system of philosophy (first taught by Patañjali). —पातञ्जल-दर्शन, अम्, n. ‘the system of Pa-tañjali,’ N. of a chapter of the Sarva-darśana-saṅgraha ascribed to Mādhavācārya. —पातञ्जल-भाष्य, अम्, n., N. of a philosophical work on the Yoga-sūtras by Vyāsa.
28787: पातञ्जलि, इस्, m. a various reading for पतञ्-जलि, q. v.
28788: पातत्रिण पातत्रिण, अस्, ई, अम्, containing the word पतत्रिन्।
28789: पातल्य पातल्य, अम्, n., Ved. a particular part of a carriage; (according to Sāy.) = कीलक, a yoke-pin.
28790: पातव्य 1. and 2. पातव्य। See under rts. 1. and 3. पा, pp. 559, 560.
28791: पातसाह पातसाह, अस्, m. = پادشاه a king.
28792: पाताण्डिनीय पाताण्डिनीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school of the Yajur-veda.
28793: पाति पाति, इस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. पा; but con-nected with rt. 1. पत्), a master, lord, owner, pos-sessor; a husband (= पति).
28794: पातिव्रत्य, अम्, n. (fr. पति-व्रता), devotedness or loyalty to a husband, conjugal fidelity.
28795: पात्नीवत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पत्नी-वत्), Ved. be-longing to Agni-patnīvat, i. e. to Agni together with the wives of the gods; containing the word पत्नीवत्।
28796: पात्नीशाल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पत्नी-शाला), Ved. being or contained in the पत्नी-शाला।
28797: 2. पात्य, अम्, n. dominion. (For 1. पात्य see p. 563, col. 3.)
28798: पातृ पातृ। See under rts. 1. and 3. पा।
28800: पात्र 1. and 2. पात्र। See under rts. 1. and 3. पा, pp. 559, 560.
28801: पात्रट पात्रट, अस्, आ, अम्, spare, emaciate, thin; (अस्), m. a cup, pot; ragged garments.
28802: पात्रपाक पात्र-पाक, अस्, m. decoction of medicinal herbs; (incorrectly for पत्त्र-पाक।)
28803: पाथ पाथ, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. पा), fire; the sun; (अम्), n. water [cf. पीथ]; N. of a Sāman; = पथ।
28804: पाथस्, अस्, n., Ved. a spot, place; food; air; water. —पाथो-ज, अम्, n. ‘water-born,’ a lotus. —पाथो-द, अस्, m. ‘water-giver,’ a cloud. —पा-थो-धर, अस्, m. ‘water-bearer,’ a cloud. —पा-थो-धि, इस्, m. ‘receptacle of waters,’ the ocean. —पाथो-निधि, इस्, m. ‘treasure-house of waters,’ the ocean. —पाथो-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. possessing room or space.
28805: पाथिस्, इस्, m. the sea; the eye; (इस्), n. a blotch, scab; water (?).
28806: पाथ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in a spot or place; (Sāy.) N. of a Ṛṣi.
28807: पाथेय पाथेय, अम्, n. (fr. पथिन्), pro-vender or provisions &c. for a journey, viaticum; the sign of the zodiac Virgo (= पाथोन). —पाथेय-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with provisions for a journey, provisioned.
28808: पाथोन पाथोन (corrupted fr. the Gr. παρθένος), Ved. the sign of the zodiac Virgo.
28809: पाथ्न्य पाथ्न्य, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic of Dadhīca.
28810: पाद् पाद् (fr. rt. 2. पद्), see 3. पद्, p. 529; used at the end of comps., cf. द्वि-पाद्, त्रि-पाद्, and see Gram. 145.
28811: पाद, अस्, m. the foot (of men and animals; sometimes added in token of respect to proper names or titles of address, e. g. आकर्णयन्तु देव-पादाः, let your Majesty listen; कुमारिल-पादाः, the venerable Kumārila); the foot or leg of an inanimate object (as of a bedstead); a column, pillar; a foot as a measure (= 12 Aṅgulis); the foot or root of a tree; the foot of a mountain, a hill at the foot of a mountain; the bottom (of a bag); a ray or beam of light (rays being considered as the feet or hands of the heavenly bodies); a quarter, a fourth part (this sense is perhaps derived from the foot of a quadruped being one out of four); a quarter of a weight of gold (= 1(1/4) Paṇa); the fourth part of a book, (the Adhyāyas in the Śaunakīyā Catur-adhyā-yikā, in the Śārīraka-mīmāṃsā, and in Pāṇini's grammar are divided severally into four Pādas, as also the Dhanur-veda and the Vāyu-Purāṇa; while, on the other hand, the Adhyāyas in Vopa-deva's grammar contain more than four Pādas); the fourth part of a Śloka or of any verse; the line of a hymn or stanza of the Ṛg-veda or of any stanza; the quadrant of a circle; a part in general; [cf. Goth. fōtu-s, ‘a foot:’ Lith. páda-s, ‘the sole of the foot;’ pénda-s, ‘a vestige:’ probably Hib. fadadh, ‘kindling, lighting;’ fadaidhim, ‘I kindle, excite, provoke.’] —पाद-कटक, अस्, अम्, m. n. or पाद-कीलिका, f. an ornament for the feet or ankles, an anklet. —पाद-कृच्छ्र, अस्, m. ‘quarter-penance,’ a sort of penance (eating and fasting on alternate nights). —पाद-क्षेप, अस्, m. a footstep. —पाद-गण्डिर, अस्, m. morbid enlargement of the legs and feet. —पाद-गृह्य or पादे-गृह्य, ind., Ved., see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. II. 1, 72. —पाद-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. ‘foot-knot,’ the ankle. —पाद-ग्रहण, अम्, n. laying hold of or clasping the feet (of a Brāhman or superior as a mark of respectful salutation). —पाद-घृत, अम्, n. melted butter for anointing the feet. —पाद-चतुर or पाद-चत्वर, अस्, m. a slan-derer, calumniator; a goat; a sand-bank; hail; the religious fig-tree, Ficus Religiosa. —पाद-चापल्य, अम्, n. ‘foot-unsteadiness,’ fidgeting or shuffling with the feet. —पाद-चार, अस्, m. going on foot, walk-ing; the daily position of the planets; (एण), ind. on foot. —पाद-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, going or walking on foot, having feet for locomotion; fighting on foot; (ई), m. a footman, pedestrian, a foot-soldier. —पाद-चिह्न, अम्, n. foot-mark, foot-print. —पाद-ज, अस्, m. ‘born from the foot (of Brahmā),’ a Śūdra, man of the fourth and servile tribe. —पाद-जल, अम्, n. water for the feet; water in which the feet have been washed; (अस्, आ, अम्), that of which a fourth part is water, mixed with one fourth of water. —पाद-जाह, अम्, n. = पाद-मूल, that part of the foot to which the leg is articulated, the tarsus. —पाद-तल, अम्, n. the sole or lower part of the foot; (ए), ind. under the feet. —पाद-तस्, ind. out of the feet, from the feet, at or near the feet, (पादतः कृ, to put down at the feet); at the foot (of a bed); in the south-west (Manu III. 89, according to Kullūka, this may also mean ‘at the foot of the bed’); by or with a quarter; after a quarter of a verse (Ved.); step by step, by degrees. —पाद-त्र, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), or पाद-त्रा, f. ‘foot-covering,’ a shoe. —पाद-त्राण, अम्, n. ‘foot-protecting,’ a boot, shoe. —पाद-दारी or पाद-दारिका, f. ‘foot-rending,’ a chap in the feet, a chilblain. —पाद-दाह, अस्, m. a burning sensation in the feet (said to be in India an excruciating pain difficult to remedy). —पाद-धावन, अम्, n. washing the feet. —पाद-धावनिका, f. sand used for rubbing the feet. —पाद-नख, अस्, m. a toe-nail. —पाद-नालिका, f. an ornament for the feet, an anklet. —पाद-निचृत्, त्, f., scil. गायत्री, a defective metre, in which one syllable is wanting in each Pāda; (also wrongly spelt पाद-निवृत्।) —पा-द-निष्क, अस्, m. = पन्-निष्क, p. 529. —पाद-न्यास, अस्, m. placing the feet, a dance or measured step. —पाद-प, अस्, m. ‘imbibing nourishment with the foot or root,’ a plant, tree; ‘protecting the feet,’ (fr. rt. 3. पा) a foot-stool, cushion for the feet; (आ), f. a shoe, slipper. —पादप-खण्ड, अस्, m. a group or clump of trees. —पाद-पद्धति, इस्, f. a line of footsteps, a track, trail. —पाद-पद्म, अस्, m. ‘foot-lotus,’ a foot beautiful as a lotus. —पाद-परिघट्टन, अम्, n. trampling with the feet, treading upon. —पादप-रुहा, f. a climbing plant, parasitical plant. —पाद-पालिका, f. an orna-ment for the feet, an anklet. —पाद-पाश, अस्, m. a foot-rope for cattle or horses; an anklet of small bells, &c.; (ई), f. a chain for the feet, a fetter; a foot-carpet or mat. —पाद-पीठ, अम्, n. a foot-stool. —पादपीठिका, f. any common or vulgar trade, as that of a barber, &c.; white stone. —पाद-पीवी, f. a shoe; (incorrectly for पाद-पीठी?). —पाद-पूरण, अस्, आ, अम्, (Ved.) filling out a part or line of a verse (as a particle), expletive; (अम्), n. the filling out a line or the measure of a verse. —पाद-प्रक्षालन, अम्, n. ‘washing the feet,’ N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva. —पाद-प्रणाम, अस्, m. bowing to the feet, prostration. —पाद-प्रतिष्ठान, अम्, n. a foot-stool. —पा-द-प्रधारण, अम्, n. ‘foot-covering,’ a shoe. —पाद-प्रहार, अस्, m. ‘foot-blow,’ a kick. —पाद-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, bound or held toge-ther by quarters of verses (as a metre). —पाद-बन्-ध, अस्, m. any tie for the foot, a chain or fetter for the feet. —पाद-बन्धन, अम्, n. a fetter for the feet; a stock of cattle (so called from the foot-ropes with which cattle are tied). —पाद-भाग, अस्, m. a fourth part, quarter. —पाद-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, possessing a quarter, being only a quarter. —पाद-मिश्र, see Pāṇ. VI. 3, 56. —पाद-मुद्रा, f. the impression of a footstep, foot-print, trace. —पाद-मूल, अम्, n. ‘root of the foot,’ the part of the foot to which the leg is articulated, tarsus; the sole of the foot; the heel; a polite designation of a person; the foot of a mountain. —पाद-युद्ध, अम्, n. ‘foot-fight,’ fighting on foot. —पाद-रक्ष, अस्, m. a foot-protector, foot-guard; (आस्), m. pl. armed men who run by the side of an elephant in battle to protect its feet from wounds. —पाद-रक्षण, अम्, n. a cover for the feet; a leather boot or shoe, a stocking. —पाद-रजस्, अस्, n. the dust of the feet. —पाद-रज्जु, उस्, f. a tether or rope for the foot of an elephant. —पाद-रथी, f. ‘foot-vehicle,’ a shoe, boot, slipper. —पाद-रोहण, अस्, m. ‘growing from roots,’ the Indian fig-tree. —पाद-लग्न, अस्, आ, अम्, sticking to the foot. —पाद-लेप, अस्, m. an unguent for the feet. —पाद-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having feet, possessed of feet. —पाद-वन्दन, अम्, n. ‘saluting the feet,’ respectful salutation. —पा-द-वल्मीक, अस्, m. morbid enlargement of the legs and feet, elephantiasis. —पाद-विग्रह, अस्, m. (probably) a mode of reading in which the divisions in verses are carefully marked; (अस्, आ, अम्), hav-ing a quarter of the compass or extent. —पाद-विधान, अम्, n. ‘the arrangement of the parts of a verse,’ N. of a work ascribed to Śaunaka. —पाद-विरजस्, आस्, f. a shoe, slipper, stocking (as keeping रजस् or dust from the feet?). —पाद-वीथी, f. a shoe; (probably an incorrect form, cf. पाद-पीवी।) —पाद-वृत्त, औ, m. du., Ved. the two component elements of the quarter of a verse, i. e. the long and short syllable; (अस्), m. epithet of a Svarita separated from the preceding Ud-ātta by a hiatus. —पाद-वेष्टनिक, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a stocking. —पाद-शब्द, अस्, m. the sound or noise of footsteps (= पच्-छब्द). —पाद-शस्, ind. foot by foot; verse by verse, stanza by stanza; by a fourth part. —पाद-शाखा, f. ‘branch of the foot,’ a toe. —पाद-शीली, f. an ornament for the feet, an anklet; (probably an incorrect form.) —पाद-शु-श्रूषा, f. obedience towards the feet (a respectful expression for शुश्रूषा). —पाद-शेष, अम्, n. a quarter, fourth part. —पाद-शैल, अस्, m. a hill at the foot of or near a mountain. —पाद-शोथ, अस्, m. swelling of the feet, gout. —पाद-शौच, अम्, n. cleaning the feet (= पच्-छौच). —पाद-सं-हिता। f. the union of words in a quarter of a verse. —पाद-सेवन, अम्, n. or पाद-सेवा, f. ‘foot-salutation,’ showing respect by touching the feet, service, duty. —पाद-स्तम्भ, अस्, m. a supporting beam, pillar, post. —पाद-स्फोट, अस्, m. ‘cracking of the feet,’ chilblain, a sore or ulcer on the foot. —पाद-स्वेदन, अम्, n. perspiration of the feet, causing perspiration in the feet. —पाद-हत, अस्, आ, अम्, struck with the feet, kicked, trodden on, touched with the feet. —पाद-हर्ष, अस्, m. numb-ness of the feet after pressure upon the crural nerves. —पाद-हारक, अस्, आ, अम्, taken away with the feet; (अस्), m. one who takes away or steals any-thing with the feet (?). —पाद-हीनात्, ind. without division or transition; on a sudden, all at once. —पादा-कुलक (°द-आक्°), अस्, अम्, m. or n. half a line of a stanza. —पादार्पण (°द-अर्°), अम्, n. setting down the feet. —पादावनेजन (°द-अव्°), अस्, ई, अम्, used for washing the feet (Ved.); washing the feet. —पादावर्त (°द-आव्°), अस्, m. a wheel worked by the feet for raising water from a well; a square foot. —पादावसेचन (°द-अव्°), अम्, n. washing the feet; water for washing the feet, water in which the feet have been washed. —पादाष्ठील (°द-अष्°), अस्, m. the ankle; contusion of the feet (?). —पा-दासन (°द-आस्°), अम्, n. a footstool. —पादास्-फालन (°द-आस्°), अम्, n. trampling or shuffling of the feet, motion of the feet (as in wrestling or struggling), floundering. —पादाहत (°द-आह्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘struck with the foot,’ kicked, trodden, touched by the foot. —पादाहति (°द-आह्°), इस्, f. a blow with the foot, kick; treading, trampling. —पादे-गृह्य = पाद-गृह्य. —पादोत्फाल (°द-उत्°), अस्, m. shuffling or moving the feet. —पादोदक (°द-उद्°), अम्, n. ‘foot-water,’ water for washing the feet, water in which the feet of a Brāhman have been washed, water hallowed by the washing of sacred feet. —पादोदक-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place at Benares. —पादो-दर (°द-उद्°), अस्, m. a serpent (‘using the belly in place of feet’).

(fr. rt. 1. पृ or rt. पॄ), cross-ing [cf. दुष्-प्°]; the further shore or opposite bank of a river; the further side, concluding bound; the end or limit of anything, the utmost reach or extent; quicksilver; N. of a sage, a son of Pṛthu-ṣeṇa and father of Nīpa; of a son of Samara and father of Pṛthu; of a son of Aṅga and father of Divi-ratha; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a class of deities under the ninth Manu; (आ), f., N. of a river (said to flow from the Pāriyātra mountains or the central and western portion of the Vindhya chain); (ई), f. a quantity of water; a small water-jar, drinking-vessel, glass, cup; a milk-pail; a rope for tying an elephant's feet; pollen; (अम्), n. (with Jainas) an Arhat or deified saint and teacher. —पार-गति, इस्, f. going through, reading, studying through. —पार-गमन, अम्, n. reaching the opposite shore, crossing, going to the end. —पार-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, arriving at the opposite shore, crossing over. —पार-तस्, ind., Ved. on the opposite bank, on the further side. —पार-दण्डक, अस्, m. 28939: पारारुक पारारुक, अस्, m. a rock; [cf. पारटीट।]

(according to the Nirukta) destroying both banks (an epithet of the Sarasvatī; Sāy. = पारावार-घातिनी or = दूर-देशे विद्यमा-नस्यापि वृक्षादेर् हन्त्री; but the right meaning probably is), hitting the remote (demon), slaying from afar. —पारावत-देश, अस्, m., N. of a district men-tioned in the Ratna-koṣa. —पारावत-पदी, f. or पारावताङ्घ्रि (°त-अङ्°), ‘pigeon's foot,’ Cardios-permum Halicacabum (so called from the form of the leaf). —पारावताङ्घ्रि-पिच्छ, अस्, m. a pigeon.
28941: पारावति, इस्, m. a patronymic of Vasu-rocis.
28942: पारावदघ्नी पारावद-घ्नी, a wrong reading for पारावत-घ्नी, q. v.
28945: पाराशर पाराशर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पराशर), proceeding or derived from Parāśara or from Pārā-śarya; (अस्), m. a patronymic from Parāśara and N. of the poet Vyāsa; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school; (ई), f. a daughter of Parāśara; (अम्), n. the rules of Pārāśara for the conduct of the mendicant order. —पाराशरी-पुत्र, अस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher. —पाराशरोपपुराण (°र-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
28946: पाराशरकल्पिक, अस्, ई, अम्, one who studies the Parāśara-kalpa; (अस्), m. a follower of Parāśara the institutor of rules for the mendicant order.
28947: पाराशरि, इस्, m. a patronymic of Vyāsa.
28948: पाराशरिन्, ई, m. a mendicant of the school of Parā-śara or of Pārāśarya; a religious mendicant in general.
28949: पाराशर्य, अस्, m. a patronymic of the poet Vyāsa; N. of a teacher.
28950: पारिकर्मिक पारिकर्मिक, अस्, m. (fr. परि-कर्मन्), one who takes charge of the lesser vessels or utensils.
28951: पारिकाङ्क्षिन् पारिकाङ्क्षिन्, ई, m. an ascetic (who devotes himself to devout contemplation), a contemplative saint, a Brāhman in the fourth period of life, a religious mendicant; (also पारिकाङ्क्षक; cf. परि-काङ्क्षित।)
28952: पारिकुट पारिकुट, अस्, m., Ved. an at-tendant, servant.
28953: पारिक्षित पारिक्षित, अस्, ई, अम्, epithet of the verses of the Atharva-veda XX. 127, 7-10; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Janam-ejaya.
28954: पारिक्षितीय, अस्, m., Ved. (according to the commentator) the brother of Pari-kṣit.
28955: पारिखेय पारिखेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-खा), surrounded by a ditch or fosse, belonging to a ditch.
28956: पारिग्रामिक पारिग्रामिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-ग्रामम्), situated round a village.
28957: पारिजात पारिजात, अस्, m. (fr. परि + जात), the coral tree, Erythrina Indica (a splendid tree losing its leaves in June and then covered with large crimson flowers, sometimes identified with the Man-dāra); the wood of this tree; N. of one of the five trees of paradise (which was produced at the churning of the ocean and came into the possession of Indra from whom it was afterwards taken by Kṛṣṇa); fragrance; N. of a Ṛṣi; N. of a Nāga of the race of Airāvata. —पारिजात-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of flowers of the celestial Pārijāta. —पारिजात-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing the celestial Pārijāta. —पारिजात-सरस्वती-मन्त्र, आस्, m. pl., N. of certain magical formulas. —पारिजात-हरण, अम्, n. ‘carrying off of the Pārijāta tree,’ N. of sections of the Hari-vaṃśa and Viṣṇu-Purāṇa (describing the taking of the Pārijāta tree by Kṛṣṇa from Indra); N. of a comedy by Gopāla-dāsa.
28958: पारिजातक, अस्, m. the coral tree, Erythrina Indica; one of the five trees of paradise; N. of a sage.
28959: पारिण पारिण, अस्, m., N. of a man.
28960: पारिणाय्य पारिणाय्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. परि-णाय = परि-णय), relating to marriage, obtained on the occasion of marriage; (अम्), n. property or paraphernalia received by a woman at the time of marriage; marriage settlement.
28961: पारिणाह्य पारिणाह्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-णाह), household furniture and utensils.
28962: पारितथ्या पारितथ्या, f. (fr. परि + तथ्य?), a string of pearls for binding the hair, a trinket worn on the forehead where the hair is parted.
28963: पारितवत् पारित-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, containing the word पारित or other forms of the Caus. of rt. 1. पृ।
28964: पारितोषिक पारितोषिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-तोष), gratifying, delighting, pleasing, making happy, satisfactory, consolatory; (अम्), n. a reward, gratuity (given as a token of satisfaction).
28965: पारिध्वजिक पारिध्वजिक, अस्, m. (fr. परि + ध्वज), a standard-bearer.
28966: पारिन्द्र पारिन्द्र, अस्, m. a lion (= पा-रीन्द्र).
28967: पारिपन्थिक पारिपन्थिक, अस्, m. (fr. परि-पन्थम्), a highwayman, robber, thief.
28968: पारिपाट्य पारिपाट्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-पाटी), regularity, methodicalness, successiveness.
28969: पारिपात्र पारिपात्र, अस्, m. (fr. परि + पात्र?), N. of one of the seven principal mountain ranges of India (the central or western portion of the Vindhya chain which skirts the province of Malwa); N. of a son of Ahīna-gu; (also read पा-रियात्र।)
28970: पारिपात्रक or पारियात्रक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain range, the central or western portion of the Vindhya chain.
28971: पारिपात्रिक or पारियात्रिक, अस्, m. an inhabitant of the Pāripātra or Pāriyātra mountain range.
28972: पारिपान्थिक पारिपान्थिक, अस्, m. probably only a wrong reading for पारिपन्थिक, q. v.
28973: पारिपार्श्व पारिपार्श्व, अम्, n. (fr. परि-पार्श्व), retinue, attendants, followers.
28974: पारिपार्श्वक, अस्, इका, अम्, standing at the side, attending on; (अस्), m. an attendant; an assistant of the manager of a play; an actor who serves in place of a chorus in the drama and is one of the inter-locutors in the prologue; (इका), f. a female attendant, a chamber-maid.
28975: पारिपार्श्विक, अस्, ई, अम्, standing at the side, belonging to a retinue; attending on; (अस्), m. an attendant; an assistant of the manager of a play.
28976: पारिपेल पारिपेल, अम्, n. = परिपेलव, q. v.
28977: पारिप्लव पारिप्लव, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. परि-प्लव), swimming; moving to and fro, shaking, unsteady, tremulous, trembling; perturbed, troubled in mind; ‘moving in a circle,’ epithet of a particular legend recited at the Aśva-medha and repeated at certain intervals throughout the year (Ved.); (अस्), m. a boat; N. of a sage (?) in the fifth Manv-antara; (अम्), n., N. of a Tīrtha. —पारिप्लव-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, being in a boat. —पारिप्लव-नेत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having tremulous or swimming eyes.
28978: पारिप्लवीय, अम्, n., Ved. an oblation accom-panying the recitation of the Pāriplava legend.
28979: पारिप्लाव्य, अस्, m. a goose; (अम्), n. perplexity, agitation; tremulousness.
28980: पारिबर्ह पारिबर्ह and पारिवर्ह, अस्, m. = परि-बर्ह or परि-वर्ह, q. v.; a wedding present; N. of one of the sons of Garuḍa.
28981: पारिभद्र पारिभद्र, अस्, m. (fr. परि + भद्र), the coral tree, Erythrina Indica; the Nimb tree, Azadirachta Indica; a species of pine, Pinus Devadāru; the Saral, Pinus Longifolia; N. of a son of Yajña-bāhu; (अम्), n., N. of a Varṣa in Śālmala-dvīpa named after Pāribhadra.
28982: पारिभद्रक, अस्, m. the tree Erythrina Fulgens; the Nimb tree, Azadirachta Indica; (अम्), n. Costus Speciosus or Arabicus.
28983: पारिभाव्य पारिभाव्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-भू), surety, security, bail (= प्रातिभाव्य); a drug, a species of Costus, Costus Speciosus or Arabicus.
28984: पारिभाषिक पारिभाषिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-भाषा), universally received, generally current, usual, common; technical (as a term).
28985: पारिमाण्डल्य पारिमाण्डल्य, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-मण्डल), having the measure or being of the size of an atom; (अम्), n. an atom (as a measure of space), a mote in a sun-beam.
28986: पारिमाण्य पारिमाण्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-माण), circumference, compass.
28987: पारिमित्य पारिमित्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-मित), the being confined or limited, limitation.
28988: पारिमुखिक पारिमुखिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-मुखम्), being before or round the face, being near or present.
28989: पारिमुख्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being before or round the face, being near or present; (अम्), n. the being before the face, presence.
28990: पारियात्र पारियात्र, अस्, m., N. of a moun-tain; of a country; [cf. पारिपात्र।]
28991: पारियात्रक, N. of a place mentioned in the Romaka-Siddhānta.
28992: पारियानिक पारियानिक, अस्, m. (fr. परि + यान), a travelling carriage.
28993: पारिरक्षिक पारिरक्षिक, अस्, m. (fr. परि-रक्षा), a Brāhman in the fourth period of life, an ascetic or religious mendicant.
28994: पारिवत्स पारिवत्स, अस्, m. (fr. परि + वत्स), a calf belonging (to the cows mentioned in Hari-vaṃśa 11877).
28995: पारिवित्त्य पारिवित्त्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-वित्त), the being unmarried while a younger brother is married, the condition of an elder brother who is unmarried while the younger is married.
28996: पारिवेत्त्र्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-वेत्तृ), the marry-ing of a younger brother before the elder; the being unmarried while a younger brother is married.
28997: पारिव्राजक पारिव्राजक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-व्राजक), intended for a religious mendicant; (अम्), n. the wandering life of a religious mendicant.
28998: पारिव्राज्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-व्राज्), the wandering life of a religious mendicant; (also incorrectly written पारिव्रज्य।)
28999: पारिश पारिश, अस्, m. a species of tree (= फलीश, commonly called पलाश-पिपुल and गज-हण्ड).
29000: पारिशील पारिशील, अस्, m. a cake (= अपूप).
29001: पारिशेष्य पारिशेष्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-शेष), that which is left over, a remainder; (आत्), ind. this alone remaining, there being no alternative.
29002: पारिषद् पारिषद्, त्, त्, त् (fr. परि-षद्), one who is present at an assembly (?).
29003: पारिषत्क, अस्, आ, अम्, one who studies or knows what has been settled in an assembly (?).
29004: पारिषद, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to an assembly or council, one who belongs to an assembly or council; (अस्), m. a person present at an assembly or congre-gation, a spectator; an assessor at a council; a king's companion; (आस्), m. pl. the retinue or attendants of a god; (अम्), n. taking part in an assembly; (अस्, अम्), m. or n. (?), N. of a village in the North.
29005: पारिषदक, अस्, ई, अम्, done by an assembly.
29006: पारिषद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = परिषदं सम-वैति, = परिषदि साधुः, one who is present at an assembly, a spectator.
29007: पारिसारक पारिसारक, अस्, ई, अम्, containing the word परि-सारक।
29008: पारिहारिक पारिहारिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परि-हार), taking away, seizing; surrounding; (अस्), m. a maker of garlands; (ई), f. a kind of riddle.
29009: पारिहार्य, अस्, m. a bracelet; (अम्), n. taking, seizure.
29010: पारिहास्य पारिहास्य, अम्, n. (fr. परि-हास), jest, joke, fun; (एन), ind. in fun.
29011: पारी पारी, f. (fr. rt. पॄ), a cup, drinking-vessel, &c. See पार, p. 566, col. 2.
29012: पारीक्षित् पारीक्षित्, त्, m. = पारीक्षित, a patronymic of Janam-ejaya.
29013: पारीक्षित, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to or treating of Parī-kṣit, derived from Parī-kṣit; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Janam-ejaya; N. of a sovereign to whom the Bhāgavata-Purāṇa or life of Kṛṣṇa is supposed to have been addressed; N. of the successor of the preceding.
29015: पारीणह्य पारीणह्य, अम्, n. (fr. परी-णह्), household furniture or utensils; [cf. पारिणाह्य।]
29016: पारीन्द्र पारीन्द्र, अस्, m. a lion (= पा-रिन्द्र); a large snake, boa.
29018: पारीरण पारीरण, अस्, m. = परीरण, q. v.
29019: पारु पारु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 3. पा), the sun; fire (= पेरु).
29020: पारुच्छेप पारुच्छेप, अस्, ई, अम्, derived from Parucchepa; भारद्वाजम् पारुच्छेपम्, N. of a Sāman.
29021: पारुच्छेपि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Parucchepa.
29022: पारुषक पारुषक, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a species of flower; [cf. परूषक।]
29023: पारुषेय पारुषेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परुष), Ved. spotted, freckled.
29024: पारुष्य, अम्, n. roughness [cf. त्वक्-प्°], harsh-ness; harshness of language, abuse, reproach, con-tumelious or scurrilous language, opprobrious or unfriendly speech, insult; violence (in word or deed, cf. दण्ड-प्°, वाक्-प्°); squalor; the forest or grove of Indra; aloe wood or Agallochum; (अस्), m. a N. of Bṛhas-pati, the planet Jupiter.
29025: पारुष्ण पारुष्ण, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of bird.
29026: पारेगङ्गम् पारे-गङ्गम्, पारे-विशोक, पारे-सिन्धु। See under पार।
29027: पारेरक पारेरक, अस्, m. a sword, sci-mitar (?).
29028: पारोक्ष पारोक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परोक्ष), undiscernible, unintelligible, obscure, mysterious.
29029: पारोक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, undiscernible, invisible, hidden; (अम्), n. mysteriousness, mystery.
29030: पारोवर्य पारोवर्य, अम्, n. (fr. परो-ऽव-रम्), tradition.
29031: पार्घट पार्घट, अम्, n. ashes, = अर्घट; [cf. पार्पर।]
29032: पार्जन्य पार्जन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. पर्जन्य), belonging to Parjanya.
29033: पार्ण पार्ण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्ण), made or consisting of leaves, leafy; raised from leaves (as a tax); made of the wood of the Butea Frondosa; (अस्), m. a patronymic.
29034: पार्णवल्कि, इस्, m. (fr. पर्ण-वल्क), a patro-nymic of Ni-gada.
29035: पार्थ 1. पार्थ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृथि), Ved. an epithet of twelve sacred texts, ascribed to Pṛthi Vainya, repeated during the ceremony of unction in the Rāja-sūya sacrifice; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Tānva; (अम्), n., N. of several Sāmans.
29036: पार्थ्य, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic from Pṛthi.
29037: पार्थ 2. पार्थ, अस्, m. (fr. rt. पृथ् for प्रथ् and connected with पृथु, wide), a prince, king (= पार्थिव); (fr. पृथा), a metronymic of Yudhi-ṣṭhira, Bhīma-sena, and Arjuna, especially of the last; N. of a son of Paṅgu and king of Kaśmīra; N. of a man; the plant Terminalia Arjuna; (आस्), m. pl. an epithet of the five sons of Pāṇḍu. —पार्थ-ज, अस्, m. the son of Pārtha. —पार्थ-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city near the con-fluence of the Go-dāvarī and Vi-darbhā. —पार्थ-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of sons of Pṛthā. —पार्थ-सारथि, इस्, m., N. of the author of the Tantra-ratna. —पार्थसारथि-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of a commentator on Jaimini's Nyāya-sūtras. —पार्-थानुग (°थ-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, followed by (Pārtha, i. e.) Arjuna.
29038: पार्थव, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or peculiar to Pṛthu; (अम्), n. width, greatness, immensity.
29039: पार्थवि, an earthy substance, rotten wood; (pro-bably a wrong reading for पार्थिव।)
29040: पार्थिव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृथिवी for पृथ्वी, f. of पृथु), earthen, earthly, terrestrial, relating to the earth, springing or derived from the earth, made of earth, earthy; ruling or possessing the earth; fit for kings or princes, royal, princely; अ-पार्थिव, unearthly, i. e. heavenly, celestial; (अस्), m. a dweller on the earth, inhabitant of the earth; a lord of the earth, king, prince, sovereign, warrior; an earthen vessel; the 19th (or 53rd) year in Jupiter's cycle of 60 years; (आस्), m. pl. a patronymic; (ई), f. ‘earth-born,’ an epithet of Sītā; of Lakṣmī; (अम्), n. an earthy substance; (आनि), n. pl., Ved. the regions of the earth (Sāy. = पृथिव्याम् भवानि स्थानानि). —पार्थिव-ता, f. or पार्थिव-त्व, अम्, n. the dignity or rank of king, royalty. —पार्थिव-नन्-दिनी, f. the daughter of a king. —पार्थिवर्षभ (°व-ऋ°), अस्, m. ‘king-bull,’ an excellent king. —पार्थिव-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, m. best of kings, an excellent sovereign. —पार्थिव-सुता or पार्थिवात्-मजा (°व-आत्°), f. the daughter of a king. —पार्-थिवाधम (°व-अध्°), अस्, m. the lowest or meanest of kings. —पार्थिवेन्द्र (°व-इन्°), अस्, m. the chief or greatest of princes.
29041: पार्थक्य पार्थक्य, अम्, n. (fr. पृथक्), severalty, individuality, separation, separateness, sin-gleness, difference, variety.
29042: पार्थुरश्म पार्थुरश्म, अम्, n. (fr. पृथु-रश्मि), Ved. epithet of various Sāmans.
29043: पार्पर पार्पर, अस्, m. a handful of rice; consumption (= क्षय-रोग); a filament of the Nauclea Cadamba; ashes; = कीनाश; = गदान्तर (a kind of disease ?); a N. of Yama.
29045: पार्यन्तिक पार्यन्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्य्-अन्त), final, concluding, last.
29046: पार्व पार्व, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्वन्), = पार्-वण; (probably an incorrect form.)
29047: पार्वण, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to a division of time or of the month; increasing, waxing full (as the moon); (अस्), m. a kind of deer; the general funeral ceremony to be offered to all the Manes at the Parvan (or conjunction of the sun and moon, at which double oblations are offered, three cakes to the father, paternal grandfather and great-grandfather, and three to the maternal grandfather, his father and grandfather; and the crumbs of each set to the remoter ancestors in each line).
29048: पार्वायनान्तीय, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. पर्वन् + अय-नान्त), occurring at the end of a Parvan or solstice (as a sacrifice &c.).
29049: पार्वत पार्वत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्वत), being or living in the mountains, growing on or coming from the mountains, consisting of moun-tains, mountainous; (अस्), m. the tree Melia Sem-pervirens (= महा-निम्ब); (ई), f. a mountain stream; a female cowherd or Gopī; a N. of Durgā (as being the daughter of Hima-vat the king of the snowy mountains); N. of a cave in mount Meru; of various women (named after the goddess); an epithet of Draupadī (incorrectly for पार्षती); a kind of fragrant earth; a red clay commonly called Saurāṣṭrī or Surat earth; N. of various plants; the olibanum tree, Boswellia Thurifera; Grislea To-mentosa; = Celtis Orientalis; = क्षुद्र-पाषाण-भेदा; = जीवनी। —पार्वती-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. ‘dis-trict of Pārvatī (Durgā),’ N. of one of the four especially sacred districts of Orissa. —पार्वती-नन्-दन, अस्, m. ‘son of Pārvatī,’ an epithet of Kārtti-keya. —पार्वती-पश्चात्ताप-वर्णन, अम्, n., N. of the sixth chapter of the Gīta-gaṅgādhara, a poem by Kalyāṇa. —पार्वती-प्रवर्तन, अम्, n., N. of the ninth chapter of the Gīta-girīśa, a poem by Rāma. —पार्वती-प्रसादन, अम्, n., N. of the fifth chapter of the Gīta-gaṅgādhara. —पार्वती-मोक्षण, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa. —पार्वतीश्वर-लिङ्ग (°ती-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga. —पार्वती-सम्प्रदान, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa.
29050: पार्वतायन, अस्, m. a patronymic; N. of a chamberlain.
29051: पार्वति, इस्, m. a patronymic of Dakṣa.
29052: पार्वतिक, अम्, n. a multitude of mountains, mountain-range.
29053: पार्वतीय, अस्, ई, अम्, living or dwelling in the mountains, mountainous; (अस्), m. a mountaineer; epithet of a particular sovereign ruling in the moun-tains; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a mountain tribe.
29054: पार्वतेय, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to the mountains, mountain-born; (अस्), m., N. of a prince of mountaineers; a species of culinary plant bearing a pungent fruit; (ई), f. the smaller or upper mill-stone; (अम्), n. antimony (= सौवीराञ्जन).
29055: पार्शव 1. पार्शव, अस्, m. (fr. 1. पर्शु), a prince of the Parśus.
29057: पार्श्व, अस्, अम्, m. n. the region of the ribs or the part of the body below the armpit; the side, flank (either of animate or inanimate objects); a side of any square figure; a curved knife (Ved.); (अस्), m., N. of an ancient Buddhist teacher; (with Jainas) N. of the twenty-third Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; (औ), m. du. heaven and earth; (अम्), n. a multitude of ribs, the thorax; the extremity of the fore-axle nearest the wheel to which the outside horses of a four-horse chariot are attached; a fraudu-lent or crooked expedient, dishonourable means; (आनि), n. pl. the ribs (Ved.); (ए), ind. at the side, near, on, upon, (opposed to दूर-तस्, दूरे); aside; (अयोस्), ind. on both sides; (आत्), ind. away from; (अम्), ind. near to, to, towards; (अस्, आ, अम्), near, proximate, by the side of. —पार्श्व-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going at the side (of any one), accompanying, being in close proximity to, an attendant; (आस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्श्व-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, being at the side, attending, accompanying, being close to or beside; sheltered, screening. —पार्श्व-गमन, अम्, n. the act of going by the side, accompanying. —पार्श्व-चर, अस्, m. an attendant; (आस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्श्व-तस्, ind. by or from the side, at the side, near, sideways, aside. —पार्श्व-द, अस्, m. ‘turning the side towards another,’ an attendant; (आस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्श्व-दाह, अस्, m. a burning pain in the side. —पार्श्व-देश, अस्, m. the region of the ribs, the side. —पार्श्व-द्रुम, आस्, m. pl. the trees at the side, the trees on every side. —पार्श्व-नाथ, अस्, m. (with Jainas) N. of an Arhat; the Jaina pontiff. —पार्श्वनाथ-काव्य, अम्, n., N. of a poem by Padma-sundara celebrating the preceding Arhat. —पार्श्व-परिवर्तन, अम्, n. ‘the turning round on the other side or from one side to the other,’ epithet of a festival on the eleventh day of the light half of the month Bhādra (Viṣṇu being sup-posed to turn upon the other side in his sleep on this day). —पार्श्व-परिवर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being or going by the side (of any one). —पार्श्व-पिप्पल, अम्, n. a species of Harītakī (= Hindī गजहड्). —पार्श्व-भाग, अस्, m. ‘side-portion,’ the side, flank (of an elephant). —पार्श्व-रुज्, क्, f. pain in the side. —पार्श्व-वक्त्र, अस्, m. whose face is in his side,’ N. of a being attendant upon Śiva (Hari-vaṃśa 14851). —पार्श्व-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, standing by the side, an attendant; situated at the side, adjacent; (इनस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्-श्व-विवर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being by the side of, living with. —पार्श्व-शय, अस्, आ, अम्, lying or sleeping on the side; sleeping at the side. —पार्श्व-शायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, ‘lying on the side,’ epithet of a particular position of the moon. —पार्श्व-शूल, अस्, m. a shooting pain in the side, spasm of the chest, stitch; pleurisy. —पार्श्व-संस्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, lying on the side. —पार्श्व-सूत्रक, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a kind of ornament. —पार्श्व-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing at the side or next to, being near or close to, adjacent, proximate; (अस्), m. an associate, com-panion; a stage manager's assistant (said to serve as a sort of chorus to the Indian drama, being some-times an actor in the prelude and interpreter of the plot). —पार्श्व-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, standing at the side, being near or close to. —पार्श्वानुचर (°व-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘attending at the side,’ an attendant, body-servant, lackey. —पार्श्वायात (°व-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has approached close to. —पार्श्वा-सन्न (°व-आस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, standing by the side, standing next, present. —पार्श्वासीन (°व-आस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sitting by the side. —पार्श्वास्थि (°व-अस्°), इ, n. ‘side-bone,’ a rib. —पार्श्वैकादशी (°व-एक्°), f., N. of a particular festival (= पार्श्व-परिवर्-तन). —पार्श्वोदर-प्रिय (°व-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘fond of (moving) sideways on the belly,’ a crab.
29058: पार्श्वक, अस्, m. a rib; (अस्, आ, अम्), one who seeks wealth or other objects by dishonest or indirect or side means; a pilferer, swindler.
29059: पार्श्वतीय, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. पार्श्व-तस्), being on or belonging to the side, situated at the side.
29060: पार्श्विक, अस्, ई, अम्, lateral, belonging to the side; (अस्), m. a sidesman, partisan; an associate, companion; a juggler; one who seeks money by dishonest means; N. of an ancient Buddhist teacher.
29061: पार्श्व्य, औ, m. du. heaven and earth (a various reading for पार्श्वौ).
29062: पार्शव 2. पार्शव, अस्, m. a warrior armed with an axe.
29064: पार्षकि पार्षकि, इस्, m. a patronymic.
29065: पार्षत पार्षत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृषत), belonging to the spotted antelope, made of the skin of the spotted antelope; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Dru-pada and his son Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna; (ई), f. a patronymic of Draupadī; an epithet of Durgā (in this sense a wrong reading for पार्वती); N. of two plants, Boswellia Thurifera; = जीवनी।
29066: पार्षद् पार्षद्, त्, f. (for परि-षद?), an assembly; (दस्), m. pl. the attendants or retinue of a god.
29067: पार्षद, अस्, m. (fr. पर्षद्), an associate, companion, attendant; a train, retinue (especially of a god); a person present in a congregation or assembly, a spectator; (perhaps) a councillor, dis-tinguished personage; (अम्), n. a text-book received by any particular grammatical school, a N. given to the Prātiśākhyas; N. of a work on ceremonies. —पार्षद-ता, f. the office of an attendant (espe-cially of the attendant of a deity).
29068: पार्षदीय, अस्, आ, अम्, conformable to the received text-book of any particular grammatical school.
29069: पार्षद्य, अस्, m. = पारिषद्य, a member of an assembly or council, assessor; (आस्), m. pl. the attendants or retinue of a god (especially of Śiva).
29070: पार्षद्वाण पार्षद्वाण, अस्, m. (fr. पृषद्-वाण), N. of a man.
29071: पार्षिका पार्षिका, f., N. of a woman.
29073: पार्ष्टेय पार्ष्टेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृष्टि), being within the ribs.
29074: पार्ष्ठिक पार्ष्ठिक, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. being after the manner of the Pṛṣṭhya (Ṣaḍ-aha).
29075: पार्ष्णि पार्ष्णि, इस्, m. f., rarely पार्ष्णी, f. (said to be fr. rt. पृष्), the heel; the extremity of the fore-axle to which the outside horses of a four-horse chariot are attached (the two inner horses being harnessed to the धुर् or chariot-pole); the rear of an army; the back; a kick; enquiry, asking (?); (इस्), f. a foolish or licentious woman; a N. of Kuntī the wife of Pāṇḍu. —पार्ष्णि-क्षेम, अस्, m., N. of a divinity. —पार्ष्णि-ग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, seizing from behind, threatening from behind; (अस्), m. a follower. —पार्ष्णि-ग्रहण, अम्, n. attacking or threatening (an enemy) in the rear. —पार्ष्णि-ग्राह, अस्, आ, अम्, attacking or menac-ing (an enemy) in the rear; (अस्), m. an enemy in the rear; a commander in the rear of an army; an ally who supports a prince (Manu VII. 207). —पार्ष्णि-त्र, अम्, n. ‘rear-protecting,’ a rear-guard, reserve, a body of forces in the rear. —पार्ष्-णि-वाह्, ट्, ऊही, ट्, or पार्ष्णि-वाह, अस्, आ, अम्, draw-ing (i. e. harnessed to) the extremities of the axle-tree; (अस्), m. an outside horse. —पार्ष्णि-सारथि, इस्, m. a charioteer who drives one of the outside horses; (ई), m. du. the two charioteers who drive the outer horses attached to the extremities of the axle-tree.
29076: पाल् पाल्। See Caus. of rt. 3. पा।
29077: पाल, अस्, m. a guard, guardian, protector, nourisher, keeper; a herdsman; a protector of the earth, a prince; a spitting-pot, spittoon; N. of a Nāga of the race of Vāsuki; of a prince; (ई), f. a herdsman's wife; [cf. पालि।] —पाल-कवि-राज, अस्, m., N. of a poet (also called Śrī-pāla-kavi-rāja). —पाल-काव्य, अम्, n. ‘the poem of Pāla,’ N. of a work. —पाल-घ्न, अस्, m. a mushroom. —पाल-बणिज्, क्, m. = कन्या-पाल; (a wrong form for पान-बणिज्।) —पाली-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a par-ticular religious observance.
29078: पालक, अस्, इका, अम्, guarding, protecting, nourish-ing; (अस्), m. a guardian, protector, cherisher, nourisher; a foster-father; a prince, ruler, sovereign; a horse-keeper, a groom; one who maintains or observes; N. of several princes; a species of plant with a poisonous bulb, Plumbago Zeylanica; a horse. —पालक-गोत्र, अम्, n. the family or tribe of one's adoptive parents. —पालकाख्या (°क-आख्°), f., N. of the mother of Dhanvantari.
29079: पालन, अस्, ई, अम्, the act of protecting, guarding, fostering, nourishing, cherishing; (अम्), n. guarding, providing with a guardian, protecting, protection, preserving, cherishing, fostering, nourishing; main-taining, keeping, observing; the milk of a cow that has recently calved.
29080: पालनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be guarded or protected, to be cherished or nourished; fit to be preserved or maintained; to be observed or respected.
29081: पालयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, guarding, protecting, cherishing.
29082: पालयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, protecting, cherishing; a protector, guardian.
29083: पालित, अस्, आ, अम्, guarded, protected, cherished, nourished; (अस्), m. a species of tree (= शाखोट); N. of a son of Parā-jit (or Parā-vṛt); (आ), f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda.
29084: पालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, protecting, guarding, cherishing, nourishing; (ई), m., N. of a son of Pṛthu.
29085: पाल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be protected or guarded, to be cherished; being under (any one's) protection or guardianship; to be observed or kept, to be main-tained.
29086: पालकाप्य पालकाप्य, अस्, m., N. of an ancient sage or Muni; a form of the divine physician Dhanvantari.
29087: पालक्क पालक्क, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a country.
29088: पालक्या पालक्या, f. the plant Beta Ben-galensis.
29089: पालङ्क पालङ्क, अस्, m. the olibanum tree, Boswellia Thurifera; a species of beet-root, Beta Bengalensis; a hawk; (ई), f. the resin of the olibanum tree, incense.
29090: पालङ्क्य, अस्, आ, m. f. gum olibanum, incense; (अम्, आ), n. f. the plant Beta Bengalensis.
29091: पालङ्गिन् पालङ्गिन्, इनस्, m. pl., N. of a school called after a disciple of Vaiśampāyana.
29092: पालल पालल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पलल), made of powdered sesamum seed.
29093: पालवी पालवी, f. a kind of vessel.
29094: पालहरि पालहरि, इस्, m. (probably a patro-nymic fr. पलहर), N. of a man.
29095: पालागल पालागल, अस्, m., Ved. a runner, messenger; (according to others) a bearer of false tidings; (ई), f. the fourth and least respected wife of a prince.
29096: पालाल पालाल, अस्, ई, अम् (probably incor-rectly for पाल्वल), living in a marsh.
29097: पालाश पालाश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पलाश), com-ing from or belonging to the tree Butea Frondosa, made of the wood of the Butea Frondosa; green; (अस्), m. green (the colour). —पालाश-खण्ड and पालाश-षण्ड, अस्, m. an epithet of Magadha (a country in India, the western part of Behar).
29098: पालि पालि, इस्, f. (fr. Caus. of rt. 3. पा?; said to be fr. rt. पल्), the tip of the ear; an edge, margin; a boundary, limit; the sharp side of any-thing, the sharp edge or point of a sword or any cutting instrument; a line, row, range; a raised bank, dike, causeway, bridge; the lap, bosom; the hip, haunch; a mark, spot, stain; a particular mea-sure of capacity (= प्रस्थ); a louse; a woman with a beard; prescribed food, maintenance of a scholar during the period of his studies by his teacher; praise, eulogium; a circumference; (ई), f. an edge, margin; the sharp edge of a sword; a line, row, range; a woman with a beard; a louse; a pot, boiler; an oblong pond; a causeway, bridge. —पा-लिं-हिर, अस्, m. a kind of snake, (perhaps a wrong reading for पालिं-हर, seizing by the tip of the ear.)
29099: पालिका, f. the tip of the ear; the sharp edge of a cutting instrument; a sort of ladle or knife for skimming milk, curds, &c.; a cheese or butter knife.
29100: पालित्य पालित्य, अम्, n. (fr. पलित), grey-ness (of age), hoariness.
29101: पालिन्द पालिन्द, अस्, m. incense; a species of jasmine, Jasminum Pubescens; (ई), f. a species of creeper, Ichnocarpus Frutescens; = पालिन्धी।
29102: पालिन्धी पालिन्धी, f. a species of Ipomœa with dark blossoms.
29103: पालीवत पालीवत, अस्, m. a species of tree.
29104: पाल्लवा पाल्लवा, f. (fr. पल्लव), scil. क्रीडा, a game played with twigs.
29105: पाल्वल पाल्वल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पल्वल), coming from a tank or pool.
29106: पावक पावक, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. rt. 1. पू), (Ved.) pure, clear, bright, shining; (Sāy.) = शोधक, cleansing, purifying (said of Agni, Āditya, Sūrya, and the Maruts; of water, of the dawn, of day and night, &c.); (अस्), m. epithet of a particular Agni (in the Purāṇas said to be a son of Agni Abhi-mānin and Svāhā or of Antar-dhāna and Śikhaṇḍinī; cf. पव-मान, शुचि); fire in general; Agni or the god of fire; social fire, a fire lighted in common; a fire lighted on taking possession of a house; a species of tree, Premna Integrifolia or Spinosa (see अरणि); a species of plant, Plumbago Zeylanica (= चित्रक); Semecarpus Anacardium; a plant used as a vermifuge, Carthamus Tinctorius (= विडङ्ग); a symbolical expression for the number three (like all other words for ‘fire’); epithet of a kind of Ṛṣi, a saint, a person purified by religious abstraction, one who purifies from sin; (ई), f. the wife of Agni. —पावक-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. ‘having the name Pāvaka,’ an epithet of Agni; containing the word पावक। —पावक-वर्चस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. brightly resplen-dent (as Agni). —पावक-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being of pure or brilliant aspect; (Sāy.) = अग्नि-समान-तेजस्क, resembling the brilliance of fire. —पावक-शोचिस्, इस्, इस्, इस्, (voc. anomalously -चे), Ved. shining brightly. —पावकारणि (°क-अर्°), इस्, m. the tree Premna Integrifolia or Spinosa (see अरणि). —पावकेश्वर (°क-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
29107: पावकि, इस्, m. ‘son of Fire,’ an epithet of Skanda or Kārttikeya; of Su-darśana; of Hari (?).
29108: पावन, अस्, ई, अम्, purifying, purificatory, expur-gatory, freeing from sin, sanctifying; purified, pure, holy; (अस्), m. fire (generally or for various cere-monial purposes); incense; a species of Verbesina with yellow flowers; a kind of demigod otherwise called a Siddha; N. of one of the Viśve Devāḥ; an epithet of the inspired poet Vyāsa; (ई), f. the plant Termi-nalia Chebula; holy basil; a cow; N. of a river; the Ganges or the goddess Gaṅgā; (अम्), n. the act of cleansing, purifying, sanctifying, expiation, puri-fication (by acts of austerity and devotion); a means of purification; penance; water; cow-dung; the seed of the plant Elæocarpus Ganitrus (of which rosaries are made); a species of grass, Costus Speci-osus; a sectarial mark (= चित्रक). —पावन-त्व, अम्, n. the property of cleansing or purifying. —पा-वन-ध्वनि, इस्, m. a conch-shell.
