29183: पिङ्गर, अस्, m., N. of a man.
29184: पिङ्गल, अस्, आ, अम्, reddish-brown, tawny, brown, yellowish; (अस्), m. tawny colour, a dull brown or yellow hue; fire; a monkey; an ichneumon; a small kind of owl; a species of snake; a particular vegetable poison; (with Jainas) N. of a treasure; N. of one of Kuvera's divine treasures; of an attendant of the Sun; the sun (?); an epithet of Śiva or of a kindred being; N. of a Rudra; of a Yakṣa; of an attendant of Śiva; of a Dānava; of a fabulous being in the form of a Nāga (or serpent of the lower regions, the reputed author of the Chaṇḍas or treatise on prosody, regarded as one of the Vedāṅgas, and describing Prākṛt as well as Sanskrit metres; he is identified by some with Patañjali, the author of the celebrated commentary on Pāṇini called the Mahā-bhāṣya; by the Hindūs he is considered as a Muni or inspired and divine personage); N. of various ancient sages; N. of the fifty-first (or twenty-fifth) year in a sixty years' cycle of Jupiter; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a species of bird, a kind of owl; the Śiśu tree, Dalbergia Sissoo; a kind of metal; a particular vessel of the body (the right of three canals running from the os coccygis to the head, which according to the anatomy of the Yoga school of philosophy are the chief passages of breath and air); the female elephant of the South quarter; N. of a courtezan who became remarkable for her piety; of an astrological house or period; heart-pea; (अम्), n. a particular metal (= राज-रीति), brass; yellow orpiment. —पिङ्गल-छन्दो-ग्रन्थ-टीका, f., N. of a commentary by Citra-sena on Piṅgala's Chandaḥ-śāstra. —पिङ्गल-नाग, अस्, m. the serpent-demon Piṅgala. —पिङ्गल-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a commen-tary on Piṅgala's Chandaḥ-śāstra. —पिङ्गल-सार-विकाशिनी, f. ‘explaining the substance of Piṅgala,’ N. of a commentary by Ravi-kara on Piṅgala's Chandaḥ-śāstra. —पिङ्गलाक्ष (°ल-अक्°), अस्, m. ‘tawny-eyed,’ an epithet of Śiva. —पिङ्गला-तन्त्र and पिङ्गलामृत (°ल-अम्°), अम्, n., N. of two Tantras. —पिङ्गलेश्वर (°ल-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga; (ई), f. a form of Dākṣāyaṇī. —पिङ्गलेश्-वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place.
29185: पिङ्गलक, अस्, इका, अम्, (Ved.) reddish-brown, tawny; (अस्), m., N. of a Yakṣa; N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants; (इका), f. a kind of bee; a variety of the owl; a sort of crane; N. of a woman.
29186: पिङ्गलित, अस्, आ, अम्, made reddish-brown, become tawny.
29187: पिङ्गाश, अस्, m. the chief of a community of wild tribes; the head man or proprietor of a village; a kind of fish, Pimelodius Pangasius (= पिङ्गास्य); (ई), f. the indigo plant; (अम्), n. virgin gold.
29188: पिञ्ज, अस्, आ, अम्, confused, confounded, disturbed in mind; (अस्), m. the moon; a species of camphor; killing, slaughter; (आ), f. hurting, injuring, injury; turmeric; cotton; a species of tree resembling the vine-palm; a switch; (अम्), n. strength, power.
29189: पिञ्जट, अस्, m. the concrete rheum of the eyes.
29190: पिञ्जन, अम्, n. a bow or bow-shaped instrument used for cleaning cotton.
29191: पिञ्जर, अस्, आ, अम्, reddish-yellow, yellow or tawny, of the colour of gold; (अस्), m. tawny-brown or reddish-yellow colour, a mixture of red and yellow; a horse (probably a bay or chesnut); N. of a mountain; (अम्), n. gold; yellow orpiment; the flower of Mesua Roxburghii; a cage; the ribs or the cavity formed by them, the thorax; a skeleton; [cf. पञ्जर।] —पिञ्जर-ता, f. yellowish-red (the colour).
29192: पिञ्जरक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. orpiment.
29193: पिञ्जरित, अस्, आ, अम्, coloured reddish-yellow.
29194: पिञ्जल, अस्, आ, अम्, extremely perplexed or con-founded, disturbed, overcome with terror or grief; panic-struck, being in great disorder; (आ), f., N. of a river; (ई), f. two blades of Kuśa grass serving as an implement to hold certain articles at a sacrifice; (अम्), n. the leaf of the Kuśa grass; the plant Cur-cuma Zerumbet (हरिद्राभ); yellow orpiment.
29195: पिञ्जलक, अस्, आ, अम्, in उत्-पिञ्जलक, extremely confounded or disturbed, being in great disorder.
29197: पिञ्जिका, f. a roll of cotton from which threads are spun.
29198: पिञ्जूल, अम्, n., Ved. a bundle of stalks, a bundle of grass, &c.; the wick of a lamp; (sometimes spelt पिञ्जुल।)
29199: पिञ्जूलक, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants.
29200: पिञ्जूष, अस्, m. the wax of the ear (= पेञ्जूष).
29201: पिञ्जेट, अस्, m. the excretion or concrete rheum of the eyes; [cf. पिञ्जट।]
29202: पिञ्जोला पिञ्जोला, f. the noise or rustling of leaves.
29203: पिट् पिट्, cl. 1. P. पेटति, पेटितुम्, to sound; to assemble or heap together.
29204: पिट, अस्, m. a basket for holding grain, a sort of cupboard or granary made of bamboos or canes; a basket, box; (अम्), n. a house, a hovel; a roof.
29205: पिटक, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (usually n.), a basket, box; a large basket or receptacle of basket-work for keeping grain &c., a granary; a collection of writings [cf. त्रि-प्°]; a boil, blister, ulcer; a kind of orna-ment on Indra's banner; (अस्), m., N. of a man.
29206: पिटक्या, f. a multitude of baskets.
29207: पिटाक, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 49; (अस्), m., N. of a man; N. of a sage.
29208: पिटङ्काकी पिटङ्काकी or पिटङ्कोकी, f. the plant Cucumis Colocynthis.
29209: पिटङ्काश पिटङ्काश, अस्, m. a kind of fish, a species of pike, Esax Scolopax, Silurus Pabda.
29210: पिट्टक पिट्टक, अम्, n. the tartar or excre-tion of the teeth; [cf. किट्ट, किट्टक, पिप्पिका।]
29211: पिट्टय पिट्टय (fr. पिट्ट = पिष्ट?), Nom. P. पिट्टयति, -यितुम्, Ved. to stamp or press into a solid mass.
29212: पिट्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, stamped into a solid mass, pressed flat.
29213: पिठ् पिठ्, cl. 1. P. पेठति, पेठितुम्, to injure, hurt, kill; to feel pain or affliction.
29215: पिठर, अस्, ई, अम्, m. f. n. a pot, pan; (अस्), m. an addition to a building shaped like a hollow vessel, a hut made of bamboos and mats, or accord-ing to some a kind of store-room or scullery; N. of a particular Agni; N. of a Dānava; (अम्), n. a churning-stick; the root of Cyperus Rotundus.
29216: पिठरक, अस्, m. (?), a pot, pan; N. of a Nāga. —पिठरक-कपाल, अस्, अम्, m. n. a fragment of a pot, potsherd.
29217: पिठीनस् पिठीनस्, आस्, m., N. of a man.
29218: पिडक पिडक, अस्, m. or पिडका, f. a small boil, pimple, papula, pustule. —पिडका-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having boils, pimples, &c.
29219: पिडकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having boils, &c.
29220: पिण्ड् पिण्ड् (probably akin to rt. पिष्; considered by some as a Nom. fr. पिण्ड below), cl. 1. A., 10. P. पिण्डते, पिण्डितुम्, पिण्-डयति, -यितुम्, to roll into a lump or ball, to put together, join, unite; to accumulate; to assemble.
29221: पिण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. (in most senses usually m.), a round mass, ball, globe, lump, knob, clod (e. g. अयः-पिण्ड, a ball or lump of iron; अग्नि-पिण्डौ, the knobs at the end of a pair of tongs; cf. नेत्र-प्°, मृत्-प्°); a roundish lump of food, a bite, morsel, mouthful; a cake or ball of meal offered to the Manes, a ball or lump of meat or rice mixed up with milk, curds, flowers, &c., and offered at the several Śrāddhas to the Manes by the nearest surviving relations (= नि-वाप); food; sustenance, means of living, livelihood, subsistence [cf. पर-पिण्डाद]; alms; flesh, meat; the embryo or fetus in an early stage of gestation; the body; the projection of an elephant's frontal sinus; a round button; anything roundish, thick, gross, or solid; thickness (one of the three dimensions in geometry); a heap, cluster, quantity, collection; an object; a particular part of a house; a sort of portico or shed in front of the door; myrrh, incense, frankincense; the side imme-diately below the armpit (?); Vangueria Spinosa; the flower of the China rose; (in arithmetic) sum, total amount; (in astronomy) a sine expressed in numbers [cf. ज्या-प्°]; the twenty-fourth part of the quadrant of a circle, or 3° 45; N. of a man; (औ), m. du. the fleshy parts of the shoulder situated above the collar-bone; (अम्), n. power, might; an army; iron; fresh butter; (ई), f. a round mass, &c. (= पिण्ड, m.); a long gourd, Cucurbita Lagenaria (= अ-लाबु); a species of date tree; the flowering shrub Tabernæ-montana Coronaria (= तगर); the plant Jonesia Aśoka; a species of palm, Phœnix Dactylifera; the nave of a wheel; performance of certain gesticulations during the silent repetition of prayers while medi-tating on real or divine knowledge; a house; N. of a woman. —पिण्ड-कन्द, अस्, m. a species of bulbous plant (= पिण्डालु). —पिण्ड-खर्जूर, अस्, m. or पिण्ड-खर्जूरिका or पिण्ड-खर्जूरी, f. a species of date tree. —पिण्ड-गोस, अस्, m. gum myrrh. —पिण्ड-तर्कुक, आस्, m. pl., Ved. the ancestors preceding the great-grandfather (who eat the remnants of the oblations made to the Manes). —पिण्ड-तस्, ind. from a ball or lump. —पिण्ड-तैल, अम्, n. or पिण्ड-तैलक, अस्, m. incense, olibanum. —पिण्ड-त्व, अम्, n. the being a lump or ball; पिण्डत्वं गम्, to attain the condition of a lump. —पिण्ड-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving or qualified to give the funeral cake to deceased ancestors; supplying with bread or with the means of subsistence; (अस्), m. the nearest male relation who offers the funeral cake; a patron, master. —पिण्ड-दातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who gives or is qualified to give the funeral cake to deceased ancestors. —पिण्ड-दान, अम्, n. offering a cake of meal (especially in the oblation to the Manes); presentation of the obsequial cake; the funeral oblation made to deceased ancestors on the evening of new moon. —पिण्ड-निर्वपण, अम्, n. presenting obsequial cakes to the Manes, the sacrifice to the Manes. —पिण्ड-पद, अम्, n. a kind of arithmetical calculation. —पिण्ड-पात, अस्, m. giving alms. —पिण्डपातिक, अस्, m. one who lives on alms. —पिण्ड-पात्र, अम्, n. the vessel in which the obsequial cakes are offered to the Manes; alms (lit. an alms-dish). —पिण्ड-पाद or पिण्ड-पाद्य, अस्, m. ‘thick-footed,’ an elephant. —पिण्ड-पितृ-यज्ञ, अम्, n., Ved. the oblation of obsequial cakes to deceased ancestors on the evening of new moon. —पिण्ड-पुष्प, अस्, m. the tree Jonesia Aśoka; the China rose; the pomegranate tree; (अम्), n. the blossom of the Aśoka tree; the flower of the China rose; a lotus; the flower of the plant Tabernæmontana Coronaria. —पिण्डपुष्पक, अस्, m. a kind of vegetable, Chenopodium Album. —पिण्ड-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, bearing (long) round fruits; (आ), f. a bitter gourd. —पिण्ड-बीज or पिण्ड-वीज, अस्, m. a flowering shrub, Nerium (or Oleander) Odorum. —पिण्डबीजक, अस्, m. Pterospermum Acerifolium (= कर्णिकार). —पिण्ड-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, partaking of a funeral oblation, entitled to a share in the funeral cake, eating or receiving the cakes offered at a funeral ceremony; (जस्), m. pl. de-ceased ancestors, the Manes. —पिण्ड-भृति, इस्, f. means of subsistence, livelihood. —पिण्ड-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of a lump (of clay). —पिण्ड-मात्रोपजीविन् (°र-उप्°), ई, इनी, इ, subsisting on a mere morsel. —पिण्ड-मुस्ता, f. a species of grass, Cyperus Pertenuis. —पिण्ड-मूल or पिण्ड-मू-लक, अम्, n. a carrot, Daucus Carota (= गर्जर)। —पिण्ड-यज्ञ, अस्, m. the oblation of obsequial cakes to deceased ancestors. —पिण्ड-लेप, अस्, m. the particles or fragments of the obsequial cakes which cling to the hands, (these are offered to the three ancestors preceding the great-grandfather.) —पिण्ड-लोप, अस्, m. an interruption in offering the funeral cake; a neglect of the solemn obsequies in honour of deceased ancestors. —पिण्ड-वत्, ind. like a lump or ball. —पिण्ड-सम्बन्ध, अस्, m. relationship between a living person and one deceased sufficiently near to qualify the former to offer the obsequial cake to the latter; [cf. स-पिण्ड।] —पिण्ड-सम्बन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, qualified by near relationship to a living person to receive the obsequial cake from him at the oblation to the Manes. —पिण्ड-सेक्तृ, ता, m., N. of a Nāga. —पिण्ड-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘mingled in a lump,’ mixed or intermingled together. —पिण्डान्वाहार्य (°ड-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, to be eaten after the funeral cake has been offered (Manu III. 123). —पिण्डान्वाहार्यक, अम्, n. (with श्राद्ध) a meal in honour of the Manes after offering the funeral cakes. —पिण्डाभ्र (°ड-अभ्°), अम्, n. hail. —पिण्डायस (°ड-अय्°), अम्, n. steel. —पिण्डालु (°ड-आलु), उस्, m., N. of two bulbous plants; = कन्द-गुडूची; an esculent medicinal root described as sweet, cooling, and diuretic (= Hindī peḍālu Bengālī cuvaḍiālu; in this sense also पिण्डालुक, अम्, n.). —पिण्डाश or पिण्डाशक (°ड-आश्°), or पिण्डाशन (°ड-अश्°), अस्, or पिण्डाशिन् (°ड-आश्°), ई, m. ‘eating morsels,’ a beg-gar. —पिण्डाह्वा (°ड-आह्°), f. the resin of Gardenia Gummifera (= नाडी-हिङ्गु). —पिण्डी-खण्ड, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a small wood of Tabernæmontana Coronaria trees (or of Aśoka trees). —पिण्डी-जङ्घ, अस्, m., N. of a man or of his descendants. —पिण्डी-तगर, अस्, m. a species of Tabernæmontana Coro-naria (= कफ-वर्धन). —पिण्डीतगरक, अस्, m. Tabernæmontana Coronaria. —पिण्डी-तरु, उस्, m. a species of tree (= महा-प्°). —पिण्डी-पुष्प, अम्, n. Jonesia Aśoka. —पिण्डी-लेप, अस्, m. a kind of unguent. —पिण्डी-शूर, अस्, m. ‘a cake-hero,’ a cowardly boaster, cotquean, braggart. —पिण्डोदक-क्रिया (°ड-उद्°), f. an oblation of obsequial cakes and water. —पिण्डोद्धरण (°ड-उद्°), अम्, n. participating in funeral offerings, presenting them to common ancestors. —पिण्डोपनिषद् (°ड-उप्°), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
29222: पिण्डक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a lump, lump of food; a round swelling or protuberance [cf. मस्तक-प्°]; the calf of the leg; incense, myrrh; a species of bulbous plant (= पिण्डालु); a carrot, Daucus Carota; (in astronomy) a sine expressed in numbers; (अस्), m. a Piśāca, goblin, demon; (इका), f. a globular swelling or protuberance, a fleshy swelling (in the shoulders, arms, legs, &c.), a wen (?); the calf of the leg; the instep; the nave of a wheel; a stool or seat of various shapes and dimensions; a base or pedestal for the image of a deity or for a Liṅga (Ved.); a kind of shrub (= श्वेताम्लि).
29223: पिण्डन, अम्, n. forming globes, taking a globular form (as water); (अस्), m. a mound or bank.
29224: पिण्डरक, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), a bridge.

29226: पिण्डस, अस्, m. a beggar, mendicant living upon alms; [cf. पिण्डाश under पिण्ड।]
29228: पिण्डार, अस्, m. a beggar, religious mendicant; a buffalo-herdsman, neatherd, cowherd; a species of tree, Flacourtia Sapida; Trewia Nudiflora; an expression of censure; N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. a kind of vegetable (= Hindī पिण्डारा).
29229: पिण्डारक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; N. of a Vṛṣṇi; of a son of Vasu-deva and Rohiṇī; of a river considered holy by the Hindūs; (अम्), n., N. of a place of pilgrimage in Guzerat. —पिण्डारक-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place.
29230: पिण्डि, इस्, f. the nave of a wheel (= पिण्डी, पिण्डिका).
29231: पिण्डिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having large calves (?). See पिण्डिका under पिण्डक, col. 2.
29232: पिण्डित, अस्, आ, अम्, rolled into a ball or lump, pressed into a solid mass; thick, massy, lumpish; formed into a mass, heaped together, collected; mixed, intermingled with; united; added, multiplied; counted, numbered; (अस्), m. incense.

29234: पिण्डिल, अस्, आ, अम्, having large calves (= स्थूल-जङ्घ); skilled in calculations; (अस्), m. a skilful calculator or arithmetician, a calculator of nati-vities, astrologer, astronomer; a bridge, mound, balk, causeway; (आ), f. a species of cucumber, Cucumis Maderaspatanus (= गोडुम्बा).
29235: पिण्डी-कृ, cl. 8. P. 29238: पिण्डीर, अस्, आ, अम्, sapless, juiceless, arid, dry; (अस्), m. the pomegranate tree [cf. कृष्ण-प्°]; cuttle-fish bone; sea foam.
29239: पिण्डोल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
29240: पिण्डोलि, इस्, f. leavings of a meal, fragments dropped from the mouth, orts.
29241: पिण्डिपाल पिण्डिपाल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a weapon with a single point; [cf. भिन्दि-पाल।]
29242: पिण्या पिण्या, f. heart-pea, Cardiosper-mum Halicacabum (= पण्या).
29243: पिण्याक पिण्याक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. पिष्), the residue of seeds which have been ground for oil; oil-cake; incense; saffron; Asa Fœtida; (आ), f. a species of plant.
29245: पितु पितु, उस्, m., Ved. (fr. rt. प्यै), juice, drink; nourishment; (Sāy.) = पालकम् अन्-नम्, nourishing food. —पितु-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. bestowing or providing food. —पितु-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. enjoying or partaking of food; (Sāy.) = अन्-नार्थिन्, seeking or earning food. —पितु-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. bringing food. —पितु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. accompanied by food, abounding in food, nou-rishing. —पितु-षणि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. bestowing or granting food. —पितु-स्तोम, अस्, m. ‘praise of food,’ N. of the hymn Ṛg-veda I. 187.
29246: पितूय, Nom. P. पितूयति, -यितुम्, Ved. to long for food, desire food.
29247: पितृ पितृ, ता, m. (fr. rt. 3. पा), a father; (in the Veda पितृ is an epithet of Bṛhas-pati, Varuṇa, Prajā-pati, and especially of heaven or the sky; अन्तरा पितरम् मातरञ्-च, between heaven and earth; according to Sāy. पितृ = पालक, a protector); (तरौ), m. du. father and mother, parents, (in the Veda an epithet of the Araṇis or two pieces of wood regarded as the parents of Fire, and of heaven and earth regarded as the parents of all beings); (तरस्), m. pl. fathers, forefathers, ancestors; a father and his brothers, father and uncles, paternal ancestors; the spirits of departed an-cestors, the Manes or spirits of the dead (they are of two kinds, viz. either the spirits of the father, grand-fathers, and great-grandfathers of an individual or the progenitors of mankind generally, to both classes of whom Śrāddhas or obsequial worship is paid and oblations of food called Piṇḍas presented; they in-habit a peculiar region, which, according to some, is the Bhuvas or region of the air, according to others, the orbit of the moon, and are considered as the regents of the Nakṣatras Maghā and Mūla); [cf. Zend pita, base pa-tar: Gr. πα-τήρ, πάτρω-ς: Lat. pa-ter, Jup-piter: Goth. fa-dar: Old Germ. fa-tar, fa-ter, ‘father;’ fataro, ‘uncle:’ Angl. Sax. faeder, ‘father;’ fadhu, ‘aunt, father's sister:’ Hib. athair, ‘father,’ for pathair.], —पितरि-शूर, अस्, m. ‘a hero against his father,’ a cowardly boaster. —पिता-पुत्र, औ, m. du. father and son. —पितापुत्र-विरोध, अस्, m. a contest between father and son. —पितापुत्र-समागम, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist Sūtra. —पितापुत्रीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to father and son; containing the words पितृ and पुत्र; (with सम्प्रदान) the transmission (of bodily capacities and powers) from father to son. —पिता-मह, अस्, m. a paternal grandfather; a N. of Brahmā the great father of all; N. of the author of a Dharma-śāstra; of the author of an astronomical work; (आस्), m. pl. the ancestors, Manes; (ई), f. a paternal grandmother. —पितामह-सरस्, अस्, n. or पितामहस्य सरस्, N. of a place of pilgrimage. —पिता-सुमति-संवाद, अस्, m., N. of a part of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa. —पितुः-पुत्र, अस्, m. a father's son. —पितुः-ष्वसृ or पितुः-स्वसृ, सा, f. a father's sister. —पितृ-कर्मन्, अ, or पितृ-कार्य, अम्, n. obsequial rites, sacrifice offered to deceased ancestors. —पितृ-कल्प, अस्, m. (perhaps) legends relating to ancestors; N. of a long period of time, Brahmā's day of new moon. —पितृ-कानन, अम्, n. ‘grove of ancestors,’ a cemetery. —पितृ-कुल्या, f. ‘rivulet of the Pitṛs,’ N. of a river rising in the Malaya mountains. —पितृ-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. committed against parents or an-cestors (as sin). —पितृ-कृत्य, अम्, n. or पितृ-क्रिया, f. obsequial rites, oblations offered to the spirits of deceased ancestors. —पितृ-गण, अस्, m. the whole body of ancestors collectively, a group or class of Manes or deceased progenitors who were sons of the Ṛṣis or Prajā-patis, (the principal classes, according to Manu III. 194-199, are the Soma-sads, descended from Vi-rāj, the Agni-ṣvāttas from Marīci, Barhi-shads from Atri, Soma-pās from Bhṛgu, Haviṣ-mats from Aṅgiras, Ājya-pas from Pulastya, and Su-kālins from Vasiṣṭha; there are also the Agni-dagdhas and An-agnidagdhas, Kāvyas and Saumyas.) —पितृ-गणा, f. an epithet of Durgā. —पितृ-गाथा, आस्, f. pl. ‘songs of the ancestors,’ an epithet of particular songs. —पितृ-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, be-longing or pertaining to a father. —पितृ-गृणा, f. probably a wrong reading for पितृ-गणा, q. v. —पितृ-गृह, अम्, n. a father's house, paternal mansion; ‘house of ancestors,’ a burial ground, ceme-tery. —पितृ-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘the genius of the Manes,’ N. of a demon causing disease. —पितृ-घातक, अस्, or पितृ-घातिन्, ई, m. ‘slaying a father,’ a parricide. —पितृ-चेट, अस्, m., N. of a man. —पितृ-तम, अस्, m., Ved., in पितृतमः पित्रीणां, best of the ancestors (Sāy. = पाल-कानाम् मध्ये अतिशयेन पालकः, a defender in the highest degree among defenders). —पितृ-तर्-पण, अम्, n. ‘refreshing the Manes,’ gifts in honour of deceased progenitors, distributed at the Śrāddhas or funeral ceremonies; an oblation to the Manes; the act of throwing water out of the right hand at seasons of ablution as an offering to the Manes or deceased ancestors in general; the part of the hand between the thumb and fore-finger sacred to the Manes; sesamum (= तिल). —पितृ-तस्, ind., Ved. from the father, on the father's side. —पितृ-तिथि, इस्, f. day of new moon, a day sacred to the Manes of either deceased parent, the day appointed for obsequial rites to deceased ancestors. —पितृ-तीर्थ, अम्, n. ‘the place of pilgrimage for proge-nitors,’ epithet of the city called Gayā (where the performance of funeral sacrifices is peculiarly meri-torious and efficacious); the part of the hand be-tween the fore-finger and thumb sacred to the Manes. —पितृतीर्थ-माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —पितृ-त्व, अम्, n. fatherhood, paternity; the state or condition of a Pitṛ or deified progenitor. —पितृ-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, given by a father (a term applied to a woman's peculiar property); (अस्), m., N. of a man. —पितृ-दयिता, f., N. of a work. —पितृ-दान or पितृ-दानक, अम्, n. a gift in honour of deceased an-cestors, an offering to the Manes. —पितृ-दाय, अस्, m. property inherited from a father, patrimony. —पितृ-देव, आस्, m. pl. the Manes and the gods; the divine Manes; (अस्, आ, अम्), worshipping a father; relating to the worship of the Manes or deceased ancestors. —पितृ-देवत or पितृ-देवत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the Manes for deities, sacred to the Manes. —पितृ-दैवत, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the worship of the Manes; governed or presided over by the Manes; (अम्), n. epithet of the tenth lunar asterism or Maghā. —पितृ-दैवत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the worship of the Manes; (अम्), n., N. of a sacrifice offered to the Manes on the day called Aṣṭakā. —पितृ-द्रव्य, अम्, n. ‘father's substance,’ patrimony. —पितृ-नामन्, आ, म्नी, अ, called after the father's name; [cf. मातृ-नामन्।] —पितृ-पक्ष, अस्, m. paternal side, paternal relationship; the half month of the Manes, N. of the dark half in the Gauṇa Āśvina, so termed as peculiarly appointed for the celebration of obse-quial rites to the Pitṛs or Manes; a father's relations, relatives by the father's side; (अस्, आ, अम्), being on the father's side. —पितृ-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of the Manes,’ an epithet of Yama, regent of the dead; (अयस्), m. pl. the Manes and the lords of creatures (Prajā-patis). —पितृ-पद, अम्, n. the world or state of the Manes. —पितृ-पात्र, अम्, n. a cup or other vessel used at obsequial rites. —पितृ-पितृ, ता, m. a father's father, paternal grandfather. —पितृ-पीत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. drunk by ancestors or deceased progenitors. —पितृ-पूजन, अम्, n. worship of the Manes. —पितृ-पैतामह, अस्, ई, अम्, inherited or derived from father and grandfather; (आस्), m. pl. fathers and grandfathers, ancestors. —पितृपैता-महिक, अस्, ई, अम्, inherited or derived from father and grandfather. —पितृ-प्रसू, ऊस्, f. a father's mother; ‘mother of the Manes,’ twilight (the time when the Manes of departed ancestors are abroad). —पितृ-प्राप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, received from a father; inherited patrimonially. —पितृ-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to the Pitṛs,’ a species of plant (= भृङ्ग-राज). —पितृ-बन्धु, उस्, m. a kinsman by the father's side, as the son of the paternal grandfather's sister, of the paternal grandmother's sister, and of the father's maternal uncle; (उ), n. relationship by the father's side. —पितृ-बान्धव, अस्, m. a kins-man in the paternal line. —पितृ-भक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, dutifully attached to a father. —पितृ-भक्ति, इस्, f. filial duty to a father. —पितृभक्ति-तरङ्-गिणी, f., N. of a work. —पितृ-भूति, इस्, m., N. of a commentator on Kātyāyana's Śrauta-sūtras. —पितृ-भोजन, अम्, n. a father's food; food offered to the Manes; (अस्, अम्), m. n. the plant Phaseolus Radi-atus (a species of pulse = माष). —पितृ-भ्रातृ, ता, m. a father's brother, paternal uncle. —पितृ-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a father, having an illus-trious father; accompanied by the Manes, connected with the Manes (as Soma or Yama); mentioning the Manes or deceased ancestors. —पितृ-मन्दिर, अम्, n. a father's house, paternal mansion; ‘dwelling-place of ancestors,’ a cemetery. —पितृ-मातृ-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of father and mother, orphan. —पितृ-मेध or पितृ-यज्ञ, अस्, m. sacrifice offered to the Manes, obsequial offerings. —पितृ-याण, Ved. or पितृ-यान, अस्, आ, अम्, trodden by the Manes; (अम्), n. the path trodden by the Manes, the way leading to the Manes; the vehicle of the Manes, a car to convey holy persons after their decease to heaven. —पितृ-राज्, ट्, or पितृ-राज, अस्, or पितृ-राजन्, आ, m. ‘king of the Manes,’ an epithet of Yama. —पितृ-रूप, अस्, m., N. of a Rudra. —पितृ-लोक, अस्, m. a father's house, paternal mansion; the world or sphere of the Manes (to which various situations are ascribed, but principally the Bhuvas region or mid-heaven). —पितृ-वंश, अस्, m. the paternal family. —१। पितृ-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a father, whose father is living. —२। पितृ-वत्, ind. like a father; like the Manes; as if for the Manes; as in the sacrifice offered to the Manes. —पि-तृ-वन, अम्, n. ‘grove of ancestors,’ a cemetery, a place where dead bodies are burnt or buried. —पि-तृवने-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, haunting a cemetery; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; a goblin. —पितृ-वर्तिन्, ई, m. ‘staying or abiding with ancestors,’ N. of a Brāhman (= king Brahma-datta). —पितृ-वसति, इस्, f. ‘abode of departed ancestors,’ a cemetery. —पितृ-वाक्-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, attentive to the voice of parents, obedient to parents. —पितृ-वित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. acquired by ancestors; (Sāy.) = पितुः सकाशाल् लब्ध, derived from a father, patrimonial. —पितृ-व्रत, अस्, m. a worshipper of the Manes; (अम्), n. worship of ancestors, obsequial rites. —पितृ-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a Dānava. —पितृ-श्रवण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. bringing honour to a father; (Sāy. = पिता प्रख्यायते येन पु-त्रेण तादृशः।) —पितृ-श्राद्ध, अम्, n. a funeral ceremony or obsequial rites in honour of a father or deceased ancestor. —पितृ-षद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. living unmarried with a father or with parents; ‘dwelling with the Manes,’ an epithet of Rudra. —पितृ-षदन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. inhabited by the Manes. —पितृ-ष्वसृ, सा, f. a father's sister, paternal aunt (= पितुः-ष्वसृ). —पितृ-ष्वस्रीय, अस्, आ, m. f. a father's sister's son or daughter, a paternal aunt's son or daughter. —पितृ-सन्निभ, अस्, आ, अम्, like a father, fatherly, paternal. —पितृ-सामान्य, अम्, n. ancestors collectively. —पितृ-सू, ऊस्, f. a father's mother; ‘mother of the Manes,’ twilight; [cf. पितृ-प्रसू।] —पितृ-सूक्त, अम्, n., N. of a Vedic hymn. —पितृ-स्थान, अस्, m. a guardian; (अम्), n. the sphere of the Manes. —पितृस्थानीय, अस्, m. a guardian (who takes the place of a parent). —पितृ-स्वसृ, सा, f. an incorrect form for पितृ-ष्वसृ। —पितृस्वस्रीय, अस्, आ, m. f., see पितृष्वस्रीय। —पितृ-हत्या, f. the murder of a father, parricide. —पितृ-हन्, आ, m. a parricide. —पितृ-हू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, invoking or dedicated to the Pitṛs; (ऊस्), f., scil. द्वार्, N. of the southern aper-ture of the human body, i. e. of the right ear; [cf. देव-हू।] —पितृ-हूय, अम्, n., Ved. invoking or summoning deceased ancestors. —पित्रर्जित (°तृ-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, derived from a father; property originally acquired by a father. —पित्रर्थम् (°तृ-अर्°), ind. for a father's sake.
29248: पितृक, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) paternal, parental, ancestral, relating or belonging to parents or progenitors, obsequial.
29249: पितृव्य, अस्, m. a father's brother, paternal uncle; any elderly male relation; [cf. Gr. πάτρω-ς; Lat. patruus.]
29250: पित्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, derived from a father, relating to a father, paternal, patrimonial, ancestral, belonging to a father or to progenitors, usual or customary with a father; relating to deceased ancestors, consecrated to the Manes, referring or devoted to the Manes, obsequial; in Manu II. 59. पित्र्यं तीर्थम् = the part of the hand sacred to deified progenitors, i. e. the part between the fore-finger and thumb; (अस्), m. the eldest brother (who takes the place of a father); the month Māgha; (आ), f. the Nakṣatra Maghā (presided over by the Manes); the day of full moon, the worship of the Manes on the day of full moon; (अम्), n., scil. कर्म, the worship of the Manes; the Nakṣatra Maghā; the part of the hand between the fore-finger and thumb. —पित्र्या-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. (perhaps) possess-ing property inherited from a father; (Sāy.) = पितृ-मत्, q. v.
29251: पित्त पित्त, अम्, n. (etymology doubtful), bile, the bilious humor, one of the three humors of the body (the other two being वात and कफ; it is especially secreted between the stomach and bowels, and thence flows through the liver, and distributes itself in the spleen, heart, eyes, and skin; its chief quality is heat); [cf. कूर्म-प्°, गो-प्°, रक्त-प्°, पैत्तिक।] —पित्त-कोष, अस्, m. the gall-bladder. —पित्त-क्षोभ, अस्, m. excess and disturbance of the bilious humor. —पित्त-गदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering from bilious complaints, bilious. —पित्त-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-destroying,’ anti-bilious; (अम्), n. an antidote to bilious com-plaints; ghee ?; (ई), f. a plant, Cocculus Cordifolius. —पित्त-ज्वर, अस्, m. bilious fever. —पित्त-द्रा-विन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘bile-dispersing,’ removing bile; (ई), m. the sweet citron (= मधुर-जम्बीर). —पित्त-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, containing bile, bilious. —पित्त-निवर्हण, अस्, आ, अम्, destroying bile. —पित्त-प्रकृति, इस्, इस्, इ, being of a bilious temperament. —पित्त-प्रकोप, अस्, m. excess and vitiation of the bilious humor. —पित्त-रक्त, अम्, n. plethora; [cf. रक्त-पित्त।] —पित्त-रोगिन्, ई, इणी, इ, suffering from bilious complaints, bilious. —पित्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having bile, bilious. —पित्त-वायु, उस्, m. flatulence arising from excess and vitiation of the bilious humor. —पित्त-विदग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, burnt up by bile, impaired or destroyed by bile. —पित्त-विनाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-destroying,’ antibilious. —पित्त-शमन, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-alleviating,’ antibilious. —पित्त-स्यन्द, अस्, m. a bilious form of ophthalmia; [cf. पित्ताभिष्यन्द।] —पित्त-हर, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-removing,’ antibilious. —पित्-तातीसार (°त-अत्°), अस्, m. ‘bile-dysentery,’ a bilious form of diarrhœa. —पित्तातीसारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, suffering from a bilious form of dysentery. —पित्ताभिष्यन्द (°त-अभ्°), अस्, m. a bilious form of ophthalmia; [cf. पित्त-स्यन्द।] —पित्तारि (°त-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of bile,’ i. e. anything antibilious; N. of various plants and vegetable substances used to coun-teract biliousness (= पर्पट, लाक्षा, and वर्वर). —पित्तोपहत (°त-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, impaired or destroyed by bile.
29252: पित्तल, अस्, आ, अम्, bilious, relating to the bilious humor, secreting bile; (आ), f. the plant Jussiæa Repens; (ई), f., N. of a plant, = मूर्वा; (अम्), n. brass, bell-metal; a species of birch tree (the bark of which is used for writing upon; cf. भूर्ज-पत्त्र).
29253: पित्थ पित्थ, अस्, m., N. of a man.
29254: पित्सत् पित्सत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. Desid. of rt. 2. पत्), being about to fly or fall, habitually falling or coming down; (अन्), m. a bird; [cf. Gr. ψίττακος; Lat. psittacus.]
29255: पित्सल, अम्, n. a road, path, way.
29256: पित्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, being about to fly or fall.
29257: पिपतिषत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, about to fly or fall, inclined or addicted to falling repeatedly; (अन्), m. a bird.
29258: पिपतिषा, f. wish or inclination to come down or fall.
29259: पिपतिषु, उस्, उस्, उ, being about to fall; (उस्), m. a bird.
29260: पिद्व पिद्व, अस्, m., Ved. a species of animal.
29262: पि-दधत्, अत्, अती, अत्, covering, veiling, hiding.
29263: पि-धातव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be covered or hidden; to be stopped up, to be shut or closed.
29264: पि-धान, अम्, n. covering, stopping up, shut-ting; (अस् or अम्), m. or n. (?), a covering, cover, concealment; a lid, top, cover; a sheath; a wrap-per, cloak; [cf. Cambro-Brit. fedon, ‘a screen.’] —पिधान-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, provided with a cover, covered with a lid.
29265: पिधानक, अस्, m. a cover, lid; a sheath, scab-bard [cf. खड्ग-प्°].
29267: पि-धायक, अस्, इका, अम्, covering, hiding, con-cealing. —पिधायक-ता, f. the state or act of covering.
29268: पि-हित, अस्, आ, अम्, shut, covered, hidden, con-cealed; filled with; (अम्), n. a particular figure of speech, showing any person by insinuation that one knows his secrets.
29269: पिनस पिनस, अस्, m. = पीनस, q. v.
29271: पि-नद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, tied on, put on, fastened, bound; dressed, accoutred; wrapped, covered, con-cealed; pierced, penetrated.
29272: पिनद्धक, अस्, इका, अम्, dressed, clothed, covered.
29273: पि-नह्य, ind. having put on or dressed.
29274: पिनाक पिनाक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. 3. पा), a staff, stick; a bow; the club or bow of Rudra-Śiva; a trident or three-pronged spear; the trident of Śiva; a shower or fall of dust, falling dust; (अस्), m., N. of a man; (ई), f. a kind of stringed instrument, a sort of violin. —पिनाक-गोप्तृ, ता, m. ‘preserver of the Pināka,’ an epithet of Śiva. —पिनाक-धृक् (see धृक्), or पिनाक-भृत्, त्, m. ‘bearer of the Pināka,’ an epithet of Śiva. —पिनाक-पाणि, इस्, m. ‘Pināka in hand,’ an epithet of Śiva.

29277: पिन्यास पिन्यास, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. 2. अस् with पि-नि), Asa Fœtida; [cf. पिण्याक।]
29278: पिन्व् पिन्व्, cl. 1. P. A. पिन्वति, -ते, पिपिन्व, पिपिन्वे, पिन्विष्यति, -ते, पिन्वितुम्, Ved. to cause to swell, to distend, to cause to overflow or run over, to cause to abound; to cause to abound in milk (Ṛg-veda I. 112, 3, where, according to Sāy., पिन्वथः = पयसा पूरित-वन्तौ); to sprinkle, wet, moisten, water; to dis-charge, pour forth; to grant, bestow; (A.) to swell, to be distended, to overflow; [cf. rt. प्यै।]

29280: पिन्वन, अम्, n., Ved. a particular vessel used in religious ceremonies.
29281: पिन्वन्त्यपीया, f., Ved., scil. ऋच्, an epithet of the verse beginning पिन्वन्त्य् अपो (Ṛg-veda I. 64, 6).
29282: पिन्वमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being swollen, swelling, being full or filled.
29283: पिपतिषत् पिपतिषत्, पिपतिषा, पिपतिषु। See under पित्सत्, col. 1.
29284: पिपविषु पिपविषु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. पू), wishing to purify.
29285: पिपाठक पिपाठक, अस्, m., N. of a moun-tain.
29286: पिपासत् पिपासत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. पा), thirsting, thirsty.
29287: पिपासा, f. thirst, desire to drink. —पिपासा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, thirsting, thirsty.
29288: पिपासित, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing to drink, thirsty, athirst.
29289: पिपासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, wishing to drink, thirsty.
29290: पिपासु, उस्, उस्, उ, thirsty, athirst.
29291: पिपिली पिपिली, f. = पिपीलि, an ant.
29292: पिपिष्वत् पिपिष्वत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. a rt. पि for पी), Ved. (perhaps) swollen, overfull, super-abundant; (according to Sāy.) favourable to the hus-bandman.
29293: पिपीतक पिपीतक, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman who was the first to perform a particular ceremony in honour of Viṣṇu on the twelfth day of the light half of the month Vaiśākha; (ई), f. the twelfth day of the light half of the month Vaiśākha (when giving away water is an act of merit, so called after the Brāhman Pipītaka).
29294: पिपील पिपील, अस्, ई, m. f. (perhaps a re-duplicated form fr. rt. पीड्), an ant.
29295: पिपीलक, अस्, m. a large black ant; (इका), f. the common small red ant; a female ant. —पिपीलिका-परिसर्पण, अम्, n. the running about of ants.
29296: पिपीलिक, अस्, m. an ant; (अम्), n. a kind of gold supposed to be collected by ants. —पिपीलिक-मध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘thin in the middle like an ant,’ N. of any metre the middle Pāda of which is shorter than the preceding and following. —पिपी-लिक-मध्यमा, f., N. of a species of the Anuṣṭubh metre. —पिपीलिका-मध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, a kind of fasting (beginning on the day of full moon with fifteen mouthfuls, decreasing by one daily until the day of new moon, and after that increasing by one daily until the next day of full moon).
29297: पिपृच्छिषु पिपृच्छिषु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. Desid. of rt. प्रछ्), about to ask or inquire, wishing to ask.
29298: पिप्पका पिप्पका, f., Ved. a species of bird; [cf. पिप्पीक।]
29299: पिप्पटा पिप्पटा, f. a kind of sweetmeat.
29300: पिप्पल पिप्पल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 3. पा), the holy fig-tree, Ficus Religiosa [cf. अश्वत्-थ]; a kind of bird; a nipple (so called from its similarity to a berry); the sleeve of a jacket or coat; N. of a son of Mitra and Revatī; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school of the Atharva-veda; (आस्), f., N. of a river; (ई), f. a berry; long pepper, Piper Longum (both plant and berry; cf. कपि-प्°, जल-प्°, तोय-प्°); (अम्), n. a berry in general, the berry of the tree Ficus Religiosa; sensual enjoyment; water; the sleeve of a coat; [cf. Gr. πίπερι, πέπερι; Lat. piper.] —पिप्पलाद (°ल-अद°), अस्, m. ‘eater of berries,’ N. of an ancient teacher of the Atharva-veda; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school of the Atharva-veda (also पिप्पलादकास्). —पिप्पलाद-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —पिप्-पलाद-श्रुति, इस्, f., N. of a work mentioned in the Parāśara-smṛti. —पिप्पला-वती, f., N. of a river. —पिप्पली-मूल, अम्, n. the root of long pepper. —पिप्पली-लवण, ए, n. du. pepper and salt.
29301: पिप्पलक, अम्, n. a nipple; sewing thread.
29302: पिप्पलायन, अस्, m., N. of a man.
29303: पिप्पलि, इस्, f. long pepper; वसिष्ठस्य पिप्पलि, N. of a Sāman. —पिप्पलि-श्रोणि, इस्, f., N. of a river.
29304: पिप्पलीका, f. a species of plant (= अश्वत्थी).
29305: पिप्पलू पिप्पलू, ऊस्, m. or f. (?), N. of a man (or woman ?).
29306: पिप्पिका पिप्पिका, f. the tartar of the teeth; [cf. पिट्टक।]
29307: पिप्पीक पिप्पीक, अस्, m., Ved. a species of animal, probably a bird; [cf. पिप्पका।]
29308: पिप्रीषा पिप्रीषा, f. (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. प्री), Ved. desire of pleasing or showing kindness.
29309: पिप्रीषु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of pleasing, wishing to give pleasure.
29310: पिप्रु पिप्रु, उस्, m. (fr. rt. पॄ?), Ved., N. of a demon (who was conquered and whose strong-holds were destroyed by Indra).
29311: पिप्लु पिप्लु, उस्, m. (perhaps for अपि-प्लु; said to be fr. rt. प्लुष् with अपि), a freckle, mark, mole. —पिप्लु-कर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, having a mark on the ear. —पिप्लु-प्रच्छादन, अस्, ई, अम्, covering or concealing a mole.
29312: पिब पिब or पिव, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. पा), drinking, who or what drinks; [cf. त्रि-प्°।] —पिब-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. containing a form of the verb पिबति।
29313: पिबत् or पिवत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, drinking, who or what drinks.
29314: पिब्दमान पिब्दमान, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps fr. a reduplicated form of rt. 2. पद्), Ved. becoming or being firm or solid, becoming or being hard or compact.
29315: पिब्दन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. firm, hard, solid, compact; (अम्), n. (according to Sāy.) a Rakṣas.
29316: पियारु पियारु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. the Sautra rt. 1. पीय्), Ved. censuring, blaming, deriding, mis-chievous (Sāy. = हिंसक).
29317: पियाल पियाल, अस्, m. (= प्रियाल, q. v., but said to be fr. the Sautra rt. 1. पीय्), the tree Buchanania Latifolia (called in Hindī also Chironji, whence it has been named Chironjia Sapida; in Bengal it is commonly called Piya or Piyal); (अम्), n. the fruit of Buchanania Latifolia.
29318: पिल् पिल्, cl. 10. P. पेलयति, -यितुम्, to throw, cast; to send; to incite; [cf. rts. पेल्, विल्।]
29319: पिलु, उस्, or पिलुक, अस्, m. a species of tree (= पीलु; cf. पैलव).
29320: पिलुनी, f. a species of plant (= मूर्वा; a wrong form for पिलु-पर्णी; cf. पीलु-पर्णी).
29321: पिलि पिलि, इस्, m., N. of a man.
29322: पिलिन्दवत्स पिलिन्द-वत्स, अस्, m., N. of a disciple of Śākya-muni.
29323: पिलिप्पिल पिलिप्पिल, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. slip-pery.
29324: पिल्ल पिल्ल, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be a substi-tute for क्लिन्न), blear-eyed; (अस्), m. a bleared eye.
29325: पिल्लका, f. a female elephant, (the elephant's eye being usually moist.)
29326: पिश् 1. पिश्, cl. 6. P. A. पिंशति, -ते, पिपेश, पिपिशे, पेशिष्यति, -ते, अपेशीत्, पेशितुम्, Ved. to adorn, deck, decorate, embellish; to prepare, make ready (especially meat, by cutting it up and carving it); to shape, fashion, mould, form; to be decomposed, to be reduced to consti-tuent parts; to be organized; to light, enlighten: Caus. पेशयति, Aor. अपीपिशत्: Desid. पिपिशिषति, पिपेशिषति; Intens. पेपिश्यते, पेपेष्टि, to be richly adorned.
29327: 2. पिश्, f. an ornament, decoration; (Sāy.) = रूपं हिरण्यादि।
29328: पिश, अस्, m., Ved. (according to Sāy.) = रुरु, a sort of deer (probably so called from its colour).
29329: पिशङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम्, reddish, reddish-brown, of a tawny or brown colour; (अस्), m. tawny colour; N. of a serpent-demon. —पिशङ्ग-ता, f. or पिशङ्ग-त्व, अम्, n. the being of a tawny colour, tawniness. —पिशङ्ग-भृष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. (perhaps) having red fangs; (Sāy.) = ईषद्-रक्त-वर्ण, being of a pale-red hue, tawny-coloured. —पिशङ्ग-राति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. giving reddish (i. e. golden) gifts (said of Indra); (Sāy.) = बहुरूप-धनेन्द्र, lord of manifold wealth. —पिशङ्ग-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being of a reddish or yellow appearance; (Sāy.) = हिरण्य-रूप, golden-coloured. —पिशङ्ग-सन्-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. 29330: पिशङ्गक, अस्, m., N. of an attendant of Viṣṇu.
29331: पिशङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, brown, tawny.
29332: पिशङ्गिल, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved., N. of a colour (?); (according to Mahī-dhara) = पिशं + गिल।
29333: पिशाच, अस्, m. (perhaps fr. पिश for पिशित, ‘flesh,’ and rt. 1. अञ्च्), N. of a class of demons (perhaps originally a personification of the ignis fatuus; in the Veda they are enumerated after gods, men, Manes, Asuras, and Rākṣasas; in later times they are described as the children of Krodhā); a sprite, fiend, goblin, ogre, malevolent being (some-thing between an infernal imp and a ghost, always described as fierce and malignant); N. of a Rakṣas; (ई), f. a female imp, a she-demon [cf. स्त्री-प्°]; N. of a daughter of Dakṣa and mother of the Piśācas; a species of Valeriana (= गन्ध-मांसी). —पिशाच-ता, f. or पिशाच-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a Piśāca. —पिशाच-द्रु, उस्, m. a species of tree, Trophis Aspera (the favourite haunt of the Piśācas). —पिशाच-बाधा, f. demoniacal possession. —पि-शाच-भाषा, f. ‘Piśāca language,’ a gibberish or cor-ruption of Sanskrit used in plays. —पिशाच-मोचन, अम्, n. ‘release of the Piśāca,’ N. of a place of pilgrim-age. —पिशाचमोचन-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a place of pilgrimage. —पिशाच-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a species of tree, Trophis Aspera (= शाखोट). —पिशाच-सञ्-चार, अस्, m. demoniacal possession. —पिशाच-सभ, अम्, n. an assemblage of goblins or fiends; the place or hall of their assembly, pandemonium. —पिशाचा-लय (°च-आल्°), अस्, m. ‘abode of Piśācas,’ N. of a particular luminous phenomenon, phosphorescence. —पिशाची-करण, अम्, n. transforming into a Piśāca. —पिशाचोरग-राक्षस (°च-उर्°), आस्, m. pl. Piśācas, serpents, and Rākṣasas.
29334: पिशाचक, अस्, m. a Piśāca; (इका), f. = पिशाची (at the end of comps., e. g. गन्ध-प्°, धन-प्°); N. of a river; scil. भाषा, the language of the Piśā-cas. —पिशाचक-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a village.
29335: पिशाचकिन्, ई, m. an epithet of Kuvera the god of wealth (the treasures of this deity being guarded by Piśācas and other malignant beings).
29336: पिशाचि, इस्, m., Ved. a Piśāca.
29337: पिशित, अम्, n. flesh which has been cut up or prepared, flesh, meat; a small piece; (आ), f. spikenard, Nardostachys Jatamansi (= जटा-मांसी). —पिशित-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating flesh; (क्), m. one who eats flesh. —पिशिताश (°त-आश), अस्, आ, अम्, eating flesh; (अस्), m. an epithet of flesh-eating demons, as Rāk-ṣasas or Piśācas; a fiend; a cannibal. —पिशिताशन (°त-अश्°), अस्, ई, अम्, flesh-eating, meat-eating; (अस्), m. a demon, fiend, cannibal, Rakṣas, Piśāca (de-scribed as a child of Ni-kaṣā); epithet of a wolf. —पिशिताशिन् (°त-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, eating flesh or meat, carnivorous; (ई), m. a demon, goblin, can-nibal; N. of an attendant of Śiva. —पिशितेप्सु (°त-ईप्°), उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of flesh, eager for or greedy after meat.
29338: पिशी, f. spikenard, Nardostachys Jatamansi (= पिशिता).
29339: पिशुन, अस्, आ, अम्, informing against, betraying, treacherous; disparaging, calumniating, backbiting, calumnious, slanderous; cruel, wicked, malignant, mischievous, harsh, unkind; exciting hopes and dis-appointing them; vile, low, contemptible, infamous; stupid, a fool; making known, indicating, evincing, displaying, reminding, commemorating, memorable for (at the end of comps., e. g. तुल्यानुराग-प्°, manifesting an equal attachment; क्षत्र-प्रध-न-प्°, memorable for the conflict of Kṣatriyas); (अस्), m. a betrayer, traitor, informer, spy, tale-bearer, backbiter, calumniator, slanderer; epithet of a goblin dangerous to pregnant women; cotton (which betrays by hanging to the clothes); an epi-thet of Nārada (the messenger and informant of the gods); a crow; N. of a Brāhman; N. of a minister of Dushyanta; (आ), f. a species of plant, Medicago Esculenta; (अम्), n. informing against, betraying, sycophancy; saffron (which betrays an unfaithful lover); [cf. Gr. πικ῏πό-ς, πευκεδανό-ς, πευκάλιμο-ς, ἐχε-πευκές: Lith. pī1k-ta-s, ‘bad;’ pýk-ti, ‘to be angry;’ peīk-ti, ‘to despise, to blame.’] —पिशुन-ता, f. slander, scandal, backbiting, betrayal, syco-phancy. —पिशुन-वचन or पिशुन-वाक्य, अम्, n. evil speech, bad report, detraction, slander.
29340: पिशुनय, Nom. P. पिशुनयति, -यितुम्, to betray, make known, indicate, make manifest.
29341: पिशिक पिशिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people in the South.
29342: पिशील पिशील or पिशीलक, अम्, n., Ved. (a wooden) vessel or dish. —पिशील-वीणा, f. a kind of stringed instrument or guitar, the strings of which are stretched across a frame (= शूर्प-वीणा).
29344: पिष् पिष्, cl. 7. P. (ep. also A.) पिनष्टि, पिंष्टे (Impv. 2nd sing. पिण्ढि), पि-पेष, पेक्ष्यति, अपिषत्, पेष्टुम् (ep. Impf. अपिंषत्, Pot. पिषेत्), to grind, pound, crush; to bruise, hurt, injure, destroy; cl. 10. P. or Caus. पेष-यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अपीपिषत्, to grind, pound; to injure; to give; to be strong; to dwell; cl. 1. 10. P. पेषति, पेषयति, to go, move; [cf. Gr. πτίσσ-ω for πίσσ-ω, πίτυρον, πτίσ-μα, πίσ-ο-ς, πίσ-ινο-ς, πίσσο-; Lat. pins-o, pīs-o, pis-tor, pis-tillu-m, pistrīnum, pis-tura, pis-u-m, Piso, pī-lu-m, pī-la, pī-lu-s; Lith. pes-tà, ‘a mill.’]

A. पीयूषवर्षायते, -यि-तुम्, to become or turn into a shower of nectar.
29399: 2. पीयूष, Nom. P. पीयूषति, पीयूषितुम्, to become or turn into nectar.
29400: पीव, अस्, आ, अम्, (according to Sāy.) = आ-प्या-यित, fat.
29401: पीवत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, fat; (probably the original form of पीवन् below.)

29403: पीवर, अस्, आ, or ई, अम् (said to be fr. rt. 1. पा), fat, stout, large, fleshy, corpulent, plump, thick, dense; (अस्), m. a tortoise; N. of one of the Sap-tarshis under Manu Tāmasa; (आ), f. Physalis Flex-uosa, Asparagus Racemosus; N. of a daughter of the Gandharva Huhu; (ई), f. a young woman; a cow; [cf. Gr. πιαρό-ς, πιερό-ς, πιαλέο-ς, πίειρα.]; —पी-वर-त्व, अम्, n. fatness, thickness, largeness, heavi-ness, density. —पीवर-स्तनी, f. a woman with large breasts; a cow with a large udder. —पीवरी-कृ, cl. 8. 29404: पीवस्, आन्, असी, अस् (a kindred form to पीवन्), fat, stout; (अस्), n., Ved. fat; [cf. 29405: पीवस, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. abounding with fat, fat, abundant; swelling, swollen, inflated; (Sāy.) = पीन, robust; = अ-च्छिन्न, untorn.
29406: पीविष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, extremely fat.

29408: पीनसिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a cold.
29409: पीपरि पीपरि, इस्, m. a species of Plaksha of low growth.
29410: पीय् 1. पीय् (a Sautra rt.), to gladden.
29411: पीय् 2. पीय्, cl. 1. P. पीयति, &c., Ved. to blame, abuse, treat disrespectfully or with contempt; to give pleasure.
29412: पीयक, अस्, m., Ved. ‘an abuser,’ (probably) N. of a class of demons.
29413: पीयत्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. scornful.
29414: पीयु, उस्, उस्, उ (said to be fr. rt. 1. पा), Ved. scornful, injurious (as an Asura); (उस्), m. an owl; a crow; time; fire; the sun (?); gold.
29416: पीयूक्षा पीयूक्षा, f. a species of plant.
29417: पीयूष 1. 2. पीयूष। See under पीन, col. 1.
29418: पील् पील्, cl. 1. P. पीलति, पीलितुम्, to check, impede, obstruct; to stop, to cease to be or do; to become stupid.
29419: पीलक, अस्, m. the large black ant; [cf. पिपील and पीलुक।]

29421: पीलुक, अस्, m., N. of a tree, Careya Arborea or Salvadora Persica or any other exotic or unknown tree [cf. काक-प्°, काल-प्°]; an ant.
29422: पीलुनी, f. the plant Sanseviera Zeylanica (= मूर्वा).
29423: पीला पीला, f., Ved. epithet of a particular scent; N. of a woman.
29424: पीव् पीव्, cl. 1. P. पीवति, पीवितुम्, to be fat or corpulent, to be thick.
29425: पीव पीव, पीवन्, पीवर, पीवस्, पीवस, पीविष्ठ। See col. 2.
29426: पीवा पीवा, f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. पा), water.
29427: पुंस् 1. पुंस् (perhaps a Nom. fr. 2. पुंस् below), cl. 10. P. पुंसयति, -यितुम्, to crush, grind; to pain, punish.
29428: पुंस् 2. पुंस्, पुमान्, m. (voc. पुमन्, the strong cases being fr. पुमांस्, the middle fr. पुम्, and the weak fr. पुंस्, but loc. pl. पुन्सु not पुंसु by Pāṇ. VIII. 2, 65; said to be fr. rt. 3. पा), a male, male being, man [cf. न-प्°]; a human being; a servant, attendant; the soul, spirit (= पुरुष; परः पुमान्, the Supreme Spirit, soul of the universe, Viṣṇu); (in grammar) a word in the masculine gender; [cf. स्त्री-पुं-नपुंसक; Lat. mas, mar-is for mas-is, mas-culus, the syllable pu being rejected in these words but appearing in pu-sus, pu-sa, pu-bes perhaps for pu-mes.] —पुं-युग्, क्, or पुं-योग, अस्, m. connection with a man; cohabitation with men. —पुं-रत्न, अम्, n. ‘a jewel of a man,’ an excel-lent man. —पुं-राशि, इस्, m. a male sign of the zodiac, an epithet of Aries and the signs following. —पुं-रूप, अम्, n. the form or shape of a man; पुं-रूपं कृ, to assume the form of a man. —पुं-लिङ्ग, अम्, n. the characteristic sign of a man, virility, manhood, the male organ; (in gram-mar) the masculine gender; (अस्, आ, अम्), having the characteristics of a man; masculine. —पुंलिङ्ग-ता, f. masculineness, the being of the masculine gender. —पुंलिङ्ग-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m., N. of a part of the Nāma-liṅgānuśāsana by Amara-siṃha. —पुं-वत्, ind. like a man, as a man, as with a man; like the masculine gender, in the masculine form or gender. —पुं-वत्स, अस्, m. a bull-calf; (अस्, आ, अम्), having bull-calves, surrounded by bull-calves. —पुंवद्-विधान, अम्, n. ceremonies as on the birth of a male. —पुं-वृष, अस्, m. the musk rat. —पुं-वेश, अस्, आ, अम्, wearing male attire, dressed like a man. —पुंश्-चली, f. ‘running after men,’ a frequenter of men, harlot, an unchaste woman; N. of an Apsaras. —पुंश्चलीय, अस्, m. the son of a harlot. —पुंश्-चलू, ऊस्, f., Ved. a harlot; (उस्), m. a whoremonger. —पुंश्-चिह्न, अम्, n. the characteristic of a male, membrum virile. —पुंस-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (पुंस substituted for पुंस्), Ved. having a son. —पुं-सवन, अस्, आ, अम्, bringing forth a male, causing the birth of a male child; (अम्), n. (with or without व्रत) the first of the essential ceremonies of Hindū initiation, a reli-gious and domestic festival held on the mother's per-ceiving the first signs of a living conception; a fetus; milk. —पुंसानुज (°सा-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, (perhaps) having an elder brother. —पुं-सुवन, अम्, n., Ved. bringing forth a male child. —पुंस्-कटी, f. a man's hip. —पुंस्-कामा, f. ‘desirous of man,’ a woman wishing for a lover or husband. —पुंस्-कोकिल, अस्, m. the male of the Indian cuckoo. —पुंस्कोकिल-त्व, अम्, n. the being a male cuckoo, the state or con-dition of a male cuckoo. —पुंस्-त्व, अम्, n. the being a male, the state of a male, masculineness, manhood, virility; semen virile; (in grammar) the masculine gender. —पुंस्-पुत्र, अस्, m. a male child, boy. —पुंस्-प्रजनन, अम्, n. the male organ of generation. —पुंस्-प्रवाद, अस्, m. (in Vedic grammar) a masculine base. —पुंस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, containing the word पुंस् or the masculine gender. —पुङ्-खेऽट, अस्, m. a male planet. —पुङ्-गव, अस्, m. a bull; a kind of drug commonly called Māṣāṇi; (at the end of a comp.) a hero or eminent person, chief, best, most excellent [cf. कुरु-प्°, गज-प्°, नर-प्°।] —पुङ्गव-केतु, उस्, उस्, उ, characterized or symbolized by a bull; (उस्), m. an epithet of Śiva. —पुङ्-गुण-जन्तु-जीव, अस्, m. the living or animal soul combined with the qualities of man. —पुञ्-जन्म-कर, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), ‘effecting the birth of males,’ a constellation under which male children are born. —पुञ्-जन्म-द, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), ‘granting the birth of males,’ a constellation under which male children are born. —पुञ्-जन्मन्, अ, n. the birth of a male child. —पुञ्जन्म-योग, अस्, m. ‘star of the birth of males,’ a constellation under which male children are born. —पुन्-दास, अस्, m. a male slave. —पुन्-ध्वज, अस्, m. ‘having the mark of a male,’ the male of any species of animal. —पुन्-नक्षत्र, अम्, n. a Nakṣatra regarded as a male, male asterism; an asterism under which males are pro-created. —पुन्-नाग, अस्, m. ‘an elephant among men,’ a distinguished man; a white elephant; N. of a tree, Rottleria Tinctoria (from the blossoms of which a yellowish dye is prepared); a white lotus; a nutmeg. —पुन्-नाट or पुन्-नाड, अस्, m. the plant Cassia Tora (= चक्र-मर्द). —पुन्-नाम-धेय, अस्, m. ‘that which is called man,’ one of the male sex, a male. —१। पुन्-नामन्, आ, म्नी, अ (for 2. see under पुत्), having a masculine name; (आ), m. the tree Rottleria Tinctoria. —पुम्-अनुजा, f. (probably) ‘born after a male child,’ having an elder brother; born after or like a man. —पुम्-अपत्य, अम्, n. male offspring. —पुम्-अर्थ, अस्, m. the aim of man. —पुम्-आख्या, f. a name for male beings, a designation of a male being. —पुम्-आचार, अस्, m. the custom or usage of men. —पुम्-भू-मन्, आ, m. a word of the masculine gender in the plural number.

29432: पुंस्ति पुंस्ति, N. of a Sāman.

29435: पुङ्ख पुङ्ख, अस्, m. the feathered part of an arrow, the lower part of an arrow which comes in contact with the bow-string and contains the feathers and shaft; a hawk, falcon (= मङ्गलाचार, q. v.).
29436: पुङ्खित, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with a Puṅkha.
29437: पुङ्खिलतीर्थ पुङ्खिल-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a place of pilgrimage (= राम-तीर्थ).
29438: पुङ्ग पुङ्ग, अस्, अम्, m. n. a heap, collec-tion, quantity; [cf. पुञ्ज।]

29441: पुच्छ पुच्छ, अस्, अम्, m. n. a tail; the hinder part; the tail of a peacock; a horse's tail; any hairy tail; the end of anything; [cf. probably Gr. πῡγή, perhaps πύματος.] —पुच्छ-जाह, अम्, n. the root of the tail. —पुच्छ-दा, f. a bulbous plant used as a remedy for sterility, = लक्ष्म-ना-कन्द; (probably a corruption of पुत्र-दा।) —पुच्छ-धि, इस्, m., Ved. the root of the tail. —पुच्छ-मूल or पुच्छाग्र (°छ-अग्°), अम्, n. the tip of the tail. —पुच्छाण्डक (°छ-अण्°), अस्, m., N. of a Nāga of the race of Takṣaka. —पुच्छेश्वर (°छ-ईश्°), अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a place or of a temple.
29443: पुच्छिका in क्रोष्टु-प्°, क्रोष्टुक-प्°, q. v.

(perhaps for अपि + युञ्ज fr. rt. युज्), a heap, lump, mass, quantity, collec-tion, multitude; [cf. नख-पुञ्ज-फला, पुङ्ग, पूग; Gr. πύξ perhaps an abbreviated dat. pl., πύκ-τη-ς, πύγ-μαχ-ο-ς, πυγ-μή, πυγ-ών, πυκ-νό-ς, πυκ-ι-νό-ς; Lat. pug-nu-s, pug-na, pug-nā-re, pug-io, pug-il, pugillu-s, pugillaris; Old Germ. fû-st; Old Slav. pe-stĭ.] —पुञ्ज-राज, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian and author of a commentary on the Sarasvatī-prakriyā. —पुञ्ज-शस्, ind. in heaps. —पुञ्जी-कृ, cl. 8. 29463: पुणतामकर पुणतामकर, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Ātmatva-jāti-vicāra and Sādṛśya-vāda, (also called Mahā-deva.)
29464: पुण्ट् पुण्ट्, cl. 10. P. पुण्टयति, -यितुम्, to speak; to shine.

29466: पुण्ड पुण्ड, अस्, m. = पुण्ड्र, a mark, sign. —पुण्ड-वर्धन = पुण्ड्र-वर्धन, q. v.
29467: पुण्डरीक पुण्डरीक, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. पुण्), a lotus-flower, especially a white lotus, (used at the end of an adj. comp. as expressive of beauty, see Gaṇa Vyāghrādi to Pāṇ. II. 1, 56); a white umbrella; a kind of drug; a mark on the forehead (in this sense perhaps also m.); N. of a sacred bathing-place; (अस्), m. a kind of sacrifice; a species of rice; a fragrant kind of mango; Artemisia Indica (= द-मनक); a variety of the sugar-cane; a silk-worm (?); a kind of leprosy; fever in an elephant; white (the colour); a tiger; a kind of serpent; N. of a Nāga; a pitcher, student's water-pot; N. of the elephant of the south-east quarter; N. of an ancient king; of a son of Nabha or Nabhas; (with Jainas) N. of a Gaṇa-dhara; N. of a hermit the son of Śveta-ketu and Lakṣmī; of a mountain; (आ), f., N. of an Apsaras; of a daughter of Vasiṣṭha and wife of Prāṇa or Pāṇḍu. —पुण्डरि-स्रजा, f. 29468: पुण्डरीयक, अस्, m., N. of a divinity enu-merated among the Viśve Devāḥ; (अम्), n. Ketmia Mutabilis (= स्थल-पद्म); a kind of drug (com-monly called पुण्डरीय).
29469: पुण्डर्य, अम्, n. a creeper; a medicinal plant used as a remedy for diseased eyes (= प्र-पौण्डरीक).
29470: पुण्ड्र पुण्ड्र, अस्, m. a red variety of the common sugar-cane, Saccharum Officinarum; a white lotus, a lotus in general; a species of tree (= ह्रस्व-प्लक्ष); a kind of creeper, Gærtnera Racemosa (= अति-मुक्तक, वासन्ती); a mark or line made on the forehead with sandal &c., sectarial mark; a worm; N. of a Daitya or infernal being considered incarnate in Śiśu-pāla; N. of a son of Bali; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people and of their country (the modern Bengal and Behar, ‘the country of the sugar-cane’); N. of a mythical city between the mountains Hima-vat and Hema-kūṭa. —पुण्ड्र-केलि, इस्, m. an elephant. —पुण्ड्र-देश, अस्, m., N. of a district. —पुण्ड्र-नगर, अम्, n. ‘city of the Puṇḍras,’ N. of a town; [cf. पौण्ड्रनागर।] —पुण्ड्र-वर्धन, अम्, n., N. of a town in Gauḍa; (also spelt पुण्ड-वर्धन।)
29471: पुण्ड्रक, अस्, m. a red variety of the common sugar-cane, Saccharum Officinarum; a kind of creeper, Gærtnera Racemosa; a species of tree; a mark on the forehead, sectarial mark; one who lives by breeding silk-worms; N. of a man (?).
29472: पुण्ढ्र, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a mark, sign, sectarial mark; [cf. पुण्ड्र।]
29473: पुण्य पुण्य, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. 1. पू; according to others fr. rt. 1. पुष् or rt. पुण्; not met with in the earliest language), good, pure, holy, right, righteous, virtuous, just, sacred; happy, prosperous, favourable, propitious, auspicious, lucky; bright, fine, beautiful, pleasing; sweet, fra-grant (as an odour); solemn, festive, ferial; (अम्), n. good, right, virtue, moral or religious merit; a good or meritorious act; purity, purification; a reli-gious ceremony, especially one performed by a wife in order to retain her husband's affections and to obtain a son; a brick trough for watering cattle, = कोष्ठक; (अस्), m., N. of a man; of a lake (in this sense perhaps n.); (आ), f. holy basil, Ocymum Sanctum; N. of a daughter of Kratu and San-natī. —पुण्य-कर्तृ, ता, m. ‘right-doer,’ an upright or virtuous man. —पुण्य-कर्मन्, अ, n. a virtuous or meritorious act; (आ, आ, अ), whose actions are holy or meritorious, doing good works, upright, righteous, virtuous, pious; [cf. पुण्यैक-कर्मन्।] —पुण्य-काल, अस्, m. an auspicious time. —पु-ण्यकाल-ता, f. a propitious period. —पुण्य-कीर्त्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, bearing a good name, famous, celebrated; N. of a Buddhist (whose form was assumed by Viṣṇu). —पुण्य-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, ‘right-doing,’ up-right, virtuous; N. of a divinity enumerated among the Viśve Devāḥ. —पुण्य-कृत्या, f. a good action. —पुण्य-क्षय, अस्, m. decay or loss of religious merit. —पुण्य-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. a holy place or district, a place by visiting which merit is acquired, a place of pilgrimage. —पुण्य-गन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, sweet-scented, fragrant; (अस्), m. the Campaka, Michelia Champaka. —पुण्य-गन्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, or पुण्य-गन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, sweet-scented, fragrant. —पुण्य-गृह, अम्, n. a house of charity, an alms-house; a temple. —पुण्य-जन, अस्, m. a good or pious or virtuous man; N. of a class of supernatural beings; a Yakṣa or attendant of Kuvera the god of wealth; a fiend, goblin, Rākṣasa. —पु-ण्यजनेश्वर (°न-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of the Yakṣas,’ Kuvera the Hindū deity of wealth. —पुण्य-जल, अस्, आ, अम्, containing pure water. —पुण्य-जित, अस्, आ, अम्, gained or attained by good works. —पुण्य-तर, अस्, अम्, purer, holier. —पुण्य-तरी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make purer or cleaner. —पुण्य-ता, f. or पुण्य-त्व, अम्, n. purity, holiness. —पुण्य-तीर्थ, अम्, n. a holy shrine or place of pilgrimage. —पुण्य-तृण, अम्, n. holy grass; N. of the white variety of Kuśa grass. —पुण्य-दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, of beautiful appear-ance, beautiful; (अस्), m. the blue jay, = चाष; (अम्), n. visiting holy shrines. —पुण्य-दुह्, -धुक्, क्, क्, yielding or granting happiness or beatitude. —पुण्य-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian. —पुण्य-नामन्, आ, m., N. of one of the attend-ants of Skanda. —पुण्य-पुण्य-ता, f. perfect holi-ness. —पुण्य-पुरुष, अस्, m. a godly or good man, a man rich in moral merit. —पुण्य-प्र-ताप, अस्, m. the might and efficacy of virtue or of the merit acquired by a course of virtuous acts. —पुण्य-प्रद, अस्, आ, अम्, conferring merit, meritorious. —पुण्य-प्रसव, आस्, m. pl. (with Buddhists) N. of a class of deities. —पुण्य-फल, अम्, n. the fruit or reward of good works or merito-rious actions; (अस्), m. ‘having good fruit,’ the garden of Lakṣmī; a grove. —पुण्य-बल, अस्, m., N. of a king of Puṇya-vatī. —पुण्य-भरित, अस्, आ, अम्, extremely blessed, abounding in holiness or bliss. —पुण्य-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, or पुण्य-भाजिन्, ई, इनी, इ, possessing happiness, partaker of bliss, happy; pos-sessing merit, virtuous. —पुण्य-भू, ऊस्, f. the holy land of the Hindūs (bounded on the north by the Himālayas, on the south by the Vindhya mountains, and on the east and west by the sea, = Āryāvarta). —पुण्य-भूमि, इस्, f. the holy land of the Hindūs [cf. पुण्य-भू above]; the mother of a male child. —पुण्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, formed or con-sisting of good. —पुण्य-मित्र, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist patriarch. —पुण्य-योग, अस्, m. the influ-ence or effect of virtuous actions done in a former life. —पुण्य-रात्र, अस्, m. a good or auspicious night; a night on which any religious commemora-tion or ceremony is held; [cf. पुण्याह।] —पुण्य-राशि, इस्, m., N. of a man; N. of a mountain. —पुण्य-लब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, attained by good works (as a reward in heaven). —पुण्य-लोक, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to a better world, sharing in a better world (Ved.); (अस्), m. heaven, paradise. —पुण्यलोक-त्र, ind., Ved. in a better world. —पुण्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing merit, merito-rious, pure, holy, righteous, pious, virtuous; pleasing, beautiful; fortunate, lucky, auspicious; happy; (अती), f., N. of a country. —पुण्य-वर्धन, अम्, n., N. of a town; (probably a wrong reading for पुण्ड्र-वर्धन।) —पुण्य-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a prince of Vi-darbha. —पुण्य-वाग्-बुद्धि-कर्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, pure in word, thought, and deed. —पुण्य-विजित, अस्, आ, अम्, acquired by merit, merited. —पुण्य-शकुन, अस्, m. a bird of good omen. —पुण्य-शाला, f. a house of charity, alms-house. —पुण्य-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, being of a virtuous disposition, disposed to virtuous acts, virtuous, pious, righteous. —पुण्य-श्री-गर्भ, अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva. —पुण्य-श्लोक, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘well spoken of,’ of good fame or reputation; (अस्), m. an epithet of Nala; of Yudhi-ṣṭhira; of Kṛṣṇa; (आ), f. an epithet of Draupadī; of Sītā. —पुण्यश्लोक-दिदृक्षा, f. the desire of seeing Nala. —पुण्य-श्लोक-पराङ्मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having the face averted from Nala. —पुण्य-सञ्चय, अस्, m. a store of virtue or religious merit. —पुण्य-सम, अम्, n. a good year. —पुण्य-सार, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —पुण्य-सुन्दर, अस्, m., N. of a gram-marian who arranged the Dhātu-pāṭha of Hema-candra's grammar in alphabetical order. —पुण्य-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a man; of a prince of Ujjayinī. —पुण्य-स्तम्भ-कर, अस्, m., N. of a man. —पुण्य-स्थान, अम्, n. a sacred place, conse-crated ground. —पुण्यात्मन् (°य-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, pure-souled, righteous, virtuous, pious, holy. —पु-ण्यालङ्कृत (°य-अल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, adorned by virtue; (अस्), m., N. of a demon. —पुण्याह (°य-अह), अम्, n. a good or happy or auspicious day, holiday; पुण्याहं वच् in Caus., to wish any one a happy or pleasant day. —पुण्याहन् (°य-अहन्), अ, n., Ved. = पुण्याह above. —पुण्याह-वाचन, अम्, n. the declaration of a holiday, repeating at sacrifices &c. ‘this is a holiday’ three times, wishing any one a happy day. —पुण्यैक-कर्मन् (°य-एक्°), आ, आ, अ, one whose actions are only virtuous. —पुण्योदका (°य-उद्°), f. ‘having sacred waters,’ N. of a river in the next world. —पुण्योदय (°य-उद्°), अस्, m. the resulting of good fortune (as the effect of virtuous acts done in a former life). —पुण्योद्यान (°य-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having beautiful gardens.
29474: पुण्यक, अम्, n. a religious ceremony, festival; a meritorious act or obligation of a religious nature (as fasting, praying, &c.); a ceremony performed by a woman in order to retain her husband's affections and to obtain a son; the observance of this cere-mony; the present made to a wife on that occasion. —पुण्यक-व्रत, अम्, n. the worship of Kṛṣṇa for a year, with daily presents, to be performed by a woman desirous of a son.
29475: पुत् पुत् or पुद्, n. hell, a particular hell to which the childless are condemned, a division of the infernal regions considered to be the abode of those who die childless; (a word invented to explain पुत्र; see Manu IX. 138.) — 2. पुन्-नामन्, आ, म्नी, अ (for 1. see under 2. पुंस्), having the name Put, called Put.

29478: पुतीसृञ्जय पुती-सृञ्जय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (a wrong reading for पूति-सृञ्जय।)
29479: पुत्तल पुत्तल, पुत्तलक, पुत्तिका। See p. 581, cols. 1, 2.
29480: पुत्र पुत्र, अस्, m. (perhaps connected with पितृ; said to be fr. rt. 1. पू, but according to others fr. rt. 1. पुष्; traditionally said to be a comp. पुत्-त्र, ‘preserving from the hell called Put,’ Manu IX. 138), a son, child, the young of an animal; (at the end of a comp.) used as a diminutive to express ‘any little thing of its kind’ [cf. शिला-प्°]; the fifth mansion from the point of conjunction of the sun and a zodiacal sign (in astrol.), the fifth house; N. of a son of Brahmiṣṭha; of a son of Priya-vrata; of a son of a Brāhman; (औ), m. du. two sons, a son and daughter; (ई), f. a daughter; a doll [cf. दारु-प्°]; (at the end of a comp.) used as a diminutive to express ‘any little thing of its kind’ [cf. असि-प्°]; an epithet of Pārvatī; a species of plant. पुत्र in the voc. sing. is sometimes used as a mode of addressing young persons, ‘my son,’ ‘my child;’ [cf. Pers. pusr, ‘a son;’ Gr. πῶλο-ς, πωλ-ίο-ν; Lat. pullu-s, (Marci-)por, pu-er, pu-era, pu-su-s, pusa, pû-pu-s, pû-pa, pûpilla, pu-tu-s; Goth. fula (n) = Old Germ. folo, ‘a foal;’ Armor. paotr, ‘a boy.’] —पुत्र-कन्दा, f. a bulbous plant supposed to cause fecundity (= लक्ष्-मणा-कन्द). —पुत्र-कर्मन्, अ, n. a ceremony or sacrifice on the birth of a son. —पुत्र-कलत्र-नाश-भीत, अस्, आ, अम्, fearful or apprehensive of the destruction of wife and children. —पुत्र-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. desirous of sons or children. —पुत्रकामेष्टि (°म-इष्°), इस्, f., Ved. an obla-tion or sacrifice made by one desirous of offspring. —पुत्रकाम्य, Nom. 29500: पुनर् is often used to introduce further details or simply as a connecting particle in a sentence, in the sense of ‘further,’ ‘furthermore,’ ‘besides,’ ‘now.’ As an adversative particle पुनर् is equivalent to ‘on the other hand,’ ‘on the contrary,’ ‘but,’ ‘yet,’ ‘still,’ ‘and yet,’ ‘notwithstanding,’ ‘nevertheless,’ ‘however.’ The construction वा पुनर् often takes the place of the simple वा, e. g. अद्रोहेणैव भू-तानाम् अल्प-द्रोहेण वा, पुनः, with no injury or with the least possible injury to animated beings, Manu IV. 2. पुनर् अपि, even again, and on the other hand, also. किम् पुनर्, how much more! how much less! see किम्. —पुनः-पद, अम्, n., Ved. ‘a repeated portion of a verse,’ the burden (of a hymn), refrain; 29516: पुरस्, ind. before, in front, in advance, in the presence of, before the eyes of (with gen., e. g. तस्य पुरो वाचम् आददे, he commenced a speech in his presence; or in the earlier language with the abl. or loc., opposed to पश्चा, पश्चात्, पृष्ठे); 29517: पुरस्तात्, ind. before, in front of (with abl. or gen.) in advance, towards the front, forward, at the beginning or commencement, in the first place; ere; previously, formerly, first; before the eyes of, in the presence of; eastward, towards the east, in the east, from the east [cf. उत्तर-प्°]; in the preceding part (of a book), further on, in the sequel. —पु-रस्ताज्-जप, अस्, m., Ved. a preceding Japa. —पु-रस्ताज्-ज्योतिस्, इस्, इस्, इस्, N. of a kind of Triṣṭubh, the first Pāda of which contains eight syllables. —पुरस्ताद्-उद्धार, अस्, m., Ved. a part given in advance. —पुरस्ताद्-धोम, अस्, m. (fr. पुरस्तात् + होम), Ved. an introductory sacrifice. —पुरस्ताद्-धोम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having an introductory sacrifice. —पुरस्ताद्-बृहती, f., Ved. a kind of Bṛhatī metre, the first Pāda or which contains twelve syllables.
29518: पुरस्तात्न, अस्, आ (?), अम्, preceding, going before.
29519: पुरा, ind. (perhaps and old inst. sing. fr. a form पुर for पर), in former times, formerly, of old, in the olden time, in the days of old, of yore; before, hitherto, up to the present time (with न, ‘never’); firstly, in the first place, first, at first (opposed to पश्चा, पश्चात्); soon, ere long, shortly, in a short time, by and by (in this sense giving a future sense to the pres. by Pāṇ. III. 3, 4, e. g. पुरा दूषयति स्थलीम्, ere long he will contaminate the earth, Raghu-v. XII. 30; आलोके ते निपतति पुरा, soon she will fall within [the range of] thy sight, Megh. 84); before, ere (with abl. and in the earlier language also with dat.); for the defence or safety of (Ved.); securely from (Ved.); with the exception of, except, besides (Ved.); [cf. पुरस्, पूर्व; Gr. πάροι, πάροιθε, παροίτερος, πάλαι, πάλαιος, perhaps πέλας, πλήσιος; Lat. por in por-tendere; Goth. faura, faur; Angl. Sax. for, fora-, fore-.] —पुरा-कथा, f. a story of the past, an old legend. —पुरा-कल्प, अस्, m. a former creation, former age; a story or tale of the past. —पुरा-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done formerly or of old, done long ago; done or observed previously; begun, commenced. —पुरा-कृति, इस्, f. the former mode of action. —पुरा-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. former, existing from of old or from aforetime (Sāy. = पूर्व-जात, चिरन्तन). —पुरा-योनि, इस्, इस्, इ, of ancient origin or lineage; an epithet of kings. —पुरा-वसु, उस्, m. an epithet of Bhīṣma. —पुरा-विद्, त्, त्, त्, knowing the events of former times, knowing or acquainted with the past; an epithet of kings. —पुरा-वृत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, that which has occurred or taken place in former times, long since transpired; one who has lived in former times; relating to ancient times, referring to times of yore; (अम्), n. former conduct, former mode of action; any old or legendary event; history, any account of former events traditionary or heroic. —पुरावृत्त-कथा, f. or पुरावृत्ताख्यान (°त-आख्°), अम्, n. an old story or legend, a story of the past. —पुरावृत्ताख्यान-कथन (°त-आख्°), अम्, n. telling old stories, relating tales of the past. —पुरा-साह्, षाट्, ट्, ट्, Ved. superior from ancient times; (Sāy.) = पुराणाम् अभिभवितृ, conqueror of cities. —पुरोद्भव (°रा-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, of former or prior origin; (आ), f. a species of plant, a drug (= महा-मेदा). —पुरोपनीत (°रा-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, formerly obtained or possessed.
29520: पुराण, अस्, आ, or ई, अम् (opposed to नूतन, नव), belonging to ancient or olden times, ancient, old, aged, primeval; worn out, laid aside; (अम्), n. a thing of the past, past event; a tale of the past, ancient history legendary and traditionary, legend (= Gr. λόγος, μῦθος); the N. given to certain well-known sacred works, supposed to have been com-piled by the poet Vyāsa, and comprising the whole body of modern Hindū mythology (each of which should treat of five topics; cf. पञ्च-लक्षण। There are eighteen acknowledged Purāṇas, usually reckoned as follow: 1. Kūrma-p°; 2. Garuḍa-p°; 3. Vṛhan-nāradīya-p°; 4. Padma-p°; 5. Brahma-p°; 6. Brahma-vaivarta-p°, which is of very modern origin; 7. Brahmāṇḍa-p°; 8. Bhaviṣya-p°; 9. Bhā-gavata-p°, or the life of Kṛṣṇa, by some considered a modern work; 10. Matsya-p°; 11. Mārkaṇḍeya-p°; 12. Liṅga-p°; 13. Vāmana-p°; 14. Vāyu-p°, which is probably one of the oldest; 15. Vārāha-p°; 16. Viṣṇu-p°; 17. Śiva-p°; 18. Skanda-p°. Some authorities sub-stitute the Agni-p° for the Vāyu-p°; and others add the Narasiṃha-p°, which is considered by some as an Upa-p°, q. v.; by some the Purāṇas are divided into four or by others into six Saṃhitās or collections); (अस्), m. a Karṣa or measure of silver (= 16 Paṇas of cowries); N. of a Ṛṣi. —पुराण-कल्प, अस्, m. former creation; a story or tale of former time; [cf. पुरा-कल्प।] —पुराण-ग, अस्, m. [cf. 3. ग], ‘singing of the past,’ an epithet of Brahma; a reciter of the Purāṇas. —पुराण-पुरुष, अस्, m. ‘the primeval male,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu. —पुराण-प्रोक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, proclaimed by ancient sages. —पुराण-महिमोपवर्णन (°म-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of the 132nd chapter of the Bhūmi-khaṇḍa or second part of the Padma-Purāṇa. —पुराण-मा-हात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Liṅga-Purāṇa. —पुराण-वत्, ind., Ved. as of old. —पु-राण-विद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. knowing the events of the past; knowing the Purāṇas. —पुराण-विद्या, f. or पुराण-वेद, अस्, m., Ved. a knowledge of the events of the past. —पुराण-समुच्चय, अस्, m., N. of a book mentioned in Kamalākara-bhaṭṭa's Śūdra-dharma-tattva. —पुराण-सर्वस्व, अम्, n. ‘essence of the Purāṇas,’ N. of a work by Halā-yudha taken mostly from the Purāṇas and giving a general outline of universal knowledge. —पुराण-सार, अम्, n. ‘substance of the Purāṇas,’ N. of a work mentioned in Mādhava's Parāśara-smṛti-vyākhyā. —पुराणान्त (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. an epi-thet of Yama. —पुराणावतार (°ण-अव्°), अस्, m., N. of the first chapter of the Padma-Purāṇa. —पु-राणोक्त (°ण-उक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, enjoined by or written in the Purāṇas.
29521: पुराणक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga.
29522: पुराण्य, Nom. P. पुराण्यति, &c., to talk of the past, relate past events.
29523: पुरातन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the past, former, old, ancient; worn out; (आस्), m. pl. the ancients; (अम्), n. an ancient story, old legend; (ए), ind. in past times, formerly.
29524: 1. पुरो-धा, cl. 3. P. A. -दधाति, -धत्ते, -धातुम्, (P.) to place or set before, place foremost or in front, regard before others, value highly, honour, esteem, pay chief attention to, apply one's self to; to weigh, ponder; (A.) to place at the head or in front, to place before, lay down before; to charge, commission, appoint, especially to appoint to priestly functions; to enjoin upon, charge with. —पुरो-धस्, आस्, m. an appointed priest or one appointed to a particular charge, a family priest, king's domestic chaplain (= पुरो-हित; in Mahā-bh. Vana-p. 10635, the form पुरो-ध, अस्, m. occurs); N. of a man said to be the author of the hymn Vājasaneyi-Saṃ-hitā XI. 17. —२। पुरो-धा, f. charge, commission, standing in the place of any one, representation; the rank or office of a Puro-hita, q. v. —पुरो-धातृ, ता, m., Ved. the giver of a charge or commission; the appointer of the Puro-hita. —पुरो-धान, अम्, n. priestly ministration. —पुरो-धानीय, अस्, m., Ved. = पुरो-हित. —पुरोधिका, f. preferred to other women, a favourite wife. —पुरो-हित, अस्, आ, अम्, placed foremost or in front; charged, com-missioned, appointed; (अस्), m. one holding a charge or commission, an agent, an appointed priest or one appointed to any particular charge, a family priest, a king's domestic chaplain, a priest who con-ducts all the ceremonials and sacrifices of the family. —पुरोहित-त्व, अम्, n. the rank of a Puro-hita. —पुरो-हिति, इस्, f. priestly ministration (Sāy. = पुरो-धान, पौरोहित्य). —पुरोहितिका, f., N. of a woman, or a mode of addressing a favourite (?).
29525: पुर् 3. पुर्, ऊर्, f. (probably fr. rt. पॄ), a rampart, wall; a stronghold, castle, fortress, fortified city, town; the body (considered as the stronghold of the पुरुष, q. v.); intellect (= महत्); N. of a Daśa-rātra (Ved.). —पुरञ्-जन, अस्, m. the living principle, life, the soul (personified as a king); (ई), f. understanding, intelligence (personified as the wife of a king). —पुरञ्-जय, अस्, m. ‘city-conqueror,’ N. of a hero on the side of the Kurus; of a son of Sṛñjaya and father of Janam-ejaya; of a son of Bhajamāna and Sṛñjarī; (= ककुत्-स्थ) N. of a son of Śaśāda; = काकुत्स्थ; N. of a son of Vindhya-śakti; of Medhāvin; of an elephant, the son of Airāvaṇa. —पुरन्-द, अस्, m. = पुरन्-दर। —पुरन्-दर, अस्, m. ‘town-splitter’ or ‘fortress-destroyer,’ an epithet of Indra (as breaking cities into fragments with his thunderbolt?); the Indra of the seventh Manv-antara; an epithet of Agni; of Śiva; a thief, house-breaker; (आ), f. an epithet of Gaṅgā; (अम्), n. a species of pepper, Piper Chaba. —पु-रन्दर-चाप, अस्, m. Indra's bow, the rainbow. —पुरन्दर-पुरी, f., N. of a town in Mālava. —पुरि-शय, अस्, आ, अम् (a word formed to explain पुरुष), reposing in the fortress or fastness (i. e. the body). —पुरो-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ (fr. पुरस्, acc. pl. of 3. पुर् + हन्), Ved. breaking castles, destroying strong-holds. —पूर्-द्वार्, र्, f. or पूर्-द्वार, अम्, n. the gate of a city. —पूर्-पति, इस्, m., Ved. the lord of a castle or city. —पूर्-भिद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. breaking down strongholds or castles. —पूर्-भिद्य, अम्, n., Ved. the breaking of strongholds or castles; (Sāy.) = सङ्ग्राम, war. —पूर्-याण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. leading or conducting to the fastness (i. e. to the celestial world).
29526: पुर, अम्, n. a fortress, castle, fortified town; a town, city, a place containing large buildings surrounded by a ditch and extending not less than one Kos in length (if it extends for half that distance it is called a खेट, if less than that, a कर्वट or small market town; any smaller cluster of houses is called a ग्राम or village); ‘the city’ κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i. e. Pāṭali-putra or Patna; a house, dwelling, abode, residence; an upper story; the female apartments, gynæceum; a store-house, repository; a brothel; the body; the skin; the calyx of a flower or any receptacle or cup formed of leaves; a fragrant grass, a species of Cyperus (= नागर-मुस्ता); a kind of resin, bdellium; N. of a constellation; N. of the subdivisions of the Vedānta work called Tri-puṭī or Tri-purī; (अस्), m. a kind of resin, bdellium; yellow Barleria; N. of a demon; N. of a man; (आ), f. a stronghold, castle (at the end of a comp.; cf. जीव-प्°, देव-प्°); a kind of perfume; the east; (ई), f. a fort, stronghold, castle; a town, city; the body; [cf. Gr. πόλι-ς, πολί-χ-νη, πολί-χ-νιο-ν, πολί-τη-ς, πτολί-ε-θρο-ν, perhaps also πύργος;]; per-haps Lat. urbs; perhaps Lith. pil-ī-s, ‘a castle.’] —पुर-कोट्ट, अम्, n. ‘city-stronghold,’ a citadel. —पुर-जित्, त्, m. ‘conqueror of fortresses or conqueror of Pura,’ an epithet of Śiva;
