33408: प्र-हर्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, greatly delighted, de-lighted, very happy.
33409: प्र-हर्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, causing gladness, gladden-ing; (इणी), f. turmeric [cf. प्र-हर्षणी]; a kind of metre, = प्र-हर्षणी।
33410: प्र-हर्षुल, अस्, m. the planet Mercury; [cf. प्र-हर्षण।]
33411: प्र-हृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, exceedingly pleased, overjoyed, rejoiced, delighted, happy, joyful, glad. —प्रहृष्ट-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, delighted at heart, rejoiced in mind, exceedingly glad. —प्र-हृष्ट-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, of pleasing form; erect in form. —प्रहृष्ट-रोमन्, आ, m. ‘having brist-ling hair,’ N. of an Asura. —प्रहृष्टात्मन् (°ट-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, delighted in soul, rejoiced in mind.
33413: प्रहेणक प्र-हेणक, अम्, n. a kind of pastry; victuals or sweetmeats distributed at festivals; [cf. प्र-हेलक।]
33415: प्रहेलक प्र-हेलक, अम्, n. (fr. rt. हिल् with प्र), a riddle, enigma; a kind of pastry; sweet-meats &c. distributed at festivals (= प्र-हेणक).
33416: प्र-हेला, f. playful dalliance, loose or free be-haviour; प्रहेलया, sportively, freely, without con-striant.
33417: प्र-हेलि, इस्, or प्रहेलिका, f. an enigma, riddle, puzzling or enigmatical question.
33418: प्रहोष प्र-होष, प्रहोषिन्। See p. 651, col. 3.
33419: प्रह्राद प्र-ह्राद, अस्, m. (fr. rt. ह्राद् with प्र), N. of the chief of the Asuras with the patro-nymic Kāyādhava (the father of Vi-rocana); N. of a son of Hiraṇya-kaśipu (he was an enemy of Indra and friend of Viṣṇu; cf. प्र-ह्लाद).
33420: प्रह्रादि, अयस्, m. pl. the attendants of the Asura Pra-hrāda.
33421: प्रह्रास प्र-ह्रास, अस्, m. (fr. rt. ह्रस् with प्र), shortening, decrease; languishing, fading away.
33422: प्रह्लाद् प्र-ह्लाद्, cl. 1. A. -ह्लादते, -ह्लादि-तुम्, to be delighted: Caus. -ह्लादयति, -यितुम्, to cause to rejoice, gladden, delight, exhilarate; to extinguish (?).
33423: प्र-ह्लत्ति, इस्, f. pleasure, happiness, joy; (less correctly for प्र-ह्लन्नि।)
33424: प्र-ह्लन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, pleased, glad, happy.
33425: प्र-ह्लन्नि, इस्, f. pleasure, delight, happiness.
33426: प्र-ह्लाद, अस्, m. joyful excitement, pleasure, joy, happiness; sound, noise; N. of a pious Daitya (son of Hiraṇya-kaśipu; he was remarkable for his devotion to Viṣṇu, and was on this account perse-cuted by his father; he was made king of the Daityas by Viṣṇu, and was regent of one of the divisions of Pātāla, cf. प्र-ह्राद and see Viṣṇu-Purāṇa I. 17); N. of a Nāga; of a Prajā-pati; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
33427: प्र-ह्लादक, अस्, इका, अम्, causing joy or pleasure, refreshing.
33428: प्र-ह्लादन, अस्, ई, अम्, causing joy or pleasure; (अस्), m., N. of a poet; (अम्), n. the act of causing joy or pleasure, refreshing.
33429: प्र-ह्लादयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to rejoice, gladdening, delighting.
33430: प्र-ह्लादित, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoiced, delighted.
33431: प्र-ह्लादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, causing joy, delighting; refreshing.
33432: प्रह्व प्र-ह्व, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. ह्वृ with प्र), bent forwards, inclined, sloping, slanting; bent, bowed, stooping; bowing humbly, humble, modest; inclined towards, intent upon, devoted to, attached to, engrossed by, engaged in; (ई), f., N. of a Śakti. —प्रह्वाञ्जलि (°व-अञ्°), इस्, इस्, इ, stooping or bowing with the palms of the hands joined and put to the forehead in token of respect. —प्रह्वी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, bent forwards, bowed, bent; subjected, conquered, won.
33433: प्र-ह्वण, अम्, n. bowing down in reverence.
33434: प्र-ह्वाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. bent forwards, bent, bowed, stooping.
33435: प्रह्वल् प्र-ह्वल्, cl. 1. P. -ह्वलति, -लितुम्, to stagger forwards, quake, tremble.
33436: प्रह्वलीका प्र-ह्वलीका, f. an incorrect form for प्र-वल्हिका, q. v.
33437: प्रह्वे प्र-ह्वे, cl. 1. P. A. -ह्वयति, -ते, -ह्वातुम्, to call to, call upon, call, summon, invoke.
33438: प्र-ह्वाय, अस्, m. calling, summoning, invoking, invocation.
33439: प्रा 1. प्रा [cf. rt. पॄ], cl. 2. P. प्राति, पप्रौ, प्रास्यति, अप्रासीत् (Ved. अप्रास्), प्रायात् or प्रेयात्, प्रातुम्, Ved. to fill: Pass. प्रा-यते, to be filled or full.
33440: 2. प्रा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. filling (at the end of comps.; cf. अन्तरिक्ष-प्रा, क्रतु-प्रा).
33441: 1. प्राण, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see under 1. प्राण्, p. 654, col. 3), filled, full, replete.
33442: प्रात, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. filled, full (Sāy. = पूर्ण).
33443: प्राति, इस्, f. filling; the span of the thumb and forefinger.
33444: प्रांशु प्रांशु (प्र-अं°), उस्, उस्, उ, high, tall, lofty, of great stature; long; (उस्), m., N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata; of a son of Vatsa-prī (or Vatsa-prīti). —प्रांशु-ता, f. height, loftiness. —प्रांशु-लभ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be obtained or reached (only) by a tall person.
33446: प्राकट्य प्राकट्य, अम्, n. publicity, mani-festation, notoriety.
33447: प्राकर प्राकर, अस्, m., N. of a son of Dyuti-mat; (अम्), n., N. of the Varṣa called after Prākara.
33448: प्राकरणिक प्राकरणिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्र-करण), appertaining to the subject of discussion, belonging to a chapter, belonging to a class or genus.
33449: प्राकर्ष प्राकर्ष, अम्, n. (fr. प्र-कर्ष), N. of a Sāman.
33450: प्राकर्षिक, अस्, ई, अम्, deserving preference.
33451: प्राकषिक प्राकषिक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कष् with प्र-आ), a dancer employed by a woman, one supported by another's wife; a catamite.
33452: प्राकाम्य प्राकाम्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्र-काम), freedom of will; wilfulness, following or obeying one's own will or inclination; irresistible will or fiat (one of the eight attributes of Śiva).
33453: प्राकार प्रा-कार, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. कॄ and प्रा for प्र), an encircling wall, enclosure, fence, rampart (especially a surrounding wall elevated on a mound of earth). —प्राकार-कर्ण, अस्, m. ‘wall-ear,’ N. of a minister of the owl-king Ari-mardana. —प्राकार-भञ्जन, अस्, ई, अम्, breaking down ramparts. —प्राकारमर्दि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Prākāra-mardin. —प्राकार-मर्दिन्, ई, m. ‘rampart-crusher,’ N. of a man. —प्राकार-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing on a wall, stationed on a rampart.
33454: प्राकारीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for a wall, of or be-longing to a wall; enclosed by a wall, walled.
33455: प्राकारुक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. कॄ with प्र-आ?), Ved. scattering about (?).
33456: प्राकाश प्राकाश, अस्, m. (fr. प्र-काश), Ved. a metallic mirror; (according to some commentators) a kind of ornament.
33457: प्राकाश्य, अम्, n. the being evident or manifest, publicity; celebrity, fame, renown.
33458: प्राकृ प्रा-कृ (प्र-आ-कृ), cl. 8. P. A. -क-रोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, Ved. to drive away.
33459: प्राकृत प्राकृत, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. प्र-कृति), original, natural, not artificial, essential, unchanged, unaltered, unmodified; normal, ordinary, usual, com-mon, uncultivated, unrefined, provincial, plebeian, vulgar; vernacular; (in the Sāṅkhya phil.) belong-ing to or derived from Prakṛti or the original ele-ment; (in astronomy) an epithet of one of the seven divisions of the planetary courses, (according to Parāśara comprising the Nakṣatras Svāti, Bha-raṇī, Rohiṇī, and Kṛttikā); प्राकृतो लयः or प्रलयः or प्रति-सञ्चरः, resolution or reabsorp-tion into Prakṛti or the original element, the disso-lution of the universe; (अस्), m. a low man, a man following a degraded profession; (अम्), n. any pro-vincial or vernacular dialect akin to Sanskrit, espe-cially spoken by the female characters and the inferior personages of plays. —प्राकृत-काम-धेनु, उस्, f., N. of a Prākṛt grammar. —प्राकृत-चन्द्रिका, f., N. of a Prākṛt grammar by Vara-ruci (= प्राकृत-प्रकाश); also of one by Vāmanā-cārya. —प्राकृत-ज्वर, अस्, m. common or usual fever (occurring from affections of the wind in the rainy season, of the bile in the autumn, and of the phlegm in the spring). —प्राकृत-त्व, अम्, n. original or natural state or condition. —प्राकृत-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary on the Saṅkṣipta-sāra. —प्रा-कृत-पाद, अस्, m., N. of a Prākṛt grammar by Nārāyaṇa. —प्राकृत-पिङ्गल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), Piṅgala's work on Prākṛt metres. —प्रा-कृत-प्रकाश, अस्, m., N. of a Prākṛt grammar by Vara-ruci (= प्राकृत-चन्द्रिका). —प्राकृत-प्रलय, अस्, m. the total dissolution of the world. —प्राकृत-भाषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, talking or speaking Prākṛt. —प्राकृत-मनोरमा, f., N. of Bhā-maha's commentary on the Prākṛta-prakāśa; (also called Mano-ramā.) —प्राकृत-मानुष, अस्, m. a common or ordinary man. —प्राकृत-मित्र, अम्, n. a natural friend or ally, a sovereign whose king-dom is separated by that of another from the country with which he is allied; [cf. प्राकृतारि, प्राकृतो-दासीन।] —प्राकृत-लक्षण, अम्, n., N. of a work ascribed to Pāṇini. —प्राकृत-लङ्केश्वर (°का-ईश्°), अस्, m. (?), N. of a Prākṛt grammar. —प्रा-कृत-शासन, अम्, n. a manual of the Prākṛt dia-lects. —प्राकृत-सर्वस्व, अम्, n., N. of a Prākṛt grammar by Mārkaṇḍeya-kavīndra. —प्राकृतारि (°त-अरि), इस्, m. a natural enemy, a sovereign of an adjacent country (whose dominions intercept those of the Prākṛta-mitra, q. v.). —प्राकृतोदासीन (°त-उद्°), अस्, m. a natural neutral, a sovereign whose dominions are situated beyond those of the natural ally.
33460: प्राकृतायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Pra-kṛta.
33461: प्राकृतिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to Pra-kṛti or the original element, material, natural, illusory.
33463: प्राक्रियाकौमुद प्राक्रियाकौमुद, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to the Prakriyā-kaumudī, q. v.
33464: प्राक्षालन प्राक्षालन, an incorrect form for प्र-क्षालन, q. v.
33465: प्राखर्य प्राखर्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्र-खर), sharpness; pungency; ardour; wickedness.
33466: प्रागद्य प्रागद्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. प्र-गदिन्), see Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
33468: प्रागल्भ्य प्रागल्भ्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्र-गल्-भ), boldness, confidence; resoluteness, determina-tion; pride, arrogance, effrontery; pomp, parade, rank; proficiency. —प्रागल्भ्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of confidence, bold; vain, proud.
33469: प्रागहि प्रागहि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher.
33470: प्रागहीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or referring to Prāgahi.
33471: प्रागाथ प्रागाथ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्र-गाथ), belonging to the Pragāthas, i. e. to the eighth Maṇḍala of the Ṛg-veda; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Kali; of Bharga; of Haryata.
33472: प्रागाथिक, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the eighth Maṇḍala of the Ṛg-veda.
33473: प्रागार प्रागार, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), a building, a house; a principal building (?).
33475: प्राग्र प्राग्र (प्र-अग्°), अम्, n. the highest point, summit. —प्राग्र-सर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, going at the head, foremost, first, best. —प्राग्र-हर, अस्, ई, अम्, taking the best share, chief, principal.
33476: प्राग्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, chief, principal, most excellent.
33477: प्राग्राट प्राग्राट, अम्, n. thin coagulated milk.
33478: प्राघर्मसद् प्राघर्म-सद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. abid-ing in a region of light; (Sāy. = प्रकर्षेण दीप्त-स्थाने वर्तमानः।)
33479: प्राघात प्राघात, अस्, m. war, battle; (in-correctly for प्र-घात।)
33480: प्राघार प्राघार, अस्, m. (fr. rt. घृ with प्र), dropping, oozing, trickling out, aspersion or pouring out of any oily substance.
33481: प्राघुण प्राघुण, अस्, m. a guest, a visitor, one demanding hospitality; [cf. प्राहुण।]
33482: प्राघुणक or प्राघुणिक, अस्, m. = प्राघुण।
33483: प्राघूर्णक or प्राघूर्णिक, अस्, m. various forms for प्राघुणक, प्राघुणिक above.
33484: प्राङ्ग प्राङ्ग, अस्, m. a small kind of drum or tabor (= पणव).
33485: प्राङ्गण or प्राङ्गन, अम्, n. a court, a yard, a court-yard [cf. अङ्गन, अङ्गण]; a kind of drum.
33487: प्राचण्ड्य प्राचण्ड्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्र-चण्ड), violence, vehemence, passion.
33488: प्राचार प्राचार (प्र-आच्°), अस्, आ, अम्, con-trary to or deviating from ordinary institutions and observances (?); (अस्), m. a particular insect.
33489: प्राचार्य (प्र-आच्°), अस्, m. a pupil, scholar (?).
33490: प्राचिन्वत् प्राचिन्वत्, अन्, m., N. of a son of Janam-ejaya (= प्र-चिन्वत्).
33492: प्राचीर प्राचीर, अम्, n. an enclosure, hedge, fence, wall; [cf. क्षौणी-प्°, मही-प्°।]
33493: प्राचुर्य प्राचुर्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्रचुर), mul-titude, quantity; abundance, copiousness, plentiful-ness, plenty; (एण), ind. in a mass; fully, in detail.
33494: प्राचेतस् प्राचेतस्, असस्, m. pl. an epithet of the ten sons of Prācīna-barhis (= प्र-चेतस्).
33495: प्राचेतस, अस्, m. a patronymic from Pra-cetas; a patronymic of Manu; of Dakṣa; of Vālmīki.
33497: प्राछ् प्राछ्, ट्, ट्, ट् (fr. rt. प्रछ्), asking, inquiring, an inquirer, questioner. —प्राड्-विवाक, अस्, m. ‘one who interrogates and discriminates,’ a judge, magistrate, the presiding officer in a court of judicature (Manu VIII. 79, 181).
33498: प्राजक प्राजक, अस्, m. (fr. rt. अज् with प्र), a driver, charioteer, coachman.
33499: प्राजन, अस्, अम्, m. n. a whip, goad.
33501: प्राजितृ, ता, m. a driver, charioteer, coachman.
33503: प्राजया प्राजया, see Gaṇa Sākṣādādi to Pāṇ. I. 4, 74.
33504: प्राजहित प्राजहित, अस्, m., Ved. a Gārha-patya fire maintained during a longer period of time, an older Gārhapatya fire.
33505: प्राजापत प्राजापत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रजा-पति), see Gaṇa Mahiṣyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 4, 48.
33506: प्राजापत्य, अस्, आ (or ती), अम्, belonging to or derived from Prajā-pati, relating to Prajā-pati, sacred to Prajā-pati; (अस्), m., with or without विवाह or विधि, the third or according to Manu the fourth form of marriage (that in which the father gives his daughter to the bridegroom without receiving a present from him, but with the convic-tion that the two will live faithfully together, Manu III. 30); scil. उपवास, a kind of penance (lasting twelve days, food being eaten during the first three once in the morning, during the next three once in the evening, in the next three only if given as alms, and a plenary fast being observed during the three remaining days); scil. तिथि, the eighth day in the dark half of the month Pauṣa; a patronymic of Pataṅ-ga; of Prajā-vat; of Yakṣma-nāśana; of Yajña; of Vimada; of Viṣṇu; of Saṃvaraṇa; of Hiraṇya-garbha; (with Jainas) N. of the first black Vāsudeva; a N. of the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, = प्र-याग; (अम्), n. a particular sacrifice performed before appointing a daughter to raise issue in default of male heirs; scil. भ or नक्षत्र, the asterism Rohiṇī; generative energy, procreative power; (अस् or अम्), m. or n. (?), the heaven or sphere of the Manes, = पितृ-लोक; (आ), f. giving away the whole of one's property before entering upon the life of an ascetic or mendicant; a patro-nymic of Dakṣiṇā; scil. शकटी, N. of an asterism, the chariot of Rohiṇī (probably = α β γ δ ε Tauri). —प्राजापत्य-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of belonging or referring to Prajā-pati.
33507: प्राजापत्यक, अस्, &c., belonging or referring or sacred to Prajā-pati.
33508: प्राजावत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रजा-वत्), see Gaṇa Mahiṣyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 4, 48.
33509: प्राजेश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रजेश), Ved. sacred to Prajā-pati; (अम्), n. the Nakṣatra Rohiṇī.
33510: प्राजेश्वर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रजेश्वर), sacred to Prajā-pati.
33511: प्राजिधर प्राजिधर, अस्, m., N. of a man.
33512: प्राजिमठिका प्राजिमठिका, f., N. of a place.
33514: प्राज्ञ प्राज्ञ, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. प्र-ज्ञा), intellectual, (opposed to शारीर, तैजस); intelligent, wise, clever; patient in investigation; (Ved.) having no deep insight; (अस्), m. a wise or learned man, a Paṇḍit, a skilful or clever man; a kind of parrot with red stripes on the neck and wings; (आ or ई), f. a clever or intelligent woman; (ई), f. the wife of an intellectual man, wife of a Paṇḍit; (आ), f. intelligence, understanding. —प्राज्ञ-कथा, f. a story of a wise man, tale about a wise man. —प्राज्ञ-त्व, अम्, n. or प्राज्ञ-ता, f. wisdom, learning. —प्राज्ञ-मान, अम्, n. respect for learned men. —प्राज्ञ-मानिन् or प्राज्ञम्-मानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, thinking one's self wise, fancying one's self a learned man.
33515: प्राज्य प्राज्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. प्र with rt. अज् or fr. प्र + आज्य, clarified butter used for obla-tions?), abundant, plentiful, much, many, great, im-portant; lofty. —प्राज्य-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Rājāvali-patākā. —प्राज्य-विक्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, possessing great power. —प्राज्य-वृष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, sending rain in abundance (said of Indra).
33516: प्राञ्च् प्राञ्च् (प्र-अञ्च्), प्राङ्, प्राची, प्राक्, turned towards the front, directed forwards, being before, in front, foremost; turned towards, inclined towards, disposed, ready, willing (Ved.); turning eastward, eastern, easterly; previous, prior, former; प्राञ्चं कृ, to place in front, bring, offer, provide (Ved.); to promote, further, advance (Ved., Sāy. = प्रकर्षेण गच्छन्तं कृ); to spread out, stretch out (Ved.); प्राञ्चस्, m. pl. the people of the east, eastern people; eastern grammarians; प्राचि, f. the east; प्राक्, ind. (with abl. or rarely with gen. or acc.), before (in place or time or order), in front; up to, as far as (especially in the technical language of grammatical Sūtras, e. g. प्राक् कडारात्, up to the word Kaḍāra); in the east; first, at first, formerly, previously, in the former part (of a book); at dawn, at day-break, early in the morning; प्राग् एव, recently, just; (in Buddhist writings) = किम् उत, how much more? much more, still more; प्राचा, ind., Ved. forwards, onwards; (Sāy.) = ऋजुना मार्गेण, by a straight path; प्राचस्, ind., Ved. from the front. —प्राक्-कर्मन्, अ, n. preparatory or preliminary medical treatment; an action done in a former life. —प्राक्-कल्प, अस्, m. a former age or era. —प्राक्-काल, अस्, m. a former age or time, a previous time. —प्राक्कालीन, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to former or ancient times, pertaining to a previous time, anterior, ancient, previous, former. —प्राक्-कूल, अस्, आ, अम्, having the points turned towards the east (said of blades of Kuśa grass; ac-cording to Kullūka on Manu II. 75 = प्राग्-अग्र); (अम्), n. the point of a blade of Kuśa grass turned towards the east; (also written प्राक्-तूल; cf. प्राचीन-कूल।) —प्राक्-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done be-fore; (अम्), n. an action done in a former life. —प्राक्-केवल, अस्, आ, अम्, manifested from the first in a distinct form (without preliminary symp-toms, as a disease). —प्राक्-चरणा, f. an epithet of the female organ of generation. —प्राक्-चिरम्, ind. before it is too late, in good time. —प्राक्-छाय, अम्, n. a shadow's falling eastward. —प्राक्-तनय, अस्, m. a former pupil (perhaps a wrong reading for प्राप्त-नय). —प्राक्-तूल = प्राक्-कूल, q. v. —प्राक्-पद, अम्, n. a preceding word, the first member of a compound. —प्राक्-पुण्य-प्रभव, अस्, आ, अम्, caused by merits accrued in a former existence, resulting from good works done in a former state of being. —प्राक्-पुष्पा, f., see Vārtt. 1. to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 64. —प्राक्-फल, अस्, m. the bread-fruit tree (= पनस). —प्राक्-फल्गुनी, f. the eleventh of the lunar mansions (= पूर्व-फल्गुनी, q. v.). —प्राक्फल्गुनी-भव, अस्, m. Bṛhaspati or the planet Jupiter (born when the moon was in the mansion Prākphalgunī). —प्राक्-फाल्गुन or प्राक्फाल्गुनेय, अस्, m. the planet Jupiter. —प्राक्-फाल्गुनी = पूर्व-फाल्गुनी, q. v. —प्राक्-शस्, ind. from the front, from the east. —प्राक्-शिरस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, or प्राक्-शिरस or प्राक्शिरस्क, अस्, आ, अम्, having the head turned forwards or to the east. —प्राक्-शृङ्ग-वत्, आन्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi. —प्राक्-श्लिष्ट, a various reading for प्राश्लिष्ट, q. v. —प्राक्-संस्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, turned or directed eastwards. —प्राक्-सन्ध्या, f. morning twilight. —प्राक्-सवन, अम्, n. a morning libation. —प्राक्-सोम, अस्, आ, अम्, or प्राक्-सौमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, preceding the Soma sacrifice. —प्राक्-स्रोतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, flowing eastward (sometimes wrongly spelt प्राक्-श्रोतस्). —प्राग्-अग्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having the tip or point turned forwards or towards the east (as a blade of grass). —प्राग्-अपम्, ind. (fr. प्राक् and अपम् fr. अपाक्), Ved. from the front towards the back, in a backward direction. —प्राग्-अपरायत (°र-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, extending eastward and westward; [cf. प्राग्-आयत।] —प्राग्-अभाव, अस्, m. previous non-existence of anything, antecedent non-existence or privation, the non-existence of any-thing which may yet be; non-existence (of an effect) previous (to production); (in law) the non-possession of property that may be possessed. —प्रा-गभाव-विचार, अस्, m., N. of a Nyāya work. —प्राग्-अभिहित, अस्, आ, अम्, before-mentioned, pre-viously mentioned. —प्राग्-अवस्था, f. a former state, previous existence. —प्राग्-आयत, अस्, आ, अम्, extend-ing towards the east; [cf. प्राग्-अपरायत।] —प्राग्-आह्निक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the forenoon (= पौर्वाह्णिक). —प्राग्-उक्ति, इस्, f. previous utter-ance. —प्राग्-उत्तर, अस्, आ, अम्, north-eastern; (एण), ind. to the north-east of (with abl.), north-eastwards. —प्राग्-उदक्-प्लवन, अस्, आ, अम्, in-clining towards the north-east, situated in a north-easterly direction. —प्राग्-उदङ्मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having the face turned to the east or north. —प्राग्-उदञ्च्, अङ्, ईची, अक्, north-eastern; (ईची), f., scil. दिश्, the north-east quarter, the north-east; (अक्), ind. to the north-east. —प्राग्-गमन-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a forward motion, going forwards. —प्राग्-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going before, preceding, intending to go before; a precursor. —प्राग्-गुण, अस्, आ, अम्, pos-sessing the previously mentioned quality. —प्राग्-ग्रीव, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the neck turned towards the east. —प्राग्-जन्मन्, अ, n. a former birth, former life. —प्राग्-जाति, इस्, f. a former birth (= पूर्व-जन्-मन्). —प्राग्-ज्योतिष, अम्, n., N. of a city, the dwelling-place of the demon Naraka; (अस्), m., with or without राजा, the king of Prāg-jyotiṣa, an epithet of Bhaga-datta; N. of a country, = काम-रूप; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people living in the city of Prāg-jyotiṣa or its environs; (अम्), ind. before day-break (?), —प्राग्ज्योतिष-ज्येष्ठ, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu. —प्राग्-दक्षिण, अस्, आ, अम्, south-eastern; (अम्), ind. to the south-east, south-eastwards. —प्राग्-दक्षिणाञ्च् (°ण-अञ्च्), आङ्, आची, आक्, turned to the south-east, south-eastward. —प्राग्-दण्ड, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the stem or stalk turned towards the east. —प्राग्-दिश्, क्, f. ‘the eastern quarter,’ the east. —प्राग्-देश, अस्, m. the eastern country, country of the eastern people; a former or previous place. —प्राग्-द्वार्, र्, f. a door on the east side. —प्राग्-द्वार, अस्, आ, अम्, having doors towards the east; an epithet of the seven lunar mansions beginning with Kṛttikā; (ए), ind. in front of or before the door. —प्राग्द्वारिक, अस्, ई, अम्, having the door on the eastern side. —प्राग्-बोधि, N. of a mountain. —प्राग्-भक्त, अम्, n. taking medicine before a meal. —प्राग्-भाग, अस्, m. the fore part. —प्राग्-भार, अस्, m. the top or peak of a moun-tain; a multitude, heap; bending, inclining, leaning [cf. प्राचीन-प्°]; (अस्, आ, अम्), inclined, bent. —प्राग्-भाव, अस्, m. prior or previous existence; superiority, excellence; the top of a mountain (in this sense a various reading for प्राग्-भार). —प्राग्-भाव-तस्, ind. from a prior state of existence. —प्राग्-रूप, अम्, n. symptom of disease (= पूर्व-रूप)। —प्राग्-वंश, अस्, आ, अम्, having the supporting beam turned eastwards (Ved.); (अस्), m. the space before the Vedi, (perhaps) a kind of sacrificial chamber having columns or beams towards the east and situ-ated opposite to the Vedi, (according to Malli-nātha on Raghu-v. XV. 61 = प्राचीन-स्थूणो यज्ञ-शाला-विशेषः; according to others, a room in which the family and friends of the person performing the sacrifice assemble); a former dynasty or generation; an epithet of Viṣṇu (?). —प्राग्-वचन, अम्, n. a for-mer decision; anything formerly decided or decreed. —प्राग्-वट, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a city. —प्राग्-वत्, ind. as before, as previously, as for-merly, as in former times, as in the preceding part (of a book). —प्राग्-वृत्त, अम्, n. former behaviour; (in law) = प्राङ्-न्याय, q. v. —प्राग्-वृत्तान्त, अम्, n. a former event, previous adventure, a story of the past. —प्राग्-वेष or प्राग्-वेश, अस्, m. a former dress. —प्राग्-हार, a various reading for प्राग्-भार, q. v. —प्राङ्-आयत, an incorrect form for प्राग्-आयत, q. v. —प्राङ्-नासिका or प्राङ्-नासिकी, f., see Scholiast on Pāṇ. IV. 1, 60. —प्राङ्-न्याय, अस्, m. (in law) a former trial of a cause, the plea of a former trial, special plea; (अस्, आ, अम्), Ved. turned forwards or eastwards according to rule. —प्राङ्न्या-योत्तर (°य-उत्°), अम्, n. the rejoinder of the defendant that the charge against him has already been tried. —प्राङ्-मुख, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, having the face turned forward or towards the east, facing the east (Manu II. 51); inclined towards, desirous of, wishing. —प्राचा-जिह्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. moving the tongue forwards (said of Agni; Sāy. = प्राग्-देश-स्थित-जिह्वा-स्थानीय-ज्वाल). —प्राचा-मन्-यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. striving to move forwards (said of Indra; Sāy. = अप्रतिहत-क्रोध). —प्राची-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of the east,’ an epithet of Indra. —प्राची-मूल, अम्, n. the eastern horizon.
33517: प्राक्तन, अस्, ई, अम्, former, prior, previous, anterior, antecedent, preceding; early, old, ancient, (opposed to इदानीन्तन); relating to a former state of existence, resulting from acts done in a former life. —प्राक्तन-कर्मन्, अ, n. any act formerly done or done in a former state of existence; fate, destiny. —प्राक्तन-जन्मन्, अ, n. a former birth.
33518: प्राक्तस् or प्राक्तात्, ind., Ved. from the front, from the east.
33519: प्रागिवीय (fr. प्राग् इव), see Pāṇ. V. 3, 70.
33521: प्राग्दिशीय (fr. प्राग् दिशः), see Scholiast on Pāṇ. V. 3, 2.
33522: प्राग्दीव्यतीय (fr. प्राग् दीव्यतः), see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 83.
33523: प्राग्धितीय, a wrong reading for प्राग्घितीय।
33524: प्राचा, ind. See p. 653, col. 3, and p. 654, col. 1.
33525: प्राचिका, f. a musquito; a female falcon.
33526: प्राचीन, अस्, आ, अम्, turned towards the front or towards the east, belonging to the front or east, eastern, easterly; former, prior, preceding, ancient, old; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a hedge, fence, wall; (आ), f. a species of plant, Clypea Hernandifolia; (अम्), ind. in front, forwards; eastwards, to the east of (with abl.); before (with abl.); अतः प्राचीनम्, further on from that point. —प्राचीन-आवीतिन् = प्राचीना-वीतिन्, q. v. —प्राचीन-कल्प, अस्, m. a former Kalpa or period of the world's duration. —प्राचीन-कूल, अस्, आ, अम्, = प्राक्-कूल, q. v. —प्राचीन-गर्भ, अस्, m., N. of an ancient Ṛṣi also called Apāntara-tamas. —प्राचीन-गाथा, f. an ancient story or tradition. —प्राचीन-गौड, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Saṃvatsara-pradīpa. —प्राचीन-ग्रीव, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the neck turned forwards or towards the east. —प्राचीन-ता, f. or प्राचीन-त्व, अम्, n. anti-quity, oldness. —प्राचीन-तिलक, अस्, m. ‘having a mark towards the east (?),’ the moon. —प्राचीन-पक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the feathers turned forwards (as an arrow). —प्राचीन-पनस, अस्, m. ‘the eastern Jaka tree,’ the plant Ægle Marmelos. —प्राचीन-प्रक्रिया, f., N. of a grammatical work (= प्रक्रिया-कौमुदी). —प्राचीन-प्राग्भार, अस्, आ, अम्, bending or inclining towards the east. —प्राचीन-बर्हिस्, इस्, m. ‘eastern light (?),’ N. of a Prajā-pati of the race of Atri; of a son of Havir-dhāman (or Havir-dhāna) and father of the ten Pracetasas; of a son of Manu; an epithet of Indra. —प्राचीन-मत, अम्, n. an ancient opinion, a belief sanctioned by antiquity. —प्राचीन-योग, अस्, m., N. of a man; of an ancient teacher, the father of Patañjali. —प्राचीनयोगी-पुत्र, अस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher. —प्राचीनयोग्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Prācīna-yoga; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school. —प्रा-चीन-रश्मि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having the reins directed forwards (Sāy. = देवाभिमुख). —प्राचीन-वंश, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the supporting beam turned forwards or towards the east; [cf. प्राग्-वंश।] —प्राचीन-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a commentary on the Uṇādi-sūtras. —प्राचीन-शाल, अस्, m., N. of a man. —प्राचीन-शिव-स्तुति, इस्, f. an ancient hymn in praise of Śiva. —प्राचीनाग्र (°न-अग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the points turned towards the east (said of sacred grass). —प्राचीनामलक (°न-आम्°), अस्, m. the plant Flacourtia Cataphracta; (अम्), n. the fruit of the Flacourtia Cataphracta. —प्राचीनावीत (°न-आव्°), अम्, n. the sacrificial cord worn over the right shoulder and passed under the left arm (as at a Śrāddha). —प्राचीनावीतिन् (°न-आव्°), ई, इनी, इ, or प्राचीनोपवीत (°न-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, wearing the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder and under the left arm (Manu II. 63).
33527: प्राचैस्, ind., Ved. forwards; [cf. उच्चैस्, नीचैस्, पराचैस्।]
33528: प्राच्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in front, situated in front; being in the east, living in the east, belonging to the east, eastern, easterly; preceding, prior, ante-rior, previous; ancient, old, (opposed to आधुनिक); an epithet of particular songs belonging to the Sāma-veda; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of the east, the eastern country, the country south or east of the river Sarasvatī (which flows from the north-east towards the south-west); (आ), f., scil. भाषा, the dialect spoken in the east of India. —प्राच्य-पद-वृत्ति, इस्, f. (in Ved. gram.) a term applied to the rule according to which ए remains in particular cases unchanged before अ. —प्राच्य-भाषा, f. the dialect of the east of India. —प्राच्य-वृत्ति, इस्, f. a kind of metre. —प्राच्य-सप्तसम, see Scholiast on Pāṇ. VI. 2, 12. —प्राच्याध्वर्यु, see Scholiast on Pāṇ. VI. 2, 10.
33529: प्राच्यक, अस्, आ, अम्, situated in the east, eastern, easterly.
33530: प्राच्यायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Prācya.
33531: प्राञ्ज् प्राञ्ज् (प्र-अञ्ज्), cl. 7. P. प्राणक्ति, प्राञ्जितुम्, प्राङ्क्तुम्, Ved. (?), to adorn, deco-rate, embellish, beautify.
33532: प्राञ्जन, अम्, n., Ved. paint or cement (on an arrow).
33533: प्राञ्जल प्राञ्जल, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. प्र + अञ्-जलि?), straight; honest, upright, sincere. —प्राञ्जल-ता, f. straightness; honesty.
33534: प्राञ्जलि प्राञ्जलि (प्र-अञ्°), इस्, इस्, इ, hold-ing out the open hands slightly hollowed and placed side by side (as if to hold an offering; a common mark of respect and salutation, cf. अञ्जलि, कृताञ्-जलि); joining the palms of the hands in a suppli-cating manner (Manu II. 192). —प्राञ्जलि-द्वैत-भृत्, तस्, m. pl., N. of a school.
33537: प्राडाहति प्राडाहति, इस्, m. a patronymic; see Gaṇa Taulvalyādi to Pāṇ. II. 4, 61.
33539: प्राण् 1. प्राण् or प्रान् (प्र-अण् or प्र-अन्), cl. 2. P. प्राणिति (according to Vopa-deva IX. 27, also प्रानिति), &c., to breathe in; inhale, inspire; to blow (as the wind, Ved.); to live; to smell (intrans.): Caus. P. A. प्राणयति, -ते, Aor. प्राणिणत्, to cause to breathe, give life to, animate: Desid. प्राणिणिषति।
33540: 2. प्राण् (प्र-अण्), ण्, ण्, ण्, breathing (?); see Pāṇ. VIII. 4, 20.
33541: 2. प्राण, अस्, m. (for 1. see under rt. 1. प्रा, p. 652), breathing, breath, respiration, inspiration and expira-tion, breath of life, spirit, vital action or life generally, vitality; a vital organ, organ of sense, vital air, (the vital airs are variously enumerated as three, viz. प्राण, अपान, and व्य्-आन; or five, viz. प्राण, अपान, सम्-आन, व्य्-आन, उद्-आन; or with the other vital organs six or seven, or nine or ten, or thirteen; the fivefold enumeration being however the most usual; and the first of the five or प्राण being used from its seat in the lungs to express pre-eminently life and vitality); air inhaled, wind; circulation of nutriment, digestion; the place of breathing, the mouth and nose (?); any one as dear as the breath of life, any beloved object (e. g. त्वम् मे प्राणः, thou art as dear to me as the breath of life; cf. पति-प्राण); the spirit (as opposed to the body); the spirit or life of a poem, poetical talent, inspiration; the soul (= पुरुष); vigorous action, energy, strength, power, might [cf. यथा-प्राणाम्]; breathing, aspiration (in the pronunciation of letters); a breath as a measure of time, viz. the time required for the pronunciation of ten long syllables = (1/6) Vināḍikā; N. of a Kalpa, the sixth day in the light half of a month of Brahmā; myrrh; a mystical expression for the letter य्; an epithet of Brahma the Supreme Spirit; N. of a son of the Vasu, Dhara; of one of the eight Vasus; of a Marut; of one of the seven sages in the second Manv-antara; of a son of Dhātṛ; of a son of Vi-dhātṛ the brother of Dhātṛ; (आस्), m. pl. the five vital airs or modes of inspiration and expiration collectively (see above); life, vitality, the vital organs or organs of sense, (according to Kullūka, Manu IV. 143, प्राणाः = चक्षुर्-आदीनीन्द्रियाणि); (प्रा-णान् मुच्, to resign or lay down one's life; प्राणान् हा or परि-त्यज्, to quit life; प्राणान् रक्ष्, to save life; प्राणान् नि-हन्, to destroy life); प्रा-णैस्, ind. with all the soul, with all the strength, with might and main; [cf. Gr. φρήν, ὀσ-φραίνομαι; Cambro-Brit. fion, ‘the breath or respiration, a puff of breath, a sigh.’] —प्राण-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘life-making,’ refreshing the spirits; (अस्), m., N. of the father of the author of the Medinī. —प्रा-ण-कर्मन्, अ, n. a vital function. —प्राण-कृच्-छ्र, अम्, n. danger to life, peril of life. —प्राण-कृष्ण, अस्, m., N. of an author of various works. —प्राण-ग्रह, अस्, m., N. of a particular Soma vessel. —प्राण-घातक, अस्, ई, अम्, life-destroying, de-structive to life, killing. —प्राण-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, life-destroying, deadly, mortal. —प्राण-च्छिद्, त्, त्, त्, cutting off life, shortening life, murderous. —प्रा-ण-च्छेद, अस्, m. the cutting off of life, murder. —प्राण-तोषणी, f., N. of a compendium of Tantra works. —प्राण-त्याग, अस्, m. abandonment of life, expiring, death, suicide. —प्राण-द, अस्, आ, अम्, life-giving, saving life; (अस्), m. a species of plant, = जीवक; (आ), f. the plant Terminalia Chebula (= हरीतकी); a species of medicinal plant, = ऋद्धि; (अम्), n. water; blood. —प्राण-दक्षिणा, f. the gift of life; प्राणदक्षिणां दा, to grant any one his life. —प्राण-दण्ड, अस्, m. the punishment of death. —प्राण-दयित, अस्, आ, अम्, dear as life; (अस्), m. a husband. —प्राण-दातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, a life-giver, one who saves another's life. —प्राण-दान, अम्, n. the gift of life, saving any one's life; resigning or laying down life; anointing the Havis with Ghṛta during the recitation of sacred texts supposed to restore life (Ved.). —प्राण-दावत्, आन्, m., Ved. life-giving, conferring life. —प्राण-दुरोदर, अम्, n. playing or gambling for life, staking life. —प्राण-द्यूत, अम्, n. staking life or existence, a battle for life, fighting for life. —प्राण-द्यूताभिदेवन (°त-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, played or fought with life as a stake (said of a battle in which life is as it were gambled with or staked, see Mahā-bh. Śalya-p. 760). —प्राण-द्रोह, अस्, m. an attack or attempt upon (any one's) life. —प्राण-धर, अस्, m., N. of a man. —प्राण-धार, अस्, आ, अम्, possessing life, living, animate; (अस्), m. a living being. —प्राण-धारण, अम्, n. the support or maintenance of life, prolongation of life, suste-nance; a means of supporting life; retaining life, vitality. —प्राण-धृक्, क्, क्, Ved. sustaining the breath, prolonging the act of inhaling the breath; [cf. धृक्, p. 459, col. 1.] —प्राण-नाथ, अस्, m. ‘lord of life,’ a husband, lover; an epithet of Yama; N. of a heresiarch who held a controversy with Śaṅkara at Pra-yāga. —प्राण-नाश, अस्, m. de-struction or cessation of breath. —प्राण-निग्रह, अस्, m. checking or obstructing the breath. —प्राण-पत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्राण-पति), see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 84. —प्राण-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of life,’ the soul; a husband; the heart (?). —प्राण-पत्नी, f. ‘wife of the vital breath,’ the voice. —प्राण-परि-क्रय, अस्, m. the price of life, staking one's life or existence. —प्राण-परिक्षीण, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose life is drawing to a close. —प्राण-परि-ग्रह, अस्, m. possession of breath or life, life, existence. —प्राण-परित्याग, अस्, m. abandoning or resigning life. —प्राण-परीप्सा, f. desire of sav-ing life, wish to escape. —प्राण-पा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. life-protecting, preserving life. —प्राण-प्रद, अस्, आ, अम्, life-bestowing, restoring life, saving life; (आ), f. a species of medicinal plant (= ऋद्धि)। —प्राण-प्रदायक, अस्, इका, अम्, or प्राण-प्रदायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, life-bestowing, restoring life, saving life. —प्राण-प्रयाण, अम्, n. departure of the breath of life, end of life. —प्राण-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, dear as life; (अस्), m. a lover. —प्राण-बाध, अस्, m. danger to life, fear for life, extreme peril. —प्रा-ण-बुद्धि, इस्, f. sing. (?), life and intelligence. —प्राण-भक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘breath-eating,’ ‘air-eating,’ inhaling merely the odour of food or drink. —प्राण-भय, अम्, n. fear for one's life, danger to life. —प्राण-भास्वत्, वान्, m. the ocean (‘the light of life?’). —प्राण-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, being the breath of life. —प्राण-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, supporting life (Ved.); containing life, possessed of life, living, sentient; (त्), m. a living being, a man; an epithet of particular bricks used in the erection of an altar. —प्राण-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. consisting of breath, endowed with breath or life, living, breathing. —प्राणमय-कोष, अस्, m. one of the cases or investitures of the soul, the vital case. —प्राण-मोक्षण, अम्, n. giving up the ghost, resigning life, suicide. —प्राण-यम, अस्, m. sus-pending the breath (= प्राणायाम). —प्राण-यात्रा, f. support of life, subsistence. —प्राणयात्रिक, अस्, आ, अम्, necessary for the support of life. —प्राणयात्रिक-मात्र, अस्, ई, अम्, possessing only the necessaries of life. —प्राण-योनि, इस्, f. the source or spring of life. —प्राण-रक्षणार्थम् (°ण-अर्°), ind. for the preservation of life. —प्राण-रक्षा, f. protec-tion or preservation of life. —प्राण-रन्ध्र, अम्, n. ‘breath-aperture,’ the mouth; nostril. —प्राण-रोध, अस्, m. checking or suppressing the breath; danger to life; N. of a particular hell. —प्राण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having breath or life, breathing, living, animated; possessing power, strong, powerful. —प्रा-ण-विद्या, f. the science of the breath or vital airs. —प्राण-विनाश, अस्, m. destruction or loss of life. —प्राण-विप्लव, अस्, आ, अम्, depriving of life. —प्राण-वियोग, अस्, m. ‘the separation of breath or life,’ the departure of the spirit at the hour of dissolution, death. —प्राण-वृत्ति, इस्, f. living, acti-vity, vital function. —प्राण-व्यय, अस्, m. ‘expen-diture of life,’ giving up the ghost, death. —प्राण-शक्ति, इस्, f. a particular Śakti of Viṣṇu. —प्राण-शरीर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. whose (only) body is the breath of life or spirit. —प्राण-संयम, अस्, m. checking or suspending the breath (as a religious exercise). —प्राण-संरोध, अस्, m. checking or obstructing the breath. —प्राण-संवाद, अस्, m. a controversy between the vital airs, dispute between the organs of sense (an imaginary contest or con-troversy between the senses supposed to be disputing for precedence). —प्राण-संशय, अस्, m. danger to life. —प्राण-संहिता, f. a manner of reciting the Vedic texts, pronouncing as many letters as possible during one breath. —प्राण-सङ्कट, अम्, n. danger to life, great peril. —प्राण-सद्मन्, अ, n. the abode of the vital airs, the body. —प्राण-सन्त्याग, अस्, m. abandoning or resigning life. —प्राण-सन्देह, अस्, m. danger to life, risk of life, great peril. —प्राण-सन्न्यास, अस्, m. giving up the ghost, dying. —प्राण-सम, अस्, आ, अम्, equal to or as dear as life; (अस्), m. a lover, a husband; (आ), f. a wife. —प्राण-सम्भृत, अस्, m. wind, air; (perhaps a wrong form for प्राण-सम्-भूत।) —प्राण-सम्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. reaching to the nose; dear as life. —प्राण-सार, अस्, आ, अम्, whose whole essence consists of life, spirited, full of strength, vigorous. —प्राण-सूत्र, अम्, n. the thread of life. —प्राण-हर, अस्, ई, अम्, taking away life, threatening life, causing death, destructive. —प्राण-हारक, अस्, इका, अम्, taking away life, causing death; (अम्), n. a kind of poison (= वत्स-नाभ)। —प्राण-हारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, taking away life, causing death, mortal, deadly. —प्राणाकर्षिन् (°ण-आक्°), ई, इणी, इ, attracting the vital spirit. —प्राणाग्निहोत्र (°ण-अग्°), अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of an Upaniṣad. —प्राणाघात (°ण-आघ्°), अस्, m. destruction of life, killing a living being. —प्राणाचार्य (°ण-आच्°), अस्, m. a physician to a king. —प्राणातिपात (°ण-अत्°), अस्, m. an attack upon life, taking away life, kill-ing a living being. —प्राणात्मन् (°ण-आत्°), आ, m. the vital or animal soul, the lowest of the three souls of a human being (the other two are called जीवात्मन् and परमात्मन्, q. q. v. v.). —प्राणात्यय (°ण-अत्°), अस्, m. the passing away of life; (ए), ind. at a time when life is in danger of ceasing. —प्राणाद (°ण-आद), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘eating away life,’ causing death, fatal. —प्राणाधिक (°ण-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘more than life,’ dearer than life; superior in vigour. —प्राणाधिनाथ (°ण-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of life,’ a husband. —प्राणाधिप (°ण-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘ruler of the breath of life,’ the soul. —प्राणान्त (°ण-अन्°), अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), the end of life, death; प्राणान्तं दण्डम् अर्हति, he deserves death as a punishment, i. e. he deserves the punishment of death. —प्राणान्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, destructive to life, fatal, mortal, capital (as punishment); dangerous; last-ing to the end of life, ending with life; (अम्), n. murder, assassination; (अम्), ind. until death. —प्राणाप-हारिन् (°ण-अप्°), ई, इणी, इ, taking away life, fatal, deadly. —प्राणापान (°ण-अप्°), औ, m. du. two of the vital airs, air inhaled and exhaled; Inspiration and Expiration personified and identified with the Aśvins. —प्राणाबाध (°ण-आब्°), अस्, m. injury or danger to life, any act injurious to life. —१। प्राणायन (°ण-अय्°), अम्, n. an organ of sense. —प्राणायाम (°ण-आय्°), अस्, m. restraining or suspending the breath or breathing in a peculiar way through the nostrils during the mental recitation of the names or attributes of some deity, (it is differently performed, cf. पूरक, कुम्भक, रेचक।) —प्राणायामिन् (°ण-आय्°), ई, इनी, इ, checking or suppressing the breath. —प्राणार्थ-वत् (°ण-अर्°), आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of life and riches. —प्राणेश (°ण-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of life,’ a lover, husband; ‘lord of breath,’ N. of a Marut; (आ), f. a wife. —प्राणेश्-वर (°ण-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of (my) life,’ a hus-band, lover; a particular formula; (ई), f. a wife. —प्राणोत्क्रमण (°ण-उत्°), अम्, n. the departure of the spirit, flight of the soul, death. —प्राणोत्-सर्ग (°ण-उत्°), अस्, m. giving up the ghost, dying. —प्राणोपहार (°ण-उप्°), अस्, m. food (regarded as an oblation to life).
33542: प्राणक, अस्, m. a living being, an animal or sentient being; a species of plant (= जीवक); myrrh; cloth, clothes (?).
33543: प्राणत्, अन्, अती, अत्, breathing, living.
33544: प्राणथ, अस्, m. breathing; air, wind; the lord of all created beings (= प्रजा-पति); a sacred bathing-place; (अस्, आ, अम्), strong, powerful.
33545: प्राणन, अस्, m. the throat; (अम्), n. the act of breathing, respiration; living, life; producing life, calling into life; (अस्, आ, अम्), giving life to, pro-ducing life. —प्राणनान्त (°न-अन्°), अस्, m. the end of life.
33546: प्राणन्त, अस्, m. air, wind; a kind of collyrium, = रसाञ्जन; (ई), f. sneezing; sobbing.
33547: प्राणयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, restoring to life, resusci-tating, reanimating.
33548: 2. प्राणायन, अस्, m., Ved. the offspring of the vital airs (in Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā XIII. 54; according to Mahī-dhara प्राणायन = प्राणस्यापत्य).
33549: प्राणिणिषु, उस्, उस्, उ (see Pāṇ. VIII. 4, 21), wishing to breathe or live, wishing for life.
33550: प्राणित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to breathe, kept alive, animated, longing to do (anything).
33551: प्राणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, breathing, living, alive; (ई), m. a living or sentient being, living creature, animal; a man. —प्राणि-घातिन्, ई, इनी, इ, killing living beings. —प्राणि-जात, अम्, n. a class or species of animals. —प्राणि-त्व, अम्, n. the state of a living being, sentient existence, life. —प्राणि-द्यूत, अम्, n. gambling with fighting animals, setting animals to fight for wagers, a fight of animals exhibited for sport, cock-fighting, ram-fighting, &c. —प्राणि-पीडा, f. giving pain to sentient beings, cruelty to animals. —प्राणि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of or peopled with living beings. —प्राणि-मातृ, ता, f. the mother of a living being; a kind of shrub (= गर्भ-दात्री)। —प्राणि-योधन, अम्, n. setting animals to fight (= प्राणि-द्यूत above). —प्राणि-हिंसा, f. doing harm to any living creature, injuring or killing an animal. —प्राणि-हित, अस्, आ, अम्, favourable or good for living beings; (आ), f. a shoe, a boot, (in this sense probably for प्राणहिता, q. v.) —प्राण्य्-अङ्ग, अम्, n. a part or limb of an animal or man, any animal product (as flesh, bone, milk, ghee, &c.).
33552: प्राणतज प्राणतज, आस्, m. pl. (with Jainas) N. of a subdivision of the Kalpa-bhavas.

33554: प्राणाय्य प्राणाय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, proper, fit, suited.
33555: प्राणावाय प्राणावाय, अम्, n., N. of the twelfth of the fourteen Pūrvas or ancient writings of the Jainas.
33556: प्राणाह प्राणाह, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. नह् with प्रा), Ved. cement (used in building).
33557: प्राणीत्य प्राणीत्य, अम्, n. (probably incor-rect for प्रामीत्य), debt.

(fr. 1. प्र), early in the morning, at day-break, at dawn [cf. अभि-प्°]; on the next morning, to-morrow morning, early on the morrow, to-morrow; Morning personified as a son of Puṣpārṇa and Prabhā; प्रातः प्रातः, every morning; [cf. Gr. πρωΐ; Old Germ. fro, fruo; Mod. Germ. frühe.] —प्रातः-कर्मन्, अ, or प्रातः-कार्य, अम्, n. morning business, a morning ceremony; [cf. प्रातः-कृत्य below.] —प्रातः-काल, अस्, m. morning-time, the early time of day, early morning, first break of day. —प्रातः-कृत्य, अम्, n. matutinal duty, morning ceremonies, a reli-gious duty performed in the morning (as worship, ablution, purification, &c.). —प्रातः-प्रहर, अस्, m. the morning watch, the first part of the day (from six to nine o'clock); प्रातः-प्रहरे गते, the morning watch being past, at nine o'clock in the morning. —प्रातः-सन्ध्या, f. morning twi-light, dawn, the morning devotions of a Brāhman; morning sacrifice. —प्रातः-समय, अस्, m. the morning-time, early morning, day-break. —प्रातः-सव, अस्, m. or प्रातः-सवन, अम्, n. the morning libation of Soma (accompanied with ten ceremonial observances, viz. the प्रातर्-अनुवाक, अभि-षव, बहिष्-पवमान-स्तोत्र, सवनीयाः पशवः, धिष्ण्य्-उपस्थान, सवनीयाः पुरोडाशाः, द्वि-देवत्य-ग्रहाः, द्वि-देवत्य-भक्ष, ऋतु-या-जाः, आज्य or प्रüग शस्त्र). —प्रातःसवनिक or प्रातःसवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging or relating to the morning libation of Soma. —प्रा-तः-साव, अस्, m., Ved. the morning preparation of Soma, morning libation. —प्रातः-स्नान, अम्, n. bathing at sun-rise, morning ablution. —प्रातः-स्नायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bathing early in the morning. —प्रातर्-अनुवाक, अस्, m., Ved. ‘morning recita-tion,’ the hymn recited at the commencement of the Prātaḥ-savana. —प्रातर्-अभिवाद, अस्, m., Ved. morning salutation. —प्रातर्-अह्न, अस्, m. the early part of the day, forenoon; N. of a man. —प्रातर्-आश, अस्, m. the morning meal, breakfast, (अ-प्रातराश, not breakfasting.) —प्रातराशित, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has had the morning meal, one who has breakfasted. —प्रातर्-आहुति, इस्, f., Ved. the morning oblation, the second half of the daily Agni-hotra sacrifice. —प्रातर्-इत्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. going out early in the morning; coming at day-break, an early guest (Sāy. = प्रातर् आगतः). —प्रातर्-गेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sung or chanted in the morning; (अस्), m. a minstrel employed to wake the king in the morning. —प्रातर्-जित्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. victorious at day-break; conquering the morning. —प्रातर्-दिन, अम्, n. the early part of the day, forenoon. —प्रातर्-दुग्ध, अम्, n., Ved. morning milk. —प्रातर्-दोह, अस्, m. milking in the morn-ing, morning milk. —प्रातर्-भोक्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who makes an early meal; (ता), m. a crow. —प्रातर्-भोजन, अम्, n. the morning meal, breakfast. —प्रातर्-यावन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. going out early in the morning, an early guest [cf. प्रातर्-इत्वन्]; (आणा), m. du. an epithet of the Aśvins (Sāy. = प्रातर् एव यज्ञ-गन्तारौ). —प्रातर्-युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. yoked or harnessed early in the morning. —प्रातर्-युज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. yoking or harnessing early in the morning; yoked or harnessed early in the morning (said of a chariot, Sāy. = प्रातः-काले ऽश्वैर् युज्यमानः); (जा), m. du. an epithet of the Aśvins (Sāy. = प्रातः-सवन-ग्र-हेण संयुक्तौ). —प्रातर्-वस्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. shining in the morning; [cf. दोषा-वस्तृ।] —प्रातर्-होम, अस्, m. the morning sacrifice. —प्रातस्-तराम्, ind. very early in the morn-ing. —प्रातस्-त्रिवर्गा, f. an epithet of the river Gaṅgā (Mahā-bh. Anuśāsana-p. 1846).
33560: प्रातस्तन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to the morning, matutinal; (अम्), n., Ved. early morning (the first of five parts of the day, the other four being सङ्-गव or morning, midday, afternoon, and evening).
33561: प्रातस्त्य, अस्, &c., belonging or relating to the morning, matutinal.

33563: प्रातर्दन प्रातर्दन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to or derived from Pra-tardana.
33564: प्राति प्राति। See under rt. 1. प्रा, p. 652.
33565: प्रातिकण्ठिक प्रातिकण्ठिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-कण्ठम्), seizing by the throat (?).
33566: प्रातिका प्रातिका, f. the China rose, Hibis-cus Rosa Sinensis (= जवा).
33567: प्रातिकामिन् प्रातिकामिन्, ई, m. (fr. प्रति-कामम्), a servant, a messenger.
33568: प्रातिकूलिक प्रातिकूलिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-कूल), opposed to, opposing.
33569: प्रातिकूल्य, अम्, n. contrariety, adverseness, con-tradiction, hinderance, opposition, resistance, hostility, unfriendliness, unpleasantness.
33570: प्रातिजनीन प्रातिजनीन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-जन), suitable against an adversary.
33571: प्रातिज्ञ प्रातिज्ञ, अम्, n. (fr. प्रति-ज्ञा), the subject under discussion.
33572: प्रातिथेयी प्रातिथेयी, f. (fr. प्र-तिथि), N. of a female sage; (also read प्रातीथेयी।)
33573: प्रातिदैवसिक प्रातिदैवसिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-दिवसम्), happening or occurring daily.
33574: प्रातिनिधिक प्रातिनिधिक, अस्, m. (fr. प्रति-निधि), Ved. a substitute, proxy.
33575: प्रातिपक्ष प्रातिपक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-पक्ष), belonging to an enemy, hostile; adverse, contrary.
33576: प्रातिपक्ष्य, अम्, n. hostility, enmity; अस्मा-कम् प्रातिपक्ष्यम्, enmity against us.
33577: प्रातिपथिक प्रातिपथिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्र-तिपथिक), going along a road or path.
33578: प्रातिपद प्रातिपद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. प्रति-पद्), forming the beginning or commencement; (अस्), m., N. of a man.
33579: प्रातिपदिक, अम्, n. the crude form or base of a noun, a crude word or noun as formed by either Kṛt or Taddhita affix before receiving a case-termination, a noun in its uninflected state, (when the case-termina-tion is added, the प्रातिपदिक becomes a पद or real word); (अस्), m. an epithet of fire; (अस्, ई, अम्), in express terms, express, explicit; [cf. प्रति-प-दम्।] —प्रातिपदिकानुरोध (°क-अन्°), अस्, m. conformity with the words or express terms of any statement; (आत्), ind. in conformity with express terms, expressly.
33580: प्रातिपीय प्रातिपीय or प्रातिपेय, अस्, m. a patronymic of Balhika.
33581: प्रातिपौरुषिक प्रातिपौरुषिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति + पौरुष), relating or belonging to manliness or valour.
33582: प्रातिबोध प्रातिबोध, अस्, m. a patronymic from Prati-bodha; see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 104.
33583: प्रातिबोधायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Prati-bodha; see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. IV. 1. 100.
33584: प्रातिभ प्रातिभ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-भा), belonging or relating to divination; (अम्), n., scil. ज्ञान, divination; quick apprehension or conception.
33585: प्रातिभाव्य प्रातिभाव्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्रति-भू), the act of becoming bail or surety, suretiship, being answerable for the appearance of the debtor or for his being trustworthy or for the payment of his debt in case of his failing to do it.
33586: प्रातिभासिक प्रातिभासिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-भास), having only the appearance of, exist-ing only in appearance; bearing a resemblance, re-sembling, looking like.
33587: प्रातिरूप्य प्रातिरूप्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्रति-रूप), similarity of form, &c.
33588: प्रातिलोमिक प्रातिलोमिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-लोम), against the hair or the grain, contrary to natural course or order, hostile, disagreeable.
33589: प्रातिलोम्य, अम्, n. contrary direction, contrariety, inverted order, inversion, the being at variance with the natural or established order of things, reverse-ness; opposition, hostility, hostile feeling; (आत्), ind. out of opposition to.
33590: प्रातिवेशिक प्रातिवेशिक, अस्, m. (fr. प्रति-वेश), a neighbour.
33591: प्रातिवेश्मक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-वेश्मन्), be-longing to a neighbour's house, neighbouring; (अस्), m. a neighbour.
33592: प्रातिवेश्य, अस्, m. a neighbour who lives opposite, a next-door neighbour, (according to Kullūka = नि-रन्तर-गृह-वासिन्); a neighbour in general.
33594: प्रातिशाख्य प्रातिशाख्य, अम्, n. (fr. प्रति-शाखम्), a grammatical treatise on the rules regu-lating the euphonic combination of letters and their pronunciation peculiar to one of the different Śākhās or branches of the Vedas, i. e. to one of those versions of the Vedic texts handed down in different families in different parts of India, (the Prātiśākhyas do not undo words in the same way as the Vyākaraṇa, but take actually formed words as they occur in the hymns and teach the phonetic changes they undergo, the mode of pronouncing the accents, &c.; there exist four Prātiśākhyas, 1. a Prātiśākhya to the Śākala-śākhā of the Ṛg-veda, called Śākala-prāti-śākhya and ascribed to Śaunaka; 2. to a Śākhā of the Taittirīya or Black Yajur-veda; 3. to a Śākhā of the Mādhyandinas who belong to the family of the Vājasaneyins or authors of the White Yajur-veda, whence this is called the Vājasaneyi-prātiśākhya, it is attributed to Kātyāyana; 4. an Atharva-veda-prā-tiśākhya, called Śaunakīyā Caturādhyāyikā; but no Prātiśākhya has yet been found to the Sāma-veda.) —प्रातिशाख्य-कृत्, त्, m. the author of a Prātiśā-khya. —प्रातिशाख्य-भाष्य, अम्, n., N. of a com-mentary by Ūaṭa on the Ṛg-veda-prātiśākhya.
33595: प्रातिश्रुत्क प्रातिश्रुत्क, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-श्रुत्), Ved. existing in the echo.
33596: प्रातिस्विक प्रातिस्विक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-स्व), own, peculiar, proper, not common to others; granting to every one his own due.
33597: प्रातिहत प्रातिहत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रति-हत), epithet of a particular Svarita (= तैरोवि-राम, q. v.).
33598: प्रातिहन्त्र, अम्, n. (fr. प्रति-हन्तृ), the state or condition of a revenger; vengeance.
33599: प्रातिहर्त्र प्रातिहर्त्र, अम्, n. (fr. प्रति-हर्तृ, rt. हृ with प्रति), the office or duty of the Prati-hartṛ, q. v.
33600: प्रातिहार, अस्, m. (fr. प्रति-हार), a juggler.
33602: प्रातिहारिक, अस्, ई, अम्, containing Prati-hāras (as a Vedic hymn); (अस्), m. a juggler, conjurer.
33603: प्रातिहार्य, अम्, n. juggling, conjuring, legerde-main; working miracles; a miracle, miraculous phe-nomenon.
33604: प्रातीतिक प्रातीतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रतीति), existing in the mind or imagination, mental.
33605: प्रातीथेयी प्रातीथेयी, a various reading for प्रातिथेयी, q. v.
33606: प्रातीप प्रातीप, अस्, m. (fr. प्रतीप), a patronymic of Śāntanu.
33607: प्रातीपिक, अस्, ई, अम्, contrary, reverse, retrograde.
33608: प्रातृद प्रातृद, अस्, m. a patronymic from Pra-tṛd.
33609: प्रात्यक्ष प्रात्यक्ष or प्रात्यक्षिक, अस्, ई, अम्, perceptible to the eyes, &c. (= प्रत्यक्ष, q. v.).
33610: प्रात्यग्रथि प्रात्यग्रथि, इस्, m. a patro-nymic from Pratyag-ratha.
33611: प्रात्यन्तिक प्रात्यन्तिक, अस्, m. (fr. प्रत्य्-अन्त), a prince of the Pratyantas; a lord of the marches, keeper of the borders (?).
33612: प्रात्ययिक प्रात्ययिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रत्य्-अय), relating to or attended with confidence or trust, confidential, trusty, having faith in; (अस्), m., scil. प्रति-भू, a surety for the trustworthiness of a debtor.
33613: प्रात्यवेक्षा प्रात्यवेक्षा, wrongly for प्रत्य्-अवेक्षा, q. v.
33614: प्रात्यहिक प्रात्यहिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्रत्य्-अहम्), occurring or happening every day, daily.
33615: प्राथमिक प्राथमिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. प्र-थम), belonging or relating to the first, primary, first, initial, initiative, prior, previous; happening or occurring for the first time.
33616: प्राथमकल्पिक, अस्, m. (fr. प्रथम + कल्प), one who has just commenced the perusal of the Vedas, a student; a term applied to a Yogi just commencing his course.
33617: प्राथम्य, अम्, n. the being first, priority, pre-cedence.
33618: प्राद् प्राद् (प्र-अद्), cl. 2. P. प्रात्ति, प्रात्-तुम्, to eat up, consume, devour.
33619: प्रादक्षिण्य प्रादक्षिण्य, अस्, m. (fr. प्र-दक्षिण), keeping the right side towards anything while moving round it, circumambulation by starting from the left and coming round to the right (by way of reverence).
33620: प्रादा प्रा-दा (प्र-आ-), cl. 3. P. A. -ददाति, -दत्ते, -दातुम्, to give, bestow.
33621: प्रादाय, ind. having given or bestowed.
33622: प्रादित्य प्रादित्य (प्र-आद्°), अस्, m., N. of two princes.
33623: प्रादुराक्षि प्रादुराक्षि, इस्, m. a patronymic; (perhaps an incorrect form for प्रादुर्-अक्षि।)
33624: प्रादुस् प्रादुस्, ind. (perhaps fr. प्रा for 1. प्र + 1. दुर्, i. e. before or outside the door, in open daylight; said to be fr. rt. अद् with प्र; accord-ing to Pāṇ. VIII. 3, 41, the final स् is changed into ष् before क् and प्; and according to Pāṇ. VIII. 3, 87, the radical स् of rt. 1. अस्, ‘to be,’ is changed to ष् after प्रादुस् whenever in the conjugation of this rt. the initial अ is dropped, e. g. प्रादुः षन्ति, not प्रा-दुः सन्ति; प्रादुस् appears to occur only in con-nection with the rts. 1. अस्, 1. भू, and 1. कृ, except in the comp. प्रादुष्-पीतम् given as an example by the Scholiast on Pāṇ. VIII. 3, 41); apparently, evidently, manifestly, visibly, in sight. According to native lexicographers the senses in which प्रादुस् is used may be expressed by the following Sanskrit words, प्राकाश्य, नामन्, सम्-भाव्य, सम्-भव, प्र-वृत्ति, वृत्ति।
33625: प्रादुर्-अस् (see rt. 1. अस्), cl. 2. P. अस्ति, &c., to be apparent or evident, to be manifest; to appear, arise, exist.

33627: प्रादुष्-कृ, cl. 8. P.
