37639: मुर, अस्, m., N. of a Daitya slain by Kṛṣṇa; (आ), f. a species of fragrant plant (named after the Daitya); said to be the N. of the wife of Nanda and mother of Candra-gupta; (अम्), n. encompass-ing, surrounding. —मुर-जित्, त्, m. ‘conqueror of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुर-द, अस्, m. ‘Mura-cutting,’ the discus of Viṣṇu. —मुर-द्विष्, ट्, m. ‘foe of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुर-भिद्, त्, m. ‘cleaver of Mura,’ epi-thet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुर-मर्दन, अस्, m. ‘crusher of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुर-रिपु, उस्, m. ‘enemy of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुर-वैरिन्, ई, m. ‘enemy of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुर-हन्, हा, m. ‘slayer of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. —मुरारि (°र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu; N. of the author of the Murāri-nāṭaka or Anargha-rāghava; N. of a commentary on the Kātantra grammar. —मुरारि-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a pupil of Caitanya. —मुरारि-नाटक, अम्, n., N. of a drama by Mu-rāri, = Anargha-rāghava. —मुरारि-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a teacher. —मुरारि-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of a scholar, = Murāri (author of the Murāri-nāṭaka). —मुरारि-विजय, अस्, m., N. of a drama.
37640: मुरगण्ड मुरगण्ड, अस्, m. an eruption on the face (= वरण्ड).
37642: मुरचीपत्तन मुरची-पत्तन, N. of a town in the Dekhan, (also read मरीचि-पत्तन।)
37643: मुरज मुरज, अस्, m. (thought by some to be a comp. of मुर + ज), a kind of drum, tam-bourine; a Śloka artificially arranged in the form of a drum; (आ), f. a great drum; N. of Kuvera's wife. —मुरज-फल, अस्, m. the jack fruit tree, Arto-carpus Integrifolia.
37644: मुरजक, अस्, m., N. of one of Śiva's attendants.
37645: मुरण्ड मुरण्ड, अस्, m. a country to the north-west of Hindūstān (called also Lampāka, and now Lamghan in Cabul); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; [cf. मुरुण्ड।]
37646: मुरन्दला मुरन्दला, f., N. of a river (= मुरला; thought by some to be Narma-dā).
37647: मुरमण्ड मुरमण्ड (probably incorrect) for मुरगण्ड, q. v.
37648: मुरल मुरल, अस्, m. (probably fr. rt. 4. मुर्), a species of fresh-water fish; a king of the Muralas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f., N. of a river in the country of the Keralas, = मुरन्-दला, q. v.; (ई), f. a flute, pipe. —मुरली-धर, अस्, m. ‘flute-bearer,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa.
37649: मुरलिका, f., N. of a woman.
37650: मुरवार मुरवार, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Turuṣkas.
37651: मुरसिदाबाद मुरसिदाबाद, N. of a city (مرشد آباد).
37652: मुराद मुराद, अस्, m. a proper N.
37653: मुरु मुरु, उस्, m., N. of a country; N. of a Daitya slain by Kṛṣṇa [cf. मुर]; (said to be) a species of plant (in explanation of मौर्वी); a kind of iron. —मुरु-देश, अस्, m., N. of a country; [cf. मरु-देश।]
37654: मुरुङ्गी मुरुङ्गी, f. Moringa Pterygos-perma, (also spelt मुरङ्गी।)
37655: मुरुण्ड मुरुण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a king; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, [cf. Μαροῦνδαι, a people mentioned by Ptolemy.]
37656: मुरुण्डक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain in Udyāna.
37657: मुरुताणदेश मुरुताण-देश, अस्, m., N. of a country.
37658: मुर्छ् मुर्छ्, cl. 1. P. मूर्छति, मुमूर्छ, मूर्छिष्यति, अमूर्छीत्, मूर्छितुम्, to settle into a fixed or solid form, assume definite shape or substance, acquire consistency; to congeal, become dense, thicken, coagulate, stiffen; to become torpid or stupefied, become senseless, lose conscious-ness, faint away, swoon, be troubled in mind; to be infatuated; to increase, grow, become strong, gather strength, become stronger or more intense, acquire vehemence or power, be powerful or effectual, take effect, (मारुतस्य रंहः शिलोच्छये न मूर्-छति, the velocity of the wind has no power against a mountain); to be a match for; to be frequent; to fill, penetrate, pervade; to make to sound loudly, play loudly: Caus. मूर्छयति, -यितुम्, to cause to settle into a fixed or solid form, give form to, form (Ved.); to congeal, curdle (Ved.); to stupefy, cause to faint, make senseless; to strengthen, augment; to excite; to cause to sound loudly, play (a musical instrument).
37659: मूर्ख, अस्, आ, अम्, stupid, foolish, silly, igno-rant, dull, unintelligent; inexperienced in (with loc.); (अस्), m. a fool, blockhead; a sort of bean, Phaseolus Radiatus. —मूर्ख-ता, f. or मूर्ख-त्व or मूर्ख-भूय, अम्, n. stupidity, folly, foolishness, dulness. —मूर्ख-भ्रातृक, अस्, m. one who has a foolish brother. —मूर्ख-मण्डल, अम्, n. a collection or assemblage of fools. —मूर्ख-व्यसनि-नायक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a foolish and vicious commander. —मूर्ख-शत, अम्, n. a hundred fools. —मूर्खी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to become stupid or foolish.
37660: मूर्खिमन्, आ, m. dulness, stupidity, folly (= मूर्ख-ता).
37661: मूर्छत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming senseless, faint-ing, swooning.
37662: मूर्छन, अस्, ई, अम्, stupefying, causing insen-sibility (applied to one of the five arrows of Kāma-deva or Cupid); strengthening, augmenting, con-firming; (अम्, आ), n. f. fainting, swooning, syncope; vehemence, violence, prevalence, growth, increase, (in this sense usually अम्, n.); swelling or rising of sounds, an intonation, note, a tone or semitone in the musical scale, the seventh part of a Grāma or scale, (each Grāma or scale consisted of seven notes and contained also seven Mūrchanās); modulation, melody, (in these senses usually आ, f.); a particular process in metallic preparations, calcining quicksilver with sulphur, (in this sense only अम्, n.)

37664: मूर्छा, f. fainting, loss of consciousness, a swoon, stupor; spiritual stupor or blindness, delusion, hallu-cination; the rising of sounds, diatonic scale; a par-ticular process in calcining metals. —मूर्छाक्षेप (°छा-आक्°), अस्, m. (in rhetoric) expressing vehement dissent or disapprobation by fainting. —मूर्छा-परीत, अस्, आ, अम्, overcome with faintness or swooning, fainting away, insensible, (according to a Scholiast = निश्चेतन।) —मूर्छा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, suffering from faintness, swooning away.
37665: मूर्छाल, अस्, आ, अम्, fainting, fainted, swooning, insensible.
37666: मूर्छित, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, rendered sense-less, fainted, fainting, insensible, bewildered, infatu-ated; intoxicated; stupid, ignorant; rendered vehe-ment or violent, intensified; grown, increased, aug-mented, swollen; rising upwards, lofty; filled with; calcined (as quicksilver; cf. मूर्छन); (अम्), n. epithet of a kind of song or air.
37667: मूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, thickened, congealed, coagu-lated, curdled (Ved.); settled into any fixed shape, formed, substantial, solid, material, corporeal, em-bodied, incarnate; real (said of the practically useful division of time as opposed to the अ-मूर्त, the unreal or imaginary division); stupefied, unconscious, fainted, insensible. —मूर्त-त्व, अम्, n. the posses-sion of a form, embodiment, corporality, incarnate existence, materiality. —मूर्त-मात्र, अम्, n. that which is merely material, only corporeal.
37668: मूर्ति, इस्, f. (often written मूर्त्ति), any solid body, any tangible or material form, (in philosophy) anything which has definite shape and limits (as earth, air, fire, water, and mind, but not आकाश, ether), a material element (especially as a component part of the human body), body, form, visible shape, matter, substance; embodiment, manifestation, in-carnation, personification, (मूर्तिर् धर्मस्य शाश्-वती, an eternal personification of justice; cf. तपो-म्°); an image, statue, figure, form; beauty; N. of the first astrological house; N. of a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma; (इस्), m., N. of one of the sages under the tenth Manu; [cf. perhaps Gr. βρέτας, μορφή.] —मूर्ति-तस्, ind. from the form, bodily, substantially. —मूर्ति-त्व, अम्, n. the being or having a body, corporeity, embodiment, materiality, (मूर्तित्वे परिकल्पितः, made into bodily shape.) —मूर्ति-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, having a body, em-bodied, corporeal, incarnate. —मूर्ति-प, अस्, m. ‘image-keeper,’ a priest who guards an idol. —मूर्ति-भाव, अस्, m. the state of assuming a solid form, corporeity. —मूर्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a material or bodily form, material, embodied, corpo-real, incarnate, personified [cf. ख-म्°, विश्व-म्°]; (आन्), m., N. of a son of Kuśa; (अत्), n. a body. —मूर्ति-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, possessing a particular form. —मूर्ति-मात्रा, f. a particle of matter. —मूर्ति-लिङ्ग, perhaps = Prāg-jyotiṣa, the city of Naraka.
37669: मुर्भिणी मुर्भिणी, f. a chafing-dish, small fire-place, fire-pan.
37670: मुर्मुर मुर्मुर, अस्, m. (an onomatopoetic word), a fire made of chaff, burning chaff; the god of love; N. of one of the horses of the sun; (आ), f., N. of a river.

37672: मुल् मुल् = rt. मूल्, q. v.

37675: मुशल्लह मुशल्लह or मुसल्लह, an astro-logical term (مصالحة).

37686: मुषीवन्, आ, m. (मुषीवाणम्, acc. c.), Ved. a thief, robber.
37687: मुष्क, अस्, m. (perhaps originally ‘a little mouse,’ fr. मुष् = 2. मूष् + क), a testicle; the scrotum; a species of tree (= मुषक); a muscular or stout person (= मांसल); a thief; a crowd, heap, quantity, multitude, mass; (औ), m. du. pudenda muliebria. —मुष्क-कच्छू, ऊस्, f. an eruption on the scrotum. —मुष्क-देश, अस्, m. the region of the scrotum. —मुष्क-द्वय, अम्, n. the two testicles. —मुष्क-भार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having large testicles, (Sāy. = प्रवृद्ध-मुष्क।) —मु-ष्क-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having testicles; an epithet of Indra as author of Ṛg-veda X. 38. —मुष्क-शून्य, अस्, m. ‘one who is without testicles,’ a castrated person, eunuch, guard of the women's apartments. —मुष्क-शोफ, अस्, m. swell-ing of the testicles. —मुष्क-स्रोतस्, अस्, n. the vas deferens (in anatomy). —मुष्काबर्ह (°क-आब्°), अस्, m., Ved. one who gelds or castrates.
37688: मुष्कक, अस्, m. a species of tree (the ashes of which are used as a cautery).
37689: मुष्कर, अस्, आ, अम्, having testicles; (अस्), m. a man with large testicles; a species of small animal or insect (Atharva-veda VI. 14, 2).
37690: मुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, a rare form for मुषित, q. v.; (अम्), n. theft, robbery.
37691: मुष्टि, इस्, m. f. stealing, filching, pilfering; the closed or clenched hand (perhaps originally ‘the hand closed to grasp anything stolen’); the fist, (गूढाङ्गुष्ठ-कृत-मुष्टि, the clenched fist with the thumbs turned in); a fistful, handful [cf. दर्भ-म्°, कुश-म्°, केश-म्°, गाढ-म्°]; a par-ticular measure (= a handful = 1 Pala); a hilt or handle (of a sword, &c.); a compendium, abridg-ment; (according to Mahī-dhara on Vājasaneyi-s. XXIII. 24) the penis (= लिङ्ग); [cf. Old Germ. fust; Angl. Sax. fyst.] —मुष्टि-करण, अम्, n. clenching the fist. —मुष्टि-ता, f. firmness of grasp. —मुष्टि-देश, अस्, m. the part of a bow which is grasped in the hand, the middle of a bow. —मु-ष्टि-द्यूत, अम्, n. a kind of game, odd or even, (commonly called पुरमुट्खेला।) —मुष्टिन्-धम, अस्, ई, अम्, blowing into the closed hand. —मुष्टिन्-धय, अस्, आ, अम्, sucking the fist or closed hand; (अस्), m. a child, boy. —मुष्टि-पात, अस्, m. pummelling, boxing. —मुष्टि-प्र-हार, अस्, m. a blow with the fist. —मुष्टि-बन्-ध, अस्, m. clenching the fist, closing the hand (in taking hold of anything); a handful. —मुष्टि-बन्धन, अम्, n. the act of clenching the fist. —मुष्टि-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having a fist-like face. —मुष्टि-मेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be measured or spanned with the hand, (मध्येन मुष्टि-मेयेन, with a waist which might be spanned with the fingers.) —मुष्टि-युद्ध, अम्, n. a fight with fists, pugilistic encounter. —मुष्टि-सङ्ग्राह-पी-डित, अस्, आ, अम्, squeezed by a grasp with the fist, griped. —मुष्टि-हत्या, f., Ved. a hand to hand engagement. —मुष्टि-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ, Ved. fight-ing hand to hand (said of common soldiers as opposed to those who fought in chariots). —मुष्टी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to close the hand, clench the fist. —मुष्टी-कृत्य, ind. having clenched the fist. —मुष्टी-मुष्टि, ind. fist to fist, hand to hand fighting, fisticuffs.
37692: मुष्टिक, अस्, m. a particular position of the hands; a goldsmith; N. of an Asura; (आस्), m. pl., N. of an outcast race, = डोम्बास्; (आ), f. the fist, hand; (अम्), n. a fight with fists, pugilistic encounter, fisticuffs. —मुष्टिक-घ्न, अस्, m. ‘slayer of Muṣṭika,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu. —मुष्टिक-स्वस्-तिक, अस्, m. a particular position of the hands in dancing. —मुष्टिका-कथन, अम्, n. talking with the fingers. —मुष्टिकान्तक (°क-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘annihilator of Muṣṭika,’ an epithet of Bala-deva, the brother of Kṛṣṇa.
37693: मुष्णत्, अन्, अती, अत्, stealing, robbing, taking away, depriving of; captivating; excelling, surpass-ing, eclipsing.
37694: मुष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being robbed, being plundered.
37695: मुस्तु, उस्, m. f. = मुष्टि, the fist.
37697: मुष्ठक मुष्ठक, अस्, m. black mustard.
37698: मुस् मुस् [cf. rt. 2. मुष्, cl. 4], cl. 4. P. मुस्यति, &c., to break in pieces, cleave, divide, cut, destroy.
37699: मुसल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (often spelt मुषल and less correctly मुशल), a pestle, a kind of wooden pestle used for cleaning rice; a mace, club, (चक्र-मुसलः सङ्ग्रामः, a battle fought with discuses and clubs); a particular surgical instrument; a par-ticular constellation; the twenty-second astronomical Yoga or division of the moon's path; N. of a son of Viśvāmitra; (ई), f. the plant Curculigo Orchioides; Salvinia Cucullata; the house-lizard. —मुसला-मु-सलि, ind. club against club. —मुसलायुध (°ल-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, club-armed; (अस्), m. an epithet of Bala-deva. —मुसली-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भ-वितुम्, to become a club. —मुसलोलूखल (°ल-उल्°), अम्, n. a pestle and mortar.
37700: मुसलक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain; (इका), f. a common lizard.
37701: मुसलित, अस्, आ, अम्, see Gaṇa Tārakādi to Pāṇ. V. 2, 36.
37702: मुसलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, armed with a club; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva; of Bala-deva.
37703: मुसलीय or मुसल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, deserving to be pounded to death or to be put to death with a club.
37704: मुस्र, अम्, n. a pestle; a tear (in this sense = अश्रु, q. v.).
37705: मुसटी मुसटी, f. a white variety of Pani-cum Italicum, (also read मुशटी।)
37707: मुसारगल्व मुसारगल्व, coral or a kind of white coral.
37708: मुस्त् मुस्त्, cl. 10. P. मुस्तयति, मुस्त-यितुम्, to gather, collect, heap up, accu-mulate.
37709: मुस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. a species of grass, Cyperus Rotundus; (अम्), n. the root of the Musta grass; [cf. भद्र-म्°।] —मुस्त-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —मुस्ताद (°त-अद or °त-आद), अस्, m. ‘grass-eater,’ a hog, a wild boar. —मुस्ताभ (°त-आभ्°), अम्, n. a species of Cyperus.
37710: मुस्तक, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. a species of grass, Cyperus Rotundus; (अस्), m. a particular vegetable poison.
37713: मुह् 1. मुह्, cl. 4. P. मुह्यति, मुमोह, मोहिष्यति or मोक्ष्यति, अमुहत्, मो-हितुम् or मोग्धुम् or मोढुम्, to become stupe-fied or unconscious, to be faint, lose consciousness, to be perplexed or embarrassed; to be disturbed in mind; to err or be mistaken; to be foolish or stupid or infatuated; to fail: Caus. मोहयति, -यि-तुम्, Aor. अमूमुहत्, to stupefy, bewilder, per-plex, infatuate, deprive of consciousness; to throw into disorder; to cause to err; to mistake (A., e. g. अध्वानम् मोहयन्ते, they mistake the way): Intens. मोमुह्यते, मोमोग्धि, मोमोढि, to be in great perplexity or greatly embarrassed.
37714: मुग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, perplexed, stupid, ignorant; infatuated, enamoured; foolish, silly, sim-ple, mistaken, erring; inexperienced, artless, inno-cent, rendered attractive by youthful simplicity, charming, tender, lovely, beautiful; (आ), f. a young and beautiful female. —मुग्ध-कथा, f. a story of a fool, tale about a fool. —मुग्ध-ता, f. or मुग्ध-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity, silliness, ignorance; simplicity, artlessness, loveliness, charmingness, grace-fulness. —मुग्ध-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, lovely-eyed, hav-ing beautiful eyes. —मुग्ध-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or मुग्ध-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, silly, simple, a simpleton. —मुग्ध-बोध, अम्, n. ‘instructing the igno-rant’ (scil. व्याकरण), N. of a celebrated grammar by Vopa-deva (a grammarian who is supposed to have flourished in the thirteenth century, and who is regarded as a great authority in Bengal). —मुग्ध-बोध-परिशिष्ट, अम्, n. a supplement or appendix to the Mugdha-bodha. —मुग्धबोध-प्रदीप, अस्, m., N. of a commentary on the Mugdha-bodha. —मुग्धबोध-सम्बोधिनी, f., N. of a com-mentary on the Mugdha-bodha. —मुग्ध-बोधिनी, f., scil. टीका, N. of a commentary by Bharata-malla on the Amara-koṣa and of a commentary by Bha-rata-mallika (probably identical with the preceding author) on the Bhaṭṭi-kāvya. —मुग्ध-भाव, अस्, m. stupidity, simplicity, inexperience. —मुग्ध-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, perplexed, embarrassed, infatuated, mistaken. —मुग्धाक्षी (°ध-अक्°), f. a lovely-eyed woman. —मुग्धाग्रणी (°ध-अग्°), ईस्, m. the greatest of simpletons, the stupidest of the stupid. —मुग्धा-चक्र, अम्, n. a particular mystical circle. —मुग्धानन (°ध-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, lovely-faced.
37715: 2. मुह्, क्, क्, क्, or ट्, ट्, ट्, perplexing, embarrass-ing, infatuating; [cf. मनो-मुह्।]
37716: मुहिर, अस्, आ, अम्, foolish, stupid; (अस्), m. a blockhead [cf. मुहेर]; ‘the bewilderer,’ epithet of the god of love.
37717: मुहु, ind. = मुहुस्, Ved. suddenly, in a moment.
37718: मुहुक, अम्, n., Ved. a moment, instant; [cf. मुहूर्त।]
37719: मुहुस्, ind. (perhaps originally ‘in a bewildering manner’), suddenly, all at once, in a moment, in an instant (Ved.); for a moment, for a time, awhile; at every moment, repeatedly, constantly; मुहुस् — मुहुस्, at one moment — at another; at one time  — at another; मुहुर् मुहुस्, at every moment, repeatedly, again and again, over and over again; on the other hand; [cf. पुनर्।] —मुहुर्-गीर्, ईर्, ईर्, ईर्, Ved. swallowing suddenly; (Sāy.) ever being hymned (= सर्वदा गीयमानः). —मुहुर्-भा-षा, f. or मुहुर्-वचस्, अस्, n. repeating what is said, repetition, tautology. —मुहुर्-भुज्, क्, m. ‘constantly eating,’ a horse. —मुहुश्-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, occurring repeatedly, recurring over and over again. —मुहुस्-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, loving or desiring again and again. —मुहुस्-तनैस्, ind. at repeated intervals, repeatedly, constantly.
37720: मुहूर्त, अस्, अम्, m. n. a moment, an instant, any short space of time, (मुहूर्तात्, after an instant, immediately, directly, at once; मुहूर्तेन, after an instant, after a little while; कु-मुहूर्त, an inau-spicious moment, cf. दुर्-म्°, प्रति-म्°); a particu-lar division of time (see Manu 1. 64); the thirtieth part of a day, a period of forty-eight minutes; (अस्), m. an astrologer; (आस्), m. pl. the Muhūrtas or Hours personified as the children of Muhūrtā; (आ), f., N. of a daughter of Dakṣa (wife of Dharma or Manu and mother of the Muhūrtas). —मुहूर्त-कल्प-द्रुम, अस्, m. and मुहूर्त-गण-पति, इस्, m., N. of works. —मुहूर्त-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m., N. of an astrological work by Rāma the son of Ananta. —मुहूर्त-ज, आस्, m. pl. children of Mu-hūrtā; [cf. मौहूर्तिक।] —मुहूर्त-तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a work. —मुहूर्त-दीपक, अस्, m., N. of an astrological work by Mahā-deva. —मुहूर्त-दीपिका, f., N. of a work. —मुहूर्त-मार्तण्ड, अस्, m., N. of an astrological work by Nārāyaṇa. —मुहूर्त-वल्लभा, f., N. of a commentary on the Muhūrta-mārtaṇḍa. —मुहूर्त-स्तोम, आस्, m. pl., N. of an Ekāha.
37721: मुहूर्तक = मुहूर्त, a moment, instant; an hour.
37722: मुहेर, अस्, m. = मुहिर, a fool, blockhead; [cf. perhaps Gr. μῶρο-ς; Lat. moru-s, mor-osu-s.]
37723: मूढ, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, bewildered, per-plexed, confounded, confused [cf. दिङ्-म्°], uncer-tain how to act; infatuated; stupid, dull, silly, foolish, simple, ignorant; mistaken, deceived, erring, gone astray or adrift; wrong, out of the right place (as the fetus in delivery), abortive; causing confusion, confounding; epithet of a particular position in the Yoga system; (अस्), m. a fool, blockhead, dolt, idiot; a sluggard; (आस्), m. pl. an epithet of the elements in the Sāṅkhya philosophy. —मूढ-गर्भ, अस्, m. difficult delivery; a dead fetus. —मूढ-ग्राह, अस्, m. a confused notion, misconception, infatuation. —मूढ-चक्षुर्-गद-च्छेतृ, ता, m. the remover of the defect of vision of the foolish. —मूढ-चेतन, अस्, आ, अम्, or मूढ-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, bewildered in mind, foolish, simple, silly. —मूढ-ता, f. or मूढ-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity, infatuation, bewilderment, confusion, simplicity, folly, ignorance; error, mistake, (ग्रन्थि-मूढता, mis-take or confusion in disentangling a knot.) —मूढ-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or मूढ-बुद्धि, or मूढ-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, ‘silly-minded, ’ silly, simple, foolish. —मू-ढ-प्रभु, उस्, m. the chief of fools, a great blockhead. —मूढ-रथ, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants. —मूढ-वत्, ind. like a fool. —मूढ-सत्त्व, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘silly-minded,’ infatuated, insane. —मूढात्मन् (°ढ-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, bewildered or stupefied in mind, un-conscious, insensible, foolish, a fool. —मूढेश्वर (°ढ-ईश्°), अस्, m. the greatest of fools, a great sim-pleton, arrant blockhead; N. of an ascetic.
37726: मू 1. मू (connected with rts. मव्, मव्य्), cl. 1. A. मवते (sometimes P. -ति), to bind, tie, make fast: Caus. Aor. अमीमवत्: Desid. of Caus. मिमावयिषति, see Scholist on Pāṇ. VII. 4, 80.
37728: मूक, अस्, आ, अम्, dumb, silent, speechless, mute [cf. एड-म्°, कल्ल-म्°]; wretched, poor; (अस्), m. a mute; a poor man; N. of a Dānava; of a Nāga; [cf. 37729: मूकिमन्, आ, m. dumbness, muteness, silence.
37730: 2. मूत, अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. see rt. 1. मीव्), bound, tied; woven; (अस्, अम्), m. n., Ved. a woven basket; a woven band of cloth or fillet. —मूत-कार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of plaited work or basket work.
37731: मूतक, अम्, n., Ved. a little basket.
37732: मूकलराय मूकलराय, अस्, m., N. of a king.
37733: मूचीप मूचीप, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; [cf. मूतिब।]
37734: मूजवत् मूज-वत्, आन्, m., N. of a moun-tain; (अन्तस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
37735: मूजालदेव मूजाल-देव, अस्, m. a proper N.

37738: मूतिब मूतिब, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
37739: मूत्र मूत्र, अम्, n. (probably connected with rt. 1. मिह्; but according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 162. fr. rt. मुच्, to discharge; by others connected with rts. 1. मीव् and मिन्व्), the fluid secreted by the kidneys, urine. —मूत्र-कर, अस् ई, अम्, producing urine. —मूत्र-कृच्छ्र, अम्, n. painful discharge of urine in minute quantities, strangury; a class of urinary affections (of which eight kinds are enume-rated, including gravel, stone, &c.). —मूत्र-कृच्-छ्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, labouring under painful discharge of urine, suffering from strangury. —मूत्र-कृत-वासस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. steeped or soaked in urine. —मूत्र-कोश, अस्, m. the scrotum. —मूत्र-क्षय, अस्, m. insufficient secretion of urine. —मू-त्र-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. a knot or induration on the neck of the bladder. —मूत्र-घात = मूत्राघात, q. v. —मूत्र-जठर, अस्, अम्, m. n. swelling of the belly in consequence of retention of urine. —मू-त्र-दोष, अस्, m. urinary disease. —मूत्र-निरो-ध, अस्, m. obstruction or retention of urine. —मू-त्र-पतन, अस्, m. the civet cat. —मूत्र-पथ, अस्, m. the urinary passage. —मूत्र-परीक्षा, f. examination of urine, uroscopy; N. of a chapter of the Śārṅgadhara-saṃhitā. —मूत्र-पुट, अम्, n. ‘urine-cavity,’ the lower belly. —मूत्र-पुरीष, अम्, n. urine and excrement. —मूत्र-प्रसेक, अस्, m. the urethra. —मूत्र-फला, f. Cucumis Utilissi-mus (= कर्कटी); another species of cucumber (= त्रपुषी). —मूत्र-भावित, अस्, आ, अम्, saturated with urine. —मूत्र-मार्ग, अस्, m. ‘urine-canal,’ the urethra. —मूत्रमार्ग-निरोधन, अम्, n. obstruction of the urethra. —मूत्र-वर्धक, अस्, इका, अम्, increasing urine, diuretic. —मूत्र-वह, अस्, आ, अम्, conveying urine. —मूत्र-विबन्ध-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, preventing suppression of urine, causing discharge of urine. —मूत्र-विष, अस्, आ, अम्, poisonous with urine. —मूत्र-वृद्धि, इस्, f. copious secretion of urine. —मूत्र-शकृत्, त्, n. urine and excrement. —मूत्र-शुक्र, अम्, n. a disease in which semen and urine are ejected toge-ther. —मूत्र-शूल, अस्, m. urinary colic. —मूत्र-सङ्क्षय, अस्, m. insufficient secretion of urine (= मूत्र-क्षय). —मूत्र-सङ्ग, अस्, m. urinary obstruction, a painful and bloody discharge of urine. —मूत्र-सङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering from the above disease. —मूत्राघात (°र-आघ्°), अस्, m. affection of the urine, urinary disease (of which twelve or thirteen kinds are enumerated). —मूत्रातीत (°र-अत्°), अस्, m. ‘past the proper time for voiding urine,’ a particular kind of retention of urine. —मू-त्राशय (°र-आश्°), अस्, m. ‘urine-receptacle,’ the lower belly. —मूत्रासाद = मूत्रौक-साद, q. v. —मूत्रोत्सङ्ग (°र-उत्°) = मूत्र-सङ्ग, q. v. —मूत्रौक-साद (°र-ओक्°), अस्, m. a disease in which the urine assumes various colours and is voided with pain.
37740: मूत्रय, Nom. P. मूत्रयति, -यितुम्, to dis-charge urine; to make water against or upon (with acc.): Intens. मोमूत्र्यते।
37741: मूत्रल, अस्, आ, अम्, promoting (the secretion of) urine, diuretic; (आ), f. Cucumis Utilissimus; another species of cucumber, = वालुकी; (अम्), n. a species of cucumber (= त्रपुष).
37742: मूत्रित, अस्, आ, अम्, voided as urine, discharged like urine; soiled with urine.
37743: मूत्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, urinary, belonging or relating to urine.
37744: मूर 1. मूर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = मूढ, stupefied, bewildered, stupid, dull, foolish; [cf. अ-म्°, अ-प्रम्°।]
37745: मूर 2. मूर, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps fr. a form मू = rt. 1. मीव्), Ved. rushing, impetuous; (accord-ing to Sāy.) destroying killing (= मारक, fr. rt. मृ). —मूर-देव, अस्, m., Ved. epithet of a par-ticular kind of demon; (Sāy.) sporting in destruction (= मारण-क्रीड).
37746: मूर 3. मूर, अम्, n., Ved. = मूल, a root.
37747: मूरु मूरु, N. of a country.
37749: मूर्खलिका मूर्खलिका, f. an arrow in the form of a bird's heart.
37751: मूर्ण मूर्ण। See under rt. मॄ, p. 793.
37752: मूर्त मूर्त, मूर्ति। See p. 786, col. 1.
37753: मूर्धन् मूर्धन्, आ, m. (in Uṇādi-s. 1. 158. said to be fr. rt. मुर्व्, to bind), the forehead, brow, skull; the head in general; a head, chief, leader, superior, (सर्वेषाम् भूतानाम् मूर्धा राजा, the king is the head of all creatures); the highest or foremost or most prominent part, surface, top, point, peak, summit, (पर्वतस्य मूर्धा, the top or peak of a mountain); ‘the summit,’ epithet of a particular spiritual condition with Buddhists; (in geometry) the base, (opposed to अग्र); मूर्ध्नि or मूर्धनि, at the head or highest point, at the beginning or commencement, in the front, (अतिष्-ठन् मनुजेन्द्राणाम् मूर्ध्नि, he stood at the head of the kings of men; सङ्ग्राम-मूर्धनि, in the front of the battle); before, above, over. —मूर्ध-कर्णी or मूर्ध-कर्परी, f. or मूर्-ध-खोल, अम्, n. a broad-brimmed hat (worn as a shelter from rain); an umbrella. —मूर्ध-ज, अस्, m. ‘head-born,’ the hair of the head, (in this sense usually आस्, m. pl.); the mane; N. of a king (a Cakra-vartin). —मूर्धज-राग, अस्, m. colouring or dyeing the hair. —मूर्ध-ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. = ब्रह्म-रन्ध्र, q. v. —मूर्ध-तस्, ind., Ved. upon the head. —मूर्ध-तैलिक, अस्, m., with वस्ति, epithet of a kind of Errhine for the head. —मूर्धन्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. containing the word मूर्धन्; (आन्), m., N. of a Gandharva; of an Āṅgirasa or Vāma-devya, author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 88. —मूर्ध-पात, अस्, m. the splitting of the skull. —मूर्ध-पिण्ड, अस्, m. a lump upon the head (of an elephant in rut). —मूर्ध-पुष्प, अस्, m. the tree Mimosa Sirissa (शिरीष). —मूर्ध-रस, अस्, m. the scum of boiled rice, rice-water. —मूर्-ध-वेष्टन, अम्, n. a turban, fillet, diadem. —मूर्धान्त (°ध-अन्°), अस्, m. the crown of the head. —मूर्धाभिषिक्त (°ध-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the head sprinkled, anointed, inaugu-rated, consecrated, installed; (अस्), m. a consecrated king; a man of the Kṣatriya or warrior caste; a royal counsellor, minister; = मूर्धावसिक्त below. —मूर्धाभिषेक (°ध-अभ्°), अस्, m. ‘head-sprinkling,’ the act of consecrating any one (as king), anointing, inaugurating. —मूर्धावसिक्त (°ध-अव्°), अस्, m. epithet of a particular mixed caste, the son of a Brāhman father by a Kṣatriya mother; = मूर्धाभिषिक्त, a consecrated king.
37754: मूर्ध = मूर्धन् (at the end of certain comps., cf. द्वि-म्°, त्रि-म्°).
37756: मूर्धन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being on or in the head, belonging to the head, capital; coming from the head or skull, cerebral (a term applied to a class of letters representing sounds formed high in the mouth or by keeping back the tip of the tongue as far as possible in the head and slightly turning it upwards, e. g. ऋ, ॠ, ट्, ठ्, ड्, ढ्, ण्, र्, ष्; these letters are sometimes called linguals); uppermost, highest, su-perior, pre-eminent; (आ), f., N. of the mother of Veda-śiras.
37758: मूर्वा मूर्वा, f. (according to some also मूर्वी, f.; probably fr. rt. मुर्व्), Sanseviera Rox-burghiana, a sort of creeper from the fibres of which bow-strings and the girdle of the Kṣatriyas are made, a sort of hemp for bow-strings; [cf. मौर्व।] —मूर्वा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of Mūrvā.
37760: मूल् मूल् (more properly to be regarded as a Nom. fr. मूल below), cl. 1. P. मूलति (according to Vopa-deva also A. -ते), मु-मूल, मूलितुम्, to be rooted or firm, stand fast, take or strike root: Caus. मूलयति (according to Vopa-deva also मोलयति), मूलयितुम्, Aor. अमू-मुलत्, to plant, transplant; to grow, sprout, shoot, germinate.
37761: मूल, अम्, n. a root (literally and metaphorically); the root of any plant or tree, (मूलं कृ, to take or strike root); the root of Arum Campanulatum; the root of long pepper and of Costus Speciosus or Ara-bicus; basis, groundwork, beginning, origin, com-mencement, cause, (मूलाद् आरभ्य, having com-menced at the beginning); the bottom of anything, foot, (शैलस्य मूलम्, the foot of a mountain); basis, lower part, lower end, (वीणाया मूलम्, the lower end of a lute which rests against the body of a player); the end or juncture of anything by which it is joined to anything else [cf. बाहु-म्°, कर्ण-म्°]; outermost edge or border; original, original text of any work (as distinguished from the scholia or commentary); an old or hereditary servant or dependant, an aboriginal native or inhabitant; ori-ginal property, capital, principal, stock; a chief or capital city; square root; the twenty-fourth or, according to some, seventeenth or nineteenth lunar asterism containing eleven stars, (in this sense अस्, अम्, m. n.; cf. नक्षत्र); immediate neigh-bourhood or proximity; a copse, thicket; a vendor not a true owner, (according to Kullūka on Manu VIII. 202. मूलम् = अ-स्वामी विक्रेता); a particular position of the fingers [cf. मूल-बन्ध]; (अस्), m. an epithet of Sadā-śiva; (आ), f. Asparagus Race-mosus; the asterism Mūla; (ई), f. a species of small house-lizard; (अस्, आ, अम्), original, first; own, proper, peculiar, (in Manu VII. 184. मूल is said to mean a king's own territory.) —मूल-कर्मन्, अ, n. ‘root-machination,’ magical employment of roots, magic; [cf. मूली-कर्मन्, मूल-कृत्।] —मूल-कार, अस्, m. the author of an original work. —मूल-कारण, अम्, n. first or original cause. —मूल-कारिका, f. a fire-place, furnace, oven. —मूल-कृच्छ्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘root-austerity,’ a kind of penance, living solely on roots. —मूल-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. preparing roots for magical uses. —मूल-केशर, अस्, m. a citron. —मूल-खा-नक, अस्, m. ‘root-digger,’ one who digs for roots, a collector of roots. —मूल-गुण, अस्, m. ‘root-multiplier,’ the coefficient of a root (in algebra). —मूलगुण-जाति, इस्, f. assimilation and reduction of the root's coefficient with a fraction. —मूल-ग्रन्थ, अस्, m. an original text; an epithet of the very words uttered by Śākya-muni. —मूल-च्छेद, अस्, m. ‘root-cutting,’ cutting away the roots, cutting up by the roots, uprooting. —मूल-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘root-born,’ growing from roots, pro-duced from a root, radical; formed at the roots of trees (as an ant-hill); (अस्), m. a plant growing from a root (as a lotus); (अम्), n. green ginger. —मूल-जाति, इस्, f. chief or principal origin; = मू-लगुण-जाति, col. 2. —मूल-तस्, ind. from the root, on the root, on the lower side (Ved.), (आ मूलतस्, from the root upwards, from the beginning.) —मू-ल-त्रिकोण, अम्, n. epithet of the third astrological house. —मूल-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a root, the being a root, the having a foundation or source in anything, (मूलत्वात् प्रजानां राजा स्कन्धः, the king is the stem through his subjects being the root; वेद-मूलत्व, the statement that the Veda is the original source of all knowledge; शास्त्र-मूलत्व, the being founded upon the Śās-tras.) —मूल-देव, अस्, m. = मूर-देव, an epithet of Kaṃsa [cf. मूल-भद्र]; N. of the murderer of Su-mitra the son of Agni-mitra; of an author; of a preceptor. —मूल-द्रव्य, अम्, n. original pro-perty, capital, principal, stock; [cf. मूल-धन।] —मूल-द्वार, अम्, n., Ved. principal door. —मू-ल-द्वारवती, f. the original or ancient Dvāra-vatī, the older part of that city; [cf. लघु-द्वारवती, मूल-नगर।] —मूल-धन, अम्, n. original property, capital. —मूल-धातु, उस्, m. lymph. —मूल-नगर, अम्, n. old town, (opposed to the suburbs or शाखा-नगर।) —मूल-नाश or मूल-नाशक, अस्, m. a proper N. —मूल-निकृन्तन, अस्, ई, अम्, cutting away the roots, utterly destroying, destroying root and branch. —मूल-पर्णी, f. a species of plant (= मण्डूक-पर्णी). —मूल-पाक, अस्, m., see Pāṇ. VII. 3, 53. —मूल-पुरुष, अस्, m. the male representative of a family, the last male of a race. —मूल-पुलिश-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m. the original Siddhānta of Puliśa. —मूल-पुष्-कर, अम्, n. = पुष्कर-मूल, q. v. —मूल-पोती, f. a species of culinary plant (= पोतिका). —मूल-प्रकृति, इस्, f. (in phil.) the original root or germ out of which matter or all apparent forms are evolved, the primary cause or ‘originant;’ (अयस्), f. pl. the four principal sovereigns to be considered in time of war (viz. the Vi-jigīṣu, Ari, Madhyama, and Ud-āsīna; cf. प्र-कृति, शाखा-प्रकृति). —मूल-प्रणिहित, अस्, आ, अम्, (perhaps) placed under the surveillance or brought under the notice of old (thieves employed as spies; according to Kullūka on Manu IX. 269 = राज-नियुक्त-पुराण-चौर-वर्गे सावधान-भूताः). —मूल-फल-द, अस्, m. the Jaka or bread-fruit tree. —मूल-फलाशन (°ल-अश्°), अम्, n. feeding on roots and fruits. —मूल-बणिग्-धन, अम्, n. a merchant's original property or capital. —मूल-बन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, (probably) having roots, deep-rooted; (अस्), m. a particular po-sition of the fingers. —मूल-बर्हण, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. tearing up by the roots, uprooting; (ई, अम्), f. n. the Nakṣatra Mūla; (अम्), n. the act of uprooting. —मूल-भद्र, अस्, m. an epithet of Kaṃsa, the uncle of Kṛṣṇa; [cf. मूल-देव।] —मूल-भव, अस्, आ, अम्, springing or growing from roots. —मूल-भार, अस्, m. a load of roots. —मूल-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become the root or original. —मूल-भृत्य, अस्, m. an old or here-ditary servant, one whose father, grandfather, &c. were servants before him, (opposed to आ-गन्तु।) —मूल-मन्त्र, अस्, m. an original or funda-mental text; an epithet of a particular sacred text. —मूल-माधव, N. of a place. —मूलमा-धव-तीथ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —मूल-मित्र, अस्, m. a proper N. —मूल-रस, अस्, m. Sanseviera Zeylanica. —मूल-राज, अस्, m., N. of a king. —मूल-रामायण, अम्, n. the ori-ginal Rāmāyaṇa, i. e. Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa. —मूल-वचन, अम्, n. ‘primary word,’ an original text. —मूल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing edible roots; (perhaps) practising magic with roots. —मूल-वाप, अस्, m. one who plants roots. —मूल-वारिन्, ई, m. a proper N. —मूल-वित्त, अम्, n. ‘original property,’ capital, principal. —मूल-विद्या, f. ‘principal science,’ epithet of a particular Mantra (= द्वादशाक्षर, q. v.). —मूल-विनाशन, अम्, n. radical or entire destruction. —मूल-विभुज, अस्, आ, अम्, bending down roots; (अस्), m. a chariot. —मूल-विरेचन, अम्, n. a purgative prepared from roots. —मूल-व्यसन-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the hereditary occupation of executing criminals (Manu X. 38). —मूल-व्रतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, living exclusively on roots. —मूल-शकुन, अस्, m. (in augury) the first bird. —मूल-शाकट or मूल-शाकिन, अम्, n. a field planted with edible roots. —मूल-श्रीपति-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —मूल-सङ्घ, अस्, m. a society or sect. —मूल-सर्वास्तिवाद (°व-अस्°), आस्, m. pl., N. of a Buddhist school. —मूल-साधन, अम्, n. a chief instrument, principal expedient. —मूल-सूत्र, अम्, n. a principal Sūtra. —मूल-स्थल, अम्, n., N. of a place. —मूल-स्थान, अम्, n. principal place; foundation, base; the air, atmosphere; God; Mool-tan; (ई), f. an epithet of Gaurī. —मूलस्थान-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha (= भास्कर). —मूल-स्थायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, existing from the begin-ning; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva. —मूल-स्रोतस्, अस्, n. the fountain-head of a river, principal current. —मूल-हर, अस्, आ, अम्, taking away the roots of anything, uprooting, utterly destroying, eradicating. —मूल-हर-त्व, अम्, n. the state of plucking up by the roots, eradicating, utter ruin. —मूलाधार (°ल-आध्°), अम्, n., scil. चक्र, epithet of a mystical circle situated above the generative organs; (accord-ing to a Scholiast) the navel. —मूलाभ (°ल-आभ्°), अम्, n. a radish. —मूलाभिधर्म-शास्त्र (°ल-अभ्°), अम्, n. the original Abhidharma-śāstra —मू-लायतन (°ल-आय्°), अम्, n. an original residence. —मूलाविद्या-विनाशक (°ल-अव्°), अस्, इका, अम्, (probably) destroying ignorance at its roots, eradi-cating ignorance. —मूलाशिन् (°ल-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, ‘root-eating,’ living upon roots. —मूलाह्वा (°ल-आह्°), अम्, n. a radish. —मूली-कर्मन्, अ, n. = मूल-कर्मन्, q. v. —मूली-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become a root, become a source or origin. —मूलोच्छेद (°ल-उच्°), अस्, m. cutting up the roots, utter destruction. —मूलोत्खात (°ल-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, dug up by the roots, utterly destroyed; (अम्), n. digging up roots. —मूलोत्पाटन (°ल-उत्°), अम्, n. the digging up of roots. —मूलोत्पाटन-जीविन्, ई, m. one who lives by digging for roots (= मूल-खानक). —मू-लौषधि (°ल-ओष्°), इस्, f. a species of plant.
37762: मूलक, अस्, इका, अम्, (at the end of comps.) having roots, rooted in, springing from; born under the constellation Mūla; (अस्, अम्), m. n. an esculent root; a radish [cf. चाणक्य-म्°, नेपाल-म्°]; a sort of yam; (अस्), m. a kind of vegetable poison; N. of a prince, a son of Aśmaka; (इका), f. a root. —मूलक-पण, अस्, m. a handful or bunch of radishes, &c. 37805: मृगयस्, आस्, m., Ved. a wild animal.

37807: मृगयाण, अस्, आ, अम्, searching for, hunting after, chasing, pursuing.
37808: मृगयित्वा, ind. having searched, having investi-gated.
37809: मृगयु, उस्, m. a huntsman; a jackal; an epi-thet of Brahmā.
37810: मृगव, (with Buddhists) a particular high number.
37811: मृगव्य, अम्, n. hunting, the chase; the butt or mark in archery, a target.
37812: मृगार, अस्, m., N. of the author of the hymns Atharva-veda IV. 23-29; of a minister of Prasena-jit [cf. मृग-धर]; = मृगार-सूक्त below. —मृगार-सूक्त, अम्, n. the hymns Atharva-veda IV. 23-29. —मृगारेष्टि (°र-इष्°), इस्, f. epithet of Taittirīya-saṃhitā IV. 7, 15, and of Atharva-veda IV. 23-29.
37813: मृगित, अस्, आ, अम्, chased, hunted after, sought, searched for, pursued.
37814: मृगू, ऊस्, f., Ved. (according to Sāy.), N. of the mother of Rāma Mārgaveya.
37815: मृग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be hunted after, to be sought or inquired after.
37816: मृग्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being searched for, being sought or inquired after.
37817: मृच् मृच्, क्, f. (fr. rt. मर्च्), Ved. threaten-ing; injury; a snare; [cf. अ-मृक्त।]
37818: मृचय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (perhaps) liable to destruction or decay, transitory, going, moving.
37819: मृच्चय मृच्-चय, मृच्-छकटिका। See under 2. मृद्, p. 792, col. 2.
37820: मृछ् मृछ् or मर्छ्, cl. 6. A. मृच्छते, &c., to pass away, perish.
37821: मृज् 1. मृज् [cf. rts. मार्ज्, मृश्], cl. 2. P. मार्ष्टि (ep. also A. मार्ष्टे, 3rd pl. मृजन्ति or मार्जन्ति; Ved. 3rd sing. मृजति, -ते), Impf. अमार्ट् (3rd pl. अमृजन् or अमार्जन्), Impv. मार्ष्टु (2nd sing. मृड्ढि), ममार्ज (3rd pl. ममृजुस् or ममार्जुस्), मार्जिष्यति or मार्क्ष्-यति (Ved. म्रक्ष्यते), अमार्जीत् or अमार्क्षीत् (Ved. अमृक्षत्), मार्जितुम् or मार्ष्टुम्, to wipe, rub, cleanse, clean, purify, wash off, clear away; to rub, stroke; to make smooth or glossy, curry (as a horse); to deck, adorn, make ready; (A.) to wipe off (impu-rity from one's self) upon some one else (loc. c.); to go (Ved.); cl. 1. P. मर्जति, मृञ्जति, &c., to sound, (in this sense connected with rts. मुज्, मुञ्ज्, cf. rt. मार्ज्); cl. 10. P. A. or Caus. मार्जयति, -ते (Ved. मर्जयति, -ते), -यितुम्, to wipe off; to wash or cleanse one's self (in this sense only A.), purify one's self, become purified; to adorn; to move about, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 39, 3. मर्जयन्त = परिचर्यन्ते): Pass. मृज्यते, Aor. अमार्जि, to be wiped or washed, &c.: Caus. मार्ज-यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अममार्जत् or अमीमृजत्, to cause to wipe or cleanse, &c.: Desid. मिमार्जिषति or मिमृक्षति: Intens. मरीमृज्यते (Ved. मर्-मृज्यते), मरीमार्ष्टि, मरिमार्ष्टि, मर्मार्-ष्टि, to rub or wipe off repeatedly, to keep rubbing or wiping off; (A.) to be continually cleansing one's self; [cf. Zend marez, ‘to wipe:’ Gr. ἀμέλγ-ω, ἄμελξις, ἀμολγεύ-ς, ἀμολγαῖο-ς, ἀμέργ-ω, ἀμοργός, ἀμόργη, ὀμόργ-νυ-μι, ὄμοργ-μα, γλάγος (for μλάγος), γάλα, γάλακτος (for μλακτο): Lat. mulg-e-o, mulc-tu-s, mulctra, mulctru-m, merg-a, merg-e(t)s, mulier, lac (for mlac): Old Germ. milch-u, ‘I milk:’ Goth. miluks, ‘milk:’ Angl. Sax. meoluc, meolc, melcan, mearc, mearcian, ge-mearc: Slav. mlz-a: Lith. melz-u: perhaps Hib. breugaim, ‘I soothe;’ bleaghaim, ‘I milk.’]
37822: मार्जित, अस्, आ, अम् (equally to be connected with rt. मार्ज्), wiped, cleansed, purified, clean, smooth, bright; washed away, removed; rubbed, smeared, besmeared, &c.; see मार्जित, p. 774, col. 1.
37823: 2. मृज्, ट्, ट्, ट्, (at the end of a comp.) wiping, rubbing; wiping off or away.
37824: मृज, अस्, m. a kind of drum.
37825: मृजत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, wiping away, cleansing, effacing, (also प्र-मृजत्, Kirātārj. III. 4, 3.)
37826: मृजा, f. wiping, cleansing, washing, purifying, purification, ablution; purity, cleanliness; a pure skin, clear complexion; complexion. —मृजा-न-गर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —मृजान्वय (°जा-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, possessing or endowed with clean-liness, cleansed, clean. —मृजा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, pos-sessed of cleanliness.
37827: मृजित, अस्, आ, अम्, wiped, wiped away, rubbed off, removed.
37828: मृज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cleansed, to be purified; to be wiped away or removed (= 2. मार्ग्य).
37829: 1. मृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see p. 793, col. 1), washed, cleansed, clean, pure; smeared, besmeared; prepared, dressed, savoury, (मृष्टम् अन्नम्, deli-cate food, dainties; cf. मिष्ट); (अम्), n. pepper. —मृष्ट-गन्ध, अस्, m. (probably) an agreeable or appetizing smell or savour. —मृष्टगन्ध-पवन, अस्, m. a fragrant breeze. —मृष्ट-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, exceedingly delicate or savoury. —मृ-ष्ट-लुञ्चित, अस्, आ, अम्, torn up (as a root) and washed. —मृष्ट-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. containing a form of rt. 1. मृज्. —मृष्ट-वाक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking sweetly (= मिष्ट-वाक्य). —मृष्ट-सलिल, अस्, आ, अम्, having bright or pure water.
37830: 1. मृष्टि, इस्, f. (for 2. see p. 793, col. 1), cleans-ing, cleaning, preparation, dressing (of food, Manu III. 255); a savoury repast, (according to Kullūka = अन्नादेः संस्कार-विशेष।)
37831: मृष्टेरुक, अस्, आ, अम्, eating dainties or deli-cacies, luxurious, selfish; liberal.
37832: मृड् मृड् (Ved. मृऌ), cl. 6. 9. P. मृ-डति, मृड्नाति, ममर्ड, मर्डिष्यति, अमर्डीत्, मर्डितुम् (Ved. cl. 6. P. मृऌअति, cl. 10. P. मृऌअयति, &c.), to be gracious or favour-able, be gracious towards (with dat.); to forgive, par-don, spare; to treat graciously, rejoice, delight, make happy; to rejoice, be delighted or happy: Caus. मर्डयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अमीमृडत् or अममर्-डत्: Desid. मिमर्डिषति: Intens. मरीमृड्यते, मरीमर्ट्टि; [cf. Gr. μείλ-ια, μείλιχο-ς, μειλίχ-ιο-ς, μει-λιχ-ίη, μειλίσσω, μειλ-εῖν: Lat. blan-dus: Goth. mild-s, ‘affectionate:’ Old Germ. mil-ti, ‘mild:’ Slav. mil-ŭ, ‘pitiable;’ mil-ovati, ‘to pity;’ mil-ostĭ, ‘pity:’ Lith. myl-iu; meilù-s, ‘lovely;’ méile, ‘love.’]
37833: मृड, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. मृदु, col. 3], showing mercy, gracious (Ved.); (अस्), m. a N. of Agni or Fire; of Śiva; (आ, ई), f. an epithet of Pārvatī [cf. मृडानी]; (अम्), n., scil. हिरण्य, a particular weight of gold (?).
37834: मृडन, अम्, n. the act of showing grace or favour, making happy, delighting.
37835: मृडय, अस्, आ, अम्, showing grace or mercy; अ-मृडय, unmerciful.
37836: मृडाकु, उस्, m. a proper N.
37837: मृडानी, f. the wife of Mṛḍa or Śiva, i. e. Pār-vatī. —मृडानी-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a work.
37838: मृडितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. = मर्डितृ, one who shows favour.
37839: मृडीक, अस्, m. ‘gracious,’ N. of Śiva; a fish; (according to some) an antelope, [cf. मृग।]
37840: मृऌअयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. showing grace or favour, favouring. —मृऌअयत्-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. exceedingly gracious.
37841: मृऌअयाकु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. gracious, kindly dis-posed, showing grace, making happy.
37842: मृऌईक, अम्, n., Ved. grace, mercy, kindness; (अस्), m., N. of a Vāsiṣṭha, author of the hymns Ṛg-veda IX. 97, 25-27, and X. 150.
37843: मृडङ्कण मृडङ्कण, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 24. fr. rt. मृड्), a child, boy.
37844: मृण् मृण् (connected with rts. मृ, मॄ), cl. 6. P. मृणति, ममर्ण, मृणितुम्, to kill, slay; [cf. Gr. μάρναμαι.]
37845: मृणाल मृणाल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be also ई, f.), the edible fibrous root of some kinds of lotus, a lotus fibre or small fibre attached to the stalk of a water-lily; (ई), f. a lotus fibre; (अम्), n. the root of the fragrant grass Andropogon Muricatus. —मृणाल-भङ्ग, अस्, m. the fracture of a lotus fibre. —मृणाल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing lotus fibres or roots. —मृणाल-सूत्र, अम्, n. the fibre of a lotus stalk.
37846: मृणालक, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of comps.) = मृणाल; (इका), f. the edible root of a lotus; a proper N.
37847: मृणालिन्, ई, m. a lotus; (इनी), f. a lotus plant; a group of lotuses; a place where lotuses grow.
37848: मृण्मय मृण्-मय, incorrectly for मृन्-मय under 2. मृद्, col. 3.
37849: मृत मृत। See under rt. मृ, p. 789, col. 3.
37850: मृतण्ड मृतण्ड, अस्, m., N. of the father of the sun; the sun; [cf. मृताण्ड, मार्तण्ड।]
37851: मृतामद मृतामद, अम्, n. blue vitriol.
37852: मृतालक मृतालक or मृत्ताल or मृत्ता-लक, अम्, n. (probably connected with 2. मृद्), a kind of loam or clay.
37853: मृत्कर मृत्-कर। See under 2. मृद् below.
37854: मृत्यव मृत्यव, probably incorrect for मृत्-पच below.
37857: मृद् 1. मृद् [cf. rts. म्रद्, मृड्], cl. 9. P. मृद्नाति (ep. also A. मृद्नीते), cl. 1. P. मर्दति (ep. also A. -ते), ममर्द (3rd pl. ममृ-दुस् or ममर्दुस्), ममृदे, मर्दिष्यति, अमर्-दीत्, मर्दितुम्, to press, squeeze; to grind, pound, bruise, reduce to powder, pulverize; to crush, dash to pieces, trample upon, treat harshly, lay waste; to overcome, surpass; to rub, stroke, wipe, (हस्तेन ममृदे ललाटम्, he wiped his forehead with his hand); to rub against, touch, graze, pass through (as a constellation, in astronomy); to rub away, wipe away, destroy; (according to Naigh. II. 14) to go, (in this sense cl. 1. P.): Pass. मृद्यते, to be pressed or ground, &c.: Caus. मर्दयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अममर्दत् or अमीमृदत्, to press or squeeze hard, to crush, break, trample upon, tread under foot, oppress, treat harshly, wear out, torment, plague, destroy, kill; to rub; to cause to be trampled upon, &c.: Desid. मिमर्दिषति, to desire to crush, wish to pound; to be about to crush, &c.: Intens. मरी-मृद्यते, मरीमर्त्ति, &c.; [cf. Gr. ἀ-μέρδ-ω, μύλ-η, μέλδ-ω, ἀ-μαλδ-ύν-ω, ἄ-μαλο-ς: Lat. mord-e-o, mand-o, mol-o, mol-a, malleus (for mar-deus): Goth. malvja, ‘I pound;’ mala, ‘I grind;’ malo, ‘a moth:’ Angl. Sax. s-melte, ‘to melt;’ malt, meltan, miltan, smeortan: Old Germ. smilzu; smylt, ‘serene, calm;’ malz, smerzan: Lith. malù, ‘I grind;’ mald-inu, mal-inu, ‘I cause to be ground;’ molj, ‘a moth:’ Hib. meilim, ‘I grind;’ millim, ‘I spoil, ruin.’]
37858: मृत्तिका, f. earth, clay, loam; fresh earth; a kind of fragrant earth. —मृत्तिका-वती, f., N. of a town.
37859: मृत्सा, f. good earth or clay; earth, clay; a kind of fragrant earth.
37860: मृत्स्न, अस्, अम्, m. n. dust, powder; (आ), f. good earth or clay; a kind of fragrant earth; clay; [cf. मार्त्स्न।] —मृत्स्ना-भाण्डक, अम्, n. a kind of earthen vessel (= उष्ट्रिका).
37861: 2. मृद्, त्, f. earth, soil, clay, loam; a piece of earth, lump of clay; a mound of earth; a kind of fragrant earth; [cf. पाण्डु-म्°।] —मृच्-चय, अस्, m. a heap of earth. —मृच्-छकटिका, f. (i. e. मृत् + शकटिका), a small cart made of clay, toy-cart; (आ, अम्), f. n., N. of a celebrated drama (supposed to be the oldest Sanskrit play extant) by king Śūdraka. —मृच्छ-कटिका-सेतु, उस्, m., N. of a commentary by Lallā-dīkṣita on the above drama. —मृच्-छिला-मय, अस्, ई, अम् (i. e. मृत् + शिला + मय), made of clay and stone. —मृत्-कण, a small lump or clod of earth or clay. —मृत्कण-ता, f. the state of a clod of earth. —मृत्-कर, अस्, m. a worker in clay, potter. —मृत्-कांस्य, अम्, n. an earthen pitcher, earthen vessel. —मृत्-किरा, f. ‘earth-scattering,’ an earth-worm; a species of cricket. —मृत्-खलिनी, f. a species of plant (= चर्म-कशा). —मृत्-पच, अस्, m. a baker of clay, potter. —मृत्-पात्र, अम्, n. a vessel of clay, earthen vessel, earthenware. —मृत्-पिण्ड, अस्, m. a clod of earth, lump of clay. —मृत्पिण्ड-तस्, ind. from a lump of clay. —मृत्-प्रक्षेप, scattering earth over anything (as a means of purification, Manu V. 125). —मृत्-फली, f. Costus Speciosus or Arabicus. —मृद्-आह्वया, f. a species of fragrant earth. —मृद्-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the earth, growing in clay; (अस्), m. a species of fish. —मृद्-घट, अस्, m. an earthen pot or pitcher. —मृद्-भाण्ड, अम्, n. a vessel of clay, earthen pot, earthenware. —मृद्-भाण्डावशेषम् (°ड-अव्°), ind. so that only an earthen vessel is left. —मृद्-वारि-शुचि, इस्, इस्, इ, purified with earth and water (Manu V. 106). —मृन्-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of earth or clay, earthen; मृन्-मयम् पात्रम्, an earthenware vessel. —मृन्-मरु, उस्, m. a stone, rock (?). —मृल्-लोष्ट, अम्, n. a lump of clay, clod of earth.
37862: मृदव, अम्, n. (fr. मृदु), contrasting excel-lence or merit of any kind with demerit (in drama-tical language).
37863: मृदा, f., Ved. = 2. मृद्; [cf. probably Lat. merda; Goth. mulda; Angl. Sax. molde.] —मृ-दा-कर, अस्, m. a thunderbolt.
37864: मृदित, अस्, आ, अम्, pressed, squeezed; crushed, bruised, pounded, ground, trampled upon, trampled down, laid waste; rubbed; (अम्), n. a particular disease of the membrum virile.
37865: मृदिनी, f. good earth or soil.
37866: मृदु, उस्, उस् or वी, उ (compar. म्रदीयस्, su-perl. म्रदिष्ठ, q. q. v. v.; cf. rt. म्रद्, from which in Uṇādi-s. 1. 29. मृदु is said to be de-rived), ‘easily pressed or squeezed,’ soft, tender, sup-ple, flexible, pliant; mild, gentle; weak, moderate; blunt; slow; (उस्), m. the planet Saturn [cf. मन्द]; N. of a king; (वी), f. a vine with red grapes [cf. मृ-द्वीका]; (उ), n. softness, mildness, gentleness; [cf. Gr. βραδύς (fr. μραδύς like βροτό-ς fr. μροτό-ς); Lat. bardus, mollis (fr. molvis for modvis or morvis), mollities, mollīre, blandus; Old Germ. milti; Mod. Germ., Angl. Sax., and Eng. mild; Russ. molodyĭ, ‘young;’ Hib. meirbh, ‘slow, tedious, weak.’] —मृदु-कृष्णायस, अम्, n. ‘soft-iron,’ lead. —मृदु-कोष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, having relaxed bowels, relaxed, easily affected by medicine. —मृदु-क्रिया, f. the act of softening, mollify-ing. —मृदु-गण, अस्, m. = मृदु-वर्ग below. —मृदु-गन्धिक, अस्, m. a species of plant. —मृदु-गमन, अस्, आ, अम्, going softly, having a soft or gentle gait; (आ), f. a goose or female swan. —मृदु-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going softly, having a soft or gentle gait. —मृदु-चर्मिन्, ई, m. a species of birch tree (= चर्मिन्). —मृदु-चाप, अस्, m., N. of a Dānava. —मृदु-च्छद, अस्, m. a species of birch tree; a kind of mountain Pīlu tree. —मृदु-जातीय, अस्, आ, अम्, somewhat soft, slightly weak. —मृदु-ता, f. or मृदु-त्व, अम्, n. softness, gentleness, tenderness, mildness, weakness; मृदु-तां गम् or व्रज्, to become mild or weak, be appeased. —मृदु-ताल, अस्, m. a species of tree (= श्री-ताल). —मृदु-तीक्ष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, soft and violent, gentle and harsh, (used as an epithet of the two Nakṣatras Kṛttikā and Vi-śākhā.) —मृदु-त्वच्, क्, or मृदु-त्वच, अस्, m. ‘having a soft bark,’ a species of birch tree. —मृदु-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘soft-leafed,’ a rush, reed. —मृदु-परुष-गुण, औ, m. du. ‘the qualities of mild and harsh,’ mildness and harshness. —मृदु-पर्वक, अस्, m. or मृदु-पर्वन्, अ, n. ‘soft-jointed,’ a reed, cane. —मृदु-पाणि, इस्, इस्, इ, ‘soft-handed,’ having a delicate hand. —मृदु-पीठक, अस्, m. a kind of sheat-fish, silurus. —मृदु-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘having soft flowers,’ Acacia Sirissa (= शिरीष). —मृदु-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, commencing softly, friendly at first, gentle, tender; (अम्), ind. mildly or friendly at first, gently, tenderly, blandly, softly, coaxingly. —मृदु-प्रयत्न, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
