39426: रावण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the Caus.), screaming, roar-ing, crying, bellowing, bewailing, making lamentation; (अस्), m. ‘the Vociferator,’ N. of the ruler of Laṅkā or Ceylon and the famous chief of the Rākṣasas or demons whose subjugation and destruction by Rāma-candra, the seventh incarnation of Viṣṇu, form the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa, (as son of Viśravas, he was younger brother of Kuvera, but by a different mother, Ilavilā being the mother of Kuvera, and Keśinī of the three other brothers, Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Kumbha-karṇa; both Rāvaṇa and Kuvera, the god of wealth, are often called Paulastya, as grandchildren of the Ṛṣi Pulastya, one of the seven or ten mind-born sons of Brahmā, and as Kuvera is king of the Yakṣas, so is Rāvaṇa of the Rākṣasas, the latter, however, are always malignant beings [see राक्षस], and Rāvaṇa himself is one of the worst of the many impersonations of evil common in Hindū mythology; he is the Satan of the Rāmāyaṇa as Duryodhana is of the Mahā-bhārata; he has ten heads [whence his names Daśa-grīva, Daśānana, &c.] and twenty arms, symbolizing strength; his power is described as so great, that where he is ‘there the sun does not give out its heat, the winds through fear of him do not blow, the fire ceases to burn, and the ocean becomes motionless;’ he even, by his power, defeated his own brother Vaiśravaṇa or Kuvera, and carried off his self-moving car, called Puṣpaka, the wonders of which are described in the Rāmāyaṇa; this potency was, as usual, acquired by self-inflicted austerities, which had obtained from Brahmā a boon, in virtue of which Rāvaṇa was invulnerable by gods and divine beings of all kinds, though not by men or a god in human form; as Viṣṇu became incarnate in Rāma-candra to destroy Rāvaṇa, so other gods produced innume-rable monkeys, bears, and various semi-divine animals to do battle with the legions of demons, his subjects, under Khara, Dūṣaṇa, and his other generals; see हनु-मत्); a patronymic from Ravaṇa; N. of the author of a commentary on the Sāma-veda; of one on the Ṛg-veda; of the author of the Arka-cikitsā; of a king of Kaśmīra (mentioned together with Indra-jit and Vibhīṣaṇa); (said to be fr. rt. रह्; probably connected with rts. रभ्, ग्रभ्), ‘the looser’ or ‘the seizer,’ N. of a Daitya or demon who is supposed to seize the sun and moon and thus cause eclipses, (according to the common myth he was a son of Vipra-citti and Sinhikā, and had four arms, his lower part ending in a tail; he was the instigator of all mischief among the Daityas, and when the gods had produced the Amṛta or nectar from the churned ocean, he disguised himself like one of them and drank a portion of it, but the Sun and Moon having detected his fraud and informed Viṣṇu, the latter severed his head and two of his arms from the rest of his body; the portion of nectar he had swallowed having secured his immortality, the head and tail were transferred to the stellar sphere, the head wreaking its vengeance on the Sun and Moon by occasionally swallowing them for a time, while the tail, under the name of Ketu, gave birth to a numerous progeny of comets and fiery meteors: in astronomy Rāhu is variously regarded as a dragon's head, as the ascending node of the moon, or as one of the planets); an eclipse or (rather) the moment of occultation or obscuration; the regent of the south-west quarter. —राहु-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘gone to Rāhu,’ darkened, ob-scured, eclipsed. —राहु-ग्रसन or राहु-ग्र-हण, अम्, n. ‘seizure or swallowing by Rāhu,’ an eclipse of the sun or moon. —राहु-ग्रस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘swallowed by Rāhu,’ eclipsed. —राहु-ग्रास or राहु-ग्राह, अस्, m. an eclipse of the sun or moon, the immersion at an eclipse. —राहु-च्छत्त्र, अम्, n. green ginger. —राहु-दर्शन, अम्, n., Ved. ‘appearance of Rāhu,’ an eclipse. —राहु-पर्-वन्, अ, n. the day or period of an eclipse. —राहु-पीडा, f. ‘oppression by Rāhu,’ an eclipse. —राहु-पूजा, f. the worship of Rāhu. —राहु-भेदिन्, ई, m. ‘severing Rāhu,’ epithet of Viṣṇu. —राहु-मूर्ध-भिद्, त्, or राहु-मूर्ध-हर, अस्, m. ‘decapitator of Rāhu,’ epithet of Viṣṇu. —राहु-रत्न, अम्, n. 39477: रिङ्ख् रिङ्ख् (connected with rts. रिख्, रख्, रङ्ख्, रिङ्ग्, रङ्ग्), cl. 1. P. रिङ्खति, &c., to go, move, creep, crawl (said of young children); to go slowly; to slip.

39488: रिच् रिच्, cl. 7. P. A. रिणक्ति, रिङ्क्ते, रिरेच, रिरिचे, रेक्ष्यति, -ते, अरिचत् or अरैक्षीत् (Vedic forms अरिरेचीत्, अरैक्), अरिक्त (1st sing. अरिक्षि), रेक्तुम्, to empty, make empty, evacuate, clear, purge, remove, separate, divide; to resign, give up, deliver up, part with, sell, (but ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda IV. 24, 9. ‘to recover, get back’); to leave, leave behind, bequeath; cl. 10. 1. P. रेचयति, रेचति, &c., to divide, separate; to disconnect, disjoin; to leave, abandon; to join, mix: Pass. रिच्यते, Aor. अरेचि, to be emptied, &c.; to be deprived of, lose, be freed from; to be destroyed, perish: Caus. रेचयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अरीरिचत्, to cause to empty, make empty; to discharge, emit (as breath); to abandon, give up: Desid. रिरिक्षति, -ते: Intens. रेरिच्यते, रेरेक्ति; [cf. Germ. bleibe; Angl. Sax. lyfan, be-lijan, lafan, lœn, lœnan; Lith. lek-u, lik-ti, lek-as, pa-laiki-s.]
39489: रिक (?), अम्, n. the heart, mind; law, litigation.
39490: रिक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, emptied, cleared, purged; empty, void; unloaded, unburdened; hollow, hol-lowed (as the hands); having nothing, poor, indi-gent; vain, worthless, valueless; epithet of one of the four wagtails (employed in augury); free from, devoid of, deprived of, destitute of, without; (आ), f., scil. तिथि, epithet of the fourth, ninth, or fourteenth days of the lunar fortnight; (अम्), n. an empty place, empty space, vacuum, void, vacuity; a desert, wilderness, wood, forest. —रिक्त-कुम्भ, अम्, n., Ved. (the sound of) an empty vessel, a hollow sound, empty or senseless language. —रिक्त-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. making empty, emptying; causing a vacuum. —रिक्त-गुरु, see Pāṇ. VI. 2, 42. —रिक्त-ता, f. emptiness, vacuity, void, empty space or space in general. —रिक्त-पाणि, इस्, इस्, इ, empty-handed, bringing no present. —रिक्त-भाण्ड, अम्, n. an empty vessel; (अस्, आ, अम्), having no vessels or effects. —रिक्त-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, empty-minded, thinking of nothing —रिक्त-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, empty-handed, having empty hands, bringing no present; carrying away no present. —रिक्तार्क (°त-अर्°), अस्, m. a Sunday falling on one of the Riktā days. —रिक्ती-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make empty or void, remove, take away; to steal; to get back, recover. —रिक्तीकृत-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, emptied or deprived of heart.
39491: रिक्तक, अस्, आ, अम्, empty, void; unladen, un-burdened.
39492: रिक्थ, अम्, n. (frequently written ऋक्थ), pro-perty left at death, inheritance, portion, bequest; property in general, possessions, substance, wealth; gold. —रिक्थ-ग्राह, अस्, आ, अम्, receiving an in-heritance, inheriting property; (अस्), m. an inheritor, heir. —रिक्थ-जात, अम्, n. the aggregate of a property, collected estate (of a deceased person). —रिक्थ-भागिन्, ई, इनी, इ, or रिक्थ-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, inheriting or sharing property, dividing the pro-perty (of a deceased person), an inheritor, heir. —रिक्थ-विभाग, अस्, m. the division or sharing of (a deceased person's) property, partition of inherit-ance; a share in an inheritance. —रिक्थ-हर or रिक्थ-हार, अस्, आ, or ई, अम्, receiving an inherit-ance, inheriting property; (अस्), m. an heir. —रिक्-थ-हारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, receiving or inheriting pro-perty; (ई), m. an heir, one who succeeds to property; a maternal uncle; the seed of the Indian fig-tree.
39493: रिक्थाद (°थ-आद), अस्, आ, अम्, receiving an inheritance; (अस्), m. an heir, son.
39494: रिक्थिन्, ई, इनी, इ, inheriting property; possessing property, wealthy; (ई), m. an heir.
39495: रिक्थीय in अ-रिक्थीय, अस्, आ, अम्, incapable of inheriting property, having no claim to inheritance.
39496: रिच्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being emptied, being purged, being left clear, being freed from, being delivered from.

39498: रेक, रेच, रेचित, &c. See p. 852, col. 3.

39500: रिटि रिटि, इस्, f. the crackling or roaring of flame; a musical instrument; black salt.

39509: रिपु, उस्, उस्, उ (according to Uṇādi-s. P. रिफति, रिरेफ, &c., to utter a murmuring gut-tural sound, to utter a rough or grating or burring sound, to pronounce the letter र् [cf. रेफ below]; to murmur or snarl at, revile, find fault with, blame, despise; (according to lexicographers also capable of the following senses), to speak, say, relate; to boast, (कत्थने being a various reading for कथने); to give; to fight; to hurl, kill, (in this sense = rts. ऋफ्, रिम्फ्): Pass. रिफ्यते, to be murmured or spoken in a grating or burring manner, to have or take the pronunciation of the letter र्।

P.): Pass. रिभ्यते, to be praised or glorified; [cf. Gr. ῥοίβδην, ῥοῖβδος, ῥοιβδέω.]

39527: रेभिल and रेभिलक, अस्, m. a proper N.

39540: रिरी रिरी, f. yellow brass, pale brass, prince's metal; [cf. रीरी, रीति।]
39541: रिल्हण रिल्हण or रिह्लण, अस्, m. a proper N.

P. रिशति, रिरेश, रेक्ष्यति, अरि-क्षत्, रेष्टुम्, Ved. to tear, rend, tear off, break off, pluck off, injure, hurt; to feed on, graze: Caus. रेशयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अरीरिशत्: Desid. रिरिक्षति, to wish to injure: Intens. रेरिश्यते, रेरेष्टि; [cf. 39549: 1. रिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. रिष्ट see below), Ved. torn, torn off, broken, injured; wearied.

39652: रुद्र, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 22. fr. rt. 1. रुद् above; according to others fr. rt. 1. रु + द्र fr. rt. 2. द्रु, to run; connected with रोदस्, q. v., and perhaps with रुधिर), crying, howling, roaring, one who cries or roars, dreadful, horrible, terrific, awful; great, large; (according to the fanciful etymologies of native writers, the following meanings are also assigned to this word), driving away evil; running about and roaring; praiseworthy, to be praised, (according to Naigh. III. 16) = स्तोतृ, a praiser, panegyrist, worshipper; (अस्), m. ‘the Roarer’ or ‘Howler,’ N. of the god of tempests and father of the Rudras or Maruts, (originally perhaps the mere personified roaring of the storms, but as the crackling or raging of fire may resemble the sound of wind, so in the Veda the god of storms is some-times identified with the god of fire; though gene-rally represented as a destroying deity whose terrible shafts bring death or disease on men and cattle, he is also addressed as benevolent and auspicious [शिव], and is even supposed to have a healing efficacy from his chasing away vapours and purifying the atmo-sphere; hence he has various epithets in the Veda, such as ‘multiform,’ ‘terrible as a wild beast,’ ‘tawny-coloured,’ ‘wearing braided hair’ [कपर्दिन्], ‘ce-lestial boar,’ ‘armed with a strong bow and fleet arrows,’ ‘cause of prosperity to man and beast,’ ‘pos-sessor of healing remedies,’ ‘greatest of physicians,’ &c.; he is of course ruler of the Rudras, who are the same as the storm winds, more usually called Maruts, and who are often associated with Indra [see मरुत्]: in the later mythology the epithet शिव, ‘propitious,’ which does not occur as a name in the Veda, was employed as the real name of the destroy-ing deity, being at first applied as an euphemism to propitiate him: moreover the character of the deity lost its special connection with storms, and developed into a personification of the destroying principle generally, though even the Epic and Purānic Śiva was regarded as the generator as well as destroyer: moreover a new class of beings, described as eleven in number, though still called Rudras, took the place of the original Rudras or Maruts: in the Veda only three groupings of deities into classes appear to be recognised, Indra belonging to the Vasus, Varuṇa to the Ādityas, and Rudra to the Rudras or Maruts; but in Manu XI. 221. the Maruts are enumerated as a fourth group, being there distinguished from the eleven Rudras: in Viṣṇu-Purāṇa I. 7. Rudra is said to have sprung from Brahmā's forehead, and to have afterwards separated himself into a figure half male and half female, the former portion sepa-rating again into the eleven Rudras, who were so called because they ‘ran about crying aloud’ [रुद-नाद् द्रावणाच्-च, cf. rts. 1. रुद्, 2. द्रु]; hence these later Rudras are sometimes regarded as inferior manifestations of Śiva, and most of their names are also names of Śiva; these names are variously given in the different Purāṇas; those of the Vāyu are Ajaikapād, Ahvi-bradhna, Hara, Nir-ṛta, Īśvara, Bhuvana, Aṅgāraka, Ardha-ketu, Mṛtyu, Sarpa, Kapālin: according to other accounts the Rudras are represented as children of Kaśyapa and Surabhī or of Brahmā and Surabhī or of Bhūta and Su-rūpā); a form or manifestation or N. of Śiva (in the later mythology, as explained above; according to the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa I. 8. Rudra is one of the eight forms of Śiva; he is elsewhere reckoned among the Dik-pālas as regent of the north-east quarter); a symbo-lical expression for the number eleven (from the eleven Rudras, see above); a mystical epithet of the letter ए; Calotropis Gigantea; N. of various persons; of a lexicographer; of a poet; of a king; (आस्), m. pl. the Rudras (described above); an abbreviated expression for the texts or hymns ad-dressed to the Rudras [cf. रुद्र-जप]; (आ), f., N. of a wife of Vasu-deva; of a daughter of Rau-drāśva; = रुद्र-जटा; (ई), f. a kind of lute or guitar; [cf. रुद्र-वीणा; cf. perhaps also Gr. λύρα.] —रुद्र-कलश, अम्, n. ‘Rudra's vessel,’ a parti-cular kind of pot or vessel used in making oblations to the planets. —रुद्र-कवीन्द्र (°वि-इन्°), अस्, m. a proper N. XXXVIII. 16) being invoked by praisers or worshippers. —रुद्र-हृदय, अम्, n., N. of an Upaniṣad. —रुद्राक्रीड (°र-आक्°), अस्, m. ‘Rudra's play-ground,’ a cemetery, place where dead bodies are burnt or buried (Rudra being supposed to dance and sport in such places at evening twilight). —रुद्राक्ष (°र-अक्°), अस्, m. ‘Rudra-eyed,’ a kind of tree, Elæocarpus Ganitrus; (अम्), n. the berry of this tree (used for rosaries); a rosary; N. of an Upaniṣad, (the gender here and in the preced-ing sense is doubtful.) —रुद्राक्ष-माला, f. a rosary made of Rudrākṣa berries. —रुद्राचार्य (°र-आच्°), अस्, m. a proper N. —रुद्राध्याय (°र-अध्°), अस्, m. epithet of particular prayers addressed to Rudra. —रुद्राध्यायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, one who recites or repeats the above prayers. —रुद्रायण (°र-अय्°), अस्, m., N. of a king of Roruka. —रुद्रारि (°र-अरि), इस्, m. Rudra's enemy; N. of Kāma-deva; (इस्, इस्, इ), having Rudra for an enemy, hostile to Rudra. —रुद्रावर्त (°र-आव्°), N. of a place of pilgrimage. —रुद्रावसृष्ट (°र-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. let go or hurled by Rudra. —रुद्रावास (°र-आव्°), अस्, m. Rudra's abode, i. e. Kāśi or Be-nares. —रुद्रैकादशिनी (°र-एक्°), f. the eleven Rudra hymns. —रुद्रोपनिषद् (°र-उप्°), त्, f., N. of two Upaniṣads. —रुद्रोपस्थ (°र-उप्°), अस्, m. ‘Rudra's generative organ,’ N. of a mountain.
39653: रुद्रक, अस्, m. a proper N.
39654: रुद्रट, अस्, m. an abbreviated form of Rudra-bhaṭṭa.

Rudra's majesty or power; (Sāy.) pleasure, delight (= सुख).

39658: रोद, अस्, m., Ved. weeping, wailing, lamenting, lamentation.
39659: रोदन, अम्, n. the act of weeping or wailing, bewailing, lamentation; weeping, a tear, tears; (ई), f. Alhagi Maurorum.

39662: रोदितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be bewailed or lamented.

39666: रोरुद्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, weeping or crying bitterly.

39670: 1. रोध, अस्, m. sprouting, growing, &c.; [cf. 2. अव-र्°, न्यग्-र्°।] —रोधावरोध (°ध-अव्°), probably ‘moving up and down.’
39671: रुध् 2. रुध्, cl. 7. P. 39672: रुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, stopped, checked, impeded, restrained, obstructed, suppressed, opposed; held, withheld; kept, kept back; shut, closed, shut up, secured; invested, besieged, blockaded; shut in, enclosed, confined, surrounded, begirt, fenced in; covered, covered up; (अस्), m., N. of a town; (आ), f. a siege. —रुद्ध-गिर्, ईर्, ईर्, ईर्, having the utterance choked or impeded. —रुद्ध-प्रवाह, अस्, आ, अम्, having the stream obstructed. —रुद्ध-मूत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having the urine suppressed; suffering from retention of urine.
39673: रुद्धक, अम्, n. citron, (perhaps for रुचक।)
39674: रुद्ध्वा, ind. having stopped or checked, having restrained or obstructed.
39675: 3. रुध्, त्, त्, त्, stopping, restraining, impeding, holding; [cf. कर-र्°।]
39676: रुध, अस्, आ, अम्, stopping, restraining, hinder-ing, repelling.
39677: रुधि-क्रा, m., Ved., N. of an Asura or demon conquered by Indra.
39678: रुन्धत्, अन्, अती, अत्, stopping, hindering, op-posing, impeding; resisting, refusing.
39679: रुरुत्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to obstruct or oppose; wishing to bind or tie up (as the hair).
39680: रोद्धव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be closed or shut.
39681: रोद्धृ, धा, ध्री, धृ, one who stops or obstructs, one who shuts in, a besieger.
39682: 2. रोध, अस्, m. (for 1. रोध see col. 1), the act of stopping, checking, arresting, restraining, hindering, impeding, preventing, &c.; restraint, stoppage, obstruction, suppression, prevention, pro-hibition; shutting up, confining; closing, blocking up; siege, blockade (of a town); attacking, making war upon; a dam, bank, shore [cf. रोधस् below]; a proper N.; N. of a hell. —रोध-कृत्, त्, m. epi-thet of the forty-fifth year in the Jupiter cycle of sixty years. —रोध-चक्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (rivers) forming eddies on the bank, (Sāy. = रोधन-शीलानि चक्राणि यासु।) —रोध-वक्रा, f. = रोधो-वक्रा।
39683: रोधक, अस्, इका, अम्, stopping, checking, re-straining, confining, shutting up, besieging, block-ading.
39684: रोधन, अस्, ई, अम्, obstructing, impeding, being an obstacle or hindrance; (अस्), m. the planet Mer-cury; (आ), f. = रोधस्; (अम्), n. the act of stop-ping, checking, restraining, preventing, impeding, oppressing; the act of confining, confinement, re-straint; besieging, blockading.
39685: रोधस्, अस्, n. a bank, embankment, dam, ob-struction; a mound, high bank, wall, a shore; the brink of a well; a flank, epithet of a woman's hips; [cf. तट।] —रोधः-पतन-कलुष, अस्, आ, अम्, (rendered) muddy by the falling in of a bank. —रो-धस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having high banks (said of rivers; Ved.); (अती), f., N. of a river. —रोधो-वक्रा, f. ‘winding along its banks,’ a river. —रोधो-वती, f. ‘having banks,’ a river. —रोधो-वप्र, अस्, m. a rapid river.
39686: रोधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, stopping, checking, restraining, hindering, preventing, prohibiting; shutting up, closing; destroying; a species of plant, (gender doubtful.)
39687: रोध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be stopped or checked, to be restrained, &c.
39688: रुधिर रुधिर, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 52. fr. rt. 2. रुध्; according to some fr. a lost rt. रुध्; according to others connected with rts. 1. रुध् and 1. रुह्; cf. रोहित), red, blood-red, bloody (Ved.); (अस्), m. the blood-red planet, i. e. Mars; a kind of precious stone [cf. रु-धिराख्य]; (अम्), n. blood; saffron; N. of a town; [cf. शोणित-पुर: cf. also Gr. ἐρεύθ-ω, ἐρυθ-ρός, ἔρευθ-ος, ἐρυθρ-ιά-ω, ἐρυσίβη, ῥούσιος:] Lat. ruber, rufu-s, rutilu-s (for old ruthilus), rob-igo: Old Norse riod-r, ‘ruddy;’ rioda: Goth. ga-riud-jo: Old Germ. rot, rost: Angl. Sax. read, roder: Slav. rud-e-ti, ruzd-a: Lith. raud-a, rud-a-s, rūdi-s: Hib. ruadh, ruaid, ‘red, reddish;’ ruaidhim, ‘I redden.’] —रुधिर-ताम्राक्ष, अस्, ई, अम्, having blood-red eyes. —रुधिर-पायिन्, ई, m. ‘drinking blood,’ a Rākṣasa or demon. —रु-धिर-प्रदिग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, besmeared with blood. —रुधिर-प्लावित, अस्, आ, अम्, swimming with blood, soaked in blood. —रुधिर-रूषित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with blood. —रुधिर-लेप, अस्, m. blood-stain, smear of blood. —रुधिर-विन्दु, उस्, m. a drop of blood. —रुधिराक्ष (°र-अक्°) = रुधि-राख्य below (according to some). —रुधिराख्य (°र-आख्°), अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘blood-named, red as blood,’ epithet of a particular precious stone. —रुधिराध्या-य (°र-अध्°), अस्, m., N. of a chapter of the Kālikā-Purāṇa treating of the sacrifice of animals. —रुधि-रानन (°र-आन्°), अम्, n. epithet of one of the five retrograding motions of Mars. —रुधिरान्ध (°र-अन्°), ‘whose waters are blood,’ N. of a hell. —रुधिरामय (°र-आम्°), अस्, m. ‘blood-disease,’ hemorrhage (= रक्त-पित्त). —रुधिराविल (°र-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, blood-stained, soiled with blood. —रुधिराशन (°र-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, feeding on blood (said of Rākṣasas &c.). —रुधिरोद्गारिन् (°र-उद्°), ई, इणी, इ, spitting blood, vomiting blood; (ई), m. epithet of the fifty-seventh year in the Jupiter cycle of sixty years.

39694: रुमण्वत्, आन्, m. a proper N.; N. of a moun-tain (‘possessing salt’).

39696: रुरु रुरु, उस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s. 39697: रुरुक, अस्, m., N. of a king.
39701: रुवण्य रुवण्य, रुवथ। See p. 847, col. 3.

39704: रुश् रुश् (connected with and in some forms and meanings identified with rt. 1. रुष्), cl. 6. P. रुशति, रुरोश, रोक्ष्यति, अरुक्षत्, रोष्टुम्, to hurt, injure, kill; to vex, displease, annoy: Caus. रोशयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अरूरुशत्: Desid. रुरुक्षति: Intens. रोरुश्यते, रोरोष्टि।

39706: रुशङ्गु रुशङ्गु, उस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi.
39707: रुशत् 2. रुशत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत् (probably to be regarded as a participle connected with rt. 1. रुच्), Ved. brilliant, bright, light-coloured, white; [cf. Gr. λευκός] —रुशत्-पशु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having white cattle; (Sāy.) having brilliant rays or blazing with the oblation (= रुशद्-रश्मि or प्रकाशित-हविस्). —रुशद्-ऊर्मि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having glis-tening waves, having bright flames (said of Fire; Sāy. = दीप्त-ज्वाल). —रुशद्-गु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having white or bright cattle; bright-rayed, (Sāy. = रोचमान-रश्मि); (उस्), m. a proper N. —रु-शद्-रथ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a light-coloured carriage; (अस्), m. a proper N. —रुशद्-वत्स, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a bright or white calf or offspring, (the Dawn is so called as parent of the Sun.)
39708: रुशना रुशना, f., N. of one of the wives of Rudra.
39709: रुशम रुशम, अस्, m. a proper N.; (आ), f. a proper N., (Ruśamā is said to have contended with Indra as to which of the two would run fastest round the earth, and to have won by the artifice of only going round Kurukṣetra.)
39710: रुशेकु रुशेकु, उस्, m., N. of a king.
39711: रुष् 1. रुष् (connected with and in some forms and meanings identified with rt. रुश्; allied also to रुक्ष् in 1. रुक्ष), cl. 1. P. रोषति, रुरोष, रोषिष्यति, अरोषीत् or अरुषत्, रोषितुम् or रोष्टुम्, to hurt, injure, kill; to vex, annoy, displease, make angry, disgust; to take ill, be offended (Ved.); cl. 4. रुष्यति, to be vexed or annoyed; to be offended; to be cross or angry; to injure, &c.: cl. 10. or Caus. रोषयति, -यि-तुम्, Aor. अरूरुषत्, to vex, annoy, displease, irritate; to enrage, exasperate: Desid. रुरुषिषति, रुरोषि-षति: Intens. रोरुष्यते, रोरोष्टि; [cf. probably Gr. λύσσα, λυσσάω, λυσσαίνω, (perhaps also) ἀλυσταίνω, ἀλυκταίνω, ἀλαλὐκτημαι; Goth. in-rauht-jan.]

39713: रुषङ्गु, उस्, m., N. of a Brāhman.

39717: रुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, enraged, irritated, offended, angry, furious; (अस्), m., N. of a Muni.

39725: रोषित, अस्, आ, अम्, enraged, exasperated, irritated.

39774: रेचक, अस्, इका, अम्, emptying, purging, purga-tive, aperient, cathartic; emptying the lungs, emitting the breath; (अस्), m. the act of breathing out or exha-lation, expiration or emission of breath, (especially) expelling the breath out of one of the nostrils (in the practice of Yoga); a syringe; N. of various aperient medicines; the purging-nut plant, Croton Jamalgota; nitre, saltpetre; N. of a forester in the Vikramorvaśī; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (अम्), n. a purge, cathartic.
39775: रेचन, अस्, ई, अम्, purging, purgative, cathartic, aperient; (ई), f., N. of various plants (= त्रि-वृत्, दन्ती, गुन्द्रा, रोचनिका, काम्पिल्ल, कालाञ्जनी); (अम्, आ), n. f. the act of emptying, making empty or void, lessening, diminishing; emitting the breath; purging, looseness; evacuation.
39777: रेचित, अस्, आ, अम्, left void or empty, freed from, cleared; purged; (अम्), n., N. of one of a horse's paces, cantering [cf. rt. 1. रेज्]; a particular position of the hands in dancing.
39779: रेख रेख, अस्, m. (fr. रिख् = rt. लिख्), a line, &c. (= रेखा below); a proper N.; (आ). f. a line; a streak, stripe; a row, series [cf. लेखा]; a continuous line; drawing; the first or prime me-ridian (considered to be a line drawn from Laṅkā to Meru, i. e. from Ceylon supposed to lie on the equator to the North-pole); = आभोग, fulness, satis-faction; = छद्मन्, deceit, fraud; a small quantity, little portion; [cf. probably Old Germ. riga.] —रे-खांश (°खा-अं°), अस्, m. a degree of longitude. —रेखाकार (°खा-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, formed in lines, striped. —रेखा-गणित, अम्, n. ‘line-reckon-ing,’ geometry. —रेखान्तर (°खा-अन्°), अम्, n. geographical longitude, distance east or west from the first meridian, (see रेखा above.) —रेखा-न्यास, अस्, m. the marking down of lines or lineaments.
39781: रेखाय, Nom. A. रेखायते, &c., to praise, flatter; to vex, distress, annoy.
39783: रेखिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having lines (on the hand &c.), lined.
39785: रेज् 1. रेज् [cf. rt. 1. राज्], cl. 1. A. रेजते (Ved. also P. रेजति), &c., to shine; to shake, tremble, quiver, flicker (Ved.); to cause to tremble or shake (Ved. P.); (according to Naigh. II. 14) to go (P.): Caus. रेजयति, &c., to cause to tremble or quake, to shake.
39786: 2. रेज्, ट्, ट्, ट्, shining; shaking, a shaker; (ट्), m., N. of Agni or fire.
39787: रेजमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. quaking, trembling.
39788: रेट् रेट्, cl. 1. P. A. रेटति, -ते, रिरेट, रिरेटे, रेटितुम्, to speak; to ask, seek, request: Caus. रेटयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अरिरेटत्: Desid. रिरेटिषति, -ते: Intens. रेरेट्यते, रेरेट्टि।
39789: रेड् रेड् or रेऌ (a Vedic rt. probably con-nected with rt. 1. रिष्), to be angry, &c., (according to Naigh. II. 12. रेऌअते = क्रुध्यति।)
39790: रेणु रेणु, उस्, m. (according to some also उस्, उ, f. n.; according to Uṇādi-s. III. 38. fr. rt. 1. री), dust, a grain or atom of dust, sand, &c.; the pollen of a flower; N. of a particular medicinal drug (= रेणुका, पर्पट); N. of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda IX. 70, X. 89, (his patronymic is Vaiśvāmitra); of a son of Vikukṣi; (उस्), f., N. of a wife of Viśvā-mitra. —रेणु-ककाट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. furrowing through or tossing up the dust; (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VI. 28, 4 = रजस उद्भेदकः।) —रेणु-कारिका, f., N. of a Kārikā. —रेणु-गर्भ, अस्, m. ‘sand-vessel,’ (probably) a kind of hour glass (used for astronomical purposes). —रेणु-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of dust, the being dust, dustiness. —रेणु-दीक्षित, अस्, m., N. of an author. —रेणु-प, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —रेणु-पदवी, f. a path of dust. —रेणु-पालक, अस्, m. a proper N. —रेणु-मत्, आन्, m., N. of a son of Viśvā-mitra by Reṇu. —रेणु-रूषित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with dust, dusty; (अस्), m. an ass. —रेणु-वास, अस्, आ, अम्, dwelling in dust, covered with the pollen of flowers; (अस्), m. a bee. —रेणु-शस्, ind. to dust, into dust, (रेणुशः कृ, to make into dust, turn to dust.) —रेणु-सार or रेणु-सारक, अस्, m. ‘essence of dust, ‘camphor.
39791: रेणुक, अस्, m., N. of a Yakṣa; of a mythical elephant; of a particular formula recited over weapons; (आ), f. a particular drug or medicinal substance (said to be fragrant, but bitter and slightly pungent in taste, and of a greyish colour; it is procured in grains about the size of pepper-corns); a sort of pulse; N. of the wife of Jamad-agni and mother of Paraśu-rāma, (she was the daughter of Reṇu and of king Prasena-jit); N. of a Kārikā composed by Hari-hara. —रेणुकाचार्य (°क-आच्°), अस्, m., N. of an author. —रेणुका-सुत, अस्, m. ‘son of Reṇukā,’ i. e. Pa-raśu-rāma.
39793: रेतस् रेतस्, अस्, n. (fr. rt. 1. री), a flow, flood, stream, current, flow of water or rain (Ved.); flow of semen, seminal fluid, semen, sperm, virile energy; seed, offspring, progeny, posterity, descendants (Ved.); quicksilver (regarded as ‘Śiva's semen’); sin, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda IV. 3, 7 = पाप।) —रेतः-कुल्या, f. a stream or river of semen virile (in a particular hell). —रेतः-सिच्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. discharging semen; an epithet of particular Iṣṭakās. —रेतः-सिच्य, अम्, n., Ved. discharge of semen. —रेतस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessed of seed, abounding in seed, impregnat-ing, prolific, productive; (आन्), m. epithet of Agni. —रेतस्-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. abounding in seed, pro-lific, productive. —रेतो-धा, आस्, f., Ved. the act of impregnating, impregnation; (आस्, आस्, अम्), impreg-nating, fertilizing; (आस्), m. a father. —रेतो-धेय, अम्, n., Ved. impregnation. —रेतो-मार्ग, अस्, m. the seminal duct or canal.
39794: रेत = रेतस्, semen virile. —रेत-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born or produced from seed; any beloved offspring or child; (आ), f. sand.
39796: रेतस at the end of a comp. = रेतस्; [cf. अग्नि-र्°, कपोत-र्°।]
39797: रेतस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. conveying seed, (the first verse of the Bahiṣpavamāna Stotra is so called.)
39798: रेतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. abounding in seed; impreg-nating.
39800: रेत्र, अम्, n. semen virile; quicksilver; nectar, ambrosia; perfumed or aromatic powder; (these meanings are sometimes given to वेत्र, which is confounded with रेत्र।)
39801: रेधक रेधक, अस्, m. a proper N., (also read रेचक।)
39802: रेप् रेप्, cl. 1. A. रेपते, &c., to go, move; to sound.

39804: रेफ रेफ, रेफस्, रेफिन्। See p. 846, col. 2.

39806: रेभ् रेभ्। See rt. रिभ्, p. 846, col. 3.

39808: रेरिवन् रेरिवन्, आ, m., Ved. = प्रेरयितृ।
39809: रेरिह रेरिह, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens. of rt. रिह्, q. v.), Ved. continually or repeatedly licking.

39812: रेव् रेव् or रेब्, cl. 1. A. रेवते, रेबते, &c., to go, move, flow; to leap, jump, go by leaps.

39814: रेवट, अस्, m. a boar; a bamboo cane; a whirl-wind; a kind of poison; oil of the Morunga tree; the fruit of the plantain; (अम्), n. a muscle or conch-shell with its windings or spiral lines going from right to left.
39815: रेवण, अस्, m. a proper N.
39816: रेवत् रे-वत्, रे-वती। See below and p. 854.
39817: रेवत रेवत, अस्, m. the citron tree; Ca-thartocarpus Fistula; N. of various persons; of a son of Andhaka or of Ānarta; of the father of Revatī and father-in-law of Bala-rāma; of a Varṣa (?) .
39818: रेवतक, अस्, m. a proper N.; (अम्), n. a species of plant.

39824: 1. रेषण, अम्, n. the howl of a wolf, howling, yelling, roaring.
39825: रेषा, f. howling, yelling (of wolves); neighing.
39826: रेषित, अस्, आ, अम्, yelled, sounded; (अम्), n. neighing, roaring.
39827: रेष् 3. रेष्, ट् (fr. rt. 1. रिष्), in Vājasa-neyi-s. VI. 18. according to Mahī-dhara = रिष्टा or हिंसिता, (perhaps referrible to rt. रिश्, to injure.)
39828: रेष, अस्, m., Ved. injury, hurt, receiving injury.
39829: 2. रेषण, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. injuring, hurting; (अम्), n. the act of injuring, injury, hurt, damage; failure.
39830: रेषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, injuring, hurting; [cf. पुरु-ष-र्°।]
39831: रेष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, one who injures or hurts, an injurer.

39834: रेहत् रेहत्, see Gaṇa Bhṛśādi to Pāṇ. III. 1, 12.
39835: रेहाय, Nom. A. रेहायते, &c., see Gaṇa Bhṛ-śādi to Pāṇ. III. 1, 12.
39836: रै 1. रै, cl. 1. P. रायति, ररौ, रातुम्, to bark, bark at (with acc.); to sound; [cf. Lat. latrare.]
39837: 2. रै, आस् (?) , m. barking, sound, noise.

(connected with रयि, q. v., fr. rt. 1. रा; acc. रायम्, Ved. राम् = Lat. rem; for other cases see Gram. 132), property, possessions, goods, wealth, gold; costliness; (रै), ind., see Gaṇa Cādi to Pāṇ. 39839: रे-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (रे contracted fr. रयि + वत्), having prosperity or wealth, rich, wealthy, opulent, prosperous; grand in external appearance, shining, glittering, beautiful, illustrious; (अत्), ind., Ved. ra-diantly, beautifully; (अती), f., N. of the fifth Nak-ṣatra, (see नक्षत्र; sometimes also अत्यस्, f. pl.); the day of Revatī; N. of the evil genius or goddess presiding over a particular sickness, (some-times identified with Durgā, sometimes with Aditi); N. of the wife of Mitra; of a daughter of the Lustre (कान्ति) of the Nakṣatra Revatī and mother of Manu Raivata; of the wife of Bala-rāma (daughter of Kakudmin); of a wife of Amṛtodana; (अत्यस्) f. pl. ‘the wealthy ones, the shining ones,’ epithet of cows (Ved.); waters, water, a quantity of water (Ved.); epithet of the verse Ṛg-veda I. 30, 13 (so called from रेवती being the first word; the Raivata Sāman is formed from this verse; according to Pāṇ. 39840: रेवत्य (a Vedic adjective fr. रेवती, Pāṇ. IV. 4, 122), illustrious, beautiful, &c. (?)

39843: रैय, Nom. P. रैयति, &c., to desire riches.

39846: रैवतिक, अस्, m. a metronymic from Revatī.
39848: रैवत्य, अम्, n. (fr. रेवत्), riches, wealth; रैवत्य ऋषभः, N. of a Sāman.
39849: रैख रैख, अस्, m. (fr. रेख), a patro-nymic.
39850: रैणव रैणव, अस्, m. (fr. रेणु), a patro-nymic; (अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.

39852: रैतस रैतस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. रेतस्), Ved. be-longing to seed or semen, seminal.
39853: रैतिक रैतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. रीति), of or belonging to brass, brazen.

39933: रोहत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, rising, mounting, ascending, growing.

39940: रोहिणिका, f. a woman with a red face (either from anger or from being coloured with pigments); inflammation of the throat.
39941: रोहिणी, f. (fem. of रोहित, col. 2; see also the fem. of रोहिन्, col. 2), a red cow, (in the Veda perhaps also) a red mare; a cow in general, (in Hindū mythology Rohiṇī is represented as a daughter of Surabhi and mother of cattle; she is also said to be the mother of Kāma-dhenu, the cow of plenty); N. of the ninth Nakṣatra or lunar asterism (personified as a daughter of Dakṣa, and the favourite wife of the Moon, called ‘the Red one,’ from the colour of the star Aldebaran or principal star in the constellation; the Nakṣatra contains five stars, probably α, β, γ, δ, ε, Tauri, and according to Hindū notions is figured by a wheeled carriage or sometimes by a temple or a fish); N. of the lunar day belonging to the above Nakṣatra; lightning; a young girl, one in whom menstruation has just commenced, a girl nine years of age; inflammation of the throat (of various kinds); N. of various plants, a kind of vegetable (= कटु-रोहिणी, सोम-वल्क, काश्मरी, हरीतकी, मञ्जिष्-ठा); N. of a wife of Vasu-deva and mother of Bala-rāma; of a wife of Kṛṣṇa; of the wife of Mahā-deva; of a daughter of Hiraṇya-kaśipu; of one of the sixteen Vidyā-devīs; (according to Pāṇ. IV. 4, 34, Vārtt. 1, there is an adj. रोहिणी, meaning ‘born under the Nakṣatra Rohiṇī.’) —रोहिणी-कान्त, अस्, m. ‘the lover of Rohiṇī,’ epithet of the Moon. —रोहिणी-चन्द्र-व्रत and रोहिणी-चन्द्र-शयन, अम्, n., N. of two religious observances. —रोहिणी-तनय, अस्, m. the son of Rohiṇī, i. e. Bala-rāma. —रोहिणी-तपस्, N. of a work. —रो-हिणी-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —रोहिणी-त्व, अम्, n., Ved. the state or condition of the Nakṣatra Rohiṇī. —रोहिणी-पति, इस्, m. the husband of Ro-hiṇī, i. e. the Moon. —रोहिणी-प्रिय, अस्, m. the lover of Rohiṇī, i. e. the Moon. —रोहिणी-भव, अस्, m. the son of Rohiṇī, i. e. the planet Mercury. —रोहिणी-योग, अस्, m. the conjunction of the moon with the Nakṣatra Rohiṇī. —रोहिणी-रमण, अस्, m. ‘the lover of the cow,’ a bull; the lover or husband of Rohiṇī, i. e. the Moon. —रोहिणी-वल्-लभ, अस्, m. the lover of Rohiṇī, i. e. the Moon. —रोहिणी-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a particular reli-gious observance. —रोहिणीश (°नी-ईश), अस्, m. the lord or husband of Rohiṇī, i. e. the Moon. —रोहिणी-शकट, अस्, अम्, m. n. an asterism, probably α, β, γ, δ, ε, Tauri. —रोहिणी-षेण, अस्, m. a proper N.; [cf. रोहिणि-षेण।] —रोहिणी-सुत, अस्, m. ‘son of Rohiṇī, ‘the planet Mercury. —रोहिण्य्-अष्टमी, f. the eighth day in the dark half of the month Bhādra when the moon is in conjunction with the Nakṣatra Rohiṇī.
39942: रोहित्, त्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 99. fr. rt. 1. रुह्), the sun; a species of fish, = रोहित; (त्), f. a red mare (Ved.); the female of a deer, doe; a sort of creeper; (तस्), f. pl. epithet of rivers (ac-cording to Naigh. I. 13); the fingers (according to Naigh. II. 5); (त्, त्, त्), red, of a red colour. —रो-हिद्-अश्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having red mares (said of Agni).
39943: रोहित, अस्, आ or (more commonly) रोहिणी, अम् [cf. लोहित], red, of a red colour [cf. रुधिर]; coloured; (अस्), m. red (the colour), a red horse; a fox; a form of Fire or the Sun (Ved.); another deity in Atharva-veda XIII. 1; N. of the hymns of the above Veda in which the god Rohita is mentioned; a kind of deer; a species of fish, Cyprinus Ro-hita; a kind of tree, Andersonia Rohitaka; a sort of ornament made of precious stones; a particular form of rainbow, (see रोहितम् below); N. of a son of Hari-ścandra; of a Manu; of a son of Kṛṣṇa; of a son of Vapuṣ-mat (king of Śālmala); of a river; (आस्), m. pl. epithet of a class of Gandharvas; of a class of gods under the twelfth Manu; (इणी), f., see col. 1; (अम्), n. a kind of rainbow appearing in a straight form, Indra's bow unbent and invisible to mortals; blood; saffron. —रोहित-कूल, N. of a place. —रोहित-कूलीय and रोहित-कूलीयाद्य and रोहित-कूलीयोत्तर, अम्, n., N. of Sāmans. —रो-हित-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —रोहित-गिरीय, आस्, m. pl. the inhabitants of the mountain Rohita-giri. —रोहित-पुर, अम्, n., N. of the town founded by Rohitaka the son of Hari-ścandra. —रो-हित-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having a red horse. —रोहित-वस्तु, N. of a place. —रोहिताक्ष (°त-अक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, red-eyed, having red eyes. —रो-हिताञ्जि (°त-अञ्°), इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. marked with red. —रोहिताश्व, अस्, आ, अम्, having red horses; (अस्), m. the god of fire, Agni; N. of a son of Hari-ścandra. —रोहितैत (°त-एत), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. variegated with red.

39955: रौक्षक रौक्षक, अस्, m. a patronymic.

39987: रौहिण रौहिण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. रोहिणी), born under the Nakṣatra Rohiṇī; (अस्), m. the sandal tree; the Indian fig-tree; N. of Agni; of a demon vanquished by Indra; a proper N. 40456: लिङ्ग, अम्, n. (perhaps connected with rt. लग्), a mark, sign, token, emblem, badge, anything which distinguishes or defines, distinguishing or discrimi-nating mark, characteristic mark, characteristic, sec-tarian mark; a symptom, mark of disease; a false badge, any badge or mark assumed with a view to deceive; a spot, stain; a proof, evidence, means of proof, proof from a sure sign or token; (in logic) = व्याप्य, the predicate of a proposition or the mark which characterizes the subject (as in the pro-position ‘there is fire because there is smoke, and fire has smoke, ‘smoke is the लिङ्ग), inference, conclusion, reason, (काव्य-लिङ्ग, a particular figure of speech in which the grounds of a statement are explained after the statement has been made); the sign of gender or sex, organ of generation; gender (in grammar, cf. पुं-लिङ्ग); the male organ; Śiva's genital organ or Śiva worshipped in the form of a Phallus, (this is usually of stone or marble, and set up in temples appropriated to Śiva; there were formerly twelve principal Śiva-liṅgas in India, of which two or three of the best known are Soma-nātha in Gujarāt, Mahākāla at Ujjayinī, Viśveśvara at Be-nares, &c.); the image of a god, an idol; the subtile frame or body which is not destroyed by death, the indestructible original of the gross or visible body [cf. लिङ्ग-शरीर, सूक्ष्म-श्°]; = प्रातिपदिक, a nominal base, the crude form or base of a noun (shortened by Vopa-deva into लि); (according to some) Prakṛti or Pradhāna (i. e. the primary germ out of which all phenomena are evolved in the Sāṅkhya phil.); the effect or product (i. e. according to others, that which is evolved out of a primary cause, and becomes in its turn a producer, = व्यक्त in the Sāṅkhya phil.); (ई), m. = लिङ्ग-वत्, q. v.; (इणी), f., N. of Dākṣāyaṇī in Naimiṣa. —लिङ्ग-नाश, अस्, m. loss of character-istic marks; a particular disease of the eyes, (loss of vision from cataract &c., considered to be a discolora-tion of the pupil); loss of the penis. —लिङ्ग-प-रामर्श, अस्, m. the groping after or seeking for a sign or token (in logic), the consideration of a sign or characteristic (as that smokiness is a sign of fire). —लिङ्ग-पीठ, अम्, n. the pedestal of a Liṅga. —लिङ्ग-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of one of the eigh-teen Purāṇas (in which Śiva, supposed to be present in the Agni-liṅga or great fiery Liṅga, gives an account of the creation &c. as well as of his own incarnations in opposition to those of Viṣṇu). —लिङ्ग-प्रतिष्ठा-विधि, इस्, m. rules for the establishment of a Liṅga. —लिङ्ग-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. the majesty or pre-eminence of the Liṅga, N. of a section of several Purāṇas. —लिङ्ग-मूर्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, having the form of the Phallus (said of Śiva). —लिङ्ग-लेप, अस्, m., N. of a particular disease. —लिङ्ग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having marks, possessed of signs or tokens; having various sexes or genders; furnished with a Liṅga or wearing a small repre-sentation of the Liṅga of Śiva round the neck or on one arm (applied as an epithet to a particular Śaiva sect, also called Jaṅgamas). —लिङ्ग-वर्धन, अस्, ई, अम्, causing erections of the male organ; (अस्), m. Feronia Elephantum. —लिङ्ग-वर्धिन्, ई, इनी, ई, causing erections; (इनी), f. Achyranthes Aspera. —लिङ्ग-विपर्यय, अस्, m. change of gender. —लिङ्ग-विशेष-विधि, इस्, m. rules for the different genders, N. of a grammatical treatise ascribed to Vara-ruci. —लिङ्ग-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, making a live-lihood by false appearance or assumed outward marks, hypocritical; (इस्), m. a religious hypocrite, one who assumes the dress &c. of an ascetic to gain a liveli-hood. —लिङ्ग-वेदी, f. the pedestal of a Liṅga. —लिङ्ग-शरीर, अम्, n. the subtile body which accompanies the grosser in all its transmigrations and is not destroyed by death. —लिङ्ग-शास्त्र, अम्, n. a grammatical treatise on gender. —लिङ्ग-सम्-भूता, f., N. of a particular plant. —लिङ्ग-स्थ, अस्, m. a religious student. —लिङ्ग-हनी, f. = मूर्वा। —लिङ्गाग्र (°ग-अग्°), अस्, m. glans penis. —लिङ्-गानुशासन (°ग-अन्°), अम्, n. the doctrine or laws of grammatical gender. —लिङ्गार्चन (°ग-अर्°), अम्, n. worship of the Liṅga or Phallus. —लिङ्गार्-चन-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work. —लिङ्-गार्चा-प्रतिष्ठा-विधि (°ग-अर्°), इस्, m., N. of a work.

41015: वण्टनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be apportioned, divisi-ble, to be divided.
41016: वण्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, divided into shares, distri-buted.
41017: वण्टाल वण्टाल or वण्ठाल, अस्, m. a spade, shovel, hoe; a boat; a kind of battle, the contest of heroes; [cf. वण्डाल।]
41018: वण्ठ् वण्ठ्, cl. 1. A. वण्ठते, ववण्ठे, वण्ठितुम्, to go or move alone, go un-accompanied.
41019: वण्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, crippled, maimed; unmarried; (अस्), m. an unmarried man; a servant; a dwarf; a javelin; [cf. वण्ड।]
41020: वण्ठर, अस्, m. the new shoot of the Tāl or palm tree; the sheath that envelopes the young bamboo; a rope for tying a goat, &c.; the female breast; a dog's tail; a dog; a cloud.
41021: वण्ड् वण्ड् (connected with rt. वण्ट्), cl. 1. A. वण्डते, ववण्डे, वण्डितुम्, to partition, apportion, share, divide; to surround, encompass; to cover; cl. 10. P. वण्डयति, &c., to partition, share, divide.
41022: वण्ड वण्ड, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. 1. वन् or वण्), maimed, defective, crippled (espe-cially in the hands or feet or tail), one whose hands have been cut off [cf. वण्ठ]; impotent, emasculated [cf. पण्ड]; (अस्), m. a man who is circumcised or has no prepuce, (probably a wrong reading for चण्ड); an ox without a tail [cf. अ-वण्ड]; (आ), f. an unchaste woman, (probably a wrong reading for रण्डा।)
41023: वण्डर, अस्, m. a niggard, miser; a eunuch or attendant on the women's apartments.
41024: वण्डाल वण्डाल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. वण्ड्), a particular mode of fighting, the contest of heroes; a boat; a spade, a hoe.
41025: वत् 1. वत्, ind. an affix (technically termed वति) added to words to imply likeness or resem-blance, and generally translatable by ‘as,’ ‘like’ (e. g. ब्राह्मण-वत्, like a Brāhman).
41026: वत् 2. वत्, a Vedic rt. usually connected with अपि, (probably) cl. 1. वतति, &c., to understand, comprehend, apprehend, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 3, 10. वतेम = सम्भ-जेमहि, ‘may we share in or possess or obtain,’ where वत् is said to stand for rt. 1. वन्): Caus. वातयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अवीवतत्, to cause to under-stand, make intelligible; to excite, awaken, (Sāy. = प्रापयति, आगमयति, प्रेरयति।)
41027: वतत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, understanding, comprehending, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 60, 6 = गच्छत्, going.)
41028: वातयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to understand; exciting, &c., (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 165, 13. अपि-वातयत् = सम्पूर्णम् प्रापयत्, causing to obtain completely.)
41029: वत 1. वत, ind. in the earlier language generally written बत, q. v.; for 2. वत see p. 883, col. 1), a particle expressing sorrow, com-passion, pleasure, surprise, &c., and generally trans-latable by ‘ah!’ ‘alas!’ ‘oh!’ also used as a vocative particle; (in later Sanskrit वत is often found in the middle of a sentence.)
41030: वतंस व-तंस or व-तंसक, अस्, m. = अव-तंस, a garland; a ring-shaped ornament, ear-ring, ear-ornament; a crest.
41031: वतण्ड वतण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a Muni; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of Vataṇḍa, (तण्ड-वतण्-डास्, m. pl. the descendants of Taṇḍa and Vataṇḍa); (ई), f. a female descendant of Vataṇḍa.
41032: वति वति, see under rt. 1. वन्। (For the affix वति see 1. वत्, col. 1.)
41033: वतू वतू, ऊस्, f. a river of heaven; (ऊस्), m. one who speaks the truth, a road; a disease of the eyes.
41034: वतोका व-तोका, f. = अव-तोका, a cow mis-carrying from accident.
41035: वत्स वत्स, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 62. fr. rt. वद्), a calf, a young animal or the young of any animal, offspring, child, (वत्स, voc. c. ‘my dear child, my darling,’ used as a term of en-dearment; जीवद्-वत्सा, a woman whose child is still alive); a son, boy, (बाल-वत्सा, a woman whose son is still a boy); a year [cf. वत्सर]; N. of a son or descendant of Kaṇva; of a descendant of Agni (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 187); of a descendant of Kaśyapa; of the author of a law-book; of a son of Pratardana; of a son of Prasena-jit; of a son of Akṣa-mālā; of a son of Uru-kṣepa; of a son of Soma-śarman; N. of a country (its chief town is Kauśāmbhī); (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of Vatsa; N. of the inhabitants of Vatsa and of the country; (आ), f. a female calf; a little daughter, little girl, (वत्से, voc. c. ‘my dear child,’ used as a term of endearment); (अम्), n. the breast, chest, (according to some authorities also अस्, m.); [cf. Gr. ἰτ-αλό-ς (for ϝιταλός,); Lat. vitulu-s, vitula; Osk. Viteliu (= Italia); Slav. tel-ici; Bohem. tel-e; Lith. telycza.] —वत्स-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, child-loving, fondly loving or affectionate towards offspring; (आ), f. a cow longing for her calf; a mother anxious after her child. —वत्स-गुरु, उस्, m. a teacher of children, preceptor. —वत्स-तन्त्री, ईस्, f. a rope for tying calves. —वत्स-तर, अस्, m. ‘more than a calf,’ a weaned calf, young ox or bull, bullock, steer, (also applied to the young of goats); N. of Kṛṣṇa; of Bala-deva. —वत्स-पालन, अम्, n. the act of keeping calves. —वत्स-प्रचेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. minding or taking care of Vatsa or the Vatsas, (Sāy. = स्तोतरि प्रकृष्ट-ज्ञान, favourably-minded towards a worshipper.) —वत्स-प्री, ईस्, m., N. of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda IX. 68, X. 45, 46, (his patronymic is Bhālandana.) —वत्स-प्रीति, इस्, m. = वत्स-प्री. —वत्स-बन्धा, f. a cow longing for her calf. —वत्स-बालक, अस्, m., N. of a brother of Vasu-deva. —वत्स-भूमि, इस्, f. the land of the Vatsas, N. of a country; (आन्), m., N. of one of the sons of Śūra. —वत्स-विन्द, अस्, m. a proper N.; (आस्), m. pl. Vatsa-vinda's descendants. —वत्स-वृद्-ध, अस्, m., N. of a son of Uru-kriya. —वत्स-व्यूह, अस्, m., N. of a son of Vatsa. —वत्स-शाला, f. a calf-shed; (अस्, आ, अम्), born in a calf-shed. —वत्-साक्षी (°स-अक्°), f. a kind of cucumber, Cucumis Madraspatanus. —वत्साङ्क (°स-अङ्°), अस्, m. a proper N. —वत्साजीव (°स-आज्°), अस्, आ, अम्, living by calves, obtaining a livelihood by keeping calves; (अस्), m. epithet of a Piṅgala. —वत्सादन (°स-अद्°), अस्, ई, अम्, eating calves; (अस्), m. a wolf; (ई), f. ‘eating its own offspring,’ Cocculus Cordifolius (so called as not bringing all its berries to maturity). —वत्सासुर (°स-अस्°), अस्, m., N. of an Asura. —वत्सेश or वत्सेश्वर (°स-ईश्°), अस्, m. a king of Vatsa.
41036: वत्सक, अस्, m. a little calf, calf, or young animal in general; a child, offspring; a medicinal plant, Wrightia Antidysenterica; N. of a son of Śūra; of an Asura; (इका), f. a calf, female calf, a heifer, young cow; (अम्), n. green or black sulphate of iron. —वत्सक-वीज, अम्, n. the seed of Wrightia Antidysenterica.
41037: वत्सर, अस्, m. the fifth year in a cycle of five or six years; the sixth year in a cycle of six years; a year; the Year personified as a son of Dhruva and Bhrami; N. of Viṣṇu; of a Sādhya; of a son of Kaśyapa; [cf. Gr. ἔτος (ϝέρος), ἐτήσιο-ς, ἐτησίαι, δυσετηρία; Lat. vetus, vetus-tu-s, vetulu-s; Lith. wasara; Slav. vetuchu.] —वत्सरादि (°र-आदि), इस्, m. the first month of the Hindū year, the month Mārgaśīrṣa. —वत्सरान्तक (°र-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘Year-destroyer,’ N. of the month Phālguna. —वत्-सरार्ण (°र-ऋण), अम्, n. a debt or loan for a year (?); see Vopa-deva II. 9.
41038: वत्सल, अस्, आ, अम्, child-loving, affectionate towards offspring, affectionate in general; kind, lov-ing, tender; fond of, wholly given up to, devoted to, longing for (sometimes with loc., e. g. गावो वत्सेषु वत्सलाः, cows longing for their calves); (अस्), m. a fire fed with grass (i. e. quickly burning away); N. of one of Skanda's attendants; (आ), f. a cow fond of her calf; (अम्), n. affection, fondness. —वत्सल-ता, f. or वत्सल-त्व, अम्, n. affectionateness, loving-ness, tenderness, affection.
41039: वत्सलय, Nom. P. वत्सलयति, &c., to make tender or affectionate (especially towards offspring or children).
41040: वत्साय, Nom. P. वत्सायति, &c., to represent or be like a calf.
41041: वत्सायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, acting like a calf.
41042: वत्सार, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kaśyapa.
41043: वत्सिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a calf; (ई), m. (perhaps) ‘having many children,’ N. of Viṣṇu.
41044: वत्सिमन्, आ, m. childhood, youth, early youth.
41045: वत्सीय, अस्, आ, अम्, proper or fit for a calf; (अस्), m. a cowherd.
41046: वत्सणुरकतीर्थ वत्सणुरक-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
41047: वथ्सर वथ्सर, अस्, m. = वत्सर (accord-ing to the grammarian Pauṣkarasādi).
41048: वद् वद् (sometimes lengthened in ep. into वाद् on account of the metre), cl. 1. P. A. वदति, वदते, उवाद (3rd du. ऊदतुस्, 3rd pl. ऊदुस्; according to Vopa-deva VIII. 52, 2nd sing. also वेदिथ, 3rd du. वेदतुस्, 3rd pl. वेदुस्), ऊदे (3rd du. ऊदाते, 3rd pl. ऊदिरे), वदिष्यति, -ते, अवादीत्, अवदिष्ट, Prec. उद्यात्, वदितुम्, to speak, say, utter, tell, speak to, address (with acc. of the thing said and of the person addressed and sometimes with prep. अभि and acc., both P. and A. being used indiscriminately, e. g. यद् वदसि माम्, that which thou sayest to me; माम् अभि वदति, he speaks to me; किं वदामि or वदे, what must I say? मैवं वद or वदस्व, do not speak so; स-त्यं वद or वदस्व, speak the truth; देवानां वचनात् त्वां वदामि or वदे, I speak to thee in the name of the gods; प्रतिवाक्यं वद or वद-स्व, speak a reply); to speak about, declare, proclaim, announce, communicate, inform, notify; to maintain, affirm; to designate, call, name; to raise the voice, sign, utter a cry (said of birds &c.); to discuss, dispute about, contend, quarrel (Ved. A.); to be called, be con-sidered (Ved. A.); to state authoritatively (?), be an authority (A.); to exert one's self, strive for (A.): Pass. उद्यते, Aor. अवादि, Part. उदित (see 2. उदित), to be said or spoken, to be addressed or spoken to; to be declared or announced, to be published or proclaimed: Caus. वादयति, -यते, -यितुम्, Aor. अवीवदत्, to cause to speak or say, to urge or invite to speak; to cause to sound forth, play (a musical instrument; generally P.), to play music; to cause to be played by any one (inst.); to speak, recite, rehearse: Pass. of Caus. वाद्यते: Desid. विवदि-षति, -ते, to desire to speak: Intens. वावद्यते, वावत्ति, वावदीति, to speak aloud; to sound loudly; [cf. Gr. ὕδ-ω, ὑδ-έ-ω, ὕδ-η-ς, ἀ(ϝ)είδ-ω, ἀοιδό-ς, ἀοιδή, ἀηδών, (according to some) αὐδή, αὐδάω, (perhaps also) φράζω, φραδάω: (probably) Lat. vas (vad-is): (perhaps) Old Germ. far-wāzan: Old Sax. for-wātan: Lith. vad-i-n-u, ‘I call:' Slav. vad-i-ti, vāda, ‘accusation;’ us-ta, ‘mouth:’ Hib. feadaim, ‘I say;' (perhaps) luadhaim, ‘I men-tion;’ raidim, ‘I say.’]
41049: वद, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking, able to speak, speak-ing well or sensibly, (frequently at the end of comps.; cf. प्रियं-व्°, कु-व्°); (अस्), m., N. of a so-called Veda (with the Magians).
41050: वदक = वद in दुर्-वदक, q. v.
41051: वदत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, speaking, saying, telling.
41052: वदन, अम्, n. the act of speaking or saying; sounding (Ved.); the mouth, face, countenance, (काल-वदन, ‘the face of Time,’ N. of a Śaiva work), aspect, appearance, look; the front, point; the first term, initial quantity or term of a progres-sion (in algebra); the summit or apex of a triangle; [cf. 41054: वदन्ति, इस्, or वदन्ती, f. speech, discourse, talk, (according to some only used in किं-व्°, q. v.)
41055: वदन्तिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
41056: वदन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = वदान्य below.
41057: वदमान, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking, saying, telling; calling; explaining, declaring; glorifying, boasting.

41059: वदावद, अस्, आ, अम्, or वदावदिन्, ई, इनी, इ (probably an old Intens., cf. 2. महामह), speak-ing much, talkative, chattering, speaking, a speaker; able to speak well, eloquent.
41060: वदितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be said or spoken.
41061: वदितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, saying, speaking, a speaker.
41062: वदिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. speaking very well, speaking best.
41063: वद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be spoken &c., (used only in comp., cf. अ-वद्य, अन्-अवद्य); an epithet of the days of the dark lunar fortnight, (see वद्य-पक्ष); (अम्), n. speech, speaking about, con-versing, (only at the end of a comp., cf. ब्रह्म-व्°, सत्य-व्°।) —वद्य-पक्ष, अस्, m. the dark fort-night of the lunar month (in which the moon is waning).
41065: वदरिक, अस्, m. a jujube tree.
41066: वदाम वदाम, अस्, m. (fr. the Persian بادام), an almond.
41067: वदाल वदाल, अस्, m. a kind of Silurus or sheat-fish; an eddy or whirlpool.
41068: वदालक, अस्, m. = वदाल, a kind of sheat-fish.
41069: वदि वदि, ind. (according to some for ब-दि, contracted fr. बहुल-दिन, but cf. वद्य), in the dark half of any month, (affixed to the names of months in giving dates at the end of MSS.; cf. वैशाख-व्°।)
41070: वद्दिवास वद्दिवास, N. of a place.
41071: वद्ध्री वद्ध्री। See under वध्र, p. 883.
41072: वध् वध् (a defective rt. frequently written बध्, see 3. बध्, properly only used in the Aorist and Precative tenses, the other tenses being supplied fr. rt. हन्, q. v.), Aor. P. A. अव-धीत्, अवधिष्ट, (मा वधिष्ठाः, do not kill); Prec. 1st sing. वध्यासम्, 3rd sing. वध्यात्, (in the Veda the Potential also occurs, e. g. 1st sing. वधेयम्, 3rd sing. वधेत्; in epic poetry the 2nd Fut. 41387: वर्चस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, bestowing vital power or vigour (Ved.); relating to वर्चस्; acting on the excrement; (आ), f., scil. इष्टका, a term applied to certain sacrificial bricks (at the laying of which a par-ticular Mantra containing the word वर्चस् is used).

41390: वर्चटी वर्चटी (?) , f. a kind of rice; a harlot.
41392: वर्ण् वर्ण् (more properly regarded as a Nom. fr. वर्ण below), cl. 10. P. वर्-णयति (according to some also A. —ते), वर्णयाम्-आस, अववर्णत्, -त, वर्णयितुम् (anom. Inf. वर्णितुम्), to paint, colour, dye; to depict, deli-neate, picture, write, describe, enumerate, relate, tell, explain, illustrate; to praise, extol; to illumi-nate; to spread, extend; to exert one's self; to send, cast (or to grind, pound): Pass. वर्ण्यते, Aor. अवर्णि, to be coloured; to be described; to be praised, &c.
41393: वर्ण, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 10. fr. rt. वृ), a covering, cloak, mantle; a cover, covering, lid; outward appearance, exterior, form, figure; colour, hue, tint, dye, paint; lustre, beauty; a coloured cloth thrown over an elephant, housings; staining or anointing the body with coloured un-guents; dress, embellishment; gold; the purity of gold as ascertained by its streak; sort, kind, species, class, race, tribe; class of men, order, caste (as being originally perhaps connected with colour or com-plexion; but the word वर्ण is more properly applicable to the four principal classes described in Manu's code, viz. Brāhmans, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras, and not to the numerous mixed castes of later times; the more modern word for ‘caste’ is जाति); a letter, sound, vowel, syllable, word, (in these and some of the preceding senses said to be also अम्, n.); quality, property; a musical mode; a particular time in music, the order or arrangement of a song, &c.; praise, commendation, renown, fame, glory, celebrity; (in algebra) an unknown magnitude or quantity; (in arithmetic) the figure one, (according to some) a coefficient; a religious observance; (अम्), n. coloured unguent or perfume; saffron; (आ), f. a kind of plant or leguminous shrub, Cajanus Indicus; [cf. Slav. vran, ‘black;] a raven:’ Russ. voronj, ‘the azure colour of swords;’ vornoi, ‘black;’ voron, ‘a raven:’ Lith. warnas, ‘a raven.’] —वर्ण-कवि, इस्, m., N. of a son of Kuvera. —वर्ण-कूपिका, f. any vessel containing colour or paint, an ink-bottle, ink-stand. —वर्ण-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, causing or giving colour. —वर्ण-क्रम, अस्, m. order or succession of colours; order of castes; order or series of letters, alphabetical arrangement, the alphabet; (एण), ind. according to the order of the castes —वर्ण-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘gone to colour,’ coloured, described; algebraical. —वर्ण-चारक, अस्, m. a painter, colourer. —वर्ण-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced from castes, relating to castes. —वर्ण-ज्येष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, highest in caste; (अस्), m. a Brāhman. —वर्ण-तनु, उस्, f., N. of a particular Mantra addressed to Sarasvatī. —वर्ण-तस्, ind. by or with colour &c. —वर्ण-ता, f. or वर्ण-त्व, अम्, n. the state of colour, colour, (अन्य-वर्ण-त्व, the being of another colour); the state or condition of caste, division into classes; the state or condition of a letter or sound. —वर्ण-ताल, अस्, m., N. of a king. —वर्ण-तूलि, इस्, or वर्ण-तूलिका or वर्ण-तूली, f. ‘letter-brush,’ a pen, pencil, paint-brush. —वर्ण-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving colour, colouring, dyeing; giving tribe, &c.; (अम्), n. a kind of fragrant yellow wood. —वर्ण-दातृ, ता, m. a granter or bestower of colour, &c.; (त्री), f. turmeric. —वर्ण-दूत, अस्, m. ‘a letter as a mes-senger,’ a letter, epistle. —वर्ण-दूषक, अस्, इका, अम्, violating or disturbing the distinctions of caste. —वर्ण-देशना, f. ‘instruction in sounds,’ N. of a lexicon. —वर्ण-द्वय-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consist-ing of two syllables. —वर्ण-धर्म, अस्, m. the particular duty or occupation of each caste or tribe. —वर्ण-पात, अस्, m. the dropping or omission of a letter in pronunciation. —वर्ण-पात्र, अम्, n. a vessel or receptacle for colours, paint-box, (according to some this word should be वर्ण-पत्त्र, a leaf on which a painter mixes his colours, a pallet.) —वर्ण-पुष्प, अम्, n. the blossom of the globe-amaranth; (ई), f. a kind of plant (= उष्ट्र-काण्डी)। —वर्ण-पुष्पक, अस्, m. globe-amaranth. —वर्-ण-प्रकर्ष, अस्, m. excellence or beauty of colour. —वर्ण-प्रबोध, अस्, m., N. of a work. —वर्ण-प्रसादन, अम्, n. aloe wood, Agallo-chum. —वर्ण-भेदिनी, f. a kind of plant (?). —वर्ण-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of colours; consisting of letters or sounds. —वर्ण-मातृ, ता, f. ‘letter-mother,’ a pen, pencil, &c. —वर्ण-मा-तृका, f., N. of Sarasvatī. —वर्ण-मात्रा, f. a kind of metre. —वर्ण-माला, f. order or series of letters, (especially) rows of letters (written on a board or in a diagram), the alphabet. —वर्ण-राशि, इस्, m. ‘mul-titude or series of letters,’ the alphabet. —वर्ण-रेखा or वर्ण-लेखा or वर्ण-लेखिका, f. chalk or a white substance often confounded with chalk. —वर्ण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having colour, &c.; (अती), f. turmeric. —वर्ण-वर्ति, इस्, or वर्ण-वर्तिका, f. a writing-pen, pencil, &c. —वर्ण-वादिन्, ई, m. a speaker of praise, panegyrist. —वर्ण-विपर्यय, अस्, m. the change or substitution of one letter for another. —वर्ण-विलासिनी, f. turmeric. —वर्ण-विलोडक, अस्, m. a plagiarist; a house-breaker. —वर्ण-विवेक, अस्, m. ‘distinction of words,’ N. of a dictionary. —वर्ण-वृत्त, अम्, n. metre regulated by the number of syllables, (this term applies to a common class of metres, such as the Śloka or Anuṣṭubh, the Indra-vajrā, &c., which are regulated by the number of syllables in the half-line; cf. मात्रा-वृत्त।) —वर्ण-व्यवस्थिति, इस्, f. ‘caste-system,’ insti-tution of caste. —वर्ण-शिक्षा, f. instruction in sounds or letters. —वर्ण-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, be-longing to the best of the tribes; (अस्), m. a Brāhman or member of the highest caste. —वर्ण-संयोग, अस्, m. ‘union of tribe or caste,’ matrimonial con-nection or marriage between persons of the same caste. —वर्ण-संसर्ग, अस्, m. mixture or con-fusion of castes, matrimonial connection or marriage with members of other castes. —वर्ण-संहार, अस्, m. an assemblage or mixture of different castes, an assembly in which all the four tribes are repre-sented. —वर्ण-सङ्कर, अस्, m. mixture or blend-ing of colours; mixture or confusion of castes through intermarriage with different castes; a tribe of different origin, a man descended from a father and mother of different castes. —वर्ण-सङ्करिक, अस्, आ, अम्, one who causes a mixture of castes by marrying a member of a different caste. —वर्ण-सङ्घाट or वर्ण-सङ्घात or वर्ण-समाम्नाय, अस्, m. an assemblage or aggregate of letters, the alphabet. —वर्ण-स्थान, अम्, n. the place or organ of utterance of any sound or letter, (of these there are eight, such as ‘the throat’ &c., see under स्थान।) —वर्ण-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of caste, out-cast. —वर्णागम (°ण-आग्°), अस्, m. the addition of a letter to a word. —वर्णाङ्का (°ण-अङ्°), f. ‘letter-marker,’ a pen. —वर्णात्मन् (°ण-आत्°), आ, m. ‘consisting of sounds or letters,’ a word. —वर्-णाधिप (°ण-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘caste-presider,’ a planet presiding over a class or caste. —वर्णान्य-त्व (°ण-अन्°), अम्, n. change of complexion. —वर्-णापसद (°ण-अप्°), अस्, m. one who goes out from caste, excluded from caste, an outcast. —वर्-णापेत (°ण-अप्°), अस्, m. destitute of caste, born in a mixed caste, outcast, degraded. —वर्णार्ह (°ण-अर्°), अस्, m. a sort of bean, Phaseolus Mungo. —वर्णाश्रम (°ण-आश्°), अम्, n. caste and order, class and stage of life, (see आश्रम.) —वर्णा-श्रम-धर्म, अस्, m. the duties of caste and order. —वर्णाश्रम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, or वर्णा-श्रमिन्, ई, इनी, इ, possessed of caste and order. —वर्-णी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become or be changed into an articulate sound. —वर्णेश्वरी (°ण-ईश्°), f., N. of a goddess. —वर्णोदक (°ण-उद्°), अम्, n. coloured water. —वर्णोपेत (°ण-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having tribe or caste.

41523: वर्हिस् वर्हिस्, इस्, m. n. (in the earlier lan-guage generally written बर्हिस्, q. v.), Kuśa grass, &c., (according to some only n., see बर्हिस्); sacri-fice, oblation, (according to some only m.); (इस्), m. fire, light, lustre, splendor; (इस्), n. a kind of vegetable perfume (= ग्रन्थि-पर्ण, commonly called Ganthiāla). —वर्हिः-पुष्प, &c., see बर्-हिः-पुष्प, &c., under बर्हिस्, p. 675, col. 1.

41525: वल, अस्, m., Ved. a cloud (according to Naigh. I. 10); N. of an Asura (fabled to have stolen the cows of the gods and to have concealed them in a cave; Indra surrounded the cave with his army and recovered the cattle; in Ṛg-veda X. 68, 9, he is said to have assumed the form of a bull and to have been destroyed by Bṛhas-pati; elsewhere he is identified with a cloud); (अम्), n. strength, force; an army, &c. (see बल). —वलं-रुज, अस्, m., Ved. one who breaks the clouds.
41526: वलग (?) , a kind of magical Mantra.

41528: वलभि, इस्, m. or वलभी, f. (also written व-डभि), the wooden frame of a thatch, a roof; a turret or temporary building on the roof of a house; = वल्लभी. —वलभि-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town.

41530: वलयित, अस्, आ, अम्, encircled, surrounded, encom-passed, enclosed; whirling round.
41532: वलाक, अस्, m. (also written बलाक, q. v.), a crane; (आ), f. a female crane; a crane in general; a flight of cranes; a mistress or loved woman; (आ, ई), f. a small kind of crane.
41533: वलाकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having or attended by cranes.
41534: वलि, इस्, m. (usually written बलि, q. v.), tax, tribute, offering, oblation, &c. 41535: वलिक, अस्, अम्, m. n. the edge of a thatched roof.

41538: वली, f. See under वलि above.
41539: वलीक, अम्, n. the edge of a thatched roof.
41540: वलूक, अम्, n. the root of a lotus; (अस्), m. a bird.
41541: वलूल, अस्, आ, अम्, = बलूल, strong, powerful.

41544: वल्कलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, dressed in bark, clothed in a bark dress.
41547: वलकेश्वरतीर्थ वलकेश्वर-तीर्थ (°क-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
41548: वलक्ष वलक्ष, अस्, ई, अम्, white; (अस्), m. white, the colour; [cf. पलक्ष, बलक्ष, अव-लक्ष।] —वलक्ष-गु, उस्, m. ‘having white rays of light, ‘the moon.
41549: वलग्न व-लग्न, अस्, अम्, m. n. = अव-लग्न, the waist, middle.
41550: वलन्तिका वलन्तिका, f. a particular air or mode in music.
41551: वलम्ब व-लम्ब, अस्, m. = अव-लम्ब, a perpendicular.
41552: वलम्भ वलम्भ, N. of a country.
41553: वलासक वलासक, अस्, m. (perhaps for अव-लासक), the Koïl or Indian cuckoo; a frog.
41554: वलाहक वलाहक, अस्, m. a cloud, thunder-cloud; N. of one of the seven clouds at the destruc-tion of the world; a mountain; a kind of crane (= वलाक); N. of a Daitya; of a brother of Jayad-ratha; one of the Nāgas; one of the four horses of Viṣṇu.
41555: वलिर वलिर, अस्, आ, अम्, squint-eyed, squinting.
41556: वलिश वलिश, अम्, ई, n. f. or वलिशि, इस्, f. a fish-hook; [cf. वडिश।]
41557: वलिशान वलिशान, अस्, m., Ved. a cloud (Naigh. I. 10).
41558: वल्क् वल्क्, cl. 10. P. वल्कयति, -यितुम्, to speak.
41560: वल्ग् वल्ग्, cl. 1. P. वल्गति, ववल्ग, वल्गितुम्, to go, move; to go by leaps, jump, bounce; to gallop; to move in different ways; to fluctuate; [cf. perhaps Angl. Sax. wlœnce; Engl. walk.]
41561: वल्गत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, going, jumping.

41563: वल्गा, f. a bridle, rein. —वल्गाङ्क (°गा-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, holding a bridle.

41566: वल्गुक, अस्, आ, अम्, handsome, beautiful; (अम्), n. sandal; a wood; price.
41567: वल्गुल, अस्, m. the flying fox; (आ), f. a species of bird.
41569: वल्गूय, Nom. P. वल्गूयति, -यितुम्, to be beautiful or handsome; to be mild or gentle; to honour, praise, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda IV. 50, 70 = स्तौति).
41570: वल्गूयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming handsome or beautiful; honouring.
41571: वल्भ् वल्भ्, cl. 1. A. वल्भते, ववल्भे, वल्भितुम्, to eat, devour.
41572: वल्भन, अम्, n. the act of eating; food.
41573: वल्भित, अस्, आ, अम्, eaten, devoured.
41574: वल्मी वल्मी, f. an ant; [cf. वम्री; per-haps for वर्मी।] —वल्मी-कूट, अम्, n. an ant-hill, hillock.
41575: वल्मिक, अस्, m. for वल्मीक, an ant-hill, &c.; see below.
41576: वल्मिकि, इस्, इ, m. n. an ant-hill, &c.; see below.
41577: वल्मीक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (in Uṇādi-s. 41578: वल्युल् वल्युल् or वल्यूल् [cf. पल्युल्], cl. 10. P. वल्यूलयति, -यितुम्, to cut, cut off; to purify.
41579: वल्ल् वल्ल् [cf. rt. वल्], cl. 1. A. वल्लते, ववल्ले, वल्लितुम्, to be covered; to go, move.
41580: वल्ल, अस्, m. covering; winnowing corn; a Māṣa of silver; a weight of three Raktikās or Ratīs; prohibiting, prohibition.
41581: वल्लकी, f. the Vīṇā or Indian lute.
41582: वल्लभ, अस्, आ, अम् (in Uṇādi-s. III. 125. said to be fr. rt. वल्ल्), beloved, desired, dear; supreme, superintending, superintendent; (अस्), m. a lover, husband, friend, favourite, (काम-वल्लभ, the cinnamon tree); a superintendent, overseer; a chief herdsman; a horse (especially one with good marks); N. of a grammarian; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a beloved female, wife, mistress; (ई), f., N. of a city in Gujarāt, the capital of a line of kings. —वल्लभ-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, most beloved, dear-est. —वल्लभ-ता, f. or वल्लभ-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being loved or a favourite, love. —वल्लभ-देव, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —वल्लभ-पालक, अस्, m. a horse-keeper, groom. —वल्लभाचार्य (°भ-आच्°), अस्, m., N. of a great teacher of the Vaiṣṇava sect, (he was a successor of a less celebrated teacher named Viṣṇu-svāmin, and his followers are some-times called Vallabhācāryas, sometimes Rudra-sam-pradāyins; he was born, it is said, in the forest of Campāraṇya in 1479; at an early age he commenced travelling to propagate his doctrines, and at the court of Kṛṣṇa-deva, king of Vijaya-nagara, succeeded so well in his controversies with the Śaivas that the Vaiṣṇavas chose him as their chief; he then went to other parts of India, and finally settled down at Benares, where he composed seventeen works, the most important of which were a commentary on the Vedānta and Mīmāṃsā Sūtras and another on the Bhā-gavata-Purāṇa, which last, as inculcating the worship of Kṛṣṇa, is the chief religious work on which this sect rest their doctrines; he left behind eighty-four disciples, of each of whom some history or story is told, which stories are often repeated to large audiences on festive or solemn occasions; the Tilaka mark on the forehead of the Vallabhācāryas is described as consisting of two perpendicular lines meeting in a semicircle at the root of the nose and having a round spot of red between them.) —वल्लभाष्टक-वि-वृति (°भ-अष्°), इस्, f., N. of a work.
41583: वल्लभायित, अम्, n. a kind of coitus; [cf. पु-रुषायित।]
41584: वल्लर, अम्, n. Agallochum or aloe wood (the black variety).
41585: वल्लरि, इस्, or वल्लरी, f. a branching foot-stalk, compound pedicle; a creeping or twining plant.
41586: वल्लव, अस्, m. a herdsman [cf. गो-व्°]; a name of Bhīma-sena; a cook; (ई), f. a cowherdess.
41587: वल्लि, इस्, or वल्ली, f. a creeper, any climbing or creeping plant; (इस्), f. the earth; (ई), f. a plant, Ligusticum Ajwæn; N. of an Upaniṣad. —वल्लि-कण्टकारिका, f. the plant Solanum Jacquini. —वल्लि-दूर्वा, f. a kind of grass. —वल्लि-शाकट-पोतिका, f. = मूल-पोती. —वल्लि-सूरण, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= अत्यम्ल-पर्णी). —वल्ली-गड, अस्, m. a kind of fish (commonly called भोला or बालिकडा). —वल्ली-ज, अम्, n. ‘creeper-grown,’ pepper. —वल्ली-मुद्ग, अस्, m. a kind of kidney-bean. —वल्ली-वदरी, f. a kind of plant (= भू-वदरी). —वल्ली-वृक्ष, अस्, m. the Śāl tree, Shorea Robusta; [cf. शाल, साल।]

41591: वल्व वल्व। See बल्व, p. 677, col. 1.
41592: वल्वज वल्वज, अस्, m. (also written बल्-बज, q. v.), a sort of coarse grass, Eleusine Indica; (आ), f. a kind of grass (called in Hindī सावे वागे and, according to some, a different species from वल्वज, its synonyms are तृण-वल्वजा, तृणेक्षु दृढ-क्षुरा, दृढ-तृणा, दृढ-पत्त्री, पा-नीयाश्रा, मौञ्जी-पत्त्रा).
41593: वल्श वल्श, अस्, m. (or अम्, n.?), Ved. a branch; [cf. सहस्र-व्°।]
41594: वल्ह् वल्ह् (also written बल्ह्; cf. rt. वर्ह्), cl. 1. A. वल्हते, &c., to be good or excellent, be pre-eminent; to speak; to kill, hurt; to give or to cover; cl. 10. P. वल्हयति, &c., to speak, tell; to shine.
41595: वल्हिक वल्हिक, वल्हीक, = बल्हिक, बल्-हीक, q. q. v. v.

41649: वसिष्ठ, अस्, m. (superl. of वसु or वसु-मत्; cf. वसीयस्), ‘the most wealthy,’ N. of a very celebrated Vedic Ṛṣi or inspired sage (owner of the ‘cow of plenty,’ called Nandinī, offspring of Surabhi, which by granting all desires made him, as his name implies, master of every वसु or desirable object; he was the typical representative of Brāh-manical dignity, and the legends of his conflict with Viśvā-mitra, who raised himself from the military to the sacerdotal class, though probably founded on the actual struggles which took place between the Brāhmans and Kṣatriyas, were doubtless mostly in-vented to impress the mind with the power and superiority of the priesthood; a great many hymns of the Ṛg-veda are ascribed to these two great rivals, those of the seventh Maṇḍala, besides some others, being attributed to Vasiṣṭha, while those of the third Maṇḍala are assigned to Viśvā-mitra; in one of Vasiṣṭha's hymns he is represented as king Su-dās's family priest, an office to which Viśvā-mitra also aspired; in another hymn Vasiṣṭha claims to have been inspired by Varuṇa, and in another [Ṛg-veda VII. 33, 11] he is called the son of the Apsaras Urvaśī by Mitra and Varuṇa, whence his patronymic Maitrāvaruṇi; in Manu I. 35. he is enumerated among the ten Prajā-patis or Patriarchs produced by Manu Svāyambhuva for the peopling of the universe; in the Mahā-bhārata he is mentioned as the family priest of the solar race or family of Ikṣvāku and Rāma-candra, and in the Purāṇas as one of the arrangers of the Vedas in the Dvāpara age; in the first and second chapters of the Raghu-vaṃśa he is described as releasing king Dilīpa from his curse of childlessness by directing him to attend upon the cow Nandinī in atonement for an offence he had uninten-tionally committed against the parent cow Surabhi; according to one account Vasiṣṭha married Ūrjā, ‘Strength;’ according to another, Arundhatī, one of the Pleiades, by whom he had seven sons [see अरुन्धती]; other legends make him one of the seven great patriarchal sages regarded as forming the stars of the Great Bear [see ऋषि]; his name is often written Vaśiṣṭha, q. v., in which case it must be connected with वश and वशिन्); N. of the author of a law-book (perhaps intended to be ascribed to the Vedic Ṛṣi above); (आस्), m. pl. the family of Vasiṣṭha; (वसिष्ठस्याङ्कुश and वसिष्ठस्या-नुपदम्, N. of two Sāmans.) —वसिष्ठ-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work. —वसिष्ठ-पुत्र, आस्, m. pl. ‘the sons or descendants of Vasiṣṭha,’ N. of the authors of Ṛg-veda VII. 33, 10-14. —व-सिष्ठ-प्रमुख, अस्, आ, अम्, preceded or led by Vasiṣṭha. —वसिष्ठ-प्राची, f., N. of a place. —वसिष्ठ-भृग्व्-अत्रि-सम, अस्, आ, अम्, equal to (the three great saints) Vasiṣṭha, Bhṛgu, and Atri (all three being reckoned among the nine Prajā-patis, Manu I. 35). —वसिष्ठ-संहिता, f., N. of a philosophical treatise; 41717: वा 1. वा, ind. (excluded, like the Lat. ve, from the first place in a sentence, and generally com-ing immediately after the word to which it refers), as, like, so (not commonly used in this sense); either, or, whether; either — or not, i. e. optionally, (in grammar the word वा is placed after a rule to denote its being optional); else; or if, but if; but; only, no other; indeed, truly, even, very (in as-severation or confirmation); and (as a conjunction); वा is also sometimes used as an expletive; it is also somewhat pleonastically or perhaps emphatically added to an interrogative pronoun especially when followed by the negative न (e. g. को वा न, के वा न, which may be translated by ‘very on,’ ‘all’); वा — वा, either — or; on the one side — on the other; अथ वा, or else; or, or if, or rather, but, certainly, see अथ; न वा, or not; यदि वा, or if, or whether, whether, whether or no, see under यदि, p. 808; यद् वा, or, or else; किं वा, whether? किं वा — न वा, is it — or not? see under किम्; [cf. Gr. ἤ; Lat. ve.]
