P. -भवति, &c., to become cool. —शिशिरो-ष्ण-वर्ष (°र-उष्°), आस्, f. pl. the dewy, hot, and rainy seasons.
46758: शिशु शिशु, उस्, m. (a reduplicated form of 1. शु for rt. श्वि; according to Uṇādi-s. I. 21. fr. rt. शो; Ved. शिश्वः = शिशवः, शिश्वा = शिशुना), a child, infant; the young of any animal (as a calf, puppy, &c.); a boy under eight years of age; a lad under sixteen; a pupil, scholar; N. of a descendant of Aṅgiras (author of Ṛg-veda IX. 112). —शिशु-काल, अस्, m. childhood. —शिशु-क्रन्द, अस्, m. or शिशु-क्रन्दन, अम्, n. the weeping of a child or infant. —शिशु-क्रन्दीय, अस्, m., scil. ग्रन्थ, a book treating of infantile complaints or (perhaps) a book suitable for naughty children, (Pān. IV. 3, 88.) —शिशु-गन्धा, f. double jasmine. —शिशु-चान्द्रा-यण, अम्, n. the lunar penance of children, (eating four mouthfuls at sunrise and four mouthfuls at sun-set for a month, Manu XI. 219.) —शिशु-त्व, अम्, n. or शिशु-ता, f. childhood, boyhood, the period up to eight years of age; pupilage, the period before sixteen. —शिशु-देश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the place of a child, not far from or almost a child. —शिशु-नाग, अस्, m. a young elephant; a kind of Rākṣasa or demon; N. of a king of Magadhā (the founder of a dynasty). —शिशु-पाल, अस्, m. ‘child-cherisher,’ N. of the king of the Cedis inhabiting a country in central India, probably the same as Bun-delkhand, (see चेदि; he was son of Dama-ghoṣa, and is also called Su-nītha; his impiety in opposing the worship of Kṛṣṇa is described in the Sabhā-parvan of the Mahā-bhārata; when Yudhi-ṣṭhira was about to perform a Rājasūya sacrifice, numerous princes attended, and Bhīṣma proposed that especial honour should be paid to Kṛṣṇa, who was also present, but Śiśu-pāla objected, and after denouncing Kṛṣṇa as a contemptible person challenged him to fight, whereupon Kṛṣṇa struck off his head with his discus; the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa identifies this impious monarch with the demons Hiraṇya-kaśipu and Rā-vaṇa; his death forms the subject of Māgha's cele-brated poem called Śiśupāla-vadha.) —शिशुपालक, अस्, इका, अम्, protecting or cherishing children; (अस्), m., N. of a king (= शिशु-पाल); the plant Nauclea Cordifolia. —शिशुपाल-बध or शिशुपाल-वध, अस्, m. ‘the slaying of Śiśu-pāla,’ N. of a part of the Mahā-bhārata (see below) and of an epic poem by Māgha on the subject of Śiśu-pāla's death by the hand of Kṛṣṇa. —शिशुपाल-बध-पर्वन्, अ, n., N. of a section of the Mahā-bhārata (contained in the Sabhā-parvan 1418 — 1627, see above). —शि-शुपाल-हन्, आ, m. ‘destroyer of Śiśu-pāla,’ an epi-thet of Kṛṣṇa. —शिशु-भाव, अस्, m. the state of childhood, infancy. —शिशु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. infantine, childish, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 140, 10. शिशुमतीर् = शैशववतीर् ज्वालाः।) —शिशु-मार, अस्, m. ‘child-killing,’ the Gangetic porpoise, Delphinus Gangeticus; ‘the heavenly por-poise,’ a form of Viṣṇu (described as a collection of the stars and planets); N. or a form of Viṣṇu. —शिशुमार-शिरस्, अस्, n. the dolphin's head, a part of the heavens studded with stars, the north-east point. —शिशु-वाहक or शिशु-वाह्यक, अस्, m. ‘child-carrier,’ a wild goat. —शिशु-हत्या, f. child-murder.
46759: शिशुक, अस्, m. a child; the young of any animal; a porpoise; a fish resembling a porpoise; a tree.
46760: शिशूल, अस्, m., Ved. a child or a young animal, (Sāy. = शिशु।)
46761: शिश्वन् in सं-शिश्वन्, q. v.; (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 65, 5. शिश्वा may either = तनू-कृतः, ‘attenuated,’ as if fr. rt. शो, or = शिशुना, inst. c. of शिशु।)
46762: शिश्वायै in Ṛg-veda X. 95, 13 = शिवे, i. e. कल्-याणे समुपस्थिते सति (according to Sāy.).
46763: शिश्वि, इस्, इस्, इ, swelling, increasing, thriving, &c., in सु-शिश्वि, q. v.
46764: शिश्न शिश्न, अस्, m. (according to Yāska fr. rt. श्नथ्; according to others fr. rt. शश्), the male generative organ, (also अम्, n. in Ved.); (अम्), n., Ved. a tail; thread steeped in rice-water, (said by Sāy. to be fr. rt. स्ना, Ṛg-veda I. 105, 8.) —शिश्न-देव, अस्, m. ‘having the generative organ for a god’ or ‘sporting with that organ,’ a lustful or unchaste man, (Sāy. शिश्नेन दीव्यन्ति क्रीडन्ति इति शिश्न-देवाः अब्रह्मचर्याः इत्य् अर्थः); a tailed or priapic demon. —शिश्नोदर-परायण (°न-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, addicted to lust and gluttony.
46765: शिश्रियाण शिश्रियाण, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्रि), Ved. seeking refuge, taking refuge.
46766: शिश्विदान शिश्विदान, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 93. fr. rt. श्वित्, ‘to be white,’ with substitution of द् for त् and elision of the desiderative affix स्), ‘being pure,’ innocent, virtuous (= शुक्ल-कर्मन्); guilty, sinful, wicked (= कृष्ण-कर्-मन् according to some).
46767: शिष् 1. शिष्, cl. 1. P. शेषति, शिशेष, शेक्ष्यति, अशिक्षत्, शेष्टुम्, to hurt, injure, kill.
46768: शिष् 2. शिष्, cl. 7. P. शिनष्टि, शिशेष, शेक्ष्यति, अशिषत्, शेष्टुम्, to leave, leave remaining; to distinguish from others, indi-vidualize; (according to some also) cl. 1. P. शेषति, &c., to leave a residue, allow to remain, spare: Pass. शिष्यते, (for शिष्यते, Pass. of rt. 1. शास्, see p. 1003), to be left remaining, remain; Caus. (or cl. 10) शेषयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशीशिषत्, to cause to remain, leave, allow to remain, spare: Desid. शि-क्षति: Intens. शेशिष्यते, शेशेष्टि; [cf. Lat. quœso, quœro, quœstor, perhaps cura; Goth. qvis-teins, qvistjan, fra-qvisteins, fra-qvistjan, fra-qvistnan, us-qvistjan (based on a noun qvist = शिष्टि, in the sense of ‘leaving, abandoning’), us-haista.]
46769: 1. शिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, left, remaining, residual, anything that remains or is left. —१। शिष्ट-ता, f. or शिष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. the being left, the being residual.
46770: शिष्ट 2. शिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. शास्), ordered, commanded; disciplined, well regulated, educated, trained; tamed, obedient, docile; orderly, correct, learned, wise, good; select, (perhaps refer-rible to 1. शिष्ट); eminent, excellent, superior, prin-cipal, chief; (अस्), m. a chief; a courtier, counsellor.  — 2. शिष्ट-ता, f. or शिष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. docility; good behaviour, urbanity, civility. —शिष्ट-सभा, f. an assembly of chiefs, council of state. —शिष्ट-सभाचार (°भा-आच्°), अस्, m. history or tradition of eminent persons. —शिष्ट-सम्मत, अस्, आ, अम्, approved or loved by the learned, (Manu III. 39.) —शिष्टाचरण (°ट-आच्°), अम्, n. the conduct or procedure of the virtuous, practice of the good, gen-tlemanly behaviour. —शिष्टाचार (°ट-आच्°), अस्, m. the practice or traditional usages of the virtuous; (अस्, आ, अम्), well-behaved; the approved conduct of the wise and good, good manners, gentlemanly conduct, proper behaviour. —शिष्टाचार-विरुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, opposed to the practice of the virtuous. —शिष्टा-चाराविरुद्ध (°र-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, not opposed to the practice of the virtuous.
46771: शिष्टि, इस्, f. ruling, governing, commanding; an order, command; correction, punishment, chastise-ment.
46772: शिष्ट्वा, ind. having governed or regulated or trained; having ordered or decreed.
46773: शिष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be taught, docile [cf. अ-श्°]; (अस्), m. a scholar, pupil, disciple, (कु-शिष्य, a bad or wicked pupil); passion, anger; violence. —शिष्य-ता, f. or शिष्य-त्व, अम्, n. the state or character of a pupil, pupilage, instruction. —शिष्य-परम्-परा, f. a series or succession of pupils or disciples. —शिष्य-पुत्र, अस्, m. a pupil equal to a son. —शिष्य-प्रदेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be delivered or imparted to pupils. —शिष्य-शिष्टि, इस्, f. chastise-ment or correction of a pupil.
46774: शिष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being ruled or controlled; being instructed or trained.
46775: शिह्ल शिह्ल or शिह्लक, अस्, m. (also written सिह्ल, q. v.), olibanum, benzoin, Indian incense (= शिला-रस).
46776: शिह्लन, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Śānti-śataka, (sometimes written शिल्हन।)
46777: शी 1. शी (perhaps connected with rt. शद्), cl. 2. A. शेते (1st du. शेवहे, 3rd du. शयाते, 1st pl. शेमहे, 3rd pl. शेरते, Ved. cl. 1. शयते, but शये = शेते, Ṛg-veda III. 55, 4, cf. Pāṇ. VII. 1, 41; Ved. and ep. also P. in some tenses), Impf. अशेत (P. अशयत्, Ved. 2nd du. P. अशायतम्, 3rd du. A. अशयाताम्, 3rd pl. अशेरत), Pot. श-यीत (ep. शयेत्), Impv. शेताम् (2nd sing. शेष्व, 1st du. शयावहै, 3rd pl. शेरताम्), शिश्ये, श-यिष्यते (ep. शेष्यति), अशयिष्ट, शयितुम् (Ved. Inf. शयध्यै), to lie, lie down, lie on the ground, recline; to rest, repose; to sleep: Pass. शय्यते, Aor. अशायि: Caus. शाययति, -यितुम्, to cause to lie down, put down, throw down; to throw, put; to allow to rest: Desid. शिशयिषते: Intens. शा-शय्यते, शेशयीति, शेशेति; [cf. Gr. κεῖ-μαι (κεῖσαι = शेषे, κεῖται = शेते); κοί-τη, κοι-μά-ω, κῶ-μο-ς, κῶμα, κώ-μη: Lat. qui-e-s, qui-e-sc-o, civi-s: Goth. hai-m-s, he-thyô, haithi, heiwa, ‘house,’ in comp. heiva-franja: Old Island. hei-mr, ‘house:’ Old Germ. haim, heim, hī-wī, hi-wo, ‘husband;’ hiwa, ‘wife;’ hijan, hiwjan, ‘to marry;’ hīrāt: Mod. Germ. Heirath: Angl. Sax. ham, hœman: Lith. sze†tra, ‘a tent;’ kie†ma, ‘a village.’]
46780: शिश्यान, अस्, आ, अम्, lying, reclining.
46781: 2. शी, ईस्, f. sleep, repose; tranquillity, devotion, complete absorption in religious worship.
46782: शीक् शीक् (also written सीक्, and per-haps connected with rt. 1. सिच्), cl. 1. A. शीकते, शिशीके, शीकिष्यते, अशीकिष्ट, शीकितुम्, to sprinkle, wet, moisten; to go gently, move; cl. 1. 10. P. शिकति, शीकयति, to bear ill or impatiently, be angry; to bear patiently, be patient; to touch (= rt. चीक्); to speak (cl. 10); to shine (cl. 10).
46783: शीकर, अस्, m. thin or drizzling rain, drizzle, spray, mist, rain driven by wind; a drop of rain or water, (also written सीकर); (अम्), n. the resin of the Sarala pine or the tree itself. —शीकरौघ (°र-ओघ), अस्, आ, अम्, abounding with mist, having much spray or thin rain.
46784: शिकरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, sprinkling, drizzling.
46785: शीघ्र शीघ्र, अस्, आ, अम् (etymology doubt-ful), quick, speedy; (अस्), m. (in astronomy) con-junction; (according to others) parallax; N. of a king; (आ), f., N. of a river; a particular plant, = दन्ती; (अम्), ind. quickly, rapidly, swiftly; [cf. Gr. κιχάνω; Angl. Sax. higian.] —शिघ्र-कर्मन्, अ, n. (in astronomy) the calculation of the conjunc-tion (of a planet). —शिघ्र-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, acting speedily or expeditiously. —शिघ्र-कृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be done quickly, what must be done quickly. —शिघ्र-केन्द्र, अम्, n. (in astronomy) the dis-tance from the conjunction (of a planet), commuta-tion. —शिघ्र-कोपिन्, ई, इनी, इ, quickly angry, irri-table. —शीघ्र-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going quickly; (अस्), m., N. of a king. —शिघ्र-गन्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or शीघ्र-गमन, अस्, आ, अम्, going quickly. —शी-घ्र-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going or moving quickly, swift, expeditious. —शीघ्र-चेतन, अस्, आ, अम्, having quick intellect, very sagacious; (अस्), m. a dog. —शीघ्र-जन्मन्, आ, m. ‘having quick birth,’ the plant Cæsalpinia Bonducella; another plant (= करञ्ज). —शीघ्र-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more quick, very swift; (अम्), ind. as swiftly as possible. —शी-घ्र-ता, f. or शीघ्र-त्व, अम्, n. quickness, speed, rapidity. —शीघ्र-परिधि, इस्, m. (in astronomy) the epicycle of a conjunction. —शीघ्र-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘quick-flowering,’ a kind of plant (= अगस्त्य)। —शीघ्र-फल, अम्, n. (in astronomy) the equation of a conjunction. —शीघ्र-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, quick-witted, having quick apprehension, acute, sharp. —शी-घ्र-यान, अम्, n. rapid motion. —शिघ्र-लङ्-घन, अस्, आ, अम्, springing or jumping quickly, moving rapidly. —शिघ्र-वेग, अस्, आ, अम्, having a rapid course, impetuous. —शीघ्र-वेधिन्, ई, m. ‘quickly piercing (the mark),’ a good archer. —शी-घ्र-श्रोतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, having a rapid current (said of a river) —शीघ्रोच्च (°र-उच्°), अस्, m. ‘the apex of the swiftest motion,’ a conjunction (in astronomy).
46786: शिघ्राय, Nom. A. शीघ्रायते, -यितुम्, to be-come quick or rapid; to hasten.
46787: शीघ्रायमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming quick, going rapidly, hastening.
46788: शीघ्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, speedy, one who is quick or expeditious.
46789: शीघ्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, quick, fleet; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; of Viṣṇu; the fighting of cats.
46790: शीघ्रीय, अस्, आ, अम्, quick, speedy, rapid, swift.
46791: शीघ्र्य, अम्, n. quickness, speed, rapidity.
46792: शीत् शीत्, ind. [cf. सीत्], a sound made by drawing in the breath to express any sudden thrill of pleasure or pain (but especially pleasurable sensations during sexual enjoyments, = रति-काल-ध्वनि). —शीत्-कार, अस्, m. making the above sound शीत्; a frown. —शित्-कृत, अम्, n. the sound शीत्, a sound made by drawing in the breath to express pleasurable sensations.
46793: शीत शीत, अस्, आ, अम् (according to some fr. rt. श्यै or fr. rt. 1. शी; according to others an old pass. part. fr. rt. शो), cold, chilly, frigid; dull, apa-thetic, stupid, sluggish, sleepy, (in this sense connected with rt. 1. शी); idle, lazy, stupid; decocted, boiled; (अम्), n. cold, coldness; cold weather, the cold season; water; bark or cinnamon, = त्वच; (अस्), m. a small tree, Cordia Myxa; a kind of ratan, Calamus Fasciculatus; the plant Marsilea Quadrifolia; the Nimb tree; another plant (= पर्पट); cam-phor; (आ), f. a furrow; N. of the wife of Rāma, (in these last two tenses more usually written सीता, q. v.; but derived according to Uṇādi-s. 46968: शुम्भमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. decorating, adorn-ing; handsome, beautiful, (Sāy. = शोभमान।)
46969: शुम्भान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. decorating, illumi-nating, (Sāy. = शोभयत्।)
46971: शुम्भ शुम्भ, अस्, m., N. of an Asura or demon slain by Durgā, (he was son of Gaveṣṭhin and grandson of Prahlāda.) —शुम्भ-घातिनी or शुम्भ-मर्दिनी, f. ‘Śumbha-killing,’ an epithet of Durgā. —शुम्भ-पुर, अम्, ई, n. f. ‘the city of the Asura Śumbha,’ a town and district, (the modern Sambhalpūr in the district of Gondwāna; it is also called Eka-cakra and Hari-gṛha.) —शुम्-भ-बध or शुम्भ-वध, अस्, m. ‘killing of Śumbha,’ N. of the tenth chapter of the Devī-māhātmya of the Mārkaṇḍeya-Purāṇa.
46972: शुर शुर, अस्, m. (for शूर, q. v.), a hero; a lion, &c.
46973: शुरुध् शुरुध्, धस्, f. pl., Ved. gifts, treasures, riches; waters, water, (Sāy. = आपः, Ṛg-veda IV. 23, 8); preventers or alleviators of pain or sorrow, (Sāy. = शुचेर् दुःखस्य प्रतिरोद्धारः or शोकस्य रोधयितृ); herbs or other remedies used to allay pain; exhilarating drinks (according to some).
46974: शुल्क् शुल्क्, cl. 10. P. शुल्कयति, -यितुम्, to pay, give; to gain, acquire; to abandon, leave, forsake; to create (सर्जने); to narrate, tell; [cf. rt. श्वल्क्।]
46975: शुल्क, अस्, अम्, m. n. toll, tax, duty, customs (especially money levied at ferries, passes, and roads); a sum of money, price, (Sāy. = मूल्य); property, wealth, (Sāy. = धन); gain, profit; money ad-vanced to ratify a bargain; money given to the parents of the bride (originally as purchase-price); a present made by a bridegroom to his bride; nuptial present; a marriage-settlement or dower; a wife's perquisites or private property (such as the profits of household labour, domestic utensils, milch cattle, ornaments, servants, &c.). —शुल्क-खण्डन, अम्, n. defrauding the revenue. —शुल्क-ग्राहक, अस्, इका, अम्, or शुल्क-ग्राहिन्, ई, इणी, इ, receiving a toll or duty. —शुल्क-द, अस्, m. the giver of a nuptial present, an affianced suitor. —शुल्क-मो-षण, अम्, n. stealing or defrauding the revenue. —शुल्क-शाला, f. a custom-house; [cf. शौल्क-शालिक।] —शुल्क-सञ्ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, having (merely) the name of a nuptial gratuity. —शुल्क-स्थान, अम्, n. a toll-office, custom-house (Manu VIII. 400); any object of taxation or duty. —शुल्क-हानि, इस्, f. loss or forfeiture of wages or dower, &c. —शुल्का-भिधान (°क-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, = शुल्क-सञ्ज्ञ। —शुल्कावाप्त (°क-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, obtained as a dowry.
46976: शुल्किक शुल्किक, अस्, m., N. of a country or district; [cf. शौल्किकेय।]
46977: शुल्ल शुल्ल, अम्, n. (for शुल्व), a cord, rope, string; copper (= ताम्र; cf. शुल्व).
46978: शुल्व् शुल्व् (also written शुल्ब्), cl. 10. P. शुल्वयति, -यितुम्, to send away, dis-miss; to measure; to create.
46979: शुल्व or शुल्ब, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 95. fr. rt. 1. शुच्), a rope, cord, string, (said to be also अस्, m., आ or ई, f.); copper, a copper vessel; a sacrificial observance; institute, law, custom; a quantity of water; (आनि), n. pl., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Yajur-veda; [cf. शुल्विक।] —शुल्व-ज, अम्, n. brass. —शुल्व-दीपिका, f., N. of a work. —शुल्व-परिशिष्ट and शुल्व-वार्त्तिक and शुल्व-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of works. —शुल्वारि (°व-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of copper,’ sulphur.
46980: शुल्विक, आनि, n. pl., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Yajur-veda.
46981: शुशुक्वस् शुशुक्वस्। See under rt. 3. शुच्।
46982: शुशुक्षणि शुशुक्षणि in आ-शुशुक्षणि, q. v.
46983: शुशुमा शुशुमा, f., N. of the wife of Śukra.
46984: शुशुलूकयातु शुशुलूक-यातु, उस्, m., Ved. a demon in the shape of an owlet, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 104, 22. शुशूलूक = शिशूलूक, a small owl; cf. उलूक-यातु।)
46985: शुश्रुवस् शुश्रुवस्। See under rt. 1. श्रु।
46986: शुश्रू शुश्रू, ऊस्, f. (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. श्रु), ‘one who waits on a child,’ a mother.
46987: शुश्रूषक, अस्, आ, अम्, desirous of hearing, attentive, obedient, attending or waiting on; (अस्), m. an attendant, servant (comprehending five de-scriptions of persons, viz. a pupil, a religious pupil, a hired servant, an officer, and a slave).
46988: शुश्रूषण, अम्, n. obedience; dutiful homage, close and assiduous attendance, service, serving.
46989: शुश्रूषा, f. desire or wish to hear, desire to obey, obedience; service (said to be of five kinds, see शुश्रूषक); obsequiousness, reverence; say-ing, speaking, telling. —शुश्रूषा-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, diligent or attentive in service.
46990: शुश्रूषित्वा, ind. having attended or waited upon (as a slave upon his master, Manu XI. 110).
46991: शुश्रूषु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of hearing or obey-ing, obedient, attentive, serving, attending.
46992: शुष् शुष् (thought to be for सुष्, which again was probably for an original सुस्), cl. 4. P. शुष्यति (ep. also A. -ते), शुशोष, शोक्ष्-यति, अशुषत्, शोष्टुम्, to dry, become dry, dry up; to wither, become withered; to languish, be-come emaciated; to be afflicted: Caus. शोषयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अशूशुषत्, to make dry, dry up, wither, parch; to emaciate; to destroy; to extinguish: Desid. शुशुक्षति: Intens. शोशुष्यते, शोशोष्टि; [cf. Zend hushka: Gr. σαυαρός, σαυσαρισμός, σαυκός (= शुष्क), σαυχμός, αὐχμός, σαχνός, αὔω, αὖος, αὐστηρός: Lat. siccus: Goth. siuk, sauht: Old Germ. siuh, siuchi, siuhjan, suht: Angl. Sax. seoc, seac, sioc, sic, suht: Slav. such, ‘dry:’ Lith. sausa-s: Hib. seacadh, ‘parched, frozen;’ sioc, ‘frost;’ sican.]
46993: शुष, अस्, ई, m. f. drying, drying up; a hole in the ground.
46994: शुषत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. drying up, absorbing (moisture).
46995: शुषि, इस्, f. drying; a hole, chasm; the hollow or groove in the fang of a snake; [cf. Gr. κυσό-ς, κυσ-θό-ς; Lat. cun-nu-s; Lith. kuszy-s.]
46996: शुषिर, अस्, आ, अम्, full of holes or crevices (caused by drying), perforated, bored, pierced, full of interstices or spaces; (अम्), n. a hole, vacuity, chasm; the atmosphere; a wind-instrument; (अस्), m. fire; a rat, mouse; (आ), f. a river; a sort of per-fume (commonly called Nalī).
46997: शुषिल, अस्, m. ‘the dryer,’ air, wind.
46998: शुष्क, अस्, आ, अम्, dried, dried up, dry; shriveled, withered, emaciated, shrunk up; groundless, cause-less; unproductive, fruitless, unprofitable; offensive; (अम्), n., Ved. anything dry, dry wood (for lighting fire by attrition). —शुष्क-कलह, अस्, m. vain or useless wrangling, a quarrel about trifles. —शुष्क-ता, f. or शुष्क-त्व, अम्, n. dryness. —शुष्क-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a dry or withered leaf; a dried pot-herb. —शुष्क-पर्ण, अम्, n. a dry or withered leaf. —शुष्क-फल, अम्, n. dry fruit. —शुष्क-मत्स्य, अस्, m. a dried fish. —शुष्क-मांस, अम्, n. dry flesh, dry meat. —शुष्क-रेवती, f. epithet of a particular Mātrikā or goddess presiding over a kind of disease; [cf. रेवती, पूतना।] —शुष्क-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, dried up. —शुष्क-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a dry tree; a particular plant or shrub (= धव). —शुष्क-वैर, अम्, n. ground-less enmity. —शुष्क-व्रण, अस्, m. a dried up wound, cicatrized sore, scar. —शुष्क-स्रोत, अस्, आ, अम्, having the stream dried up. —शुष्काङ्ग (°क-अङ्°), अस्, ई, अम्, having shriveled limbs, emaciated, withered; (अस्), m. a particular plant or shrub, = धव; (ई), f. a lizard, chameleon. —शुष्कान्न (°क-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘dry food,’ rice in the husk. —शुष्कार्द्र (°क-आर्°), अम्, n. dry ginger.
46999: शुष्कल, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, m. f. n. dry flesh; flesh; one who eats flesh.
47000: शुष्ण, अस्, m. the sun; fire; N. of a demon of drought (represented in the Ṛg-veda as being over-come by Indra); (अम्), n., Ved. strength, (enume-rated among the बल-नामानि in Naigh. II. 9.) —शुष्ण-हत्य, अम्, n., Ved. the slaughter of Śuṣṇa.
47001: शुष्म, अस्, आ, अम्, strong, powerful (Ved.); (अस्), m. power, strength, vigour (Ved.); the sun; fire, flame, light; air, wind; a bird; (अम्), n. strength, prowess (= बल, Naigh. II. 9); light, lustre.
47002: शुष्मन्, आ, m. fire; a particular plant, = चि-त्रक; (अ), n. light, lustre; strength, prowess.
47003: शुष्मिण, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Śivis.
47004: शुष्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, powerful, strong; fiery, mettle-some; (इणस्), m. pl., N. of a caste living in Kuśa-dvīpa (corresponding to the Kṣatriyas). —शुष्-मिन्-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most powerful, very mighty.
47005: शुष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming dry, drying up.
47006: शुष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being dry or dried up, languishing, thirsty.
47007: शोष, अस्, m. drying up, exsiccation, dryness; pulmonary consumption; emaciation; intumescence, (for शोथ।) —शोष-सम्भव, अम्, n. the root of long pepper. —शोषापहा (°ष-अप्°), f. ‘re-moving consumption,’ a kind of plant (= क्लीत-नक).
47008: शोषक, अस्, इका, अम्, drying up, exsiccating, absorbing, absorbent.
47009: शोषण, अस्, ई, अम्, drying up, draining; causing to fade; (अस्), m. one of the arrows of Kāma-deva (god of love); the plant Bignonia Indica; (अम्), n. the act of drying up; absorption; exhaustion; suck-ing up, suction; dry ginger.
47010: शोषणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be dried up or absorbed.
47011: शोषयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be dried up, &c.
47013: शोषित, अस्, आ, अम्, dried, dried up, desiccated, absorbed, sucked up, exhausted, drained, emptied.
47014: शोषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, drying up (often at the end of comps.); (इणी), f. ether, one of the five Dhāraṇās.
47015: शूक शूक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. शो), the awn of barley, &c.; a bristle, spicule; the bristle or sharp hair of insects, &c.; compassion, clemency, tenderness; a kind of venomous insect or lizard (produced in stagnant water); a sort of water-leech (?); a kind of moss or weed growing on stagnant water (= जल-श्°); a particular remedy in which the Śūka is used; (आ), f. cowach. —शूक-कीट or शूक-कीटक, अस्, m. a kind of caterpillar covered with bristles or hairs. —शूक-तृण, अम्, n. a kind of grass. —शूक-धान्य, अम्, n. any awned or bearded grain (as barley &c.). —शूक-पिण्डि, इस्, or शूक-पिण्डी, f. cowach (= कपि-कच्छु). —शूक-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, awned, bearded; (अती), f. cowach. —शूक-शिम्बा, f. or शुक-शिम्बि, इस्, or शूक-शिम्बिका or शूक-शिम्बी, f. cowach, (also spelt शुक-शिम्बा, q. v.)
47016: शूकक, अस्, m. barley or a bearded kind of wheat resembling barley; the sentiment of compassion or tenderness.
47017: शूकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, awned, bearded (as corn, grain, &c.).
47018: शूकर शूकर, अस्, m. (said to be connected with शूक, or fr. शू, an imitative sound, + कर; cf. सूकर), a hog, pig; N. of a Naraka; (ई), f. a sow; a kind of moss, Lycopodium Imbricatum; [cf. Gr. αῦς, ὗς; Old Germ. sū; Mod. Germ. sau.] —शूकर-कन्द, अस्, m. ‘hog's root,’ a kind of bulbous plant (= वाराही-कन्द). —शूकर-दंष्-ट्र, अस्, m. a hog's tusk; N. of a kind of disease, (prolapsus ani.) —शूकर-पादिका, f. a kind of plant (= कोल-शिम्बी). —शूकराक्रान्ता (°र-आक्°), f. a kind of moss (= वराह-क्रान्ता). —शूकरेष्ट (°र-इष्°), अस्, आ, अम्, liked by hogs or swine; (अस्), m. a kind of grass (= कसेरु).
47019: शूकल शूकल, अस्, m. a restive horse; [cf. शूलक।]
47020: शूकापुट्ट शूकापुट्ट or (according to Śabda-k.) शूकापूट्ट, अस्, m. a particular gem, (perhaps) a kind of amber (= तृण-मणि).
47021: शूकुल शूकुल, अस्, m. (?), a fish in general; a kind of fish; a fragrant grass, Cyperus.
47022: शूकृत शू-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. making the sound शू or शूत्, snorting (said of a horse).
47023: शूक्ष्म शूक्ष्म, incorrect for सूक्ष्म, q. v.
47024: शूघन शूघन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. going quickly, (Sāy. शूघनासः = आशु-गन्त्र्यः, Ṛg-veda IV. 58, 7.)
47025: शूतिपर्ण शूति-पर्ण, अस्, m. (the meaning of शूति is doubtful), a kind of tree (= आरग्-बध).
47026: शूद्र शूद्र, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 19. fr. rt. 1. शुच्, to be afflicted, &c.), a man of the fourth or servile tribe (whose only business, ac-cording to Manu I. 91, was to serve the three higher castes; in Ṛg-veda X. 90, 12. the Śūdra is said to have been born from the feet of Puruṣa; in Manu I. 87. he is fabled to have sprung from the same part of the body of Brahmā; केवल-शूद्र, a pure Śūdra); (आ), f. a woman of the Śūdra tribe; (ई), f. the wife of a Śūdra. —शूद्र-कन्या, f. a Śūdra girl. —शूद्र-कृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be done by a Śūdra, proper for a Śūdra; (अम्), n. the duty of a Śūdra. —शूद्रकृत्य-विचार-तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a part of Raghu-nandana's Smṛti-tattva (illustrat-ing the duties of Śūdras at the anniversaries of the death of parents and at other ceremonies). —शूद्र-ता, f. or शूद्र-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a Śūdra or slave; servility. —शूद्र-धर्म, अस्, m. the duty of a Śūdra (i. e. the service of the three higher castes). —शूद्रधर्म-तत्त्व, अम्, n. ‘the nature of a Śūdra's duties,’ N. of a work by Kamalākara. —शूद्र-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, dear to a Śūdra, liked by Śūdras; [cf. शूद्रोदक below.] —शूद्रा-परिण-यन, अम्, n. the marrying a Śūdra female. —शू-द्रा-पुत्र, अस्, m. the son of a Śūdra woman, (the father being either a Śūdra or a man of a different caste.) —शूद्रा-भार्य, अस्, m. one who has a Śūdra woman for his wife, the husband of a Śūdra woman. —शूद्रार्ता (°र-आर्°), f. a kind of plant (= प्रियङ्गु). —शूद्रा-वेदन, अम्, n. the mar-rying a Śūdra woman. —शूद्रा-वेदिन्, ई, m. marry-ing a Śūdra woman, a man of one of the three higher classes who has married a Śūdra wife. —शू-द्राशौच (°र-अश्°), अम्, n. the impurity of a Śūdra. —शूद्रा-सुत, अस्, m. = शूद्रा-पुत्र. —शू-द्राह्निक (°र-आह्°), अम्, n. the daily ceremonies of a Śūdra. —शूद्री-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become a Śūdra. —शूद्रोदक (°र-उद्°), अम्, n. water that has been polluted by the touch of a Śūdra. —शूद्रोदक-पान-प्रायश्चित्त, अम्, n. a penance for drinking water given by a Śūdra.
47027: शूद्रक, अस्, m., N. of the first Āndhra king, (variously written Sindhuka, Śiśuka, and Śūraka); of a king (the author of the drama called Mṛc-chakaṭikā).
47028: शूद्राणी, f. the wife of a Śūdra.
47029: शून शून, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्वि, q. v.), swelled, swollen, increased, grown, prospered; mor-bidly swollen; empty, vacant (Ved., Sāy. = शून्य); (अम्), n., Ved. swelling, increase, (Sāy. = सम्-ऋद्-धि, Ṛg-veda III. 33, 13); emptiness, poverty, (Sāy. = शून्य, दारिद्र्य, Ṛg-veda II. 27, 17); an in-correct pronunciation (in Vedic phonetics).
47030: शून-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has increased.
47031: शूना शूना, f. (= सूना, q. v.), the uvula or soft palate; a slaughter-house, any place where animals are killed or are liable to be destroyed, (five of these are enumerated, viz. a fire-place, a grind-stone, a broom, a mortar, and a water-pot; cf. पञ्च-सूना।) —शूना-चक्र-ध्वज-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who keeps a slaughter-house, one who has an oil-press, and one who exhibits a vintner's sign, (Manu IV. 84.) —शूना-दोष, see सूना-दोष। —शूना-वत्, आन्, m. one who keeps a slaughter-house, a butcher. —शूना-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in or brought from a slaughter-house or any place where animals are destroyed.
47032: शून्य शून्य, अस्, आ, अम् (probably connected with शून above, fr. rt. श्वि), empty, void, hollow; vacant, barren, non-existent; utterly destitute or de-prived of, without (with inst.); ruined; nonsensical, un-meaning; guileless, unsuspicious; indifferent; lonely, private, desert, desolate, (शून्ये or शून्यम्, ind. in a lonely place, secretly); bare, naked; (अम्), n. a void, vacuum, blank; space, heaven, ether, the sky, atmosphere; a dot, spot; a cypher; naught, vacuity, nonentity, (one of the principles of Bauddha meta-physics); N. of Brahma; (आ), f. a hollow reed; a barren woman; the prickly pear; [cf. Gr. κενός, κενεός; Æol. κέννος.] —शून्य-गेह, अम्, n. an empty house. —शून्य-ता, f. or शून्य-त्व, अम्, n. emptiness, voidness, vacuity, non-existence, un-reality, the false or illusory nature of all existence. —शून्य-पदवी, f. ‘empty path,’ the road or passage of the soul, (see महा-पथ, मुद्रा-मार्ग।) —शून्य-मध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, having a hollow centre, empty inside; (अस्), m. a hollow reed. —शून्य-वत्, ind. like a cypher, annihilated or vanished as it were. —शून्य-वाद, अस्, m. the doctrine of the non-existence of anything. —शून्य-वादिन्, ई, m. ‘affirmer of non-existence,’ an atheist; a Buddhist. —शून्य-स्थान, अम्, n. an empty place. —शून्य-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, empty-handed. —शून्य-हृ-दय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘empty-hearted,’ unsuspecting, unsuspicious; absent in mind. —शून्याकृति (°य-आक्°), इस्, इस्, इ, ‘empty-formed,’ having a vacant appearance or aspect. —शून्यागार-कृतालय (°य-आग्°, °त-आल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, making an abode in de-serted houses. —शून्यालय (°य-आल्°), अस्, m. an empty or deserted house, (sleeping in such a house is forbidden.) —शून्यी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्-तुम्, to make empty, leave.
47033: शूपकार शूप-कार, अस्, m. (for सूप-कार, q. v.), one who lives by cooking for Śūdras (= शूद्र-पाकोपजीविन्).
47034: शूयमान शूयमान। See under rt. श्वि।
47035: शूर् शूर् (also written सूर्, q. v.), cl. 4. A. शूर्यते, शुशूरे, शूरितुम्, to hurt, in-jure, kill; to be firm or motionless, stand fast, be fixed; to make firm or immovable; to be senseless; cl. 10. A. शूरयते, -यितुम्, Aor. अशुशूरत्, to be valiant or powerful, act the hero; to make great effort or exertion, (in these senses rather a Nom. fr. शूर below.)
47036: शूर, अस्, m. (probably connected with शवस्), a hero, warrior, champion, valiant man, great or mighty man; a lion; a boar; the sun; N. of Yādava, the grandfather of Kṛṣṇa; the Śāl tree, Shorea Robusta; N. of certain other plants or trees, = चित्रक; = लकुच; = मसूर; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a tribe inhabiting Bhārata-varṣa; [cf. Zend śūra; Gr. κῦρ-ος, κυρό-ω, κύριος, κοίρανος, κοῦρος κόρος.] —शूर-कीट, अस्, m. ‘warrior-insect,’ an in-ferior hero. —शूर-ग्राम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a multitude of heroes. —शूर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. more heroic, very valiant. —शूर-ता, f. or शूर-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a hero, heroism, prowess, valour, bravery. —शूर-देव, अस्, m., N. of the second of the twenty-four Arhats of the future Utsarpiṇī. —शूर-पुत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having heroes as sons; (आ), f., Ved. epithet of Aditi. —शूर-पुर, अम्, n. ‘hero-town,’ N. of a town. —शूर-मठ, अस्, अम्, m. n. the college or monastery of Śūra. —शूर-मान, अम्, n. thinking one's self a hero, arrogance, vaunting. —शूर-मा-निन्, ई, m. one who thinks himself a hero, a boaster, braggart. —शूरम्-मन्य, अस्, m. one who thinks himself a hero, a boaster. —शूर-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of several kings. —शूर-वीर, अस्, m. a proper N. —शूर-श्लोक, अस्, m. a kind of arti-ficial verse; [cf. वीर-विरुद।] —शूर-साति, इस्, f., Ved. conflict of heroes, battle, war, (accord-ing to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 31, 6. शूर-साता = शूरैः सम्भजनीये युद्धे।) —शूर-सेन, अस्, m., N. of the country about Mathurā; of a king (of Mathurā and ruler of the Yadus); (आस्), m. pl., N. of the people inhabiting the above country. —शूर-सेनक, आस्, m. pl., N. of the people and country about Mathurā. —शूरसेन-ज, अस्, m. one born in Śūra-sena, an inhabitant of Śūra-sena. —शूरार्थ (°र-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, useful for or suited to heroes, for the sake of warriors. —शूरेश्वर (°र-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of Śūra,’ the tutelary deity of Śūra (or the statue of a deity); a temple built by Śūra.
47037: शूरक, अस्, m., N. of a king (= शूद्रक).
47038: शूरण, अस्, आ, अम्, high-spirited (Ved., said of horses; Sāy. = विक्रम-शील, Ṛg-veda I. 163, 10); (अस्), m. a kind of esculent root, Arum Campanu-latum; the plant Bignonia Indica. —शूरणोद्भुज (°ण-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘feeding on Arum Campanu-latum,’ a kind of yellow bird (= हरिद्राङ्ग).
47039: शूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed, firm.
47040: शूर्त शूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (probably) eager, quick, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 174, 6. शूर्ताः = क्षिप्राः or = क्षिप्ताः, वर्जिताः; in Naigh. II. 15. शूर्ताः is enumerated among the क्षिप्र-नामानि।)
47041: शूर्प् शूर्प् (perhaps rather a Nom. fr. शूर्प below), cl. 10. P. शूर्पयति, -यि-तुम्, to measure, mete out.
47042: शूर्प, अस्, अम्, m. n. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 26. fr. rt. शॄ; also written सूर्प), a winnowing basket or a kind of wicker receptacle which, when shaken about, serves as a fan for winnowing corn; (अस्), m. a measure of two Droṇas; (ई), f. a small winnowing basket or fan; a toy for children; N. of the sister of Rāvaṇa, (see शूर्प-णखा।) —शूर्प-कर्ण, अस्, m. ‘having ears like winnowing fans,’ an elephant. —शूर्प-णखा, f. or शूर्प-णखी, f. ‘having finger-nails like winnowing fans,’ N. of the sister of the Daitya Rāvaṇa, (she fell in love with Rāma and, being rejected by him, attacked Sītā, but was beaten off and mutilated by Lakṣmaṇa; in revenge she incited her brother to carry off Sītā.) —शूर्प-निष्पाव, अस्, m. a basket-full of win-nowed corn. —शूर्प-पर्णी, f. a sort of bean, Phaseolus Trilobus. —शूर्प-वात, अस्, m. the wind raised by shaking a winnowing basket. —शूर्प-श्रुति, इस्, m. ‘having ears like winnowing fans,’ an elephant.
47043: शूर्पक, अस्, m., N. of a demon (an enemy of Kāma-deva). —शूर्पकाराति or शूर्पकारि (°क-अर्°), इस्, m. ‘enemy of Śūrpaka,’ epithet of Kāma (god of love).
47044: शूर्पी, f. See above under शूर्प।
47045: शूर्पारक शूर्पारक, N. of a mythical country.
47046: शूर्म शूर्म, अस्, m. an iron image; an anvil.
47047: शूर्मि, इस्, m. f. or शूर्मिका or शूर्मी, f. = शूर्म above; [cf. सूर्मि, स्युर्मि।]
47048: शूल् शूल् (rather a Nom. fr. शूल below), cl. 1. P. शूलति, शुशूल, शूलितुम्, to be ill; to disorder, make sick, disease; to pierce, transfix, impale; to cry, make a loud noise; to collect (?).
47049: शूल, अस्, अम्, m. n. any sharp or acute pain; pain in the stomach, colic; rheumatism, gout; any sharp or pointed weapon, a pike, dart, spear, lance, spike; the trident of Śiva; a sharp iron pin or spit (on which meat is roasted); a stake for impaling criminals; a banner, ensign; the ninth astronomical Yoga; death, dying; (आ), f. a stake for impaling criminals; a harlot, prostitute; [cf. Slav. sūliza.] —शूल-गव, a kind of animal sacrifice. —शूल-ग्रन्थि, इस्, f. ‘having sharp knots,’ a kind of Dūrvā grass (= माला-दूर्वा). —शूल-घातन, अम्, n. ‘pain-destroying,’ iron rust or filings. —शूल-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, removing or allaying sharp pain, sedative, anodyne; (अस्), m. a kind of plant (= तुम्बुरु)। —शूल-द्विष्, ट्, m. ‘enemy to colic,’ Asa Fetida. —शूल-धन्वन्, आ, m. ‘having a trident for a bow,’ epithet of Śiva. —शूल-धर, अस्, m. ‘spear-holder, trident-holder,’ epithet of Śiva; (आ), f. epithet of Durgā. —शूल-धारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, spear-holding, lance-bearing, trident-holding; (इणी), f. epithet of Durgā. —शूल-धृक्, m. (see धृक्, p. 459), ‘trident-bearing,’ epithet of Śiva; (क्), f. epithet of Durgā. —शूल-नाशन, अम्, n. ‘remov-ing pain in the stomach,’ white sochal salt. —शूल-पत्त्री, f. a kind of grass (= शूली). —शूल-पाणि, इस्, m. ‘trident-handed,’ epithet of Śiva (regarded as the king of the Bhūtas); N. of the author of the Prāyaścitta-viveka and of the Tithi-dvaidha-prakaraṇa and of the Yājñavalkya-ṭīkā. —शूल-पाणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, holding or bearing a lance or spear. —शूल-भृत्, त्, m. ‘spear-holder,’ an epithet of Śiva. —शूल-भेद, अस्, m., N. of a place. —शूल-मुद्गर-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having a lance and mace in hand, armed with a lance and club. —शूल-वेदना, f. sharp or acute pain. —शूल-शत्रु, उस्, m. ‘hostile to colic,’ the castor-oil plant, Ricinus Communis. —शूल-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed on a stake, impaled. —शूल-हन्त्री, f. ‘colic-removing,’ a kind of barley (= यवानी). —शूल-हस्त, अस्, m. ‘lance-handed,’ a man armed with a lance, lancer, pikeman. —शूल-हृत्, त्, m. ‘removing colic,’ Asa Fetida. —शूला-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to roast on a spit. —शूलाकृत (°ल-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, roasted on a spit, &c.; (अम्), n. roasted meat. —शूलाग्र (°ल-अग्°), अम्, n. the point of a pike or stake, &c. —शूलेश्वरी-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —शू-लोत्खा (°ल-उत्°), f. the medicinal plant Serratula Anthelmintica. —शूलोद्यत-कर (°ल-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, with uplifted spear in hand.
47050: शूलक, अस्, m. a restive or unbroken horse; [cf. शूकल।]
47051: शूलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a spear or any sharp instrument; roasted on a spit; (अस्), m. a hare; (अम्), n. roast meat.
47052: शूलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering sharp pain, suffering from colic; armed with a spear or pike, carrying a lance or stake; (ई), m. a spearman, pikeman, lancer; epithet of Śiva (as holding a trident); a hare; N. of a Muni; (इनी), f. epithet of Durgā.
47053: शूलिन, अस्, m. the Indian fig-tree (= भाण्डीर).
47054: शूली, f. a kind of grass (= मधु-लता).
47055: शूल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, roasted on a spit; deserving impalement; (अम्), n. roasted meat. —शूल्य-पाक, अस्, m. any meat or other substance roasted on a spit. —शूल्य-मांस, अम्, n. roast meat, meat cooked on a spit.
47056: शूशुजान शूशुजान, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Sāy. = शोशुचान, दीप्यमान, Ṛg-veda X. 34, 6; cf. शुशुचान, p. 1013), Ved. glowing, resplen-dent.
47057: शूशुवस् शूशुवस्, वान्, m. (fr. rt. श्वि), Ved. one who has increased, increasing; large.
47058: शूशुवान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. growing in size, in-creasing in strength.
47059: शूष् शूष् (also written सूष्), cl. 1. P. शूषति, शुशूष, शूषितुम्, to bring forth; to beget, propagate.
47060: शूष शूष, अम्, n. (perhaps connected with rt. श्वि), Ved. strength, (according to Naigh. II. 9, Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 154, 3 = बल; cf. शुष्म; in Naigh. III. 6 = सुख); (अस्), m., N. of a pre-ceptor.
47061: शूषणि, in Ṛg-veda X. 93, 1. probably fr. a base शूषन्; regarded by some as a kind of Ved. Inf. fr. rt. श्वि।
47062: शृकाल शृकाल, अस्, m. (for शृगाल below), a jackal.
47063: शृगाल शृगाल, अस्, m. (etymology doubt-ful, but cf. Gr. κραγέτης; perhaps connected with rt. शॄ; sometimes written सृगाल), a jackal; a rogue, cheat; a coward, poltroon; an ill-natured or harsh-speaking man; N. of a demon; epithet of Kṛṣṇa; (ई), f. a female jackal; a fox; flight, re-treat; a kind of plant (= कोकिलाक्ष); another plant (= विदारी). —शृगाल-कण्टक, अस्, m. ‘jackal's thorn,’ a kind of plant, Zizyphus Scandens. —शृगाल-कोलि, इस्, m. a sort of jujube. —शृगाल-घण्टी, f. a particular plant (= कोकिलाक्ष). —शृ-गाल-जम्बु, उस्, or शृगाल-जम्बू, ऊस्, f. a kind of cucumber, Cucumis Madraspatanus; the fruit of the jujube. —शृगाल-जाति, इस्, f. birth (in a future life) as a jackal. —शृगाल-योनि, इस्, m. f. the womb of a jackal; the being born in a future birth as a jackal. —शृगाल-रूप, अस्, m. ‘jackal-formed,’ epi-thet of Śiva. —शृगाल-विन्ना, f. a kind of plant (= पृश्नि-पर्णी).
47064: शृगालिका, f. a female jackal; a fox; running away, flight, retreat; a kind of plant (= भूमि-कुष्माण्ड); a proper N.
47065: शृङ्खल शृङ्खल, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (ety-mology doubtful; perhaps connected with शिञ्जा, ‘a tinkling sound’), an iron chain; any chain or fetter; a belt or chain worn round the waist for ornament, &c.; an iron chain for confining the feet of an elephant; a measuring chain. —शृङ्खल-ता, f. or शृङ्खल-त्व, अम्, n. the being chained together; restraint; concatenation, connection, order; a series. —शृङ्खला-बन्ध or शृङ्खला-बन्धन, अम्, n. confining by chains or fetters.
47066: शृङ्खलक, अस्, m. a chain; a young camel or other young animal with wooden rings or clogs on his feet (to prevent his straying); any camel.
47067: शृङ्खलित, अस्, आ, अम्, chained, fettered, bound, confined.
47068: शृङ्खली, f. a kind of plant (= कोकिलाक्ष).
47069: शृङ्ग शृङ्ग, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 125. fr. rt. शॄ with affix ग, a nasal being inserted; according to some perhaps contracted fr. शिरङ्-ग, ‘head-going’), a horn; the top or summit of a mountain, a peak, crag; the summit of a building, pinnacle, turret; any peak or point or projection or lofty object; a cusp or horn of the moon; height, elevation, dignity, lordship, mastership, supremacy, sovereignty; the rising or bursting forth of desire, excess of love or passion; anything sharp or fine-pointed; a fountain or artificial spout of water; any horn-like vessel or instrument; a buffalo's horn or other horn used for blowing; a lotus; a mark, token, sign; (अस्), m. a medicinal plant and root (= जी-वक); N. of a Ṛṣi or Muni (of whom, in some parts of India, on occasions of drought, earthen images are said to be made and supplicated for rain); [cf. Gr. κέρας; Lat. cornu; Goth. haurn; Angl. Sax. horn.] —शृङ्ग-कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= शृङ्गाटक). —शृङ्ग-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —शृङ्ग-ग्राहिका, f. 47166: शैव शैव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शिव), relating or belonging to the god Śiva; (अस्), m. ‘a worshipper or follower of Śiva,’ N. of one of the three great divisions of modern Hindū sects, (the other two being the Vaiṣṇavas and Śāktas, see वैष्णव, शाक्त; the Śaivas believe in the superiority of Śiva to the other gods of the Tri-mūrti, and identify him with the Supreme Being as the destroying principle as well as source and essence of the whole universe; the temples dedicated to him in his popular symbol of the Liṅga [see शिव] are very numerous every-where, but the doctrines of the Śaivas as represented by their great teachers, such as Śaṅkara, are too philosophical for the majority of the people, who are more attracted by Viṣṇu, especially in his forms of Kṛṣṇa and Rāma: various divisions of Śaiva sects have prevailed at different times, the earlier divisions being those of the Raudras who have the Tri-śūla or trident marked on their foreheads, the Ugras who have the Ḍamaru or drum on their arms, the Bhāktas who have the Liṅga on their foreheads, the Jaṅgamas who have that symbol on their heads, and the Pāśupatas who have it marked on other parts of their bodies; the more modern divisions being the Daṇḍins or mendicant staff-bearers, including the Daś-nāmī-daṇḍins [cf. शङ्क-राचार्य], the Yogins who cultivate absorption into Śiva by suppression of breathing, fixing of the eyes, and eighty-four different attitudes, the Jaṅgamas or Liṅgavats, the Parama-haṃsas, the Aghorins, the Ūrdhva-bāhus, the Ākāśa-mukhins, and many others); 47198: शोपारीपाक शोपारी-पाक, a particular me-dicinal decoction.
47199: शोफ शोफ, अस्, m. (fr. rt. श्वि; cf. शोथ), intumescence, morbid swelling, tumefaction, bloated-ness, flabbiness. —शोफ-घ्नी, f. a kind of shrub (= शाल-पर्णी); a kind of red hogweed. —शोफ-नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, removing swellings; (अस्), m. a kind of tree (= नील). —शोफ-हृत्, त्, त्, त्, re-moving swellings; (त्), m. the marking-nut plant.
47200: शोभ शोभ, शोभन, शोभित, &c. See under rt. 1. शुभ्।
47202: शोशुचत् शोशुचत्, अत्, अती, अत् (fr. Intens. of rt. 3. शुच्), Ved. shining very brightly, very splendid.
47203: शोशुचान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining very brightly, very radiant, resplendent; [cf. शुशुचान।]
47204: शोशुच्यमान शोशुच्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. शुच्), sorrowing intensely, grieving deeply.
47205: शोशुभ्यमान शोशुभ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. शुभ्), shining very much, very brilliant.
47206: शोष शोष, शोषन, शोषित, &c. See under rt. शुष्।
47207: शोस् शोस् (?), ind. a particle of reproach or contempt.
47208: शौक शौक, अम्, n. (fr. शुक), a flock of parrots; (fr. शोक?), sorrowfulness, (according to Śabda-k. = स्त्रीणां करणम्, for करुणम्?).
47209: शौकर शौकर or शौकरव, अम्, n., N. of a particular Tīrtha (described in a chapter of the Vārāha-Purāṇa called Jambūkopākhyāna).
47210: शौक्त शौक्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुक्त), acid, acetic, acetous.
47211: 1. शौक्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, acid, acetic.
47212: शौक्तिक 2. शौक्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुक्ति), relating to a pearl.
47214: शौक्तेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to a pearl; (अम्), n. a pearl.
47215: शौक्र शौक्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुक्र), seminal, relating to sperm, &c.
47216: शौक्लिकेय शौक्लिकेय, अस्, m. a sort of poison, (probably for शौल्किकेय, q. v.)
47217: शौक्ल्य शौक्ल्य, अम्, n. (fr. शुक्ल), white-ness, clearness.
47218: शौङ्ग शौङ्ग, आस्, m. pl., N. of a Gotra.
47219: शौङ्गी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a teacher.
47220: शौङ्गेय शौङ्गेय, अस्, m. (doubtful), epi-thet of Garuḍa or a black-winged enemy of birds.
47221: शौच शौच, अम्, n. (fr. शुचि), purification from personal defilement (especially from defilement caused by the death of a relation &c.); evacuation of excrement; freedom from defilement, purity, cleanness; honesty; (अस्), m. a proper N. —शौच-कल्प, अस्, m. mode of purification, purificatory rite. —शौच-कूप, अस्, m. ‘cleansing-pit,’ a privy. —शौच-त्व, अम्, n. purity. —शौच-विधि, इस्, m. rule of purifi-cation (after defilement by the death of a relation &c.), directions for cleansing the person. —शौचा-चार (°च-आच्°), अस्, m. a purificatory rite, rule of purification established by immemorial custom, mode of cleansing the person by ablution &c. (after voiding excrement or contracting any defilement). —शौचेप्सु (°च-ईप्°), उस्, उस्, उ, wishing or intending to obtain purification.
47222: शौचिक, अस्, m. a cleanser, cleaner; a particular mixed caste (the son of a Śauṇḍika and a Kaivarta woman).
47223: शौचिवृक्षि, इस्, m., N. of an author.
47224: शौचेय, अस्, m. a washerman; a proper N.
47225: शौचद्रथ शौचद्रथ, अस्, m., Ved. a patro-nymic of a descendant of Śucad-ratha.
47226: शौट् शौट् (also written शौड्), cl. 1. P. शौटति, शुशौट, शौटितुम्, to be proud or haughty: Caus. शौटयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशु-शौटत्।
47227: शौटीर, अस्, आ, अम्, proud, haughty; (अस्), m. a hero; a proud or haughty man (but of low tribe or occupation); an upstart; one who abandons the world, an ascetic.
47228: शौटीर्य, अम्, n. pride, arrogance; heroism, prowess.
47229: शौड् शौड् (= rt. शौट्), cl. 1. P. शौडति, &c., to be proud or haughty.
47230: शौड, अस्, m., N. of a country.
47231: शौण्डर्य, अम्, n. pride, arrogance; [cf. शौ-टीर्य।]
47232: शौण्डीर, अस्, आ, अम्, proud, haughty; elevated, looking upwards; (also written शौण्डिर, शौडीर।) —शौण्डीर-ता, f. haughtiness, pride.
47233: शौण्ड शौण्ड, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुण्डा), fond of spirituous liquor, addicted to drinking; drunk, in-toxicated; (ई), f. long pepper; another sort (= चव्य).
47234: शौण्डिक, अस्, m. a distiller and vender of spirituous liquors, vintner; a particular mixed caste (the son of a Kaivarta and a Gāndhika woman); (ई), f. a female vintner or keeper of a tavern or dram shop (regarded as one of the eight Akulas according to the Śāktas).
47237: शौण्डीक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a tribe.
47238: शौद्धाक्षर शौद्धाक्षर, अस्, m., scil. सन्-धि, epithet of a particular Sandhi, (viz. the insertion of श् before चन्द्र, e. g. पुरु-श्-चन्द्र; of ष् be-fore कृ, e. g. परि-ष्-कृण्वन्, &c.)
47239: शौद्धोदनि शौद्धोदनि, इस्, m. (fr. शुद्धो-दन), ‘son of Śuddhodana,’ a patronymic of the great Buddha (founder of the Buddhist religion, see बुद्ध).
47240: शौद्र शौद्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शूद्र), servile, relating or belonging to the Śūdra or lowest tribe; (अस्), m. the son of a man of either of the first three classes by a Śūdra woman, (the last of the twelve kinds of sons acknowledged in the ancient Hindū law.)
47241: शौधिका शौधिका, f. a variety of panic, (Panicum Italicum, = रक्त-कङ्गु।)
47242: शौन शौन, अम्, n. (fr. शूना), meat kept at a slaughter-house.
47243: शौनिक, अस्, m. a butcher, poulterer, vender of the flesh of beasts or birds; chase, hunting.
47244: शौनक शौनक, अस्, m., N. of the reputed author of the Ṛg-veda Prātiśākhya and of certain Kalpa-sūtras and various other Vedic compositions and works on law, (he is described as the teacher of Kātyāyana and especially of Āśvalāyana; he is said to have united the Bāṣkala and Śākala Śākhās, and is sometimes identified with the Vedic Ṛṣi Gṛtsa-mada; but according to the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa, Śaunaka was a son of Gṛtsa-mada, and originated the system of four castes; the various legends about him are very confused.) —शौनक-कल्प-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of certain Kalpa-sūtras (ascribed to Śaunaka and supposed to have been destroyed by the author). —शौनक-गृह्य-सूत्र, अम्, n. the Gṛhya-sūtras of the Ṛg-veda ascribed to Śaunaka. —शौनकानुक्रमणी (°क-अन्°), f. an Anukra-maṇī or Vedic index ascribed to Śaunaka. —शौन-कारण्यक (°क-आर्°), अम्, n. an Āraṇyaka ascribed to Śaunaka (probably identified with the Aitareyā-raṇyaka). —शौनकोपनिषद् (°क-उप्°), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
47245: शौनकिन्, इनस्, m. pl. the pupils or followers of Śaunaka.
47246: शौनकी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
47247: शौनकीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to or composed by Śaunaka or the Śaunakīyas, (शौनकीय-च-तुराध्यायिका, ‘Śaunaka's treatise in four chapters,’ i. e. the Atharva-veda Prātiśākhya); (आस्), m. pl. the pupils or school of Śaunaka. —शौनकीय-च-तुराध्यायिका, f., N. of the above Prātiśākhya. —शौनकीय-चरण, N. of a Caraṇa (probably founded by the author of the Śākala-prātiśākhya).
47248: शौनहोत्र शौनहोत्र, अस्, m. the son of Śuna-hotra and grandson of Bharad-vāja; epithet of the Vedic Ṛṣi Gṛtsa-mada.
47249: शौभ शौभ, अस्, m. (fr. शुभ), a god, di-vinity; the Areca or betel-nut tree (= गुवाक); (अम्), n. the city of Hariścandra (fabled to be sus-pended in the air, see हरि-श्-चन्द्र).
47250: शौभनेय शौभनेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शोभना), sprung from a handsome mother; relating to any-thing handsome or brilliant.
47251: शौभाञ्जन शौभाञ्जन, अस्, m. (fr. शोभाञ्-जन, q. v.), the tree Hyperanthera Moringa.
47252: शौभिक शौभिक, अस्, m. (probably con-nected with शुभ), a juggler, conjurer (= इन्द्र-जालिक).
47253: शौभ्रेय शौभ्रेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-longing to anything white or shining (e. g. to silver, talc, sandal, &c.); (अस्), m. ‘son of Śubhrā,’ a patro-nymic.
47254: शौर शौर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शूर), relating to a hero, heroic.
47255: शौरदेव्यः, in Ṛg-veda VIII. 70, 15. appa-rently acc. pl. of शौरदेवी, qualifying गाः, ‘cows,’ and explained by Sāy. thus, दीव्यन्ति क्रीडन्त इति देवा योद्धारः शूराश्-च ते देवाश्-च शूर-देवाः, तेषां हितं शौरदेवं युद्धं तत्-सम्-बन्धिन्यो गाः।
47256: शौरसेन, अम्, n. (fr. शूर-सेन), the language spoken by the people of Śūra-sena; (ई), f. a Prākṛt dialect supposed to have been spoken at Mathurā.
47257: शौरि, इस्, m., N. of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa; of Bala-rāma (as descended from Śūra); the planet Saturn.
47258: शौर्य, अम्, n. heroism, valour, prowess, might; the heroic branch of the dramatic art, representation of war and supernatural events on the stage (= आर-भटी). —शौर्योपार्जित (°य-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ac-quired by valour.
47259: शौर्प शौर्प, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शूर्प), measured by a winnowing basket &c., belonging to a winnow-ing fan &c.
47260: शौर्पणाय्य, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
47261: शौर्पिक, अस्, ई, अम्, = शौर्प above.
47262: शौल्क शौल्क, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुल्क), relating to tolls or customs or taxes, levied (as a tax &c.); (अस्), m. a superintendant of tolls or customs, a custom-house officer.
47263: शौल्कशालिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुल्क-शाला), of or belonging to a custom-house, derived from a custom-house.
47264: शौल्कायनि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.
47265: शौल्किक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to taxes or tolls; (अस्), m. a superintendant of tolls or customs.
47266: शौल्किकेय शौल्किकेय, अस्, m. (fr. शुल्किक), a kind of poison (said to be produced in a country called Śulkika; according to some the venom of a kind of snake).
47267: शौल्फ शौल्फ, अम्, n. a kind of vegetable (commonly called Śulphā).
47268: शौल्विक शौल्विक, अस्, m. (fr. शुल्व), a cop-persmith.
47269: शौव शौव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. श्वन्), relating or belonging to dogs, canine; (अस्), m., N. of a par-ticular Udgītha; (अम्), n. a pack or number of dogs; the nature or state of a dog.
47270: शौवन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to canine nature; having the qualities of a dog; (अम्), n. the nature of a dog; the progeny of a dog.
47271: शौवापद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. श्वा-पद), relating to a wild beast or beast of prey, ferocious, savage, wild.
47272: शौवस्तिक शौवस्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. श्वस्), of or belonging to to-morrow, lasting till to-morrow, ephemeral. —शौवस्तिक-त्व, अम्, n. the lasting or enduring till to-morrow, ephemeralness.
47273: शौष्कल शौष्कल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुष्कली), eating fish and flesh; (अस्), m. an habitual eater of meat; a vender of flesh, dealer in flesh or dried meat; (अम्), n. the price of dried meat.
47274: श्चम् श्चम्, for rt. चम्, to consume, (ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 104, 2. श्चम्नन् = भक्षयन्तु, but also referrible to rt. 1. शम्।)
47275: श्चुत् 1. श्चुत् or 1. श्च्युत् (perhaps fr. a noun formed fr. an original rt. श्च्यु; cf. rts. 1. च्यु, 2. च्युत्), cl. 1. P. श्चोतति or श्च्योतति, चुश्चोत or चुश्च्योत, अश्चुतत्, अश्चोतीत्, &c., श्चोतितुम् or श्च्योतितुम्, to ooze, trickle, flow, exude, drop, distil; to sprinkle, scatter, diffuse, shed, pour out; Pass. श्चुत्यते, Aor. अश्चोति, &c.: Caus. श्चोतयति, &c.; [cf. Goth. skevjan, skura; Angl. Sax. scur.]
47276: 2. श्चुत् or 2. श्च्युत्, त्, त्, त्, distilling, sprinkling, shedding, (at the end of comps., e. g. जल-श्°, shed-ding or sprinkling water.)
47277: श्चुतित or श्च्युतित, अस्, आ, अम्, oozed, exuded, issued, sprinkled, shed; oozing, dropping, flowing.
47278: श्चुतित्वा, ind. having oozed, having exuded or flowed.
47279: श्चोत or श्च्योत, अस्, m. oozing, trickling out, sprinkling, aspersion, pouring forth.
47280: श्चोतत् or श्च्योतत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, oozing, trickling, flowing; shedding. —श्च्योतन्-मयूख, अस्, आ, अम्, diffusing light.
47281: श्चोतन, अम्, n. the act of oozing, flowing; ex-udation.
47282: श्नथ् श्नथ्, cl. 1. P. श्नथति (2nd sing. Impv. Ved. श्नथिहि), शश्नाथ, अश्न-थीत् (श्नथिष्टम्, ‘you two have destroyed,’ Ṛg-veda VII. 99, 5), श्नथितुम्, Ved. to strike, injure, hurt, destroy, slay, kill: Caus. श्नथयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशिश्नथत् (अशिश्नत् = हिनस्ति, Ṛg-veda VII. 28, 3), to do violence, kill; Desid. शिश्नथिषति: Intens. शाश्नथ्यते, शाश्नत्ति; [cf. Goth. snithan, ‘to cut;’ Old Germ. snîdu; Angl. Sax. snidhan; Hib. slethe, ‘cutting, striking.’]
47283: श्नथयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. injuring, destroy-ing, destructive.
47284: श्नथित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hurt, wounded.
47285: श्नथितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who slays or kills, a smiter; killing, destroying, destructive, deadly, fatal.
47286: श्नम् श्नम्, (in grammar) a technical term for the verbal affix न, the characteristic sign of the seventh class of roots.
47287: श्ना श्ना, (in grammar) a technical term for the affix ना, the characteristic sign of the ninth class of roots.
47288: श्नु श्नु, (in grammar) a technical term for the affix नु, the characteristic sign of the fifth class of roots.
47289: श्मन् श्मन्, अ, n. (according to some ind.), the face, mouth; the body (according to Nirukta III. 5).
47290: श्मशा श्मशा, f., Ved. the channel of a river, (Sāy. = कुल्या); the brim or rim or edge of (the Soma) vessel.
47291: श्मशान श्मशान, अम्, n. (according to Ni-rukta III. 5. fr. श्म for श्मन् = शरीर + शान = शयन; or fr. श्म = शरीरम् + शृणाति or शम्-नाति; according to others = अश्म-शयन), ‘a place of repose for bodies, place for destroying bodies,’ a cemetery, sepulchre, burning or burial-ground, (पारे-श्मशानम्, beyond the cemetery); = ब्रह्म-रन्-ध्र, q. v. —श्मशान-काली, f., N. of a female evil spirit or form of Durgā (= कालिका). —श्मशान-गोचर, अस्, आ, अम्, frequenting burning-grounds, employed in places for burning the dead, (Manu XI. 39.) —श्मशान-निवासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, dwelling in burial-grounds, a ghost, spectre. —श्मशान-भाज्, क्, m. ‘inhabiting burial-grounds,’ epithet of Śiva. —श्मशान-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, abiding in burial-grounds or cemeteries, a ghost, spectre. —श्मशान-वाट, अस्, m. a cemetery-enclosure, burying-ground. —श्मशान-वासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, dwelling in cemeteries, a ghost, spectre; (ई), m. epithet of Śiva; (इनी), f. epithet of Kālī or Durgā. —श्मशान-वेश्मन्, आ, m. ‘inhabiting cemeteries,’ epithet of Śiva or Mahā-deva; a ghost. —श्मशान-वैराग्य, अम्, n. mo-mentary despondency or abandonment of worldly desire at the sight of a cemetery. —श्मशान-शूल, अस्, अम्, m. n. an impaling stake in a cemetery. —श्मशान-साधन, अम्, n. magical rites per-formed in a cemetery to obtain control over evil spirits. —श्मशानाग्नि (°न-अग्°), इस्, m. the fire of a burning-ground. —श्मशानालय (°न-आल्°), अस्, m. ‘cemetery-house,’ a cemetery. —श्मशानालय-वासिनी (°न-आल्°), f. ‘inhabiting cemeteries,’ epithet of Kālī or Durgā.
47292: श्मश्रु श्मश्रु, उ, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. V. 28. and Nirukta III. 5. fr. श्मन्, ‘the face,’ + rt. श्रि), ‘growing on the face,’ the beard. —श्म-श्रु-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose beard has grown. —श्मश्रु-प्रवृद्धि, इस्, f. the growth of a beard. —श्मश्रु-मुखी, f. ‘beard-faced,’ a woman with a beard (= पालि, पाली). —श्मश्रु-वर्धक, अस्, m. ‘a beard-cutter,’ a barber.
47293: श्मश्रुल, अस्, आ, अम्, having a beard, bearded, one who lets his beard grow.
47294: श्मश्रूयमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being as if bearded, having something like a beard.
47295: श्मसि श्मसि, Ved. for उश्मसि, fr. rt. वश्, q. v., (Sāy. = कामयामहे, we desire, Ṛg-veda II. 31, 6.)
47296: श्मील् श्मील् (also written स्मील्; cf. rt. मील्), cl. 1. P. श्मीलति, श्मीलितुम्, to wink, contract the eyelids; to twinkle.
47298: श्मीलित, अस्, आ, अम्, winked, blinked; (अम्), n. a wink, winking.
47299: श्मे श्मे, ind. an abbreviation for पार्थु-रश्मे, (see पार्थुरश्म।)
47300: श्यत् श्यत्। See under rt. शो।
47301: श्यन् श्यन्, (in grammar) a technical term for the syllable य or characteristic sign of the fourth class of roots.
47302: श्यान श्यान, &c. See under rt. श्यै, col. 3.
47303: श्यापर्ण श्यापर्ण, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family; (अस्, आ, अम्), belonging to the Śyāparṇa family.
47304: श्यापर्णीय, अस्, m. a man belonging to the Śyāparṇa race.
47305: श्यापर्णेय, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. VI. 2, 37.
47306: श्याम श्याम, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. श्यै or connected with rt. श्वि; cf. श्येत, श्वेत), black or dark-coloured, dark-blue, dark-brown, brown; dark-green, green; dark, shady, dusky; (अस्), m. black, brown, green (the colour); a cloud; the Kokila or Indian cuckoo; a sacred fig-tree at Prayāga or Allahabad; a kind of plant (= वृद्-ध-दारक); epithet of various other trees and plants (= पीलु; = श्यामाक; = दमनक; = गन्-ध-तृण); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a Vedic Caraṇa, (a subdivision of the Maitrāyaṇīyas); the thorn-apple, Datura Metel; N. of a son of Śūra; (आ), f. night; shade, shadow; a dark woman; a woman who has not borne children; another kind of woman (de-scribed as from eight to sixteen years of age, resem-bling in complexion the blossom of the Priyaṅgu or in shape its slender stalk); a form of Durgā (much worshipped by the Tāntrikas); a cow; a small sing-ing bird with black plumage (commonly called Śāmā, Turdus Macrourus); the female of the Indian cuckoo; a kind of plant (= प्रियङ्गु); turmeric; the sacred basil; the climbing-plant Ichnocarpus or Echites Frutescens (= शारिवा); indigo (= नीलिका); a kind of dark creeper (= कृष्ण-शारिवा); epithet of various other plants and shrubs (= कृष्णा; = वागुजी; = गुडूची; = गुग्गुलु; = सोम-लता; = कृष्ण-त्रिवृता; = गुन्द्रा; = कस्तूरी; = वट-पत्त्री; = वन्दा; = नील-पुनर्णवा; = नील-दूर्वा; = पिप्पली; = शिंशपा; = श्यामाक); epi-thet of the river Yamunā or Jumnā; the seed of the lotus, = पद्म-वीज; (अम्), n. black pepper; sea-salt; [cf. Gr. κύανο-ς; Lith. sze†mas; Hib. ciar, ‘dark-brown, black.’] —श्याम-कण्ठ, अस्, m. ‘black-throated, blue-throated,’ a peacock; a kind of small bird; an epithet of Śiva; [cf. नील-कण्ठ।] —श्याम-कन्दा, f. a kind of plant (= अति-विषा). —श्याम-कर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, black-eared; (अस्), m. a horse suitable for a horse-sacrifice. —श्याम-काण्डा, f. a kind of Dūrvā grass (= गण्ड-दूर्वा). —श्याम-ग्रन्थि, इस्, f. = श्याम-काण्डा. —श्याम-ता, f. or श्याम-त्व, अम्, n. blackness, brownness, darkness. —श्याम-देव, अस्, m. a proper N. —श्याम-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘black-leaved,’ the Tamāla tree. —श्याम-भास्, आस्, आस्, आस्, of a brilliant black, glossy black. —श्याम-लता, f. the climbing-plant Ichnocarpus or Echites Fru-tescens. —श्याम-शवल, औ, m. du. Yama's two watch-dogs, (see शवल।) —श्याम-सुन्दर, अस्, m. ‘dark and beautiful,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa. —श्या-माङ्ग (°म-अङ्°), अस्, ई, अम्, black-bodied, dark-bodied, black; (अस्), m. the planet Mercury or its regent. —श्यामा-पूजा, f. the worship of Śyāmā or Durgā (on the new moon of the month Kārttika). —श्यामाम्ली (°म-अम्°), f. a kind of shrub (= नी-लाम्ली). —श्यामा-रहस्य, अम्, n., N. of a work. —श्यामी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make black or dark-coloured. —श्यामी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become black or dark-blue.
47307: श्यामक, अस्, m. a kind of edible grain, (Panicum Frumentaceum or Colonum); a gramineous plant; (अम्), n. a kind of grass (= रोहिष-तृण).
47308: श्यामल, अस्, आ, अम्, blackish, black, dark-blue, brownish, dusky; (अस्), m. black (the colour); black pepper; the sacred fig-tree; a large bee; (आ), f., N. of Durgā or Pārvatī; epithet of various plants (= अश्व-गन्धा; = कट-भी; = जम्बु; = कस्-तूरी). —श्यामल-चूडा, f. a kind of shrub (= गुञ्जा). —श्यामलेक्षु (°ल-इक्°), उस्, m. a sort of dark sugar-cane.
47309: श्यामलिका, f. the indigo plant (= नीली).
47311: श्यामाय, Nom. A. श्यामायते, -यितुम्, to be-come black or dark-blue or green, to prove impure (as gold).
47312: श्यामायनि, इस्, m., N. of a teacher of the Yajur-veda.
47313: श्यामायनीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a Vedic Caraṇa.
47314: श्यामायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, growing dark or dusk, becoming dusky.
47315: श्यामिका, f. blackness, impurity, alloy (of metals &c.).
47316: श्यामित, अस्, आ, अम्, blackened, turned or be-come black; darkened, discoloured.
47317: श्याव, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (connected with श्याम), brown, bay, of a brown or dark-brown colour, dark, dusky, livid; drawn by bay horses (said of chariots, Ved.); (अस्), m. brown (the colour); a proper N.; (आस्), m. pl. the horses of the Sun; (ई), f., Ved. night (= रात्रि, Naigh. I. 7); [cf. Russ. sivyĭ, ‘dark-grey.’] —श्याव-तैल, अस्, m. ‘having dark-brown oil,’ the mango tree. —श्याव-दत्, अन्, अती, अत्, or श्याव-दन्त or श्याव-दन्तक, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has naturally brown or discoloured teeth, brown-toothed, black-toothed; (according to some the latter two words may mean ‘having a little tooth growing between or over the two front teeth.’) —श्यावाश्व (°व-अश्°), अस्, m. ‘having brown or bay horses,’ N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi, (an Ātreya and author of several hymns in the fifth, eighth, and ninth Maṇḍalas of the Ṛg-veda.) —श्यावाश्वि, इस्, m. a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Andhīgu.
47318: श्यावक, अस्, आ, अम्, brown, bay; (अस्), m., Ved., N. of a person under the especial protection of Indra; (आस्), m. pl. the horses of the Sun.
47319: श्याल श्याल, अस्, m. (also written स्याल), a wife's brother, brother-in-law; a proper N.; (ई), f. a wife's sister; [cf. Gr. ἀέλιοι, εἰλιόνες.] —श्याल-नामन्, आ, &c., called after the name of a brother-in-law.
47320: श्यालक, अस्, m. a wife's brother; a poor or miserable brother-in-law; (अकी), f. a wife's sister; sister-in-law.
47323: श्येत श्येत, अस्, ता or श्येनी, अम् (probably connected with श्वेत), white, of a white colour; (अस्), m. white (the colour). —श्येत-कोलक, अस्, m. the Saphara fish, Cyprinus Saphore (commonly called Puṃṭī).
47324: श्येन, अस्, m. white (the colour); whiteness, paleness; a hawk, falcon, bird of prey; ‘hawk-like conduct,’ violence; a horse (Ved.); a particular sacri-ficial ceremony or imprecatory rite; N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 188); (ई), f. white, (see above under श्येत); a female hawk; N. of a daughter of Kaśyapa (regarded as the mother of hawks); a woman (described as resembling a lily-leaf); a species of the Tṛṣṭubh metre. —श्येन-कपोतीय, अम्, n. the story of the hawk and pigeon; [cf. शिवि।] —श्येन-करण, अम्, n. or श्येन-करणिका, f. acting like a hawk (i. e. rashly or desperately); burning on a separate funeral pile. —श्येन-घण्टा, f. a kind of plant (= दन्ती)। —श्येन-चित्, त्, m. a hawk-feeder, hawk-keeper, falconer; a receptacle shaped like a hawk (for sacri-ficial fire &c.) —श्येन-जित्, त्, m. a proper N. —श्येनजिद्-आख्यान, अम्, n., N. of an episode in the Mahā-bhārata. —श्येन-जीविन्, ई, m. one who lives by selling or training hawks, a falconer. —श्ये-न-पत्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. going like a hawk or going as fast as a horse. —श्येनोपदेश (°न-उप्°), अस्, m. recommendation or injunction to women to burn on a separate funeral pile.
47325: श्येनिका, f. a kind of metre.
47326: श्यैत, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family; (अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.
47327: श्यैनम्पाता, f. (fr. श्येन + पात), hawking, hunting, the chase.
47328: श्यै श्यै, cl. 1. A. श्यायते, शश्ये, श्यास्-यते, अश्यास्त, श्यातुम्, to go, move; to coagulate, be congealed, freeze; to dry up, wither: Pass. श्यायते: Caus. श्यापयति, -यितुम्: Desid. शिश्यासते: Intens. शाश्यायते, शाश्येति, शाश्याति।
47329: शीत, अस्, आ, अम्। See p. 1010, col. 2.
47330: शीन, अस्, आ, अम्। See p. 1010, col. 3.
47331: श्यान, अस्, आ, अम्, gone; coagulated, congealed; viscous, thick, sticky, adhesive (as clarified butter); shrunk up, shrunk; (अम्), n. smoke. —श्यान-पुलिन, अस्, आ, अम्, having shrunk or dry sand-banks (as a river in the hot season).
47332: श्योणाक श्योणाक or श्योनाक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. श्यै), the plant Bignonia or Calosanthes Indica, (see शोणक।)
47333: श्रङ्क् श्रङ्क् (also written श्लङ्क्, स्रङ्क्), cl. 1. A. श्रङ्कते, शश्रङ्के, श्रङ्कि-तुम्, to go, move, creep.
47334: श्रङ्ग् श्रङ्ग् (also written श्लङ्ग्, श्वङ्ग्, स्वङ्ग्), cl. 1. P. श्रङ्गति, &c., to go, move; to shake (?).
47335: श्रण् श्रण्, cl. 1. P. श्रणति, &c., cl. 10. P. (or Caus.) श्राणयति, श्रणयति, यितुम्, Aor. अशिश्रणत् and अशश्राणत्, to give, grant, present.
47336: श्रत् श्रत्, ind. (a kind of prefix combined or compounded with rt. 1. धा, and in the Veda with rt. 1. कृ, and generally implying) faith, trust, belief, (enumerated among the सत्य-नामानि in Naigh. III. 10; Sāy. श्रत् = सत्यानि, Ṛg-veda VIII. 75, 2; cf. Lat. cred in cred-o.)
47337: श्रद्-दधत्, अत्, अती, अत्, having faith; trusting, believing; respecting, venerating.
47338: श्रद्-दधान, अस्, आ, अम्, having faith, &c. (= श्रद्-दधत्); a believer. —श्रद्दधान-ता, f. faith, (Manu VII. 86.)
47339: श्रद्-ध, अस्, आ, अम्, having faith, believing in, trusting; (आ), f. faith, belief, trust, confidence, (said to be also अम्, n.); belief in the Śāstras or divine revelation; calmness or composure of mind; inti-macy; respect, reverence; hope, wish, vehement desire, the longing of a pregnant woman; purity, (the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 151. is attributed to Śraddhā Kāmāyanī.) —श्रद्धा-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done with faith. —श्रद्धा-जाड्य, अम्, n. blind or obsti-nate adherence to one's faith. —श्रद्धा-देव, अस्, m., Ved. epithet of Manu; [cf. श्राद्ध-देव।] —श्रद्धान्वित (°धा-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with faith, faithful, believing. —श्रद्धा-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. having a faithful mind, faithful-hearted. —श्रद्धा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, full of faith, believing. —श्रद्धा-युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having faith, believing. —श्रद्धा-रहित, अस्, आ, अम्, de-prived of faith, distrusting, disbelieving. —श्रद्धा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having faith, trusting, believing. —श्रद्धा-विरहित, अस्, आ, अम्, void of faith, destitute of belief. —श्रद्धा-समन्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, = श्रद्धान्वित above.
47340: श्रद्-धा (cf. perhaps cred-o for cred-do), cl. 3. P. A. -दधाति, -धत्ते, -धातुम्, to place con-fidence in, have faith in, trust, believe, (श्रद्धातुम् अर्हः, worthy to be believed, trustworthy); to respect.
47341: श्रद्-धातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who believes, a believer.
47342: श्रद्धालु, उस्, उस्, उ, disposed to trust, faithful, believing; desirous, wishing; (उस्), f. a pregnant woman longing for anything.
47343: श्रद्-धेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be trusted, reliable, worthy of confidence. —श्रद्धेय-ता, f. trust-worthiness.
47344: श्रथ् श्रथ् or श्रन्थ् (connected with rt. श्लथ्, of which it appears to be an older form; cf. also rt. ग्रथ्), cl. 1. 9. 10. P. श्र-थति, श्रन्थति, श्रथ्नाति (Ved. also A. श्रथ्-नीते), श्राथयति, श्रन्थयति, शश्रन्थ (or श-श्राथ, 3rd pl. शश्रन्थुः or श्रेथुः, Pāṇ. I. 2, 6), श्रन्थिष्यति, अश्रन्थीत् (Ved. forms शिश्रथत्, शिश्रथस्, शिश्रथन्तु, श्रथ्नास्), श्रथितुम्, श्रन्थितुम्, श्राथयितुम्, to untie, loosen, let loose, discharge, liberate, set free, release, remove; to hurt, injure, destroy, kill, (usually cl. 9. or श्र-थति for श्नथति, cf. rt. श्नथ्); to bind, tie, connect, arrange [cf. rt. ग्रथ्]; to strive eagerly, endeavour, use exertion, (in this sense only cl. 10); to delight repeatedly, amuse; cl. 1. 9. A. श्रन्थते, श्रथ्नीते (in neut. sense or Pass. refl.), to be loosened or dissolved or untied, to be loose; to be weak; to be shallow; cl. 10. P. A. श्रथ-यति, -ते, -यितुम्, to loosen, release (Ved.); to relax efforts; to be loose or relaxed, be weak or infirm: Caus. श्रन्थयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अशश्रन्थत्, -त, to cause to loosen, release, &c.; [cf. Gr. κλώθω, κάλαθος; Lat. crates, rete, res-tis (for ret-tis); Goth. af-hlathan; Old Germ. hla-dan, hlast; Angl. Sax. hladan, hlœst.]
47345: श्रथन, अम्, n. the act of untying, loosening; destroying, killing; tying, stringing, binding, con-necting; making effort, exertion; delighting repeat-edly.
47347: श्रथ्नान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. loosening, untying.
47348: श्रन्थ, अस्, m. loosening, liberating; looseness, flaccidity; tying, binding, stringing together; N. of Viṣṇu.
47349: श्रन्थन, अम्, आ, n. f. the act of loosening, untying; tying, binding, stringing together (flowers &c.); killing, destroying.
47350: श्रन्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, loosed, let loose; strung, connected, bound together; hurt, injured, killed; overcome, overpowered; delighted.
47352: श्रद्ध श्रद्-ध, श्रद्-धा, &c. See under श्रत्।
47354: श्रम् श्रम्, cl. 4. P. श्राम्यति (sometimes also A. -ते), शश्राम, अश्रमत् or अश्रमीत्, श्रमितुम्, to make effort, exert one's self, take pains; to perform acts of penance or austerity, mortify the body; to be wearied or fatigued; to be distressed or pained: Pass. श्रम्यते, Aor. अश्रमि: Caus. श्रमयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशिश्र-मत्; [cf. perhaps Angl. Sax. hearm; Old Germ. ramen, ramjan.]
47355: श्रम, अस्, m. exertion, labour, toil, taking pains; penance, austerity, mortification of the body; hard study, (श्रमं कृ, to make exertion, study); exercise, military exercise, drill; weariness, fatigue; distress, pain. —श्रम-कर्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, worn out by toil; weighed down with fatigue. —श्रम-जल, अम्, n. ‘toil-water,’ perspiration. —श्रम-मोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, bewildered by exertion, para-lysed or stupefied by fatigue. —श्रम-साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be accomplished by labour. —श्रम-सिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, accomplished by labour or exer-tion. —श्रम-स्थान, अम्, n. ‘labour-place,’ a place for work or exercise, workshop, drilling-place. —श्र-माम्बु (°म-अम्°), उ, n. ‘toil-water,’ perspiration; [cf. श्रम-जल।] —श्रमार्त (°म-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, overcome with fatigue, wearied.
47356: श्रमण, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, making effort or exertion, toiling, labouring; following a low or menial busi-ness; base, vile, bad; (अस्), m. one who performs acts of penance and austerity, an ascetic, devotee, one who restrains his passions and mortifies his body; a religious mendicant; a Buddhist ascetic; a beggar; (आ, ई), f. a woman of low caste or business; a female mendicant, (कुमार-श्रमणा, a female mendicant even in girlhood); a handsome woman; Bengal madder (= मञ्जिष्ठा); another plant (= मुण्-डीरी); Indian spikenard (= जटा-मांसी).
47357: श्रमणाय, Nom. A. श्रमणायते, -यितुम्, to become a Śramaṇa, become a beggar, be reduced to beggary.
47358: श्रमयु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. weary, overcome with fatigue.
47359: श्रमिन्, ई, इणी, इ, making great efforts, laborious, diligent; undergoing fatigue or weariness; wearying, tiring.
47360: श्रान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, wearied, fatigued, tired, ex-hausted, distressed; calmed, tranquil; (अस्), m. one whose passions are subdued, an ascetic. —श्रान्त-संवाहन, अस्, आ, अम्, soothing a weary person (by rubbing or shampooing his limbs); relieving or tending the wearied (by offering a seat &c.).
47361: श्रान्ति, इस्, f. fatigue, weariness, exhaustion.

47376: श्राद्ध श्राद्ध, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. श्रद्-धा, see श्रद्-ध), faithful, believing; (अम्), n., N. of a kind of funeral rite or ceremony in honour of the departed spirits of dead relatives observed with great, strictness at various fixed periods and on oc-casions of rejoicing as well as mourning, (these cere-monies are of three principal kinds, 1. Nitya, i. e. general and constant, in honour of the Pitṛs or deceased ancestors and progenitors collectively [also called पार्वण, अष्टक, q. q. v. v.], when three Piṇḍas or balls of meal [see पिण्ड] and water are offered to three paternal ancestors and three maternal forefathers [see पितृ]: 2. Naimittika, i. e. occasional and special, as, for instance, in behalf of a parent or some one relative recently deceased [called also एकोद्दिष्ट, q. v.]; the object being twofold, viz. first, the re-embodying of his soul in some kind of form after burning his corpse; secondly, the raising him from the regions of the atmosphere, where he would otherwise roam among demons and evil spirits, to a particular heaven above, where he is, as it were, deified among the shades of departed kins-men; the offering of the funeral Piṇḍa or ball of meal is in this case the office of the nearest male kinsman, and confers the title to any property that may be inherited: 3. Kāmya, i. e. voluntary and performed apparently by way of supererogation for the greater benefit of deceased ancestors or for ob-taining increase of religious merit, &c.: other Śrād-dha ceremonies and oblations appear to have more reference to the living than the dead, and to be performed either for the sake of पुष्टि and वृद्धि, ‘increase of prosperity,’ &c., or as thank-offerings on various joyful occasions, such as the birth of a son, when gifts and food are offered to the living relations and assisting Brāhmans present: there is also an important Śrāddha, called Daiva, in honour of the Viśva-devas or Viśve Devāḥ, ‘deities collectively’ [see विश्व]: the Śrāddha to a recently deceased relative should be offered on the day after mourning expires, and at intervals during twelve successive months, and afterwards on all anniversaries of his death; that to the Pitṛs collectively should take place on the dark fortnight of a lunation as well as at various other seasons, different names being given to the various Śrāddhas according to the times and objects of their performance, see अष्टक, एकादशी, मासिक, अन्व्-आहार्य, दश-पिण्ड-श्राद्ध, प्रेत-श्राद्ध, सपिण्डन, महालय, वृद्धि-श्राद्-ध, शुद्धि, नान्दी-मुख); gifts or offerings at a Śrāddha. —श्राद्ध-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, or श्राद्-ध-कर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who performs a Śrād-dha, the offerer of an obsequial oblation. —श्राद्ध-कर्मन्, अ, n. a Śrāddha rite, a funeral ceremony. —श्राद्ध-कल्प, अस्, m., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Yajur-veda (ascribed to Kātyāyana). —श्राद्ध-कल्प-भाष्य, अम्, n. a commentary on the Śrāddha-kalpa (ascribed to Gobhila). —श्राद्ध-कल्प-लता, f., N. of a work by Nanda-paṇḍita. —श्राद्ध-कृत्, त्, m. the performer of a funeral rite. —श्राद्ध-क्रिया, f. a Śrāddha ceremony, funeral rite. —श्राद्ध-चन्द्रिका, f. ‘Śrāddha-elucidation,’ N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m. ‘Śrāddha-gem,’ N. of a work by Śiva-rāma on funeral rites. —श्राद्ध-तत्त्व, अम्, n. ‘Śrāddha-truth,’ N. of two portions of Raghu-nandana's Smṛti-tattva (called respectively the Chandoga-śrāddha-tattva and the Yajurvedi-śrāddha-tattva). —श्राद्ध-तत्त्व-टीका, f., N. of a commentary by Kāśi-rāma on the Chandoga-śrāddha-tattva. —श्राद्ध-त्व, अम्, n. faithfulness; the being a Śrāddha. —श्राद्-ध-द, अस्, m. the offerer of a Śrāddha. —श्राद्-ध-दिन, अस्, अम्, m. n. the day of a Śrāddha, the anniversary of the death of a near relative. —श्राद्-ध-दीप-कलिका, f., N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-दीपिका, f. ‘Śrāddha-elucidation,’ N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-देव, अस्, m. any god presiding over funeral rites; a Viśva-deva; Yama (lord of the dead); Manu Vaivasvata (brother of Yama; in a former mundane age he was Manu Satya-vrata). —श्राद्ध-देवता, f. any deity presiding over obsequial rites; a Viśva-deva; a Pitṛ or progenitor; Yama. —श्राद्ध-पङ्क्ति, इस्, f., N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a work by Nīla-kaṇṭha. —श्राद्ध-प्रदीप, अस्, m., N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, or श्राद्ध-भोक्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, eating food prepared at a Śrāddha, a de-ceased ancestor. —श्राद्ध-मयूख, अस्, m. ‘Śrāddha-light,’ N. of a part of Nīla-kaṇṭha's Bha-gavad-bhāskara. —श्राद्ध-विवेक, अस्, m. ‘Śrād-dha-investigation,’ N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-शाक, अम्, n. a kind of pot-herb (= काल-शाक). —श्राद्-ध-शिष्ट, अम्, n. what remains at a Śrāddha, food that has been presented to the Pitṛs. —श्राद्ध-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘Śrāddha-compilation,’ N. of a work. —श्राद्ध-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of certain aphorisms by Kātyāyana on the rites to be per-formed at anniversaries of the death of near relatives. —श्राद्ध-स्तवक, अस्, m. a chapter on Śrāddhas. —श्राद्धोपयोगिन् (°ध-उप्°), ई, इनी, इ, service-able or appropriate for Śrāddhas.
