52819: सौगम्य सौगम्य, अम्, n. (fr. सु-गम), easiness of access, easiness of attainment, facility.
52820: सौचि सौचि, इस्, m. (fr. सूचि; cf. सूचिक), one who lives by his needle, a tailor.
52822: सौचीक सौचीक, अस्, m. a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Agni.
52823: सौजन्य सौजन्य, अम्, n. (fr. सु-जन), goodness, generosity, kindness, compassion, bene-volence, clemency; friendship.
52824: सौजात सौजात, अस्, m. (fr. सु-जात), N. of a Ṛṣi.
52826: सौति सौति, इस्, m. (fr. 2. सूत), N. of Karṇa, (so called from having been brought up by the charioteer [सूत] Adhi-ratha, see कर्ण।)
52827: 1. सौत्य, अम्, n. the office of a charioteer.
52828: सौत्य 2. सौत्य, अस्, &c. (fr. सुत्या), relating to Soma-pressing, sacrificial.
52829: सौत्र सौत्र, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सूत्र), belong-ing to a thread or string, having a thread, &c.; belonging to a Sūtra, mentioned or declared in Sūtras, according to rule or precept, preceptive, for-mulary; (अस्), m. a Brāhman; an artificial root occurring in grammatical Sūtras only and not capable of conversion into a verb, but used to form deriva-tive nouns.
52830: सौत्रान्तिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of one of the four great schools or systems of Buddhism, (see सौगत; they are said to admit the authority of the Buddhist Sūtras but not of the Abhi-dharma.)
52831: सौत्रामणी सौत्रामणी, f. (probably fr. सु-त्रामन्), a particular sacrifice (one of the seven Havir-yajñas; it is described as a substitute for the Soma sacrifice, spirituous liquors and milk being taken instead of Soma, and both liquids placed in the Soma vessels; animals are also immolated, one to the Aśvins, one to Sarasvatī, one to Indra, and one to Bṛhaspati; in Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa XII. 8, 3, 31. it is said that every one who is consecrated by the Sautrāmaṇī enters among the gods and is born in the next world [सर्व-तनूः] with his entire body).
52832: सौदर्य सौदर्य, अम्, n. (fr. सोदर), bro-therhood; (अस्, आ, अम्), having brotherhood with (at the end of a comp.).
52833: सौदामनी सौदामनी, f. (fr. सु-दामन्), lightning or a particular kind of lightning; N. of an Apsaras of Indra's heaven; of part of the Su-dāman mountain (according to some).
52834: सौदामिनी, f. a particular kind of lightning; lightning (in general); N. of an Apsaras of Indra's heaven; N. of a city or country.
52836: सौदायिक सौदायिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सु-दाय), that which is given to a woman at her marriage by her father or mother or any relative and which there-fore becomes her own property; relating to such a present; (अम्), n. a nuptial gift or present (as de-scribed above).
52837: सौदास सौदास, अस्, m. (fr. सु-दास), N. of a king of the solar race (a descendant of Ikṣvāku and Sagara in the thirteenth generation, son of king Su-dāsa, and also called Mitra-saha and Kalmāṣa-pāda).
52838: सौध सौध, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सुधा), relating or belonging to nectar, having nectar; having plaster; plastered, stuccoed; (अस्), m. a kind of plant, = दुग्ध-पाषाण; (अम्), n. a plastered or white-washed mansion; any great mansion or house; a palace, (also अस्, m. according to some); silver; opal (according to some). —सौध-कार, अस्, m. a plasterer, whitewasher; the builder or maker of a palace. —सौध-वास, अस्, m. a palatial dwelling.
52839: सौधन्य सौधन्य, अस्, &c. (probably fr. सु-धन), epithet of certain Dharmāḥ or laws.
52840: सौधन्वन सौधन्वन, अस्, m. (fr. सु-धन्-वन्), a son or descendant of Su-dhanvan.
52841: सौधातकि सौधातकि, इस्, m. (fr. सु-धातृ), a patronymic, (Pāṇ. IV. 1, 97); N. of a hermit (pupil of Vālmīki).
52842: सौधार सौधार, अस्, m. (according to some) one of the fourteen parts or divisions of a drama, (a doubtful word.)
52843: सौधाल सौधाल, अम्, n. (probably to be connected with सौध, p. 1138), a temple of Śiva.
52844: सौन सौन, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सूना), belonging or relating to a slaughter-house or to butchery, &c.; (अम्), n. butcher's meat; [cf. शौन।]
52845: सौनधर्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the law or rule of butchery,’ a state of deadly hostility.
52846: सौनिक, अस्, m. a butcher, vender of the flesh of beasts or birds.
52847: सौनन्द सौनन्द, अम्, n. the club of Bala-rāma.
52848: सौनन्दिन्, ई, m. ‘having Saunanda,’ epithet of Bala-rāma, (see p. 675.)
52849: सौन्दर्य सौन्दर्य, अम्, n. (fr. सुन्दर), beauty, loveliness, handsomeness, gracefulness, ele-gance. —सौन्दर्य-लहरी, f., N. of a mystical poem ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya (= आनन्द-लहरी).
52850: सौपन्थ्य सौपन्थ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. सु-पथ, according to some), connected with a good road.
52851: सौपर्ण सौपर्ण, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सु-पर्ण or सु-पर्णी, q. v.), belonging or relating to Su-parṇa or Su-parṇī; (अम्), n. dry ginger; the emerald; N. of a Vedic story which relates the transformation of the metres into birds that they might fetch the Soma from heaven; (ई), f. a kind of creeper (= पाताल-गरुडी).
52852: सौपर्णेय, अस्, m. a metronymic of Garuḍa; (ई), f. a female descendant of Su-parṇa; (आस्), pl. epithet of the metres (regarded as children of Su-parṇī).
52853: सौप्तिक सौप्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सुप्त), con-nected with or relating to sleep, somnolent, som-niferous, &c.; (अम्), n. a nocturnal combat; a night-attack, attack on sleeping men. —सौप्तिक-पर्वन्, अ, n., N. of the tenth book of the Mahā-bhārata (in which is described how the three surviving Kuru warriors, Aśvatthāman, Kṛta-varman, and Kṛpa, after the destruction of their army, determined on attacking the camp of the Pāṇḍavas by night and murdering them while asleep; this they accordingly did, Aśvatthāman entering the camp stealthily and, with the assistance of the god Śiva, slaughtering thousands, while the two others stood at the gate and killed all who attempted to escape; the whole Pāṇḍava army was thus destroyed, except the five Pāṇḍu princes themselves, with Kṛṣṇa and Sātyaki, who were stationed at some distance from the camp; a messenger having escaped conveyed the news to Yudhi-ṣṭhira, who, with his brothers and Draupadī, then returned to the camp and bewailed their slaughtered kindred).
52854: सौबल सौबल, अस्, m. a patronymic of Śakuni (as son of Su-bala, king of Gāndhāra).
52855: सौबली, f. a patronymic of Gāndhārī (daughter of Su-bala and wife of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra).
52857: सौभ सौभ, अम्, n. (for शौभ), N. of Hari-ścandra's city (suspended in mid-air); N. of a town of the Śālvas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people. —सौभ-पति, इस्, or सौभ-राज, अस्, m. the king of Saubha or of the Saubhas.
52858: सौभकि सौभकि, इस्, m., N. of Drupada.
52859: सौभग सौभग, अम्, n. (fr. सु-भग), good luck, happiness; prosperity, riches, wealth. —सौभग-त्व, अम्, n. a state of prosperity, hap-piness.
52860: सौभाग्य, अम्, n. auspiciousness, good fortune, fortunateness, good luck; blessedness; beauty, grace, charm; the happy and auspicious state of wife-hood (as opposed to widowhood); affection, favour; con-gratulations, good wishes; the fourth of the astor-nomical Yogas; red lead; borax (टङ्कण). —सौ-भाग्य-काण्ड, N. of part of the Atharva-veda. —सौभाग्य-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m. a particular drug or medicine compounded of various medicaments. —सौभाग्य-चिह्न, अम्, n. any mark of good fortune or blessedness; any sign or token of the blessed state of wife-hood (e. g. red pigment on the forehead, the marriage string, &c.). —सौभाग्य-तन्तु, उस्, m. the marriage string (which is cast round the neck of the bride by the bridegroom at the wedding and worn till widowhood). —सौ-भाग्य-तृतीया, f. the third day of the light half of the month Bhādra. —सौभाग्य-देवता, f. an auspicious or tutelary deity. —सौभाग्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing good fortune or blessedness, auspicious, fortunate; (अती), f. a married and un-widowed woman. —सौभाग्यवत्-ता, f. or सौ-भाग्यवत्-त्व, अम्, n. auspiciousness, prosperity. —सौभाग्य-वायन, अम्, n. auspicious offerings of sweetmeats, &c. —सौभाग्य-सुन्दरी-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa.
52861: सौभद्र सौभद्र, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सु-भद्रा), belonging or relating to Su-bhadrā, q. v.; (अस्), m. ‘son of Su-bhadrā,’ epithet of Abhimanyu; (अम्), n., scil. युद्ध, the war occasioned by the carrying off of Su-bhadrā, q. v.
52862: सौभद्रेय, अस्, m. a metronymic of Abhi-manyu; Beleric Myrobalan (= विभीतक).
52863: सौभर सौभर, अस्, m. a patronymic of Kuśika (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 127).
52864: सौभरि सौभरि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni (married to the fifty daughters of Māndhātṛ and father of 150 sons).
52865: सौभरी सौभरी, f. (fr. सोभरि), Ved. a verse composed by Sobhari.
52866: सौभागिनेय 1. सौभागिनेय, अस्, m. (fr. सु-भगा), the son of a favourite wife or of an honoured mother.
52867: सौभागिनेय 2. सौभागिनेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु-भागिनेय), belonging or relating to a good sister's son.
52869: सौभाञ्जन सौभाञ्जन, अस्, m. = सोभाञ्-जन, शोभाञ्जन, the tree Hyperanthera Moringa.
52870: सौभिक सौभिक, अस्, m. (for शौभिक), a juggler.
52871: सौभ्रात्र सौभ्रात्र, अम्, n. (fr. सु-भ्रातृ), good brotherhood, fraternity.
52872: सौमदत्ति सौमदत्ति, इस्, m. (fr. सोम-दत्त), a patronymic.
52873: सौमनस सौमनस, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. सु-मनस्), agreeable to the feelings, pleasing; relating to flowers, floral, flowery; (अस्), m., N. of the eighth day of the civil month (= कर्म-मास); (आ), f. the outer skin of the nutmeg, = जाती-पत्त्री; (ई), f., N. of the fifth night of the civil month; (अम्), n. benevolence, kindness; pleasure, satisfaction.
52874: सौमनस्य, अम्, n. satisfaction of mind, agree-ableness, enjoyment; a particular offering of flowers with holy texts placed in the hands of the priest at a Śrāddha.
52875: सौमनस्यायनी, f. the blossom of the Mālatī or great-flowering jasmine.
52876: सौमायन सौमायन, अस्, m. (fr. सोम), a patronymic of Budha; [cf. सौम्य।]
52877: सौमिक सौमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सोम), per-formed with Soma juice (said of an oblation or sacrifice), relating to the Soma juice; relating to Soma or the moon, lunar; (ई), f. a particular sacrifice performed on the day of full moon (= दीक्षणी-येष्टि).
52878: सौमित्र सौमित्र, अस्, m. (fr. सु-मित्रा), a metronymic of Lakṣmaṇa the younger brother of Rāma.
52879: सौमित्रि, इस्, m. = सौमित्र above; N. of a teacher of the Sāma-veda.
52880: सौमिल्ल सौमिल्ल, अस्, m., N. of a dramatic writer (mentioned in the Mālavikāgnimitra).
52881: सौमेचक सौमेचक, अम्, n. (probably fr. सु-मेचक), gold.
52882: सौमेधिक सौमेधिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 5. सु + मेधा), possessing supernatural knowledge or wis-dom; (अस्), m. a sage, seer.
52883: सौमेरुक सौमेरुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु-मेरु), belonging to or coming from Su-meru; (अम्), n. gold.
52884: सौम्य सौम्य, अस्, आ or मी, अम् (fr. सोम), belonging or relating to Soma or to the moon, sacred to Soma; having the nature or properties of Soma; resembling the moon; handsome, pleas-ing, good, mild, gentle, soft, benign, placid, (सौम्य, voc. c. ‘O gentle Sir,’ ‘O good Sir,’ used in address-ing another); auspicious; (अस्), m., N. of Budha or the planet Mercury (son of Soma); N. of the Vedic Ṛṣi Budha; a Brāhman (or the proper epithet by which he should be addressed, see Manu II. 125); N. of one of the nine Khaṇḍas or divisions of the earth or of Bharata-varṣa; epithet of the forty-third (or seventeenth) year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years; epithet of certain signs of the zodiac (viz. Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricornus); the Uḍumbara fig-tree; the Saumya penance, (see सौम्य-कृच्-छ्र); (in anatomy) the blood before it becomes red, serum; the gastric juice; = भास्वर (according to Śabda-k.); (आस्), m. pl., N. of the five stars in Orion's head, (also called इल्वल, q. v.); N. of a class of Pitṛs, (Manu III. 199); (आ), f., N. of Durgā; a particular metre; the moon-plant, (see सोम); various other plants, = मल्लिका; = शटी; = शाल-पर्णी; = गुञ्जा; = महिष-वल्ली; = महा-ज्योतिष्मती; = रुद्र-जटा; = महेन्द्र-वारुणी; (अम्), n., scil. अद्भुत, a particular kind of omen or prodigy (occurring in the Diva or sky). —सौम्य-कृच्छ्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. a kind of religious penance (described as subsisting for five days, severally, on sesamum, the water of boiled rice, butter-milk mixed with water, water, and parched grain, and fasting on the sixth day). —सौम्य-गन्धी, f. the Indian white rose. —सौम्य-ग्रह, अस्, m. an auspicious or benign planet (such as Mercury, Ju-piter, Venus, and the full moon). —सौम्य-ता, f. or सौम्य-त्व, अम्, n. gentleness, mildness, be-nignity, placidity; benevolence; beauty. —सौम्य-धातु, उस्, m. (according to Śabda-k. f.), the phlegmatic humor, phlegm. —सौम्य-नामन्, आ, म्नी, अ, having a soft or agreeable name (or one easily pronounced; see Manu III. 10). —सौम्य-वपुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, of an agreeable form. —सौम्य-वार, अस्, m. ‘Mercury's day,’ Wednesday. —सौम्यो-पचार (°य-उप्°), अस्, m. a mild or gentle remedy, mild measure or means of cure.
52885: सौयवस सौयवस, अस्, m. a son of Su-yavasa.
52887: सौयामि सौयामि, इस्, m. a proper N.
52888: सौर सौर, अस्, ई, अम् (in some senses fr. सूर, in others fr. सुर), belonging or relating to the sun, solar; sacred to Sūrya or the sun; celestial, divine; relating to spirituous liquor; (अस्), m. a worshipper of the sun; the planet Saturn [cf. सूर-सुत]; a solar month (consisting of thirty risings and settings of the sun or the period during which the sun is in one sign of the zodiac); a representation of a solar zodiacal sign used at marriage ceremonies; a solar day; N. of a Guru; the Tumburu plant; (ई), f. the wife of the sun; (अम्), n., N. of a col-lection of hymns addressed to Sūrya (extracted from the Ṛg-veda). —सौर-ज, अस्, m. ‘sun-born,’ the Tumburu plant. —सौर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —सौर-दिवस, अस्, m. a solar day. —सौर-नक्त, अम्, n. a particular reli-gious observance (accompanied with ceremonial ablu-tions, worship of the sun, &c.). —सौर-भुवन, अम्, n. = सूर्य-लोक, q. v. —सौर-मास, अस्, m. a solar month. —सौर-संवत्सर, अस्, m. a solar year. —सौर-संहिता, f., N. of part of the Skanda-Purāṇa. —सौर-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m., N. of one of five ancient astronomical Siddhāntas or text-books, (see सिद्धान्त, cf. सूर्य-स्°।) —सौर-सूक्त, अम्, n. a hymn addressed to Sūrya. —सौरोपपुराण (°र-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
52889: सौरक, N. of a town founded by Surendra.
52890: सौरसैन्धव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सुर-सिन्धु), belonging to the river Ganges, Gangetic; related to the Ganges (applicable as an epithet to Bhīṣma); (अस्), m. a horse of the Sun (in this sense com-pounded of सौर and सैन्धव, q. v.).
52891: सौरि, इस्, m., N. of the planet Saturn (as son of the Sun); the tree Asana (q. v.); the plant Āditya-bhaktā (q. v.). —सौरि-रत्न, अम्, n. a particular gem (sapphire).
52892: सौरिक, अस्, ई, अम्, celestial; spirituous, vinous; any-thing (such as money) due for spirits; (अस्), m. Saturn; heaven, paradise; a vender of spirituous liquor.
52893: सौरी, f. See above under सौर।
52894: सौरीय, अस्, ई, अम्, solar, belonging or suitable to the sun (= सूर्याय हित).
52895: सौरेय or सौरेयक, अस्, m. the white Barleria (a shrub bearing white flowers).
52896: सौर्य, अस्, ई, अम्, of or belonging to the sun, solar; (अस्), m. a patronymic of several Vedic Ṛṣis (authors of hymns in the Ṛg-veda).
52897: सौर्यायणि, इस्, or सौर्यायणिन्, ई, m. a de-scendant of Saurya.
52898: सौरथ सौरथ, अस्, m. (fr. सु-रथ), a hero.
52899: सौरभ सौरभ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु-रभि), fragrant; (अस्), m. a proper N.; (ई), f. a cow; a daughter of the cow Su-rabhi; (अम्), n. fragrance; saffron; N. of a commentary.
52900: सौरभक, अम्, n. a particular metre.
52901: सौरभेय, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to Su-rabhi; (अस्), m. an ox; (ई), f. a cow; the daughter of Su-rabhi. —सौरभेय-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work.
52902: सौरभ्य, अम्, n. fragrance, sweet-scentedness, odour; pleasingness, agreeableness, beauty; good cha-racter, good reputation, fame; (अस्), m., N. of Kuvera.
52903: सौरस सौरस, अस्, m., N. of a Vihāra founded by king Surendra.
52904: सौरसेन सौरसेन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people or district; (ई), f., scil. भाषा, the language spoken in the above district; [cf. शौरसेनी।]
52905: सौरसेय सौरसेय, अस्, m. (fr. सु-रसा), ‘off-spring of Su-rasā,’ epithet of Skanda.
52906: सौरस्य, अम्, n. (fr. सु-रस), well-flavoured-ness, tastiness, savoriness.
52907: सौराज्य सौराज्य, अम्, n. (fr. सु-राज), good government.
52908: सौराष्ट्र सौराष्ट्र, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. सु-राष्ट्र), belonging or relating to the district of Surāt; (अस्), m. the district of Surāt; the resin of the plant Boswellia Thurifera; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people inhabiting part of Bhārata-varṣa; (आ), f. a sort of fragrant earth, = तुवरी; (ई), f. a sort of fragrant earth found in Surāt; (अम्), n. a kind of amalgam of zinc and copper, bell-metal, brass. —सौ-राष्ट्र-देश, अस्, m. the country of Surāt. —सौ-राष्ट्र-मृत्तिका, f. Surāt earth.
52909: सौराष्ट्रक, अम्, n. a sort of white or bell-metal; a kind of amalgam of five metals (= पञ्च-लोह).
52910: सौराष्ट्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the dis-trict of Surāt; (अम्), n. a sort of poison, (according to some, of a kind of snake; according to others, a vegetable or mineral.)
52911: सौलभ सौलभ, आनि, n. pl. (fr. सु-लभ), N. of particular Brāhmaṇas.
52912: सौलभ्य, अम्, n. easiness of acquisition or at-tainment; feasibility, facility.
52913: सौल्विक सौल्विक, अस्, m. (for शौल्विक), a copper-smith.
52914: सौव 1. सौव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्व), relating to self or to one's own property; (अम्), n. an order, edict (according to some).
52915: सौवग्रामिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्व-ग्राम), be-longing or relating to one's own village.
52916: सौव 2. सौव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. स्वर्), belong-ing to heaven, being in heaven.
52917: सौवर सौवर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्वर), relat-ing to sound or to a note in music, produced or existing in a note; treating of accents.
52918: सौवर्चल सौवर्चल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु-वर्-चल or सु-वर्चला), belonging to Su-varcala or Su-varcalā, coming from the country called Su-varcala; (अम्), n. sochal salt (prepared by fusing fossil salt with myrobalan); natron, alkali.
52919: सौवर्ण सौवर्ण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु-वर्ण), made or consisting of gold, golden; weighing a Su-varṇa.
52921: सौवर्णिक, weighing a Su-varṇa (at the end of a comp., e. g. चतुः-स्°, weighing four Su-varṇas).
52922: सौवल्य सौवल्य, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people (also read सौशल्य, सौशुल्य).
52923: सौवश्व सौवश्व, अस्, m. (fr. स्व्-अश्व), a descendant of Sv-aśva.
52924: सौवश्वि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Sv-aśva.
52925: सौवश्व्य, अस्, m., Ved. the son of Sv-aśva; [cf. Pāṇ. IV. 1, 171.]
52926: सौवस्तिक सौवस्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्वस्ति), benedictive, salutatory; (अस्), m. a family Brāhman or priest.
52927: सौवाध्यायिक सौवाध्यायिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्वाध्याय), belonging or relating to sacred study.
52928: सौवास्तव सौवास्तव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु + वास्तु), having a good site, pleasantly situated.
52929: सौविद सौविद, अस्, m. (fr. सु-विद), a guard or attendant on the women's apartments.
52930: सौविदल्ल सौविदल्ल or सौविदल्लक, अस्, m. (fr. सु-विदल्ल), = सौविद above.
52931: सौविष्टकृत सौविष्टकृत, अस्, ई, अम्, dedi-cated or relating to Agni Sviṣṭa-kṛt.
52932: सौवीर सौवीर, अम्, n. (fr. सु-वीर), the fruit of the jujube; antimony; sour gruel; (अस्), m., N. of a district of country in the west of India con-nected with the country along the Indus (perhaps the district now inhabited by the Suirs); (आस्), m. pl. the people of Su-vīra; N. of a people inhabiting part of Bhārata-varṣa. —सौवीर-राज, अस्, m. a king of Sauvīra. —सौवीर-सार, अम्, n. antimony. —सौवीराञ्जन (°र-अञ्°), अम्, n. a kind of anti-mony or collyrium.
52933: सौवीरक, अस्, ई, अम्, of or belonging to Sauvīra; (अस्), m. an inhabitant of Sauvīra; a miserable Sau-vīra; N. of Jayad-ratha; the jujube tree; (अम्), n. sour barley-gruel, sour wheat-gruel.
52934: सौवीर्य, अम्, n. great heroism or fortitude.
52935: सौशील्य सौशील्य, अम्, n. (fr. सु-शील), ex-cellence of disposition, good morals.
52936: सौश्रवस सौश्रवस, अम्, n. (fr. सु-श्रवस्), celebrity, renown; (अस्), m. a patronymic.
52937: सौश्रुत सौश्रुत, आस्, m. pl. (fr. सु-श्रुत), N. of a family descended from Viśvā-mitra.
52938: सौषद्मन सौषद्मन, अस्, m. (fr. सु-षद्-मन्), a patronymic.
52939: सौष्ठव सौष्ठव, अम्, n. (fr. सु-ष्ठु), ex-cellence, superior goodness or beauty, extreme skil-fulness, cleverness; excess (of anything); lightness, suppleness, fleetness, a particular division of dramatic composition.
52940: सौस्नातिक सौस्नातिक, अस्, m. (fr. सु-स्नात), one who asks whether an ablution has been success-ful or auspicious.
52941: सौहार्द सौहार्द, अम्, n. (fr. सु-हृद्), good-heartedness, affection, friendship, friendliness; (अस्), m. the son of a friend. —सौहार्द-निधि, इस्, m. ‘treasury of friendship,’ epithet of Rāma.
52943: सौहृद, अम्, n. friendship, (कु-सौहृद, अस्, आ, अम्, one who is a bad friend); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
52944: सौहृदय, अम्, n. (fr. सु-हृदय), cordial affection; friendship.
52946: सौहित्य सौहित्य, अम्, n. (fr. सु-हित), sa-tiety, satisfaction; fulness, completion; kindness, friendliness.
52947: सौहोत्र सौहोत्र, अस्, m. (fr. सु-होत्र), a patronymic of the Vedic Ṛṣi Aja-mīḍha; of Puru-mīḍha.
52948: स्कन्द् 1. स्कन्द् = rt. स्कुन्द्, q. v.
52949: स्कन्द् 2. स्कन्द् (also written स्कन्ध्), cl. 10. P. स्कन्दयति, स्कन्दायति, &c., to collect.
52950: स्कन्द् 3. स्कन्द् (connected with rt. स्कुन्द्, q. v.), cl. 1. P. स्कन्दति (also A. -ते), चस्कन्द (2nd sing. चस्कन्दिथ or चस्कन्त्थ), स्कन्त्स्यति, अस्कदत् or अस्कान्त्सीत्, स्कन्त्तुम्, to leap, jump, spring; to jump or spring upwards, rise, mount, ascend; to raise (A., but in this sense re-garded as a form of rt. स्कुन्द्); to jump down-wards, drop, fall; to leap out, shoot out, burst out, drop out, be poured out, be spilled, ooze; to go, move, approach; to fall away; to perish (A.); to become dry: Pass. स्कद्यते, Perf. चस्कदे or च-स्कन्दे, Aor. अस्कन्दि: Caus. स्कन्दयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अचस्कन्दत्, to pour out, effuse, shed, spill, emit (seminal fluid); to omit, neglect; Desid. चि-स्कन्त्सति: Intens. चनीस्कद्यते, चनीस्कन्ति; [cf. Gr. σκάνδ-αλο-ν, σκανδάλη-θρο-ν, σχαστήρ, per-haps σκαίρω, σκάζω; Lat. scand-o, de-scend-o, (ac-cording to some also) scateo; Hib. skeinnead, ‘eruption, gushing forth.’]
52951: स्कन्त्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who leaps, &c.; [cf. वि-ष्कन्त्तृ।]
52952: स्कन्त्त्वा, ind. having jumped, &c.; having de-scended or fallen.
52953: स्कन्द, अस्, m. leaping; flowing; quicksilver; N. of Kārttikeya (son of Śiva and god of war, see कार्त्तिकेय); epithet of Śiva; a king, prince; the body; the bank of a river; a clever or learned man [cf. स्कन्ध]; a kind of disease (attacking children). —स्कन्द-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Gupta dynasty. —स्कन्द-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of one of the eighteen Purāṇas, (see स्कान्द-पुराण।) —स्कन्-द-मातृ, ता, f. the mother of Skanda, i. e. Durgā. —स्कन्द-षष्ठी, f. a festival in honour of Kārttikeya on the sixth day of the month Caitra. —स्कन्द-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a commentator (mentioned by Mādhavācārya; cf. स्कान्द-भा-ष्य). —स्कन्दांशक (°द-अं°), अस्, m. quick-silver. —स्कन्देश्वर-तीर्थ (°द-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —स्कन्दोपनिषद् (°द-उप्°), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
52954: स्कन्दक, अस्, m. one who leaps or springs; a soldier.
52955: स्कन्दन, अम्, n. emission, effusion; purging, looseness; going, moving; drying up; the suppres-sion of bleeding by cold applications.
52956: स्कन्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be emitted, to be poured out or effused.
52957: स्कन्दयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, emitting, effusing, pour-ing out, shedding; neglecting.
52958: स्कन्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, emitted, effused, shed; going.
52959: स्कन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, leaping, jumping; bursting out; effusing.
52960: स्कन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen, fallen down, descended; oozed out, trickled down; emitted, sprinkled; gone; dried up.
52961: स्कन्दिलाचार्य स्कन्दिलाचार्य (°ल-आच्°), अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
52962: स्कन्ध् स्कन्ध् (= rt. 2. स्कन्द्), cl. 10. P. स्कन्धयति, &c., to collect.
52963: स्कन्ध स्कन्ध, अस्, m. (according to Uṇā-di-s. IV. 206. fr. rt. 3. स्कन्द्, ‘to rise’), the shoulder, upper part of the back or the region from the neck to the shoulder-joint (in men and animals); the body; the stem or trunk of a tree (especially that part of the stem where the branches begin); a large branch or bough; a branch or department of human knowledge (five of which are enumerated); a sec-tion, chapter, division of a book; a division of an army, form of military array; war, battle; a body of men &c., troop, multitude, quantity, (see करि-स्क्°, नर-स्क्°, तुरङ्ग-स्क्°); the five objects of sense, (see विषय); the elements of being or the five forms of mundane consciousness (according to the Buddhist philosophy); the regalia or other articles used at the coronation of a king (as a jar filled with holy water, a parasol, a chowri, &c.); a king, prince; a sage, wise man, seer, teacher; equality of height in the humps of a pair of draught oxen; a road, path, way; an engagement, agreement; a sort of metre; a heron; N. of a poet; = भद्रादि (accord-ing to Śabda-k.); (आ), f. a branch; a creeper; [cf. perhaps Gr. σπάθη: Lat. scapula: Angl. Sax. scul-dor, sculder, scoldr: Old Germ. scultra, sculdra, scultarra: Armor. skoaz: Cambro-Brit. ysgwyz; perhaps Hib. guala for sguada or sguana.] —स्कन्-ध-चाप, अस्, m. ‘shoulder-bow,’ a sort of yoke or pole made of bamboo with a sling attached to either end for carrying burdens (= शिक्य). —स्कन्ध-ज, अस्, m. a tree growing from a principal stem (such as the gum olibanum tree &c.). —स्कन्ध-तरु, अस्, m. the cocoa-nut tree. —स्कन्ध-देश, अस्, m. ‘shoulder-region,’ the shoulder; the part about the shoulders or withers of an elephant where the driver sits. —स्कन्ध-परि-निर्वाण, अम्, n. the annihilation of the elements of being (with Buddhists). —स्कन्ध-फल, अस्, m. ‘having fruit at the top,’ the cocoa-nut tree; the Vilva; the glomerous fig-tree. —स्कन्ध-बन्ध-ना, f. a sort of fennel, Anethum Panmorium. —स्कन्-ध-मल्लक, अस्, m. a heron. —स्कन्ध-रुह, अस्, m. ‘branch-growing,’ the Indian fig-tree. —स्कन्ध-वाह or स्कन्ध-वाहक, अस्, m. ‘carrying on the shoulders,’ an ox trained to carry burdens, pack-bullock. —स्कन्ध-शाखा, f. a principal branch, the forked branch which issues from the upper stem of a tree. —स्कन्ध-शृङ्ग, अस्, m. ‘branch-horned,’ a buf-falo. —स्कन्ध-स्कन्ध, अस्, m. every shoulder. —स्कन्धाग्नि (°ध-अग्°), इस्, or स्कन्धानल (°ध-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘trunk-conflagration,’ the trunk of a tree or any large piece of timber set on fire by attrition &c. —स्कन्धावार (°ध-आव्°), अस्, m. an army or a division of it attached to the person of a king; a royal capital, royal residence; a camp. —स्कन्धोपनेय (°ध-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, to be carried on the shoulders; (अस्), m. a form of peace-offering in which fruit or grain is presented as a mark of submission.
52964: स्कन्धक, अम्, n. a kind of metre.
52965: स्कन्धस्, अस्, n. the shoulder; the trunk of a tree. —स्कन्धो-ग्रीवी, f. a kind of metre (the first, third, and fourth Pādas of which consist of eight syllables each, and the second of twelve syllables, = न्यङ्कु-सारिणी).
52966: स्कन्धिक, अस्, m. an ox trained to carry burdens (= स्कन्ध-वाह).
52967: स्कन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having shoulders, having branches, having a branched stem; (ई), m. a tree.
52968: स्कन्ध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the shoulders.
52970: स्कम्भ् स्कम्भ् or स्कभ् (probably a mere phonetic variety of rt. स्तम्भ्, q. v.; in native lists written स्कन्भ्), cl. 1. A. स्कम्भते, चस्कम्भे, &c.; cl. 5. 9. P. स्कभ्नोति, स्कभ्नाति, &c., स्कम्भितुम्, to make firm, establish, to sup-port, prop up (Ved.); to create; to stop, hinder, impede, restrain, block, obstruct: Caus. स्कभयति or स्कम्भयति (Ved. also स्कभायति), &c., to establish, support; [cf. according to some, Gr. σκῆπτρον, σκήπτω, σκίμπτω; Lat. scabellum, scam-num; Goth. ga-skapjan, ga-skafts; Angl. Sax. scapen, sceapan, sceaft; Old Germ. scafan, sca-fon, scoppon, ‘to stop.’]
52971: स्कब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, propped, supported; stopped.
52972: स्कभित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. supported, fixed, fast-ened.
52973: स्कभीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, Ved. supporting more, supporting firmly.
52974: स्कम्भ, अस्, m. support, prop, fulcrum; ‘the sup-porter, propper,’ N. of a Vedic deity, (he is identified in Atharva-veda X. 7. with the supreme Being him-self, and is there represented, like Puruṣa, as co-extensive with the universe, and comprehending every existing thing in his members; the gods and all other entities, and even such abstract conceptions as faith, truth, &c., standing to him in the relation of branches to a tree; in X. 8. he is described as a sort of universal fulcrum as well as a universally dif-fused essence, the sky and the earth being said to be supported by him, and ‘all which has soul, which breathes, which winks’ being identified with him; he is even called ज्येष्ठम् ब्रह्म, which some think may mean not only the highest divine essence, but a kind of preæval Veda, of which the existing Vedas are merely branches.) —स्कम्भ-देष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. whose gifts are firm, stable in giving (said of the Maruts).
52975: स्कम्भन, अम्, n. the act of supporting, a sup-port, prop.
52976: स्कान्द स्कान्द, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्कन्द), relat-ing to Skanda or Kārttikeya; relating to Śiva; (अम्), n. the Skanda-Purāṇa. —स्कान्द-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of one of the eighteen Purāṇas (also called स्कन्द-पुराण; it is supposed to be lost or only to exist in fragments, the most celebrated of which is the Kāśī-khaṇḍa, which gives a description of the temples or Liṅgas of Śiva near Benares, with direc-tions for worshipping that god, and various legends chiefly intended to glorify Kāśī and exalt the sanctity of its shrines). —स्कान्द-भाष्य, अम्, n., N. of a commentary.
52977: स्कु स्कु, cl. 5. 9. P. A. स्कुनोति, स्कुनाति, स्कुनुते, स्कुनीते, चुस्काव, चुस्कुवे, स्को-ष्यति, -ते, अस्कौषीत्, अस्कोष्ट, स्कोतुम्, to go by leaps, jump; to raise, lift; to cover, overspread; to approach: Caus. स्कावयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अचुस्क-वत्: Desid. चुस्कूषति, -ते: Intens. चोस्कूयते (Ved. चोष्कूयते), चोस्कोति; [cf. Gr. σκευ-ή, σκεῦ-ος, σκευά-ζ-ω, σκῦ-το-ς, κύ-τ-ος, ἐπι-σκύ-νιο-ν: Lat. ob-scu-ru-s, scu-tu-m, cu-ti-s, corium, cavere, cautus, causa: probably Angl. Sax. scuva, scoh, sceo, scunian, scawian, sceawian: Goth. skoh: Old Germ. scur, skiuhan.]
52978: चोष्कूयमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. bestowing, giv-ing, (Sāy. = प्रयच्छत्, Ṛg-veda I. 33, 3, = द-दत्, Nirukta VI. 22.)
52979: स्कुन्द् स्कुन्द् (connected with rt. 3. स्कन्द्, q. v.; cf. rt. स्कु), cl. 1. A. स्कुन्दते, चस्कुन्दे, &c., स्कुन्दितुम्, to jump, go by leaps or jumps; to raise, lift, (see rt. 3. स्कन्द्।)
52980: स्कुम्भ् स्कुम्भ् (connected with rt. स्कम्भ्; in native lists regarded as a Sautra rt. and written स्कुन्भ्), cl. 5. 9. P. स्कुभ्नोति, स्कुभ्-नाति, &c., to hold, stop, hinder.
52981: स्कोटिका स्कोटिका, f. a kind of bird (pro-bably a sort of wagtail, = खञ्जनिका).
52982: स्खद् स्खद् [cf. rt. क्षद्], cl. 1. A. स्ख-दते, चस्खदे, स्खदितुम्, to cut, cut or tear to pieces; to destroy; to hurt, injure, kill; to rout, defeat; to harass, fatigue, exhaust; to make firm; to be firm: Caus. स्खदयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अचिस्खदत्।
52983: स्खदन, अम्, n. cutting or tearing to pieces; the act of hurting or killing, injury; harassing, de-feating, discomfiting; firmness.
52984: स्खल् स्खल् (connected with rts. छल्, स्फल्), cl. 1. P. स्खलति, चस्खाल, स्खलिष्यति, अस्खालीत्, स्खलितुम्, to stumble, tumble, fall, fall down, trip, slip; to totter, waver; to fall or deviate from the right course; to make mistakes, blunder, err, fail; to make mistakes in speaking, stammer, falter, stutter, hesitate; to drop, drip, trickle; to go, move; disappear; to gather, collect: Pass. स्खल्यते, Perf. चस्खले (Kirāt. XVIII. 6), Aor. अस्खालि: Caus. स्खलयति or स्खालयति, &c., to cause to stumble, trip up; [cf. Lat. scelus, culpa; Goth. skula, skulan; Angl. Sax. sceal, sculan, scyld.]
52985: स्खलत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, stumbling, tripping; blun-dering; stuttering; dropping, trickling. —स्खलद्-वाक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, making mistakes in speaking, stammering, faltering, blundering. —स्खलन्-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, erring in judgment, weak-minded.
52986: स्खलन, अम्, n. the act of stumbling, slipping, tripping, falling, tottering; falling or deviating from the right course; blundering, an error, mistake, blunder; blundering in speech or pronunciation; dropping, dripping, trickling, effusion, emission; dashing or clashing together, shock, collision; mutual striking or rubbing together.
52987: स्खलित, अस्, आ, अम्, stumbled, slipped, tripped, fallen; dropped down; shaking, fluctuating, waver-ing, tottering, unsteady; erring; stuttering, stammer-ing, faltering, hesitating; intoxicated, drunk; agi-tated, disturbed; dropped, effused, emitted; trickling down; interrupted, stopped, obstructed; confounded; gone; (अम्), n. tumbling, falling; deviation from the right course; blunder, fault, error, sin; deceit, treachery; circumvention, stratagem (in war). —स्ख-लित-सुभगम्, ind. slipping or tripping along plea-santly, dashing or flowing along in a charming manner (said of a stream).
52988: स्खलित्वा, ind. having stumbled; having slipped or tripped.
52989: स्खुड् स्खुड् (= rts. स्थुड्, थुड्), cl. 6. P. स्खुडति, to cover.
52990: स्तक् स्तक्, cl. 1. P. स्तकति, तस्ताक, स्त-कितुम्, to resist; to strike against, repel: Caus. स्तकयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अतिष्टकत्।
52991: स्तन् स्तन्, cl. 1. P. स्तनति, तस्तान, स्त-नितुम्, to sound, make a sound, resound, reverberate; to groan, breathe hard, sigh; cl. 10. P. स्तनयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अतस्तनत्, to thunder: Caus. स्तनयति (or स्तानयति according to some), -यितुम्, Aor. अतिष्टनत् (or अतिस्तनत् according to some), to cause to resound: Desid. तिस्तनिषति: Intens, तंस्तन्यते, तंस्तन्ति; [cf. Gr. στέν-ω, στενάχ-ω, στόνο-ς, στένο-μαι, στείνομαι, στενό-ς, στεινό-ς, στεῖνος, Στέν-τωρ: Lat. tono, tonitru: Old Norse stynija, styn: Old Germ. stunôd, ‘a sigh;’ thonar, donar, ‘thunder:’ Old Sax. thunar: Angl. Sax. thunor: Lith. sten-e-ti: Slav. sten-a-ti, ‘to groan.’]
52992: स्तन, अस्, m. the breast of a woman, (probably so called from the noise made in breathing); the nipple of the breast; an udder or dug or breast of any female animal, (at the end of an adj. comp. the fem. may end in आ or ई, according to Vopa-deva IV. 17, but the more usual form is in ई।) —स्तन-कलश, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘goblet-like breast,’ a woman's breast. —स्तन-कुट्मल, अम्, n. ‘breast-bud,’ a woman's breast. —स्तन-तट, अस्, m. the slope of the breasts, (see तट।) —स्तनन्-धम, अस्, आ, m. f. = स्तनन्-धय below. —स्तनन्-धय, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, breast-sucking, sucking at the breast; (अस्, आ), m. f. an infant; a suckling. —स्तन-प, अस्, आ, अम्, or स्तन-पा, आस्, आस्, अम्, or स्तन-पायक, अस्, इका, अम्, or स्तन-पायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, breast-sucking, sucking the breast or udder; an infant at the breast, suckling. —स्तन-पान, अम्, n. the drinking or sucking of the breast. —स्तन-भर, अस्, m. ‘breast-possessing,’ a man with a breast like a woman's. —स्तन-भव, अस्, आ, अम्, being on the breast; (अस्), m. a particular posture in sexual union. —स्तन-मण्डल, अम्, n. ‘breast-orb,’ a woman's breast. —स्तन-मध्य or स्तन-मुख, अस्, m. ‘breast-point,’ a nipple. —स्तन-वृन्त, अस्, m. ‘breast-stalk,’ a nipple. —स्तन-शिखा, f. ‘breast-point,’ a nipple. —स्तनांशुक (°न-अं°), अम्, n. ‘breast-mantle,’ a cloth covering the bosom. —स्तनाग्र (°न-अग्°), अस्, m. ‘breast-point,’ a nipple. —स्तनाङ्ग-राग (°न-अङ्°), अस्, m. paint or pigment on the breasts (of women). —स्त-नान्तर (°न-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘breast-interval,’ the heart (as situated under the centre bone of the sternum); a mark on the breast (supposed to indi-cate future widowhood). —स्तना-भुज, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. feeding or nourishing with the udder (said of cows). —स्तनाभोग (°न-आभ्°), अस्, m. fulness or swelling of the breast, the expanding of the bosom of a young woman; the circumference or orb of the breast; a man with large breasts like those of a woman.
52994: स्तनन, अम्, n. sounding, sound, noise; the rumbling of clouds; groaning; breathing hard.
52995: स्तनयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, thundering. —स्तनयद्-अमास्, m. pl. (see अमा, p. 74, col. 3), Ved. roaring together, sounding in concert (said of the Maruts).
52996: स्तनयित्नु, उस्, m. thundering, thunder, the mut-tering of clouds; a cloud; lightning; sickness; death; a kind of grass (= मुस्तक). —स्तनयित्नु-घोष, अस्, आ, अम्, loud as thunder.
52997: स्तनित, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded, sounding; thun-dering; (अम्), n. the rattling of thunder, rumbling of thunder-clouds; thunder, noise; the noise of clapping the hands. —स्तनित-फल, अस्, m. the plant Vikaṇṭaka.
52998: स्तन्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्तन), ‘that which is to be drawn from the breast,’ mother's milk, milk. —स्त-न्य-त्याग, अस्, m. leaving off the mother's milk, weaning. —स्तन्य-त्याग-मात्रक, अस्, आ, अम्, only just weaned. —स्तन्य-पायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, or स्तन्य-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, sucking or feeding on milk, sucking at the breast.
53000: स्तभ स्तभ, अस्, m. a goat; a ram; [cf. स्तुभ।]
53001: स्तम् स्तम् (= rt. 1. सम्), cl. 1. P. स्तमति, तस्ताम, स्तमितु, to be confused or agitated; (according to some) not to be confused, see rt. 1. सम्; cl. 10. P. स्तमयति, to be agitated, &c.
53002: स्तम्ब स्तम्ब, अस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s. IV. 96. said to be fr. rt. 1. स्था; probably connected with स्तम्भ, q. v.), a clump of grass, &c.; a sheaf of corn; any clump or bunch or cluster; a bush, thicket; a shrub or plant having no decided stem (such as the Jhiṇṭī or Barleria); the post to which an elephant is tied; any post or pillar, (in this and the next sense probably for स्तम्भ, but said by some to be neut.); stupefaction, insensibility; a mountain; [cf. Angl. Sax. stapel.] —स्तम्ब-करि, इस्, m. ‘forming clusters,’ corn, rice. —स्तम्ब-कार, अस्, ई, अम्, making a clump, forming a cluster. —स्तम्ब-घन, अस्, m. ‘clump-destroyer,’ a small hoe for weeding or eradicating clumps of grass, &c.; a sickle for cutting corn; a basket for holding the heads of wild rice, &c. —स्तम्ब-घात = स्तम्ब-घ्न below. —स्तम्ब-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, clump-destroying, weed-destroying; (अस्), m. a hoe or sickle. —स्तम्ब-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, growing on a clump or bush; growing on a post. —स्तम्ब-पुर्, ऊर्, f., N. of the city Tāmalipta, q. v. —स्तम्ब-मित्र, अस्, m., N. of the author of Ṛg-veda X. 142, 7, 8 (having the patronymic Śārṅga). —स्तम्-ब-हन् or स्तम्ब-हनन, अम्, ई, n. f. ‘clump-destroyer,’ a hoe for eradicating weeds; a sickle for cutting corn. —स्तम्बे-रम, अस्, m. ‘delighting in clumps of high grass,’ an elephant.
53003: स्तम्भ् स्तम्भ् or स्तभ् (connected with rt. स्कम्भ्, q. v.; in native lists written स्तन्भ्), cl. 5. 9. P. स्तभ्नोति, स्तभ्नाति, (2nd sing. Impv. स्तभान), तस्तम्भ, अस्तम्भीत् or अस्तभत्, स्तम्भितुम् (originally perhaps ‘to stamp’), to fix firmly, make firm, make stiff or im-movable; to paralyze, stupefy; to prop, support, prop up, sustain; to create (Ved.); to stop, arrest, suppress, oppose, hinder; cl. 1. A. स्तम्भते, तस्तम्भे (ac-cording to some also टष्टम्भे, ष्टम्भते), &c., to become fixed or immovable, to become senseless or insensible, become stiff or rigid: Pass. स्तभ्यते, Aor. अस्तम्भि: Caus. स्तम्भयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अतस्तम्भत्, to fix, make firm or immovable, to make stiff or rigid, stupefy, paralyze, stun; to prop, support; stop, arrest, bring to a stand, suppress, re-strain: Desid. तिस्तम्भिषति: Intens. तास्तभ्यते; [cf. Gr. στέμφ-υλο-ν, ἀ-στεμφ-ής, στέμβ-ω, στεμβ-άζω, στοβέ-ω, στοβάζ-ω, στείβ-ω; Lat. stupeo, stipes; Old Germ. stamph, stamphon, stab; Mod. Germ. stampfen; Old Norse stofn.]
53004: स्तब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed, firm, stiff, rigid, hard, immovable, motionless, numb, paralyzed, senseless, stupid, dull, insensible, indifferent; stopped, brought to a stand, blocked up; obstinate, stubborn, hard-hearted; coarse; [cf. Old Germ. stīf; Mod. Germ. steif; Engl. stiff.] —स्तब्ध-कर्ण, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘stiff-eared,’ having the ears fixed, pricking up the ears. —स्तब्ध-ता, f. or स्तब्ध-त्व, अम्, n. fixedness, rigidity, immobility, steadiness, stupor, stubbornness. —स्तब्ध-रोमन्, आ, m. ‘stiff-bristled,’ a boar, hog. —स्तब्ध-लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, having fixed or unwinking eyes (applied as an epi-thet to the gods who are supposed to be known by this characteristic). —स्तब्धी-करण, अम्, n. the act of making stiff, stiffening, making rigid, para-lyzing. —स्तब्धी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made stiff, stiffened, rigid, paralyzed. —स्तब्धी-कृत्य, ind. having stiffened or made rigid. —स्तब्धी-भाव, अस्, m. the becoming stiffened or rigid, torpidity.
53005: स्तब्धि, इस्, f. fixedness, hardness, rigidity, firm-ness, immobility, stupor, numbness, obstinacy.
53007: स्तभित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = स्तब्ध।
53009: स्तभूय (fr. स्तभु), Nom. A. स्तभूयते, &c., Ved. to desire to support.
53010: स्तभूयमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. desiring to support, upholding.
53011: स्तभ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being made firm.
53012: स्तम्भ, अस्, m. fixedness, stiffness, rigidity; immobility, a prop, support, fulcrum; a pillar, column, post; a stem, stock, trunk; insensibility, stupor, stupefaction (from fear, joy, grief, &c.); numbness, paralysis, torpor; stupidity, coldness, want of feeling or excitability; stoppage, obstruction, hin-drance; suppression; a particular faculty acquired by magical means, the supernatural suppression or ar-resting of any feeling or force (as of hunger, thirst, or the forces of fire, water, &c.; this is one of the षट्-कर्मन् described as taught in the Tantras, see p. 1032, col. 3; many varieties of Stambha are enumerated, e. g. जल-स्त्°, वह्नि-स्त्°, वायु-स्त्°, क्षुत्-स्त्°, पिपासा-स्त्°, निद्रा-स्त्°, and in the case of the first of these one effect of this faculty is to enable a person to walk on the waters); N. of a Ṛṣi; [cf. Angl. Sax. steb.] —स्तम्भ-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing obstruction; causing stiffness, paralyzing; (अस्), m. a fence, railing, &c. —स्तम्भ-कारण, अम्, n. cause of obstruction or impediment. —स्तम्-भ-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a place. —स्तम्भ-पूजा, f. worship of the posts of the temporary pavilions erected for marriages or other festive occasions. —स्तम्भी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become a post. —स्तम्भोत्कीर्ण (°भ-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, carved out of a post of wood (as a statue).
53013: स्तम्भक, अस्, इका, अम्, fixing, propping, stop-ping, restraining.
53014: स्तम्भकिन्, ई, m. a kind of musical instrument covered with leather.
53015: स्तम्भन, अम्, n. the act of fixing firmly, making stiff or hard or rigid, making like a post, (रम्भा-स्तम्भन, the turning of the nymph Rambhā into a pillar by the curse of Viśvā-mitra, see Rāmāyaṇa I. 64); paralyzing, stupefying, stunning, benumbing; propping or supporting, holding up-right; stopping, making immovable, hindering, arresting, bringing to a stand, suppression, obstruc-tion; stopping of hemorrhage, staunching the flow of blood; anything employed as a styptic or astrin-gent; a particular magical act or faculty, suppression of any of the bodily feelings or forces of nature by supernatural means, (see under स्तम्भ; जल-स्तम्भन = जल-स्तम्भ); (अस्, ई, अम्), fixing immovably, paralyzing, supporting, stopping; (अस्), m. ‘the paralyzer,’ epithet of one of the five arrows of Kāma-deva, (the names of the other four are Unmādana, Śoṣaṇa, Tāpana, and Sammohana.)
53016: स्तम्भनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be fixed firmly; to be propped; to be stopped.
53017: स्तम्भित, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed firmly; stiffened, benumbed, paralyzed, stupefied, senseless; propped up, supported; stopped, brought to a standstill, sup-pressed; staunched; restrained, constrained. —स्तम्-भित-रम्भ, अम्, n., N. of a particular Troṭaka or drama; [cf. रम्भा-स्तम्भन above.] —स्तम्-भित-वाष्प-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, suppressing the flow of tears. —स्तम्भिताश्रु (°त-अश्°), उस्, उस्, उ, one who has suppressed his tears.
53018: स्तम्भित्वा, ind. having fixed, having stopped, having suppressed.
53019: स्तम्भिन्, ई, इनी, इ, supporting; stopping, re-straining; (इनी), f. one of the five Dhāraṇās or elements (= earth, see भ्रमणी).
53020: स्तर स्तर, स्तरण, स्तरिमन्, &c. See p. 1144, col. 1.
53022: स्तवरक स्तवरक, अस्, m. (doubtful), a fence, railing (= आवरक).
53023: स्तामु स्तामु, उस्, m. (= स्तोतृ, Naigh. III. 16), Ved. a praiser, worshipper.
53025: स्ति स्ति, स्ति-पा। See under rt. स्त्यै।
53026: स्तिघ् स्तिघ्, cl. 5. A. स्तिघ्नुते, तिष्-टिघे, अस्तेघिष्ट, स्तेघितुम्, to as-cend; to assail: Caus. स्तेघयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अतिष्टिघत्: Desid. तिस्तिघिषते or तिस्तेघिषते: Intens. तेष्टिघ्यते, तेष्टेग्धि; [cf. Gr. στείχ-ω, ἔ-στιχ-ον, στίχο-ς, στοῖχο-ς, στιχάο-μαι: Goth. steig-a, staig-a, ‘a path:’ Old Germ. steg-a, ‘an ascent, path:’ Mod. Germ. steig-en, ‘to rise:’ Slav. stiz-a, ‘a path:’ Lith. staig-ù-s, ‘quick;’ staigiō-s, ‘to hasten:’ Hib. staighre, ‘a step, stair.’]
53027: स्तिप् स्तिप् (also written स्तेप्), cl. 1. A. स्तेपते, तिष्टिपे, &c., to ooze, drip, drop.
53028: स्तिभि स्तिभि, इस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 121. fr. rt. स्तम्भ्), an obstacle, obstruction; the ocean; a cluster, clump, bunch (= फल-स्त-वक; cf. स्तम्ब).
53029: स्तिम्भि, इस्, m. = स्तिभि above (according to some).
53030: स्तिम् स्तिम् or स्तीम् (connected with rt. तिम्), cl. 4. P. स्तिम्यति, स्तीम्यति, तिष्टेम, तिष्टीम, &c., to be or become wet or moist; to become fixed or immovable.
53031: स्तिमित, अस्, आ, अम्, [cf. तिमित], wet, moist; still, motionless, unmoved, steady, fixed, rigid (as the eye), immovable, benumbed; tender, soft; gratified, pleased; (अम्), n. moisture. —स्तिमित-त्व, अम्, n. steadiness, fixedness, stillness, absence of motion, absorption. —स्तिमित-वायु, उस्, m. still air. —स्तिमित-समाधि-शुचि, इस्, इस्, इ, pure with steady meditation. —स्तिमितायताक्ष (°त-आय्°, °त-अक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, one who keeps his large eyes fixed or still.
53034: स्तीर्वि स्तीर्वि, इस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 54. fr. rt. 1. स्तृ), an officiating priest at a sacri-fice (especially an Adhvaryu versed in the Yajur-veda); grass (= तृण-जाति); sky, atmosphere (= नभस्); water (= पयस्); blood (= रुधिर); Indra (= शक्र).
53035: स्तु स्तु, cl. 2. P. A. स्तौति or स्तवीति (1st du. स्तुवस् or स्तुवीवस्, 3rd pl. स्तुवन्ति), स्तुते or स्तुवीते, Impf. अस्तौत् or अस्तवीत् (1st sing. अस्तवम्), Impv. स्तौतु or स्तवीतु (2nd sing. स्तुहि or स्तुवीहि), Perf. तुष्टाव (2nd sing. तुष्-टोथ, 1st du. तुष्टुव, 1st pl. तुष्टुम), तुष्-टुवे, स्तोष्यति, -ते, अस्तावीत्, अस्तोष्ट, स्तोतुम् or (according to Vopa-deva also) स्तवितुम् (Ved. Inf. स्तुषे, स्तवध्यै), to praise, laud, eulogize, glorify, extol, celebrate; to hymn, praise or celebrate in song, worship by hymns; cl. 1. A. स्तवते (Ved. स्तवे), to be praised (Ved.): Pass. स्तूयते, &c., Aor. अस्तावि, to be praised, &c.: Caus. स्तावयति, Aor. अतुष्टवत्: Desid. तुष्टूषति, -ते: Intens. तोष्टूयते, तोष्टोति; [cf. perhaps Gr. στό-μα, Æol. στύ-μα: Goth. staua, ‘a judge;’ stauja, ‘to judge.’]
53036: स्तव, अस्, m. praising, celebrating, hymning; praise, eulogium, panegyric. —स्तव-राज, अस्, m., N. of a particular mystical prayer or incantation. —स्तवावलि, इस्, or स्तवावली (°व-आव्°), f., N. of a work by Kavi-candra.
53037: स्तवक, अस्, इका, अम्, praising, eulogising; (अस्), m. a panegyrist, praiser; praise, eulogium; a cluster of blossoms, bunch of flowers, nosegay, tuft, (in these senses said to be fr. rt. 1. स्था according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 96); N. of the chapters in the Kusu-māñjali; a quantity, multitude; [cf. स्तोम।] —स्त-वकाचित (°क-आच्°), अस्, आ, अम्, covered with blos-soms, in blossom.
53038: स्तवकित, अस्, आ, अम्, full of blossoms.
53039: स्तवथ, अस्, m., Ved. praise, (Sāy. = स्तोत्र।)
53040: स्तवन, अम्, n. praising, praise; a hymn.
53041: स्तवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised, praiseworthy, laudable.
53042: स्तवमान, अस्, आ, अम्, lauding, praising.
53043: स्तवान्, nom. c. masc., Ved. being praised or lauded, (Sāy. = स्तूयमान, Ṛg-veda VI. 24, 8.)
53044: स्तवान, अस्, आ, अम्, being praised, being lauded or glorified, (Sāy. = स्तूयमान।)
53045: स्तवितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised, &c.
53046: स्तवितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, a praiser, praising.
53048: स्ताव, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. praising, one who praises, a praiser; (अस्), m. praise.
53049: स्तावक, अस्, m. a praiser, panegyrist, eulogiser, flatterer.
53050: स्ताविन्, ई, इनी, इ, praising, hymning.
53051: स्ताव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be praised, praise-worthy.
53052: स्तुत्, त्, त्, त् (at the end of comps.), praising, cele-brating, (see देव-स्त्°, यथा-स्त्°, छन्दः-स्त्°।)
53053: स्तुत, अस्, आ, अम्, praised, eulogised, hymned, glorified; flattered; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva. —स्तुत-स्वामि-क्षेत्र, अम्, n., N. of a sacred place.
