VI. 3, 44.) —स्त्री-ता, f. or स्त्री-त्व, अम्, n. womanhood, wife-hood; feminineness, effeminacy. —स्त्री-धन, अम्, n. ‘woman's wealth,’ a wife's peculiar property or any property belonging to a woman over which she has independent control (said to be of six kinds, viz. अध्य्-अग्निक, a gift upon or in presence of the nuptial fire by a member of either family; अध्य्-आवाहनिक, that which is taken from the father's house at the time of the bridal procession or when the bride is conducted to her husband's home; आधिवेदनिक, a settlement on a first wife when her husband contracts a second marriage; प्रीति-दत्त, a gift of affection; शुल्क, a kind of dower or money given to a woman to induce her to go to her husband's house; अन्व्-आधेय, a gift from her own or husband's family after marriage: according to others the six kinds are, भर्तृ-दाय, पितृ-दत्त, मातृ-द्°, भ्रातृ-द्°, with the first two enumerated above: other varieties of woman's pro-perty are बन्धु-दत्त, q. v., यौतक, q. v., सौ-दायिक, q. v., पारिणाय्य, q. v., लावण्यार्जित, q. v., and पादवन्दनिक, the last being a gift to a wife from a husband in return for her पाद-वन्दन, q. v., on her entering his house). —स्त्री-धर्म, अस्, m. the duty of a woman or wife; the laws concerning women; menstruation. —स्त्रीधर्म-योग, अस्, m. the application of laws or customs relative to women. —स्त्री-धर्मिणी, f. a woman during menstruation. —स्त्री-धव, अस्, m. a woman's husband; a man, male. —स्त्री-ध्वज, अस्, m. ‘having the mark of a female,’ the female of any species of animal. —स्त्री-नाथ, अस्, आ, अम्, having a woman as lord or pro-tector, protected by a woman. —स्त्री-नामन्, आ, म्नी, अ, having a female name. —स्त्री-निबन्धन, अम्, n. a woman's peculiar province, domestic duty, housewifery. —स्त्री-पण्योपजीविन् (°य-उप्°), ई, m. one who makes a living by keeping women for prostitution. —स्त्री-पर, अस्, m. one who is devoted to women, a woman-lover, libertine. —स्त्री-पर्वत-देश, अस्, m., N. of a district. —स्त्री-पर्वन्, अ, n., N. of the eleventh book of the Mahā-bhārata. —स्त्री-पिशाची, f. a fiend-like wife. —स्त्री-पुंस्, मान्, m. a woman who has become a man. —स्त्री-पुंस, औ, m. du. wife and husband, man and wife, the union of man and wife. —स्त्री-पुंस-लक्षणा, f. a wo-man who has the characteristic marks of both male and female, a hermaphrodite. —स्त्री-पुन्-धर्म, अस्, m. the law (which regulates the duties) of man and wife, the mutual duties of husband and wife or of man and woman. —स्त्री-पुन्-नपुं-सक, masculine, feminine, and neuter. —स्त्री-पूर्व or स्त्री-पूर्वक or स्त्री-पूर्विक, अस्, m. or स्त्री-पूर्विन्, ई, m. one who has been a woman for-merly or in a former birth, (according to Śabda-k. स्त्री-पूर्व = स्त्री-जित, ruled by a woman.) —स्त्री-प्रत्यय, अस्, m. (in grammar) a feminine affix, an affix used in forming feminines from Prātipadikas. —स्त्री-प्रमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, having a wife for an authority, one who is ruled by a wife. —स्त्री-प्र-सङ्ग, अस्, m. intercourse with women. —स्त्री-प्रसू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, bearing females, bringing forth daughters only. —स्त्री-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, liked or loved by women; (अस्), m. the Mango tree. —स्त्री-बाध्य, अस्, m. one who suffers himself to be dis-tressed by a woman. —स्त्री-बुद्धि, इस्, f. the female understanding. —स्त्री-भृत्य, आस्, m. pl. women and servants. —स्त्री-भोग, अस्, m. enjoyment of women, sexual intercourse. —स्त्री-मत्, आन्, m. a wife-pos-sessor, a married man. —स्त्री-मन्त्र, अस्, m. a woman's counsel, female stratagem. —स्त्री-मुख-प, अस्, m. ‘drinking the mouth of women,’ the Aśoka tree (= दोहली). —स्त्री-यन्त्र, अम्, n. ‘wo-man-vessel,’ woman regarded as a vessel or machine, a woman who works like a machine. —स्त्री-याचित-पुत्र, अस्, m. a son obtained through a wife's solicita-tions. —स्त्री-रञ्जन, अम्, n. ‘delighting women,’ betel (which with the areca-nut is much chewed by Hindū women). —स्त्री-रत्न, अम्, n. a jewel or gem of a woman, an excellent woman; N. of Lak-ṣmī. —स्त्री-राज्य, अम्, n. the kingdom of women (a country placed by some in the region of Bhotan). —स्त्री-रोग, अस्, m. any disease incident to women. —स्त्री-लिङ्ग, अम्, n. the female organ; the feminine gender. —स्त्रीलिङ्ग-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being in the feminine gender, being a feminine. —स्त्री-वध, अस्, m. the slaying of a woman. —स्त्री-वश, अम्, n. subjection to women, submissiveness to a wife. —स्त्री-वाक्याङ्कुश-प्रक्षुण्ण (°य-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, driven or urged on by the goad of women's words. —स्त्री-विधेय, अस्, आ, अम्, submissive to a wife, governed by a wife, uxorious. —स्त्री-वियोग, अस्, m. separation from a wife. —स्त्री-विवाह, अस्, m. ‘wo-man-marriage,’ the act of contracting marriage with a woman. —स्त्री-वृत, अस्, आ, अम्, surrounded or at-tended by women. —स्त्री-संसर्ग, अस्, m. inter-course with women, female society. —स्त्री-सं-स्थान, अस्, आ, अम्, having a female shape. —स्त्री-सङ्ग, अस्, m. attachment or addiction to women; intercourse with a woman. —स्त्री-सङ्ग्रहण, अम्, n. the act of embracing a woman (improperly), adultery, seduction. —स्त्री-सभ, अम्, n. an assembly of women, collection of females. —स्त्री-सम्बन्ध, अस्, m. matrimonial connection with a woman; con-nection by marriage; relation or reference to women. —स्त्री-सेवा, f. ‘woman-service,’ addiction to wo-men. —स्त्री-स्वभाव, अस्, m. the nature or disposi-tion of women; a guard of the women's apartments, eunuch. —स्त्री-स्वरूप, अस्, आ, अम्, or स्त्री-स्वरूप-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, or स्त्री-स्वरूपिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having a woman's shape or figure. —स्त्री-हत्या, f. the murder of a woman. —स्त्री-हन्तृ, ता, m. the mur-derer of a woman. —स्त्री-हरण, अम्, n. the carry-ing off or forcible abduction of a woman; rape. —स्त्री-हारिन्, ई, m. the carrier off of a woman; one who commits rape, a ravisher. —स्त्र्य्-अभिगमन, अम्, n. the act of approaching a woman, sexual inter-course. —स्त्र्य्-आजीव, अस्, m. one who lives by his wife; one who lives by keeping women for pros-titution.
53136: स्त्रीक = स्त्री (at the end of an adj. comp., e. g. स-स्त्रीक, q. v.).
53137: स्त्रैण, अस्, ई, अम्, female, feminine; suited or belonging to women; being among women; (अम्), n. womanhood, feminineness; the female sex; the nature of woman; a multitude of women; sexual enjoyment (Ved.). —स्त्रैण-ता, f. or स्त्रैण-त्व, अम्, n. effeminacy.
53138: स्त्रैराजक, आस्, f. pl. (probably) the women of Strī-rājya.
53140: स्थ स्थ। See under rt. 1. स्था, col. 3.
53141: स्थकर स्थकर (connected with स्थगर below), a betel-nut (according to some; cf. स्थगी).
53142: स्थग् स्थग्, cl. 1. P. स्थगति, तस्थाग, अस्थगीत्, &c., to cover, hide, conceal: Caus. स्थगयति, &c., to cover, veil, hide, make invisible; [cf. Gr. στέγ-ω, στέγ-η, τέγη, στέγος, τέγος, στεγ-ανό-ς, στεγ-νό-ς: Lat. teg-o, tec-tu-m, teg-i-men, teg-ula: Old Norse thek, ‘a roof:’ Old Germ. dak-jan: Angl. Sax. theccan, thaca: Lith. steg-iu, ‘I cover;’ stoga-s, ‘a roof.’]
53143: स्थग, अस्, आ, अम्, fraudulent, dishonest, shame-less, abandoned; (अस्), m. a rogue, cheat; (ई), f. a betel box.
53144: स्थगन, अम्, n. the act of covering or conceal-ing, concealment.
53145: स्थगर, a kind of plant (= पुत्र-जीवक); (perhaps) a betel-nut; [cf. स्थगी above.]
53146: स्थगिका, f. a courtezan; the office of betel-bearer.
53147: स्थगित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered, concealed, hidden.
53148: स्थगु, उस्, m. a hump, an excrescence or pro-tuberance on the back.
53149: स्थण्डिल स्थण्डिल, अम्, n. (according to some connected with rt. स्थल्), a piece of ground (levelled, squared, and prepared for a sacrifice); a barren field; a heap of clods; a boundary, limit, land-mark; (अस्), m., N. of a Ṛṣi. —स्थण्डिल-शायिन्, ई, m. a devotee who sleeps on the bare ground or on the sacrificial Sthaṇḍila (on account of a religious vow). —स्थण्डिल-सितक, अम्, n. an altar. —स्थण्-डिले-शय, अस्, m. an ascetic who sleeps on the bare ground or on the Sthaṇḍila; a proper N.
53150: स्थण्डिलेयु, उस्, m., N. of a king.
53151: स्थन स्थन (fr. rt. 1. अस्), Ved. = भवथ, (Ṛg-veda VIII. 18, 15.)
53153: स्थपुट स्थपुट, अस्, आ, अम्, being in con-tracted or difficult circumstances; unevenly raised, elevated and depressed, bent down. —स्थपुट-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, being in contracted and uneven places, being on raised places and in hollows. —स्थपुटी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made uneven, raised and depressed; (according to one commentator) covered with grass, &c.
53154: स्थल् स्थल् (connected with rt. 1. स्था), cl. 1. P. स्थलति, तस्थाल, स्थलिष्-यति, अस्थालीत्, स्थलितुम्, to stand firm, be firm: Caus. स्थालयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अतिष्ठलत्, to cause to stand firm, fix firmly: Desid. of Caus. तिस्थालयिषति: Desid. तिस्थलिषति: Intens. ता-स्थल्यते, तास्थल्ति; [cf. Gr. στέλλ-ω, ἔσταλκα, ἐ-στάλη-ν, στόλο-ς, στάλ-ιξ, στελεό-ν;] Lat. prœ-stol-o-r, stul-tu-s, stol-i-du-s (?); Old Germ. stil, stallan, stellan; Lith. stelloju, ‘I appoint.’]
53155: स्थल, अम्, ई, n. f. firm or dry ground, terra firma, dry land (as opposed to ‘water’); shore, strand, beach; ground or land (in general), soil; place, spot, site; field, tract, district; station; (अम्, आ), n. f. a spot of dry ground artificially raised and drained; (ई), f. a deity of the soil, local or tutelary divinity; (अम्), n. a piece of raised ground, mound, terrace; a topic, case, subject (of a description &c.), point under discussion; part (of a book); a tent, house of cloth; [cf. Old Germ. stal, ‘a place;’ stul-lan, stelza, stolv: Goth. ga-stalds: Angl. Sax. stal, stœl, stillan, stille: Mod. Germ. stall.] —स्थल-कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= अग्रा-म्य-कन्द). —स्थल-कमल, अम्, n. or स्थल-कमलिनी, f. the flowering shrub, Hibiscus Muta-bilis. —स्थल-कुमुद, अस्, m. the Kara-vīra plant. —स्थल-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone or left on dry land. —स्थल-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, land-going, living on dry land, not aquatic (opposed to जल-चर). —स्थल-च्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen or removed from a place or position. —स्थल-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, land-born, ter-restrial, not aquatic. —स्थल-तस्, ind. from dry land, from terra firma. —स्थल-ता, f. the state of being dry ground. —स्थल-देवता, f. a local or rural deity, tutelary god presiding over some par-ticular spot. —स्थल-नलिनी, f. = स्थल-पद्मिनी below. —स्थल-पद्म, अस्, m. = मानक; (अम्), n. the shrub Hibiscus Mutabilis; another plant (= छत्त्र-पत्त्र, तमालक). —स्थल-पद्मिनी, f. the shrub Hibiscus Mutabilis. —स्थल-मञ्जरी, f. the plant Achyranthes Aspera. —स्थल-मार्ग, अस्, m. or स्थल-वर्त्मन्, अ, n. a way or road by land, (स्थल-वर्त्मना, inst. c. by land, as opposed to जल-मार्गेण, by water.) —स्थल-विग्रह, अस्, m. a battle on level ground. —स्थल-शुद्धि, इस्, f. purification or clearance of a place from impurity. —स्थल-शृङ्गाट or स्थल-शृङ्गाटक, अस्, m. the plant Tribulus Lanuginosus (= गो-क्षुर)। —स्थल-सीमन्, आ, m. a land-mark, boundary. —स्थल-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing or being on dry ground, being on terra firma, being on shore. —स्थलान्तर (°ल-अन्°), अम्, n. another place. —स्थलारूढ (°ल-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, alighted on the ground. —स्थले-रुह, अस्, आ, अम्, growing on dry ground; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= गृह-कु-मारी); another plant (= दग्धा). —स्थले-शय, अस्, आ, अम्, sleeping on dry ground; (अस्), m. any amphibious animal (such as a tortoise, otter, &c.).
53156: स्थली, f. dry ground, &c.; see under स्थल above. —स्थली-देवता, f. a local divinity, deity of the soil or tutelary deity presiding over some par-ticular spot (as a field, grove, village, &c.), a kind of faun or dryad.
53157: स्थलीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or belonging to dry ground, terrestrial; belonging to a place, local.
53158: स्थलेयु, उस्, m., N. of a king.
53160: स्थविष्ठ स्थविष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, (superl. of स्थूल), largest, most bulky; very big, very fat or corpulent.
53161: स्थवीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of स्थूल), larger, bigger, more bulky, fatter, stronger; very fat, very corpulent.
53162: स्था 1. स्था, cl. 1. P. (ep. and in some special significations also A.) तिष्ठति, -ते (स्थात् = तिष्ठतु, Ṛg-veda II. 3, 10), तस्थौ (2nd sing, तस्थिथ or तस्थाथ, 1st du. तस्थिव), तस्थे, स्थास्यति, -ते, अस्थात् (3rd pl. अस्थुः), अस्-थित (3rd pl. अस्थिषत), Prec. स्थेयात्, स्था-सीष्ट, स्थातुम्, to stand (often with inst., e. g. पादाभ्यां स्था, to stand on the feet; जानुभ्यां स्था, to stand on the knees, i. e. to kneel); to stand still, stand firmly; to stay, stop, abide, dwell, remain, rest, wait; to stop, cease, desist; to rest on, depend on (sometimes A.); to be in any situation or state or position; to be, exist, live; to be at hand, be near or at the side; to abide or continue or be en-gaged in any act or course of action, practice, per-form, behave, occupy one's self with, (sometimes with loc., e. g. शासने स्था, to abide in a command, i. e. to be obedient; sometimes with inst., e. g. सामादिभिः स्था, to practice or continue practising conciliation, &c.; मौन-व्रतेन स्था, to continue observing a vow of silence; sometimes with ind. part., especially if a habit or continuous course of action is implied, e. g. धर्मम् आश्रित्य तिष्ठति, he continues prac-tising virtue); to stand as a prostitute, give one's self up to sexual embrace, offer one's self to (A., e. g. देव-दत्ताय तिष्ठते, she offers herself to Deva-datta, Pāṇ. 1. 4, 34): Pass. स्थीयते, 2nd fut. स्था-स्यते or स्थायिष्यते, Aor. अस्थायि, to be stood; to be stayed or remained or abided, to be fixed or located, &c. (frequently used impersonally, e. g. मया स्थीयताम्, let it be abided by me, i. e. I must abide): Caus. स्थापयति, -ते (sometimes regarded as a nominal fr. स्थिर), -यितुम्, Aor. अतिष्ठिपत्, -त, to cause to stand; to cause to stand still or firmly; to fix, settle, establish, set up, found, institute, erect, build; to place, put, lo-cate, set, lay; to stop, arrest, restrain, hold in; to cause to be in any state or position; to cause to continue, make durable; to cause to live; to give in marriage; to make (with two acc.); to instruct in (with two acc.): Desid. तिष्ठासति, -ते: Intens. तेष्ठीयते, तास्थाति; [cf. Zend hi-stā-mi = Sans. ति-ष्ठा-मि: Gr. ἵ-στη-μι, ἔ-στη-ν, στά-σι-ς, στα-μίν, στά-μνο-ς, ἰ-στό-ς, στή-μην, στή-λη, στα-τήρ, στα-θ-ερό-ς, στα-θ-μό-ς, στῆ-θ-ο-ς, στε-νό-ς; (with the Caus. may be compared also, according to some) στέφ-ω (for στεπ-ω), στέμ-μα, στέφ-ος, στέφ-ανο-ς, στεφ-άνη, τόπ-ο-ς: Lat. st-o, si-st-o, stă-ti-m, stă-ti-o, Sta-tor, stă-tu-s, stă-tu-o, stă-tua, stā-men, stă-bu-lu-m, stă-bi-li-s; (also with the Caus.) stipa-re, stipatores, stipulāri, stapia; (according to some also) stup-eo, stup-idu-s: Old Germ. stā-m, stedi, standa, stat: Goth. stan-dan, ‘to stand;’ stath-s, ‘a place;’ stol-s, ‘a stool, throne:’ Angl. Sax. stan-dan, stand, studu, stund: Slav. sta-ti, ‘to stand:’ Lith. stó-ti, ‘to stand;’ sta-tù-s, ‘stand-ing;’ statý-ti, ‘to place;’ sto-na-s, ‘a stand, sta-tion;’ stá-kle-s, ‘a loom:’ Hib. sta-d, ‘stop, delay, state, condition;’ stadaim, ‘I stand, stop.’]
53163: तस्थिवस्, वान्, -थुषी, वत्, one who has stood.
53164: स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing, staying, abiding, being situated, living, existing (generally found at the end of comps., e. g. गर्भ-स्°, जल-स्°, दूर-स्°); a place, spot, ground, = स्थल (according to Śabda-k.). —स्थ-पति, इस्, m. (probably fr. स्थ + पति, but according to some from the Caus. of rt. 1. स्था), ‘ground-lord,’ a sovereign, chief, king (according to Kātyāyana's Śrauta-sūtras XXII. 11, 11, &c. a Stha-pati is a Vaiśya, or even a person of lower caste, who has celebrated the Go-sava sacrifice after being chosen king); an architect; a master carpenter or mason, wheelwright; a charioteer; one who sacrifices to Vṛhas-pati, a performer of the Vṛhas-pati sacrifice; a guard or attendant of the women's apartments; N. of Kuvera; (इस्, इस्, इ), chief, best, principal.
53165: स्थवि, इस्, m. a weaver; heaven (= स्वर्ग); = जङ्गम (according to Śabda-k.).
53166: स्थविर, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed, firm, steady [cf. स्था-विर]; old, aged, ancient, (सप्तत्या स्थविरः, one who is seventy years old, see स्थाविर); (अस्), m. an old man; a beggar; epithet of Brahmā; (आ), f. an old woman; a kind of plant, = महा-श्रावणी; (अम्), n. = शैलेय।
53167: 2. स्था, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. standing, stationary, (ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda X. 88, 4. स्थाः = स्था-वरं वृक्षादि रूपम्; see also Nirukta V. 3.)
53168: स्थाणु, उस्, उस्, उ, firm, fixed, steady, stable, im-movable, motionless; (उस्), m., N. of Śiva; a stake, post, pile; a peg, pin, pillar; the gnomon of a dial; a spear, dart; a nest of white ants; the drug or per-fume called Jīvaka, q. v.; (उस्, उ), m. n. a branchless trunk or stem, the trunk of a lopped tree or of any tree, any bare stock or stem. —स्थाणु-च्छेद, अस्, m. one who cuts down the trunks of trees, one who clears away timber, (Manu IX. 44.) —स्थाणु-तीर्-थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —स्थाणु-भ्रम, अस्, m. mistaking anything for a post. —स्थाणु-वत्, ind. like a post. —स्थाणु-वनौकस् (°न-ओक्°), आस्, आस्, अस्, inhabiting Śiva's forest. —स्थाण्व्-ईश्वर, अस्, m., N. of a particular Śiva-liṅga.
53169: स्थातव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be stood; to be stayed or remained; to be fixed.
53170: स्थातुस्, n. (according to some modern scholars an old nom. sing. neut. for the later स्थातृ), Ved. anything standing or stationary (opposed to चरथ, see Ṛg-veda I. 58, 5).
53171: स्थातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, who or what stands or stays stationary, standing (frequently opposed to जगत् in the phrase स्थातुर् जगतश्च, e. g. विश्वस्य स्था-तुर् जगतश्च गोपाः, the preserver of everything that stands and moves, Ṛg-veda VII. 60, 2); [cf. Lat. stator.]
53172: स्थान, अम्, n. the act of standing or staying, stay, continuance, the being fixed or stationary; state, condition; a stationary state or condition, (one of the three aims or results of state policy; it is de-scribed as a kind of neutral or middle state character-ized by neither loss nor gain, failure nor success); the act of standing firm so as to resist a charge, firm or calm bearing of troops, (Manu VII. 190); halt; the stamina of a kingdom, that which constitutes its chief strength or by virtue of which it exists, (regarded as consisting of four parts, viz. army, treasury, city, and territory, Manu VII. 56); the place of standing or staying, any place, spot, locality, site, situation, position, posture, station, post; office, appointment, rank, dignity, degree; proper or right place; the place or organ of utterance of any letter (which, ac-cording to Pāṇini, are eight, viz. कण्ठ, the throat; तालु, the palate; मूर्धन्, the top of the palate; दन्त, the teeth; ओष्ठ, the lips; कण्ठ-तालु, the throat and palate; कण्ठोष्ठ, the throat and lips; दन्तोष्ठ, the teeth and lips; to which may be added नासिका, which is the place of utterance for the true Anusvāra, and उरस्, the chest, which is said to be the place of Visarga); dwelling-place, abode, house; country, region, district; a town, city; a par-ticular place or sphere assigned after death to those who do their duty or neglect it, (that of virtuous Brāhmans is called Prājāpatya; of Kṣatriyas, Aindra; of Vaiśyas, Māruta; of Śūdras, Gāndharva; similarly, neglectors of duty have places of punishment assigned to them); a holy place; an altar; an open place in a town, green, plain, square; part or division of a book, section, chapter; the part or character of an actor; interval, opportunity, leisure; an object (e. g. शुल्क-स्थ्°, an object of toll, taxation; पूजा-स्थ्°, object of honour; कोप-स्थ्°, object of anger); a modulation of the voice, note, tone (of which, ac-cording to the Ṛg-veda-Prātiśākhya, there are three; see मन्द्र); likeness, resemblance; intimation; (स्थाने), loc. c. in the right or proper place, pro-perly, suitably, appropriately, justly, fitly, truly; at the right or appropriate moment, opportunely; some-times; in the place of, in the room of, in lieu of, instead of (with gen.; in Pāṇini's grammar, when the gen. c. stands alone, the word स्थाने has to be supplied, thus हन्तेर् जः means that ज is to be sub-stituted ‘in place of’ हन्, see Pāṇ. I. 1, 49); on account of, because of; like, resembling, similarly, as; [cf. δύστηνος (i. e. δυσ-στηνος), ἄ-στηνος, ἀστήν, ἀσταίνω, δυσταίνω.] —स्थान-चञ्चला, f. the plant Ocimum Pilosum (= वर्वरी). —स्थान-चिन्तक, अस्, m. an officer who superintends places of residence or official dwellings or provides quarters for an army, a kind of quarter-master. —स्थान-च्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्थान-भ्रष्ट below. —स्थान-तस्, ind. according to place or station; in regard to the place or organ of utterance. —स्था-न-त्याग, अस्, m. desertion of post, leaving one's place. —स्थान-पाल, अस्, m. ‘place-protector, place-keeper,’ a watchman, sentinel, policeman. —स्थान-प्रच्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, ejected from a station or post, removed from an office, &c. —स्थान-भूमि, इस्, f. a dwelling-place, mansion. —स्थान-भ्रष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen or removed from any place or station, ejected from an office, displaced, out of place. —स्थान-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. the greatness or glory of any place, a kind of divine virtue sup-posed to be inherent in a sacred spot, and to operate upon those who visit it. —स्थान-योग, अस्, m. as-signment of suitable places, proper mode or place for preserving articles, (Manu IX. 332.) —स्थान-रक्-षक, अस्, m. = स्थान-पाल. —स्थान-विभाग, अस्, m. subdivision of a number according to the places of its figures. —स्थान-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, abid-ing in one place, staying at home. —स्थनाध्य-क्ष (°न-अध्°), अस्, m. the superintendent of any place or post; a local governor; a watchman, police-officer. —स्थानान्तर (°न-अन्°), अम्, n. another place. —स्थानान्तर-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to another place, gone away. —स्थानान्य-त्व (°न-अन्°), अम्, n. difference or diversity of place. —स्था-नाभाव (°न-अभ्°), अस्, m. the want of a place or situation. —स्थानासन (°न-आस्°), ए, n. du. stand-ing and sitting down. —स्थानासन-विहार-वत्, आन्, m. (a pupil) occupying the station and seat and place of religious exercises (of his preceptor, Manu II. 248). —स्थानासेध (°न-आस्°), अस्, m. confine-ment to a place, imprisonment, arrest. —स्थानेश्वर (°न-ईश्°), N. of a place.
53173: स्थानक, अम्, n. a position, situation; a par-ticular point or situation in dramatic action, (पताका-स्थानक, a striking situation introduced as an episode into the regular plot of a drama); a city, town; a basin or trench dug for water at the root of a tree; froth or a kind of scum on spirits or wine; a mode of recitation; a division or section of the Taittirīya branch of the Yajur-veda.
53174: स्थानिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to a place or site, local; (in grammar) that which takes the place of anything else or is substituted for it; (अस्), m. any one holding an official post, a placeman, the governor of a place, superintendent of a district, manager of a temple.
53175: स्थानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a place, having fixedness, placed, abiding, permanent; having a substitute; (ई), m. (in Pāṇini's grammar) the original form or primitive element (i. e. that form for which anything is substi-tuted; the substituted form which takes its place being called आदेश); that which has a place, that which has a place in a sentence or is actually expressed. —स्था-नि-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, being the original or primitive form. —स्थानि-वत्, ind. (in grammar) like the original form or primitive element, (the आदेश or substituted form is said to be स्थानि-वत् when it is liable to all the rules which hold good for the primi-tive.) —स्थानिवत्-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being like the original form or element. —स्थान्य्-आश्रय, अस्, आ, अम्, depending on the primitive form (said of a grammatical operation).
53176: स्थानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or suitable to any place, prevailing in any place, local; (अम्), n. a town, city.
53177: स्थापक, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. the Caus.), causing to stand, placing, fixing, establishing, founding, order-ing, regulating; (अस्), m. the establisher or director of the stage-business, a kind of stage-manager; the founder of a temple, erector of an image.
53178: स्थापत्य, अस्, m. (fr. स्थ-पति), a guard of the women's apartments; (अम्), n. architecture, building, erecting. —स्थापत्य-वेद, अस्, m. ‘the science of architecture,’ one of the four Upa-vedas, (see उप-वेद।)
53179: स्थापन, अम्, n. (fr. the Caus.), the act of caus-ing to stand, placing, fixing, establishing, erecting, founding, instituting, regulating, directing, appoint-ing; fixing the thoughts, concentration of the mind, abstraction; a dwelling, habitation; a ceremony per-formed when a mother perceives the first signs of living conception, = पुं-सवन; (आ), f. placing, fixing, establishing, regulating, arranging (as a drama &c.), stage-management; (ई), f. a kind of plant (= पाठा).
53180: स्थापनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be placed or fixed or established.
53181: स्थापयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to stand, fixing, placing, establishing.
53182: स्थापयित्वा, ind. having placed or fixed, having established or erected, &c.
53183: स्थापित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused or made to stand, fixed, established, placed, located, deposited; set up, erected; founded, instituted, endowed, set apart; placed in any post or situation, appointed; ordered, regulated, directed, enjoined, ordained, enacted; set-tled, ascertained, certain; firm, steady.
53184: स्थापितवत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has placed or fixed, &c.
53185: स्थाप्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be placed or deposited; to be fixed or established; (अम्), n. a deposit, pledge (= निक्षेप). —स्थाप्यापहरण (°य-अप्°), अम्, n. the stealing or embezzling of a deposit.
53186: स्थामन्, अ, n. strength, power, stamina; fixity, stability.
53187: स्थायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, standing, staying, being, situ-ated (often at end of comps., cf. अन्तर-स्थ्°); abid-ing, stopping, fixed, stationary, enduring, continuing, permanent, constant, lasting (as a feeling or state, see स्थायि-भाव below); steady, firm, unchange-able, invariable; (इ), n. anything lasting, a permanent state or condition (opposed to व्य्-अभिचारिन्, q. v.). —स्थायि-ता, f. or स्थायि-त्व, अम्, n. permanency, steadiness, fixedness, constancy, invariableness. —स्था-यि-भाव, अस्, m. a particular fixed or permanent condition of mind or body, lasting feeling (as form-ing a class of feelings or conditions which are fa-vourite subjects of description in poetical and dramatic compositions; these Sthāyi-bhāvas are opposed to the Vyabhicāri-bhāvas, and are said in the Sāhitya-darpaṇa to be eight in number, viz. 1. रति, love or desire; 2. हास, mirth; 3. शोक, sorrow; 4. क्रो-ध, resentment; 5. उत्साह, high-mindedness or heroism; 6. भय, terror; 7. जुगुप्सा, disgust or aversion; 8. विस्मय, surprise; to which is some-times added a ninth, viz. शम, quietism).
53188: स्थायुक, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, disposed to stay or last, apt to endure, of a steady nature, abiding, stopping, stationary, steady, firm; (अस्), m. the overseer of a village.
53189: स्थाल, अम्, n. a plate or dish (generally made of some metal and used in eating); a cooking-pot, caldron or any culinary utensil. —स्थाल-रूप, अम्, n. the form or representation of a pot.
53190: स्थाली, f. an earthen pot or pan, cooking-pot, caldron, kettle, boiler; a particular vessel used in the preparation of Soma; the substitution of a cooked offering of rice &c. for the offering of meat at the Māṃsāṣṭakā, q. v.; the trumpet-flower, Bignonia Suaveolens. —स्थाली-दरण, अम्, n. the breaking of a pot. —स्थाली-पक्व, अस्, आ, अम्, cooked or dressed in a pot, boiled. —स्थाली-पाक, अस्, m., Ved. a particular religious act performed by a house-holder, a cooked offering of rice, &c.; (आस्), m. pl., scil. मन्त्राः, epithet of particular Vedic hymns. —स्थाली-पुरीष, अम्, n. the sediment or dirt sticking to a kettle or cooking-pot. —स्थाली-पु-लाक, अस्, m. boiled rice in a cooking-pot; an illus-tration derived from the rule of boiled rice in a pot (by which all the grains are equally moistened by the heated water). —स्थाली-विल, अम्, n. the interior or hollow of a caldron or cooking-pot. —स्थाली-विलीय or स्थाली-विल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be boiled or cooked in a pot. —स्थाली-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a kind of plant or tree (= नन्दी-वृक्ष, अश्वत्थ-भेद).
53191: स्थावन्, आ, अरी, अ, standing, stable, stationary.
53192: स्थावर, अस्, आ, अम्, standing still, not moving, not having the power of motion, not locomotive, fixed to one spot, fixed, stationary, firm, stable, immov-able, (opposed to जङ्गम, q. v.); inert, inactive, slow (said of poison); regular, established; (अस्), m. a mountain; (अम्), n. any stationary or inanimate object (as a plant, mineral, &c.; these stationary objects constituted the seventh creation of Brahmā or तस्थुषां सर्ग, see under सर्ग; cf. Manu I. 41); a bow-string; immovable property, real estate (such as land or houses); a heir-loom, family possession (such as jewels &c. which have been long preserved in a family and ought not to be sold). —स्थावर-ता, f. fixedness, stability, the quality of being stationary, immobility; the state of a vegetable or mineral, (Manu XII. 9.) —स्थावर-जङ्गम, अम्, n. or आनि, n. pl. things stationary and movable or inanimate and animate, (Manu I. 41.) —स्थाव-रादि (°र-आदि), n. the poison called Vatsa-nābha, q. v. —स्थावरास्थावर (°र-अस्°), अम्, n. things stationary and movable, immovable and movable property.
53193: स्थाविर, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. स्थविर), thick, firm (Ved.); (अम्), n. old age (described as commencing after seventy in men and after fifty in women, and ending at ninety, after which period a man is called वर्षीयस्).
53194: स्थासक, अस्, m. perfuming or smearing the body with fragrant unguents (of sandal &c.); a bubble of water or any fluid.
53195: स्थासु, उ, n. bodily strength or stamina.
53196: स्थास्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, disposed to stand, firm, stationary, immovable, fixed, stable; durable, per-manent, eternal; a tree or plant (= वृक्ष; cf. स्थावर). —स्थास्नु-ता, f. firmness, stability, dura-bility.
53197: स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, stood, stayed, remained, stopped; standing; standing up, risen; staying, resting, abiding, (उच्चावचेषु स्थित, abiding in all things high and low); being, situated, existing, living; stood still, standing still, desisted, stopped; fixed, permanent, settled, steady, firm, immovable; steadfast, determined, resolved, decreed, established; steady or steadfast in conduct; faithful to a promise or agreement; upright, virtuous; agreed, engaged, contracted, promised; being close at hand, ready; (अम्), n. (in Vedic grammar), scil. पद, a word standing by itself (i. e. without the particle इति in the Pada text; opposed to उप-स्थित). —स्थित-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, steady-minded, firm-minded, firm, unmoved, calm. —स्थित-पाठ्य, (in the drama) recitation in Prākṛt by a woman standing. —स्थित-प्रज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in judgment or wisdom, free from fancies or hallucinations, calm, contented. —स्थित-प्रेमन्, आ, m. ‘firm in affection,’ a firm or faithful friend. —स्थितोपस्थित (°त-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, (a word) with and without the particle इति (in the Pada text; see स्थित above).
53198: स्थितवत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has stood or stayed or abided.
53199: स्थिति, इस्, f. standing, staying, remaining, con-tinuing, living, residing, abiding; stay, residence; standing still, stopping, continuance in one state; remaining stationary, stability, duration, fixedness, fixity, a firm position; stop, cessation; pause; any situation, state, position; posture, condition, natural state, state of a case; good condition, well-doing, welfare; station, high station, rank, dignity; per-manence; continuance or steadfastness in the path of duty, steadiness, correctness of conduct, propriety, good manners; consistency; establishment of good order (in a government); settled rule, sure or fixed decision, ordinance, decree, axiom, maxim; settled determination; term, limit, boundary; (in philo-sophy) inertia, resistance to motion; one of the three states through which the system of created things and every individual being passes, (these three states are, 1. उत्पत्ति, arising into being; 2. स्थिति, continuance in life; 3. लय, dissolution); (in astronomy) duration of an eclipse; (in Vedic grammar) the standing of a word by itself (i. e. without the particle इति, see स्थित). —स्थिति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing firmness or stability, firm, stable; steady (in purpose or conduct), upright, firm, virtuous. —स्थिति-स्थापक, अस्, आ, अम्, fixing in a (former or original) state or condition, capable of placing in or restoring to a (previous) form or position, having elastic properties; (अस्), m. (ac-cording to some also अम्, n.), the capability of placing in or recovering a (previous) position or condition, elasticity.
53200: स्थित्वा, ind. having stood or stayed or stopped, &c.
53201: स्थिर, अस्, आ, अम्, firm, fixed, steady, steadfast; unfluctuating, permanent, enduring, durable, settled, lasting; not moving, immovable, still, placid, calm, quiescent, cool, composed, collected, free from pas-sion; steadfast or steady in conduct; constant, faithful, determined; certain, sure, convinced; firm, hard, solid, strong; (अस्), m. a deity, immortal; epithet of Śiva; of Kārttikeya; a mountain; a tree; a bull; final emancipation from existence; the planet Saturn; a particular plant (= 1. धव); N. of a particular astronomical Yoga; of certain zodiacal signs (viz. Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; so called because any work done under these signs is supposed to be lasting); (आ), f. a strong-minded woman; the earth; the shrub Śāla-parṇī; a medi-cinal root (= काकोली); the silk-cotton tree; [cf. Gr. στερεό-ς, στεῤῤό-ς, στέρι-φο-ς, στερίφη, στεῖρα, στήρ-ιγξ, στηρίζ-ω, στελεόν: Lat. steri-li-s, stīr-ia, stilla, stolidus, stultus: Goth. stairo: Old Germ. staren, storren, stornen, ga-starken, starh-jan, &c.: Angl. Sax. starian, starc: Lith. styr-u, ‘to be stiff or benumbed;’ ster-va, ‘a carcass.’] —स्थिर-कुट्टक, अस्, m. (in algebra) a steady pulverizer, constant multiplier, common divisor (ap-plied to a particular kind of common divisor). —स्थिर-गन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, having durable per-fume, strong-scented; (अस्), m. the Campaka tree, Michelia Champaca; (आ), f. Pandanus Odoratissimus (= केतकी); the trumpet-flower (= पाटला). —स्थि-र-चक्र, अस्, m. a particular Jina or Bodhi-sattva (= मञ्जु-श्री). —स्थिर-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, or स्थिर-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, firm-minded, firm, resolute, constant, steady. —स्थिर-च्छद, अस्, m. ‘firm-leafed,’ the birch tree (= भूर्ज-पत्त्र). —स्थिर-च्छाय, अस्, m. ‘having deep shade,’ a tree which gives shelter to travellers; any tree. —स्थिर-जिह्व, अस्, m. ‘firm-tongued,’ a fish. —स्थिर-जीविता, f. ‘firm-lived,’ the silk-cotton tree. —स्थिर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more firm, fixed, stationary; very firm or permanent, durable, eternal. —स्थिर-ता, f. or स्थिर-त्व, अम्, n. firmness, stability, steadiness, steadfastness; moral firmness, fortitude; fearlessness. —स्थिर-दंष्ट्र, अस्, m. ‘strong-toothed,’ a snake; N. of Viṣṇu in the boar-Avatāra; = ध्वनि (according to Śabda-k.). —स्थिर-धन्वन्, आ, आ, अ, having or armed with a strong bow (said of Rudra, Ṛg-veda VII. 46, 1). —स्थिर-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, firm-minded, resolute, per-severing. —स्थिर-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘firm-leafed,’ the marshy date tree. —स्थिर-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘firm-flowered,’ the Campaka tree; the Vakula tree. —स्थिर-पुष्पिन्, ई, m. ‘strong-flowered,’ the Tilaka tree. —स्थिर-प्रतिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, persist-ing in an assertion, pertinacious; faithful to a promise. —स्थिर-प्रतिबन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, firm in resist-ance, pertinacious, obstinate. —स्थिर-प्रतिष्ठा, f. a firm resting-place, fixed residence. —स्थिर-प्रेमन्, आ, आ, अ, firm or steady in affection, a firm friend. —स्थिर-प्स्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having con-stant food; 53257: स्नात्, आन्, आती or आन्ती, आत्, bathing, performing ablution.
53258: स्नात, अस्, आ, अम्, bathed, washed, purified by ab-lution, pure; (अस्), m. one whose spiritual instruc-tion is finished; an initiated householder. —स्नाता-नुलिप्त (°त-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who is both bathed and anointed.
53259: स्नातक, अस्, m. a Brāhman who has performed the ceremony of ablution (cf. आ-प्लव) required on his finishing his first Āśrama or period of studentship as a Brahma-cārin (and on becoming initiated into the second Āśrama or order of a Gṛha-stha, q. v.); a Brāhman just returned from the house of his pre-ceptor and become a married man or initiated house-holder, (three kinds of Snātakas are enumerated, 1. the Vidyā-snātaka or Brahma-cārin, who, at the end of his period of studentship, has completed a course of study of the Vedas only; 2. the Vrata-snātaka, who has completed the prescribed Vratas or vowed observances, such as fasting, continence, &c., without becoming perfect in the Vedas; 3. the Vidyā-vrata-snātaka or Ubhaya-snātaka, who has com-pleted both the Vedas and the Vratas; this last is of course regarded as the highest kind, see Kullūka on Manu III. 2); a Brāhman who is a Bhikṣu or asker of alms for any religious object or legitimate purpose, (nine kinds are enumerated in Manu XI. 1); any man of the first three classes who is an initiated householder.
53260: स्नातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who bathes or washes, a bather.
53261: स्नात्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fit for ablutions, capable of being used for bathing, (Sāy. स्नात्वाः = स्नानार्-हाः, Ṛg-veda X. 71, 7.)
53262: स्नात्वा (Ved. also स्नात्वी), ind. having bathed or washed, having performed ablutions.
53263: स्नान, अम्, n. bathing, washing, ablution, dipping in water, wetting, purification by bathing, religious or ceremonial ablution, bathing in sacred waters (considered as a daily observance or as an essential part of some ceremonial); the ceremony of bathing or anointing an idol; anything used in ablution (e. g. water, perfumed powder for the body, &c.). —स्ना-न-तृण, अम्, n. ‘bathing-grass,’ Kuśa grass. —स्ना-न-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary by Gopī-nātha on the Snāna-sūtra. —स्नान-द्रोणी, f. a bathing-tub. —स्नान-यात्रा, f. ‘bathing procession,’ the festival held on the day of full moon in the month Jyeṣṭha (when images of Kṛṣṇa as Jagan-nātha are carried out and bathed; in Orissa this festival is called Ratha-yātrā). —स्नानयात्रिक, अस्, आ, अम्, attend-ing the above procession at the bathing of Jagan-nātha. —स्नान-वस्त्र, अम्, n. a cloth put on for bathing, a bathing-dress, wet cloth. —स्नान-विधि, इस्, m. the rules of ablution, proper manner of bathing; N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Sāma-veda. —स्नान-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, fond of bathing, observing or performing ablution (especially in sacred waters). —स्नान-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a Sūtra work (ascribed to Kātyāyana). —स्नानसूत्र-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a summary of a commentary by Hari-jīvana-miśra on the Snāna-sūtra. —स्नानागार (°न-आग्°), अम्, n. a bath-room. —स्नानोत्तीर्ण (°न-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, rising up from a bath, one who has just completed his ablutions.
53264: स्नानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for bathing or ablution, suitable for bathing; (अम्), n. water or any article (such as unguents, perfumed powders, &c.) proper for bathing. —स्नानीय-वस्त्र, अम्, n. a cloth tied round the waist for bathing, a bathing dress.
53265: स्नापक, अस्, m. (fr. the Caus.), a servant who bathes his master or attends him while bathing (bringing water and pouring it over his person).
53266: स्नापन, अम्, n. the act of causing to bathe or attending a person while bathing, (Manu II. 209.) —स्नापनोच्छिष्ट-भोजन (°न-उच्°), ए, n. du. the act of bathing another person and eating his leavings, (Manu II. 209.)
53267: स्नापित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to bathe, attended on while bathing, immersed.
53268: स्नायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bathing; (ई), m. a bather, per-former of ablutions.
53269: स्नास्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, about to bathe or perform an initiatory ceremonial ablution; (अन्), m. a religious student about to become a Snātaka, (Manu II. 245.)
53270: स्नायु स्नायु, उस्, f. (according to some उस्, m.; said in Uṇādi-s. I. 1. to be fr. rt. स्ना), a sinew, tendon, muscle (described as वायु-वाहिनी-नाडी, ‘a tubular vessel conveying vital air’); the string of a bow; [cf. probably Gr. νεῦρο-ν, νευρ-ά; Lat. ner-vu-s, nerviœ, nervosus; Old Germ. snar-a, snar-ahha, snuor, narwa; Old Sax. naru; Lith. nar-a-s, ner-u.] —स्नायु-बन्धन, अम्, n. a sinew-string. —स्नायु-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of tendons. —स्नायु-युत, अस्, आ, अम्, possessed of tendons, (Manu VI. 76.) —स्नायु-रज्जु, उस्, उस्, उ, having tendons for cords (said of the body). —स्नाय्व्-अर्मन्, अ, n. a kind of disease of the eyes.
53272: स्नाव, अस्, m. (the form स्नावानि, neut. pl., occurs), a tendon, muscle; (according to some) the vascular membrane investing the bones; [cf. probably Old Germ. senwa; Angl. Sax. sinu, sinw, senw.]
53273: स्नावन्, आ, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 112. fr. rt. स्ना), a muscle, sinew (Ved.); = रसिक, a lover (?).
53275: स्निट् स्निट्, cl. 10. P. स्नेटयति, to go; to love, be in love; [cf. rt. 1. स्निह् below.]
53276: स्निह् 1. स्निह्, cl. 4. P. स्निह्यति, सिष्णेह, स्नेहिष्यति or स्नेक्ष्यति, अस्निहत्, स्नेहितुम् or स्नेग्धुम् or स्नेढुम्, (probably originally) to be adhesive or sticky or viscid; to be bland; to be easily attached; to have affection for, love, regard; to be fond of (with gen.); to be kind to or pleased with; cl. 10. P. स्नेहयति, &c., to be unctuous or greasy: Pass. स्निह्यते, Aor. अस्नेहि: Caus. स्नेहयति, &c., Aor. असिष्णिहत्, to make unctuous, anoint, lubricate; to cause to love, &c.; to dissolve, destroy, kill, slay, (in Naigh. II. 19. स्नेह-यति and [according to some readings] स्नेहति are enumerated amongst the वध-कर्माणः): Desid. सिस्नेहिषति, सिस्निहिषति, सिस्निक्षति: Intens. सेष्णिह्यते, सेष्णेग्धि or सेष्णेढि।
53277: स्निग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, oily, oleaginous, unctuous, greasy, fat, sticky, viscid, cohesive, adhesive; emol-lient, smooth; glossy, shining, resplendent; moist, wet; cooling; bland, kind, amiable; attached, lov-ing, tender, affectionate, friendly, well affected; lovely, agreeable; coarse, thick, dense; (अस्), m. a friend; a sort of pine, (see स्निग्ध-दारु below); the red castor-oil plant; scil. गण्डूष, a particular mode of rinsing the mouth; (आ), f. marrow, = मेदा; (अम्), n. oil; bees'-wax; light, lustre; thickness, coarseness. —स्निग्ध-जन, अस्, m. an affectionate or friendly person, a friend. —स्निग्ध-तण्डुल, अस्, m. a kind of rice of quick growth (= षष्टिक)। —स्निग्ध-ता, f. or स्निग्ध-त्व, अम्, n. unctuous-ness, oiliness; blandness; tenderness, kindness, affec-tion, love. —स्निग्ध-दारु, उ, n. a sort of pine, Pinus Longifolia (= सरल); another kind, Pinus Devadaru. —स्निग्ध-पत्त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having smooth or glossy leaves; (अस्, आ), m. f. the jujube, Zizyphus Jujuba; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= काश्-मरी); another kind (= पालक्या). —स्निग्ध-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. ‘having smooth leaves,’ a kind of grass; other plants (= घृत-करञ्ज; = गुच्छ-करञ्ज). —स्निग्ध-पिण्डीतक, अस्, m. a kind of Madana tree. —स्निग्ध-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, having unctuous fruit, having glossy fruit; (आ), f. the ich-neumon plant (= नाकुली). —स्निग्ध-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, having a glossy or bright colour; having a soft or agreeable complexion.
53278: स्निग्ध्वा or स्निहित्वा, ind. becoming unctuous, becoming bland or affectionate.
53279: 2. स्निह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, or क्, क्, क्, loving, affectionate; one who loves.
53280: स्नीढ, अस्, आ, अम्, attached, bland, tender, loving.
53282: स्नीहिति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. killing, slaying.
53283: स्नीहिती, f., Ved. killing, slaying; malevolent, (Sāy. = वध-कारिणी, Ṛg-veda I. 74, 2.)
53284: स्नेह, अस्, m. oiliness, unctuousness, fattiness, greasiness, lubricity, viscidity (as one of the twenty-four Guṇas of the Vaiśeṣika branch of the Nyāya phil.); moisture; blandness, tenderness, love, affec-tion, kindness; filial love or affection; any unctuous or oleaginous substance, oil, grease, fat, an unguent; a fluid of the body; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a caste (cor-responding to the Vaiśyas). —स्नेह-गुणित, अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with love or affection. —स्नेह-च्छेद, अस्, m. interruption of friendship, cessation or loss of regard. —स्नेह-पक्व, अस्, आ, अम्, cooked or dressed with oil. —स्नेह-पात्र, अम्, n. a worthy object of affection. —स्नेह-पूर्वम्, ind. preceded by affection, affectionately, tenderly, fondly. —स्नेह-प्रवृत्ति, इस्, f. ‘course of friendship,’ affection, love. —स्नेह-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, fond of oil; (अस्), m. a lamp. —स्नेह-भाण्ड, अम्, n. an oil-vessel, pot of oil. —स्नेहभाण्ड-जीविन्, ई, m. living by oil-vessels, an oilman. —स्नेह-भू, ऊस्, m. phlegm, rheum, the phlegmatic humor. —स्नेह-भूमि, इस्, f. ‘oil-ground, oil-source,’ any substance yielding oil or grease; any object of affection, one worthy of love. —स्नेह-रङ्ग, अस्, m. ‘oil-coloured,’ se-samum. —स्नेह-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, unctuous, oily; possessed of affection, affectionate; (अती), f. = मेदा (according to Śabda-k.). —स्नेह-वस्ति, इस्, f. a clyster or injection of oil, oily enema. —स्नेह-विद्-ध, अस्, m. ‘pierced or impregnated with oil,’ a sort of pine, Pinus Devadaru (according to Śabda-k. अम्, n.). —स्नेह-विमर्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, rubbed or anointed with oil. —स्नेह-वीज, अस्, आ, अम्, having oily seeds, causing unctuousness, &c.; (अस्), m. the Piyāla tree. —स्नेह-व्यक्ति, इस्, f. manifestation or display of friendship. —स्नेह-संयुक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, mixed with oil, dressed with ghee, (Manu V. 24.) —स्नेह-सम्भाष, अस्, m. kind conversation. —स्नेहाक्त (°ह-अक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, anointed with oil, oiled, greased, lubricated. —स्नेहानुवृत्ति (°ह-अन्°), इस्, f. continuance of affection, affectionate or friendly intercourse. —स्नेहाश (°ह-आश), अस्, m. ‘oil-consumer,’ a lamp.
53285: स्नेहन्, आ, m. a friend; the moon; a kind of disease.
53286: स्नेहन, अस्, ई, अम्, anointing, lubricating; de-stroying; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva; (अम्), n. the act of anointing, unction, lubrication, rubbing or smear-ing with oil or unguents; unctuousness, being or becoming oily, &c.; an emollient, unguent, lini-ment.
53287: स्नेहनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be anointed or lubri-cated; to be loved.
53288: स्नेहयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. destroying, killing, murdering.
53289: स्नेहित, अस्, आ, अम्, anointed, smeared with oil; loved, beloved; kind, affectionate; (अस्), m. a loved one, friend.
53290: स्नेहितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्नेहनीय above.
53291: स्नेहिती, f., Ved. destroying, killing; [cf. स्नीहिती above.]
53293: स्नेहिन्, ई, इनी, इ, oily, unctuous, fat; attached, af-fectionate, friendly; (ई), m. an anointer, smearer; a painter; a friend.
53294: स्नेहु, उस्, m. the moon; a kind of disease; [cf. स्नेहन्।]
53295: स्नैग्ध्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्निग्ध), unctuousness, oiliness, smoothness, lubricity, blandness; tenderness, fondness; affectionateness.
53296: स्नु 1. स्नु (probably connected with rt. स्ना), cl. 2. P. स्नौति, सुष्णाव, स्नविष्-यति, अस्नावीत्, स्नवितुम्, to drip, trickle, distil, fall in drops, drop, ooze, run out, leak; to flow, stream; cl. 2. A. (Pass. reflex.) स्नुते, अस्नोष्ट or अस्ना-विष्ट: Pass. स्नूयते, स्नोता or स्नाविता, स्नोष्-यते or स्नाविष्यते, Aor. अस्नावि, to be distilled, &c.: Caus. स्नावयति, &c., Aor. असुष्णवत्: Desid. of Caus. सिस्नावयिषति or सुस्नावयिषति (according to Vopa-deva): Desid. सुस्नूषति: In-tens. सोष्णूयते, सोष्णवीति, सोष्णोति; [cf. Gr. νέ-ω (for σνεϝ-ω), νεύ-σω (for σνεύ-σω), νεῦ-σι-ς, νευ-σ-τήρ, νά-ω (for σναϝ-ω), ἀένα-ο-ς, νᾶ-μα, νᾱ-ρό-ς, νη-ρό-ς, Νη-ρ-εύ-ς, Νη-ιά-(δ)-ς; (probably also ναῦ-ς, ναύ-τη-ς, &c., see under 3. नौ, p. 518): Goth. snu, ‘to go;’ sniva, snau, snivum (for snu-um), snaivs, ‘snow:’ Old Germ. sniutan, sniumi, sneo, snê: Angl. Sax. sniwan, snytan, sneome: Lith. snega-s (w being changed to g): Slav. snêg: Hib. snuadhaim, ‘I flow;’ snuadh, ‘blood;’ sneachd, ‘snow.’]
53297: स्नव, अस्, m. oozing, drizzling, dripping, trickling.
53298: स्नवन, अम्, n. the act of oozing, trickling; distillation.
53299: स्नुत, अस्, आ, अम्, trickled, distilled, dropped, trickling, flowing, dropping, oozing.
53300: स्नुति, इस्, f. trickling, distilling, oozing, stream, flow.
53301: स्नुत्वा, ind. having trickled or oozed or flowed.
53302: स्नु 2. स्नु, उस्, उ, m. n. (a defective word optionally substituted for सानु, q. v., in certain cases; according to some fr. rt. 1. सो), the level summit or edge of a mountain, table-land; any top, surface; anything fixed or stationary (as the firmament; Sāy. = स्थित, Ṛg-veda IV. 28, 2).
53303: स्नु 3. स्नु, उस्, f. = स्नायु, a sinew, tendon, muscle. —स्नु-तस्, ind. from the sinews or muscles.
53304: स्नु 4. स्नु, a Kṛd-anta affix to roots form-ing adjectives expressive of an aptitude to be what is implied by the root; [cf. स्थास्नु।]
53305: स्नुच् स्नुच्, cl. 1. A. स्नोचते, &c., to be bright or clear (probably for rt. स्तुच्, but according to Śabda-k., under ष्णुच्, the meaning is सेचने).
53306: स्नुषा स्नुषा, f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. स्नु), a daughter-in-law; the milk-hedge plant (= 2. स्नुह्); [cf. Gr. νυό-ς; Lat. nuru-s (for snusu-s); Old Germ. snur; Angl. Sax. snoru; Slav. snochâ.]
53307: स्नुस् स्नुस्, cl. 4. P. स्नुस्यति, सुस्नोष, स्नोसितुम्, to eat; to disappear or become invisible; to take.
53308: स्नुह् 1. स्नुह्, cl. 4. P. स्नुह्यति, सुष्णोह, स्नोहितुम् or स्नोग्धुम् or स्नोढुम्, to vomit; = rt. 1. स्निह्।
53309: 2. स्नुह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, or क्, क्, क्, vomiting, one who vomits; (क्), f. the milk-hedge plant, Euphorbia Antiquorum (its milky juice has various medicinal pro-perties, and is used as an emetic; seventeen synonyms of this plant are enumerated, cf. सीहुण्ड). —स्नुक्-छद, अस्, m. a kind of reed (= क्षीर-कञ्चुकिन्).
53311: स्नुहि, इस्, or स्नुही, f. = 2. स्नुह् above.
53312: स्नेह स्नेह, स्नेहिन्। See p. 1149, col. 3.
53313: स्नै स्नै (also written स्तै, q. v.), cl. 1. P. स्नायति, &c., to dress, wrap round, envelope, adorn.
53315: स्पन्द् स्पन्द् (sometimes incorrectly con-founded with rt. स्यन्द्), cl. 1. A. स्पन्-दते, पस्पन्दे, अस्पन्दिष्ट, स्पन्दितुम्, to quiver, throb, tremble, quake, shake, palpitate, beat, to go, move (= rt. स्यन्द्): Pass. स्पद्यते (accord-ing to some), Aor. अस्पन्दि: Caus. स्पन्दयति, Aor. अपस्पन्दत्।
53316: स्पन्द, अस्, m. throbbing, throb, pulse, tremor, vibration, motion; [cf. वि-ष्पन्द।] —स्पन्द-कारिका, f., N. of a metrical version of the Spanda-sūtra. —स्पन्द-शास्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a work. —स्पन्द-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of the aphorisms of the Śaiva philosophy (= शिव-सूत्र).
53317: स्पन्दन, अम्, n. throbbing, pulsation, palpita-tion, quivering, (throbbings and quiverings of the limbs and different parts of the body are supposed by the Hindūs to indicate good or bad luck; they are therefore minutely described in certain works); tremor, vibration, agitation; the quickening of a child in the womb; rapid motion, going; (according to some) a car, chariot (Sāy. explains स्पन्दने by रथस्य गमने सति, Ṛg-veda III. 53, 19); (अस्), m. a sort of tree.
53318: स्पन्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, throbbing, quivering, palpitating, beating; going.
53319: स्पन्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, throbbed, quivered, agitated, throbbing, beating; gone; (अम्), n. a pulsation, throb.
53320: स्पन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, quivering, throbbing, palpitat-ing, beating, tremulous.
53323: स्पर्ध् स्पर्ध् (connected with rt. स्पृह्, q. v.; the older form seems to have been स्पृध्, q. v.), cl. 1. A. (ep. also P.) स्पर्धते (-ति), पस्पर्धे, स्पर्धिष्यते, अस्पर्धिष्ट, स्पर्धितुम्, to contend or compete with, contest, vie with, emulate, rival, be equal with; to envy; to challenge, defy, bid defiance to: Pass. स्पर्धते, Aor. अस्पर्धि: Caus. स्पर्धयति, Aor. अप-स्पर्धत्, &c.: Desid. पिस्पर्धिषते: Intens. पा-स्पर्ध्यते, पास्पर्द्धि; [cf. Goth. spauards; Old Germ. spurt; Angl. Sax. spyrd.]
53324: स्पर्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, emulous, envious; (आ), f. emulation, rivalry, competition, the successive eleva-tion of rivals; envy, jealousy; defiance; equality with. —स्पर्ध-ता, f. rivalry, emulation, envious-ness.
53325: स्पर्धन, अम्, n. competition, emulation; envy.
53326: स्पर्धमान, अस्, आ, अम्, vying, emulating, com-peting, contending with, envying, challenging, de-fying.
53327: स्पर्धित, अस्, आ, अम्, contended with, emulated, envied; defied.
53328: स्पर्धित्वा, ind. having contended or competed or vied with.
53329: स्पर्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, rivalling, emulating, compet-ing; emulous, envious; proud, superb.
53330: स्पर्धिष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, about to contend or compete.
53331: स्पूर्धस् (probably to be connected with rt. स्पर्ध्), Ved. envy, (Sāy. स्पूर्धसे = स्पर्ध-नाय, Ṛg-veda V. 64, 4.)

6. विशद, clean; 7. खर, hard; 8. मृदु, soft; 9. श्लक्ष्ण, smooth; 10. लघु, light; 11. गुरु, heavy); who or what affects or acts upon or in-fluences; affection, morbid affection or influence, any-thing the contact or influence of which causes pain or disease, disorder, sickness, fever; 53411: स्फल् स्फल्, cl. 1. P. स्फलति, पस्फाल, स्फलितुम्, to tremble, quiver, throb, palpitate, beat (= rt. स्फुल्, q. v.): Caus. स्फाल-यति, -यितुम्, to cause to tremble or shake, &c.; [cf. Gr. σφάλλ-ω, σφάλ-μα, ἀ-σφαλ-ής, σφαλ-ερός; Lat. fall-o, fal-sus, falla, fallax, fallac-ia; Old Germ. fallan; Lith. pula, pulti, ‘to fall.’]
53412: स्फाल, अस्, m. throbbing, quivering, palpitation, beat, trembling, shaking.
53413: स्फालन, अम्, n. the act of palpitating, shaking, quivering; causing to shake about or move; rubbing, friction; stroking or patting (a horse &c.).
53415: स्फाय् स्फाय् (thought by some to be derived from a Pass. of a lost rt. स्पन्, प् becoming फ् through the influence of initial स्; but apparently connected in some senses with rts. स्फर्, स्फुर्), cl. 1. A. स्फायते, पस्फाये, स्फा-यितुम्, to grow large or fat, become bulky, swell, expand, increase: Caus. स्फावयति (perhaps ori-ginally स्फापयति), -यितुम्, Aor. अपिस्फवत् (Pāṇ. VII. 3, 11), to cause to grow large, enlarge, augment, increase; [cf. Gr. σπά-ω, σπά-σ-μα, σπα-σ-μό-ς, ἀ-σπάζομαι, ἀγαπάω (i. e. ἀγαν-σπαω); Lat. spa-ti-um, patere; Old Germ. spannan, spa-nan; Angl. Sax. spanan, spinnan; Goth. spin-nan.]
53416: स्फात, अस्, आ, अम्, grown big, swollen, enlarged, increased.
53417: स्फाति, इस्, f. swelling, intumescence, increase, growth.
53418: 2. स्फार, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 13. fr. rt. स्फाय् above; perhaps also connected with rt. स्फर् and 1. स्फार), swelling, increase, enlargement (= वृद्धि); a bubble (in gold &c.); a protuber-ance [cf. Gr. σφαῖρα] (अस्, आ, अम्), large, increased, expanded, spreading, great; abundant; loud; (अम्), n. much, abundance. —स्फारी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भ-वति, &c., to become large or swollen, swell out, expand, spread out; to become manifest.
53419: 2. स्फारित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. स्फार above; but perhaps also connected with rt. स्फर्), swollen out, spread out, extended, large.
53420: स्फावयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, augmenting, increasing, enlarging.
53421: स्फिर, अस्, आ, अम्, abundant, much, many, large; swollen, expanded; vast, capacious, (Sāy. = वृद्-ध।)
53422: स्फीत, अस्, आ, अम्, swollen, enlarged, bulky, fat, big, large, thick; much, abundant, many, numerous; successful, prosperous; affected by hereditary disease. —स्फीत-ता, f. bulkiness, enlargement; prosperity, successful progress. —स्फीती-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to enlarge, augment.
53423: स्फीति, इस्, f. increase, enlargement; prosperity.
53424: स्फेयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of स्फिर), more abundant, very much or abundant.
53425: स्फेष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. of स्फिर), most abundant, very much or abundant.
53426: स्फार स्फार, स्फारण। See p. 1151, col. 3, and above.
53428: स्फिच् स्फिच्, क्, f. (by some connected with rt. स्फाय्, ‘to be fat’), a buttock, hip; (औ), f. du. the buttocks; [cf. Old Germ. spech; Angl. Sax. spic.] —स्फिक्-घातनक, अस्, m. a particular plant or small tree much used in medicine (= कट्-फल, p. 196, col. 1).
53429: स्फिगी, f., Ved. the buttock, hip; (this form स्फिगी seems necessary to account for स्फिग्या = कट्या, Ṛg-veda III. 32, 11; स्फिग्यम् = कटि-प्रदेशम्, Ṛg-veda VIII. 4, 8.)
53431: स्फिट् स्फिट्, cl. 10. P. स्फेटयति, &c., to hurt, injure, kill (= rt. स्फिट्ट्); to despise; to love (according to some); to cover (ac-cording to some).
53432: स्फिट्ट् स्फिट्ट्, cl. 10. P. स्फिट्टयति, &c., to hurt, kill (= rts. स्फिट्, स्फट्).
53435: स्फुट् स्फुट् (connected with rts. स्फुर्, स्फुल्), cl. 6. P. स्फुटति, cl. 1. P. A. स्फोटति, -ते, पुस्फोट, पुस्फुटे, अस्फुटत्, अस्-फुटीत्, अस्फोटीत्, स्फुटितुम् (cl. 1. स्फोटितुम्), to burst or become suddenly rent asunder, burst open, split open, part asunder, break forth, expand; to blossom, blow (generally A.); to burst into view, be-come manifested or made public, to disperse, run away; cl. 10. P. स्फुटयति, to burst, crack, break open; to burst into view: Pass. स्फुट्यते, Aor. अस्फोटि: Caus. स्फोटयति, to burst or rend sud-denly, break, split, cleave, tear open, divide; to disclose, make clear; to hurt, destroy, kill; to winnow.
53436: स्फुट, अस्, आ, अम्, burst, split open, broken, rent, torn, opened, expanded; open, blossomed, blown; clearly displayed, clear; plain, distinct, mani-fest, evident; well known or understood; bright; white; loud; spread, diffused; (in astronomy) ap-parent, true; corrected; (आ), f. the expanded hood of a serpent; (अम्), ind. distinctly, manifestly, evi-dently, certainly. —स्फुट-ता, f. openness, mani-festation; perspicuity; blossoming. —स्फुट-तार, अस्, आ, अम्, having stars clearly seen, bright with stars. —स्फुट-पौरुष, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has displayed valour or energy. —स्फुट-फल, अम्, n. (in geometry) clear or precise result (of any calculation); distinct or precise area (of a triangle &c.). —स्फुट-बन्धनी, f. a kind of plant, heart-pea (= पारावत-पदी). —स्फुट-वल्कली, f. the plant heart-pea. —स्फुट-सार, अस्, m. (probably) the true latitude of a star or planet. —स्फुट-सूर्य-गति, इस्, f. apparent or true motion of the sun. —स्फुटार्थ (°ट-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a clear meaning, intelligible, obvious, significant. —स्फुटी-करण, अम्, n. the act of displaying clearly, making distinct; making true or correct, correction.
53437: स्फुटत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, bursting open, part-ing or bursting asunder, splitting in two; blowing, blossoming; becoming manifest or clear; evolving.
53438: स्फुटन, अम्, n. the act of breaking or rending suddenly, bursting, tearing open, disruption, open-ing, expanding, blossoming.
53439: स्फुटनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be broken open or split.
53440: स्फुटि, इस्, or स्फुटी, f. cracking or chapping of the skin of the feet, sores or swelling of the feet; the fruit of the Karkaṭī or a sort of melon, Cucumis Momordica.
53441: स्फुटिका, f. (probably) a small bit broken off, little bit or piece.
53442: स्फुटित, अस्, आ, अम्, burst, broken open, split, cracked; budded, blown, expanded (as a flower); made clear, manifested, spread out; torn, destroyed; laughed at (= परि-हसित; cf. rt. स्फुण्ट्). —स्फु-टित-चरण, अस्, आ, अम्, having wide feet, splay-footed.
53443: स्फोट, अस्, m. breaking, splitting open, bursting, disclosure, (नर्म-स्फोट in dramatic action is ex-plained to mean भाव-लेशैः सूचितो ऽल्परसः, i. e. slight disclosures or glimpses of love); a swelling, boil, tumor; the idea or disclosure which bursts out or flashes on the mind when a sound is uttered; the eternal sound in the Pūrva-mīmāṃsā; (आ), f. the expanded hood of a snake. —स्फोट-वाद, अस्, m. a dissertation on the above philosophical Sphoṭa. —स्फोट-वीजक, अस्, m. ‘having bursting seeds,’ the marking-nut plant (= भल्लातक).
53444: स्फोटक, अस्, m. one who bursts or splits open; a swelling, boil, tumor.
53445: स्फोटन, अस्, ई, अम्, breaking or splitting asunder, opening, making clear, disclosing, manifesting; (अस्), m. (in Vedic grammar) = व्यञ्जक, separated utter-ance of a close combination of consonants; (अम्), n. the act of bursting or rending suddenly, splitting, cracking; tearing; winnowing grain, &c.; cracking the finger-joints, snapping the fingers; (in grammar) the separation of the letters of a double consonant; (ई), f. an instrument for splitting or cleaving, a gimlet, boring-tool, auger [cf. आ-स्फोटनी, लास्फो-टनी].
53446: स्फोटायन, अस्, m., N. of an ancient gram-marian, (Pāṇ. VI. 1, 123; he is identified by some with Kakṣīvat.)
53447: स्फोटिका, f. a kind of bird, a wagtail (= हापु-त्रिका).
53448: स्फोटित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), made to burst open, rent or torn asunder, disclosed.
53449: स्फुट्ट् स्फुट्ट्, cl. 10. P. स्फुट्टयति, &c., to despise, disrespect.
53450: स्फुड् स्फुड्, cl. 6. P. स्फुडति, &c., to cover.
53451: स्फुण्ट् स्फुण्ट्, cl. 1. P. स्फुण्टति, &c., to open, expand, &c. (= rt. स्फुट्); cl. 10. P. स्फुण्टयति, &c., to jest, joke, laugh at (= rt. स्फण्ड्).
53452: स्फुण्ड् स्फुण्ड्, cl. 1. A. स्फुण्डते, &c., to open, expand, &c. (= rt. स्फुट्); cl. 10. P. स्फुण्डयति, &c., to jest, &c. (= rt. स्फण्ड्).
53453: स्फुत् स्फुत्, an imitative sound; [cf. फुत्।] —स्फुत्-कर, अस्, m. ‘making a blowing or crackling sound,’ fire. —स्फुत्-कार, अस्, m. making the noise स्फुत्, crackling, burning.
53454: स्फुर् स्फुर् (= rt. स्फर्, which appears in the Caus. and is probably the older form, see स्फर्; the rt. स्फुर् is evidently con-nected with rts. स्फुट्, स्फुल्), cl. 6. P. स्फुरति, पुस्फोर, स्फुरिष्यति, अस्फुरीत्, Prec. स्फूर्-यात्, स्फुरितुम्, to tremble, palpitate, throb, vibrate, thrill, quiver, twitch, become agitated, struggle; to start, dart, spring, bound; to spring back, rebound; to spring up, shoot out, break forth, burst out plainly or visibly, start into view, be evident or manifest, appear clearly, become displayed or expanded; to flash, scintillate, twinkle, sparkle, shine, gleam, glitter; to flash on the mind, rush into the memory; to go tremulously; to bruise, destroy, (Sāy. स्फुरत् = स्फुरिष्यति = वाधिष्यति, Ṛg-veda I. 84, 8): Pass. स्फुर्यते, Aor. अस्फोरि: Caus. स्फोरयति, स्फारयति (see rt. स्फर्), -यितुम्, Aor. अपु-स्फुरत्, अपुस्फरत्, to cause to vibrate; to make to shine or glitter; to cast: Desid. पुस्फुरिषति: Intens. पोस्फुर्यते, पोस्फोर्ति; [cf. Zend śpar; Gr. σπαίρ-ω, ἀ-σπαίρ-ω, (probably also) σπείρω, σπέρμα, σποράς, σφυρόν; (probably) Lat. sperno; Angl. Sax. spurnan, spura; Lith. spir-ti, spar-dy-ti.]
53455: स्फुर, अस्, m. trembling, throbbing; swelling; coruscating; a shield.
53456: स्फुरण, अम्, आ, n. f. the act of trembling, throbbing, pulsation, vibration; quivering or throb-bing of parts of the body (e. g. quivering of the lips, twitching of the eyes, &c., as indicating good or bad luck); springing or breaking forth, starting into view, expansion; flashing, coruscation, scintilla-tion, twinkling, glittering; flashing on the mind.
53457: स्फुरत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, trembling, shaking, quivering, throbbing; starting, darting; springing up, breaking forth, bursting out plainly or visibly, becoming clear or manifest; flashing, glittering; flashing vividly on the mind; swelling, expanding [cf. स्फुटत्]; going, moving; going tremulously. —स्फुरद्-अधरोष्ठ (°र-ओष्°) or स्फुरद्-ओष्ठ, अस्, ई, अम्, having quivering lips, (स्फुरद्-अधरोष्ठम्, ind. with quivering or pouting lips.) —स्फुरद्-उल्का, f. a shooting meteor, aerolite. —स्फुरदुल्काकृति (°का-आक्°), इस्, इस्, इ, having the form of a shooting meteor.
53458: स्फुरित, अस्, आ, अम्, trembling, heaving, throb-bing, thrilling, palpitating; shaken, agitated; flash-ing, glittering, gleaming, playing, unsteady; swelled, swollen; (अम्), n. a throb, throbbing, tremor, quivering or twitching of the eyelids, &c., agitation or emotion of mind. —स्फुरित-शतह्रद, अस्, आ, अम्, having flashing lightning (said of a cloud). —स्फुरितोत्तराधर (°त-उत्°, °र-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having trembling upper and under lips.
53459: स्फूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, (according to some) throbbed, throbbing; suddenly risen into remembrance.
53460: स्फूर्ति, इस्, f. throb, palpitation, tremor, trem-bling, shaking, vibration; spring, bound, start; breaking forth visibly, becoming evident or apparent, manifestation, expansion; flashing on the mind or memory. —स्फूर्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, throbbing, thrilling (with joy or excitement), tremulous, agi-tated; tender-hearted; (आन्), m. a follower or wor-shipper of Śiva (= पाशुपत).
53461: स्फोरण, अम्, n. throbbing, quivering, &c. = स्फार (according to Vopa-deva).
53462: स्फुर्छ् स्फुर्छ् (also written स्वुर्छ्), cl. 1. P. स्फूर्छति, पुस्फूर्छ, स्फूर्-छितुम्, to spread, extend; to forget.
53463: स्फूर्छित, अस्, आ, अम्, spread; forgotten.
53464: 1. स्फूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्फूर्छित above.
53465: स्फुर्ज् स्फुर्ज् (probably connected with rt. स्फुर्), cl. 1. P. स्फूर्जति, पु-स्फूर्ज, स्फूर्जितुम्, to thunder, make a sound like a thunder-clap, crash, explode: Pass. स्फूर्ज्-यते: Caus. स्फूर्जयति: Desid. पुस्फूर्जिषति: Intens. पोस्फूर्ज्यते, पोस्फूर्क्ति; [cf. Lat. spargo; Angl. Sax. sprecan, sprœncan, sprengan, sprin-can, springan.]
53468: स्फूर्ज, अस्, m. the crashing sound of a thunder-clap, thunder; Indra's thunderbolt; sudden burst, (नर्म-स्फूर्ज, sudden burst of love; in dramatic action defined to mean सुखारम्भो भयान्तो नव-सङ्गमः, first union of lovers characterized by joy in the beginning and some cause of fear in the end.) —स्फूर्जा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, thundering.
53469: स्फूर्जक, अस्, m. a sort of ebony tree, Diospyros Glutinosa (= तिन्दुक).
53470: स्फूर्जथु, उस्, m. a clap of thunder, explosion.
53471: स्फूर्जन, अम्, n. the act of thundering; an explosion, crash.
53472: स्फूर्जयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. overwhelming, crushing, (Sāy. = निष्पिषत्।)
53473: स्फूर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, thundered; [cf. वि-स्फूर्-जित।]
53474: 2. स्फूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, (according to some) thun-dered.
53475: स्फुल् स्फुल् (connected with rts. स्फुर्, स्फुट्, स्फल्), cl. 6. P. स्फुलति, पु-स्फोल, Aor. अस्फुलीत्, स्फुलितुम्, to tremble, throb, vibrate; to dart forth, appear; to collect; to slay, kill, (enumerated among the वध-कर्माणः in Naigh. II. 19): Pass. स्फुल्यते, Aor. अस्फोलि: Caus. स्फोलयति, &c. (For comparisons see rt. स्फल्।)
53476: स्फुल, अम्, n. a tent (= वस्त्र-वेश्मन्).
53477: स्फुलन, अम्, n. trembling, throbbing, vibration, palpitation.
53478: स्फुलिङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (perhaps to be connected with स्फुत्, p. 1152), a spark of fire.
53479: स्फुलिङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having sparks of fire, sparkling; (इनी), f., N. of one of the seven tongues of Agni or fire.
53480: स्फोलन, अम्, n. = स्फाल (according to Vopa-deva).
53483: स्फ्य स्फ्य, अम्, n. an implement used in sacrifices (described as a piece of wood shaped like a sword for stirring the boiled rice, or, according to some, for trimming the mound used as an altar). —स्फ्य-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made or marked out by the स्फ्य. —स्फ्य-वर्तनि, इस्, m. the furrow or line made by the स्फ्य (in marking out the sacrificial ground).
53484: स्फैयकृत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्फ्य-कृत), re-lating to anything made by the स्फ्य।
53485: स्बॄ स्बॄ = rt. स्वॄ, q. v.
53486: स्म स्म (probably for 2. समा, an old inst. of 1. सम, and meaning ‘wholly, entirely’), ind. a particle added to the present tense of verbs or to present participles (generally giving them a past signification, e. g. प्रविशन्ति स्म पुरीम्, they entered the city); a pleonastic particle (often used after मा, see मा स्म under 1. मा; also in the Veda preceded by अध, q. v., and other particles).
53487: स्मत् स्मत्, ind. (probably connected with स्म; according to some an old neut. of 1. सम; but according to Sāy. a contraction of सुमत्), Ved. well, excellently, (Sāy. = सु, सुमत्); with, together with (= 2. सह; cf. Gr. μετά; Mod. Germ. mit); constantly, always, (Sāy. = नित्यम्।) —स्मत्-पुरन्-धि, इस्, m. = स्वर्ग-कुटुम्बी (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VIII. 34, 6). —स्मद्-अभीशु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having beautiful reins, (Sāy. = शोभन-रज्जु-युक्त or शोभन-शरीर-कान्ति, Ṛg-veda VIII. 25, 24.) —स्मद्-इष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy.) going well or sent together (= प्रशस्त-गति or सह-प्रेषित, Ṛg-veda VII. 87, 3). —स्मद्-ऊध्नी, f. (see ऊधस्), Ved. (a cow) always giving milk, (Sāy. = नित्यम् उधसा युक्ता, सर्वदा पयसः प्रदात्री, Ṛg-veda I. 73, 6; cf. पी-नोध्नी।) —स्मद्-दिष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. auspiciously speaking (said of Indra; Sāy. = भद्र-वाक्य, Ṛg-veda III. 45, 5); handsome-looking, (Sāy. = प्रशस्त-दर्शन, Ṛg-veda VI. 63, 9.)
53491: स्मि स्मि, cl. 1. A. स्मयते (ep. also P. -ति), सिष्मिये, स्मेष्यते, अस्मेष्ट, स्मेतुम्, to smile, laugh; to expand, bloom (as a flower): Pass. स्मीयते, Aor. अस्मायि: Caus. स्मा-ययति, -ते (also स्मापयते in वि-स्मि, q. v.), to cause to laugh, provoke or excite laughter; (A.) to laugh at, mock, despise: Desid. सिस्मयिषते: Intens. सेष्मीयते, (in Mālavikāgnimitra, Act IV, the Prākṛt सिमिसिमा-अन्ति [see s.v.] is incorrectly referred to the Intens. of rt. स्मि), सेष्मयीति, सेष्-मेति; [cf. Gr. μεῖ-δ-ος, μεί-δ-η-μα, μει-δ-ά-ω, μει-διάω, (perhaps also) σμοιός. μέμφομαι, μῶμος: Lat. mi-ru-s, ni-miru-m, mira-ri: Old Germ. smie-l-en, smie-r-en: Eng. smile: Angl. 53508: स्मर, अस्, m. remembrance, recollection; loving recollection, love; Kāma-deva (god of love). —स्मर-कर्मन्, अ, n. amorous action or conduct, any wanton act, lasciviousness. —स्मर-कूपक, अस्, m. or स्मर-कूपिका, f. ‘well of love,’ the female organ. —स्मर-गुरु, उस्, m. ‘love-preceptor,’ epithet of Viṣṇu. —स्मर-गृह, अम्, n. ‘abode of love,’ the female organ. —स्मर-चक्र, अस्, m. a particular kind of sexual union. —स्मर-च्छत्र, अम्, n. the clitoris. —स्मर-दशा, f. a state of love, state of the body produced by being in love, (ten such states are enu-merated, e. g. anxious thought, sleeplessness, emacia-tion, loss of appetite, fainting, &c.) —स्मर-दायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, causing or exciting love (= कामोद्दीपक)। —स्मर-दीपिका, f., N. of a work. —स्मर-ध्व-ज, अस्, m. ‘love-sign,’ ‘love-emblem,’ the male organ; a fabulous fish (regarded as the emblem of Kāma-deva; cf. मकर-ध्वज); a musical in-strument; (आ), f. a bright moonlight night (accord-ing to some); (अम्), n. the female organ. —स्मर-प्रिया, f. ‘dear to Kāma,’ epithet of Rati (Kāma-deva's wife). —स्मर-भासित, अस्, आ, अम्, love-illuminated, inflamed by love. —स्मर-मन्दिर, अम्, n. ‘love-palace,’ the female organ. —स्मर-मोह, अस्, m. infatuation of love, passion, love. —स्मर-मोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, infatuated by love, overcome by passion. —स्मर-लेखनी, f. the Śārikā bird. —स्मर-वल्लभ, अस्, m. ‘love's fa-vourite,’ epithet of A-niruddha. —स्मर-वाण-पङ्क्ति, इस्, f. the five arrows of Kāma-deva collec-tively (see पञ्च-वाण). —स्मर-वीथिका, f. ‘love-shop,’ a prostitute, harlot. —स्मर-वृद्धि-सञ्-ज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular shrub (= काम-वृद्धि)। —स्मर-शवर, अस्, m. ‘love-barbarian,’ cruel love. —स्मर-शासन, अस्, m. ‘chastiser of Kāma-deva,’ epithet of Śiva (see अन्-अङ्ग). —स्मर-सख, अस्, m. ‘love's friend,’ the moon. —स्मर-स्तम्भ, अस्, m. ‘love-column,’ the male organ. —स्मर-स्मर्य, अस्, m. a donkey, ass (= गर्द-भ). —स्मर-हर, अस्, m. ‘love-destroyer,’ epi-thet of Śiva (see अन्-अङ्ग). —स्मराकुल or स्म-राकुलित (°र-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, agitated by love, love-sick. —स्मरागार (°र-आग्°), अम्, n. ‘love-abode,’ the female organ. —स्मराङ्कुश (°र-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘love-hook,’ a finger-nail; a lover, lascivious person. —स्मरातुर (°र-आत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, love-sick, pining with love. —स्मरान्ध (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, love-blinded, infatuated with passion. —स्मरारि (°र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of Kāma-deva,’ epithet of Śiva. —स्मरार्त (°र-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, love-sick. —स्मरासव (°र-आस्°), अस्, m. ‘love-liquid,’ saliva. —स्मरोत्सुक (°र-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, pining or languishing with love, love-sick.
53509: स्मरण, अम्, n. the act of remembering, re-membrance, memory, recollecting, recollection, re-miniscence; tradition, traditional precept, (इति स्मर-णात्, ‘from its being so mentioned in the Smṛti,’ cf. स्मृति); mental recitation (of the name of a deity), calling upon the name of a god; regretting, remem-bering with regret; thinking upon, anxious thought. —स्मरण-पदवी, f. ‘road to mere memory,’ death. —स्मरणानुग्रह (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. the favour of remembrance, kind remembrance. —स्मर-णापत्य-तर्पक (°ण-अप्°), अस्, m. ‘satisfying memory's offspring,’ a turtle, tortoise. —स्मरणा-यौगपद्य (°ण-अय्°), अम्, n. the non-simulta-neousness of recollections.
53510: स्मरणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be remembered, memo-rable, to be borne in mind.
53511: स्मरत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, remembering, recollecting, considering.
53512: स्मर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be remembered, memo-rable.

53520: स्मारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, remembering; reminding.
53521: स्मार्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्मृति), relating to memory, memorial, remembered, coming within the range of memory; recorded in the Smṛtis, prescribed in the inspired codes of law, based on Smṛti, q. v.; sanc-tioned by law, canonical, legal; following the doc-trine of the law-books; domestic (applied to the domestic fire which every Brāhman is bound to keep up); (अस्), m. a Brāhman skilled in jurisprudence or traditional law (especially one belonging to a sect founded by Śaṅkarācārya, whose expositions of the principle of unity, according to the Vedānta doc-trine, they professedly follow, though holding Śiva in especial honour; their chief establishment is at Śṛṅga-giri, but they are said to be found throughout the south of India); (अम्), n. any act or rite enjoined by Smṛti or allowed by traditional usage, a legal act. —स्मार्त-कर्मन्, अ, n. a rite enjoined in the Smṛtis, one of the less important domestic rites. —स्मार्त-काल, अस्, m. the period to which memory may extend (i. e. a century, according to some lawyers). —स्मार्त-सूत्र, अम्, n. any Sūtra work based on Smṛti (opposed to श्रौत-सूत्र or Sūtras based on श्रुति, see सूत्र). —स्मार्त-होम-परि-शिष्ट, अम्, n., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Sāma-veda.
53522: स्मार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be remembered, memo-rable.
53523: स्मृत, अस्, आ, अम्, remembered, recollected, called to mind; recorded, mentioned, said, declared, termed, styled, named; enjoined by Smṛti or traditional law, declared or propounded in the law-books. —स्मृत-मात्र, अस्, आ, अम्, only remembered or thought of.
53524: स्मृति, इस्, f. remembrance, memory, reminiscence, recollection, thinking of or upon (any person or thing), calling to mind; Memory (personified as a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Aṅgiras); what is remembered, that which is borne in mind from the beginning, tradition, law; the institutes or body of traditional or memorial law (as handed down ori-ginally by Manu, Yājñavalkya, and other great legis-lators who were supposed to have been inspired, and to have based their precepts on the Veda and divine revelation, though the laws they promulgated were called Smṛti, ‘what is remembered,’ in contradistinc-tion to Śruti, ‘what is heard or revealed,’ and to Ācāra, ‘established usage;’ the very essence of Smṛti being that it was delivered memoriter by human authors, and not directly revealed, as explained in Manu II. 10, see श्रुति; in its widest acceptation Smṛti is said to include the Vedāṅgas, the Sūtras or aphorisms both श्रौत and गृह्य, the institutes of Manu and other inspired law-givers, the Itihāsas, such as the Rāmāyaṇa and Mahā-bhārata, and the Purāṇas, but the term Smṛti is more usually re-stricted to the metrical codes of Manu, Yājñavalkya, Parāśara, &c., see स्मृति-शास्त्र below); any par-ticular law-book or code of laws; any particular law or rule of law, canon, legal text (e. g. अनुमिता स्मृतिः प्रत्यक्षया स्मृत्या बाध्यते, a Smṛti which is only inferred is set aside by a visibly exist-ing Smṛti; these authors are sometimes classed in three divisions, under the three heads of सात्त्विक, राजस, and तामस, according to the tendency of their writings.) —स्मृति-शील, ए, n. du. traditions and moral prac-tices. —स्मृति-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, one of whom only remembrance remains, a deceased or defunct person; that of which nothing is left but remembrance. —स्मृति-शैथिल्य, अम्, n. temporary failure or loss of memory. —स्मृति-सङ्ग्रह or स्मृति-समुच्चय, अस्, m. ‘law-collection,’ N. of two legal works. —स्मृति-सम्मत, अस्, आ, अम्, approved by law. —स्मृति-सागर and स्मृति-सागर-सङ्-ग्रह and स्मृति-सागर-सार, N. of various legal works. —स्मृति-साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, capable of being proved by law. —स्मृति-सार, अस्, m. ‘essence of law,’ N. of a work by Deva-yājñika; of another work by Yādavendra; of another by Hari-nātha. —स्मृति-सारावली (°र-आव्°), f. ‘line of es-sence of law,’ N. of a work. —स्मृति-सिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, established by law. —स्मृति-हारिका, f. ‘memory-seizer,’ N. of a daughter of Duḥsahana (described in the fifty-first chapter of the Mārkaṇ-ḍeya-Purāṇa as exercising an evil influence on the memory). —स्मृति-हेतु, उस्, m. a cause of recollec-tion, any mental act stirring the memory, impression on the mind, reflection, association of ideas, recollec-tion. —स्मृत्य्-अन्तर, अम्, n. another law-book. —स्मृत्य्-अपेत, अस्, आ, अम्, departed from memory, forgotten; 53690: स्वधा स्व-धा or स्वधा, f. (fr. स्व + rt. 1. धा; but in Uṇādi-s. IV. 174. connected with rt. स्वद्; cf. स्वदित), Ved. one's own condition or nature, own peculiarity or individuality; innate or inherent power or strength, (स्वधया, by one's own power or strength; Sāy. = स्वकीयेन बलेन, by one's own nature or determination, spontaneously); ‘self-contained, self-sustained,’ N. of Māyā or Pra-kṛti (as the source of the phenomenal world; in this sense Svadhā is sometimes translated ‘Nature,’ as, for example, in the celebrated hymn Ṛg-veda X. 129. आनीद् अवातं स्वधया तद्, ‘that one, i. e. the supreme Being breathed calmly along with Na-ture;’ and in Naigh. III. 30. स्वधे, fem. du., is enumerated among the द्यावा-पृथिवी-नामधे-यानि); manner, habit, custom, usage, (अनु स्वधाम्, according to one's wont or custom, as usual; ac-cording to one's own determination, according to pleasure); one's own portion or share; the sacrificial offering due to each god; the food or oblation offered to the Pitṛs or spirits of deceased ancestors (in this sense especially in later Sanskrit); the Śrād-dha or funeral ceremony itself; the Food or Obla-tion to the Pitṛs &c. personified (as a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of the Pitṛs; also represented as a wife of Aṅgiras, of a Rudra, and of Agni); an ob-lation or offering or food (in general, = अन्न, Naigh. II. 7; = उदक, Naigh. I. 12); (स्वधा), ind. an exclamation or prayer used on presenting an oblation to the gods or Manes of departed ancestors and pro-genitors [cf. स्वाहा, श्रौषट्, वौषट्, वषट्], the highest form of blessing used at a Śrāddha, (स्व-धास्तु, ‘let there be Svadhā!’ this, according to Manu III. 252, is the highest benison at a Śrāddha); [cf. according to some Gr. ἔθ-ος, ἦθ-ος, ἠθεῖο-ς, εἴ-ωθ-α, ἐθ-ίζ-ω; Lat. suetus; Goth. sidus; Angl. Sax. sidu, siodo.] —स्वधा-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, offer-ing oblations to deceased ancestors or deified pro-genitors, performing funeral obsequies (Manu IX. 127); (अस्), m. = स्वधा-कार. —स्वधा-कार, अस्, m. pronouncing the exclamation or blessing स्व-धा; the formula स्वधा. —स्वधा-निनयन, अम्, n. ‘Svadhā-performing,’ a sacred text used in making the oblation to the Pitṛs, (Manu II. 172.) —स्वधा-पति, इस्, m., Ved. lord of the Svadhā. —स्वधा-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘fond of the Svadhā,’ Agni or fire; black sesamum, (तिल or sesamum being offered to the Manes, Manu III. 267.) —स्वधा-भुज्, क्, m. ‘Svadhā-eating,’ a Pitṛ, deceased or deified ancestor; a deity. —स्वधा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having natural power, self-controlled, self-reliant, in-dependent, powerful, (Sāy. स्वधा-वान् = बल-वान्, Ṛg-veda II. 20, 6; in Ṛg-veda VII. 88, 5. स्व-धावः, voc. case masc. 53727: स्वर् 2. स्वर्, ind. (probably connected with rt. 4. सु or 3. सू, and apparently originally written सुवर्, cf. सूर, सूर्य; but according to some fr. a lost rt. स्वर् = सुर्, ‘to shine,’ cf. सुर), the sun (Ved.; according to Sāy. = स्वरण-शील आदित्य, Ṛg-veda V. 45, 1); heaven, paradise, the world of the gods, abode of the deities; the heaven of Indra and temporary abode of the virtuous after death; the sky, ether; the space above the sun or between the sun and the polar star, the region of the planets and constellations; a mystical word pronounced after ॐ and before the Gāyatrī by every Brāhman in commencing his daily prayers, (it is the third of the three Vyāhṛtis, भूर्, भुवः, स्वर्, and denotes the space of the sky above de-scribed as distinguished from the earth and atmo-sphere, see Manu II. 76. and cf. भुवस्, व्य्-आहृति; the mystical word स्वर् is represented as produced from the Sāma-veda, just as भूर् and भुवः are supposed to come from the Ṛg-veda and Yajur-veda respectively); radiance, splendor; water, (in Naigh. I. 12. enumerated among the उदक-नामानि); epi-thet of Śiva; [cf. Zend hvare, ‘the sun;’ qaretha, qarenanh, ‘splendor:’ Gr. Σείρ-ιο-ς, Σείρ, σειρ-ιά-ω, σειρ-ία-σι-ς, σείρ-ινο-ς, σέλ-ας, σελ-ήνη: Lat. ser-enu-s, sol: Goth. sauil, ‘the sun:’ Old Norse sôl: Lith. saule: Slav. slŭ-nĭce, ‘the sun:’ Hib. speur, ‘the sky;’ (perhaps) soir, ‘the east, morning.’] —स्वः-काम्य, Nom.
