53764: स्वस्तिक, अस्, m. any lucky or auspicious object, a kind of mystical mark made on persons or things to denote good luck, (it is shaped like a Greek cross with the extremities of the four arms bent round in the same direction; amongst Jainas it is one of the twenty-four auspicious marks and is the emblem of the seventh Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī); the crossing of the arms; the meeting of four roads; a mansion or palace of a particular shape (described as surrounded by a terrace or portico on the north, west, and south sides, and having the door on the east); a particular symbol made with ground rice and shaped like a triangle (= तण्डुल-चूर्ण-निर्मित-त्रिकोणाकाराधिवास-द्रव्य; it is used in fumi-gating the image of Durgā, and is said to symbolize the Liṅga); a kind of cake; a voluptuary, libertine; garlic; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a mansion or temple of a parti-cular form with a portico or terrace in front; a particular mode of sitting practised by Yogins; a kind of vege-table (= सितावर). —स्वस्तिकासन (°क-आस्°), अम्, n. a particular mode of sitting, (see above.)
53769: स्वाङ्किक स्वाङ्किक, अस्, m. (perhaps fr. स्व + अङ्की, q. v.), a drummer, (according to Śabda-k. = मार्दङ्गिक।)
53770: स्वाच्छन्द्य स्वाच्छन्द्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्व-च्छन्द), the power of following one's own will or fancy, independence, (स्वाच्छन्द्यात्, by one's own will, of one's own free choice, voluntarily.)
53772: स्वातन्त्र्य स्वातन्त्र्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्व-तन्-त्र), the power of following one's own will, freedom of will, independence; (in phil.) free will.
53773: स्वाति स्वाति, इस्, m. f. (said to be fr. 5. सु + rt. 2. अत्), an auspicious constellation; the star Arcturus (as forming the fifteenth lunar asterism); N. of a son of Ūru, (in this sense masc.); (इस्), f. one of the wives of the Sun; a sword. —स्वाति-योग, अस्, m. conjunction with Svāti.
53774: स्वाती, f. Arcturus; a wife of the Sun; a sword.
53775: स्वाद् स्वाद्। See rt. स्वद्, p. 1159.
53781: स्वापतेय स्वापतेय, अम्, n. (fr. स्व + पति), wealth, property.
53782: स्वापद स्वापद, अस्, m. (for श्वापद), a wild beast.
53784: स्वाभाविक स्वाभाविक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्व-भाव), belonging to one's own nature, natural, native, peculiar, inherent; (आस्), m. pl. a sect of Buddhist philosophers who accounted for all things by the laws of nature.
53785: स्वाभाव्य, अम्, n. naturalness, natural state or character.
53787: स्वायम्भुव स्वायम्भुव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्व-यम्-भू), relating to Svayam-bhū or the Self-ex-istent; derived from the Self-existent or Brahman; (अस्), m. the son of Svayam-bhū, epithet of the first Manu; (ई), f. = ब्राह्मी, (Śabda-k.) —स्यायम्-भुव-मनु-पितृ, ता, m. ‘father of the Manu Svāyambhuva,’ Brahmā.
53789: स्वायुज् either स्व्-आयुज् or स्वायुज् (स्व-अय्°) or स्वा-युज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. easily yoked; putting them-selves spontaneously to the chariot.
53790: स्वारसिक स्वारसिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्व-रस), possessing inherent flavour or sweetness (said of a poem &c.).
53791: स्वारस्य, अम्, n. the possessing natural savori-ness or excellence.
53792: स्वाराज् स्वा-राज्, ट्, m. (fr. 2. स्वर् + राज्), the ruler of heaven, i. e. Indra.
53793: स्वाराज्य, अम्, n. the dominion of heaven, Indra's heaven; union with Brahma, identification with the Self-refulgent (in this sense fr. स्व-राज्), a state of self-effulgence.
53794: स्वारूपा स्वारूपा, f., N. of a place; [cf. स्व-रूपा।]
53795: स्वारोचिष स्वारोचिष, अस्, m. (fr. स्व-रोचिस्), N. of the second Manu.
53796: स्वारोचिस्, इस्, m. the second Manu.
53798: स्वालक्षण्य स्वालक्षण्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्व-लक्-षण), the peculiar characteristics or natural dis-position, (Manu IX. 19.)
53799: स्वाल्प स्वाल्प, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्व्-अल्प), little, small; few; (अम्), n. littleness; paucity.
53800: स्वास्थ्य स्वास्थ्य, अम्, n. (fr. स्व-स्थ), self-reliance, self-dependence, self-possession, fortitude, resoluteness, firmness; sound state, health, prosperity, happiness, comfortableness, competence; compla-cency, contentment, satisfaction.
53801: स्वाहा स्वाहा (probably for स्व्-आधा, i. e. 5. सु + rt. धा with आ, but cf. स्व-धा), ‘anything good placed on the fire,’ a good oblation or offering (to Agni, Indra, &c.), that part of an offering which is given to all the gods indiscriminately, (in this sense probably ind., but in the next fem.); the Ob-lation personified (as a wife of Agni and goddess presiding over burnt-offerings; Svāhā's body is said to consist of the four Vedas, and her limbs are the six Aṅgas or members of the Veda; she is repre-sented also as a wife of the Rudra Paśu-pati; cf. स्व-धा); a female Bauddha divinity; in Naigh. I. 11. स्वाहा is enumerated among the वाङ्-नामानि; (ind.) an exclamation used in making oblations to the gods (often used like ‘Hail!’ and governing a dat. case, e. g. अग्नये or सोमाय स्वाहा; cf. स्व्-अस्ति). —स्वाहा-कार, अस्, m. utterance of the term Svāhā; the formula Svāhā (uttered at the end of the Yājyā verses). —स्वाहा-कृति, इस्, f., Ved. an oblation made with the Svāhā-kāra, (Ṛg-veda X. 110, 11. is ad-dressed to the Svāhā-kṛtis.) —स्वाहा-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of the Svāhā,’ Agni. —स्वाहा-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘fond of the Svāhā,’ Agni. —स्वाहा-भुज्, क्, m. ‘eating the Svāhā,’ a deity.
53802: स्वित् स्वित् or स्विद्, ind. a particle of inter-rogation or inquiry (often implying doubt or surprise, and translateable by ‘hey?’ ‘what?’ ‘can it be that?’); an expletive (often redundant, but sometimes per-haps used disjunctively, and equivalent to ‘either,’ ‘or’).
53803: स्विद् स्विद्, cl. 4. P. स्विद्यति, सिष्वेद, स्वेत्स्यति, अस्विदत्, स्वेत्तुम्, to sweat, perspire; cl. 1. A. स्वेदते, सिष्विदे, स्वेदितुम्, to be anointed; to be greasy or unctuous; to pour forth, shed (?) ; to be disturbed: Caus. स्वेदयति, -यितुम्, Aor. असिस्विदत्, to cause to sweat; to make warm, heat: Desid. of Caus. सिस्वेदयिषति: Desid. सि-ष्वित्सति: Intens. सेष्विद्यते, सेष्वेत्ति; [cf. Gr. ἱδ-ί-ω, ἷδος, ἱδ-ρό-ς, ἱδ-ρώ(τ)-ς, σίδηρος; Lat. sud-ā-re, sud-or, sud-ariu-m; Old Norse sveit-i; Old Germ. sveiz; Goth. sveitan; Angl. Sax. swœtan; Eng. sweat.]
53804: स्विदित, अस्, आ, अम्, sweated, melted; sweating, perspiring.
53805: स्विन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, perspired, sweated, covered with perspiration, perspiring; steeped. —स्विन्नाङ्-गुलि (°न-अङ्°), इस्, इस्, इ, having perspiring or moist fingers.
53806: स्वेद, अस्, आ, अम्, sweating, perspiring; toiling; (अस्), m. perspiration, sweat; warmth, heat; vapour. —स्वेद-चूषक, अस्, m. ‘perspiration-sucker,’ a cooling breeze. —स्वेद-च्छिद्, त्, त्, त्, ‘cutting per-spiration,’ absorbing or allaying perspiration, cooling. —स्वेद-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, sweat-produced, engendered by heat and moisture, generated by warm vapour or steam (said of insects and vermin). —स्वेद-जल, अस्, m. ‘sweat-water,’ perspiration. —स्वेद-मलोज्झित-देह (°ल-उज्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one whose body is freed from perspiration and impurity; (अस्), m. a Jaina of the highest order, a holy or sainted teacher of the Jainas. —स्वेद-लेश, अस्, m. a little perspiration. —स्वेद-विन्दु, उस्, m. or स्वेद-विप्लुष्, ट्, f. a drop of perspiration. —स्वेदाञ्जि (°द-अञ्°), इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having streaming ornaments (said of the Maruts; Sāy. = क्षरद्-आभरण, Ṛg-veda X. 67, 6). —स्वे-दानुविद्ध (°द-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, covered or streaked with perspiration. —स्वेदोद (°द-उद) or स्वेदोदक (°द-उद्°), अम्, n. ‘sweat-water,’ per-spiration.
53807: स्वेदन, अम्, n. perspiration, sweat; sweating, causing to perspire; any instrument or remedy for causing perspiration, a diaphoretic, sudorific; (ई), f. an iron plate or pan used as a cooking utensil, a fry-ing-pan, saucepan.
53808: स्वेदनिका, f. a boiler, saucepan, iron plate or pan used as a cooking utensil, frying-pan; a room for cooking, kitchen.
53809: स्वेदित, अस्, आ, अम्, sweated, warmed, heated, steamed.
53810: स्वेद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sweated or treated by sudorific means.
53812: स्वीकरण स्वी-करण, स्वी-कृत, स्वीय, &c. See p. 1158, col. 3.
53813: स्वुर्छ् स्वुर्छ् (= rt. स्फुर्छ्, q. v.), cl. 1. P. स्वूर्च्छति, &c., to spread, extend, expand; to forget.
53814: स्वृ स्वृ, cl. 1. P. स्वरति, सस्वार (3rd pl. सस्वरुस्), स्वरिष्यति, अस्वारीत् or अस्वार्-षीत्, स्वर्तुम्, स्वरितुम्, to sound, utter, recite, (ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 88, 5. the form सस्वर् = उच्चारितवान्, but in VII. 60, 10. = अन्तर्-हित, see सस्वर्, s.v.); to praise, sing the praises of (Ved.); to pain, afflict [cf. rt. स्वॄ]; to be pained; (according to Naigh. II. 14), to go: Caus. स्वारयति, यितुम्, Aor. असिस्वरत्: Pass. स्वर्यते, to be marked with the Svarita accent: Desid. सिस्वरिषति or सुस्वूर्षति: Intens. सास्वर्यते, सास्वर्ति; [cf. Zend gar; Gr. σῦρ-ιγξ, σῡρίζ-ω, σῡριγ-μό-ς, σύριγ-μα, ὕραξ, ὕρον; Lat. su-sur-ru-s, ab-sur-du-s, sur-du-s; probably Goth. svaran; Angl. Sax. swaran, swerian; Slav. svir-a-ti, svir-ĕlĭ, ‘a pipe;’ Lith. sur-ma, ‘a flute, pipe.’]
53815: स्वर, अस्, m. sound, noise; voice; tone, tune, music, a primary musical sound, note of the musical scale or gamut (of which there are seven, commonly thus arranged, 1. निषाद, 2. ऋषभ, 3. गान्-धार, 4. षड्ज, 5. मध्यम, 6. धैवत, 7. पञ्चम; these notes are described as resem-bling respectively the notes of an elephant, bull, goat, peacock, curlew or heron, horse, and Koil; they are designated by their initial letters or syllables thus, नि, ऋ, ग, ष, म, ध, प, and the order is some-times changed, षड्ज being placed first, पञ्चम fifth, and निषाद last); a symbolical expression for the number seven; a vowel (either ह्रस्व short, दीर्घ long, or प्लुत prolated); an accent, tone (of which there are three, viz. उदात्त, अनुदात्त, and स्वरित, see below); air breathed through the nostrils, nasal sound; snoring; (आ), f., N. of the chief wife of Brahmā (Gāyatrī being the other). —स्वर-गता-ध्यय (°त-अध्°), अस्, m., N. of the first book of the Saṅgīta-darpaṇa; of the first book of the Saṅ-gīta-ratnākara. —स्वर-ग्राम, अस्, m. the musical scale, gamut. —स्वर-तत्त्वोदय (°व-उद्°), अम्, n., N. of treatise on astrology by Jīva-nātha. —स्वर-पत्तन, अम्, n. ‘abode of accents,’ N. of the Sāma-veda (this Veda being chanted with a peculiar rhythm, and the efficacy of its prayers depending on their proper accentuation). —स्वर-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, composed in musical measure (said of a song &c.). —स्वर-भक्ति, इस्, f. ‘vowel-fracture,’ (in Vedic phonetics) a vowel-sound phonetically inserted in the pronunciation of र् or ल् when these letters are fol-lowed by a sibilant or other consonant without the intervention of a vowel (e. g. वर्ष pronounced वरिष). —स्वर-भङ्ग, अस्, m. interruption or indistinctness of utterance, broken articulation, crack-ing of the voice, hoarseness, fluttering of the voice, any defect in speaking (caused by emotion or morbid affections of the chest). —स्वर-भङ्गिन्, ई, m. ‘note-separating,’ a kind of bird. —स्वर-भेद, अस्, m. = स्वर-भङ्ग above. —स्वर-मण्ड-लिका, f. a kind of Vīṇā or stringed musical instru-ment (also read सुर-खण्डलिका). —स्वर-लासिका, f. a flute, pipe. —स्वर-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having sound, sonorous; having a voice, vocal; having an accent, accentuated. —स्वर-शास्त्र, अम्, n. a trea-tise on the modulations of sound or on the passage of the air through the nostrils. —स्वर-शुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, correct in musical measure. —स्वर-शून्य, अस्, आ, अम्, devoid of sound, without musical notes, unmelodious, unmusical. —स्वर-संयोग, अस्, m. the junction of vowels. —स्वर-सङ्क्रम, अस्, m. a transition or succession of sounds or notes; the musical scale, gamut. —स्वर-सन्धि, इस्, m. the junction or coalition of vowels. —स्वर-सामन्, आनस्, m. pl. epithet of particular days in a Sattra or sacrificial session. —स्वरांश (°र-अं°), अस्, m. a half or quarter tone in music. —स्वरान्तर (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘vowel-interval,’ the interval between two vowels, hiatus, = विवृत्ति; (ए), ind. in the middle of vowels, between two vowels. —स्वरोदय (°र-उद्°), अस्, m. the arising or production of sound (thought to be connected with certain tubular vessels of the body); (अस्, अम्), m. n., N. of a work on that subject; an astro-logical dissertation on the indications which the human breath affords under particular circumstances and astral conjunctions of the duration of life and future events; (अस्, आ, अम्), followed by a vowel. —स्वरोदय-विवरण, N. of a work on the tubular vessels of the body (regarded as passages of air and channels of sound). —स्वरोपध (°र-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, preceded by a vowel.
53816: स्वरण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. illustrious, celebrated, (Sāy. = देवेषु प्रकाशन-वत्, Ṛg-veda I. 18, 1.)
53817: स्वरित, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded; sounded as a note, pitched; articulated; accented; having the mixed or circumflex accent, circumflexed; (अस्), m. the third or mixed tone between high and low, which is thought to correspond with the circumflex accent, (the other two tones being called Ud-ātta and An-udātta, q.q. v.v.; the Ud-ātta sound of a vowel is said to result from the employing the upper half of the organs of utterance, and the An-udātta from em-ploying the lower half, while the Svarita represents a sustained mixed intonation neither high nor low, which is well illustrated by the expression तिर्यग्-गमन, i. e. a horizontal or wavy movement of the hand as distinguished from a direct upward and downward motion; Pāṇini, however, applies the term अन्-उदात्त, ‘non-elevated,’ to the neutral accent-less tone, and uses the term सन्न-तर or अन्-उदात्त-तर for ‘the very or proper An-udātta,’ i. e. the true grave accent which precedes the Udātta; in I. 2, 31. he calls the Svarita सम्-आहार, i. e. ‘a combination’ of the elevated and non-elevated tones; the Svarita accent is denoted in the Ṛg-veda by a small upright stroke above the syllable, the Anudātta-tara by a horizontal mark underneath, and the Udātta is left unmarked; but the Svarita mark may denote either a dependent or an independent Svarita, i. e. one produced by an Udātta immediately preceding or a real Svarita belonging to the word itself, and commonly produced by the suppression of an Udātta syllable; again, as a word is supposed to have only one real accent, so words which have real Svaritas of their own do not have Udātta accents; they are called आदि-स्वरित, मध्य-स्वरित, अन्त-स्वरित, according as they have Svaritas on the first, middle, or last syllable; it must also be borne in mind that when a dependent Svarita is immediately followed by an Udātta, the Svarita becomes a kind of Anudātta-tara, and is so marked, see ताथाभाव्य; there were, doubtless, different kinds of Svarita pronunciation.) —स्वरित-त्व, अम्, n. the state of having the Svarita accent. —स्वरितोपध (°त-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, pre-ceded by the Svarita; having the penultimate marked with the Svarita.
53818: स्वरितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who sings, a singer (Ved.); one who pains or afflicts, a painer (= उप-तापयितृ, but perhaps to be connected with rt. स्वॄ).
53819: स्वरु, उस्, m. sunshine; a sacrifice; part of a sacrificial post (or a slip of wood from it); the sacri-ficial post, (Sāy. = यूप); a thunderbolt; an arrow; a kind of scorpion; (उस्, उस्, उ), Ved. (perhaps) per-fect, entire, (Sāy. = स्वरवः = स्व-शकलवन्तः, Ṛg-veda III. 8, 6.)
53820: स्वरुस्, उस्, m. a thunderbolt (= स्वरु above).
53821: स्वर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be praised.
53822: स्वर्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being accented with the Svarita, circumflexed.
53823: स्वार, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to sound or accent.
53824: स्वृतीक स्वृतीक, अम्, n., Ved. water (= उदक, Naigh. I. 12; cf. स्मृतीक).
53825: स्वॄ स्वॄ or स्बॄ (= rt. सॄ; cf. rt. शॄ, also rt. स्वृ in one of its senses), cl. 9. P. स्वृ-णाति, स्बृणाति, &c., to hurt, kill.
53826: स्वेक् स्वेक् (= rt. स्रेक्), cl. 1. A. स्वेकते, &c., to go.
53830: स्वैतवः स्वैतवः, Nom. pl. masc., Ved. going auspiciously, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda V. 41, 9. = शोभन-गमनाः, as if fr. सु + ऐत-वः; in the Pada text the word is divided into स्व-एतवः।)

53900: हनु, उस्, m. f. the jaw (also हनू, ऊस्, f. and हनु, उ, n., and in the sense ‘jaw,’ thought to be con-nected with rt. 2. हा, but according to Sāy. so called, as हनन-साधन, ‘an instrument of destruc-tion’); (उस्), f. anything which destroys or injures life; a weapon; death, dying; disease, sickness; a kind of drug; a wanton woman, prostitute; [cf. Gr. γένυ-ς, γέν-ειο-ν, γν-άθο-ς, γναθ-μό-ς; Lat. gen-a; Goth. kinnu-s; Old Germ. kinni; Angl. Sax. cinn, cyn.] —हनु-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘jaw-seizure,’ locked jaw. —हनु-भेद, अस्, m. the gaping or parting asunder of the jaws. —हनुमज्-जयन्ती, f. the day of full moon of the month Caitra (being the supposed birthday of Hanumat). —हनु-मत्, आन्, m. ‘having (large) jaws,’ N. of a monkey-chief (one of the most celebrated of a vast host of semi-divine apes or monkey-like beings, who, according to Rāmā-yaṇa I. 16, were created to become the allies of Rāma-candra in his war with Rāvaṇa; the chiefs of these Simian armies were supposed to be the progeny of various gods; thus, Su-grīva, q. v., was son of the Sun, Bāli of Indra, Tāra of Vṛhas-pati, Gandha-mādana of Kuvera, Nala of Viśva-karman, Nīla of Agni, Su-ṣeṇa of Varuṇa, and the celebrated Hanu-mat of Pavana or Māruta, ‘the Wind;’ their character corresponds more to that of Genii than animals; they are all described as capable of supernatural feats, and Hanumat especially is fabled to have assumed any form at will, wielded rocks, removed mountains, mounted the air, seized the clouds, and rivalled Garuḍa in swiftness of flight; according to other legends, Hanumat was son of Śiva; his mother's name was Añjanā, q. v.); a particular sort of monkey, Simia Sinica. —हनुमन्-नाटक, अम्, n. the Hanumat drama (a celebrated drama in fourteen acts, supposed to have been written about the tenth or eleventh century of our era, and ascribed to Hanumat himself, who is said to have engraved it on rocks; it is emphatically called the Mahā-nāṭaka or great drama, and is, in fact, the story of the Rāmāyaṇa dramatized, the monkey-chief Hanumat playing a very important part in the action of the piece). —हनु-मूल, अम्, n. the root of the jaw. —हनु-स्तम्भ, अस्, m. ‘jaw-stoppage,’ locked jaw. —हनू-मत्, आन्, m. = हनु-मत् above; N. of the mythical author of the Khaṇḍa-praśasti; of the author of the Hanūman-nāṭaka. —हनूमत्-कल्प, N. of a work. —हनूमत्-कवच, अम्, n. ‘Hanūmat's breastplate,’ N. of a hymn addressed to the five-headed Hanūmat, (this hymn is taken from the Sudarśana-saṃhitā.) —हनूमत्-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a work in five chapters (describing the rites to be observed in the worship of Hanūmat; four chapters are said to be extracted from the Sudarśana-saṃhitā, and the re-maining one from the Rāmāyaṇa). —हनूमन्-नाटक, अम्, n. = हनुमन्-नाटक above.

53909: हन्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being struck or smitten; being killed.
53910: हानुक, अस्, ई, अम्, killing, hurting, mischievous.
53911: हनील हनील, अस्, m. (according to Śab-da-k.) a particular tree (= केतकी, also written ह-लीन).

53913: हपुषा हपुषा, f., N. of a particular sub-stance forming an article of trade (commonly called Habush, and said to be of a long form and black colour, and smelling like raw meat or fish; it is of two kinds).
53915: हबसोर हबसोर, N. of a place.
53916: हम् हम्, ind. an exclamation expressive of anger (= रुषोक्ति); of courtesy or respect.
53917: हमीआण हमी-आण, N. of a place.

53920: हम्भायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, lowing, bellowing.

53924: हय हय, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. हि, but connected with rt. हय् above), a horse; a symbolical expression for the number seven (that being the number of the horses of the Sun, see सप्ताश्व); a man of a par-ticular class; N. of Indra; of a Yādava king; the Yak or Bos Grunniens; (in prosody) a foot of four short syllables, proceleusmaticus; (आ), f. = हय-गन्-धा below; (ई), f. a female horse, mare. —हय-कातरा or हय-कातरिका, f. a kind of plant or tree. —हय-कोविद, अस्, आ, अम्, skilled in horses. —हय-गन्ध, अम्, n. a kind of medicinal salt, = काच-लवण; (आ), f. the plant Physalis Flexuosa; another plant (= अज-मोदा). —हय-गर्दभि, इस्, m. epithet of Śiva. —हय-ग्रीव, अस्, m. ‘horse-necked,’ N. of a form of Viṣṇu (manifested, accord-ing to one legend, in order to recover the Veda carried off by two Daityas called Madhu and Kaiṭa-bha); (ई), f. the plant Māṣa-parṇī, q. v. —हय-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to horses,’ barley; (आ), f. = हय-गन्-धा above; the Kharjūrī tree. —हय-मार or हय-मारक, अस्, m. ‘horse-killer,’ the fragrant oleander (= कर-वीर). —हय-मारण, अस्, m. ‘horse-killing,’ the sacred fig-tree, Ficus Religiosa. —हय-मेध, अस्, m. the horse-sacrifice, (see अश्व-मेध). —हयमेध-याज्, ट्, m. one who performs the horse-sacrifice. —हय-रूपिन्, ई, इणी, इ, Ved. having the shape of a horse. —हय-लीला-वती, f., N. of a work (mentioned by Malli-nātha). —हय-वाहन, अस्, m. epithet of Revanta (son of the Sun); of Kuvera. —हय-वाहन-शङ्कर, अस्, m. red mountain-ebony or a particular tree (= रक्त-काञ्चन). —हय-शाला, f. a stable for horses. —हय-शास्त्र, अम्, n. any treatise on horses, the art or science of training and managing horses. —हय-शिरस्, अस्, n. a horse's head; a mythical monster (described as vomiting forth the fire of Aurva's wrath, which was cast into the sea); (आस्), f. ‘having a horse's head,’ N. of a daughter of Vṛṣa-parvan; of a wife of Kratu. —हय-शीर्ष, अस्, m. ‘having a horse's head,’ a form of Viṣṇu. —हय-शीर्ष-पञ्चरात्र, N. of a work. —हय-सङ्ग्र-हण, अम्, n. the restraining or curbing of horses, checking horses. —हयाध्यक्ष (°य-अध्°), अस्, m. a superintendent of horses, head-groom. —हया-नन्द (°य-आन्°), अस्, m. ‘horse's-joy,’ a kind of bean, Phaseolus Mungo. —हयायुर्-वेद (°य-आय्°), अस्, m. the science of medicine applied to horses, veterinary science. —हयारि (°य-अरि), इस्, m. ‘horse-foe,’ the fragrant oleander, Nerium Odorum. —हयारूढ (°य-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, mounted on a horse; (अस्), m. a horseman, rider. —हयारोह (°य-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, mounted on horseback, a rider; (अस्), m. horsemanship, riding. —हयाशना (°य-अश्°), f. ‘horse-food,’ the gum olibanum tree. —हयेष्ट (°य-इष्°), अस्, m. ‘loved by horses,’ barley. —ह-योत्तम (°य-उत्°), अस्, m. ‘best of horses,’ a well-bred or excellent horse (= आजानेय).

53933: हरि 1. हरि, इस्, इस्, इ (perhaps to be connected with हिरि and rt. 2. हृ, q. v.; according to some an ab-breviated form of हरित्, p. 1167; in Uṇādi-s. IV. 118. said to be fr. rt. 1. हृ, p. 1175), green, greenish yellow, yellow; reddish brown, bay, tawny; (इस्), m. green (the colour); a yellow or golden colour; a reddish brown or tawny colour; N. of Viṣṇu; of Kṛṣṇa (regarded as identical with Viṣṇu); of Śiva; of Brahmā; of Indra; of Yama; a man, people, (in Naigh. II. 3. हरयः is enumerated among the मनुष्य-नामानि); N. of the Soma (so called as being हरित-वर्ण, see Nirukta IV. 19); a stone for crushing the Soma (Ved., Sāy. हरयः = ग्रावाणः, Ṛg-veda III. 44, 1); the moon; the sun; a ray of light; fire; wind, air; a horse; a bay horse, horse of Indra, (in Naigh. I. 15. हरी, m. du., is given as ‘the horses of Indra;’ and in Ṛg-veda I. 16, 1; 101, 10, &c., the plurals हरयः and हरिभिः occur; cf. हरीन्, acc. pl. ‘the horses of Indra,’ in Śakuntalā, Act 1); a lion; a parrot; the Koïl or Indian cuckoo; a peacock; a goose; an ape; a frog; a snake; one of the nine Varṣas or divisions into which the known continent is divided, (see वर्ष); N. of the poet Bhartṛ-hari (by which he is usually known); N. of several other authors; a species of the Aty-aṣṭi metre; [cf. Zend zairi, ‘yellow;’ zairina, ‘yellowish’ (= ह-रिण): Gr. χλό-η, χλο-ερό-ς, χλω-ρό-ς, χλό-ο-ς, χολή: Lat. helus (holus, olus), hel-vu-s, hel-vo-lus, gilvus: Old Germ. grô-j-u, gruo-j-u, grô-ni: Angl. Sax. growan, grœn, grene: Slav. zel-ige, ‘vegetables;’ zel-enu, ‘green:’ Lith. zel-iu, ‘to become green;’ zol-e, ‘grass;’ zal-ie-s, ‘green:’ Hib. glas, ‘green, pale.’] —हरि-कान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, beloved by Indra, dear to Indra; beautiful as a lion. —हरि-कृष्ण, अस्, m. a proper N. —हरि-केलीय, अस्, m. ‘sported in by Viṣṇu,’ the country of Bengal; (अस्, आ, अम्), belonging to or dwelling in Bengal. —हरि-केश, अस्, m. ‘yellow-haired,’ epithet of Savitṛ (Ved.); N. of one of the seven principal rays of the sun (supposed to supply heat to the stars); epithet of Śiva, (according to some so called as ‘lord of Hari and Brahmā; cf. हरि, 3. क); N. of a Yakṣa (who propitiated the god Śiva and was made by him a leader of his troops and a guardian of fields and fruits; see दण्ड-पाणि). —हरि-क्रान्ता, f. a kind of plant (= विष्णु-क्रान्ता). —हरि-क्षेत्र, N. of a place. —हरि-गण, अस्, m. a troop of horses; a proper N. —हरि-गन्ध, अम्, n. a sort of sandal (= हरि-चन्दन). —हरि-गृह, अम्, n. the abode of Hari; N. of a city and district, (also called Sam-bhalpūr, = शुम्भ-पुर, एक-चक्र।) —हरि-चन्दन, अस्, अम्, m. n. a sort of yellow sandal-wood or sandal tree (= तैल-पर्णिक, इन्द्र-चन्-दन, महा-गन्ध); one of the five trees of paradise (the other four being called Pārijāta, Man-dāra, Santāna, and Kalpa); (अम्), n. saffron; moon-light; the filament of a lotus (= पद्म-केशर); the person of a lover or mistress. —हरिचन्दना-स्पद (°न-आस्°), अम्, n. the site of yellow sandal-wood. —हरि-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of a physician (author of a commentary on the Caraka-tantra). —हरि-ज, अम्, n. (in astronomy) longitude (said to = क्षिति-ज). —हरि-जीवन-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Snāna-sūtra-paddhati. —हरि-तुरङ्गम, अस्, m., N. of Indra, (see हर्य्-अश्व।) —हरितुरङ्गमायुध (°म-आय्°), अम्, n. Indra's thunderbolt. —हरि-त्रात, अस्, आ, अम्, pro-tected by Hari. —हरि-दत्त, अस्, m. a proper N. —हरि-दर्भ, see हरिद्-गर्भ. —हरि-दास, अस्, m. a slave or worshipper of Viṣṇu; N. of a king; of the author of a commentary on the Nyāya-kusumāñjali; of the author of the Le-khaka-muktāmaṇi. —हरि-दिन, अम्, n. ‘Hari's day,’ a particular day sacred to Viṣṇu. —हरि-दीक्षित, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor. —हरि-दृश्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, see Vopa-deva IV. 13. —हरि-देव, अस्, m. the asterism Śravaṇā; a proper N. —हरि-द्रव, अस्, m. green fluid; (perhaps) Soma; a powder made from the blossoms of the Nāga-keśara tree. —हरि-द्रु, उस्, m. a kind of Curcuma (= दारु-हरिद्रा, पीत-दारु); a tree (in general). —हरि-द्वार, अम्, n. ‘Viṣṇu's gate,’ N. of a celebrated town and Tīrtha or sacred bathing-place (commonly called Hardvār or Hurdvār; this is the place where the Ganges finally leaves the mountainous districts for the level plains of Hin-dūstān, whence it is sometimes called Gaṅgā-dvāra; tens of thousands of pilgrims flock to this Tīrtha at particular seasons and seek priority of ablution in the sacred stream, the complete purgation from sin being supposed to depend on seizing the auspicious moment laid down by astrologers; it is called ‘Hari's gate,’ as leading to Vaikuṇṭha or Viṣṇu's heaven). —हरि-धायस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. yellow-rayed, having golden luminaries, (in Ṛg-veda III. 44, 3, Sāy. explains हरि-धायसम् by हरितो हरित-वर्णा धायसो धारका रश्मयो यस्याः।) —ह-रि-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Smṛti-sāra; of the author of the Rāma-vilāsa-kāvya; of the author of the Kaṇṭhābharaṇa-mārjana and the Kāvyādarśa-mārjana commentaries. —हरि-नामन्, अ, n. the name of Hari or Viṣṇu; (आ), m. the kidney-bean, Phaseolus Mungo. —हरि-नायक, अस्, m., N. of the author of a work on music. —हरि-नेत्र, अम्, n. the eye of Viṣṇu; a white lotus; an eye of a greenish colour; (अस्), m. ‘having greenish eyes,’ an owl. —हरि-पद, अम्, n. (ac-cording to some) the vernal equinox. —हरि-पर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, green-leaved; (अम्), n. a radish. —हरि-प्रबोध, N. of a work. —हरि-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, liked or loved by Viṣṇu; (अस्), m. the Kadamba tree; other plants, &c. Lakṣmī; the earth; sacred basil (= तुलसी); the twelfth day of a lunar fortnight; (अम्), n. a kind of dark sandal-wood; the root Uśīra, q. v. —हरि-बालुक, अम्, n. ‘yellow sand,’ a kind of perfume and drug (= एलवालु, q. v.). —हरि-बुङ्ग-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —हरि-भक्त, अस्, m. a worshipper of Viṣṇu. —हरि-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of the author of a work on music. —हरि-भद्र, अम्, n. = हरि-बालुक. —हरि-भाविनी or हरि-भाविणी, f. a woman who meditates on Viṣṇu. —हरि-भुज्, क्, m. ‘frog-eater,’ a snake. —हरि-मन्थ, अस्, m. the tree Premna Spinosa (the wood of which by attrition produces flame); the chick-pea (= चणक); N. of a particular country or district. —हरि-मन्थक, अस्, m. the chick-pea. —हरि-मन्थ-ज, अस्, m. ‘produced in the district Hari-mantha,’ the chick-pea; a sort of dark kidney-bean. —हरि-यूपीया, f., Ved., N. of a city or of a river. —हरि-योग, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a yoke of bay horses, yoked with horses. —हरि-योजन, अस्, m., Ved. ‘harnesser of the Hari steeds,’ Indra; [cf. हारियोजन।] —हरि-राम, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Dharmitāvacchedakatā-pratyāsatti-vicāra, the Navīna-mata-vicāra, the Maṅgala-vāda, and the Sāmagrī-vāda. —हरि-राय, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Jīcaraṇa-cihna-māhātmya. —हरि-लीला, f., N. of Vopa-deva's index to the Bhāgavata-Purāṇa. —हरिलीला-विवेक, अस्, m., N. of a com-mentary by Hemādri on the Hari-līlā. —हरि-लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, having dark-green eyes; tawny-eyed; (अस्), m. a crab; an owl. —हरि-वंश, अस्, m. the family of Kṛṣṇa (as identified with Viṣṇu); N. of a celebrated poem supplementary to the Mahā-bhārata on the history and adventures of Kṛṣṇa and his family, (it is usually regarded as part of the greater epic, though really a comparatively modern addition to it; the poem consists of no less than 16, 374 verses, comprised in three sections, called Harivaṃśa-parvan, Viṣṇu-parvan, and Bhaviṣya-parvan; in the first is contained a description of the creation of the world and a history of the solar and lunar races, the second gives a detailed biography of Kṛṣṇa, and the third an account of the future condition of the world with the corruptions about to prevail during the Kali-yuga.) —हरि-वंश-गोस्वा-मिन्, ई, m., N. of the author of the Rādhā-rasa-sudhā-nidhi. —हरि-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing Hari; (आन्), m. ‘possessing bay horses,’ N. of Indra, (in Ṛg-veda VIII. 40, 9. हरिवः, voc. c., occurs.) —हरि-वर्पस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. having a verdant form, tinted with green, green-coloured (said of the earth). —हरि-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a poet. —हरि-वर्ष, अम्, n. one of the nine divisions of Jambu-dvīpa or the known continent, (the country between the Niṣadha and Hema-kūṭa mountains, see वर्ष, p. 893); (अस्), m., N. of a king of Niṣadha (son of Agnīdhra), —हरि-वल्लभ, अस्, m. ‘beloved by Viṣṇu,’ N. of the author of the Sudhodaya; (आ), f. epithet of Lakṣmī; sacred basil (= तुलसी); another plant (= जया). —हरि-वा-सर, अम्, n. Viṣṇu's day (the eleventh or twelfth lunar day, or according to some, the first quarter of the twelfth lunar day). —हरि-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘Viṣṇu-bearer,’ Garuḍa; ‘having bay horses,’ Indra [cf. हर्य्-अश्व, हरि-हय]. —हरि-वीज, अस्, m. ‘Viṣṇu's seed,’ yellow orpiment, (see हरिताल।) —हरि-वृष, अम्, n. a division of the continent, (see हरि-वर्ष।) —हरि-शङ्कर, अस्, m., N. of a scribe; of a place. —हरि-शयन, अम्, n. the sleep of Viṣṇu. —हरि-शर, अस्, m. ‘having Viṣṇu for an arrow,’ epithet of Śiva, (Viṣṇu having served Śiva as the shaft which set the cities of Tripura on fire.) —हरि-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a poet. —हरि-शिप्र, अस्, m., Ved. ‘ruddy-jawed,’ epithet of Indra. —हरि-श्चन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम् (see चन्द्र), Ved. having golden-coloured splendor; (अस्), m., N. of the twenty-eighth king of the solar dynasty in the Tretā age, (he was son of Tri-śaṅku, and was cele-brated for his piety; according to the Mārkaṇḍeya-Purāṇa, which gives a most interesting legend de-tailing the history of this prince, he gave up his whole country, sold his wife and son, and finally himself, to satisfy the demands of Viśvā-mitra, whom he had provoked by interfering to protect the Sciences who were becoming mastered by this intensely austere sage; after enduring incredible sufferings, Hari-ścandra won the pity of the gods and was raised with his subjects to heaven; on the other hand, in the Sabhā-parvan of the Mahā-bhārata, verse 489 &c., his performance of the Rāja-sūya sacrifice is stated to have been the cause of his elevation, and in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa quite another legend is told about him, see under शुनः-शेप, p. 1014: in later legends Hari-ścandra is represented as insidiously induced by Nārada to relate his actions with unbecoming pride, whereupon he was degraded from Svarga, one stage at each sentence, till stopping in time and doing homage to the gods he was fixed with his capital in mid-air; his aerial city is popu-larly believed to be still visible in the skies at parti-cular times; cf. शौभ); (अम्), n., N. of a Liṅga. —हरिश्चन्द्र-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —हरिश्चन्द्र-पुर, अम्, n. the city of Hari-ścandra (= शौभ, see above). —हरि-श्मशारु or हरि-श्मश्रु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. ruddy-bearded, golden-bearded, having a yellow beard. —हरि-श्रम, अस्, m. a proper N. —हरि-श्रवा, f., N. of a river. —हरि-श्री, ईस्, ईस्, इ, Ved. blessed with or abounding in horses. —हरि-षाच्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. enjoying or par-taking of Soma, (Sāy. = सोमस्य सम्भक्तृ, Ṛg-veda X. 94, 12.) —हरि-षेण, अस्, m. (षेण for सेन fr. सेना), N. of the tenth of the Jaina Cakra-vartins. —हरि-ष्ठा, आस्, आस्, अम् (ष्ठा for स्था), Ved. one who stands over horses, a guider of horses, (Sāy. = हर्योः स्थातृ, Ṛg-veda VI. 17, 2.) —ह-रि-सख, अस्, m. ‘friend of Indra,’ a Gandharva. —हरि-सङ्कीर्तन, अम्, n. the act of pronouncing or repeating the name of Viṣṇu (supposed to possess great efficacy). —हरि-सुत, अस्, m. ‘son of Hari,’ N. of Arjuna; of the tenth Cakra-vartin, (also called Hari-ṣeṇa.) —हरि-सूक्त, अम्, n. a hymn addressed to Hari. —हरि-सूनु, उस्, m. ‘son of Hari,’ N. of Arjuna. —हरि-स्तोत्र, अम्, n. and हरि-स्तुति, इस्, f., N. of two Vedānta hymns (in praise of Viṣṇu). —हरि-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a priest; of the author of a commentary on the Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa. —ह-रि-हय, अस्, m. ‘having bay or gold-coloured horses,’ epithet of Indra; of the Sun; of Skanda; of Gaṇeśa. —हरि-हर, अस्, m. a particular form of deity consisting of Viṣṇu and Śiva conjoined; N. of a king; of a poet; of several other persons. —हरि-हर-कथा, f. the repeating of the names of Hari and Hara (i. e. of Viṣṇu and Śiva). —हरि-हर-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. ‘the sacred place of Viṣṇu and Śiva conjoined,’ N. of a particular Tīrtha and place of pilgrimage. —हरि-हर-पुरी, N. of a preceptor. —हरिहर-भाष्य, अम्, n., N. of a commen-tary. —हरि-हरात्मक (°र-आत्°), अस्, इका, अम्, identified with Viṣṇu and Śiva in their united state; (अस्), m. Garuḍa; the bull of Śiva (= शिव-वृष); Dakṣa (according to some); (अम्), n. = हरिहर-क्षेत्र. —हरि-हेति, इस्, f. the weapon of Viṣṇu, i. e. the Cakra or discus. —हरिहेति-हूति, इस्, m. = चक्र-वाक, a sort of duck. —हर्य्-अक्ष, अस्, m. ‘green-eyed, brown-eyed,’ a lion; N. of Kuvera; of Śiva; of a son of Pṛthu. —हर्य्-अङ्ग, अस्, m., N. of a king. —हर्य्-अश्व, अस्, m. ‘having bay horses called Hari,’ N. of Indra; of Śiva; of a son of Dṛḍhāśva; of several other persons; (आस्), m. pl., N. of 5000 sons of Dakṣa. —हर्य्-आत्मन्, आ, m. epithet of Uttama (one of the twenty-eight Vyāsas).
53934: हरिक, अस्, m. a horse of a yellowish or reddish brown colour (= हालक); a thief, (in this sense evidently fr. rt. 1. हृ); a gambler with dice.
53935: हरिण, अस्, ई, अम् (the fem. may equally belong to हरित, next col.), greenish or yellowish or reddish white, pale, whitish; (अस्), m. yellowish or reddish white (the colour); white (the colour); a deer, ante-lope, fawn, stag (one of five kinds, others being called ऋष्य, रुरु, पृषत, मृग); a goose; a minor division of the world; the sun; N. of Viṣṇu; of Śiva; (ई), f. green (the colour); yellow jasmine; a female deer, doe; a golden image; one of the four kinds of women, an excellent woman (= चि-त्रिणी, corresponding to the kind of man termed मृग); turmeric (= हरिता); madder (= मञ्-जिष्ठा); a species of the Aty-aṣṭi metre (= त-रुणी). —हरिण-कलङ्क, अस्, m. ‘deer-spotted,’ epithet of the moon. —हरिण-धामन्, आ, m. the moon. —हरिण-नयन, अस्, ई, अम्, deer-eyed, fawn-eyed, having eyes like a deer. —हरिण-नर्तक, अस्, m. a minstrel of Indra's heaven (= किन्-नर). —हरिण-प्लुत, अम्, आ, n. f. a kind of metre (described by some as a stanza having eleven syllables in every first and third Pāda, and twelve in every second and fourth; by others two kinds of metre are given). —हरिण-लोचन = हरिण-न-यन. —हरिण-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, deer-hearted, faint-hearted, timid. —हरिणाक्ष (°ण-अक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, deer-eyed, fawn-eyed; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva; (ई), f. a woman with beautiful eyes; a kind of perfume (= हट्ट-विलासिनी). —हरिणाङ्क (°ण-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘deer-marked,’ the moon; [cf. ह-रिण-कलङ्क।] —हरिणान्तर (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. a species of deer (= भार्याटिक).
53937: हरिणाय, Nom. A. हरिणायते, &c., to become a deer.
53938: हरिणी, see under हरिण. —हरिणी-वृत्त, अम्, n. the Hariṇī metre.
53939: हरित्, त्, त्, त् (in Uṇādi-s. I. 99. said to be fr. rt. 1. हृ, perhaps for original हरत्; cf. 1. हरि, हिरि, हिरण), green, of a green colour; greenish yellow, yellowish, golden-coloured; (त्), m. green (the colour); a swift horse; a horse of the Sun, (in Ṛg-veda I. 50, 8. सप्त-हरितः is explained by Sāy. as ‘the seven horses of the Sun,’ symbolical of सप्त रश्मयः, ‘the seven rays;’ see also Ṛg-veda I. 115, 4, where हरितः is explained by ‘the Sun's horses,’ as well as by रस-हरण-सीलान् रश्मीन्, ‘the rays which take up the moisture;’ the seven horses of the Sun are sometimes called mares, cf. शुन्ध्यु; they probably really symbolize the seven days of the week); the kidney-bean, Phase-olus Mungo; a lion; the sun; Viṣṇu; (त्), m. n. grass; (त्), f. a quarter, region; a point of the com-pass; turmeric; [cf. according to some, Gr. χάρι-τες, χόρτος; perhaps Lat. viridi-s (for gviridis); Goth. gulth, gras; Angl. Sax. gold, grœs.] —ह-रित्-पर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, green-leaved, having green leaves; (अम्), n. a radish; [cf. हरि-पर्ण।] —ह-रिद्-अश्व, अस्, m. ‘whose horses are called Harit,’ the sun, (see हरित् above.) —हरिद्-गर्भ, अस्, m. a green or yellowish Kuśa grass with broad leaves (= पृथु-च्छद; also read हरि-दर्भ). —ह-रिद्-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, green-coloured, of a yellowish golden colour. —हरिन्-मणि, इस्, m. ‘green-gem,’ an emerald. —हरिन्-मुद्ग, अस्, m. a sort of kidney-bean (= शारद).
53940: हरित, अस्, आ or हरिणी, अम् (connected with हरिण above; cf. its fem. हरिणी; cf. also 2. भ-रित with its fem. भरिणी), green, of a green colour; reddish brown or tawny; grassy, verdant; dark blue; (अस्), m. green (the colour); a lion; a kind of grass (= मन्थानक); N. of a son of Yuvanāśva; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a Gotra; (आ), f. Dūrvā grass; turmeric; a brown-coloured grape; other plants, = जयन्ती; = पाची; = नील-दूर्वा; (अम्), n. a kind of perfume (= स्थौणेयक)। —हरित-च्छद, अस्, आ, अम्, green-leaved, having green leaves. —हरित-तृण, अम्, n. green grass. —हरित-पत्त्रिका, f. ‘green-leaved,’ a kind of creeping plant (= पाची). —हरित-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, green-coloured. —हरित-शाक, अस्, m. the Śigru plant. —हरिताश्मन् (°त-अश्°), अ, n. ‘green-coloured stone,’ an emerald; a turquoise; sulphate of copper or blue vitriol. —हरिताश्व (°त-अश्°), अस्, m., N. of a son of Su-dyumna. —हरिती-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made green, coloured green, made verdant.
53941: हरितक, अस्, m. a green vegetable, pot-herb.
53942: हरिताय, Nom. A. हरितायते, &c., to become green or verdant.
53943: हरितायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming green.
53944: हरिताल, अस्, m. a kind of pigeon of a yellowish green colour; (ई), f. Dūrvā grass; a streak or line in the sky (= आकाश-रेखा); a sort of creeper (= खड्ग-पत्त्र); a kind of tree (according to Sāy.); the fourth day of the light half of the month Bhādra; (अम्), n. yellow orpiment or sulphuret of arsenic (described as the seed or seminal energy of Viṣṇu, = हरेर् वीर्यम्). —हरिताल-जनक, अस्, m. orpi-ment-producer (a word employed in modern Sanskrit to express the metal arsenic).
53945: हरितालक, अस्, m. a kind of pigeon of a yellowish green colour; (अम्), n. yellow orpiment; painting the person, theatrical decoration.
53946: हरितालिका, f. Dūrvā grass; the fourth day of the light half of the month Bhādra. —हरितालिका-व्रत, अम्, n. a particular religious observance on the above day.
53947: हरिद्रा, f. turmeric; the root of turmeric pow-dered, (forty-six synonyms of this plant are given.) —हरिद्राक्त (°रा-अक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, smeared or stained with turmeric. —हरिद्रा-गणपति, इस्, or हरिद्रा-गणेश, अस्, m. a particular form of the god Gaṇesa (in whose honour a Mantra is repeated, ac-companied with offerings mixed with turmeric). —हरिद्राङ्ग (°रा-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘yellow-bodied,’ a kind of yellow bird (= हरिताल). —हरिद्राभ (°रा-आभ), अस्, आ, अम्, resembling turmeric, of a yellow colour; (अस्), m. the plant Pīta-śāla, q. v.; zedoary (= कर्पूरक). —हरिद्रा-राग or हरि-द्रा-रागक, अस्, आ, अम्, turmeric-coloured; unsteady in affection or attachment, fickle, capricious (like the colour of turmeric which does not last).
53948: 1. हरिमन्, आ, m. (for 2. see under rt. 1. हृ), yellowness; yellowness (of the body), a kind of disease, (Ṛg-veda I. 50, 11, &c.); paleness.
53949: हरिय, अस्, m. a horse of a yellowish or reddish colour.
53950: हरीतकी, f. the yellow Myrobalan tree, Termi-nalia Chebula, (twenty-eight synonyms and seven varieties of this are enumerated; a form हरीतक is also found.)
53952: हरिमन्त हरिमन्त, अस्, m., N. of an Āṅgirasa (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda IX. 72).
53953: हरिले हरिले, ind. (according to some) a vocative particle used in addressing a female slave (in theatrical language).
53954: हरिष हरिष, अस्, m. (a modern form of हर्ष), joy, happiness (according to Śabda-k.).
53955: हरीषा हरीषा, f. a particular kind of seasoning or condiment.
53956: हरेणु हरेणु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 1. fr. rt. 1. हृ), pease, pulse; a creeper marking the boundary of a village; N. of Laṅkā; (उस्), f. a sort of drug or perfume (= रेणुका, q. v.); a re-spectable woman; a copper-coloured deer.
53957: हरेणुक, अस्, m. pease, pulse (= कलाय).
53959: हर्मन् हर्मन्, आ, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. हृ), gaping, yawning.
53960: हर्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, yawned; thrown, cast, sent; burned [cf. घर्म].
53961: हर्मुट हर्मुट, अस्, m. (according to some) the sun; a tortoise.
53962: हर्म्य हर्म्य, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. 1. हृ in the sense of ‘to captivate or charm the mind;’ but more probably to be connected with घर्म), a hole in the ground for cooking, a kind of pit or oven for holding fire, fire-place, hearth; a domestic hearth, home; house, building, palace, mansion, any large building or residence of a man of wealth, [cf. Zend zairimya; Lat. formus]; a fiery pit, place of torment, region of darkness, abode of evil spirits, abode of the departed, the nether world; (अस्, आ, अम्), living in houses. —हर्म्य-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. the roof or upper room of a palace. —हर्म्य-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, living in a palace. —हर्म्य-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. standing near a hearth or fire-place; being in a house. —हर्म्य-स्थल, अम्, n. the room or chamber of a mansion or palace. —हर्-म्याङ्गन (°य-अङ्°), अम्, n. the court of a palace.
53963: हर्य् हर्य्, cl. 1. P. हर्यति (sometimes also A. -ते), जहर्य, हर्यिष्यति, अहर्-यीत्, हर्यितुम्, Ved. to desire, yearn after, love, like, be pleased with, (in Naigh. II. 6. enumerated among the कान्ति-कर्माणः); to worship, pray to; to take [cf. rt. 1. हृ]; to threaten; to be weary; to go, (in Naigh. II. 14. enumerated among the गति-कर्माणः): Caus. हर्ययति, -यितुम्, Aor. अज-हर्यत्: Desid. जिहर्यिषति: Intens. जाहर्यते, जाहर्यीति, जाहर्ति; [cf. Gr. χαίρω, χαρ-ά, χάρ-μα, χάρι-ς, χαρίζομαι, χαρί-εις, γέλως, γελάω: Lat. gra-tu-s, grat-ia (Osc. her-est, Herentati-s, ‘Ve-nus:’ Umbr. heriest): Goth. faihu-gair-n-s, ‘ava-ricious;’ gair-uni, ‘affection;’ gailjan, gôljan: Old Germ. ger, giri, ‘desirous;’ geri, giri, ‘greedi-ness;’ gerôn, ‘to desire:’ Angl. Sax. gal, gagol: Lith. gor-u-ti, gor (?) : Slav. zel-e-ti (?) .]
53964: हर्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. desiring, liking, lov-ing, (Sāy. = कामयमान; in Ṛg-veda I. 57, 2. according to Sāy. हर्यतः = प्रेप्सतः or शोभ-नः, see the next.)
53965: हर्यत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. amiable, beloved, (Sāy. = स्पृहणीय, Ṛg-veda III. 5, 3); agreeable, pleasant, delicious (said of Soma); (अस्), m. a horse; a steed fit for the Aśva-medha sacrifice; N. of the author of a hymn in the Ṛg-veda, (see प्रागाथ।)
53966: हर्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. desiring, wishing, loving, (Sāy. = कामयमान।)
53970: हर्षीका हर्षीका, f. a kind of metre.
53971: हल् 1. हल्, cl. 1. P. हलति, जहाल, अहा-लीत्, &c., to plough, make furrows.
53972: हल, अम्, n. a plough; ugliness, deformity, = वैरूप्य; (आ), f. the earth; water; spirituous liquor, wine. —हल-धर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, plough-holding, having a plough; (अस्), m. a ploughman; epithet of Bala-rāma (as bearing a peculiar weapon shaped like a ploughshare; cf. सीर-पाणि). —हल-भूति, इस्, f. agriculture, husbandry. —हल-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, plough-holding, possessing a plough; (त्), m. a ploughman; Bala-rāma; [cf. सीर-भृत्।] —हल-भृति, इस्, f. ploughing, agriculture, husbandry; (इस्), m., N. of a Muni (= उप-वर्ष, कृत-कोटि, अ-याचित). —हल-मुखी, f. a kind of metre. —हल-राक्ष, अम्, n. a kind of shrub (= आहुल्य). —हल-हति, इस्, f. ‘plough-striking,’ ploughing, furrowing. —हलायुध (°ल-आय्°), अस्, m. ‘plough-weaponed,’ Bala-rāma, (see above); N. of a poet (son of Dhanañ-jaya); of the author of the Brāhmaṇa-sarvasva; of the author of the Purāṇa-sarvasva; of the author of the Abhidhāna-ratnamālā lexicon.
53973: हलय, Nom. P. हलयति, &c., to plough (= हलिं गृह्णाति, Vopa-deva XXI. 17).
53974: हलाह, अस्, m. a horse of a mixed or variegated colour, (also read हालाह।)
53975: हलि, इस्, m. a large plough, ploughshare (= जित्या, Vopa-deva XXVI. 20; = वृहद्-धल, q. v.); a furrow (according to some); agriculture.
53976: हलिन्, ई, m. a ploughman, agriculturist, cultivator; N. of Bala-rāma; (इनी), f. a number of ploughs; a kind of plant (= लाङ्गलिकी). —हलि-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to agriculturists,’ the Kadamba tree; (आ), f. spirituous liquor (= मदिरा).
53977: हली, f. the plant Kali-kārī, q. v.
53978: हलीषा, f. (probably fr. हल + ईषा), = लाङ्ग-लीषा, the handle of a plough.
53979: हल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be ploughed or tilled, arable; belonging to or proceeding from ugliness or deformity, ugly; (आ), f. a multitude of ploughs; (अम्), n. a ploughed field, arable land; ugliness; de-formity.
53980: हल् 2. हल्, m. n. (in Pāṇini's system) a technical expression for all the consonants; any con-sonant. —हल्-अन्त, अस्, आ, अम्, ending in a con-sonant.
53982: हलहला हल-हला (an imitative sound), halloo, hallooing. —हलहला-शब्द, अस्, m. shout-ing Hala-halā, hallooing, shout, outcry, tumult.
53983: हला हला, f. a female friend, (see also हला under हल); (हला), ind. a vocative particle used in addressing a female friend who is an equal (in theatrical language).
53984: हलाहल हलाहल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (= हाल-हल, q. v., sometimes also written हलहल, and said to be fr. rt. 1. हल्), a sort of deadly poison [cf. कालकूट at p. 226, col. 2]; (अस्), m. a kind of snake (= ब्रह्म-सर्प); a Jaina or Bauddha sage; a sort of lizard or newt.
53985: हलीन हलीन, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. हल्), the Teak tree (= शाक).
53986: हलीमक 1. हलीमक, अम्, n. (probably con-nected with 1. हरिमन् at p. 1167, col. 2), a sort of jaundice, paleness or yellowness of skin.
53987: हलुआण हलुआण or हलूआण, N. of a place.
53988: हल्लक हल्लक, अम्, n. the red lotus.
53989: हल्लन हल्लन, अम्, n. rolling or tossing about, rolling about in sleep.
53990: हल्लीश हल्लीश, अम्, n. one of the eighteen Upa-rūpakas or minor dramatic entertainments (de-scribed as a piece in one act, consisting chiefly of singing and dancing by one male and seven, eight, or ten female performers), a ballet; a circular dance (performed by women).
53991: हल्लीशक, अस्, m. dancing in a ring (as performed by women).
53994: हव 1. हव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. हु), an oblation, burnt-offering, sacrifice.
53995: हवङ्ग, अस्, m. (probably हवं + ग), eating rice and curds from a metal cup.
53996: 1. हवन, अम्, n. the act of offering an oblation with fire; an oblation to the gods, burnt-offering, sacrifice; (ई), f. a hole made in the ground for the sacrificial fire which is to receive a burnt-oblation.  — 1. हवन-स्यद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hastening to a sacrifice. —हवनायुस् (°न-आय्°), उस्, m. ‘having the burnt-offering for its life,’ fire.
53997: हवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be offered with fire, fit for an oblation or sacrifice, sacrificial; (अम्), n. any-thing fit for an oblation; clarified butter, ghee.
53998: हवित्री, f. a hole made in the ground for holding the sacred fire for an oblation.
53999: हविष्य, अम्, n. anything fit for an oblation; clarified butter; wild rice (or any similar wild grain); rice mixed with ghee; a hymn in praise of oblations (Ved). —हविष्य-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating clarified butter; (क्), m. fire. —हविष्यान्न (°य-अन्°), अम्, n. food fit to be eaten during certain holy days (or during the continuance of fasts and other re-ligious observances); any particularly pure food (as wheat, cow's milk, &c.). —हविष्याशिन् (°य-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, devouring clarified butter, (Manu XI. 218); (ई), m. fire.
54001: हविस्, इस्, n. anything offered as an oblation with fire, clarified butter, ghee; an oblation or burnt-offering (in general); water, (in Naigh. I. 12. enu-merated among the उदक-नामानि); epithet of Śiva. —हविः-शेष, अस्, m. the residue of an obla-tion. —हविर्-अशन, अम्, n. the act of devouring clarified butter; (अस्), m. ‘consuming oblations,’ fire. —हविर्-गन्धा, f. ‘smelling like clarified butter,’ the Śamī tree. —हविर्-गेह, अम्, n. any house or chamber in which an oblation is offered, a sacrificial hall. —हविर्-दा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. a giver of obla-tions, (said of Rudra, Ṛg-veda IV. 3, 7.) —हविर्-धान, अम्, n., Ved. ‘ghee-containing,’ an oblation; (ए), n. du. the two receptacles or vehicles on which the Soma and other offerings are put; (अस्), m., N. of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda X. 11 — 13 (having the patronymic Āṅgi). —हविर्-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating clarified butter; (क्), m. fire; N. of the Pitṛs of the Kṣatriyas. —हविर्-भू, ऊस्, f., N. of the wife of Pulastya. —हविर्-मथि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. destroying or obstructing oblations, impeding sacrificial rites. —हविर्-मन्थ, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= ग-णिकारी). —हविर्-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular sacrifice, N. of the first book of the Śata-patha-Brāhmaṇa (ac-cording to the Mādhyandina-śākhā). —हविर्-यज्ञ-संस्था, f. a kind of sacrifice, (seven Havir-yajña-saṃsthās are enumerated, viz. Agny-ādheya, Agni-hotra, Darśa-pūrṇamāsau, Cāturmāsyāni, Paśu-ban-dha, Sautrāmaṇī, and Pāka-yajña.) —हविर्-याजिन्, ई, m. ‘ghee-offerer,’ a priest. —हविष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. performing a sacrifice. —हविष्-पङ्क्ति, इस्, m., Ved., scil. यज्ञ, a sacrifice consisting of five oblations. —हविष्-पति, इस्, m., Ved. the lord of a sacrifice. —हविष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of oblations; (अन्तस्), m. pl., N. of a class of Pitṛs (re-garded as progenitors of Kṣatriyas and as descended from Aṅgiras; Manu III. 197, 198). —हविष्य्-अन्तीय, अम्, n., N. of nineteen Vedic texts begin-ning हविष्यन्तम्, (Manu XI. 251.)
54002: 1. हव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be offered in oblations, (Sāy. = होतव्य); (अस्), m., N. of a son of Atri; (अम्), n. an oblation or offering to the gods (as dis-tinguished fr. कव्य, q. v.); clarified butter, ghee. —हव्य-कव्य, अम्, n. oblations both to the gods and to the spirits of deceased ancestors, (also आनि, n. pl.) —हव्य-जुष्टि, इस्, f., Ved. the favour of an oblation, an acceptable oblation, (Sāy. = हविः-सेवा।) —हव्य-दाति, इस्, f., Ved. ‘oblation-giving,’ a sacri-ficial offering; (इस्, इस्, इ), giving sacrificial offerings. —हव्य-पाक, अस्, m. an oblation (of rice, barley, &c.) cooked with butter and milk for presentation to the gods; the vessel in which such an oblation is prepared. —हव्य-वाह्, ट्, or हव्य-वाह, अस्, m. ‘oblation-bearer,’ Agni or fire. —हव्य-वाहन, अस्, ई, अम्, bearing oblations, conveying oblations; (अस्), m. fire; epithet of the ninth Kalpa; N. of a son of Śuci. —हव्य-वाहिनी, f. ‘oblation-bearer,’ N. of a goddess. —हव्य-सूद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. flowing with oblations, affording oblations (said of cows as affording milk that yields butter for sacrificial rites). —हव्याश (°य-आश) or हव्याशन (°य-अश्°), अस्, m. ‘oblation-eater,’ fire.
54003: हव 2. हव, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. rt. ह्वे), call-ing, call; invocation, prayer; order, command; challenging, defying.
54004: 2. हवन, अम्, n. the act of calling, an invoca-tion; challenging to battle. —हवन-श्रुत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. listening to an invocation. —२। हवन-स्यद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hastening to battle.
54005: हवस्, अस्, n., Ved. a song of praise, hymn, prayer.
54006: हवीमन्, आ, m., Ved. invocation; challenging; battle, (Sāy. = सङ्ग्राम, Ṛg-veda VII. 83, 4.)
54007: 2. हव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be invoked, (Sāy. = आह्वातव्य।)
54008: हवा हवा or हवाव, ind. (a term imply-ing) undoubtedly, certainly.
54009: हस् 1. हस्, cl. 1. P. हसति, जहास, हसि-ष्यति, अहसीत्, हसितुम्, to laugh, smile; to laugh at, ridicule (with acc.); to resemble, (see हसत्): Pass. हस्यते, Aor. अहासि: Caus. हासयति, यितुम्, Aor. अजीहसत्, to cause to laugh, make laugh, provoke laughter: Desid. जिहसिषति: Intens. जा-हस्यते, जाहस्ति, to laugh immoderately; [cf. per-haps Gr. τω-θεία, τω-θάζω; probably Lat. histrio.]
54010: 2. हस्, Ved. laughter, joy; brightness, brilliance. —हस्-कर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. causing joy or prosperity; making bright, (Sāy. = वृद्धेः कर्तृ or प्रभासक, Ṛg-veda IV. 7, 3.) —हस्-कार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. causing brightness or radiance (said of lightning; Sāy. = दीप्ति-कर, Ṛg-veda I. 23, 12). —हस्-कृति, इस्, f., Ved. a song of praise; (इस्, इस्, इ), causing joy, (Sāy. = हास-कारिन् or हर्षस्य सूचक, Ṛg-veda VIII. 89, 6.)
54011: हस, अस्, m. laughter, laughing, a laugh; de-rision. —हसा-मुदौ, m. du., Ved. laughing and rejoicing.
54012: हसत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, laughing, smiling; resem-bling (i. e. smiling like, with acc., Kirāt. VIII. 44); (अन्ती), f. a portable fire-pan, small furnace, chafing-dish; Arabian jasmine; a kind of Śākinī, q. v.
54013: हसन, अम्, n. the act of laughing, laughter, a laugh; (आ), f. laughter; a joke, subject of laughter or ridicule, (Ṛg-veda IX. 112, 4.)
54014: हसनी, f. a portable fire-place or chafing-dish. —हसनी-मणि, इस्, m. ‘furnace-jewel,’ fire.
54015: हसनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, laughable; to be ridiculed, ridiculous.
54016: हसन्तिका, f. (fr. हसन्ती), a portable fire-place or small furnace.
54018: हसित, अस्, आ, अम्, laughed, laughing, smiling; expanded, blossomed, blown (as a flower); (अम्), n. laughter, jesting; smiling; the bow of Kāma (god of love).
54019: हसितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who laughs, a laugher, smiler.
54020: हसित्वा, ind. having laughed, having smiled.
54021: हस्र, अस्, आ, अम्, smiling; stupid, ignorant, a fool.
54022: हास, अस्, m. laughing, laughter; mirth, merry-making, joy; derision. —हास-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing laughter, ridiculous; laughing, merry.
54023: हासक, अस्, m. a laugher; one who causes laughter, a buffoon, merry-andrew.
54024: हासमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. laughing, being de-lighted, (Sāy. = हासं कुर्वत्, हर्ष-युक्त।)
54026: हासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, laughing, smiling, making merry.
54027: हास्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be laughed at, laughable, ridiculous; (अम्), n. laughter, laughing, mirth (one of the ten Rasas, see रस), jest, amusement; ridi-cule, derision. —हास्य-ता, f. laughableness, ridicu-lousness. —हास्य-पदवी, f. ‘road of laughter,’ ridicule, laughter, (हास्य-पदवीं या, to expose one's self to laughter, incur ridicule.) —हास्य-रस, अस्, m. the sentiment of humour, sense of humour, comic vein, facetiousness (the fifth of the ten Rasas, see रस). —हास्यार्णव (°य-अर्°), अस्, m. ‘ocean of mirth,’ N. of a drama by Jagad-īśvara. —हास्या-स्पद (°य-आस्°), अम्, n. a laughing-stock, butt for derision.
54028: हस्त हस्त, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 86. fr. rt. 1. हस्), the hand; the thirteenth as-terism, (see below); the fore-arm, cubit; a measure of length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger (= twenty-four Aṅgulas or about eighteen inches); an elephant's trunk; (in prosody) an ana-pest; quantity, abundance, mass, (in this sense only at end of comps. and when compounded with words signifying ‘hair;’ cf. केश-हस्त); (आ), f. the thir-teenth lunar asterism (represented by a hand and containing five stars, identified by some with part of the constellation Corvus); (अम्), n. a pair of leather bellows; (ए), ind. in hand, in one's possession; [cf. Gr. χανδ-άν-ω (ἔ-χαδ-ον, κέ-χανδ-α, χείσομαι); Lat. pre-hend-o, hed-era (?) ; Goth. bi-git-an, handu; Angl. Sax. gitan (= Eng. get), hand.] —हस्त-कमल, अम्, n. a lotus carried in the hand (thus when Lakṣmī was churned out of the ocean, she appeared holding a lotus). —हस्त-कौ-शल, अम्, n. skilfulness of hand, manual dexterity. —हस्त-क्रिया, f. any manual performance. —हस्त-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, come to hand, fallen into one's possession, procured, gained, obtained, secured. —हस्त-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —हस्त-गृह्य, ind., Ved. having taken the hand. —हस्त-घ्न, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of arm-guard or shield (defending the fore-arm from the blows of the bow-string). —हस्त-चापल्य, अम्, n. = हस्त-कौशल। —हस्त-च्छेदन, अम्, n. the amputation of a hand. —हस्त-च्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shaken or moved with the hand, moved or thrown violently by means of the hand. —हस्त-च्युति, इस्, f., Ved. moving or shaking about with the hand, (according to Sāy. हस्त-च्युती = हस्त-प्रच्युत्या, हस्त-गत्या, Ṛg-veda VII. 1, 1.) —हस्त-ज्योडि, इस्, m. a kind of tree or plant (= कर-ज्योडि). —हस्त-तल, अम्, n. the palm of the hand; the tip of an elephant's trunk. —हस्त-ताल, अस्, m. clapping the hands together. —हस्त-त्रय-सम्मिते, ind. at a distance of three Hastas. —हस्त-दोष, अस्, m. a slip of the hand, mistake committed by the hand. —हस्त-धात्री = हस्तामलक. —हस्त-धारण, अम्, n. warding off a blow; stopping a blow with the hand. —हस्त-पादादि (°द-आदि), the hands and feet &c., the extremities, the limbs of the body. —हस्त-पुच्छ, अम्, n. the lower part of the fore-arm, the hand below the wrist. —हस्त-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. the back of the hand (also called अप-पृष्ठ). —हस्त-प्राप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, reached with the hand, held in the hand; obtained, secured (= कर-प्राप्त)। —हस्त-मणि, इस्, m. a jewel worn on the wrist. —हस्त-मात्र, a cubit in length, (see मात्र।) —हस्त-युगल, अम्, n. the two hands. —हस्त-रत्नावली (°न-आव्°), f., N. of a work by Rāghava (treating of the various movements of the hands &c.). —हस्त-रेखा, f. a line on the hand. —हस्त-लाघव, अम्, n. lightness of hand, manual readiness, smartness, cleverness, legerdemain. —हस्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having hands, handy, dexterous, clever, skilful. —हस्त-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being or remain-ing in the hand, seized, held, caught hold of. —हस्त-वारण, अम्, n. restraining the hand (of another); warding off a blow. —हस्त-विम्ब, अम्, n. perfuming or smearing the body with unguents &c. —हस्त-संवाहन, अम्, n. rubbing or sham-pooing with the hands. —हस्त-सिद्धि, इस्, f. per-forming or effecting anything with the hand, manual labour; hire, wages, salary. —हस्त-सूत्र or हस्त-सूत्रक, ‘hand-ribbon;’ (अम्), n. a bracelet worn on the wrist. —हस्त-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, staying in the hand, being in hand, held, grasped. —हस्त-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, being in hand, held. —हस्ताक्षर (°त-अक्°), अम्, n. one's own sign manual, autograph, signature, handwriting. —हस्ताग्र (°त-अग्°), अम्, n. the extremity of the hand, the fingers. —हस्ता-ग्र-लग्न (°त-अग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘joined hand in hand,’ married; [cf. पाणि-ग्रह।] —हस्ताङ्गुलि (°त-अङ्°), इस्, f. ‘hand-finger,’ any finger of the hand. —हस्तामलक (°त-आम्°), अस्, m., N. of one of the four principal disciples of Śaṅkarācārya; (अम्), n. the fruit of Emblic Myrobalan held in the hand; N. of a short work by Hastāmalaka (containing the elements of the Vedānta). —हस्तामलक-भा-ष्य, अम्, n. a commentary on the above by Śaṅ-karācārya. —हस्तावलम्ब (°त-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, supported by the hand of another. —हस्तावाप (°त-आव्°), अस्, m. ‘hand-bracelet,’ a finger-guard, arm-guard (used by archers, = ज्याघात-वारण). —हस्ता-हस्ति, ind. hand to hand. —हस्ते-करण, अम्, n. ‘taking by the hand,’ marriage (= पाणौ-करण). —हस्ते-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to take in hand, take possession of, make one's own. —हस्ते-कृत्य, ind. having taken possession of.
54029: हस्तक, अस्, m. a position of the hands.
54030: हस्तिक, अस्, n. a multitude or collection of ele-phants (= गज-त).

54033: हस्तिना-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city founded by king Hastin, q. v., (it was situated about fifty-seven miles north-east of the modern Dillī or Delhi on the banks of an old channel of the Ganges, and was the capital of the kings of the Lunar line, as Ayodhyā was of the Solar dynasty; hence it forms a central scene of action in the Mahā-bhārata; here Dhṛta-rāṣṭra reigned when the government was resigned by his brother Pāṇḍu, and here the five Pāṇḍava princes were educated along with their cousins the Kauravas, and here at the conclusion of the great war between them Yudhi-ṣṭhira was crowned after a triumphal progress through the streets of the city; see Śānti-parvan 1386-1410: other names for this celebrated town are गजाह्वय, नाग-साह्वय, नागाह्व, हास्तिन।)

54134: हेतु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. 54325: हर्ष, अस्, m. bristling, erection (especially of the hair, but also said of other things); thrilling, thrill, rapture, delight, glee, joy, pleasure, gladness, exultation, happiness; Joy (personified as a son of Dharma); N. of a king of Kaśmīra (celebrated as a great patron of learning; he was son of Hīra and was said to be himself a writer and poet, author of the Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya, the Chanda-praśasti, the Nāgānanda-nāṭaka, the Naiṣadīya-carita, the Ratnāvalī, &c.); (अस्, आ, अम्), happy, delighted. —हर्ष-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing delight, grati-fying, delighting. —हर्ष-कीर्त्ति, इस्, m., N. of the author of a commentary on the Śruta-bodha. —हर्ष-क्रोध, औ, m. du. joy and anger. —हर्-ष-चरित, अम्, n., N. of a poem. —हर्ष-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, arising from joy. —हर्ष-जड, अस्, आ, अम्, paralyzed with joy. —हर्ष-देव, अस्, m. king Harṣa, (see हर्ष above.) —हर्ष-युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, filled with joy, joyful. —हर्ष-वर्धन, अस्, m. ‘joy-promoter,’ N. of a king. —हर्ष-विवर्-धन, अस्, ई, अम्, increasing or promoting joy. —हर्ष-विवृद्ध-सत्त्व, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose vigour is increased by happiness. —हर्ष-विह्वल, अस्, आ, अम्, agitated with joy, overjoyed. —हर्ष-समन्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, filled with joy. —हर्ष-स्वन, अस्, m. a cry of joy, sound of pleasure. —हर्षान्वित (°ष-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, full of joy, happy. —हर्षाविष्ट (°ष-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, penetrated or filled with joy. —हर्षोत्कर्ष (°ष-उत्°), अस्, m. excess of happiness. —हर्षो-दय (°ष-उद्°), अस्, m. rise of joy, occurrence of pleasure.
54326: हर्षक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, delighting, gladden-ing, rejoicing, pleasing, delightful; (अस्), m., N. of a particular mountain; of a king belonging to the Śaiśunāga dynasty.
54327: हर्षण, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, causing delight, de-lighting, gladdening, delightful, pleasurable, pleasant; (अस्), m. who or what delights or rejoices; ‘glad-dener,’ epithet of one of the five arrows of Kāma-deva; the fourteenth of the astronomical Yogas; a morbid affection of the eyes; a deity presiding over Śrāddhas; a kind of Śrāddha; (अम्), n. the act of delighting or making glad, pleasing, making happy; rejoicing, being happy.
54328: हर्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoicing, joyful, cheer-ful, happy.
54329: हर्षयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to rejoice, glad-dening.
54330: हर्षयित्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, gladdening, causing de-light, delighting; (उस्), m. a son, child; (उ), n. gold.
54331: हर्षाय, Nom. A. हर्षायते, &c., to be glad.
54332: हर्षित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), made glad or happy, gladdened, delighted, happy.
54333: हर्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, rejoicing, delighting; (इणी), f. a particular plant (= वि-जया).
54334: हर्षु, Ved. joy, delight. —हर्षु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. delighted, exulting; eager for war, (Sāy. = हर्ष-युक्त, i. e. सङ्ग्रामोत्सुक, Ṛg-veda VIII. 16, 4.)
54335: हर्षुल, अस्, आ, अम्, disposed to be cheerful or happy, delighted; (अस्), m. a deer; a lover.
54336: हृषि, (probably) rejoicing; (ई), m. du. Agni and Soma, (according to Śabda-k. = अग्नी-सोमौ।) —हृषी-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. full of joy, glad, happy, (Sāy. = प्राप्त-हर्ष, Ṛg-veda II. 31, 1.)
54337: हृषित, अस्, आ, अम्, having the hair bristling or thrilling (with joy &c.); enraptured, delighted, pleased; astonished, surprised; erect, fresh (as flowers, opposed to म्लान); disappointed, deceived; bent, bowed (= प्र-णत); armed, accoutred (= वर्-मित). —हृषित-स्रज्, क्, क्, क्, having a fresh gar-land (the flowers of which are erect and unfaded).
54338: हृषीक, अम्, n. any organ of sense (= इन्द्रिय)। —हृषीकेश (°क-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of the organs of sense,’ Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa. —हृषीकेश-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
54339: हृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. हृषित], having the hair of the body bristling or thrilling (with delight or rapture), enraptured, delighted, rejoiced, pleased, glad, joyous, delighted; exulting, laughing, smiling; astonished, surprised; disappointed, deceived (= प्रति-हत). —हृष्ट-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoiced in heart. —हृष्ट-पुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, merry and fat, happy and well-fed. —हृष्ट-पुष्टाङ्ग (°ट-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, merry and fat in limb, happy and well nourished, frisky and fat. —हृष्ट-मानस, अस्, ई, अम्, rejoiced in mind, glad in heart, happy. —हृष्ट-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, thrilling with happi-ness, in a happy or cheerful mood. —हृष्ट-रोमन्, आ, आ, अ, having the hair of the body bristling or thrilling (with delight or rapture). —हृष्ट-वत्, ind. cheerfully. —हृष्ट-वदन, अस्, आ, अम्, merry-faced, having a cheerful countenance. —हृ-ष्ट-सङ्कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, pleased in mind, con-tented, glad. —हृष्ट-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, joyous-hearted, light-hearted, happy.
54340: हृष्टि, इस्, f. delight, pleasure, joy, happiness; pride, arrogance.
54341: हृष्ट्वा, ind. having rejoiced, being delighted.
54342: हे हे, ind. a vocative particle (oh! ho! &c.); a particle used in vociferating or challenging (hallo! ho there!); an interjection expressing envy or ill-will or disapprobation.
54343: हेक्का हेक्का, f. (fr. rt. हिक्क्), hiccough.
54344: हेठ् हेठ् (according to some written हेट्), cl. 1. A. P. हेठते, हेठति (according to some हेटति), जिहेठे, हेठितुम्, to be wicked; to vex, harass, obstruct; to strike, hurt, injure; cl. 9. P. हेठ्नाति, &c. = rt. हेढ्: Caus. हेठयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अजिहेठत्।
54345: हेठ, अस्, m. vexation, harassing; hindering, preventing, hindrance, obstruction, opposition; in-jury, hurt.
54346: हेड् हेड् or (in the Veda) हेल् or हेऌ (see rt. हेल्), cl. 1. A. हेडते (Ved. हेलते, हे-ऌअते), जिहेडे, हेडितुम्, to disregard, slight, neglect; to be displeased or angry (Ved.; हेऌअते = क्रुध्यति, Naigh. II. 12); cl. 1. P. हेडति, जिहेड, &c., to surround, clothe, attire: Pass. हेड्यते, Aor. अहिडि or अहीडि or अहेडि, to be surrounded or attired: Caus. हेडयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अजिहेडत्, to cause to disregard, &c.; हिडयति, -यितुम्, अजीहिडत्, to cause to surround.
54347: हेड, अस्, m. disregard, slight. —हेड-ज, अस्, m. passion, anger, displeasure.
54348: हेडमान, अस्, आ, अम्, disregarding, neglecting, neglectful.
54349: हेडस्, अस्, n., Ved. anger, wrath, (Sāy. = क्रोध।)
54350: हेऌअस्, अस्, n., Ved. = हेडस् above.
54351: हेडावुक्क हेडावुक्क, अस्, m. (= हेलावुक्क, q. v.), a horse-dealer, horse-seller.
54352: हेढ् हेढ् (also written हेठ्), cl. 9. P. हेढ्नाति, &c., to be born again; to pro-duce happiness, cause prosperity; to purify [cf. rts. खच्, खव्].
54355: हेमन् 2. हेमन्, अ, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 144. fr. rt. 1. हि, perhaps connected with 1. हरि-मन्, ‘yellowness,’ p. 1167; cf. प्र-उग for प्र-युग; or perhaps connected with हिम, 1. हेमन् at pp. 1172, 1173), gold; water, (in Naigh. I. 2. enumerated among the हिरण्य-नामानि, and in I. 12. among the उदक-नामानि); the thorn-apple; the Keśara flower. —हेम-कक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, having a golden girdle; having golden walls. —हेम-कन्दल, अस्, m. ‘having golden shoots,’ coral. —हेम-कर, अस्, m. a gold-worker, gold-smith; epithet of Śiva. —हेम-कर्तृ, ता, m. a goldsmith; a kind of bird. —हेम-कान्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, having a golden lustre; (इस्), f. a kind of Curcuma (= दारु-हरिद्रा). —हेम-कार, अस्, m. a gold-worker, goldsmith. —हेम-किञ्जल्क, अम्, n. ‘hav-ing golden filaments,’ the Nāga-keśara flower. —हे-म-किरीट-मालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, garlanded with a diadem of gold. —हेम-कुम्भ, अस्, m. a golden jar. —हेम-कूट, अस्, m. ‘golden-peaked,’ (perhaps also connected with 1. हेमन् at p. 1173, col. 1), one of the ranges of mountains dividing the known continent into nine Varṣas, (supposed to be situated north of Himālaya and forming with it the boundaries of the Kinnara or Kimpuruṣa Varṣa, see वर्ष।) —हेम-केतकी, f. a kind of tree (= स्वर्ण-केतकी). —हेम-केलि, इस्, m. ‘golden-sport,’ epithet of Agni or fire. —हेम-केश, अस्, m. ‘golden-haired,’ Śiva. —हेम-क्षीरी, f. the plant Svarṇa-kṣīrī, q. v. —हेम-गन्धिनी, f. the perfume Re-ṇukā. —हेम-गौर, अस्, ई, अम्, of a golden yellow colour; (अस्), m. the Kiṅkirāta tree. —हेमगौ-राङ्ग (°र-अङ्°), अस्, आ or ई, अम्, having limbs or a body of a golden yellow colour. —हेम-चक्र, अस्, आ, अम्, golden-wheeled, having wheels of gold. —हेम-चन्द्र, अस्, m. a golden or golden-coloured moon; N. of a king of Vaiśālī; of a phi-losopher; of a celebrated lexicographer and author (son of Jaya-siṃha-deva, author of the Abhidhāna-cintāmaṇi lexicon; of the Uṇādi-vṛtti; of a Dhātu-pāṭha; of the Vibhrama-sūtra; of a Prākṛt gram-mar; of the Chandaś-cūḍāmaṇi, &c.). —हेम-च्छन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with gold; (अम्), n. a golden covering, golden trappings (of an elephant &c.). —हेम-जीवन्ती, f. a kind of plant (= स्वर्ण-जीवन्ती). —हेम-ज्वाल, अस्, m. ‘golden-flamed,’ fire. —हेम-तरु, उस्, m. ‘golden tree,’ the Datura or thorn-apple. —हेम-तार, अम्, n. = हेम-सार, blue vitriol (= तुत्थ). —हेम-दुग्ध, अस्, m. ‘having golden or yellow juice,’ the glomerous fig-tree; (आ), f. the plant Svarṇa-kṣīrī; (ई), f. the plant Svarṇa-kṣīrī; a kind of tree (= यज्ञोडुम्बर)। —हेम-दुग्धक, अस्, इका, अम्, having golden or yellow juice; (अस्), m. = हेम-दुग्ध above. —हेम-नाभि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a golden nave or centre. —हेम-पर्वत, अस्, m. ‘golden-mountain,’ the mountain Meru. —हेम-पीठाधिदेवता (°ठ-अध्°), f. the tutelary deity of a golden foot-stool, (epithet of a monarch's foot.) —हेम-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘bearing golden flowers,’ the Campaka tree; the Lodhra tree; (ई), f. Bengal madder; other plants, = स्वर्ण-जीवन्ती, इन्द्र-वारुणी, स्वर्णुली, मु-षली, कण्टकारी; (अम्), n. the Aśoka flower; the flower of the China rose. —हेम-पुष्पक, अस्, m. the Campaka tree; the Lodhra tree; (इका), f. the golden or yellow jasmine. —हेम-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, having golden fruit; (आ), f. a kind of plantain (= स्वर्ण-कदली). —हेम-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of gold, golden. —हेम-माला, f. a golden garland; ‘golden-garlanded,’ the wife of Yama. —हेम-मालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a golden garland, golden-crowned; (ई), m. the sun. —हेम-मृग, अस्, m. a golden deer, (according to a popular legend, the Rākṣasa Mārīca transformed himself into a golden deer and so captivated Rāma-candra and his wife Sītā, that the former left his cottage in the forest to pursue the beautiful animal; during his absence the Rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, q. v., disguised as a mendicant, presented himself before Sītā and carried her off; the whole story is told in the third book or Araṇya-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa.) —हेम-यूथिका, f. the golden or yellow jasmine. —हेम-रत्न-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of gold and gems. —हेम-रागिणी, f. ‘gold-coloured,’ tur-meric. —हेम-राज, अस्, m. a proper N. —हेम-रेणु, उस्, उ, m. n. ‘golden-dust,’ a sort of atom; [cf. सु-रेणु, त्रस-र्°।] —हेम-लता, f. ‘golden-creeper,’ a kind of plant (= स्वर्ण-जीवन्ती). —हे-म-लम्ब or हेम-लम्बक, अस्, m. epithet of the fifth (or thirty-first) year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years. —हेम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, golden. —हेम-व्याकरण, अम्, n., N. of a work on grammar by Hema-sūri or Hema-candra. —हेम-शङ्ख, अस्, m. ‘having a golden conch,’ Viṣṇu. —हेम-शिखा, f. ‘gold-crested,’ the plant Svarṇa-kṣīrī, q. v. —हेम-शृङ्ग, अम्, n. a golden horn; a golden peak or summit. —हेम-शृङ्गिन्, ई, इणी, इ, golden-horned, golden-peaked. —हेम-सार, अम्, n. blue vitriol or sulphate of copper; [cf. हेम-तार।] —हेम-सूत्र or हेम-सूत्रक, अम्, n. ‘gold-string,’ a kind of necklace. —हेम-सूरि, इस्, m., N. of a grammarian (= हेम-चन्द्र). —हेम-हस्ति-रथ, अस्, m. ‘golden-elephant-chariot,’ N. of one of the sixteen Mahā-dānas; [cf. हिरण्याश्व-रथ।] —हेमाङ्ग (°म-अङ्°), अम्, n. a golden body; (अस्, आ or ई, अम्), having a golden body, golden-limbed, golden; (अस्), m. Garuḍa; a lion; the mountain Su-meru; Brahmā; Viṣṇu; the Cam-paka tree. —हेमाङ्ग-द, अस्, m., N. of a Gan-dharva. —हेमाढ्य (°म-आढ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, abounding in gold. —हेमाद्रि (°म-अद्°), इस्, m. ‘golden-mountain,’ (perhaps also connected with 1. हेमन् at p. 1173, col. 1), the mountain Su-meru; N. of a Kṣatriya king, (according to Śabda-k. author of the Cintāmaṇi-kāmadhenu-kalpadruma-smṛti-saṅgraha; also author of the Harilīlā-viveka and of a commentary on the Aṣṭāṅga-hṛdaya-saṃhitā, &c.); N. of a work. —हेमाद्रि-जरण, अस्, m. the plant Svarṇa-kṣīrī, q. v. —हेमाम्भोज (°म-अम्°), अम्, n. a golden lotus-flower. —हे-माह्व (°म-आह्°), अस्, m. ‘called after gold,’ the wild Campaka tree; the thorn-apple; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= स्वर्ण-जीवन्ती).
54356: हेम, अम्, n. (abbreviated fr. 2. हेमन्, col. 1), gold; (अस्), m. a horse of a dark or brownish colour [cf. हरिय, p. 1167]; a particular weight of gold (= माषक); N. of the father of Su-tapas; of a king; = हेम-चन्द्र, q. v.; (आ), f. a handsome woman; an Apsaras of Indra's heaven; N. of a river.
54358: हेमल, अस्, m. a goldsmith; a chameleon, lizard; the touchstone.
54360: हेम्य, अस्, आ, अम्, golden, made of gold. —हे-म्या-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having golden trappings, (Sāy. = सुवर्ण-निर्मित-कक्ष्यावत्, having a girth made of gold, Ṛg-veda IV. 2, 8.)
54363: हेय हेय। See under rts. 2. 3. हा, 1. हि।
54364: हेर हेर, अम्, n. (perhaps fr. rt. 1. हि, or connected with rt. 1. हृ), a sort of crown or tiara; turmeric; demoniacal illusion.
54365: हेरिक, अस्, m. [cf. हैरिक], a spy, secret emis-sary or agent, (said to be also written हेरक।)
54366: हेरम्ब हेरम्ब, अस्, m., N. of Gaṇeśa; a buffalo; a boastful hero (vain of his own valour); a particular Buddha (= हेरुक). —हेरम्ब-जननी, f. ‘mother of Gaṇeśa,’ Durgā. —हेरम्ब-मन्त्र, अस्, m. a particular Mantra (sacred to Gaṇeśa). —हेरम्ब-हट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a country, (said to be one of the provinces of the Deccan.)
54367: हैरम्ब, अस्, ई, अम्, connected with or belong-ing to Gaṇeśa; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a sect.
54368: हेरुक हेरुक, अस्, m. an attendant on Mahā-kāla or Śiva; (with Buddhists) an inferior Buddha.
54369: हेल् 1. हेल्। See rt. हेड्, p. 1176.
54370: हेल् 2. हेल् or हेऌ (connected with rt. हिल्) = rt. हेड्, q. v.; cl. 1. A. हेलते, &c., to disregard, slight; to be angry, &c.
54371: हीऌइत, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Sāy. fr. rt. हेड् or हेऌ), Ved. angry, displeased (= क्रुद्ध, Ṛg-veda I. 80, 5).
54372: हेलञ्ची, f. a kind of pot-herb (= हिल-मोचि).
54373: हेलन, अम्, n. the act of disregarding, slighting, disrespect, contempt [cf. अव-हेलन]; sporting amorously, wanton dalliance; [cf. rt. हिल्।]
